<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-search">search</h1>

## Get async search results

<a id="opIdasync-search-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_async_search/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_async_search/{id}`

Retrieve the results of a previously submitted asynchronous search request.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, access to the results of a specific async search is restricted to the user or API key that submitted it.

<h3 id="get-async-search-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A unique identifier for the async search.|
|keep_alive|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The length of time that the async search should be available in the cluster.<br>When not specified, the `keep_alive` set with the corresponding submit async request will be used.<br>Otherwise, it is possible to override the value and extend the validity of the request.<br>When this period expires, the search, if still running, is cancelled.<br>If the search is completed, its saved results are deleted.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specify whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response|
|wait_for_completion_timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Specifies to wait for the search to be completed up until the provided timeout.<br>Final results will be returned if available before the timeout expires, otherwise the currently available results will be returned once the timeout expires.<br>By default no timeout is set meaning that the currently available results will be returned without any additional wait.|
|return_intermediate_results|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the response should contain intermediate results if the query is still running when the wait_for_completion_timeout<br>expires or if no wait_for_completion_timeout is specified.<br>If true and the search is still running, the search response<br>will include any hits and partial aggregations that are available.<br>If false and the search is still running, the search response will not include any hits (but possibly include<br>total hits) nor will include any partial aggregations.<br>When not specified, the intermediate results are returned for running queries.|

## Delete an async search

<a id="opIdasync-search-delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_async_search/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_async_search/{id}`

If the asynchronous search is still running, it is cancelled.
Otherwise, the saved search results are deleted.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the deletion of a specific async search is restricted to: the authenticated user that submitted the original search request; users that have the `cancel_task` cluster privilege.

<h3 id="delete-an-async-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A unique identifier for the async search.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-async-search-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get the async search status

<a id="opIdasync-search-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_async_search/status/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_async_search/status/{id}`

Get the status of a previously submitted async search request given its identifier, without retrieving search results.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the access to the status of a specific async search is restricted to:

* The user or API key that submitted the original async search request.
* Users that have the `monitor` cluster privilege or greater privileges.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-the-async-search-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A unique identifier for the async search.|
|keep_alive|query|object|false|The length of time that the async search needs to be available.<br>Ongoing async searches and any saved search results are deleted after this period.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"id\" : \"FmRldE8zREVEUzA2ZVpUeGs2ejJFUFEaMkZ5QTVrSTZSaVN3WlNFVmtlWHJsdzoxMDc=\",\n  \"is_running\" : true,\n  \"is_partial\" : true,\n  \"start_time_in_millis\" : 1583945890986,\n  \"expiration_time_in_millis\" : 1584377890986,\n  \"_shards\" : {\n      \"total\" : 562,\n      \"successful\" : 188, \n      \"skipped\" : 0,\n      \"failed\" : 0\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-the-async-search-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[async_search.status.StatusResponseBase](#schemaasync_search.status.statusresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run an async search

<a id="opIdasync-search-submit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_async_search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"sort\": [\n    { \"date\": { \"order\": \"asc\" } }\n  ],\n  \"aggs\": {\n    \"sale_date\": {\n      \"date_histogram\": {\n        \"field\": \"date\",\n        \"calendar_interval\": \"1d\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_async_search`

When the primary sort of the results is an indexed field, shards get sorted based on minimum and maximum value that they hold for that field. Partial results become available following the sort criteria that was requested.

Warning: Asynchronous search does not support scroll or search requests that include only the suggest section.

By default, Elasticsearch does not allow you to store an async search response larger than 10Mb and an attempt to do this results in an error.
The maximum allowed size for a stored async search response can be set by changing the `search.max_async_search_response_size` cluster level setting.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"sort\": [\n    { \"date\": { \"order\": \"asc\" } }\n  ],\n  \"aggs\": {\n    \"sale_date\": {\n      \"date_histogram\": {\n        \"field\": \"date\",\n        \"calendar_interval\": \"1d\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-an-async-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|wait_for_completion_timeout|query|object|false|Blocks and waits until the search is completed up to a certain timeout.<br>When the async search completes within the timeout, the response won’t include the ID as the results are not stored in the cluster.|
|keep_alive|query|object|false|Specifies how long the async search needs to be available.<br>Ongoing async searches and any saved search results are deleted after this period.|
|keep_on_completion|query|boolean|false|If `true`, results are stored for later retrieval when the search completes within the `wait_for_completion_timeout`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|Indicate if an error should be returned if there is a partial search failure or timeout|
|analyzer|query|string|false|The analyzer to use for the query string|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|Specify whether wildcard and prefix queries should be analyzed|
|batched_reduce_size|query|number|false|Affects how often partial results become available, which happens whenever shard results are reduced.<br>A partial reduction is performed every time the coordinating node has received a certain number of new shard responses (5 by default).|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|The default value is the only supported value.|
|default_operator|query|object|false|The default operator for query string query (AND or OR)|
|df|query|string|false|The field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string|
|docvalue_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to return as the docvalue representation of a field for each hit|

<h3 id="run-an-async-search-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[async_search._types.AsyncSearchDocumentResponseBase](#schemaasync_search._types.asyncsearchdocumentresponsebase)|
|400|Bad Request||[async_search._types.AsyncSearchResponseException](#schemaasync_search._types.asyncsearchresponseexception)|
|404|Not Found||[async_search._types.AsyncSearchResponseException](#schemaasync_search._types.asyncsearchresponseexception)|
|429|Too Many Requests||[async_search._types.AsyncSearchResponseException](#schemaasync_search._types.asyncsearchresponseexception)|
|500|Internal Server Error||[async_search._types.AsyncSearchResponseException](#schemaasync_search._types.asyncsearchresponseexception)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run an async search

<a id="opIdasync-search-submit-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_async_search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"sort\": [\n    { \"date\": { \"order\": \"asc\" } }\n  ],\n  \"aggs\": {\n    \"sale_date\": {\n      \"date_histogram\": {\n        \"field\": \"date\",\n        \"calendar_interval\": \"1d\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_async_search`

When the primary sort of the results is an indexed field, shards get sorted based on minimum and maximum value that they hold for that field. Partial results become available following the sort criteria that was requested.

Warning: Asynchronous search does not support scroll or search requests that include only the suggest section.

By default, Elasticsearch does not allow you to store an async search response larger than 10Mb and an attempt to do this results in an error.
The maximum allowed size for a stored async search response can be set by changing the `search.max_async_search_response_size` cluster level setting.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"sort\": [\n    { \"date\": { \"order\": \"asc\" } }\n  ],\n  \"aggs\": {\n    \"sale_date\": {\n      \"date_histogram\": {\n        \"field\": \"date\",\n        \"calendar_interval\": \"1d\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-an-async-search-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of index names to search; use `_all` or empty string to perform the operation on all indices|
|wait_for_completion_timeout|query|object|false|Blocks and waits until the search is completed up to a certain timeout.<br>When the async search completes within the timeout, the response won’t include the ID as the results are not stored in the cluster.|
|keep_alive|query|object|false|Specifies how long the async search needs to be available.<br>Ongoing async searches and any saved search results are deleted after this period.|
|keep_on_completion|query|boolean|false|If `true`, results are stored for later retrieval when the search completes within the `wait_for_completion_timeout`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|Indicate if an error should be returned if there is a partial search failure or timeout|
|analyzer|query|string|false|The analyzer to use for the query string|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|Specify whether wildcard and prefix queries should be analyzed|
|batched_reduce_size|query|number|false|Affects how often partial results become available, which happens whenever shard results are reduced.<br>A partial reduction is performed every time the coordinating node has received a certain number of new shard responses (5 by default).|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|The default value is the only supported value.|
|default_operator|query|object|false|The default operator for query string query (AND or OR)|
|df|query|string|false|The field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string|
|docvalue_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to return as the docvalue representation of a field for each hit|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both|
|explain|query|boolean|false|Specify whether to return detailed information about score computation as part of a hit|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|Whether specified concrete, expanded or aliased indices should be ignored when throttled|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|lenient|query|boolean|false|Specify whether format-based query failures (such as providing text to a numeric field) should be ignored|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|The number of concurrent shard requests per node this search executes concurrently.<br>This value should be used to limit the impact of the search on the cluster in order to limit the number of concurrent shard requests|
|preference|query|string|false|Specify the node or shard the operation should be performed on|
|request_cache|query|boolean|false|Specify if request cache should be used for this request or not, defaults to true|
|routing|query|[_types.Routing](#schema_types.routing)|false|A comma-separated list of specific routing values|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Search operation type|
|stats|query|[string]|false|Specific 'tag' of the request for logging and statistical purposes|
|stored_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|A comma-separated list of stored fields to return as part of a hit|
|suggest_field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|Specifies which field to use for suggestions.|
|suggest_mode|query|object|false|Specify suggest mode|
|suggest_size|query|number|false|How many suggestions to return in response|
|suggest_text|query|string|false|The source text for which the suggestions should be returned.|
|terminate_after|query|number|false|The maximum number of documents to collect for each shard, upon reaching which the query execution will terminate early|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Explicit operation timeout|
|track_total_hits|query|[_global.search._types.TrackHits](#schema_global.search._types.trackhits)|false|Indicate if the number of documents that match the query should be tracked.<br>A number can also be specified, to accurately track the total hit count up to the number.|

## Run a scrolling search

<a id="opIdscroll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search/scroll \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_search/scroll`

IMPORTANT: The scroll API is no longer recommend for deep pagination. If you need to preserve the index state while paging through more than 10,000 hits, use the `search_after` parameter with a point in time (PIT).

The scroll API gets large sets of results from a single scrolling search request.
To get the necessary scroll ID, submit a search API request that includes an argument for the `scroll` query parameter.
The `scroll` parameter indicates how long Elasticsearch should retain the search context for the request.
The search response returns a scroll ID in the `_scroll_id` response body parameter.
You can then use the scroll ID with the scroll API to retrieve the next batch of results for the request.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the access to the results of a specific scroll ID is restricted to the user or API key that submitted the search.

You can also use the scroll API to specify a new scroll parameter that extends or shortens the retention period for the search context.

IMPORTANT: Results from a scrolling search reflect the state of the index at the time of the initial search request. Subsequent indexing or document changes only affect later search and scroll requests.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/paginate-search-results#scroll-search-results">About paginating search results</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-a-scrolling-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scroll|query|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|scroll_id|query|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|false|**Deprecated.** The scroll ID|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an integer. If false, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an object.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scroll|body|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» scroll_id|body|object|true|The scroll ID of the search.|

|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|

## Clear a scrolling search

<a id="opIdclear-scroll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search/scroll \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"scroll_id\": \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"'
```

`DELETE /_search/scroll`

Clear the search context and results for a scrolling search.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/paginate-search-results#scroll-search-results">About paginating search results</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"scroll_id\": \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scroll_id|body|object|false|The scroll IDs to clear.<br>To clear all scroll IDs, use `_all`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "succeeded": true,
  "num_freed": 0
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "succeeded": true,
  "num_freed": 0
}
```

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|404|Not Found||Inline|

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the request succeeded.<br>This does not indicate whether any scrolling search requests were cleared.|
|num_freed|number|true|none|The number of scrolling search requests cleared.|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|none|
|num_freed|number|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run a scrolling search

<a id="opIdscroll-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search/scroll/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_search/scroll/{scroll_id}`

IMPORTANT: The scroll API is no longer recommend for deep pagination. If you need to preserve the index state while paging through more than 10,000 hits, use the `search_after` parameter with a point in time (PIT).

The scroll API gets large sets of results from a single scrolling search request.
To get the necessary scroll ID, submit a search API request that includes an argument for the `scroll` query parameter.
The `scroll` parameter indicates how long Elasticsearch should retain the search context for the request.
The search response returns a scroll ID in the `_scroll_id` response body parameter.
You can then use the scroll ID with the scroll API to retrieve the next batch of results for the request.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the access to the results of a specific scroll ID is restricted to the user or API key that submitted the search.

You can also use the scroll API to specify a new scroll parameter that extends or shortens the retention period for the search context.

IMPORTANT: Results from a scrolling search reflect the state of the index at the time of the initial search request. Subsequent indexing or document changes only affect later search and scroll requests.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/paginate-search-results#scroll-search-results">About paginating search results</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-a-scrolling-search-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scroll_id|path|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|true|**Deprecated.** The scroll ID|
|scroll|query|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|scroll_id|query|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|false|**Deprecated.** The scroll ID|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an integer. If false, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an object.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scroll|body|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» scroll_id|body|object|true|The scroll ID of the search.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

## Run a scrolling search

<a id="opIdscroll-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search/scroll/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_search/scroll/{scroll_id}`

IMPORTANT: The scroll API is no longer recommend for deep pagination. If you need to preserve the index state while paging through more than 10,000 hits, use the `search_after` parameter with a point in time (PIT).

The scroll API gets large sets of results from a single scrolling search request.
To get the necessary scroll ID, submit a search API request that includes an argument for the `scroll` query parameter.
The `scroll` parameter indicates how long Elasticsearch should retain the search context for the request.
The search response returns a scroll ID in the `_scroll_id` response body parameter.
You can then use the scroll ID with the scroll API to retrieve the next batch of results for the request.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the access to the results of a specific scroll ID is restricted to the user or API key that submitted the search.

You can also use the scroll API to specify a new scroll parameter that extends or shortens the retention period for the search context.

IMPORTANT: Results from a scrolling search reflect the state of the index at the time of the initial search request. Subsequent indexing or document changes only affect later search and scroll requests.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/paginate-search-results#scroll-search-results">About paginating search results</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"scroll_id\" : \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-a-scrolling-search-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scroll_id|path|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|true|**Deprecated.** The scroll ID|
|scroll|query|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|scroll_id|query|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|false|**Deprecated.** The scroll ID|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an integer. If false, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an object.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scroll|body|object|false|The period to retain the search context for scrolling.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» scroll_id|body|object|true|The scroll ID of the search.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

## Clear a scrolling search

<a id="opIdclear-scroll-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search/scroll/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"scroll_id\": \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"'
```

`DELETE /_search/scroll/{scroll_id}`

Clear the search context and results for a scrolling search.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/paginate-search-results#scroll-search-results">About paginating search results</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"scroll_id\": \"DXF1ZXJ5QW5kRmV0Y2gBAAAAAAAAAD4WYm9laVYtZndUQlNsdDcwakFMNjU1QQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scroll_id|path|[_types.ScrollIds](#schema_types.scrollids)|true|**Deprecated.** A comma-separated list of scroll IDs to clear.<br>To clear all scroll IDs, use `_all`.<br>IMPORTANT: Scroll IDs can be long. It is recommended to specify scroll IDs in the request body parameter.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scroll_id|body|object|false|The scroll IDs to clear.<br>To clear all scroll IDs, use `_all`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.ScrollId](#schema_types.scrollid)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "succeeded": true,
  "num_freed": 0
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "succeeded": true,
  "num_freed": 0
}
```

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|404|Not Found||Inline|

<h3 id="clear-a-scrolling-search-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the request succeeded.<br>This does not indicate whether any scrolling search requests were cleared.|
|num_freed|number|true|none|The number of scrolling search requests cleared.|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|none|
|num_freed|number|true|none|none|

## Close a point in time

<a id="opIdclose-point-in-time"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_pit \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"id\": \"46ToAwMDaWR5BXV1aWQyKwZub2RlXzMAAAAAAAAAACoBYwADaWR4BXV1aWQxAgZub2RlXzEAAAAAAAAAAAEBYQADaWR5BXV1aWQyKgZub2RlXzIAAAAAAAAAAAwBYgACBXV1aWQyAAAFdXVpZDEAAQltYXRjaF9hbGw_gAAAAA==\"\n}"'
```

`DELETE /_pit`

A point in time must be opened explicitly before being used in search requests.
The `keep_alive` parameter tells Elasticsearch how long it should persist.
A point in time is automatically closed when the `keep_alive` period has elapsed.
However, keeping points in time has a cost; close them as soon as they are no longer required for search requests.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"id\": \"46ToAwMDaWR5BXV1aWQyKwZub2RlXzMAAAAAAAAAACoBYwADaWR4BXV1aWQxAgZub2RlXzEAAAAAAAAAAAEBYQADaWR5BXV1aWQyKgZub2RlXzIAAAAAAAAAAAwBYgACBXV1aWQyAAAFdXVpZDEAAQltYXRjaF9hbGw_gAAAAA==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="close-a-point-in-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|object|true|The ID of the point-in-time.<br><br>IMPORTANT: Each search request against a PIT returns in its response a `pit_id` field which may be different from the identifier you originally supplied.<br>Always use the most recently-received PIT identifier for the next request.<br>If you make concurrent search requests against the same PIT, Elasticsearch can return several different `pit_id` values in its responses.<br>In that case, use any of these values for later requests, preferring more recently-received values whenever possible.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"succeeded\": true, \n  \"num_freed\": 3     \n}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "succeeded": true,
  "num_freed": 0
}
```

<h3 id="close-a-point-in-time-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|404|Not Found||Inline|

<h3 id="close-a-point-in-time-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|If `true`, all search contexts associated with the point-in-time ID were successfully closed.|
|num_freed|number|true|none|The number of search contexts that were successfully closed.|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|succeeded|boolean|true|none|none|
|num_freed|number|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Count search results

<a id="opIdcount-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_count \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_count`

Get the number of documents matching a query.

The query can be provided either by using a simple query string as a parameter, or by defining Query DSL within the request body.
The query is optional. When no query is provided, the API uses `match_all` to count all the documents.

The count API supports multi-target syntax. You can run a single count API search across multiple data streams and indices.

The operation is broadcast across all shards.
For each shard ID group, a replica is chosen and the search is run against it.
This means that replicas increase the scalability of the count.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"
```

## Count search results

<a id="opIdcount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_count \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_count`

Get the number of documents matching a query.

The query can be provided either by using a simple query string as a parameter, or by defining Query DSL within the request body.
The query is optional. When no query is provided, the API uses `match_all` to count all the documents.

The count API supports multi-target syntax. You can run a single count API search across multiple data streams and indices.

The operation is broadcast across all shards.
For each shard ID group, a replica is chosen and the search is run against it.
This means that replicas increase the scalability of the count.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"
```

## Count search results

<a id="opIdcount-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_count \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_count`

Get the number of documents matching a query.

The query can be provided either by using a simple query string as a parameter, or by defining Query DSL within the request body.
The query is optional. When no query is provided, the API uses `match_all` to count all the documents.

The count API supports multi-target syntax. You can run a single count API search across multiple data streams and indices.

The operation is broadcast across all shards.
For each shard ID group, a replica is chosen and the search is run against it.
This means that replicas increase the scalability of the count.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"
```

## Count search results

<a id="opIdcount-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_count \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_count`

Get the number of documents matching a query.

The query can be provided either by using a simple query string as a parameter, or by defining Query DSL within the request body.
The query is optional. When no query is provided, the API uses `match_all` to count all the documents.

The count API supports multi-target syntax. You can run a single count API search across multiple data streams and indices.

The operation is broadcast across all shards.
For each shard ID group, a replica is chosen and the search is run against it.
This means that replicas increase the scalability of the count.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"term\" : { \"user.id\" : \"kimchy\" }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="count-search-results-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.<br>It supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|analyzer|query|string|false|The analyzer to use for the query string.<br>This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|If `true`, wildcard and prefix queries are analyzed.<br>This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|

## Explain a document match result

<a id="opIdexplain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_explain/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"match\" : { \"message\" : \"elasticsearch\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_explain/{id}`

Get information about why a specific document matches, or doesn't match, a query.
It computes a score explanation for a query and a specific document.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"match\" : { \"message\" : \"elasticsearch\" }\n  }\n}"
```

n + 0.5) / (n + 0.5)) from:\",\n                  \"details\":[\n                    {\n                        \"value\":1,\n                        \"description\":\"n, number of documents containing term\",\n                        \"details\":[]\n                    },\n                    {\n                        \"value\":5,\n                        \"description\":\"N, total number of documents with field\",\n                        \"details\":[]\n                    }\n                  ]\n              },\n              {\n                  \"value\":0.5555556,\n                  \"description\":\"tf, computed as freq / (freq + k1 * (1 - This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Explain a document match result

<a id="opIdexplain-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_explain/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"match\" : { \"message\" : \"elasticsearch\" }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_explain/{id}`

Get information about why a specific document matches, or doesn't match, a query.
It computes a score explanation for a query and a specific document.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\" : {\n    \"match\" : { \"message\" : \"elasticsearch\" }\n  }\n}"
```

## Get the field capabilities

<a id="opIdfield-caps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_field_caps \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_field_caps`

Get information about the capabilities of fields among multiple indices.

For data streams, the API returns field capabilities among the stream’s backing indices.
It returns runtime fields like any other field.
For example, a runtime field with a type of keyword is returned the same as any other field that belongs to the `keyword` family.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`,`read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-the-field-capabilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|The type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to retrieve capabilities for. Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|include_unmapped|query|boolean|false|If true, unmapped fields are included in the response.|
|filters|query|string \| [string]|false|A comma-separated list of filters to apply to the response.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of field types to include.<br>Any fields that do not match one of these types will be excluded from the results.<br>It defaults to empty, meaning that all field types are returned.|
|include_empty_fields|query|boolean|false|If false, empty fields are not included in the response.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» fields|body|object|false|A list of fields to retrieve capabilities for. Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|

## Get the field capabilities

<a id="opIdfield-caps-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_field_caps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_field_caps`

Get information about the capabilities of fields among multiple indices.

For data streams, the API returns field capabilities among the stream’s backing indices.
It returns runtime fields like any other field.
For example, a runtime field with a type of keyword is returned the same as any other field that belongs to the `keyword` family.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`,`read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Get the field capabilities

<a id="opIdfield-caps-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_field_caps \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_field_caps`

Get information about the capabilities of fields among multiple indices.

For data streams, the API returns field capabilities among the stream’s backing indices.
It returns runtime fields like any other field.
For example, a runtime field with a type of keyword is returned the same as any other field that belongs to the `keyword` family.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`,`read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Get the field capabilities

<a id="opIdfield-caps-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_field_caps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_field_caps`

Get information about the capabilities of fields among multiple indices.

For data streams, the API returns field capabilities among the stream’s backing indices.
It returns runtime fields like any other field.
For example, a runtime field with a type of keyword is returned the same as any other field that belongs to the `keyword` family.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`,`read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_filter\": {\n    \"range\": {\n      \"@timestamp\": {\n        \"gte\": \"2018\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Run multiple searches

<a id="opIdmsearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_msearch \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"'
```

`GET /_msearch`

The format of the request is similar to the bulk API format and makes use of the newline delimited JSON (NDJSON) format.
The structure is as follows:

```
header\n
body\n
header\n
body\n
```

This structure is specifically optimized to reduce parsing if a specific search ends up redirected to another node.

IMPORTANT: The final line of data must end with a newline character `\n`.
Each newline character may be preceded by a carriage return `\r`.
When sending requests to this endpoint the `Content-Type` header should be set to `application/x-ndjson`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-searches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|include_named_queries_score|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether hit.matched_queries should be rendered as a map that includes<br>the name of the matched query associated with its score (true)<br>or as an array containing the name of the matched queries (false)<br>This functionality reruns each named query on every hit in a search response.<br>Typically, this adds a small overhead to a request.<br>However, using computationally expensive named queries on a large number of hits may add significant overhead.|
|index|query|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|false|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to use as default|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.<br>Defaults to `max(1, (# of data nodes * min(search thread pool size, 10)))`.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|routing|query|[_types.Routing](#schema_types.routing)|false|Custom routing value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the target index; use `_slice` instead.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run multiple searches

<a id="opIdmsearch-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_msearch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"'
```

`POST /_msearch`

The format of the request is similar to the bulk API format and makes use of the newline delimited JSON (NDJSON) format.
The structure is as follows:

```
header\n
body\n
header\n
body\n
```

This structure is specifically optimized to reduce parsing if a specific search ends up redirected to another node.

IMPORTANT: The final line of data must end with a newline character `\n`.
Each newline character may be preceded by a carriage return `\r`.
When sending requests to this endpoint the `Content-Type` header should be set to `application/x-ndjson`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-searches-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|include_named_queries_score|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether hit.matched_queries should be rendered as a map that includes<br>the name of the matched query associated with its score (true)<br>or as an array containing the name of the matched queries (false)<br>This functionality reruns each named query on every hit in a search response.<br>Typically, this adds a small overhead to a request.<br>However, using computationally expensive named queries on a large number of hits may add significant overhead.|
|index|query|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|false|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to use as default|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.<br>Defaults to `max(1, (# of data nodes * min(search thread pool size, 10)))`.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|routing|query|[_types.Routing](#schema_types.routing)|false|Custom routing value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the target index; use `_slice` instead.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

<h3 id="run-multiple-searches-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_global.msearch.MultiSearchResult](#schema_global.msearch.multisearchresult)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run multiple searches

<a id="opIdmsearch-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_msearch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_msearch`

The format of the request is similar to the bulk API format and makes use of the newline delimited JSON (NDJSON) format.
The structure is as follows:

```
header\n
body\n
header\n
body\n
```

This structure is specifically optimized to reduce parsing if a specific search ends up redirected to another node.

IMPORTANT: The final line of data must end with a newline character `\n`.
Each newline character may be preceded by a carriage return `\r`.
When sending requests to this endpoint the `Content-Type` header should be set to `application/x-ndjson`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{\"query\" : {\"match\" : { \"message\": \"this is a test\"}}}\n{\"index\": \"my-index-000002\"}\n{\"query\" : {\"match_all\" : {}}}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-searches-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to search.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|include_named_queries_score|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether hit.matched_queries should be rendered as a map that includes<br>the name of the matched query associated with its score (true)<br>or as an array containing the name of the matched queries (false)<br>This functionality reruns each named query on every hit in a search response.<br>Typically, this adds a small overhead to a request.<br>However, using computationally expensive named queries on a large number of hits may add significant overhead.|
|index|query|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|false|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to use as default|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.<br>Defaults to `max(1, (# of data nodes * min(search thread pool size, 10)))`.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|routing|query|[_types.Routing](#schema_types.routing)|false|Custom routing value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the target index; use `_slice` instead.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

## Run multiple templated searches

<a id="opIdmsearch-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_msearch/template \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"'
```

`GET /_msearch/template`

Run multiple templated searches with a single request.
If you are providing a text file or text input to `curl`, use the `--data-binary` flag instead of `-d` to preserve newlines.
For example:

```
$ cat requests
{ "index": "my-index" }
{ "id": "my-search-template", "params": { "query_string": "hello world", "from": 0, "size": 10 }}
{ "index": "my-other-index" }
{ "id": "my-other-search-template", "params": { "query_type": "match_all" }}

$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" -XGET localhost:9200/_msearch/template --data-binary "@requests"; echo
```

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/search-templates">More about searching templates</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-templated-searches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If `true`, network round-trips are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|The maximum number of concurrent searches the API can run.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|The type of the search operation.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response returns `hits.total` as an integer.<br>If `false`, it returns `hits.total` as an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response prefixes aggregation and suggester names with their respective types.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch_template.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch_template.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

## Run multiple templated searches

<a id="opIdmsearch-template-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_msearch/template \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_msearch/template`

Run multiple templated searches with a single request.
If you are providing a text file or text input to `curl`, use the `--data-binary` flag instead of `-d` to preserve newlines.
For example:

```
$ cat requests
{ "index": "my-index" }
{ "id": "my-search-template", "params": { "query_string": "hello world", "from": 0, "size": 10 }}
{ "index": "my-other-index" }
{ "id": "my-other-search-template", "params": { "query_type": "match_all" }}

$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" -XGET localhost:9200/_msearch/template --data-binary "@requests"; echo
```

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/search-templates">More about searching templates</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-templated-searches-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.<br>It supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*`.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If `true`, network round-trips are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|The maximum number of concurrent searches the API can run.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|The type of the search operation.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response returns `hits.total` as an integer.<br>If `false`, it returns `hits.total` as an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response prefixes aggregation and suggester names with their respective types.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch_template.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch_template.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

## Run multiple templated searches

<a id="opIdmsearch-template-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_msearch/template \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_msearch/template`

Run multiple templated searches with a single request.
If you are providing a text file or text input to `curl`, use the `--data-binary` flag instead of `-d` to preserve newlines.
For example:

```
$ cat requests
{ "index": "my-index" }
{ "id": "my-search-template", "params": { "query_string": "hello world", "from": 0, "size": 10 }}
{ "index": "my-other-index" }
{ "id": "my-other-search-template", "params": { "query_type": "match_all" }}

$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" -XGET localhost:9200/_msearch/template --data-binary "@requests"; echo
```

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/search-templates">More about searching templates</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_string\": \"hello world\", \"from\": 0, \"size\": 10 }}\n{ }\n{ \"id\": \"my-other-search-template\", \"params\": { \"query_type\": \"match_all\" }}"
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-templated-searches-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.<br>It supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*`.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If `true`, network round-trips are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|The maximum number of concurrent searches the API can run.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|The type of the search operation.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response returns `hits.total` as an integer.<br>If `false`, it returns `hits.total` as an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response prefixes aggregation and suggester names with their respective types.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch_template.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch_template.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

`POST /{index}/_pit`

A search request by default runs against the most recent visible data of the target indices,
which is called point in time. Elasticsearch pit (point in time) is a lightweight view into the
state of the data as it existed when initiated. In some cases, it’s preferred to perform multiple
search requests using the same point in time. For example, if refreshes happen between
`search_after` requests, then the results of those requests might not be consistent as changes happening
between searches are only visible to the more recent point in time.

A point in time must be opened explicitly before being used in search requests.

A subsequent search request with the `pit` parameter must not specify `index`, `routing`, or `preference` values as these parameters are copied from the point in time.

Just like regular searches, you can use `from` and `size` to page through point in time search results, up to the first 10,000 hits.
If you want to retrieve more hits, use PIT with `search_after`.

IMPORTANT: Each search request against a PIT returns in its response a `pit_id` field which may be different from the identifier you originally supplied.
Always use the most recently-received PIT identifier for the next request.
If you make concurrent search requests against the same PIT, Elasticsearch can return several different `pit_id` values in its responses.
In that case, use any of these values for later requests, preferring more recently-received values whenever possible.

When a PIT that contains shard failures is used in a search request, the missing are always reported in the search response as a `NoShardAvailableActionException` exception.
To get rid of these exceptions, a new PIT needs to be created so that shards missing from the previous PIT can be handled, assuming they become available in the meantime.

**Keeping point in time alive**

The `keep_alive` parameter, which is passed to a open point in time request and search request, extends the time to live of the corresponding point in time.
The value does not need to be long enough to process all data — it just needs to be long enough for the next request.

Normally, the background merge process optimizes the index by merging together smaller segments to create new, bigger segments.
Once the smaller segments are no longer needed they are deleted.
However, open point-in-times prevent the old segments from being deleted since they are still in use.

TIP: Keeping older segments alive means that more disk space and file handles are needed.
Ensure that you have configured your nodes to have ample free file handles.

Additionally, if a segment contains deleted or updated documents then the point in time must keep track of whether each document in the segment was live at the time of the initial search request.
Ensure that your nodes have sufficient heap space if you have many open point-in-times on an index that is subject to ongoing deletes or updates.
Note that a point-in-time doesn't prevent its associated indices from being deleted.
You can check how many point-in-times (that is, search contexts) are open with the nodes stats API.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`

<h3 id="open-a-point-in-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of index names to open point in time; use `_all` or empty string to perform the operation on all indices|
|keep_alive|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|true|Extend the length of time that the point in time persists.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|preference|query|string|false|The node or shard the operation should be performed on.<br>By default, it is random.|

## Evaluate ranked search results

<a id="opIdrank-eval"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_rank_eval \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"requests\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"JFK query\",\n      \"request\": { \"query\": { \"match_all\": {} } },\n      \"ratings\": []\n    } ],\n  \"metric\": {\n    \"precision\": {\n      \"k\": 20,\n      \"relevant_rating_threshold\": 1,\n      \"ignore_unlabeled\": false\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_rank_eval`

Evaluate the quality of ranked search results over a set of typical search queries.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/search-rank-eval">More about ranking evaluation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"requests\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"JFK query\",\n      \"request\": { \"query\": { \"match_all\": {} } },\n      \"ratings\": []\n    } ],\n  \"metric\": {\n    \"precision\": {\n      \"k\": 20,\n      \"relevant_rating_threshold\": 1,\n      \"ignore_unlabeled\": false\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="evaluate-ranked-search-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Search operation type|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» requests|body|[[_global.rank_eval.RankEvalRequestItem](#schema_global.rank_eval.rankevalrequestitem)]|true|A set of typical search requests, together with their provided ratings.|
|» metric|body|object|false|Definition of the evaluation metric to calculate.|
|» » precision|body|object|false|none|
|» » » k|body|number|false|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|» » » relevant_rating_threshold|body|number|false|Sets the rating threshold above which documents are considered to be "relevant".|
|» » » ignore_unlabeled|body|boolean|false|Controls how unlabeled documents in the search results are counted. If set to true, unlabeled documents are ignored and neither count as relevant or irrelevant. Set to false (the default), they are treated as irrelevant.|
|» » recall|body|object|false|none|
|» » » k|body|number|false|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|» » » relevant_rating_threshold|body|number|false|Sets the rating threshold above which documents are considered to be "relevant".|
|» » mean_reciprocal_rank|body|object|false|none|
|» » » k|body|number|false|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|» » » relevant_rating_threshold|body|number|false|Sets the rating threshold above which documents are considered to be "relevant".|
|» » dcg|body|object|false|none|
|» » » k|body|number|false|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|» » » normalize|body|boolean|false|If set to true, this metric will calculate the Normalized DCG.|
|» » expected_reciprocal_rank|body|object|false|none|
|» » » k|body|number|false|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|» » » maximum_relevance|body|number|true|The highest relevance grade used in the user-supplied relevance judgments.|

|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

`GET /{index}/_rank_eval`

Evaluate the quality of ranked search results over a set of typical search queries.


<h3 id="evaluate-ranked-search-results-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» » » relevant_rating_threshold|body|number|false|Sets the rating threshold above which documents are considered to be "relevant".|
|» » » ignore_unlabeled|body|boolean|false|Controls how unlabeled documents in the search results are counted. If set to true, unlabeled documents are ignored and neither count as relevant or irrelevant. Set to false (the default), they are treated as irrelevant.|

## Run a search

<a id="opIdsearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"term\": {\n      \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_search`

Get search hits that match the query defined in the request.
You can provide search queries using the `q` query string parameter or the request body.
If both are specified, only the query parameter is used.

If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, you must have the read index privilege for the target data stream, index, or alias. For cross-cluster search, refer to the documentation about configuring CCS privileges.
To search a point in time (PIT) for an alias, you must have the `read` index privilege for the alias's data streams or indices.

**Search slicing**

When paging through a large number of documents, it can be helpful to split the search into multiple slices to consume them independently with the `slice` and `pit` properties.
By default the splitting is done first on the shards, then locally on each shard.

For instance if the number of shards is equal to 2 and you request 4 slices, the slices 0 and 2 are assigned to the first shard and the slices 1 and 3 are assigned to the second shard.

IMPORTANT: The same point-in-time ID should be used for all slices.
If different PIT IDs are used, slices can overlap and miss documents.
This situation can occur because, by default, the splitting criterion is based on Lucene document IDs, which are not stable across changes to the index.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/remote-clusters/remote-clusters-cert#remote-clusters-privileges-ccs">About adding remote clusters</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"term\": {\n      \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```
