## Create or update auto-follow patterns

<a id="opIdccr-put-auto-follow-pattern"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ccr/auto_follow/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"remote_cluster\" : \"remote_cluster\",\n  \"leader_index_patterns\" :\n  [\n    \"leader_index*\"\n  ],\n  \"follow_index_pattern\" : \"{{leader_index}}-follower\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_replicas\": 0\n  },\n  \"max_read_request_operation_count\" : 1024,\n  \"max_outstanding_read_requests\" : 16,\n  \"max_read_request_size\" : \"1024k\",\n  \"max_write_request_operation_count\" : 32768,\n  \"max_write_request_size\" : \"16k\",\n  \"max_outstanding_write_requests\" : 8,\n  \"max_write_buffer_count\" : 512,\n  \"max_write_buffer_size\" : \"512k\",\n  \"max_retry_delay\" : \"10s\",\n  \"read_poll_timeout\" : \"30s\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ccr/auto_follow/{name}`

Create a collection of cross-cluster replication auto-follow patterns for a remote cluster.
Newly created indices on the remote cluster that match any of the patterns are automatically configured as follower indices.
Indices on the remote cluster that were created before the auto-follow pattern was created will not be auto-followed even if they match the pattern.

This API can also be used to update auto-follow patterns.
NOTE: Follower indices that were configured automatically before updating an auto-follow pattern will remain unchanged even if they do not match against the new patterns.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/cross-cluster-replication/manage-auto-follow-patterns">More about auto-follow patterns</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"remote_cluster\" : \"remote_cluster\",\n  \"leader_index_patterns\" :\n  [\n    \"leader_index*\"\n  ],\n  \"follow_index_pattern\" : \"{{leader_index}}-follower\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_replicas\": 0\n  },\n  \"max_read_request_operation_count\" : 1024,\n  \"max_outstanding_read_requests\" : 16,\n  \"max_read_request_size\" : \"1024k\",\n  \"max_write_request_operation_count\" : 32768,\n  \"max_write_request_size\" : \"16k\",\n  \"max_outstanding_write_requests\" : 8,\n  \"max_write_buffer_count\" : 512,\n  \"max_write_buffer_size\" : \"512k\",\n  \"max_retry_delay\" : \"10s\",\n  \"read_poll_timeout\" : \"30s\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-auto-follow-patterns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The name of the collection of auto-follow patterns.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» remote_cluster|body|string|true|The remote cluster containing the leader indices to match against.|
|» follow_index_pattern|body|object|false|The name of follower index. The template {{leader_index}} can be used to derive the name of the follower index from the name of the leader index. When following a data stream, use {{leader_index}}; CCR does not support changes to the names of a follower data stream’s backing indices.|
|» leader_index_patterns|body|object|false|An array of simple index patterns to match against indices in the remote cluster specified by the remote_cluster field.|
|» leader_index_exclusion_patterns|body|object|false|An array of simple index patterns that can be used to exclude indices from being auto-followed. Indices in the remote cluster whose names are matching one or more leader_index_patterns and one or more leader_index_exclusion_patterns won’t be followed.|
|» max_outstanding_read_requests|body|number|false|The maximum number of outstanding reads requests from the remote cluster.|
|» settings|body|object|false|Settings to override from the leader index. Note that certain settings can not be overrode (e.g., index.number_of_shards).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» max_outstanding_write_requests|body|number|false|The maximum number of outstanding reads requests from the remote cluster.|
|» read_poll_timeout|body|object|false|The maximum time to wait for new operations on the remote cluster when the follower index is synchronized with the leader index. When the timeout has elapsed, the poll for operations will return to the follower so that it can update some statistics. Then the follower will immediately attempt to read from the leader again.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_read_request_operation_count|body|number|false|The maximum number of operations to pull per read from the remote cluster.|
|» max_read_request_size|body|object|false|The maximum size in bytes of per read of a batch of operations pulled from the remote cluster.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_retry_delay|body|object|false|The maximum time to wait before retrying an operation that failed exceptionally. An exponential backoff strategy is employed when retrying.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_write_buffer_count|body|number|false|The maximum number of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will be deferred until the number of queued operations goes below the limit.|
|» max_write_buffer_size|body|object|false|The maximum total bytes of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will be deferred until the total bytes of queued operations goes below the limit.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_write_request_operation_count|body|number|false|The maximum number of operations per bulk write request executed on the follower.|
|» max_write_request_size|body|object|false|The maximum total bytes of operations per bulk write request executed on the follower.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

```bash
  -d '"{\n  \"remote_cluster\" : \"remote_cluster\",\n  \"leader_index\" : \"leader_index\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_replicas\": 0\n  },\n  \"max_read_request_operation_count\" : 1024,\n  \"max_outstanding_read_requests\" : 16,\n  \"max_read_request_size\" : \"1024k\",\n  \"max_write_request_operation_count\" : 32768,\n  \"max_write_request_size\" : \"16k\",\n  \"max_outstanding_write_requests\" : 8,\n  \"max_write_buffer_count\" : 512,\n  \"max_write_buffer_size\" : \"512k\",\n  \"max_retry_delay\" : \"10s\",\n  \"read_poll_timeout\" : \"30s\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}/_ccr/follow`

Create a cross-cluster replication follower index that follows a specific leader index.
When the API returns, the follower index exists and cross-cluster replication starts replicating operations from the leader index to the follower index.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"remote_cluster\" : \"remote_cluster\",\n  \"leader_index\" : \"leader_index\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_replicas\": 0\n  },\n  \"max_read_request_operation_count\" : 1024,\n  \"max_outstanding_read_requests\" : 16,\n  \"max_read_request_size\" : \"1024k\",\n  \"max_write_request_operation_count\" : 32768,\n  \"max_write_request_size\" : \"16k\",\n  \"max_outstanding_write_requests\" : 8,\n  \"max_write_buffer_count\" : 512,\n  \"max_write_buffer_size\" : \"512k\",\n  \"max_retry_delay\" : \"10s\",\n  \"read_poll_timeout\" : \"30s\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-follower-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|The name of the follower index.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|wait_for_active_shards|query|object|false|Specifies the number of shards to wait on being active before responding. This defaults to waiting on none of the shards to be<br>active.<br>A shard must be restored from the leader index before being active. Restoring a follower shard requires transferring all the<br>remote Lucene segment files to the follower index.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» data_stream_name|body|string|false|If the leader index is part of a data stream, the name to which the local data stream for the followed index should be renamed.|
|» leader_index|body|object|true|The name of the index in the leader cluster to follow.|
|» max_outstanding_read_requests|body|number|false|The maximum number of outstanding reads requests from the remote cluster.|
|» max_outstanding_write_requests|body|number|false|The maximum number of outstanding write requests on the follower.|
|» max_read_request_operation_count|body|number|false|The maximum number of operations to pull per read from the remote cluster.|
|» max_read_request_size|body|object|false|The maximum size in bytes of per read of a batch of operations pulled from the remote cluster.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_retry_delay|body|object|false|The maximum time to wait before retrying an operation that failed exceptionally. An exponential backoff strategy is employed when<br>retrying.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_write_buffer_count|body|number|false|The maximum number of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will be<br>deferred until the number of queued operations goes below the limit.|
|» max_write_buffer_size|body|object|false|The maximum total bytes of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will<br>be deferred until the total bytes of queued operations goes below the limit.|

## Forget a follower

<a id="opIdccr-forget-follower"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_ccr/forget_follower \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"follower_cluster\" : \"<follower_cluster>\",\n  \"follower_index\" : \"<follower_index>\",\n  \"follower_index_uuid\" : \"<follower_index_uuid>\",\n  \"leader_remote_cluster\" : \"<leader_remote_cluster>\"\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_ccr/forget_follower`

Remove the cross-cluster replication follower retention leases from the leader.

A following index takes out retention leases on its leader index.
These leases are used to increase the likelihood that the shards of the leader index retain the history of operations that the shards of the following index need to run replication.
When a follower index is converted to a regular index by the unfollow API (either by directly calling the API or by index lifecycle management tasks), these leases are removed.
However, removal of the leases can fail, for example when the remote cluster containing the leader index is unavailable.
While the leases will eventually expire on their own, their extended existence can cause the leader index to hold more history than necessary and prevent index lifecycle management from performing some operations on the leader index.
This API exists to enable manually removing the leases when the unfollow API is unable to do so.

NOTE: This API does not stop replication by a following index. If you use this API with a follower index that is still actively following, the following index will add back retention leases on the leader.
The only purpose of this API is to handle the case of failure to remove the following retention leases after the unfollow API is invoked.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/cross-cluster-replication">About cross-cluster replication</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"follower_cluster\" : \"<follower_cluster>\",\n  \"follower_index\" : \"<follower_index>\",\n  \"follower_index_uuid\" : \"<follower_index_uuid>\",\n  \"leader_remote_cluster\" : \"<leader_remote_cluster>\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="forget-a-follower-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the leader index for which specified follower retention leases should be removed|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» follower_cluster|body|string|false|none|
|» follower_index|body|object|false|none|
|» follower_index_uuid|body|object|false|none|
|» leader_remote_cluster|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"_shards\" : {\n    \"total\" : 1,\n    \"successful\" : 1,\n    \"failed\" : 0,\n    \"failures\" : [ ]\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="forget-a-follower-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="forget-a-follower-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_shards|object|true|none|none|
|» failed|object|true|none|The number of shards the operation or search attempted to run on but failed.|
|» successful|object|true|none|The number of shards the operation or search succeeded on.|
|» total|object|true|none|The number of shards the operation or search will run on overall.|
|» failures|[[_types.ShardFailure](#schema_types.shardfailure)]|false|none|none|
|» skipped|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Pause an auto-follow pattern

<a id="opIdccr-pause-auto-follow-pattern"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ccr/auto_follow/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ccr/auto_follow/{name}/pause`

Pause a cross-cluster replication auto-follow pattern.
When the API returns, the auto-follow pattern is inactive.
New indices that are created on the remote cluster and match the auto-follow patterns are ignored.

You can resume auto-following with the resume auto-follow pattern API.
When it resumes, the auto-follow pattern is active again and automatically configures follower indices for newly created indices on the remote cluster that match its patterns.
Remote indices that were created while the pattern was paused will also be followed, unless they have been deleted or closed in the interim.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ccr`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/cross-cluster-replication/manage-auto-follow-patterns">More about auto-follow patterns</a>

<h3 id="pause-an-auto-follow-pattern-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The name of the auto-follow pattern to pause.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\" : true\n}"
```

<h3 id="pause-an-auto-follow-pattern-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /{index}/_ccr/resume_follow`

Resume a cross-cluster replication follower index that was paused.
The follower index could have been paused with the pause follower API.
Alternatively it could be paused due to replication that cannot be retried due to failures during following tasks.
When this API returns, the follower index will resume fetching operations from the leader index.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/cross-cluster-replication">About cross-cluster replication</a>

## Unfollow an index

<a id="opIdccr-unfollow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_ccr/unfollow \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /{index}/_ccr/unfollow`

Convert a cross-cluster replication follower index to a regular index.
The API stops the following task associated with a follower index and removes index metadata and settings associated with cross-cluster replication.
The follower index must be paused and closed before you call the unfollow API.

> info
> Currently cross-cluster replication does not support converting an existing regular index to a follower index. Converting a follower index to a regular index is an irreversible operation.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage_follow_index`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/cross-cluster-replication">About cross-cluster replication</a>

<h3 id="unfollow-an-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|The name of the follower index.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\" : true\n}"
```

<h3 id="unfollow-an-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

## Explain the shard allocations

<a id="opIdcluster-allocation-explain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/allocation/explain \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index\": \"my-index-000001\",\n  \"shard\": 0,\n  \"primary\": false,\n  \"current_node\": \"my-node\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_cluster/allocation/explain`

Get explanations for shard allocations in the cluster.
This API accepts the current_node, index, primary and shard parameters in the request body or in query parameters, but not in both at the same time.
For unassigned shards, it provides an explanation for why the shard is unassigned.
For assigned shards, it provides an explanation for why the shard is remaining on its current node and has not moved or rebalanced to another node.
This API can be very useful when attempting to diagnose why a shard is unassigned or why a shard continues to remain on its current node when you might expect otherwise.
Refer to the linked documentation for examples of how to troubleshoot allocation issues using this API.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/troubleshoot/elasticsearch/cluster-allocation-api-examples">Cluster allocation API examples</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index\": \"my-index-000001\",\n  \"shard\": 0,\n  \"primary\": false,\n  \"current_node\": \"my-node\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="explain-the-shard-allocations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|query|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|The name of the index that you would like an explanation for.|
|shard|query|number|false|An identifier for the shard that you would like an explanation for.|
|primary|query|boolean|false|If true, returns an explanation for the primary shard for the specified shard ID.|
|current_node|query|[_types.NodeId](#schema_types.nodeid)|false|Explain a shard only if it is currently located on the specified node name or node ID.|
|include_disk_info|query|boolean|false|If true, returns information about disk usage and shard sizes.|
|include_yes_decisions|query|boolean|false|If true, returns YES decisions in explanation.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» index|body|object|false|The name of the index that you would like an explanation for.|
|» shard|body|number|false|An identifier for the shard that you would like an explanation for.|
|» primary|body|boolean|false|If true, returns an explanation for the primary shard for the specified shard ID.|
|» current_node|body|object|false|Explain a shard only if it is currently located on the specified node name or node ID.|

## Update voting configuration exclusions

<a id="opIdcluster-post-voting-config-exclusions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/voting_config_exclusions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`

Update the cluster voting config exclusions by node IDs or node names.
By default, if there are more than three master-eligible nodes in the cluster and you remove fewer than half of the master-eligible nodes in the cluster at once, the voting configuration automatically shrinks.
If you want to shrink the voting configuration to contain fewer than three nodes or to remove half or more of the master-eligible nodes in the cluster at once, use this API to remove departing nodes from the voting configuration manually.
The API adds an entry for each specified node to the cluster’s voting configuration exclusions list.
It then waits until the cluster has reconfigured its voting configuration to exclude the specified nodes.

Clusters should have no voting configuration exclusions in normal operation.
Once the excluded nodes have stopped, clear the voting configuration exclusions with `DELETE /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`.
This API waits for the nodes to be fully removed from the cluster before it returns.
If your cluster has voting configuration exclusions for nodes that you no longer intend to remove, use `DELETE /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions?wait_for_removal=false` to clear the voting configuration exclusions without waiting for the nodes to leave the cluster.

A response to `POST /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions` with an HTTP status code of 200 OK guarantees that the node has been removed from the voting configuration and will not be reinstated until the voting configuration exclusions are cleared by calling `DELETE /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`.
If the call to `POST /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions` fails or returns a response with an HTTP status code other than 200 OK then the node may not have been removed from the voting configuration.
In that case, you may safely retry the call.

NOTE: Voting exclusions are required only when you remove at least half of the master-eligible nodes from a cluster in a short time period.
They are not required when removing master-ineligible nodes or when removing fewer than half of the master-eligible nodes.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/maintenance/add-and-remove-elasticsearch-nodes">More about node management</a>

<h3 id="update-voting-configuration-exclusions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_names|query|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|false|A comma-separated list of the names of the nodes to exclude from the<br>voting configuration. If specified, you may not also specify node_ids.|
|node_ids|query|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|false|A comma-separated list of the persistent ids of the nodes to exclude<br>from the voting configuration. If specified, you may not also specify node_names.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|When adding a voting configuration exclusion, the API waits for the<br>specified nodes to be excluded from the voting configuration before<br>returning. If the timeout expires before the appropriate condition<br>is satisfied, the request fails and returns an error.|

<h3 id="update-voting-configuration-exclusions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Clear cluster voting config exclusions

<a id="opIdcluster-delete-voting-config-exclusions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/voting_config_exclusions \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_cluster/voting_config_exclusions`

Remove master-eligible nodes from the voting configuration exclusion list.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/maintenance/add-and-remove-elasticsearch-nodes">More about node management</a>

<h3 id="clear-cluster-voting-config-exclusions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|wait_for_removal|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to wait for all excluded nodes to be removed from the<br>cluster before clearing the voting configuration exclusions list.<br>Defaults to true, meaning that all excluded nodes must be removed from<br>the cluster before this API takes any action. If set to false then the<br>voting configuration exclusions list is cleared even if some excluded<br>nodes are still in the cluster.|

## Update the cluster settings

<a id="opIdcluster-put-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"persistent\" : {\n    \"indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec\" : \"50mb\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_cluster/settings`

Configure and update dynamic settings on a running cluster.
You can also configure dynamic settings locally on an unstarted or shut down node in `elasticsearch.yml`.

Updates made with this API can be persistent, which apply across cluster restarts, or transient, which reset after a cluster restart.
You can also reset transient or persistent settings by assigning them a null value.

If you configure the same setting using multiple methods, Elasticsearch applies the settings in following order of precedence: 1) Transient setting; 2) Persistent setting; 3) `elasticsearch.yml` setting; 4) Default setting value.
For example, you can apply a transient setting to override a persistent setting or `elasticsearch.yml` setting.
However, a change to an `elasticsearch.yml` setting will not override a defined transient or persistent setting.

TIP: In Elastic Cloud, use the user settings feature to configure all cluster settings. This method automatically rejects unsafe settings that could break your cluster.
If you run Elasticsearch on your own hardware, use this API to configure dynamic cluster settings.
Only use `elasticsearch.yml` for static cluster settings and node settings.
The API doesn’t require a restart and ensures a setting’s value is the same on all nodes.

WARNING: Transient cluster settings are no longer recommended. Use persistent cluster settings instead.
If a cluster becomes unstable, transient settings can clear unexpectedly, resulting in a potentially undesired cluster configuration.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/stack-settings">More about Elastic Stack settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"persistent\" : {\n    \"indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec\" : \"50mb\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-the-cluster-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Return settings in flat format|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» persistent|body|object|false|The settings that persist after the cluster restarts.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» transient|body|object|false|The settings that do not persist after the cluster restarts.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "persistent": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "transient": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-cluster-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="update-the-cluster-settings-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|persistent|object|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|transient|object|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

## Get the cluster health status

<a id="opIdcluster-health"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/health`

You can also use the API to get the health status of only specified data streams and indices.
For data streams, the API retrieves the health status of the stream’s backing indices.

The cluster health status is: green, yellow or red.
On the shard level, a red status indicates that the specific shard is not allocated in the cluster. Yellow means that the primary shard is allocated but replicas are not. Green means that all shards are allocated.
The index level status is controlled by the worst shard status.

One of the main benefits of the API is the ability to wait until the cluster reaches a certain high watermark health level.
The cluster status is controlled by the worst index status.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-the-cluster-health-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.|
|level|query|object|false|Return health information at a specific level of detail.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If true, retrieve information from the local node only.<br>If false, retrieve information from the master node.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|wait_for_active_shards|query|object|false|Wait for the specified number of active shards.<br>Use `all` to wait for all shards in the cluster to be active.<br>Use `0` to not wait.|
|wait_for_events|query|[_types.WaitForEvents](#schema_types.waitforevents)|false|Wait until all currently queued events with the given priority are processed.|
|wait_for_nodes|query|[cluster.health.WaitForNodes](#schemacluster.health.waitfornodes)|false|Wait until the specified number (N) of nodes is available.<br>It also accepts `>=N`, `<=N`, `>N` and `<N`.<br>Alternatively, use the notations `ge(N)`, `le(N)`, `gt(N)`, and `lt(N)`.|
|wait_for_no_initializing_shards|query|boolean|false|Wait (until the timeout expires) for the cluster to have no shard initializations.<br>If false, the request does not wait for initializing shards.|
|wait_for_no_relocating_shards|query|boolean|false|Wait (until the timeout expires) for the cluster to have no shard relocations.<br>If false, the request not wait for relocating shards.|
|wait_for_status|query|[_types.HealthStatus](#schema_types.healthstatus)|false|Wait (until the timeout expires) for the cluster to reach a specific health status (or a better status).<br>A green status is better than yellow and yellow is better than red.<br>By default, the request does not wait for a particular status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|wait_for_events|immediate|
|wait_for_events|urgent|
|wait_for_events|high|
|wait_for_events|normal|
|wait_for_events|low|
|wait_for_events|languid|
|wait_for_status|green|
|wait_for_status|GREEN|
|wait_for_status|yellow|
|wait_for_status|YELLOW|
|wait_for_status|red|
|wait_for_status|RED|
|wait_for_status|unknown|
|wait_for_status|unavailable|

## Get the pending cluster tasks

<a id="opIdcluster-pending-tasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/pending_tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/pending_tasks`

Get information about cluster-level changes (such as create index, update mapping, allocate or fail shard) that have not yet taken effect.

NOTE: This API returns a list of any pending updates to the cluster state.
These are distinct from the tasks reported by the task management API which include periodic tasks and tasks initiated by the user, such as node stats, search queries, or create index requests.
However, if a user-initiated task such as a create index command causes a cluster state update, the activity of this task might be reported by both task api and pending cluster tasks API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-the-pending-cluster-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>If `false`, information is retrieved from the master node.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tasks": [
    {
      "executing": true,
      "insert_order": 0,
      "priority": "string",
      "source": "string",
      "time_in_queue": {},
      "time_in_queue_millis": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

|200|OK||Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## Get remote cluster information

<a id="opIdcluster-remote-info"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_remote/info \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_remote/info`

Get information about configured remote clusters.
The API returns connection and endpoint information keyed by the configured remote cluster alias.

> info
> This API returns information that reflects current state on the local cluster.
> The `connected` field does not necessarily reflect whether a remote cluster is down or unavailable, only whether there is currently an open connection to it.
> Elasticsearch does not spontaneously try to reconnect to a disconnected remote cluster.
> To trigger a reconnection, attempt a cross-cluster search, ES|QL cross-cluster search, or try the [resolve cluster endpoint](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elasticsearch/operation/operation-indices-resolve-cluster).

## Required authorization

## Reroute the cluster

<a id="opIdcluster-reroute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/reroute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"commands\": [\n    {\n      \"move\": {\n        \"index\": \"test\", \"shard\": 0,\n        \"from_node\": \"node1\", \"to_node\": \"node2\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"allocate_replica\": {\n        \"index\": \"test\", \"shard\": 1,\n        \"node\": \"node3\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_cluster/reroute`

Manually change the allocation of individual shards in the cluster.
For example, a shard can be moved from one node to another explicitly, an allocation can be canceled, and an unassigned shard can be explicitly allocated to a specific node.

It is important to note that after processing any reroute commands Elasticsearch will perform rebalancing as normal (respecting the values of settings such as `cluster.routing.rebalance.enable`) in order to remain in a balanced state.
For example, if the requested allocation includes moving a shard from node1 to node2 then this may cause a shard to be moved from node2 back to node1 to even things out.

The cluster can be set to disable allocations using the `cluster.routing.allocation.enable` setting.
If allocations are disabled then the only allocations that will be performed are explicit ones given using the reroute command, and consequent allocations due to rebalancing.

The cluster will attempt to allocate a shard a maximum of `index.allocation.max_retries` times in a row (defaults to `5`), before giving up and leaving the shard unallocated.
This scenario can be caused by structural problems such as having an analyzer which refers to a stopwords file which doesn’t exist on all nodes.

Once the problem has been corrected, allocation can be manually retried by calling the reroute API with the `?retry_failed` URI query parameter, which will attempt a single retry round for these shards.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"commands\": [\n    {\n      \"move\": {\n        \"index\": \"test\", \"shard\": 0,\n        \"from_node\": \"node1\", \"to_node\": \"node2\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"allocate_replica\": {\n        \"index\": \"test\", \"shard\": 1,\n        \"node\": \"node3\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="reroute-the-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dry_run|query|boolean|false|If true, then the request simulates the operation.<br>It will calculate the result of applying the commands to the current cluster state and return the resulting cluster state after the commands (and rebalancing) have been applied; it will not actually perform the requested changes.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If true, then the response contains an explanation of why the commands can or cannot run.|
|metric|query|string \| [string]|false|**Deprecated.** Limits the information returned to the specified metrics.|
|retry_failed|query|boolean|false|If true, then retries allocation of shards that are blocked due to too many subsequent allocation failures.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» commands|body|[[cluster.reroute.Command](#schemacluster.reroute.command)]|false|Defines the commands to perform.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "explanations": [
    {
      "command": "string",
      "decisions": [
        {
          "decider": "string",
          "decision": "string",
          "explanation": "string"
        }
      ],
      "parameters": {
        "allow_primary": true,
        "index": {},
        "node": {},
        "shard": 0,
        "from_node": {},
        "to_node": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "state": {}
}
```

<h3 id="reroute-the-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="reroute-the-cluster-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|
|explanations|[[cluster.reroute.RerouteExplanation](#schemacluster.reroute.rerouteexplanation)]|false|none|none|
|state|object|false|none|There aren't any guarantees on the output/structure of the raw cluster state.<br>Here you will find the internal representation of the cluster, which can<br>differ from the external representation.|

## Get the cluster state

<a id="opIdcluster-state"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/state \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/state`

Get comprehensive information about the state of the cluster.

The cluster state is an internal data structure which keeps track of a variety of information needed by every node, including the identity and attributes of the other nodes in the cluster; cluster-wide settings; index metadata, including the mapping and settings for each index; the location and status of every shard copy in the cluster.

The elected master node ensures that every node in the cluster has a copy of the same cluster state.
This API lets you retrieve a representation of this internal state for debugging or diagnostic purposes.
You may need to consult the Elasticsearch source code to determine the precise meaning of the response.

By default the API will route requests to the elected master node since this node is the authoritative source of cluster states.
You can also retrieve the cluster state held on the node handling the API request by adding the `?local=true` query parameter.

Elasticsearch may need to expend significant effort to compute a response to this API in larger clusters, and the response may comprise a very large quantity of data.
If you use this API repeatedly, your cluster may become unstable.

WARNING: The response is a representation of an internal data structure.
Its format is not subject to the same compatibility guarantees as other more stable APIs and may change from version to version.
Do not query this API using external monitoring tools.
Instead, obtain the information you require using other more stable cluster APIs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-the-cluster-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Return settings in flat format|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Return local information, do not retrieve the state from master node|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Timeout for waiting for new cluster state in case it is blocked|
|wait_for_metadata_version|query|[_types.VersionNumber](#schema_types.versionnumber)|false|Wait for the metadata version to be equal or greater than the specified metadata version|
|wait_for_timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The maximum time to wait for wait_for_metadata_version before timing out|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="get-the-cluster-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="get-cluster-statistics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[cluster.stats.StatsResponseBase](#schemacluster.stats.statsresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get cluster statistics

<a id="opIdcluster-stats-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cluster/stats/nodes/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_cluster/stats/nodes/{node_id}`

Get basic index metrics (shard numbers, store size, memory usage) and information about the current nodes that form the cluster (number, roles, os, jvm versions, memory usage, cpu and installed plugins).

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-cluster-statistics-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node filters used to limit returned information. Defaults to all nodes in the cluster.|
|include_remotes|query|boolean|false|Include remote cluster data into the response|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Period to wait for each node to respond.<br>If a node does not respond before its timeout expires, the response does not include its stats.<br>However, timed out nodes are included in the response’s `_nodes.failed` property. Defaults to no timeout.|

```bash
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /`

## Clear the archived repositories metering

<a id="opIdnodes-clear-repositories-metering-archive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/string/_repositories_metering/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_nodes/{node_id}/_repositories_metering/{max_archive_version}`

Clear the archived repositories metering information in the cluster.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="clear-the-archived-repositories-metering-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.|
|max_archive_version|path|number|true|Specifies the maximum `archive_version` to be cleared from the archive.|

## Get cluster repositories metering

<a id="opIdnodes-get-repositories-metering-info"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/string/_repositories_metering \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/{node_id}/_repositories_metering`

Get repositories metering information for a cluster.
This API exposes monotonically non-decreasing counters and it is expected that clients would durably store the information needed to compute aggregations over a period of time.
Additionally, the information exposed by this API is volatile, meaning that it will not be present after node restarts.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.|

## Reload the keystore on nodes in the cluster

<a id="opIdnodes-reload-secure-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/reload_secure_settings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"secure_settings_password\": \"keystore-password\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_nodes/reload_secure_settings`

Secure settings are stored in an on-disk keystore. Certain of these settings are reloadable.
That is, you can change them on disk and reload them without restarting any nodes in the cluster.
When you have updated reloadable secure settings in your keystore, you can use this API to reload those settings on each node.

When the Elasticsearch keystore is password protected and not simply obfuscated, you must provide the password for the keystore when you reload the secure settings.
Reloading the settings for the whole cluster assumes that the keystores for all nodes are protected with the same password; this method is allowed only when inter-node communications are encrypted.
Alternatively, you can reload the secure settings on each node by locally accessing the API and passing the node-specific Elasticsearch keystore password.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"secure_settings_password\": \"keystore-password\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="reload-the-keystore-on-nodes-in-the-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» secure_settings_password|body|object|false|The password for the Elasticsearch keystore.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"_nodes\": {\n    \"total\": 1,\n    \"successful\": 1,\n    \"failed\": 0\n  },\n  \"cluster_name\": \"my_cluster\",\n  \"nodes\": {\n    \"pQHNt5rXTTWNvUgOrdynKg\": {\n      \"name\": \"node-0\",\n      \"secure_setting_names\": [\n        \"keystore.seed\",\n        \"xpack.security.transport.ssl.keystore.secure_password\",\n        \"xpack.security.transport.ssl.truststore.secure_password\"\n      ],\n      \"keystore_path\": \"/etc/elasticsearch/elasticsearch.keystore\",\n      \"keystore_digest\": \"031757c262a50abe1b7e017230cdbab99c1be9fbd7116ff504b27a8787158f46\",\n      \"keystore_last_modified_time\": \"2025-12-09T22:06:00.408Z\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="reload-the-keystore-on-nodes-in-the-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.reload_secure_settings.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.reload_secure_settings.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats"></a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/stats`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

<h3 id="get-node-statistics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.stats.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.stats.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/string/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/{node_id}/stats`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

<h3 id="get-node-statistics-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.stats.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.stats.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/stats/_all \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/stats/{metric}`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric|path|[nodes.stats.NodeStatsMetrics](#schemanodes.stats.nodestatsmetrics)|true|Limits the information returned to the specific metrics.|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

<h3 id="get-node-statistics-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.stats.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.stats.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/string/stats/_all \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/{node_id}/stats/{metric}`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.|
|metric|path|[nodes.stats.NodeStatsMetrics](#schemanodes.stats.nodestatsmetrics)|true|Limits the information returned to the specific metrics.|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

<h3 id="get-node-statistics-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.stats.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.stats.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats-4"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/stats/_all/_all \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/stats/{metric}/{index_metric}`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric|path|[nodes.stats.NodeStatsMetrics](#schemanodes.stats.nodestatsmetrics)|true|Limits the information returned to the specific metrics.|
|index_metric|path|[_types.CommonStatsFlags](#schema_types.commonstatsflags)|true|Limit the information returned for indices metric to the specific index metrics. It can be used only if indices (or all) metric is specified.|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

<h3 id="get-node-statistics-4-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[nodes.stats.ResponseBase](#schemanodes.stats.responsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get node statistics

<a id="opIdnodes-stats-5"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_nodes/string/stats/_all/_all \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_nodes/{node_id}/stats/{metric}/{index_metric}`

Get statistics for nodes in a cluster.
By default, all stats are returned. You can limit the returned information by using metrics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`,`manage`


<h3 id="get-node-statistics-5-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|path|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|true|Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.|
|metric|path|[nodes.stats.NodeStatsMetrics](#schemanodes.stats.nodestatsmetrics)|true|Limits the information returned to the specific metrics.|
|index_metric|path|[_types.CommonStatsFlags](#schema_types.commonstatsflags)|true|Limit the information returned for indices metric to the specific index metrics. It can be used only if indices (or all) metric is specified.|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|groups|query|boolean|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the node, indices, or shards level.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|types|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|

## Get component templates

<a id="opIdcluster-get-component-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_component_template/{name}`

Get information about component templates.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<h3 id="get-component-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Name of component template to retrieve. Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns settings in flat format.|
|settings_filter|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter out results, for example to filter out sensitive information. Supports wildcards or full settings keys|
|include_defaults|query|boolean|false|Return all default configurations for the component template|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>If `false`, information is retrieved from the master node.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Create or update a component template

<a id="opIdcluster-put-component-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"number_of_shards\": 1\n    },\n    \"mappings\": {\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"enabled\": false\n      },\n      \"properties\": {\n        \"host_name\": {\n          \"type\": \"keyword\"\n        },\n        \"created_at\": {\n          \"type\": \"date\",\n          \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_component_template/{name}`

Component templates are building blocks for constructing index templates that specify index mappings, settings, and aliases.

An index template can be composed of multiple component templates.
To use a component template, specify it in an index template’s `composed_of` list.
Component templates are only applied to new data streams and indices as part of a matching index template.

Settings and mappings specified directly in the index template or the create index request override any settings or mappings specified in a component template.

Component templates are only used during index creation.
For data streams, this includes data stream creation and the creation of a stream’s backing indices.
Changes to component templates do not affect existing indices, including a stream’s backing indices.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in component templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body except before the opening curly bracket.

**Applying component templates**

You cannot directly apply a component template to a data stream or index.
To be applied, a component template must be included in an index template's `composed_of` list.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"number_of_shards\": 1\n    },\n    \"mappings\": {\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"enabled\": false\n      },\n      \"properties\": {\n        \"host_name\": {\n          \"type\": \"keyword\"\n        },\n        \"created_at\": {\n          \"type\": \"date\",\n          \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-component-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Name of the component template to create.<br>Elasticsearch includes the following built-in component templates: `logs-mappings`; `logs-settings`; `metrics-mappings`; `metrics-settings`;`synthetics-mapping`; `synthetics-settings`.<br>Elastic Agent uses these templates to configure backing indices for its data streams.<br>If you use Elastic Agent and want to overwrite one of these templates, set the `version` for your replacement template higher than the current version.<br>If you don’t use Elastic Agent and want to disable all built-in component and index templates, set `stack.templates.enabled` to `false` using the cluster update settings API.|
|create|query|boolean|false|If `true`, this request cannot replace or update existing component templates.|

## Create or update a component template

<a id="opIdcluster-put-component-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"number_of_shards\": 1\n    },\n    \"mappings\": {\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"enabled\": false\n      },\n      \"properties\": {\n        \"host_name\": {\n          \"type\": \"keyword\"\n        },\n        \"created_at\": {\n          \"type\": \"date\",\n          \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_component_template/{name}`

Component templates are building blocks for constructing index templates that specify index mappings, settings, and aliases.

An index template can be composed of multiple component templates.
To use a component template, specify it in an index template’s `composed_of` list.
Component templates are only applied to new data streams and indices as part of a matching index template.

Settings and mappings specified directly in the index template or the create index request override any settings or mappings specified in a component template.

Component templates are only used during index creation.
For data streams, this includes data stream creation and the creation of a stream’s backing indices.
Changes to component templates do not affect existing indices, including a stream’s backing indices.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in component templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body except before the opening curly bracket.

**Applying component templates**

You cannot directly apply a component template to a data stream or index.
To be applied, a component template must be included in an index template's `composed_of` list.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"number_of_shards\": 1\n    },\n    \"mappings\": {\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"enabled\": false\n      },\n      \"properties\": {\n        \"host_name\": {\n          \"type\": \"keyword\"\n        },\n        \"created_at\": {\n          \"type\": \"date\",\n          \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Delete component templates

<a id="opIdcluster-delete-component-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_component_template/{name}`

Component templates are building blocks for constructing index templates that specify index mappings, settings, and aliases.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<h3 id="delete-component-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list or wildcard expression of component template names used to limit the request.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-component-templates-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of component template names used to limit the request.<br>Wildcard (*) expressions are supported.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is<br>received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an<br>error.|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>Defaults to false, which means information is retrieved from the master node.|

|200|OK||None|

## Get component templates

<a id="opIdcluster-get-component-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_component_template \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_component_template`

Get information about component templates.

## Required authorization

<h3 id="get-component-templates-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|include_defaults|query|boolean|false|Return all default configurations for the component template|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.<br>If `false`, information is retrieved from the master node.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Import a dangling index

<a id="opIddangling-indices-import-dangling-index"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_dangling/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_dangling/{index_uuid}`

If Elasticsearch encounters index data that is absent from the current cluster state, those indices are considered to be dangling.
For example, this can happen if you delete more than `cluster.indices.tombstones.size` indices while an Elasticsearch node is offline.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="import-a-dangling-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_uuid|path|[_types.Uuid](#schema_types.uuid)|true|The UUID of the index to import. Use the get dangling indices API to locate the UUID.|
|accept_data_loss|query|boolean|false|This parameter must be set to true to import a dangling index.<br>Because Elasticsearch cannot know where the dangling index data came from or determine which shard copies are fresh and which are stale, it cannot guarantee that the imported data represents the latest state of the index when it was last in the cluster.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="import-a-dangling-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

If Elasticsearch encounters index data that is absent from the current cluster state, those indices are considered to be dangling.
For example, this can happen if you delete more than `cluster.indices.tombstones.size` indices while an Elasticsearch node is offline.

|accept_data_loss|query|boolean|false|This parameter must be set to true to acknowledge that it will no longer be possible to recove data from the dangling index.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.|

## Get the dangling indices

<a id="opIddangling-indices-list-dangling-indices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_dangling \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_dangling`

If Elasticsearch encounters index data that is absent from the current cluster state, those indices are considered to be dangling.
For example, this can happen if you delete more than `cluster.indices.tombstones.size` indices while an Elasticsearch node is offline.

Use this API to list dangling indices, which you can then import or delete.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`

## Add an index block

<a id="opIdindices-add-block"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_block/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /{index}/_block/{block}`

Add an index block to an index.
Index blocks limit the operations allowed on an index by blocking specific operation types.

<h3 id="add-an-index-block-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list or wildcard expression of index names used to limit the request.<br>By default, you must explicitly name the indices you are adding blocks to.<br>To allow the adding of blocks to indices with `_all`, `*`, or other wildcard expressions, change the `action.destructive_requires_name` setting to `false`.<br>You can update this setting in the `elasticsearch.yml` file or by using the cluster update settings API.|
|block|path|[indices._types.IndicesBlockOptions](#schemaindices._types.indicesblockoptions)|true|The block type to add to the index.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|The type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>It supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for the master node.<br>If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response from all relevant nodes in the cluster after updating the cluster metadata.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the cluster metadata update still applies but the response will indicate that it was not completely acknowledged.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|block|metadata|
|block|read|
|block|read_only|
|block|write|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\" : true,\n  \"shards_acknowledged\" : true,\n  \"indices\" : [ {\n    \"name\" : \"my-index-000001\",\n    \"blocked\" : true\n  } ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="add-an-index-block-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
