## Remove an index block

<a id="opIdindices-remove-block"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_block/metadata \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /{index}/_block/{block}`

Remove an index block from an index.
Index blocks limit the operations allowed on an index by blocking specific operation types.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="remove-an-index-block-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list or wildcard expression of index names used to limit the request.<br>By default, you must explicitly name the indices you are removing blocks from.<br>To allow the removal of blocks from indices with `_all`, `*`, or other wildcard expressions, change the `action.destructive_requires_name` setting to `false`.<br>You can update this setting in the `elasticsearch.yml` file or by using the cluster update settings API.|
|block|path|[indices._types.IndicesBlockOptions](#schemaindices._types.indicesblockoptions)|true|The block type to remove from the index.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|The type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>It supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for the master node.<br>If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response from all relevant nodes in the cluster after updating the cluster metadata.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the cluster metadata update still applies but the response will indicate that it was not completely acknowledged.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|block|metadata|
|block|read|
|block|read_only|
|block|write|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\" : true,\n  \"indices\" : [ {\n    \"name\" : \"my-index-000001\",\n    \"unblocked\" : true\n  } ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="remove-an-index-block-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="remove-an-index-block-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|

## Get tokens from text analysis

<a id="opIdindices-analyze"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_analyze \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"analyzer\": \"standard\",\n  \"text\": \"this is a test\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_analyze`

The analyze API performs analysis on a text string and returns the resulting tokens.

Generating excessive amount of tokens may cause a node to run out of memory.
The `index.analyze.max_token_count` setting enables you to limit the number of tokens that can be produced.
If more than this limit of tokens gets generated, an error occurs.
The `_analyze` endpoint without a specified index will always use `10000` as its limit.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `index`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/text-analysis">Learn more about text analysis</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"analyzer\": \"standard\",\n  \"text\": \"this is a test\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-tokens-from-text-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|query|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|Index used to derive the analyzer.<br>If specified, the `analyzer` or field parameter overrides this value.<br>If no index is specified or the index does not have a default analyzer, the analyze API uses the standard analyzer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» analyzer|body|string|false|The name of the analyzer that should be applied to the provided `text`.<br>This could be a built-in analyzer, or an analyzer that’s been configured in the index.|
|» attributes|body|[string]|false|Array of token attributes used to filter the output of the `explain` parameter.|
|» char_filter|body|[[_types.analysis.CharFilter](#schema_types.analysis.charfilter)]|false|Array of character filters used to preprocess characters before the tokenizer.|
|» explain|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes token attributes and additional details.|
|» field|body|object|false|Field used to derive the analyzer.<br>To use this parameter, you must specify an index.<br>If specified, the `analyzer` parameter overrides this value.|
|» filter|body|[[_types.analysis.TokenFilter](#schema_types.analysis.tokenfilter)]|false|Array of token filters used to apply after the tokenizer.|
|» normalizer|body|string|false|Normalizer to use to convert text into a single token.|
|» text|body|object|false|Text to analyze.<br>If an array of strings is provided, it is analyzed as a multi-value field.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» tokenizer|body|object|false|Tokenizer to use to convert text into tokens.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.analysis.TokenizerDefinition](#schema_types.analysis.tokenizerdefinition)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"detail\": {\n    \"custom_analyzer\": true,\n    \"charfilters\": [],\n    \"tokenizer\": {\n      \"name\": \"standard\",\n      \"tokens\": [\n        {\n          \"token\": \"detailed\",\n          \"start_offset\": 0,\n          \"end_offset\": 8,\n          \"type\": \"<ALPHANUM>\",\n          \"position\": 0\n        },\n        {\n          \"token\": \"output\",\n          \"start_offset\": 9,\n          \"end_offset\": 15,\n          \"type\": \"<ALPHANUM>\",\n          \"position\": 1\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"tokenfilters\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"snowball\",\n        \"tokens\": [\n          {\n            \"token\": \"detail\",\n            \"start_offset\": 0,\n            \"end_offset\": 8,\n            \"type\": \"<ALPHANUM>\",\n            \"position\": 0,\n            \"keyword\": false\n          },\n          {\n            \"token\": \"output\",\n            \"start_offset\": 9,\n            \"end_offset\": 15,\n            \"type\": \"<ALPHANUM>\",\n            \"position\": 1,\n            \"keyword\": false\n          }\n        ]\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-tokens-from-text-analysis-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|» tokenizer|object|false|none|none|
|» » name|string|true|none|none|
|» » tokens|[[indices.analyze.ExplainAnalyzeToken](#schemaindices.analyze.explainanalyzetoken)]|true|none|none|

## Clear the cache

<a id="opIdindices-clear-cache"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_cache/clear \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_cache/clear`

Clear the cache of one or more indices.
For data streams, the API clears the caches of the stream's backing indices.

By default, the clear cache API clears all caches.
To clear only specific caches, use the `fielddata`, `query`, or `request` parameters.
To clear the cache only of specific fields, use the `fields` parameter.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="clear-the-cache-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|query|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|false|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|

## Clone an index

<a id="opIdindices-clone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_clone/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.refresh_interval\": \"2s\"\n  },\n  \"aliases\": {\n    \"my_search_indices\": {}\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}/_clone/{target}`

Clone an existing index into a new index.
Each original primary shard is cloned into a new primary shard in the new index.

IMPORTANT: Elasticsearch does not apply index templates to the resulting index.
The API also does not copy index metadata from the original index.
Index metadata includes aliases, index lifecycle management phase definitions, and cross-cluster replication (CCR) follower information.
For example, if you clone a CCR follower index, the resulting clone will not be a follower index.

The clone API copies most index settings from the source index to the resulting index, with the exception of `index.number_of_replicas` and `index.auto_expand_replicas`.
To set the number of replicas in the resulting index, configure these settings in the clone request.

Cloning works as follows:

* First, it creates a new target index with the same definition as the source index.
* Then it hard-links segments from the source index into the target index. If the file system does not support hard-linking, all segments are copied into the new index, which is a much more time consuming process.
* Finally, it recovers the target index as though it were a closed index which had just been re-opened.

IMPORTANT: Indices can only be cloned if they meet the following requirements:

* The index must be marked as read-only and have a cluster health status of green.
* The target index must not exist.
* The source index must have the same number of primary shards as the target index.
* The node handling the clone process must have sufficient free disk space to accommodate a second copy of the existing index.

The current write index on a data stream cannot be cloned.
In order to clone the current write index, the data stream must first be rolled over so that a new write index is created and then the previous write index can be cloned.

NOTE: Mappings cannot be specified in the `_clone` request. The mappings of the source index will be used for the target index.

**Monitor the cloning process**

The cloning process can be monitored with the cat recovery API or the cluster health API can be used to wait until all primary shards have been allocated by setting the `wait_for_status` parameter to `yellow`.

The `_clone` API returns as soon as the target index has been added to the cluster state, before any shards have been allocated.
At this point, all shards are in the state unassigned.
If, for any reason, the target index can't be allocated, its primary shard will remain unassigned until it can be allocated on that node.

Once the primary shard is allocated, it moves to state initializing, and the clone process begins.
When the clone operation completes, the shard will become active.
At that point, Elasticsearch will try to allocate any replicas and may decide to relocate the primary shard to another node.

**Wait for active shards**

Because the clone operation creates a new index to clone the shards to, the wait for active shards setting on index creation applies to the clone index action as well.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.refresh_interval\": \"2s\"\n  },\n  \"aliases\": {\n    \"my_search_indices\": {}\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="clone-an-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the source index to clone.|
|target|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Name of the target index to create.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|wait_for_active_shards|query|object|false|The number of shard copies that must be active before proceeding with the operation.<br>Set to `all` or any positive integer up to the total number of shards in the index (`number_of_replicas+1`).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» aliases|body|object|false|Aliases for the resulting index.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[indices._types.Alias](#schemaindices._types.alias)|false|none|
|» settings|body|object|false|Configuration options for the target index.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "index": {},
  "shards_acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="clone-an-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="clone-an-index-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|
|index|object|true|none|none|
|shards_acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Close an index

<a id="opIdindices-close"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_close \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /{index}/_close`

A closed index is blocked for read or write operations and does not allow all operations that opened indices allow.
It is not possible to index documents or to search for documents in a closed index.
Closed indices do not have to maintain internal data structures for indexing or searching documents, which results in a smaller overhead on the cluster.

When opening or closing an index, the master node is responsible for restarting the index shards to reflect the new state of the index.
The shards will then go through the normal recovery process.
The data of opened and closed indices is automatically replicated by the cluster to ensure that enough shard copies are safely kept around at all times.

You can open and close multiple indices.
An error is thrown if the request explicitly refers to a missing index.
This behaviour can be turned off using the `ignore_unavailable=true` parameter.

By default, you must explicitly name the indices you are opening or closing.
To open or close indices with `_all`, `*`, or other wildcard expressions, change the` action.destructive_requires_name` setting to `false`. This setting can also be changed with the cluster update settings API.

Closed indices consume a significant amount of disk-space which can cause problems in managed environments.
Closing indices can be turned off with the cluster settings API by setting `cluster.indices.close.enable` to `false`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list or wildcard expression of index names used to limit the request.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Create an index

<a id="opIdindices-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 3,\n    \"number_of_replicas\": 2\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}`

You can use the create index API to add a new index to an Elasticsearch cluster.
When creating an index, you can specify the following:

* Settings for the index.
* Mappings for fields in the index.
* Index aliases

**Wait for active shards**

By default, index creation will only return a response to the client when the primary copies of each shard have been started, or the request times out.
The index creation response will indicate what happened.
For example, `acknowledged` indicates whether the index was successfully created in the cluster, `while shards_acknowledged` indicates whether the requisite number of shard copies were started for each shard in the index before timing out.
Note that it is still possible for either `acknowledged` or `shards_acknowledged` to be `false`, but for the index creation to be successful.
These values simply indicate whether the operation completed before the timeout.
If `acknowledged` is false, the request timed out before the cluster state was updated with the newly created index, but it probably will be created sometime soon.
If `shards_acknowledged` is false, then the request timed out before the requisite number of shards were started (by default just the primaries), even if the cluster state was successfully updated to reflect the newly created index (that is to say, `acknowledged` is `true`).

You can change the default of only waiting for the primary shards to start through the index setting `index.write.wait_for_active_shards`.
Note that changing this setting will also affect the `wait_for_active_shards` value on all subsequent write operations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `create_index`,`manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 3,\n    \"number_of_replicas\": 2\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the index you wish to create.<br>Index names must meet the following criteria:<br><br>* Lowercase only<br>* Cannot include `\`, `/`, `*`, `?`, `"`, `<`, `>`, `\|`, ` ` (space character), `,`, or `#`<br>* Indices prior to 7.0 could contain a colon (`:`), but that has been deprecated and will not be supported in later versions<br>* Cannot start with `-`, `_`, or `+`<br>* Cannot be `.` or `..`<br>* Cannot be longer than 255 bytes (note thtat it is bytes, so multi-byte characters will reach the limit faster)<br>* Names starting with `.` are deprecated, except for hidden indices and internal indices managed by plugins|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|wait_for_active_shards|query|object|false|The number of shard copies that must be active before proceeding with the operation.<br>Set to `all` or any positive integer up to the total number of shards in the index (`number_of_replicas+1`).|

## Delete indices

<a id="opIdindices-delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /{index}`

Deleting an index deletes its documents, shards, and metadata.
It does not delete related Kibana components, such as data views, visualizations, or dashboards.

You cannot delete the current write index of a data stream.
To delete the index, you must roll over the data stream so a new write index is created.
You can then use the delete index API to delete the previous write index.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `delete_index`


<h3 id="delete-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of indices to delete.<br>You cannot specify index aliases.<br>By default, this parameter does not support wildcards (`*`) or `_all`.<br>To use wildcards or `_all`, set the `action.destructive_requires_name` cluster setting to `false`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "_shards": {
    "failed": {},
    "successful": {},
    "total": {},
    "failures": [
      {
        "index": {},
        "node": "string",
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "reason": "string",
          "stack_trace": "string",
          "caused_by": {},
          "root_cause": [
            {}
          ],
          "suppressed": [
            {}
          ]
        },
        "shard": 0,
        "status": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "skipped": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.IndicesResponseBase](#schema_types.indicesresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Check indices

<a id="opIdindices-exists"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /{index}`

Check if one or more indices, index aliases, or data streams exist.

<h3 id="check-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns settings in flat format.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|include_defaults|query|boolean|false|If `true`, return all default settings in the response.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.|

<h3 id="check-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get aliases

<a id="opIdindices-get-alias-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_alias/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_alias/{name}`

Retrieves information for one or more data stream or index aliases.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`


<h3 id="get-aliases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams or indices used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}/_alias/{name}`

Adds a data stream or index to an alias.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/aliases">Aliases</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update an alias

<a id="opIdindices-put-alias-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_alias/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_alias/{name}`

Adds a data stream or index to an alias.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/aliases">Aliases</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Delete an alias

<a id="opIdindices-delete-alias"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_alias/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /{index}/_alias/{name}`

Removes a data stream or index from an alias.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="delete-an-alias-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams or indices used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of aliases to remove.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`). To remove all aliases, use `*` or `_all`.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "errors": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-alias-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[indices.delete_alias.IndicesAliasesResponseBody](#schemaindices.delete_alias.indicesaliasesresponsebody)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Check aliases

<a id="opIdindices-exists-alias-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_alias/string \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /{index}/_alias/{name}`

Check if one or more data stream or index aliases exist.

<h3 id="check-aliases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams or indices used to limit the request. Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of aliases to check. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

<h3 id="check-aliases-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update an alias

<a id="opIdindices-put-alias-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_aliases/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}/_aliases/{name}`

Adds a data stream or index to an alias.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/aliases">Aliases</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update an alias

<a id="opIdindices-put-alias-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_aliases/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_aliases/{name}`

Adds a data stream or index to an alias.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/aliases">Aliases</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"filter\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"filter\": [\n        {\n          \"range\": {\n            \"@timestamp\": {\n              \"gte\": \"now-1d/d\",\n              \"lt\": \"now/d\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"user.id\": \"kimchy\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update an index template

<a id="opIdindices-put-index-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_patterns\" : [\"template*\"],\n  \"priority\" : 1,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\" : {\n      \"number_of_shards\" : 2\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_index_template/{name}`

Index templates define settings, mappings, and aliases that can be applied automatically to new indices.

Elasticsearch applies templates to new indices based on an wildcard pattern that matches the index name.
Index templates are applied during data stream or index creation.
For data streams, these settings and mappings are applied when the stream's backing indices are created.
Settings and mappings specified in a create index API request override any settings or mappings specified in an index template.
Changes to index templates do not affect existing indices, including the existing backing indices of a data stream.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in index templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body, except before the opening curly bracket.

**Multiple matching templates**

If multiple index templates match the name of a new index or data stream, the template with the highest priority is used.

Multiple templates with overlapping index patterns at the same priority are not allowed and an error will be thrown when attempting to create a template matching an existing index template at identical priorities.

**Composing aliases, mappings, and settings**

When multiple component templates are specified in the `composed_of` field for an index template, they are merged in the order specified, meaning that later component templates override earlier component templates.
Any mappings, settings, or aliases from the parent index template are merged in next.
Finally, any configuration on the index request itself is merged.
Mapping definitions are merged recursively, which means that later mapping components can introduce new field mappings and update the mapping configuration.
If a field mapping is already contained in an earlier component, its definition will be completely overwritten by the later one.
This recursive merging strategy applies not only to field mappings, but also root options like `dynamic_templates` and `meta`.
If an earlier component contains a `dynamic_templates` block, then by default new `dynamic_templates` entries are appended onto the end.
If an entry already exists with the same key, then it is overwritten by the new definition.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_patterns\" : [\"template*\"],\n  \"priority\" : 1,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\" : {\n      \"number_of_shards\" : 2\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update an index template

<a id="opIdindices-put-index-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_patterns\" : [\"template*\"],\n  \"priority\" : 1,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\" : {\n      \"number_of_shards\" : 2\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_index_template/{name}`

Index templates define settings, mappings, and aliases that can be applied automatically to new indices.

Elasticsearch applies templates to new indices based on an wildcard pattern that matches the index name.
Index templates are applied during data stream or index creation.
For data streams, these settings and mappings are applied when the stream's backing indices are created.
Settings and mappings specified in a create index API request override any settings or mappings specified in an index template.
Changes to index templates do not affect existing indices, including the existing backing indices of a data stream.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in index templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body, except before the opening curly bracket.

**Multiple matching templates**

If multiple index templates match the name of a new index or data stream, the template with the highest priority is used.

Multiple templates with overlapping index patterns at the same priority are not allowed and an error will be thrown when attempting to create a template matching an existing index template at identical priorities.

**Composing aliases, mappings, and settings**

When multiple component templates are specified in the `composed_of` field for an index template, they are merged in the order specified, meaning that later component templates override earlier component templates.
Any mappings, settings, or aliases from the parent index template are merged in next.
Finally, any configuration on the index request itself is merged.
Mapping definitions are merged recursively, which means that later mapping components can introduce new field mappings and update the mapping configuration.
If a field mapping is already contained in an earlier component, its definition will be completely overwritten by the later one.
This recursive merging strategy applies not only to field mappings, but also root options like `dynamic_templates` and `meta`.
If an earlier component contains a `dynamic_templates` block, then by default new `dynamic_templates` entries are appended onto the end.
If an entry already exists with the same key, then it is overwritten by the new definition.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_patterns\" : [\"template*\"],\n  \"priority\" : 1,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\" : {\n      \"number_of_shards\" : 2\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Delete an index template

<a id="opIdindices-delete-index-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_index_template/{name}`

The provided <index-template> may contain multiple template names separated by a comma. If multiple template
names are specified then there is no wildcard support and the provided names should match completely with
existing templates.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<h3 id="delete-an-index-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of index template names used to limit the request. Wildcard (*) expressions are supported.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-index-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Check index templates

<a id="opIdindices-exists-index-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/string \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /_index_template/{name}`

Check whether index templates exist.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<h3 id="check-index-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Comma-separated list of index template names used to limit the request. Wildcard (*) expressions are supported.|
|local|query|boolean|false|If true, the request retrieves information from the local node only. Defaults to false, which means information is retrieved from the master node.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|If true, returns settings in flat format.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

<h3 id="check-index-templates-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get legacy index templates

<a id="opIdindices-get-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_template/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_template/{name}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get information about one or more index templates.

IMPORTANT: This documentation is about legacy index templates, which are deprecated and will be replaced by the composable templates introduced in Elasticsearch 7.8.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/templates">Learn more about templates</a>

<h3 id="get-legacy-index-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of index template names used to limit the request.<br>Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.<br>To return all index templates, omit this parameter or use a value of `_all` or `*`.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns settings in flat format.|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Create or update a legacy index template

<a id="opIdindices-put-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_template/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\n    \"te*\",\n    \"bar*\"\n  ],\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 1\n  },\n  \"mappings\": {\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"enabled\": false\n    },\n    \"properties\": {\n      \"host_name\": {\n        \"type\": \"keyword\"\n      },\n      \"created_at\": {\n        \"type\": \"date\",\n        \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_template/{name}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Index templates define settings, mappings, and aliases that can be applied automatically to new indices.
Elasticsearch applies templates to new indices based on an index pattern that matches the index name.

IMPORTANT: This documentation is about legacy index templates, which are deprecated and will be replaced by the composable templates introduced in Elasticsearch 7.8.

Composable templates always take precedence over legacy templates.
If no composable template matches a new index, matching legacy templates are applied according to their order.

Index templates are only applied during index creation.
Changes to index templates do not affect existing indices.
Settings and mappings specified in create index API requests override any settings or mappings specified in an index template.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in index templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body, except before the opening curly bracket.

**Indices matching multiple templates**

Multiple index templates can potentially match an index, in this case, both the settings and mappings are merged into the final configuration of the index.
The order of the merging can be controlled using the order parameter, with lower order being applied first, and higher orders overriding them.
NOTE: Multiple matching templates with the same order value will result in a non-deterministic merging order.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`,`manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/templates">Learn more about templates</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\n    \"te*\",\n    \"bar*\"\n  ],\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 1\n  },\n  \"mappings\": {\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"enabled\": false\n    },\n    \"properties\": {\n      \"host_name\": {\n        \"type\": \"keyword\"\n      },\n      \"created_at\": {\n        \"type\": \"date\",\n        \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » flush_threshold_size|body|object|false|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). This setting controls the<br>maximum total size of these operations, to prevent recoveries from taking too long. Once the<br>maximum size has been reached a flush will happen, generating a new Lucene commit point.|

Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|

## Create or update a legacy index template

<a id="opIdindices-put-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_template/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\n    \"te*\",\n    \"bar*\"\n  ],\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 1\n  },\n  \"mappings\": {\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"enabled\": false\n    },\n    \"properties\": {\n      \"host_name\": {\n        \"type\": \"keyword\"\n      },\n      \"created_at\": {\n        \"type\": \"date\",\n        \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_template/{name}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Index templates define settings, mappings, and aliases that can be applied automatically to new indices.
Elasticsearch applies templates to new indices based on an index pattern that matches the index name.

IMPORTANT: This documentation is about legacy index templates, which are deprecated and will be replaced by the composable templates introduced in Elasticsearch 7.8.

Composable templates always take precedence over legacy templates.
If no composable template matches a new index, matching legacy templates are applied according to their order.

Index templates are only applied during index creation.
Changes to index templates do not affect existing indices.
Settings and mappings specified in create index API requests override any settings or mappings specified in an index template.

You can use C-style `/* *\/` block comments in index templates.
You can include comments anywhere in the request body, except before the opening curly bracket.

**Indices matching multiple templates**

Multiple index templates can potentially match an index, in this case, both the settings and mappings are merged into the final configuration of the index.
The order of the merging can be controlled using the order parameter, with lower order being applied first, and higher orders overriding them.
NOTE: Multiple matching templates with the same order value will result in a non-deterministic merging order.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`,`manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/templates">Learn more about templates</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\n    \"te*\",\n    \"bar*\"\n  ],\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"number_of_shards\": 1\n  },\n  \"mappings\": {\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"enabled\": false\n    },\n    \"properties\": {\n      \"host_name\": {\n        \"type\": \"keyword\"\n      },\n      \"created_at\": {\n        \"type\": \"date\",\n        \"format\": \"EEE MMM dd HH:mm:ss Z yyyy\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

This operation is deprecated

|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Check existence of index templates

<a id="opIdindices-exists-template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_template/string \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /_template/{name}`

Get information about whether index templates exist.
Index templates define settings, mappings, and aliases that can be applied automatically to new indices.

IMPORTANT: This documentation is about legacy index templates, which are deprecated and will be replaced by the composable templates introduced in Elasticsearch 7.8.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/data-store/templates">Learn more about templates</a>

<h3 id="check-existence-of-index-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|A comma-separated list of index template names used to limit the request.<br>Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.|
|flat_settings|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether to use a flat format for the response.|
|local|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Indicates whether to get information from the local node only.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for the master node.<br>If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Analyze the index disk usage

<a id="opIdindices-disk-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_disk_usage \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /{index}/_disk_usage`

Analyze the disk usage of each field of an index or data stream.
This API might not support indices created in previous Elasticsearch versions.
The result of a small index can be inaccurate as some parts of an index might not be analyzed by the API.

NOTE: The total size of fields of the analyzed shards of the index in the response is usually smaller than the index `store_size` value because some small metadata files are ignored and some parts of data files might not be scanned by the API.
Since stored fields are stored together in a compressed format, the sizes of stored fields are also estimates and can be inaccurate.
The stored size of the `_id` field is likely underestimated while the `_source` field is overestimated.

For usage examples see the External documentation or refer to [Analyze the index disk usage example](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/index-disk-usage) for an example.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elasticsearch/operation/operation-indices-disk-usage">About analyzing index disk usage</a>

<h3 id="analyze-the-index-disk-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases used to limit the request.<br>It’s recommended to execute this API with a single index (or the latest backing index of a data stream) as the API consumes resources significantly.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|flush|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the API performs a flush before analysis.<br>If `false`, the response may not include uncommitted data.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|run_expensive_tasks|query|boolean|false|Analyzing field disk usage is resource-intensive.<br>To use the API, this parameter must be set to `true`.|

`GET /_alias/{name}`

Retrieves information for one or more data stream or index aliases.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`


<h3 id="get-aliases-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of aliases to retrieve.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To retrieve all aliases, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Check aliases

<a id="opIdindices-exists-alias"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_alias/string \
  -X HEAD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`HEAD /_alias/{name}`

Check if one or more data stream or index aliases exist.

<h3 id="check-aliases-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Comma-separated list of aliases to check. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

<h3 id="check-aliases-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get field usage stats

<a id="opIdindices-field-usage-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_field_usage_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_field_usage_stats`

Get field usage information for each shard and field of an index.
Field usage statistics are automatically captured when queries are running on a cluster.
A shard-level search request that accesses a given field, even if multiple times during that request, is counted as a single use.

The response body reports the per-shard usage count of the data structures that back the fields in the index.
A given request will increment each count by a maximum value of 1, even if the request accesses the same field multiple times.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="get-field-usage-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list or wildcard expression of index names used to limit the request.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"_shards\": {\n    \"total\": 1,\n    \"successful\": 1,\n    \"failed\": 0\n  },\n  \"my-index-000001\": {\n    \"shards\": [\n      {\n        \"tracking_id\": \"MpOl0QlTQ4SYYhEe6KgJoQ\",\n        \"tracking_started_at_millis\": 1625558985010,\n        \"routing\": {\n          \"state\": \"STARTED\",\n          \"primary\": true,\n          \"node\": \"gA6KeeVzQkGURFCUyV-e8Q\",\n          \"relocating_node\": null\n        },\n        \"stats\": {\n          \"all_fields\": {\n            \"any\": \"6\",\n            \"inverted_index\": {\n              \"terms\": 1,\n              \"postings\": 1,\n              \"proximity\": 1,\n              \"positions\": 0,\n              \"term_frequencies\": 1,\n              \"offsets\": 0,\n              \"payloads\": 0\n            },\n            \"stored_fields\": 2,\n            \"doc_values\": 1,\n            \"points\": 0,\n            \"norms\": 1,\n            \"term_vectors\": 0,\n            \"knn_vectors\": 0\n          },\n          \"fields\": {\n            \"_id\": {\n              \"any\": 1,\n              \"inverted_index\": {\n                \"terms\": 1,\n                \"postings\": 1,\n                \"proximity\": 1,\n                \"positions\": 0,\n                \"term_frequencies\": 1,\n                \"offsets\": 0,\n                \"payloads\": 0\n              },\n              \"stored_fields\": 1,\n              \"doc_values\": 0,\n              \"points\": 0,\n              \"norms\": 0,\n              \"term_vectors\": 0,\n              \"knn_vectors\": 0\n            },\n            \"_source\": {},\n            \"context\": {},\n            \"message.keyword\": {}\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"
```

## Flush data streams or indices

<a id="opIdindices-flush-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_flush \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_flush`

Flushing a data stream or index is the process of making sure that any data that is currently only stored in the transaction log is also permanently stored in the Lucene index.
When restarting, Elasticsearch replays any unflushed operations from the transaction log into the Lucene index to bring it back into the state that it was in before the restart.
Elasticsearch automatically triggers flushes as needed, using heuristics that trade off the size of the unflushed transaction log against the cost of performing each flush.

After each operation has been flushed it is permanently stored in the Lucene index.
This may mean that there is no need to maintain an additional copy of it in the transaction log.
The transaction log is made up of multiple files, called generations, and Elasticsearch will delete any generation files when they are no longer needed, freeing up disk space.

It is also possible to trigger a flush on one or more indices using the flush API, although it is rare for users to need to call this API directly.
If you call the flush API after indexing some documents then a successful response indicates that Elasticsearch has flushed all the documents that were indexed before the flush API was called.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `maintenance`


<h3 id="flush-data-streams-or-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request forces a flush even if there are no changes to commit to the index.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|wait_if_ongoing|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the flush operation blocks until execution when another flush operation is running.<br>If `false`, Elasticsearch returns an error if you request a flush when another flush operation is running.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_shards": {
    "failed": {},
    "successful": {},
    "total": {},
    "failures": [
      {
        "index": {},
        "node": "string",
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "reason": "string",
          "stack_trace": "string",
          "caused_by": {},
          "root_cause": [
            {}
          ],
          "suppressed": [
            {}
          ]
        },
        "shard": 0,
        "status": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "skipped": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="flush-data-streams-or-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.ShardsOperationResponseBase](#schema_types.shardsoperationresponsebase)|

## Flush data streams or indices

<a id="opIdindices-flush-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_flush \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_flush`

Flushing a data stream or index is the process of making sure that any data that is currently only stored in the transaction log is also permanently stored in the Lucene index.
When restarting, Elasticsearch replays any unflushed operations from the transaction log into the Lucene index to bring it back into the state that it was in before the restart.
Elasticsearch automatically triggers flushes as needed, using heuristics that trade off the size of the unflushed transaction log against the cost of performing each flush.

After each operation has been flushed it is permanently stored in the Lucene index.
This may mean that there is no need to maintain an additional copy of it in the transaction log.
The transaction log is made up of multiple files, called generations, and Elasticsearch will delete any generation files when they are no longer needed, freeing up disk space.

It is also possible to trigger a flush on one or more indices using the flush API, although it is rare for users to need to call this API directly.
If you call the flush API after indexing some documents then a successful response indicates that Elasticsearch has flushed all the documents that were indexed before the flush API was called.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `maintenance`


<h3 id="flush-data-streams-or-indices-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to flush.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To flush all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request forces a flush even if there are no changes to commit to the index.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|wait_if_ongoing|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the flush operation blocks until execution when another flush operation is running.<br>If `false`, Elasticsearch returns an error if you request a flush when another flush operation is running.|

## Force a merge

<a id="opIdindices-forcemerge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_forcemerge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_forcemerge`

Perform the force merge operation on the shards of one or more indices.
For data streams, the API forces a merge on the shards of the stream's backing indices.

Merging reduces the number of segments in each shard by merging some of them together and also frees up the space used by deleted documents.
Merging normally happens automatically, but sometimes it is useful to trigger a merge manually.

WARNING: We recommend force merging only a read-only index (meaning the index is no longer receiving writes).
When documents are updated or deleted, the old version is not immediately removed but instead soft-deleted and marked with a "tombstone".
These soft-deleted documents are automatically cleaned up during regular segment merges.
But force merge can cause very large (greater than 5 GB) segments to be produced, which are not eligible for regular merges.
So the number of soft-deleted documents can then grow rapidly, resulting in higher disk usage and worse search performance.
If you regularly force merge an index receiving writes, this can also make snapshots more expensive, since the new documents can't be backed up incrementally.

**Blocks during a force merge**

Calls to this API block until the merge is complete (unless request contains `wait_for_completion=false`).
If the client connection is lost before completion then the force merge process will continue in the background.
Any new requests to force merge the same indices will also block until the ongoing force merge is complete.

**Running force merge asynchronously**

If the request contains `wait_for_completion=false`, Elasticsearch performs some preflight checks, launches the request, and returns a task you can use to get the status of the task.
However, you can not cancel this task as the force merge task is not cancelable.
Elasticsearch creates a record of this task as a document at `_tasks/<task_id>`.

**Force merging multiple indices**

You can force merge multiple indices with a single request by targeting:

* One or more data streams that contain multiple backing indices
* Multiple indices
* One or more aliases
* All data streams and indices in a cluster

Each targeted shard is force-merged separately using the `force_merge` threadpool.
The `force_merge` threadpool has a fixed size of `max(1, allocatedProcessors / 8)` per node, which means multiple shards on a node may be force-merged in parallel.
If you expand the `force_merge` threadpool on a node then it will force merge its shards with more parallelism.

Force merge makes the storage for the shard being merged temporarily increase, as it may require free space up to triple its size in case `max_num_segments parameter` is set to `1`, to rewrite all segments into a new one.

**Data streams and time-based indices**

Force-merging is useful for managing a data stream's older backing indices and other time-based indices, particularly after a rollover.
In these cases, each index only receives indexing traffic for a certain period of time.
Once an index receive no more writes, its shards can be force-merged to a single segment.
This can be a good idea because single-segment shards can sometimes use simpler and more efficient data structures to perform searches.
For example:

```
POST /.ds-my-data-stream-2099.03.07-000001/_forcemerge?max_num_segments=1
```

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `maintenance`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/index-settings/merge">More about merge settings</a>

<h3 id="force-a-merge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.|
|flush|query|boolean|false|Specify whether the index should be flushed after performing the operation|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|max_num_segments|query|number|false|The number of segments the index should be merged into (default: dynamic)|
|only_expunge_deletes|query|boolean|false|Specify whether the operation should only expunge deleted documents|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|Should the request wait until the force merge is completed|

```json
    "failed": {},
    "successful": {},
    "total": {},
    "failures": [
      {
        "index": {},
        "node": "string",
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "reason": "string",
          "stack_trace": "string",
          "caused_by": {},
          "root_cause": [
            {}
          ],
          "suppressed": [
            {}
          ]
        },
        "shard": 0,
        "status": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "skipped": {}
  },
  "task": "string"
}
```

## Get aliases

<a id="opIdindices-get-alias-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_alias \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_alias`

Retrieves information for one or more data stream or index aliases.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`


<h3 id="get-aliases-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams or indices used to limit the request.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
