## Simulate an index template

<a id="opIdindices-simulate-template-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_index_template/_simulate/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\"my-index-*\"],\n  \"composed_of\": [\"ct2\"],\n  \"priority\": 10,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"index.number_of_replicas\": 1\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_index_template/_simulate/{name}`

Get the index configuration that would be applied by a particular index template.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_index_templates`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_patterns\": [\"my-index-*\"],\n  \"composed_of\": [\"ct2\"],\n  \"priority\": 10,\n  \"template\": {\n    \"settings\": {\n      \"index.number_of_replicas\": 1\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="simulate-an-index-template-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Name of the index template to simulate. To test a template configuration before you add it to the cluster, omit<br>this parameter and specify the template configuration in the request body.|
|create|query|boolean|false|If true, the template passed in the body is only used if no existing templates match the same index patterns. If false, the simulation uses the template with the highest priority. Note that the template is not permanently added or updated in either case; it is only used for the simulation.|
|cause|query|string|false|User defined reason for dry-run creating the new template for simulation purposes|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|include_defaults|query|boolean|false|If true, returns all relevant default configurations for the index template.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_auto_create|body|boolean|false|This setting overrides the value of the `action.auto_create_index` cluster setting.<br>If set to `true` in a template, then indices can be automatically created using that template even if auto-creation of indices is disabled via `actions.auto_create_index`.<br>If set to `false`, then indices or data streams matching the template must always be explicitly created, and may never be automatically created.|

## Split an index

<a id="opIdindices-split"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_split/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_shards\": 2\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /{index}/_split/{target}`

Split an index into a new index with more primary shards.
* Before you can split an index:

* The index must be read-only.
* The cluster health status must be green.

You can do make an index read-only with the following request using the add index block API:

```
PUT /my_source_index/_block/write
```

The current write index on a data stream cannot be split.
In order to split the current write index, the data stream must first be rolled over so that a new write index is created and then the previous write index can be split.

The number of times the index can be split (and the number of shards that each original shard can be split into) is determined by the `index.number_of_routing_shards` setting.
The number of routing shards specifies the hashing space that is used internally to distribute documents across shards with consistent hashing.
For instance, a 5 shard index with `number_of_routing_shards` set to 30 (5 x 2 x 3) could be split by a factor of 2 or 3.

A split operation:

* Creates a new target index with the same definition as the source index, but with a larger number of primary shards.
* Hard-links segments from the source index into the target index. If the file system doesn't support hard-linking, all segments are copied into the new index, which is a much more time consuming process.
* Hashes all documents again, after low level files are created, to delete documents that belong to a different shard.
* Recovers the target index as though it were a closed index which had just been re-opened.

IMPORTANT: Indices can only be split if they satisfy the following requirements:

* The target index must not exist.
* The source index must have fewer primary shards than the target index.
* The number of primary shards in the target index must be a multiple of the number of primary shards in the source index.
* The number of primary shards in the target index must be a divisor of the source index's `index.number_of_routing_shards`.
* The node handling the split process must have sufficient free disk space to accommodate a second copy of the existing index.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_shards\": 2\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="split-an-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the source index to split.|
|target|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the target index to create.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

## Split an index

<a id="opIdindices-split-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_split/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_shards\": 2\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_split/{target}`

Split an index into a new index with more primary shards.
* Before you can split an index:

* The index must be read-only.
* The cluster health status must be green.

You can do make an index read-only with the following request using the add index block API:

```
PUT /my_source_index/_block/write
```

The current write index on a data stream cannot be split.
In order to split the current write index, the data stream must first be rolled over so that a new write index is created and then the previous write index can be split.

The number of times the index can be split (and the number of shards that each original shard can be split into) is determined by the `index.number_of_routing_shards` setting.
The number of routing shards specifies the hashing space that is used internally to distribute documents across shards with consistent hashing.
For instance, a 5 shard index with `number_of_routing_shards` set to 30 (5 x 2 x 3) could be split by a factor of 2 or 3.

A split operation:

* Creates a new target index with the same definition as the source index, but with a larger number of primary shards.
* Hard-links segments from the source index into the target index. If the file system doesn't support hard-linking, all segments are copied into the new index, which is a much more time consuming process.
* Hashes all documents again, after low level files are created, to delete documents that belong to a different shard.
* Recovers the target index as though it were a closed index which had just been re-opened.

IMPORTANT: Indices can only be split if they satisfy the following requirements:

* The target index must not exist.
* The source index must have fewer primary shards than the target index.
* The number of primary shards in the target index must be a multiple of the number of primary shards in the source index.
* The number of primary shards in the target index must be a divisor of the source index's `index.number_of_routing_shards`.
* The node handling the split process must have sufficient free disk space to accommodate a second copy of the existing index.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"index.number_of_shards\": 2\n  }\n}"
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the source index to split.|
|target|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the target index to create.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|wait_for_active_shards|query|object|false|The number of shard copies that must be active before proceeding with the operation.<br>Set to `all` or any positive integer up to the total number of shards in the index (`number_of_replicas+1`).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» aliases|body|object|false|Aliases for the resulting index.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[indices._types.Alias](#schemaindices._types.alias)|false|none|
|» settings|body|object|false|Configuration options for the target index.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

```json
  "acknowledged": true,
  "shards_acknowledged": true,
  "index": {}
}
```

## Get index statistics

<a id="opIdindices-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_stats`

For data streams, the API retrieves statistics for the stream's backing indices.

By default, the returned statistics are index-level with `primaries` and `total` aggregations.
`primaries` are the values for only the primary shards.
`total` are the accumulated values for both primary and replica shards.

To get shard-level statistics, set the `level` parameter to `shards`.

NOTE: When moving to another node, the shard-level statistics for a shard are cleared.
Although the shard is no longer part of the node, that node retains any node-level statistics to which the shard contributed.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-index-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|completion_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument<br>determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values,<br>such as `open,hidden`.|
|fielddata_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.|
|fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.|
|forbid_closed_indices|query|boolean|false|If true, statistics are not collected from closed indices.|
|groups|query|string \| [string]|false|Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.|
|include_segment_file_sizes|query|boolean|false|If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).|
|include_unloaded_segments|query|boolean|false|If true, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.|
|level|query|object|false|Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the cluster, indices, or shards level.|

|» uuid|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update aliases and delete indices atomically

<a id="opIdindices-update-aliases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_aliases \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"actions\": [\n    {\n      \"add\": {\n        \"index\": \"logs-nginx.access-*\",\n        \"alias\": \"logs\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_aliases`

Applies one or more actions in a single request:

- Add a data stream or index to an alias.
- Remove a data stream or index from an alias.
- Delete an index in that same request, so the deletion and the alias changes are applied together.

For example, you can replace an index with an alias of the same name.

NOTE: Every `remove_index` action in the request runs first, before any `add` or `remove` actions, no matter where it sits in the `actions` array.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"actions\": [\n    {\n      \"add\": {\n        \"index\": \"logs-nginx.access-*\",\n        \"alias\": \"logs\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-aliases-and-delete-indices-atomically-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» actions|body|[[indices.update_aliases.Action](#schemaindices.update_aliases.action)]|false|Actions to perform.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true,\n  \"errors\": true,\n  \"action_results\": [\n    {\n      \"action\": {\n        \"type\": \"remove\",\n        \"indices\": [\n          \"logs-nginx.access-prod\"\n        ],\n        \"aliases\": [\n          \"logs-non-existing\"\n        ]\n      },\n      \"status\": 404,\n      \"error\": {\n        \"type\": \"aliases_not_found_exception\",\n        \"reason\": \"aliases [logs-non-existing] missing\",\n        \"resource.type\": \"aliases\",\n        \"resource.id\": \"logs-non-existing\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"action\": {\n        \"type\": \"add\",\n        \"indices\": [\n          \"logs-nginx.access-default\"\n        ],\n        \"aliases\": [\n          \"logs-non-existing\"\n        ]\n      },\n      \"status\": 200\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-aliases-and-delete-indices-atomically-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[indices.update_aliases.IndicesUpdateAliasesResponseBody](#schemaindices.update_aliases.indicesupdatealiasesresponsebody)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="validate-a-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|all_shards|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the validation is executed on all shards instead of one random shard per index.|
|analyzer|query|string|false|Analyzer to use for the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|If `true`, wildcard and prefix queries are analyzed.|
|default_operator|query|object|false|The default operator for query string query: `and` or `or`.|
|df|query|string|false|Field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response returns detailed information if an error has occurred.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|lenient|query|boolean|false|If `true`, format-based query failures (such as providing text to a numeric field) in the query string will be ignored.|
|rewrite|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns a more detailed explanation showing the actual Lucene query that will be executed.|
|q|query|string|false|Query in the Lucene query string syntax.|
|routing|query|[_types.Routing](#schema_types.routing)|false|A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the target index; use `_slice` instead.|

## Validate a query

<a id="opIdindices-validate-query-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_validate/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": {
```

|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|all_shards|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the validation is executed on all shards instead of one random shard per index.|
|analyzer|query|string|false|Analyzer to use for the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|If `true`, wildcard and prefix queries are analyzed.|
|default_operator|query|object|false|The default operator for query string query: `and` or `or`.|
|df|query|string|false|Field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string.<br>This parameter can only be used when the `q` query string parameter is specified.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.<br>If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.<br>Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.|

|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|

```bash
      "property2": {
        "boost": 1,
        "_name": "string",
        "case_insensitive": true,
        "rewrite": {},
        "value": "string",
        "wildcard": "string"
      }
    },
    "wrapper": {
      "boost": 1,
      "_name": "string",
      "query": "string"
    },
    "type": {
      "boost": 1,
      "_name": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  }
```
```json
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_connector/{connector_id}`

Removes a connector and associated sync jobs.
This is a destructive action that is not recoverable.
NOTE: This action doesn’t delete any API keys, ingest pipelines, or data indices associated with the connector.
These need to be removed manually.

<h3 id="delete-a-connector-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the connector to be deleted|
|delete_sync_jobs|query|boolean|false|A flag indicating if associated sync jobs should be also removed.|
|hard|query|boolean|false|A flag indicating if the connector should be hard deleted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n    \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-a-connector-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /_connector`

Connectors are Elasticsearch integrations that bring content from third-party data sources, which can be deployed on Elastic Cloud or hosted on your own infrastructure.
Elastic managed connectors (Native connectors) are a managed service on Elastic Cloud.
Self-managed connectors (Connector clients) are self-managed on your infrastructure.

```json

  "description": "string",
  "index_name": {},
  "is_native": true,
  "language": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "service_type": "string"
}
```

|» is_native|body|boolean|false|none|
|» language|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» service_type|body|string|false|none|

```json
  "id": {}
}
```

## Claim a connector sync job

<a id="opIdconnector-sync-job-claim"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_connector/_sync_job/string/_claim \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"worker_hostname\": \"some-machine\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_connector/_sync_job/{connector_sync_job_id}/_claim`

This action updates the job status to `in_progress` and sets the `last_seen` and `started_at` timestamps to the current time.
Additionally, it can set the `sync_cursor` property for the sync job.

This API is not intended for direct connector management by users.
It supports the implementation of services that utilize the connector protocol to communicate with Elasticsearch.

To sync data using self-managed connectors, you need to deploy the Elastic connector service on your own infrastructure.
This service runs automatically on Elastic Cloud for Elastic managed connectors.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"worker_hostname\": \"some-machine\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="claim-a-connector-sync-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_sync_job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the connector sync job.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» sync_cursor|body|object|false|The cursor object from the last incremental sync job.<br>This should reference the `sync_cursor` field in the connector state for which the job runs.|
|» worker_hostname|body|string|true|The host name of the current system that will run the job.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="claim-a-connector-sync-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set the connector sync job stats

<a id="opIdconnector-sync-job-update-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_connector/_sync_job/string/_stats \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"deleted_document_count\": 10,\n    \"indexed_document_count\": 20,\n    \"indexed_document_volume\": 1000,\n    \"total_document_count\": 2000,\n    \"last_seen\": \"2023-01-02T10:00:00Z\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_connector/_sync_job/{connector_sync_job_id}/_stats`

Stats include: `deleted_document_count`, `indexed_document_count`, `indexed_document_volume`, and `total_document_count`.
You can also update `last_seen`.
This API is mainly used by the connector service for updating sync job information.

To sync data using self-managed connectors, you need to deploy the Elastic connector service on your own infrastructure.
This service runs automatically on Elastic Cloud for Elastic managed connectors.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"deleted_document_count\": 10,\n    \"indexed_document_count\": 20,\n    \"indexed_document_volume\": 1000,\n    \"total_document_count\": 2000,\n    \"last_seen\": \"2023-01-02T10:00:00Z\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="set-the-connector-sync-job-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_sync_job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the connector sync job.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» deleted_document_count|body|number|true|The number of documents the sync job deleted.|
|» indexed_document_count|body|number|true|The number of documents the sync job indexed.|
|» indexed_document_volume|body|number|true|The total size of the data (in MiB) the sync job indexed.|
|» last_seen|body|object|false|The timestamp to use in the `last_seen` property for the connector sync job.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The connector-specific metadata.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» total_document_count|body|number|false|The total number of documents in the target index after the sync job finished.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_connector/string/_features \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`PUT /_connector/{connector_id}/_features`

Update the connector features in the connector document.
This API can be used to control the following aspects of a connector:

* document-level security
* incremental syncs
* advanced sync rules
* basic sync rules

Normally, the running connector service automatically manages these features.
However, you can use this API to override the default behavior.

To sync data using self-managed connectors, you need to deploy the Elastic connector service on your own infrastructure.
This service runs automatically on Elastic Cloud for Elastic managed connectors.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"features\": {\n    \"document_level_security\": {\n      \"enabled\": true\n    },\n    \"incremental_sync\": {\n      \"enabled\": true\n    },\n    \"sync_rules\": {\n      \"advanced\": {\n        \"enabled\": false\n      },\n      \"basic\": {\n        \"enabled\": true\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the connector to be updated.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» features|body|object|true|none|
|» » document_level_security|body|object|false|Indicates whether document-level security is enabled.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » incremental_sync|body|object|false|Indicates whether incremental syncs are enabled.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » native_connector_api_keys|body|object|false|Indicates whether managed connector API keys are enabled.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » sync_rules|body|object|false|none|
|» » » advanced|body|object|false|Indicates whether advanced sync rules are enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » » basic|body|object|false|Indicates whether basic sync rules are enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|

`PUT /_connector/{connector_id}/_filtering`

## Run a script

<a id="opIdscripts-painless-execute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_scripts/painless/_execute \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"script\": {\n    \"source\": \"params.count / params.total\",\n    \"params\": {\n      \"count\": 100.0,\n      \"total\": 1000.0\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_scripts/painless/_execute`

Runs a script and returns a result.
Use this API to build and test scripts, such as when defining a script for a runtime field.
This API requires very few dependencies and is especially useful if you don't have permissions to write documents on a cluster.

The API uses several _contexts_, which control how scripts are run, what variables are available at runtime, and what the return type is.

Each context requires a script, but additional parameters depend on the context you're using for that script.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"script\": {\n    \"source\": \"params.count / params.total\",\n    \"params\": {\n      \"count\": 100.0,\n      \"total\": 1000.0\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Run a script

<a id="opIdscripts-painless-execute-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_scripts/painless/_execute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"script\": {\n    \"source\": \"params.count / params.total\",\n    \"params\": {\n      \"count\": 100.0,\n      \"total\": 1000.0\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_scripts/painless/_execute`

Runs a script and returns a result.
Use this API to build and test scripts, such as when defining a script for a runtime field.
This API requires very few dependencies and is especially useful if you don't have permissions to write documents on a cluster.

The API uses several _contexts_, which control how scripts are run, what variables are available at runtime, and what the return type is.

Each context requires a script, but additional parameters depend on the context you're using for that script.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"script\": {\n    \"source\": \"params.count / params.total\",\n    \"params\": {\n      \"count\": 100.0,\n      \"total\": 1000.0\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Reset the project encryption key

<a id="opIdencryption-reset"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:9200/_encryption/_reset?accept_data_loss=true' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_encryption/_reset`

Destroy the current project encryption key (PEK) and generate a new one.
This is the recovery path for when the on-disk encrypted PEK becomes permanently
inaccessible, for example because the key encryption material protecting it was lost.

All data that was encrypted under the destroyed key becomes permanently unrecoverable.
Each feature that stores encrypted data decides how to handle its own data during the
reset: some features drop the encrypted values entirely, while others preserve the rest
of the affected data and only clear the values that can no longer be decrypted.

Because this operation causes permanent data loss, it requires the `accept_data_loss`
query parameter to be set to `true`.

<h3 id="reset-the-project-encryption-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accept_data_loss|query|boolean|true|Acknowledge that resetting the project encryption key permanently destroys all data<br>that was encrypted under the current key.<br>The request fails if this is not set to `true`.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="reset-the-project-encryption-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Activate a user profile

<a id="opIdsecurity-activate-user-profile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/profile/_activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"grant_type\": \"password\",\n  \"username\" : \"jacknich\",\n  \"password\" : \"l0ng-r4nd0m-p@ssw0rd\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/profile/_activate`

Create or update a user profile on behalf of another user.

NOTE: The user profile feature is designed only for use by Kibana and Elastic's Observability, Enterprise Search, and Elastic Security solutions.
Individual users and external applications should not call this API directly.
The calling application must have either an `access_token` or a combination of `username` and `password` for the user that the profile document is intended for.
Elastic reserves the right to change or remove this feature in future releases without prior notice.

This API creates or updates a profile document for end users with information that is extracted from the user's authentication object including `username`, `full_name,` `roles`, and the authentication realm.
For example, in the JWT `access_token` case, the profile user's `username` is extracted from the JWT token claim pointed to by the `claims.principal` setting of the JWT realm that authenticated the token.

When updating a profile document, the API enables the document if it was disabled.
Any updates do not change existing content for either the `labels` or `data` fields.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_user_profile`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"grant_type\": \"password\",\n  \"username\" : \"jacknich\",\n  \"password\" : \"l0ng-r4nd0m-p@ssw0rd\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="activate-a-user-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The user's Elasticsearch access token or JWT.<br>Both `access` and `id` JWT token types are supported and they depend on the underlying JWT realm configuration.<br>If you specify the `access_token` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» grant_type|body|object|true|The type of grant.|
|» password|body|string|false|The user's password.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» username|body|string|false|The username that identifies the user.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"uid\": \"u_79HkWkwmnBH5gqFKwoxggWPjEBOur1zLPXQPEl1VBW0_0\",\n  \"enabled\": true,\n  \"last_synchronized\": 1642650651037,\n  \"user\": {\n    \"username\": \"jacknich\",\n    \"roles\": [\n      \"admin\", \"other_role1\"\n    ],\n    \"realm_name\": \"native\",\n    \"full_name\": \"Jack Nicholson\",\n    \"email\": \"jacknich@example.com\"\n  },\n  \"labels\": {},\n  \"data\": {},\n  \"_doc\": {\n    \"_primary_term\": 88,\n    \"_seq_no\": 66\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="activate-a-user-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[security._types.UserProfileWithMetadata](#schemasecurity._types.userprofilewithmetadata)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Authenticate a user

<a id="opIdsecurity-authenticate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_authenticate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/_authenticate`

Authenticates a user and returns information about the authenticated user.
Include the user information in a [basic auth header](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication).
A successful call returns a JSON structure that shows user information such as their username, the roles that are assigned to the user, any assigned metadata, and information about the realms that authenticated and authorized the user.
If the user cannot be authenticated, this API returns a 401 status code.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"username\": \"rdeniro\",\n  \"roles\": [\n    \"admin\"\n  ],\n  \"full_name\": null,\n  \"email\":  null,\n  \"metadata\": { },\n  \"enabled\": true,\n  \"authentication_realm\": {\n    \"name\" : \"file\",\n    \"type\" : \"file\"\n  },\n  \"lookup_realm\": {\n    \"name\" : \"file\",\n    \"type\" : \"file\"\n  },\n  \"authentication_type\": \"realm\"\n}"
```

## Get roles

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/role \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/role`

Get roles in the native realm.
The role management APIs are generally the preferred way to manage roles, rather than using file-based role management.
The get roles API cannot retrieve roles that are defined in roles files.

## Bulk update API keys

<a id="opIdsecurity-bulk-update-api-keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key/_bulk_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"ids\": [\n    \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\",\n    \"H3_AhoIBA9hmeQJdg7ij\"\n  ],\n  \"role_descriptors\": {\n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\n            \"*\"\n          ],\n          \"privileges\": [\n            \"write\"\n          ]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 2,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\n        \"production\"\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"expiration\": \"30d\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/api_key/_bulk_update`

Update the attributes for multiple API keys.

IMPORTANT: It is not possible to use an API key as the authentication credential for this API. To update API keys, the owner user's credentials are required.

This API is similar to the update API key API but enables you to apply the same update to multiple API keys in one API call. This operation can greatly improve performance over making individual updates.

It is not possible to update expired or invalidated API keys.

This API supports updates to API key access scope, metadata and expiration.
The access scope of each API key is derived from the `role_descriptors` you specify in the request and a snapshot of the owner user's permissions at the time of the request.
The snapshot of the owner's permissions is updated automatically on every call.

IMPORTANT: If you don't specify `role_descriptors` in the request, a call to this API might still change an API key's access scope. This change can occur if the owner user's permissions have changed since the API key was created or last modified.

A successful request returns a JSON structure that contains the IDs of all updated API keys, the IDs of API keys that already had the requested changes and did not require an update, and error details for any failed update.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_own_api_key`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"ids\": [\n    \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\",\n    \"H3_AhoIBA9hmeQJdg7ij\"\n  ],\n  \"role_descriptors\": {\n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\n            \"*\"\n          ],\n          \"privileges\": [\n            \"write\"\n          ]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 2,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\n        \"production\"\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"expiration\": \"30d\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="bulk-update-api-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expiration|body|object|false|Expiration time for the API keys.<br>By default, API keys never expire.<br>This property can be omitted to leave the value unchanged.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» ids|body|string \| [string]|true|The API key identifiers.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary nested metadata to associate with the API keys.<br>Within the `metadata` object, top-level keys beginning with an underscore (`_`) are reserved for system usage.<br>Any information specified with this parameter fully replaces metadata previously associated with the API key.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» role_descriptors|body|object|false|The role descriptors to assign to the API keys.<br>An API key's effective permissions are an intersection of its assigned privileges and the point-in-time snapshot of permissions of the owner user.<br>You can assign new privileges by specifying them in this parameter.<br>To remove assigned privileges, supply the `role_descriptors` parameter as an empty object `{}`.<br>If an API key has no assigned privileges, it inherits the owner user's full permissions.<br>The snapshot of the owner's permissions is always updated, whether you supply the `role_descriptors` parameter.<br>The structure of a role descriptor is the same as the request for the create API keys API.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[security._types.RoleDescriptor](#schemasecurity._types.roledescriptor)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"updated\": [\n    \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\",\n    \"H3_AhoIBA9hmeQJdg7ij\"\n  ],\n  \"noops\": []\n}"
```

<h3 id="bulk-update-api-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="bulk-update-api-keys-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|object|false|none|none|
|» count|number|true|none|The number of errors|
|» details|object|true|none|Details about the errors, keyed by role name|
|» » **additionalProperties**|[_types.ErrorCause](#schema_types.errorcause)|false|none|Cause and details about a request failure. This class defines the properties common to all error types.<br>Additional details are also provided, that depend on the error type.|
|noops|[string]|true|none|none|
|updated|[string]|true|none|none|

This operation does not require authentication

```bash
  -X POST \
```

`POST /_security/realm/{realms}/_clear_cache`

Evict users from the user cache.

## Clear service account token caches

<a id="opIdsecurity-clear-cached-service-tokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string/credential/token/string/_clear_cache \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}/credential/token/{name}/_clear_cache`

Evict a subset of all entries from the service account token caches.
Two separate caches exist for service account tokens: one cache for tokens backed by the `service_tokens` file, and another for tokens backed by the `.security` index.
This API clears matching entries from both caches.

The cache for service account tokens backed by the `.security` index is cleared automatically on state changes of the security index.
The cache for tokens backed by the `service_tokens` file is cleared automatically on file changes.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="clear-service-account-token-caches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The namespace, which is a top-level grouping of service accounts.|
|service|path|[_types.Service](#schema_types.service)|true|The name of the service, which must be unique within its namespace.|
|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|A comma-separated list of token names to evict from the service account token caches.<br>Use a wildcard (`*`) to evict all tokens that belong to a service account.<br>It does not support other wildcard patterns.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_nodes": {
    "failures": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "reason": "string",
        "stack_trace": "string",
        "caused_by": {},
        "root_cause": [
          {}
        ],
        "suppressed": [
          {}
        ]
      }
    ],
    "total": 0,
    "successful": 0,
    "failed": 0
  },
  "cluster_name": {},
  "nodes": {
    "property1": {
      "name": {}
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": {}
    }
  }
```

`PUT /_security/api_key/clone`

Create a copy of an existing API key with a new ID.
The cloned key inherits the role descriptors of the source key.
This is intended for applications (such as Kibana) that need to
create API keys on behalf of a user using an existing API key credential,
since derived API keys (API keys created by API keys) are not otherwise supported.

```json
  "name": {},
  "expiration": {},
  "metadata": {
    "property1": {},
```

|» api_key|body|string|true|The credentials of the API key to clone.<br>This is the secret value returned when the key was originally created.|
|» name|body|object|false|A name for the cloned API key.<br>If not provided, the name of the source key is used.|

|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

## Get API key information

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/api_key`

Retrieves information for one or more API keys.
NOTE: If you have only the `manage_own_api_key` privilege, this API returns only the API keys that you own.
If you have `read_security`, `manage_api_key` or greater privileges (including `manage_security`), this API returns all API keys regardless of ownership.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_own_api_key`,`read_security`


<h3 id="get-api-key-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|false|An API key id.<br>This parameter cannot be used with any of `name`, `realm_name` or `username`.|
|name|query|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|false|An API key name.<br>This parameter cannot be used with any of `id`, `realm_name` or `username`.<br>It supports prefix search with wildcard.|
|owner|query|boolean|false|A boolean flag that can be used to query API keys owned by the currently authenticated user.<br>The `realm_name` or `username` parameters cannot be specified when this parameter is set to `true` as they are assumed to be the currently authenticated ones.|
|realm_name|query|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|false|The name of an authentication realm.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `id` or `name` or when `owner` flag is set to `true`.|
|username|query|[_types.Username](#schema_types.username)|false|The username of a user.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `id` or `name` or when `owner` flag is set to `true`.|
|with_limited_by|query|boolean|false|Return the snapshot of the owner user's role descriptors<br>associated with the API key. An API key's actual<br>permission is the intersection of its assigned role<br>descriptors and the owner user's role descriptors.|
|active_only|query|boolean|false|A boolean flag that can be used to query API keys that are currently active. An API key is considered active if it is neither invalidated, nor expired at query time. You can specify this together with other parameters such as `owner` or `name`. If `active_only` is false, the response will include both active and inactive (expired or invalidated) keys.|
|with_profile_uid|query|boolean|false|Determines whether to also retrieve the profile uid, for the API key owner principal, if it exists.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"api_keys\": [ \n    {\n      \"id\": \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\", \n      \"name\": \"my-api-key\", \n      \"creation\": 1548550550158, \n      \"expiration\": 1548551550158, \n      \"invalidated\": false, \n      \"username\": \"myuser\", \n      \"realm\": \"native1\", \n      \"realm_type\": \"native\",\n      \"metadata\": { \n        \"application\": \"myapp\"\n      },\n      \"role_descriptors\": { }, \n      \"limited_by\": [  \n        {\n          \"role-power-user\": {\n            \"cluster\": [\n              \"monitor\"\n            ],\n            \"indices\": [\n              {\n                \"names\": [\n                  \"*\"\n                ],\n                \"privileges\": [\n                  \"read\"\n                ],\n                \"allow_restricted_indices\": false\n              }\n            ],\n            \"applications\": [ ],\n            \"run_as\": [ ],\n            \"metadata\": { },\n            \"transient_metadata\": {\n              \"enabled\": true\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Create an API key

<a id="opIdsecurity-create-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"name\": \"my-api-key\",\n  \"expiration\": \"1d\",   \n  \"role_descriptors\": { \n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"index-a*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"read\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"role-b\": {\n      \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"index-b*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"all\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"application\": \"my-application\",\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 1,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/api_key`

Create an API key for access without requiring basic authentication.

IMPORTANT: If the credential that is used to authenticate this request is an API key, the derived API key cannot have any privileges.
If you specify privileges, the API returns an error.

A successful request returns a JSON structure that contains the API key, its unique id, and its name.
If applicable, it also returns expiration information for the API key in milliseconds.

NOTE: By default, API keys never expire. You can specify expiration information when you create the API keys.

The API keys are created by the Elasticsearch API key service, which is automatically enabled.
To configure or turn off the API key service, refer to API key service setting documentation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_own_api_key`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/configuration-reference/security-settings#api-key-service-settings">About API key service settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"name\": \"my-api-key\",\n  \"expiration\": \"1d\",   \n  \"role_descriptors\": { \n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"index-a*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"read\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"role-b\": {\n      \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"index-b*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"all\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"application\": \"my-application\",\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 1,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|refresh|query|[_types.Refresh](#schema_types.refresh)|false|If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expiration|body|object|false|The expiration time for the API key.<br>By default, API keys never expire.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|object|false|A name for the API key.|
|» role_descriptors|body|object|false|An array of role descriptors for this API key.<br>When it is not specified or it is an empty array, the API key will have a point in time snapshot of permissions of the authenticated user.<br>If you supply role descriptors, the resultant permissions are an intersection of API keys permissions and the authenticated user's permissions thereby limiting the access scope for API keys.<br>The structure of role descriptor is the same as the request for the create role API.<br>For more details, refer to the create or update roles API.<br><br>NOTE: Due to the way in which this permission intersection is calculated, it is not possible to create an API key that is a child of another API key, unless the derived key is created without any privileges.<br>In this case, you must explicitly specify a role descriptor with no privileges.<br>The derived API key can be used for authentication; it will not have authority to call Elasticsearch APIs.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[security._types.RoleDescriptor](#schemasecurity._types.roledescriptor)|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the API key. It supports nested data structure. Within the metadata object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|refresh|true|
|refresh|false|
|refresh|wait_for|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"id\": \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\",        \n  \"name\": \"my-api-key\",\n  \"expiration\": 1544068612110,         \n  \"api_key\": \"ui2lp2axTNmsyakw9tvNnw\", \n  \"encoded\": \"VnVhQ2ZHY0JDZGJrUW0tZTVhT3g6dWkybHAyYXhUTm1zeWFrdzl0dk5udw==\"  \n}"
```

## Invalidate API keys

<a id="opIdsecurity-invalidate-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"ids\" : [ \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\" ]\n}"'
```

`DELETE /_security/api_key`

This API invalidates API keys created by the create API key or grant API key APIs.
Invalidated API keys fail authentication, but they can still be viewed using the get API key information and query API key information APIs, for at least the configured retention period, until they are automatically deleted.

To use this API, you must have at least the `manage_security`, `manage_api_key`, or `manage_own_api_key` cluster privileges.
The `manage_security` privilege allows deleting any API key, including both REST and cross cluster API keys.
The `manage_api_key` privilege allows deleting any REST API key, but not cross cluster API keys.
The `manage_own_api_key` only allows deleting REST API keys that are owned by the user.
In addition, with the `manage_own_api_key` privilege, an invalidation request must be issued in one of the three formats:

- Set the parameter `owner=true`.
- Or, set both `username` and `realm_name` to match the user's identity.
- Or, if the request is issued by an API key, that is to say an API key invalidates itself, specify its ID in the `ids` field.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_api_key`,`manage_own_api_key`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"ids\" : [ \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\" ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="invalidate-api-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|object|false|none|
|» ids|body|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|A list of API key ids.<br>This parameter cannot be used with any of `name`, `realm_name`, or `username`.|
|» name|body|object|false|An API key name.<br>This parameter cannot be used with any of `ids`, `realm_name` or `username`.|
|» owner|body|boolean|false|Query API keys owned by the currently authenticated user.<br>The `realm_name` or `username` parameters cannot be specified when this parameter is set to `true` as they are assumed to be the currently authenticated ones.<br><br>NOTE: At least one of `ids`, `name`, `username`, and `realm_name` must be specified if `owner` is `false`.|
|» realm_name|body|string|false|The name of an authentication realm.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `ids` or `name`, or when `owner` flag is set to `true`.|
|» username|body|object|false|The username of a user.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `ids` or `name` or when `owner` flag is set to `true`.|

## Create a cross-cluster API key

<a id="opIdsecurity-create-cross-cluster-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/cross_cluster/api_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"name\": \"my-cross-cluster-api-key\",\n  \"expiration\": \"1d\",   \n  \"access\": {\n    \"search\": [  \n      {\n        \"names\": [\"logs*\"]\n      }\n    ],\n    \"replication\": [  \n      {\n        \"names\": [\"archive*\"]\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"description\": \"phase one\",\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 1,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/cross_cluster/api_key`

Create an API key of the `cross_cluster` type for the API key based remote cluster access.
A `cross_cluster` API key cannot be used to authenticate through the REST interface.

IMPORTANT: To authenticate this request you must use a credential that is not an API key. Even if you use an API key that has the required privilege, the API returns an error.

Cross-cluster API keys are created by the Elasticsearch API key service, which is automatically enabled.

NOTE: Unlike REST API keys, a cross-cluster API key does not capture permissions of the authenticated user. The API key’s effective permission is exactly as specified with the `access` property.

A successful request returns a JSON structure that contains the API key, its unique ID, and its name. If applicable, it also returns expiration information for the API key in milliseconds.

By default, API keys never expire. You can specify expiration information when you create the API keys.

Cross-cluster API keys can only be updated with the update cross-cluster API key API.
Attempting to update them with the update REST API key API or the bulk update REST API keys API will result in an error.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/remote-clusters/remote-clusters-api-key">About adding remote clusters</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"name\": \"my-cross-cluster-api-key\",\n  \"expiration\": \"1d\",   \n  \"access\": {\n    \"search\": [  \n      {\n        \"names\": [\"logs*\"]\n      }\n    ],\n    \"replication\": [  \n      {\n        \"names\": [\"archive*\"]\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"description\": \"phase one\",\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 1,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-cross-cluster-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» access|body|object|true|The access to be granted to this API key.<br>The access is composed of permissions for cross-cluster search and cross-cluster replication.<br>At least one of them must be specified.<br><br>NOTE: No explicit privileges should be specified for either search or replication access.<br>The creation process automatically converts the access specification to a role descriptor which has relevant privileges assigned accordingly.|
|» » replication|body|[[security._types.ReplicationAccess](#schemasecurity._types.replicationaccess)]|false|A list of indices permission entries for cross-cluster replication.|
|» » search|body|[[security._types.SearchAccess](#schemasecurity._types.searchaccess)]|false|A list of indices permission entries for cross-cluster search.|
|» expiration|body|object|false|Expiration time for the API key.<br>By default, API keys never expire.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the API key.<br>It supports nested data structure.<br>Within the metadata object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|object|true|Specifies the name for this API key.|
|» certificate_identity|body|string|false|The certificate identity to associate with this API key.<br>This field is used to restrict the API key to connections authenticated by a specific TLS certificate.<br>The value should match the certificate's distinguished name (DN) pattern.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"created\": true,\n  \"token\": {\n    \"name\": \"Jk5J1HgBuyBK5TpDrdo4\",\n    \"value\": \"AAEAAWVsYXN0aWM...vZmxlZXQtc2VydmVyL3Rva2VuMTo3TFdaSDZ\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-cross-cluster-api-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-cross-cluster-api-key-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|Generated API key.|
|expiration|object|false|none|Expiration in milliseconds for the API key.|
|id|object|true|none|Unique ID for this API key.|
|name|object|true|none|Specifies the name for this API key.|
|encoded|string|true|none|API key credentials which is the base64-encoding of<br>the UTF-8 representation of `id` and `api_key` joined<br>by a colon (`:`).|

## Create a service account token

<a id="opIdsecurity-create-service-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string/credential/token/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}/credential/token/{name}`

Create a service accounts token for access without requiring basic authentication.
This route serves both kinds of service account, but the privileges differ: `manage_service_account` authorizes tokens of built-in accounts in the `elastic` namespace only, and tokens of a user-managed account require `manage_security`.

NOTE: Service account tokens never expire.
You must actively delete them if they are no longer needed.

IMPORTANT: On Serverless, non-operator users can create tokens for only `elastic/fleet-server` and `elastic/fleet-server-remote`.
Creating tokens for any other service account requires operator privileges.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_service_account`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="create-a-service-account-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The name of the namespace, which is a top-level grouping of service accounts.|
|service|path|[_types.Service](#schema_types.service)|true|The name of the service.|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The name for the service account token.<br>If omitted, a random name will be generated.<br><br>Token names must be at least one and no more than 256 characters.<br>They can contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), dashes (`-`), and underscores (`_`), but cannot begin with an underscore.<br><br>NOTE: Token names must be unique in the context of the associated service account.<br>They must also be globally unique with their fully qualified names, which are comprised of the service account principal and token name, such as `<namespace>/<service>/<token-name>`.|
|refresh|query|[_types.Refresh](#schema_types.refresh)|false|If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|refresh|true|
|refresh|false|
|refresh|wait_for|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"created\": true,\n  \"token\": {\n    \"name\": \"token1\",\n    \"value\": \"AAEAAWVsYXN0aWM...vZmxlZXQtc2VydmVyL3Rva2VuMTo3TFdaSDZ\" \n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-service-account-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-service-account-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|boolean|true|none|none|
|token|object|true|none|none|
|» name|object|true|none|none|
|» value|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Delegate PKI authentication

<a id="opIdsecurity-delegate-pki"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/delegate_pki \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n\"x509_certificate_chain\": [\"\"]\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/delegate_pki`

This API implements the exchange of an X509Certificate chain for an Elasticsearch access token.
The certificate chain is validated, according to RFC 5280, by sequentially considering the trust configuration of every installed PKI realm that has `delegation.enabled` set to `true`.
A successfully trusted client certificate is also subject to the validation of the subject distinguished name according to thw `username_pattern` of the respective realm.

This API is called by smart and trusted proxies, such as Kibana, which terminate the user's TLS session but still want to authenticate the user by using a PKI realm—-​as if the user connected directly to Elasticsearch.

IMPORTANT: The association between the subject public key in the target certificate and the corresponding private key is not validated.
This is part of the TLS authentication process and it is delegated to the proxy that calls this API.
The proxy is trusted to have performed the TLS authentication and this API translates that authentication into an Elasticsearch access token.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `all`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/pki">Learn more about pki</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n\"x509_certificate_chain\": [\"\"]\n}"
```

<h3 id="delegate-pki-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» x509_certificate_chain|body|[string]|true|The X509Certificate chain, which is represented as an ordered string array.<br>Each string in the array is a base64-encoded (Section 4 of RFC4648 - not base64url-encoded) of the certificate's DER encoding.<br><br>The first element is the target certificate that contains the subject distinguished name that is requesting access.<br>This may be followed by additional certificates; each subsequent certificate is used to certify the previous one.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"access_token\": \"dGhpcyBpcyBub3QgYSByZWFsIHRva2VuIGJ1dCBpdCBpcyBvbmx5IHRlc3QgZGF0YS4gZG8gbm90IHRyeSB0byByZWFkIHRva2VuIQ==\",\n  \"type\": \"Bearer\",\n  \"expires_in\": 1200,\n  \"authentication\": {\n    \"username\": \"Elasticsearch Test Client\",\n    \"roles\": [],\n    \"full_name\": null,\n    \"email\": null,\n    \"metadata\": {\n      \"pki_dn\": \"O=org, OU=Elasticsearch, CN=Elasticsearch Test Client\",\n      \"pki_delegated_by_user\": \"test_admin\",\n      \"pki_delegated_by_realm\": \"file\"\n    },\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"authentication_realm\": {\n      \"name\": \"pki1\",\n      \"type\": \"pki\"\n    },\n    \"lookup_realm\": {\n      \"name\": \"pki1\",\n      \"type\": \"pki\"\n    },\n    \"authentication_type\": \"realm\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="delegate-pki-authentication-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="delegate-pki-authentication-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|string|true|none|An access token associated with the subject distinguished name of the client's certificate.|
|expires_in|number|true|none|The amount of time (in seconds) before the token expires.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of token.|
|authentication|object|false|none|none|
|» username|string|true|none|none|
|» roles|[string]|true|none|none|
|» full_name|string \| string \| null|true|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» email|string \| string \| null|true|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» token|object|false|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|string|false|none|none|
|» metadata|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» enabled|boolean|true|none|none|
|» authentication_realm|object|true|none|none|
|» » name|string|true|none|none|

|» » name|string|true|none|none|
|» » type|string|true|none|none|
|» » domain|string|false|none|none|
|» authentication_type|string|true|none|none|
|» api_key|object|false|none|none|

## Create or update role mappings

<a id="opIdsecurity-put-role-mapping"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/role_mapping/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"roles\": [ \"user\"],\n  \"enabled\": true, \n  \"rules\": {\n    \"field\" : { \"username\" : \"*\" }\n  },\n  \"metadata\" : { \n    \"version\" : 1\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/role_mapping/{name}`

Role mappings define which roles are assigned to each user.
Each mapping has rules that identify users and a list of roles that are granted to those users.
The role mapping APIs are generally the preferred way to manage role mappings rather than using role mapping files. The create or update role mappings API cannot update role mappings that are defined in role mapping files.

NOTE: This API does not create roles. Rather, it maps users to existing roles.
Roles can be created by using the create or update roles API or roles files.

**Role templates**

The most common use for role mappings is to create a mapping from a known value on the user to a fixed role name.
For example, all users in the `cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com` LDAP group should be given the superuser role in Elasticsearch.
The `roles` field is used for this purpose.

For more complex needs, it is possible to use Mustache templates to dynamically determine the names of the roles that should be granted to the user.
The `role_templates` field is used for this purpose.

NOTE: To use role templates successfully, the relevant scripting feature must be enabled.
Otherwise, all attempts to create a role mapping with role templates fail.

All of the user fields that are available in the role mapping rules are also available in the role templates.
Thus it is possible to assign a user to a role that reflects their username, their groups, or the name of the realm to which they authenticated.

By default a template is evaluated to produce a single string that is the name of the role which should be assigned to the user.
If the format of the template is set to "json" then the template is expected to produce a JSON string or an array of JSON strings for the role names.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/mapping-users-groups-to-roles">About mapping users to roles</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"roles\": [ \"user\"],\n  \"enabled\": true, \n  \"rules\": {\n    \"field\" : { \"username\" : \"*\" }\n  },\n  \"metadata\" : { \n    \"version\" : 1\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-role-mappings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The distinct name that identifies the role mapping.<br>The name is used solely as an identifier to facilitate interaction via the API; it does not affect the behavior of the mapping in any way.|
|refresh|query|[_types.Refresh](#schema_types.refresh)|false|If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Mappings that have `enabled` set to `false` are ignored when role mapping is performed.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional metadata that helps define which roles are assigned to each user.<br>Within the metadata object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|A list of role names that are granted to the users that match the role mapping rules.<br>Exactly one of `roles` or `role_templates` must be specified.|
|» role_templates|body|[[security._types.RoleTemplate](#schemasecurity._types.roletemplate)]|false|A list of Mustache templates that will be evaluated to determine the roles names that should granted to the users that match the role mapping rules.<br>Exactly one of `roles` or `role_templates` must be specified.|
|» rules|body|object|false|The rules that determine which users should be matched by the mapping.<br>A rule is a logical condition that is expressed by using a JSON DSL.|
|» » any|body|[[security._types.RoleMappingRule](#schemasecurity._types.rolemappingrule)]|false|none|
|» » all|body|[[security._types.RoleMappingRule](#schemasecurity._types.rolemappingrule)]|false|none|
|» » field|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue) \| [[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue)]|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue)|false|A field value.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue)]|false|none|
|» » except|body|object|false|none|
|» run_as|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|refresh|true|
|refresh|false|
|refresh|wait_for|

> Example responses

```json
"{\n  \"role_mapping\" : {\n    \"created\" : true \n  }\n}"
```

All of the user fields that are available in the role mapping rules are also available in the role templates.
Thus it is possible to assign a user to a role that reflects their username, their groups, or the name of the realm to which they authenticated.

By default a template is evaluated to produce a single string that is the name of the role which should be assigned to the user.
If the format of the template is set to "json" then the template is expected to produce a JSON string or an array of JSON strings for the role names.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/mapping-users-groups-to-roles">About mapping users to roles</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"roles\": [ \"user\"],\n  \"enabled\": true, \n  \"rules\": {\n    \"field\" : { \"username\" : \"*\" }\n  },\n  \"metadata\" : { \n    \"version\" : 1\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-role-mappings-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|refresh|query|[_types.Refresh](#schema_types.refresh)|false|If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Mappings that have `enabled` set to `false` are ignored when role mapping is performed.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional metadata that helps define which roles are assigned to each user.<br>Within the metadata object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|A list of role names that are granted to the users that match the role mapping rules.<br>Exactly one of `roles` or `role_templates` must be specified.|
|» role_templates|body|[[security._types.RoleTemplate](#schemasecurity._types.roletemplate)]|false|A list of Mustache templates that will be evaluated to determine the roles names that should granted to the users that match the role mapping rules.<br>Exactly one of `roles` or `role_templates` must be specified.|
|» rules|body|object|false|The rules that determine which users should be matched by the mapping.<br>A rule is a logical condition that is expressed by using a JSON DSL.|
|» » any|body|[[security._types.RoleMappingRule](#schemasecurity._types.rolemappingrule)]|false|none|
|» » all|body|[[security._types.RoleMappingRule](#schemasecurity._types.rolemappingrule)]|false|none|

|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue)|false|A field value.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.FieldValue](#schema_types.fieldvalue)]|false|none|

## Create or update users

<a id="opIdsecurity-put-user"></a>
