
`PUT /_security/user/{username}`

Add and update users in the native realm.
A password is required for adding a new user but is optional when updating an existing user.
To change a user's password without updating any other fields, use the change password API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"password\" : \"l0ng-r4nd0m-p@ssw0rd\",\n  \"roles\" : [ \"admin\", \"other_role1\" ],\n  \"full_name\" : \"Jack Nicholson\",\n  \"email\" : \"jacknich@example.com\",\n  \"metadata\" : {\n    \"intelligence\" : 7\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|[_types.Username](#schema_types.username)|true|An identifier for the user.<br><br>NOTE: Usernames must be at least 1 and no more than 507 characters.<br>They can contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), spaces, punctuation, and printable symbols in the Basic Latin (ASCII) block.<br>Leading or trailing whitespace is not allowed.|
|refresh|query|object|false|Valid values are `true`, `false`, and `wait_for`.<br>These values have the same meaning as in the index API, but the default value for this API is true.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» username|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string \| string \| null|false|The email of the user.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» full_name|body|string \| string \| null|false|The full name of the user.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the user.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» password|body|object|false|The user's password.<br>Passwords must be at least 6 characters long.<br>When adding a user, one of `password` or `password_hash` is required.<br>When updating an existing user, the password is optional, so that other fields on the user (such as their roles) may be updated without modifying the user's password|
|» password_hash|body|string|false|A hash of the user's password.<br>This must be produced using the same hashing algorithm as has been configured for password storage.<br>For more details, see the explanation of the `xpack.security.authc.password_hashing.algorithm` setting in the user cache and password hash algorithm documentation.<br>Using this parameter allows the client to pre-hash the password for performance and/or confidentiality reasons.<br>The `password` parameter and the `password_hash` parameter cannot be used in the same request.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|A set of roles the user has.<br>The roles determine the user's access permissions.<br>To create a user without any roles, specify an empty list (`[]`).|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether the user is enabled.|


|---|---|---|---|---|

## Get service accounts

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-service-accounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}`

Get a list of service accounts that match the provided path parameters.
Built-in service accounts ship with Elasticsearch in the `elastic` namespace; user-managed service accounts are created with the put user-managed service account API.

NOTE: When `type` is omitted, a request without a namespace reports built-in accounts only, which preserves the response of a whole-cluster listing.
A request scoped to a namespace reports both kinds, so an account you created is found without naming its kind.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_service_account`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="get-service-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The name of the namespace.<br>Omit this parameter to retrieve information about all service accounts.<br>If you omit this parameter, you must also omit the `service` parameter.|
|service|path|[_types.Service](#schema_types.service)|true|The service name.<br>Omit this parameter to retrieve information about all service accounts that belong to the specified `namespace`.|
|type|query|[security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountType](#schemasecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccounttype) \| [[security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountType](#schemasecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccounttype)]|false|A comma-separated list of the kinds of service account to return.<br>If it is omitted, it defaults to `built_in` when no namespace is given and to `built_in,user_managed` otherwise.|
|with_profile_uid|query|boolean|false|If `true`, each user-managed service account also includes the profile UIDs of the users who created and last replaced it, under the `created_by_profile_uid` and `updated_by_profile_uid` fields.<br>A profile UID is included only for a user who has an activated user profile.|

## Create user-managed service accounts

<a id="opIdsecurity-put-user-managed-service-account"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"roles\": [\n    \"my_role\"\n  ],\n  \"enabled\": true\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}`

Create a service account in a namespace of your own, or replace one that already exists.
A replacement is not a partial update: every write applies the defaults, so an account that was disabled and is then written again without `enabled` comes back enabled.

Creating an account whose name still has leftover service tokens is rejected.
Delete those tokens first.

NOTE: The `elastic` namespace is reserved for the built-in service accounts that ship with Elasticsearch.
The `manage_service_account` privilege does not authorize this API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"roles\": [\n    \"my_role\"\n  ],\n  \"enabled\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-user-managed-service-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The namespace, which is a top-level grouping of service accounts.<br>It must start with a letter or digit and can contain only letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, up to a maximum of 128 characters.<br>It cannot be `elastic`, which is reserved for built-in service accounts.|
|service|path|[_types.Service](#schema_types.service)|true|The service name.<br>It must start with a letter or digit and can contain only letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, up to a maximum of 128 characters.|
|refresh|query|object|false|If `wait_for` (the default) then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `true` then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» roles|body|[string]|true|The names of the roles to grant to the service account, up to a maximum of 1000.<br>The roles are resolved when the account authenticates, so they do not have to exist yet.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the account can authenticate.<br>Tokens can still be created for a disabled account; they just cannot be used until the account is enabled.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-text description of the account, as sent on the last PUT of the account.<br>It has no meaning to Elasticsearch. Absent when the account has no description.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"created\": true\n}"
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|boolean|true|none|A successful call returns a JSON structure that shows whether the service account has been created or updated.<br>When an existing service account is replaced, `created` is set to `false`.|

## Delete user-managed service accounts

<a id="opIdsecurity-delete-user-managed-service-account"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}`

Delete a service account from a namespace of your own.

Deleting an account that still has service tokens is rejected unless `force` is `true`.
A forced delete leaves the tokens behind: they cannot authenticate while no account of that name exists, and recreating the account is rejected until they are deleted.

NOTE: The `elastic` namespace is reserved for the built-in service accounts that ship with Elasticsearch.
A name that no user-managed service account could have is rejected rather than reported as not found.
The `manage_service_account` privilege does not authorize this API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="delete-user-managed-service-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The namespace, which is a top-level grouping of service accounts.<br>It must start with a letter or digit and can contain only letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, up to a maximum of 128 characters.<br>It cannot be `elastic`, which is reserved for built-in service accounts.|
|service|path|[_types.Service](#schema_types.service)|true|The service name.<br>It must start with a letter or digit and can contain only letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, up to a maximum of 128 characters.|
|refresh|query|object|false|If `wait_for` (the default) then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `true` then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `false` (the default), deleting a service account that still has service tokens is rejected.<br>If `true`, the account is deleted and its tokens are left in place.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"found\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-user-managed-service-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="delete-user-managed-service-accounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|found|boolean|true|none|If the service account is successfully deleted, the request returns `{"found": true}`.<br>Otherwise, the response will have status code 404 and `found` is set to `false`.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Enroll a node

<a id="opIdsecurity-enroll-node"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/enroll/node \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/enroll/node`

Enroll a new node to allow it to join an existing cluster with security features enabled.

The response contains all the necessary information for the joining node to bootstrap discovery and security related settings so that it can successfully join the cluster.
The response contains key and certificate material that allows the caller to generate valid signed certificates for the HTTP layer of all nodes in the cluster.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"http_ca_key\" : \"MIIJlAIBAzCCCVoGCSqGSIb3DQEHAaCCCUsEgglHMIIJQzCCA98GCSqGSIb3DQ....vsDfsA3UZBAjEPfhubpQysAICCAA=\", \n  \"http_ca_cert\" : \"MIIJlAIBAzCCCVoGCSqGSIb3DQEHAaCCCUsEgglHMIIJQzCCA98GCSqGSIb3DQ....vsDfsA3UZBAjEPfhubpQysAICCAA=\", \n  \"transport_ca_cert\" : \"MIIJlAIBAzCCCVoGCSqGSIb3DQEHAaCCCUsEgglHMIIJQzCCA98GCSqG....vsDfsA3UZBAjEPfhubpQysAICCAA=\", \n  \"transport_key\" : \"MIIEJgIBAzCCA98GCSqGSIb3DQEHAaCCA9AEggPMMIIDyDCCA8QGCSqGSIb3....YuEiOXvqZ6jxuVSQ0CAwGGoA==\", \n  \"transport_cert\" : \"MIIEJgIBAzCCA98GCSqGSIb3DQEHAaCCA9AEggPMMIIDyDCCA8QGCSqGSIb3....YuEiOXvqZ6jxuVSQ0CAwGGoA==\", \n  \"nodes_addresses\" : [                          \n    \"192.168.1.2:9300\"\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="enroll-a-node-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="enroll-a-node-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|http_ca_key|string|true|none|The CA private key that can be used by the new node in order to sign its certificate for the HTTP layer, as a Base64 encoded string of the ASN.1 DER encoding of the key.|
|http_ca_cert|string|true|none|The CA certificate that can be used by the new node in order to sign its certificate for the HTTP layer, as a Base64 encoded string of the ASN.1 DER encoding of the certificate.|
|transport_ca_cert|string|true|none|The CA certificate that is used to sign the TLS certificate for the transport layer, as a Base64 encoded string of the ASN.1 DER encoding of the certificate.|
|transport_key|string|true|none|The private key that the node can use for TLS for its transport layer, as a Base64 encoded string of the ASN.1 DER encoding of the key.|
|transport_cert|string|true|none|The certificate that the node can use for TLS for its transport layer, as a Base64 encoded string of the ASN.1 DER encoding of the certificate.|
|nodes_addresses|[string]|true|none|A list of transport addresses in the form of `host:port` for the nodes that are already members of the cluster.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update application privileges

<a id="opIdsecurity-put-privileges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/privilege \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"myapp\": {\n    \"read\": {\n      \"actions\": [ \n        \"data:read/*\" , \n        \"action:login\" ],\n        \"metadata\": { \n          \"description\": \"Read access to myapp\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/privilege`

To use this API, you must have one of the following privileges:

* The `manage_security` cluster privilege (or a greater privilege such as `all`).
* The "Manage Application Privileges" global privilege for the application being referenced in the request.

Application names are formed from a prefix, with an optional suffix that conform to the following rules:

* The prefix must begin with a lowercase ASCII letter.
* The prefix must contain only ASCII letters or digits.
* The prefix must be at least 3 characters long.
* If the suffix exists, it must begin with either a dash `-` or `_`.
* The suffix cannot contain any of the following characters: `\`, `/`, `*`, `?`, `"`, `<`, `>`, `|`, `,`, `*`.
* No part of the name can contain whitespace.

Privilege names must begin with a lowercase ASCII letter and must contain only ASCII letters and digits along with the characters `_`, `-`, and `.`.

Action names can contain any number of printable ASCII characters and must contain at least one of the following characters: `/`, `*`, `:`.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/security-privileges">About Elasticsearch privileges</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"myapp\": {\n    \"read\": {\n      \"actions\": [ \n        \"data:read/*\" , \n        \"action:login\" ],\n        \"metadata\": { \n          \"description\": \"Read access to myapp\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n}"
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|refresh|query|[_types.Refresh](#schema_types.refresh)|false|If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[security.put_privileges.Actions](#schemasecurity.put_privileges.actions)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|refresh|true|
|refresh|false|
|refresh|wait_for|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"myapp\": {\n    \"read\": {\n      \"created\": true \n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Get service accounts

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-service-accounts-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/service/{namespace}`

Get a list of service accounts that match the provided path parameters.
Built-in service accounts ship with Elasticsearch in the `elastic` namespace; user-managed service accounts are created with the put user-managed service account API.

NOTE: When `type` is omitted, a request without a namespace reports built-in accounts only, which preserves the response of a whole-cluster listing.
A request scoped to a namespace reports both kinds, so an account you created is found without naming its kind.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_service_account`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="get-service-accounts-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The name of the namespace.<br>Omit this parameter to retrieve information about all service accounts.<br>If you omit this parameter, you must also omit the `service` parameter.|
|type|query|[security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountType](#schemasecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccounttype) \| [[security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountType](#schemasecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccounttype)]|false|A comma-separated list of the kinds of service account to return.<br>If it is omitted, it defaults to `built_in` when no namespace is given and to `built_in,user_managed` otherwise.|

## Get service account credentials

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-service-credentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/service/string/string/credential \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}/credential`

To use this API, you must have at least the `read_security` cluster privilege (or a greater privilege such as `manage_service_account` or `manage_security`).

The response includes service account tokens that were created with the create service account tokens API as well as file-backed tokens from all nodes of the cluster.

NOTE: For tokens backed by the `service_tokens` file, the API collects them from all nodes of the cluster.
Tokens with the same name from different nodes are assumed to be the same token and are only counted once towards the total number of service tokens.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/service-accounts">More about service accounts</a>

<h3 id="get-service-account-credentials-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|[_types.Namespace](#schema_types.namespace)|true|The name of the namespace.|
|service|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The service name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"service_account\": \"elastic/fleet-server\",\n  \"count\": 3,\n  \"tokens\": {\n    \"token1\": {},        \n    \"token42\": {}        \n  },\n  \"nodes_credentials\": { \n    \"_nodes\": {          \n      \"total\": 3,\n      \"successful\": 3,\n      \"failed\": 0\n    },\n    \"file_tokens\": {      \n      \"my-token\": {\n        \"nodes\": [ \"node0\", \"node1\" ] \n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-service-account-credentials-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-service-account-credentials-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|service_account|string|true|none|none|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|tokens|object|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|[_types.Metadata](#schema_types.metadata)|false|none|none|
|nodes_credentials|object|true|none|Service account credentials collected from all nodes of the cluster.|
|» _nodes|object|true|none|General status showing how nodes respond to the above collection request|
|» » failures|[[_types.ErrorCause](#schema_types.errorcause)]|false|none|none|
|» » total|number|true|none|Total number of nodes selected by the request.|
|» » successful|number|true|none|Number of nodes that responded successfully to the request.|
|» » failed|number|true|none|Number of nodes that rejected the request or failed to respond. If this value is not 0, a reason for the rejection or failure is included in the response.|
|» file_tokens|object|true|none|File-backed tokens collected from all nodes|
|» » **additionalProperties**|[security.get_service_credentials.NodesCredentialsFileToken](#schemasecurity.get_service_credentials.nodescredentialsfiletoken)|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get security index settings

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/settings`

Get the user-configurable settings for the security internal index (`.security` and associated indices).
Only a subset of the index settings — those that are user-configurable—will be shown.
This includes:

* `index.auto_expand_replicas`
* `index.number_of_replicas`

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


<h3 id="get-security-index-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

|» » » retention_lease|object|false|none|The maximum period to retain a shard history retention lease before it is considered expired.<br>Shard history retention leases ensure that soft deletes are retained during merges on the Lucene<br>index. If a soft delete is merged away before it can be replicated to a follower the following<br>process will fail due to incomplete history on the leader.|

Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|

## Update security index settings

<a id="opIdsecurity-update-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"security\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }\n    },\n    \"security-tokens\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }      \n    },\n    \"security-profile\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }      \n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/settings`

Update the user-configurable settings for the security internal index (`.security` and associated indices). Only a subset of settings are allowed to be modified. This includes `index.auto_expand_replicas` and `index.number_of_replicas`.

NOTE: If `index.auto_expand_replicas` is set, `index.number_of_replicas` will be ignored during updates.

If a specific index is not in use on the system and settings are provided for it, the request will be rejected.
This API does not yet support configuring the settings for indices before they are in use.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"security\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }\n    },\n    \"security-tokens\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }      \n    },\n    \"security-profile\": {\n        \"index\": {\n          \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-all\"\n        }      \n    }\n}"
```

|» » » » flush_threshold_size|body|object|false|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). Although these operations are available for reads, they will need<br>to be replayed if the shard was stopped and had to be recovered. This setting controls the<br>maximum total size of these operations, to prevent recoveries from taking too long. Once the<br>maximum size has been reached a flush will happen, generating a new Lucene commit point.|

Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|

## Get security stats

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/stats`

Gather security usage statistics from all node(s) within the cluster.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"nodes\": {\n    \"CLeCBfYETO2mQ1R2Il5-SA\": {\n      \"roles\": {\n        \"dls\": {\n          \"bit_set_cache\": {\n            \"count\": 1,\n            \"memory\": \"16b\",\n            \"memory_in_bytes\": 16,\n            \"hits\": 212,\n            \"misses\": 1,\n            \"evictions\": 0,\n            \"hits_time_in_millis\": 5,\n            \"misses_time_in_millis\": 0\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Get a token

<a id="opIdsecurity-get-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/oauth2/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"grant_type\" : \"client_credentials\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/oauth2/token`

Create a bearer token for access without requiring basic authentication.
The tokens are created by the Elasticsearch Token Service, which is automatically enabled when you configure TLS on the HTTP interface.
Alternatively, you can explicitly enable the `xpack.security.authc.token.enabled` setting.
When you are running in production mode, a bootstrap check prevents you from enabling the token service unless you also enable TLS on the HTTP interface.

The get token API takes the same parameters as a typical OAuth 2.0 token API except for the use of a JSON request body.

A successful get token API call returns a JSON structure that contains the access token, the amount of time (seconds) that the token expires in, the type, and the scope if available.

The tokens returned by the get token API have a finite period of time for which they are valid and after that time period, they can no longer be used.
That time period is defined by the `xpack.security.authc.token.timeout` setting.
If you want to invalidate a token immediately, you can do so by using the invalidate token API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_token`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/set-up-basic-security-plus-https#encrypt-http-communication">More about setting up https</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"grant_type\" : \"client_credentials\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-a-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» grant_type|body|object|false|The type of grant.<br>Supported grant types are: `password`, `_kerberos`, `client_credentials`, `refresh_token`, and `_user_managed_service_account`.|
|» scope|body|string|false|The scope of the token.<br>Currently tokens are only issued for a scope of FULL regardless of the value sent with the request.|
|» password|body|object|false|The user's password.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>This parameter is not valid with any other supported grant type.|
|» kerberos_ticket|body|string|false|The base64 encoded kerberos ticket.<br>If you specify the `_kerberos` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>This parameter is not valid with any other supported grant type.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The string that was returned when you created the token, which enables you to extend its life.<br>If you specify the `refresh_token` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>This parameter is not valid with any other supported grant type.|
|» service_account_token|body|string|false|The service account token of a user-managed service account, as returned by the create service account token API.<br>If you specify the `_user_managed_service_account` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>This parameter is not valid with any other supported grant type.|
|» username|body|object|false|The username that identifies the user.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>This parameter is not valid with any other supported grant type.|

## Invalidate a token

<a id="opIdsecurity-invalidate-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/oauth2/token \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"token\" : \"dGhpcyBpcyBub3QgYSByZWFsIHRva2VuIGJ1dCBpdCBpcyBvbmx5IHRlc3QgZGF0YS4gZG8gbm90IHRyeSB0byByZWFkIHRva2VuIQ==\"\n}"'
```

`DELETE /_security/oauth2/token`

The access tokens returned by the get token API have a finite period of time for which they are valid.
After that time period, they can no longer be used.
The time period is defined by the `xpack.security.authc.token.timeout` setting.

The refresh tokens returned by the get token API are only valid for 24 hours.
They can also be used exactly once.
If you want to invalidate one or more access or refresh tokens immediately, use this invalidate token API.

NOTE: While all parameters are optional, at least one of them is required.
More specifically, either one of `token` or `refresh_token` parameters is required.
If none of these two are specified, then `realm_name` and/or `username` need to be specified.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"token\" : \"dGhpcyBpcyBub3QgYSByZWFsIHRva2VuIGJ1dCBpdCBpcyBvbmx5IHRlc3QgZGF0YS4gZG8gbm90IHRyeSB0byByZWFkIHRva2VuIQ==\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="invalidate-a-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string|false|An access token.<br>This parameter cannot be used if any of `refresh_token`, `realm_name`, or `username` are used.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|A refresh token.<br>This parameter cannot be used if any of `refresh_token`, `realm_name`, or `username` are used.|
|» realm_name|body|object|false|The name of an authentication realm.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `refresh_token` or `token`.|
|» username|body|object|false|The username of a user.<br>This parameter cannot be used with either `refresh_token` or `token`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"invalidated_tokens\":9, \n  \"previously_invalidated_tokens\":15, \n  \"error_count\":2, \n  \"error_details\":[ \n    {\n      \"type\":\"exception\",\n      \"reason\":\"Elasticsearch exception [type=exception, reason=foo]\",\n      \"caused_by\":{\n        \"type\":\"exception\",\n        \"reason\":\"Elasticsearch exception [type=illegal_argument_exception, reason=bar]\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\":\"exception\",\n      \"reason\":\"Elasticsearch exception [type=exception, reason=boo]\",\n      \"caused_by\":{\n        \"type\":\"exception\",\n        \"reason\":\"Elasticsearch exception [type=illegal_argument_exception, reason=far]\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="invalidate-a-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="invalidate-a-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error_count|number|true|none|The number of errors that were encountered when invalidating the tokens.|
|error_details|[[_types.ErrorCause](#schema_types.errorcause)]|false|none|Details about the errors.<br>This field is not present in the response when `error_count` is `0`.|
|invalidated_tokens|number|true|none|The number of the tokens that were invalidated as part of this request.|
|previously_invalidated_tokens|number|true|none|The number of tokens that were already invalidated.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Grant an API key

<a id="opIdsecurity-grant-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key/grant \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"grant_type\": \"password\",\n  \"username\" : \"test_admin\",\n  \"password\" : \"x-pack-test-password\",\n  \"api_key\" : {\n    \"name\": \"my-api-key\",\n    \"expiration\": \"1d\",\n    \"role_descriptors\": {\n      \"role-a\": {\n        \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n        \"indices\": [\n          {\n          \"names\": [\"index-a*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"read\"]\n          }\n        ]\n      },\n      \"role-b\": {\n        \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n        \"indices\": [\n          {\n          \"names\": [\"index-b*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"all\"]\n          }\n        ]\n      }\n    },\n    \"metadata\": {\n      \"application\": \"my-application\",\n      \"environment\": {\n        \"level\": 1,\n        \"trusted\": true,\n        \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/api_key/grant`

Create an API key on behalf of another user.
This API is similar to the create API keys API, however it creates the API key for a user that is different than the user that runs the API.
The caller must have authentication credentials for the user on whose behalf the API key will be created.
It is not possible to use this API to create an API key without that user's credentials.
The supported user authentication credential types are:

* username and password
* Elasticsearch access tokens
* JWTs
* service account tokens of user-managed service accounts

The user, for whom the authentication credentials is provided, can optionally "run as" (impersonate) another user.
In this case, the API key will be created on behalf of the impersonated user.
Run as is not supported with the `_user_managed_service_account` grant type.

This API is intended be used by applications that need to create and manage API keys for end users, but cannot guarantee that those users have permission to create API keys on their own behalf.
The API keys are created by the Elasticsearch API key service, which is automatically enabled.

A successful grant API key API call returns a JSON structure that contains the API key, its unique id, and its name.
If applicable, it also returns expiration information for the API key in milliseconds.

By default, API keys never expire. You can specify expiration information when you create the API keys.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `grant_api_key`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"grant_type\": \"password\",\n  \"username\" : \"test_admin\",\n  \"password\" : \"x-pack-test-password\",\n  \"api_key\" : {\n    \"name\": \"my-api-key\",\n    \"expiration\": \"1d\",\n    \"role_descriptors\": {\n      \"role-a\": {\n        \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n        \"indices\": [\n          {\n          \"names\": [\"index-a*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"read\"]\n          }\n        ]\n      },\n      \"role-b\": {\n        \"cluster\": [\"all\"],\n        \"indices\": [\n          {\n          \"names\": [\"index-b*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"all\"]\n          }\n        ]\n      }\n    },\n    \"metadata\": {\n      \"application\": \"my-application\",\n      \"environment\": {\n        \"level\": 1,\n        \"trusted\": true,\n        \"tags\": [\"dev\", \"staging\"]\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="grant-an-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|refresh|query|object|false|If 'true', Elasticsearch refreshes the affected shards to make this operation<br>visible to search.<br>If 'wait_for', it waits for a refresh to make this operation visible to search.<br>If 'false', nothing is done with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» api_key|body|object|true|The API key.|
|» » name|body|object|true|none|
|» » expiration|body|object|false|Expiration time for the API key. By default, API keys never expire.|
|» » role_descriptors|body|object \| [object]|false|The role descriptors for this API key.<br>When it is not specified or is an empty array, the API key has a point in time snapshot of permissions of the specified user or access token.<br>If you supply role descriptors, the resultant permissions are an intersection of API keys permissions and the permissions of the user or access token.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[security._types.RoleDescriptor](#schemasecurity._types.roledescriptor)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|[security._types.RoleDescriptor](#schemasecurity._types.roledescriptor)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the API key.<br>It supports nested data structure.<br>Within the `metadata` object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» grant_type|body|object|true|The type of grant. Supported grant types are: `access_token`, `password`, and `_user_managed_service_account`.|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The user's access token.<br>If you specify the `access_token` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» client_authentication|body|object|false|The client authentication for a JWT that requires it, which is what is normally sent in the `ES-Client-Authentication` request header.<br>It is valid only with the `access_token` grant type, when the access token is a JWT.|
|» » scheme|body|object|true|The client authentication scheme.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The client authentication value, which is what normally follows the scheme in the `ES-Client-Authentication` request header.|
|» service_account_token|body|string|false|The service account token of a user-managed service account, as returned by the create service account token API.<br>If you specify the `_user_managed_service_account` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» username|body|object|false|The user name that identifies the user.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» password|body|object|false|The user's password.<br>If you specify the `password` grant type, this parameter is required.<br>It is not valid with other grant types.|
|» run_as|body|object|false|The name of the user to be impersonated.<br>It is not valid with the `_user_managed_service_account` grant type.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "api_key": "string",
  "id": {},
  "name": {},
  "expiration": {},
  "encoded": "string"
}
```

## Authenticate OpenID Connect

<a id="opIdsecurity-oidc-authenticate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/oidc/authenticate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"redirect_uri\" : \"https://oidc-kibana.elastic.co:5603/api/security/oidc/callback?code=jtI3Ntt8v3_XvcLzCFGq&state=4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I\",\n  \"state\" : \"4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I\",\n  \"nonce\" : \"WaBPH0KqPVdG5HHdSxPRjfoZbXMCicm5v1OiAj0DUFM\",\n  \"realm\" : \"oidc1\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/oidc/authenticate`

Exchange an OpenID Connect authentication response message for an Elasticsearch internal access token and refresh token that can be subsequently used for authentication.

Elasticsearch exposes all the necessary OpenID Connect related functionality with the OpenID Connect APIs.
These APIs are used internally by Kibana in order to provide OpenID Connect based authentication, but can also be used by other, custom web applications or other clients.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"redirect_uri\" : \"https://oidc-kibana.elastic.co:5603/api/security/oidc/callback?code=jtI3Ntt8v3_XvcLzCFGq&state=4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I\",\n  \"state\" : \"4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I\",\n  \"nonce\" : \"WaBPH0KqPVdG5HHdSxPRjfoZbXMCicm5v1OiAj0DUFM\",\n  \"realm\" : \"oidc1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="authenticate-openid-connect-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» nonce|body|string|true|Associate a client session with an ID token and mitigate replay attacks.<br>This value needs to be the same as the one that was provided to the `/_security/oidc/prepare` API or the one that was generated by Elasticsearch and included in the response to that call.|
|» realm|body|string|false|The name of the OpenID Connect realm.<br>This property is useful in cases where multiple realms are defined.|
|» redirect_uri|body|string|true|The URL to which the OpenID Connect Provider redirected the User Agent in response to an authentication request after a successful authentication.<br>This URL must be provided as-is (URL encoded), taken from the body of the response or as the value of a location header in the response from the OpenID Connect Provider.|
|» state|body|string|true|Maintain state between the authentication request and the response.<br>This value needs to be the same as the one that was provided to the `/_security/oidc/prepare` API or the one that was generated by Elasticsearch and included in the response to that call.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Logout of OpenID Connect

<a id="opIdsecurity-oidc-logout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/oidc/logout \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"token\" : \"dGhpcyBpcyBub3QgYSByZWFsIHRva2VuIGJ1dCBpdCBpcyBvbmx5IHRlc3QgZGF0YS4gZG8gbm90IHRyeSB0byByZWFkIHRva2VuIQ==\",\n  \"refresh_token\": \"vLBPvmAB6KvwvJZr27cS\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/oidc/logout`

Invalidate an access token and a refresh token that were generated as a response to the `/_security/oidc/authenticate` API.

If the OpenID Connect authentication realm in Elasticsearch is accordingly configured, the response to this call will contain a URI pointing to the end session endpoint of the OpenID Connect Provider in order to perform single logout.

Elasticsearch exposes all the necessary OpenID Connect related functionality with the OpenID Connect APIs.
These APIs are used internally by Kibana in order to provide OpenID Connect based authentication, but can also be used by other, custom web applications or other clients.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"token\" : \"dGhpcyBpcyBub3QgYSByZWFsIHRva2VuIGJ1dCBpdCBpcyBvbmx5IHRlc3QgZGF0YS4gZG8gbm90IHRyeSB0byByZWFkIHRva2VuIQ==\",\n  \"refresh_token\": \"vLBPvmAB6KvwvJZr27cS\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="logout-of-openid-connect-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string|true|The access token to be invalidated.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The refresh token to be invalidated.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"redirect\" : \"https://op-provider.org/logout?id_token_hint=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c&post_logout_redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Foidc-kibana.elastic.co%2Floggedout&state=lGYK0EcSLjqH6pkT5EVZjC6eIW5YCGgywj2sxROO\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="logout-of-openid-connect-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="logout-of-openid-connect-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|redirect|string|true|none|A URI that points to the end session endpoint of the OpenID Connect Provider with all the parameters of the logout request as HTTP GET parameters.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Prepare OpenID connect authentication

<a id="opIdsecurity-oidc-prepare-authentication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/oidc/prepare \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"realm\" : \"oidc1\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/oidc/prepare`

Create an oAuth 2.0 authentication request as a URL string based on the configuration of the OpenID Connect authentication realm in Elasticsearch.

The response of this API is a URL pointing to the Authorization Endpoint of the configured OpenID Connect Provider, which can be used to redirect the browser of the user in order to continue the authentication process.

Elasticsearch exposes all the necessary OpenID Connect related functionality with the OpenID Connect APIs.
These APIs are used internally by Kibana in order to provide OpenID Connect based authentication, but can also be used by other, custom web applications or other clients.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"realm\" : \"oidc1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="prepare-openid-connect-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» iss|body|string|false|In the case of a third party initiated single sign on, this is the issuer identifier for the OP that the RP is to send the authentication request to.<br>It cannot be specified when *realm* is specified.<br>One of *realm* or *iss* is required.|
|» login_hint|body|string|false|In the case of a third party initiated single sign on, it is a string value that is included in the authentication request as the *login_hint* parameter.<br>This parameter is not valid when *realm* is specified.|
|» nonce|body|string|false|The value used to associate a client session with an ID token and to mitigate replay attacks.<br>If the caller of the API does not provide a value, Elasticsearch will generate one with sufficient entropy and return it in the response.|
|» realm|body|string|false|The name of the OpenID Connect realm in Elasticsearch the configuration of which should be used in order to generate the authentication request.<br>It cannot be specified when *iss* is specified.<br>One of *realm* or *iss* is required.|
|» state|body|string|false|The value used to maintain state between the authentication request and the response, typically used as a Cross-Site Request Forgery mitigation.<br>If the caller of the API does not provide a value, Elasticsearch will generate one with sufficient entropy and return it in the response.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"redirect\" : \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/c2id-login?scope=openid&response_type=id_token&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmy.fantastic.rp%2Fcb&state=4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I&nonce=WaBPH0KqPVdG5HHdSxPRjfoZbXMCicm5v1OiAj0DUFM&client_id=elasticsearch-rp\",\n  \"state\" : \"4dbrihtIAt3wBTwo6DxK-vdk-sSyDBV8Yf0AjdkdT5I\",\n  \"nonce\" : \"WaBPH0KqPVdG5HHdSxPRjfoZbXMCicm5v1OiAj0DUFM\",\n  \"realm\" : \"oidc1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="prepare-openid-connect-authentication-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="prepare-openid-connect-authentication-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nonce|string|true|none|none|
|realm|string|true|none|none|
|redirect|string|true|none|A URI that points to the authorization endpoint of the OpenID Connect Provider with all the parameters of the authentication request as HTTP GET parameters.|
|state|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Find API keys with a query

<a id="opIdsecurity-query-api-keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_query/api_key \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"ids\": {\n      \"values\": [\n        \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_security/_query/api_key`

Get a paginated list of API keys and their information.
You can optionally filter the results with a query.

To use this API, you must have at least the `manage_own_api_key` or the `read_security` cluster privileges.
If you have only the `manage_own_api_key` privilege, this API returns only the API keys that you own.
If you have the `read_security`, `manage_api_key`, or greater privileges (including `manage_security`), this API returns all API keys regardless of ownership.
Refer to the linked documentation for examples of how to find API keys:

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_own_api_key`,`read_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/query-api-keys">About query API key information</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"ids\": {\n      \"values\": [\n        \"VuaCfGcBCdbkQm-e5aOx\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Find roles with a query

<a id="opIdsecurity-query-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_query/role \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"sort\": [\"name\"]\n}"'
```

`GET /_security/_query/role`

Get roles in a paginated manner.
The role management APIs are generally the preferred way to manage roles, rather than using file-based role management.
The query roles API does not retrieve roles that are defined in roles files, nor built-in ones.
You can optionally filter the results with a query.
Also, the results can be paginated and sorted.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"sort\": [\"name\"]\n}"
```

## Find roles with a query

<a id="opIdsecurity-query-role-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_query/role \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"sort\": [\"name\"]\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/_query/role`

Get roles in a paginated manner.
The role management APIs are generally the preferred way to manage roles, rather than using file-based role management.
The query roles API does not retrieve roles that are defined in roles files, nor built-in ones.
You can optionally filter the results with a query.
Also, the results can be paginated and sorted.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"sort\": [\"name\"]\n}"
```

## Find users with a query

<a id="opIdsecurity-query-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_query/user \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"query\": {\n        \"prefix\": {\n            \"roles\": \"other\"\n        }\n    }\n}"'
```

`GET /_security/_query/user`

Get information for users in a paginated manner.
You can optionally filter the results with a query.

NOTE: As opposed to the get user API, built-in users are excluded from the result.
This API is only for native users.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"query\": {\n        \"prefix\": {\n            \"roles\": \"other\"\n        }\n    }\n}"
```

## Find users with a query

<a id="opIdsecurity-query-user-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/_query/user \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"query\": {\n        \"prefix\": {\n            \"roles\": \"other\"\n        }\n    }\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/_query/user`

Get information for users in a paginated manner.
You can optionally filter the results with a query.

NOTE: As opposed to the get user API, built-in users are excluded from the result.
This API is only for native users.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"query\": {\n        \"prefix\": {\n            \"roles\": \"other\"\n        }\n    }\n}"
```

## Authenticate SAML

<a id="opIdsecurity-saml-authenticate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/saml/authenticate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"content\" : \"PHNhbWxwOlJlc3BvbnNlIHhtbG5zOnNhbWxwPSJ1cm46b2FzaXM6bmFtZXM6dGM6U0FNTDoyLjA6cHJvdG9jb2wiIHhtbG5zOnNhbWw9InVybjpvYXNpczpuYW1lczp0YzpTQU1MOjIuMD.....\",\n  \"ids\" : [\"4fee3b046395c4e751011e97f8900b5273d56685\"]\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/saml/authenticate`

Submit a SAML response message to Elasticsearch for consumption.

NOTE: This API is intended for use by custom web applications other than Kibana.
If you are using Kibana, refer to the documentation for configuring SAML single-sign-on on the Elastic Stack.

The SAML message that is submitted can be:

* A response to a SAML authentication request that was previously created using the SAML prepare authentication API.
* An unsolicited SAML message in the case of an IdP-initiated single sign-on (SSO) flow.

In either case, the SAML message needs to be a base64 encoded XML document with a root element of `<Response>`.

After successful validation, Elasticsearch responds with an Elasticsearch internal access token and refresh token that can be subsequently used for authentication.
This API endpoint essentially exchanges SAML responses that indicate successful authentication in the IdP for Elasticsearch access and refresh tokens, which can be used for authentication against Elasticsearch.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/saml">More about SAML authentication</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"content\" : \"PHNhbWxwOlJlc3BvbnNlIHhtbG5zOnNhbWxwPSJ1cm46b2FzaXM6bmFtZXM6dGM6U0FNTDoyLjA6cHJvdG9jb2wiIHhtbG5zOnNhbWw9InVybjpvYXNpczpuYW1lczp0YzpTQU1MOjIuMD.....\",\n  \"ids\" : [\"4fee3b046395c4e751011e97f8900b5273d56685\"]\n}"
```

<h3 id="authenticate-saml-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» content|body|string|true|The SAML response as it was sent by the user's browser, usually a Base64 encoded XML document.|
|» ids|body|object|true|A JSON array with all the valid SAML Request Ids that the caller of the API has for the current user.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|none|
|» realm|body|string|false|The name of the realm that should authenticate the SAML response. Useful in cases where many SAML realms are defined.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"access_token\" : \"46ToAxZVaXVVZTVKOVF5YU04ZFJVUDVSZlV3\",\n  \"username\" : \"Bearer\",\n  \"expires_in\" : 1200,\n  \"refresh_token\": \"mJdXLtmvTUSpoLwMvdBt_w\",\n  \"realm\": \"saml1\",\n  \"in_response_to\": \"4fee3b046395c4e751011e97f8900b5273d56685\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="authenticate-saml-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="authenticate-saml-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|string|true|none|The access token that was generated by Elasticsearch.|
|username|string|true|none|The authenticated user's name.|
|expires_in|number|true|none|The amount of time (in seconds) left until the token expires.|
|refresh_token|string|true|none|The refresh token that was generated by Elasticsearch.|
|realm|string|true|none|The name of the realm where the user was authenticated.|
|in_response_to|string|false|none|The id of the request that initiated the authentication process.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Logout of SAML completely

<a id="opIdsecurity-saml-complete-logout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/saml/complete_logout \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"realm\": \"saml1\",\n  \"ids\": [ \"_1c368075e0b3...\" ],\n  \"query_string\": \"SAMLResponse=fZHLasMwEEVbfb1bf...&SigAlg=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2F09%2Fxmldsig%23rsa-sha1&Signature=CuCmFn%2BLqnaZGZJqK...\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/saml/complete_logout`

Verifies the logout response sent from the SAML IdP.

NOTE: This API is intended for use by custom web applications other than Kibana.
If you are using Kibana, refer to the documentation for configuring SAML single-sign-on on the Elastic Stack.

The SAML IdP may send a logout response back to the SP after handling the SP-initiated SAML Single Logout.
This API verifies the response by ensuring the content is relevant and validating its signature.
An empty response is returned if the verification process is successful.
The response can be sent by the IdP with either the HTTP-Redirect or the HTTP-Post binding.
The caller of this API must prepare the request accordingly so that this API can handle either of them.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/saml">More about SAML authentication</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"realm\": \"saml1\",\n  \"ids\": [ \"_1c368075e0b3...\" ],\n  \"query_string\": \"SAMLResponse=fZHLasMwEEVbfb1bf...&SigAlg=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2F09%2Fxmldsig%23rsa-sha1&Signature=CuCmFn%2BLqnaZGZJqK...\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="logout-of-saml-completely-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» realm|body|string|true|The name of the SAML realm in Elasticsearch for which the configuration is used to verify the logout response.|
|» ids|body|object|true|A JSON array with all the valid SAML Request Ids that the caller of the API has for the current user.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|none|
|» query_string|body|string|false|If the SAML IdP sends the logout response with the HTTP-Redirect binding, this field must be set to the query string of the redirect URI.|
|» content|body|string|false|If the SAML IdP sends the logout response with the HTTP-Post binding, this field must be set to the value of the SAMLResponse form parameter from the logout response.|

<h3 id="logout-of-saml-completely-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /_security/saml/invalidate`

Submit a SAML LogoutRequest message to Elasticsearch for consumption.

NOTE: This API is intended for use by custom web applications other than Kibana.
If you are using Kibana, refer to the documentation for configuring SAML single-sign-on on the Elastic Stack.

The logout request comes from the SAML IdP during an IdP initiated Single Logout.
The custom web application can use this API to have Elasticsearch process the `LogoutRequest`.
After successful validation of the request, Elasticsearch invalidates the access token and refresh token that corresponds to that specific SAML principal and provides a URL that contains a SAML LogoutResponse message.
Thus the user can be redirected back to their IdP.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/saml">More about SAML authentication</a>

> Body parameter


|» query_string|body|string|true|The query part of the URL that the user was redirected to by the SAML IdP to initiate the Single Logout.<br>This query should include a single parameter named `SAMLRequest` that contains a SAML logout request that is deflated and Base64 encoded.<br>If the SAML IdP has signed the logout request, the URL should include two extra parameters named `SigAlg` and `Signature` that contain the algorithm used for the signature and the signature value itself.<br>In order for Elasticsearch to be able to verify the IdP's signature, the value of the `query_string` field must be an exact match to the string provided by the browser.<br>The client application must not attempt to parse or process the string in any way.|
|» realm|body|string|false|The name of the SAML realm in Elasticsearch the configuration. You must specify either this parameter or the `acs` parameter.|

## Logout of SAML

<a id="opIdsecurity-saml-logout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/saml/logout \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"token\" : \"46ToAxZVaXVVZTVKOVF5YU04ZFJVUDVSZlV3\",\n  \"refresh_token\" : \"mJdXLtmvTUSpoLwMvdBt_w\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/saml/logout`

Submits a request to invalidate an access token and refresh token.

NOTE: This API is intended for use by custom web applications other than Kibana.
If you are using Kibana, refer to the documentation for configuring SAML single-sign-on on the Elastic Stack.

This API invalidates the tokens that were generated for a user by the SAML authenticate API.
If the SAML realm in Elasticsearch is configured accordingly and the SAML IdP supports this, the Elasticsearch response contains a URL to redirect the user to the IdP that contains a SAML logout request (starting an SP-initiated SAML Single Logout).

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/saml">More about SAML authentication</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"token\" : \"46ToAxZVaXVVZTVKOVF5YU04ZFJVUDVSZlV3\",\n  \"refresh_token\" : \"mJdXLtmvTUSpoLwMvdBt_w\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="logout-of-saml-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string|true|The access token that was returned as a response to calling the SAML authenticate API.<br>Alternatively, the most recent token that was received after refreshing the original one by using a `refresh_token`.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The refresh token that was returned as a response to calling the SAML authenticate API.<br>Alternatively, the most recent refresh token that was received after refreshing the original access token.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"redirect\" : \"https://my-idp.org/logout/SAMLRequest=....\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="logout-of-saml-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="logout-of-saml-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|redirect|string|true|none|A URL that contains a SAML logout request as a parameter.<br>You can use this URL to be redirected back to the SAML IdP and to initiate Single Logout.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Prepare SAML authentication

<a id="opIdsecurity-saml-prepare-authentication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/saml/prepare \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"realm\" : \"saml1\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_security/saml/prepare`

Create a SAML authentication request (`<AuthnRequest>`) as a URL string based on the configuration of the respective SAML realm in Elasticsearch.

NOTE: This API is intended for use by custom web applications other than Kibana.
If you are using Kibana, refer to the documentation for configuring SAML single-sign-on on the Elastic Stack.

This API returns a URL pointing to the SAML Identity Provider.
You can use the URL to redirect the browser of the user in order to continue the authentication process.
The URL includes a single parameter named `SAMLRequest`, which contains a SAML Authentication request that is deflated and Base64 encoded.
If the configuration dictates that SAML authentication requests should be signed, the URL has two extra parameters named `SigAlg` and `Signature`.
These parameters contain the algorithm used for the signature and the signature value itself.
It also returns a random string that uniquely identifies this SAML Authentication request.
The caller of this API needs to store this identifier as it needs to be used in a following step of the authentication process.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/saml">More about SAML authentication</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"realm\" : \"saml1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="prepare-saml-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» acs|body|string|false|The Assertion Consumer Service URL that matches the one of the SAML realms in Elasticsearch.<br>The realm is used to generate the authentication request. You must specify either this parameter or the `realm` parameter.|
|» realm|body|string|false|The name of the SAML realm in Elasticsearch for which the configuration is used to generate the authentication request.<br>You must specify either this parameter or the `acs` parameter.|
|» relay_state|body|string|false|A string that will be included in the redirect URL that this API returns as the `RelayState` query parameter.<br>If the Authentication Request is signed, this value is used as part of the signature computation.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"redirect\": \"https://my-idp.org/login?SAMLRequest=fVJdc6IwFP0rmbwDgUKLGbFDtc462%2B06FX3Yl50rBJsKCZsbrPbXL6J22hdfk%2FNx7zl3eL%2BvK7ITBqVWCfVdRolQuS6k2iR0mU2dmN6Phgh1FTQ8be2rehH%2FWoGWdESF%2FPST0NYorgElcgW1QG5zvkh%2FPfHAZbwx2upcV5SkiMLYzmqsFba1MAthdjIXy5enhL5a23DPOyo6W7kGBa7cwhZ2gO7G8OiW%2BR400kORt0bag7fzezAlk24eqcD2OxxlsNN5O3MdsW9c6CZnbq7rntF4d3s0D7BaHTZhIWN52P%2BcjiuGRbDU6cdj%2BEjJbJLQv4N4ADdhxBiEZbQuWclY4Q8iABbCXczCdSiKMAC%2FgyO2YqbQgrIJDZg%2FcFjsMD%2Fzb3gUcBa5sR%2F9oWR%2BzuJBqlPG14Jbn0DIf2TZ3Jn%2FXmSUrC5ddQB6bob37uZrJdeF4dIDHV3iuhb70Ptq83kOz53ubDLXlcwPJK0q%2FT42AqxIaAkVCkqm2tRgr49yfJGFU%2FZQ3hy3QyuUpd7obPv97kb%2FAQ%3D%3D\"}\",\n  \"realm\": \"saml1\",\n  \"id\": \"_989a34500a4f5bf0f00d195aa04a7804b4ed42a1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="prepare-saml-authentication-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="prepare-saml-authentication-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|true|none|A unique identifier for the SAML Request to be stored by the caller of the API.|
|realm|string|true|none|The name of the Elasticsearch realm that was used to construct the authentication request.|
|redirect|string|true|none|The URL to redirect the user to.|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<a id="opIdsecurity-saml-service-provider-metadata"></a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/saml/metadata/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_security/saml/metadata/{realm_name}`

Generate SAML metadata for a SAML 2.0 Service Provider.

The SAML 2.0 specification provides a mechanism for Service Providers to describe their capabilities and configuration using a metadata file.
This API generates Service Provider metadata based on the configuration of a SAML realm in Elasticsearch.

<h3 id="create-saml-service-provider-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm_name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The name of the SAML realm in Elasticsearch.|

> Example responses

```json
"{\n\"metadata\": \"\"\"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?><md:EntityDescriptor xmlns:md=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata\" entityID=\"https://<kibana_url>\"><md:SPSSODescriptor AuthnRequestsSigned=\"false\" WantAssertionsSigned=\"true\" protocolSupportEnumeration=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol\"><md:SingleLogoutService Binding=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect\" Location=\"https://<kibana_url>/logout\"/><md:AssertionConsumerService Binding=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST\" Location=\"https://<kibana_url>/api/security/saml/callback\" index=\"1\" isDefault=\"true\"/></md:SPSSODescriptor></md:EntityDescriptor>\"\"\"\n}"
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="create-saml-service-provider-metadata-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Suggest a user profile

<a id="opIdsecurity-suggest-user-profiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/profile/_suggest \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"name\": \"jack\",  \n  \"hint\": {\n    \"uids\": [  \n      \"u_8RKO7AKfEbSiIHZkZZ2LJy2MUSDPWDr3tMI_CkIGApU_0\",\n      \"u_79HkWkwmnBH5gqFKwoxggWPjEBOur1zLPXQPEl1VBW0_0\"\n    ],\n    \"labels\": {\n      \"direction\": [\"north\", \"east\"]  \n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_security/profile/_suggest`

Get suggestions for user profiles that match specified search criteria.

NOTE: The user profile feature is designed only for use by Kibana and Elastic's Observability, Enterprise Search, and Elastic Security solutions.
Individual users and external applications should not call this API directly.
Elastic reserves the right to change or remove this feature in future releases without prior notice.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_security`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"name\": \"jack\",  \n  \"hint\": {\n    \"uids\": [  \n      \"u_8RKO7AKfEbSiIHZkZZ2LJy2MUSDPWDr3tMI_CkIGApU_0\",\n      \"u_79HkWkwmnBH5gqFKwoxggWPjEBOur1zLPXQPEl1VBW0_0\"\n    ],\n    \"labels\": {\n      \"direction\": [\"north\", \"east\"]  \n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="suggest-a-user-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|query|string \| [string]|false|A comma-separated list of filters for the `data` field of the profile document.<br>To return all content use `data=*`.<br>To return a subset of content, use `data=<key>` to retrieve content nested under the specified `<key>`.<br>By default, the API returns no `data` content.<br>It is an error to specify `data` as both the query parameter and the request body field.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A query string used to match name-related fields in user profile documents.<br>Name-related fields are the user's `username`, `full_name`, and `email`.|
|» size|body|number|false|The number of profiles to return.|
|» data|body|string \| [string]|false|A comma-separated list of filters for the `data` field of the profile document.<br>To return all content use `data=*`.<br>To return a subset of content, use `data=<key>` to retrieve content nested under the specified `<key>`.<br>By default, the API returns no `data` content.<br>It is an error to specify `data` as both the query parameter and the request body field.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» hint|body|object|false|Extra search criteria to improve relevance of the suggestion result.<br>Profiles matching the spcified hint are ranked higher in the response.<br>Profiles not matching the hint aren't excluded from the response as long as the profile matches the `name` field query.|
|» » uids|body|[[security._types.UserProfileId](#schemasecurity._types.userprofileid)]|false|A list of profile UIDs to match against.|
|» » labels|body|object|false|A single key-value pair to match against the labels section<br>of a profile. A profile is considered matching if it matches<br>at least one of the strings.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| [string]|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n    \"metadata\" : \"<?xml version=\\\"1.0\\\" encoding=\\\"UTF-8\\\"?><md:EntityDescriptor xmlns:md=\\\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata\\\" entityID=\\\"https://kibana.org\\\"><md:SPSSODescriptor AuthnRequestsSigned=\\\"false\\\" WantAssertionsSigned=\\\"true\\\" protocolSupportEnumeration=\\\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol\\\"><md:SingleLogoutService Binding=\\\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect\\\" Location=\\\"https://kibana.org/logout\\\"/><md:AssertionConsumerService Binding=\\\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST\\\" Location=\\\"https://kibana.org/api/security/saml/callback\\\" index=\\\"1\\\" isDefault=\\\"true\\\"/></md:SPSSODescriptor></md:EntityDescriptor>\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="suggest-a-user-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="suggest-a-user-profile-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total|object|true|none|Metadata about the number of matching profiles.|
|» value|number|true|none|none|
|» relation|object|true|none|none|
|took|number|true|none|The number of milliseconds it took Elasticsearch to run the request.|
|profiles|[[security._types.UserProfile](#schemasecurity._types.userprofile)]|true|none|A list of profile documents, ordered by relevance, that match the search criteria.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update an API key

<a id="opIdsecurity-update-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/api_key/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"role_descriptors\": {\n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"write\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 2,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"production\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/api_key/{id}`

Update attributes of an existing API key.
This API supports updates to an API key's access scope, expiration, and metadata.

To use this API, you must have at least the `manage_own_api_key` cluster privilege.
Users can only update API keys that they created or that were granted to them.
To update another user’s API key, use the `run_as` feature to submit a request on behalf of another user.

IMPORTANT: It's not possible to use an API key as the authentication credential for this API. The owner user’s credentials are required.

Use this API to update API keys created by the create API key or grant API Key APIs.
If you need to apply the same update to many API keys, you can use the bulk update API keys API to reduce overhead.
It's not possible to update expired API keys or API keys that have been invalidated by the invalidate API key API.

The access scope of an API key is derived from the `role_descriptors` you specify in the request and a snapshot of the owner user's permissions at the time of the request.
The snapshot of the owner's permissions is updated automatically on every call.

IMPORTANT: If you don't specify `role_descriptors` in the request, a call to this API might still change the API key's access scope.
This change can occur if the owner user's permissions have changed since the API key was created or last modified.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_own_api_key`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"role_descriptors\": {\n    \"role-a\": {\n      \"indices\": [\n        {\n          \"names\": [\"*\"],\n          \"privileges\": [\"write\"]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"environment\": {\n      \"level\": 2,\n      \"trusted\": true,\n      \"tags\": [\"production\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-an-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the API key to update.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
