## Update a cross-cluster API key

<a id="opIdsecurity-update-cross-cluster-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/cross_cluster/api_key/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"access\": {\n    \"replication\": [\n      {\n        \"names\": [\"archive\"]\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"application\": \"replication\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/cross_cluster/api_key/{id}`

Update the attributes of an existing cross-cluster API key, which is used for API key based remote cluster access.

To use this API, you must have at least the `manage_security` cluster privilege.
Users can only update API keys that they created.
To update another user's API key, use the `run_as` feature to submit a request on behalf of another user.

IMPORTANT: It's not possible to use an API key as the authentication credential for this API.
To update an API key, the owner user's credentials are required.

It's not possible to update expired API keys, or API keys that have been invalidated by the invalidate API key API.

This API supports updates to an API key's access scope, metadata, and expiration.
The owner user's information, such as the `username` and `realm`, is also updated automatically on every call.

NOTE: This API cannot update REST API keys, which should be updated by either the update API key or bulk update API keys API.

To learn more about how to use this API, refer to the [Update cross cluter API key API examples page](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/update-cc-api-key-examples).

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_security`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/remote-clusters/remote-clusters-api-key">About adding remote clusters</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"access\": {\n    \"replication\": [\n      {\n        \"names\": [\"archive\"]\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"application\": \"replication\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-a-cross-cluster-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the cross-cluster API key to update.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» access|body|object|true|The access to be granted to this API key.<br>The access is composed of permissions for cross cluster search and cross cluster replication.<br>At least one of them must be specified.<br>When specified, the new access assignment fully replaces the previously assigned access.|
|» » replication|body|[[security._types.ReplicationAccess](#schemasecurity._types.replicationaccess)]|false|A list of indices permission entries for cross-cluster replication.|
|» » search|body|[[security._types.SearchAccess](#schemasecurity._types.searchaccess)]|false|A list of indices permission entries for cross-cluster search.|
|» expiration|body|object|false|The expiration time for the API key.<br>By default, API keys never expire. This property can be omitted to leave the value unchanged.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the API key.<br>It supports nested data structure.<br>Within the metadata object, keys beginning with `_` are reserved for system usage.<br>When specified, this information fully replaces metadata previously associated with the API key.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» certificate_identity|body|string|false|The certificate identity to associate with this API key.<br>This field is used to restrict the API key to connections authenticated by a specific TLS certificate.<br>The value should match the certificate's distinguished name (DN) pattern.<br>When specified, this fully replaces any previously assigned certificate identity.<br>To clear an existing certificate identity, explicitly set this field to `null`.<br>When omitted, the existing certificate identity remains unchanged.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"updated\": true\n}"
```

|200|OK||Inline|

## Update user profile data

<a id="opIdsecurity-update-user-profile-data"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_security/profile/string/_data \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"labels\": {\n    \"direction\": \"east\"\n  },\n  \"data\": {\n    \"app1\": {\n      \"theme\": \"default\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_security/profile/{uid}/_data`

Update specific data for the user profile that is associated with a unique ID.

NOTE: The user profile feature is designed only for use by Kibana and Elastic's Observability, Enterprise Search, and Elastic Security solutions.
Individual users and external applications should not call this API directly.
Elastic reserves the right to change or remove this feature in future releases without prior notice.

To use this API, you must have one of the following privileges:

* The `manage_user_profile` cluster privilege.
* The `update_profile_data` global privilege for the namespaces that are referenced in the request.

This API updates the `labels` and `data` fields of an existing user profile document with JSON objects.
New keys and their values are added to the profile document and conflicting keys are replaced by data that's included in the request.

For both labels and data, content is namespaced by the top-level fields.
The `update_profile_data` global privilege grants privileges for updating only the allowed namespaces.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_user_profile`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"labels\": {\n    \"direction\": \"east\"\n  },\n  \"data\": {\n    \"app1\": {\n      \"theme\": \"default\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-user-profile-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uid|path|[security._types.UserProfileId](#schemasecurity._types.userprofileid)|true|A unique identifier for the user profile.|
|if_seq_no|query|[_types.SequenceNumber](#schema_types.sequencenumber)|false|Only perform the operation if the document has this sequence number.|
|if_primary_term|query|number|false|Only perform the operation if the document has this primary term.|
|refresh|query|object|false|If 'true', Elasticsearch refreshes the affected shards to make this operation<br>visible to search.<br>If 'wait_for', it waits for a refresh to make this operation visible to search.<br>If 'false', nothing is done with refreshes.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» labels|body|object|false|Searchable data that you want to associate with the user profile.<br>This field supports a nested data structure.<br>Within the labels object, top-level keys cannot begin with an underscore (`_`) or contain a period (`.`).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» data|body|object|false|Non-searchable data that you want to associate with the user profile.<br>This field supports a nested data structure.<br>Within the `data` object, top-level keys cannot begin with an underscore (`_`) or contain a period (`.`).<br>The data object is not searchable, but can be retrieved with the get user profile API.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-user-profile-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get SSL certificates

<a id="opIdssl-certificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ssl/certificates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ssl/certificates`

Get information about the X.509 certificates that are used to encrypt communications in the cluster.
The API returns a list that includes certificates from all TLS contexts including:

- Settings for transport and HTTP interfaces
- TLS settings that are used within authentication realms
- TLS settings for remote monitoring exporters

The list includes certificates that are used for configuring trust, such as those configured in the `xpack.security.transport.ssl.truststore` and `xpack.security.transport.ssl.certificate_authorities` settings.
It also includes certificates that are used for configuring server identity, such as `xpack.security.http.ssl.keystore` and `xpack.security.http.ssl.certificate settings`.

The list does not include certificates that are sourced from the default SSL context of the Java Runtime Environment (JRE), even if those certificates are in use within Elasticsearch.

NOTE: When a PKCS#11 token is configured as the truststore of the JRE, the API returns all the certificates that are included in the PKCS#11 token irrespective of whether these are used in the Elasticsearch TLS configuration.

If Elasticsearch is configured to use a keystore or truststore, the API output includes all certificates in that store, even though some of the certificates might not be in active use within the cluster.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/set-up-basic-security#encrypt-internode-communication">About setting up transport tls</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[\n  {\n    \"path\": \"certs/elastic-certificates.p12\",\n    \"format\": \"PKCS12\",\n    \"alias\": \"instance\",\n    \"subject_dn\": \"CN=Elastic Certificate Tool Autogenerated CA\",\n    \"serial_number\": \"a20f0ee901e8f69dc633ff633e5cd5437cdb4137\",\n    \"has_private_key\": false,\n    \"expiry\": \"2021-01-15T20:42:49.000Z\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"certs/elastic-certificates.p12\",\n    \"format\": \"PKCS12\",\n    \"alias\": \"ca\",\n    \"subject_dn\": \"CN=Elastic Certificate Tool Autogenerated CA\",\n    \"serial_number\": \"a20f0ee901e8f69dc633ff633e5cd5437cdb4137\",\n    \"has_private_key\": false,\n    \"expiry\": \"2021-01-15T20:42:49.000Z\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"certs/elastic-certificates.p12\",\n    \"format\": \"PKCS12\",\n    \"alias\": \"instance\",\n    \"subject_dn\": \"CN=instance\",\n    \"serial_number\": \"fc1905e1494dc5230218d079c47a617088f84ce0\",\n    \"has_private_key\": true,\n    \"expiry\": \"2021-01-15T20:44:32.000Z\"\n  }\n]"
```

<h3 id="get-an-enrich-policy-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policies|[[enrich._types.Summary](#schemaenrich._types.summary)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create an enrich policy

<a id="opIdenrich-put-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_enrich/policy/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"geo_match\": {\n    \"indices\": \"postal_codes\",\n    \"match_field\": \"location\",\n    \"enrich_fields\": [ \"location\", \"postal_code\" ]\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_enrich/policy/{name}`

Creates an enrich policy.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"geo_match\": {\n    \"indices\": \"postal_codes\",\n    \"match_field\": \"location\",\n    \"enrich_fields\": [ \"location\", \"postal_code\" ]\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-enrich-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Name of the enrich policy to create or update.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

## Delete an enrich policy

<a id="opIdenrich-delete-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_enrich/policy/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_enrich/policy/{name}`

Deletes an existing enrich policy and its enrich index.

<h3 id="delete-an-enrich-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Enrich policy to delete.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-enrich-policy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run an enrich policy

<a id="opIdenrich-execute-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_enrich/policy/string/_execute \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /_enrich/policy/{name}/_execute`

Create the enrich index for an existing enrich policy.

<h3 id="run-an-enrich-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Enrich policy to execute.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request blocks other enrich policy execution requests until complete.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": {
    "phase": {},
    "step": "string"
  },
  "task": {}
}
```

<h3 id="run-an-enrich-policy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="run-an-enrich-policy-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|object|false|none|none|
|» phase|object|true|none|none|
|» step|string|false|none|none|
|task|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get enrich stats

<a id="opIdenrich-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_enrich/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_enrich/_stats`

Returns enrich coordinator statistics and information about enrich policies that are currently executing.

<h3 id="get-enrich-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

<a id="opIdeql-get-status"></a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_eql/search/status/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_eql/search/status/{id}`

Get the current status for an async EQL search or a stored synchronous EQL search without returning results.

<h3 id="get-the-async-eql-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the search.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"id\": \"FmNJRUZ1YWZCU3dHY1BIOUhaenVSRkEaaXFlZ3h4c1RTWFNocDdnY2FSaERnUTozNDE=\",\n  \"is_running\" : true,\n  \"is_partial\" : true,\n  \"start_time_in_millis\" : 1611690235000,\n  \"expiration_time_in_millis\" : 1611690295000\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-the-async-eql-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-the-async-eql-status-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|true|none|Identifier for the search.|
|is_partial|boolean|true|none|If true, the search request is still executing. If false, the search is completed.|
|is_running|boolean|true|none|If true, the response does not contain complete search results. This could be because either the search is still running (is_running status is false), or because it is already completed (is_running status is true) and results are partial due to failures or timeouts.|
|start_time_in_millis|object|false|none|For a running search shows a timestamp when the eql search started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.|
|expiration_time_in_millis|object|false|none|Shows a timestamp when the eql search will be expired, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. When this time is reached, the search and its results are deleted, even if the search is still ongoing.|
|completion_status|number|false|none|For a completed search shows the http status code of the completed search.|

This operation does not require authentication

## Get EQL search results

<a id="opIdeql-search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_eql/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    process where (process.name == \"cmd.exe\" and process.pid != 2013)\n  \"\"\"\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_eql/search`

Returns search results for an Event Query Language (EQL) query.
EQL assumes each document in a data stream or index corresponds to an event.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/eql">Learn more about EQL</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    process where (process.name == \"cmd.exe\" and process.pid != 2013)\n  \"\"\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-eql-search-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|Comma-separated list of index names to scope the operation|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|If true, returns partial results if there are shard failures. If false, returns an error with no partial results.|
|allow_partial_sequence_results|query|boolean|false|If true, sequence queries will return partial results in case of shard failures. If false, they will return no results at all.<br>This flag has effect only if allow_partial_search_results is true.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether network round-trips should be minimized as part of cross-cluster search requests execution|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|keep_alive|query|object|false|Period for which the search and its results are stored on the cluster.|
|keep_on_completion|query|boolean|false|If true, the search and its results are stored on the cluster.|
|wait_for_completion_timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Timeout duration to wait for the request to finish. Defaults to no timeout, meaning the request waits for complete search results.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» query|body|string|true|EQL query you wish to run.|
|» case_sensitive|body|boolean|false|none|
|» event_category_field|body|object|false|Field containing the event classification, such as process, file, or network.|
|» tiebreaker_field|body|object|false|Field used to sort hits with the same timestamp in ascending order|
|» timestamp_field|body|object|false|Field containing event timestamp.|
|» fetch_size|body|object|false|Maximum number of events to search at a time for sequence queries.|
|» filter|body|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|Query, written in Query DSL, used to filter the events on which the EQL query runs.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)|false|An Elasticsearch Query DSL (Domain Specific Language) object that defines a query.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|
|» keep_alive|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» keep_on_completion|body|boolean|false|none|
|» wait_for_completion_timeout|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» allow_partial_search_results|body|boolean|false|Allow query execution also in case of shard failures.<br>If true, the query will keep running and will return results based on the available shards.<br>For sequences, the behavior can be further refined using allow_partial_sequence_results|
|» allow_partial_sequence_results|body|boolean|false|This flag applies only to sequences and has effect only if allow_partial_search_results=true.<br>If true, the sequence query will return results based on the available shards, ignoring the others.<br>If false, the sequence query will return successfully, but will always have empty results.|
|» size|body|object|false|For basic queries, the maximum number of matching events to return. Defaults to 10|
|» fields|body|[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat) \| [[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|Array of wildcard (*) patterns. The response returns values for field names matching these patterns in the fields property of each hit.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)|false|A reference to a field with formatting instructions on how to return the value|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|none|
|» result_position|body|object|false|none|
|» runtime_mappings|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.mapping.RuntimeField](#schema_types.mapping.runtimefield)|false|none|
|» max_samples_per_key|body|number|false|By default, the response of a sample query contains up to `10` samples, with one sample per unique set of join keys. Use the `size`<br>parameter to get a smaller or larger set of samples. To retrieve more than one sample per set of join keys, use the<br>`max_samples_per_key` parameter. Pipes are not supported for sample queries.|

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-esql">esql</h1>

## Run an async ES|QL query

<a id="opIdesql-async-query"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/async \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM library,remote-*:library\n    | EVAL year = DATE_TRUNC(1 YEARS, release_date)\n    | STATS MAX(page_count) BY year\n    | SORT year\n    | LIMIT 5\n  \"\"\",\n  \"wait_for_completion_timeout\": \"2s\",\n  \"include_ccs_metadata\": true\n}"'
```

`POST /_query/async`

Asynchronously run an ES|QL (Elasticsearch query language) query, monitor its progress, and retrieve results when they become available.

The API accepts the same parameters and request body as the synchronous query API, along with additional async related properties.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql">More about ES|QL reference</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM library,remote-*:library\n    | EVAL year = DATE_TRUNC(1 YEARS, release_date)\n    | STATS MAX(page_count) BY year\n    | SORT year\n    | LIMIT 5\n  \"\"\",\n  \"wait_for_completion_timeout\": \"2s\",\n  \"include_ccs_metadata\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="run-an-async-esql-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Get async ES|QL query results

<a id="opIdesql-async-query-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/async/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_query/async/{id}`

Get the current status and available results or stored results for an ES|QL asynchronous query.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, only the user who first submitted the ES|QL query can retrieve the results using this API.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql">More about ES|QL reference</a>

<h3 id="get-async-esql-query-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the query.<br>A query ID is provided in the ES\|QL async query API response for a query that does not complete in the designated time.<br>A query ID is also provided when the request was submitted with the `keep_on_completion` parameter set to `true`.|
|drop_null_columns|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether columns that are entirely `null` will be removed from the `columns` and `values` portion of the results.<br>If `true`, the response will include an extra section under the name `all_columns` which has the name of all the columns.|
|format|query|[esql._types.EsqlFormat](#schemaesql._types.esqlformat)|false|A short version of the Accept header, for example `json` or `yaml`.|
|keep_alive|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The period for which the query and its results are stored in the cluster.<br>When this period expires, the query and its results are deleted, even if the query is still ongoing.|
|wait_for_completion_timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The period to wait for the request to finish.<br>By default, the request waits for complete query results.<br>If the request completes during the period specified in this parameter, complete query results are returned.<br>Otherwise, the response returns an `is_running` value of `true` and no results.|

|---|---|
|format|csv|
|format|json|
|format|tsv|
|format|txt|
|format|yaml|
|format|cbor|
|format|smile|
|format|arrow|

## Delete an async ES|QL query

<a id="opIdesql-async-query-delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/async/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_query/async/{id}`

If the query is still running, it is cancelled.
Otherwise, the stored results are deleted.

If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, only the following users can use this API to delete a query:

* The authenticated user that submitted the original query request
* Users with the `cancel_task` cluster privilege

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql">More about ES|QL reference</a>

<h3 id="delete-an-async-esql-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the query.<br>A query ID is provided in the ES\|QL async query API response for a query that does not complete in the designated time.<br>A query ID is also provided when the request was submitted with the `keep_on_completion` parameter set to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-async-esql-query-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Stop async ES|QL query

<a id="opIdesql-async-query-stop"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/async/string/stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_query/async/{id}/stop`

This API interrupts the query execution and returns the results so far.
If the Elasticsearch security features are enabled, only the user who first submitted the ES|QL query can stop it.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql">More about ES|QL reference</a>

<h3 id="stop-async-esql-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Get ES|QL data sources

`GET /_query/data_source/{name}`

Returns one or more data sources used in ES|QL data federation.
A concrete-name miss returns `404`; a wildcard pattern or list-all request with no match
returns `200` with an empty array.

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-data-federation">ES|QL Data Federation</a>

|name|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|A comma-separated list of data source names or wildcard patterns. Omit to return all data sources.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"data_sources\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"prod_s3_logs\",\n      \"type\": \"s3\",\n      \"description\": \"Production S3 logs bucket\",\n      \"settings\": {\n        \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n        \"auth\": \"static_credentials\",\n        \"access_key\": \"::es_redacted::\",\n        \"secret_key\": \"::es_redacted::\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

|200|OK||Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_sources|[[esql._types.ESQLDataSource](#schemaesql._types.esqldatasource)]|true|none|The matching data sources.<br>Credential values in each data source's settings are redacted as `::es_redacted::` in the response.|

## Create or update an ES|QL data source

<a id="opIdesql-put-data-source"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/data_source/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"type\": \"s3\",\n  \"description\": \"Production S3 logs bucket\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n    \"auth\": \"static_credentials\",\n    \"access_key\": \"<AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID>\",\n    \"secret_key\": \"<AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY>\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_query/data_source/{name}`

Creates or replaces a named, type-specific data source configuration for ES|QL data federation.
Datasets reference data source configurations to access external data. Names must be lowercase
and follow index or alias naming rules.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-data-federation">ES|QL Data Federation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"type\": \"s3\",\n  \"description\": \"Production S3 logs bucket\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n    \"auth\": \"static_credentials\",\n    \"access_key\": \"<AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID>\",\n    \"secret_key\": \"<AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY>\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-data-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The data source name to create or update.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The time to wait for the request to be completed.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The data source type. Currently, `s3` is supported.<br>The value must be lowercase and contain no whitespace.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-text description of the data source.|
|» settings|body|object|false|Type-specific connection and authentication settings.<br>For `s3`, connection settings include `region` and `endpoint`. Authentication settings<br>include `auth` and the credentials required by the selected authentication method.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-data-source-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update an ES|QL dataset

<a id="opIdesql-put-dataset"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/dataset/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"data_source\": \"prod_s3_logs\",\n  \"resource\": \"s3://logs-bucket/access/**/*.parquet\",\n  \"description\": \"Production access logs\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"partition_detection\": \"hive\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_query/dataset/{name}`

Creates or replaces a dataset that references a data source in ES|QL data federation.
Dataset names participate in the index namespace and must follow index or alias naming rules.
Returns `404` if the referenced data source does not exist.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-data-federation">ES|QL Data Federation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"data_source\": \"prod_s3_logs\",\n  \"resource\": \"s3://logs-bucket/access/**/*.parquet\",\n  \"description\": \"Production access logs\",\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"partition_detection\": \"hive\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The dataset name to create or update.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The time to wait for the request to be completed.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» data_source|body|object|true|The name of the referenced data source. The data source must already exist.|
|» resource|body|string|true|The URI that identifies the data to read, resolved against the referenced data source.<br>It can include glob patterns. For example, a recursive pattern can match<br>all Parquet files under the `s3://logs-bucket/access` prefix.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-text description of the dataset.|
|» mappings|body|object|false|User-declared mapping on the dataset definition|
|» » dynamic|body|object|false|The policy for columns that are not declared in `properties`.<br>`true` (the default) infers undeclared columns and overlays the declarations; `false` makes the declaration the entire schema, so undeclared columns are not queryable.|
|» » properties|body|object|false|The per-column declarations, keyed by logical column name.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[esql._types.DatasetFieldMapping](#schemaesql._types.datasetfieldmapping)|false|A per-column declaration inside a dataset mapping's `properties`.|
|» » _id|body|object|false|The `_id` meta-field configuration, sourcing the document identity from a column.|
|» » » path|body|string|true|The name of the column that provides the document identity.|
|» settings|body|object|false|Format and parsing-specific settings that configure how the resource is read.<br>Common keys include `format`, which explicitly selects a registered format, and<br>`partition_detection`, which accepts `auto`, `hive`, `template`, or `none`. Additional<br>keys depend on the format reader. Compression can be inferred from the resource URI.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-dataset-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update an ES|QL view

<a id="opIdesql-put-view"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/view/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM addresses\n    | RENAME city.country.name AS country\n    | EVAL country = CASE(country == \"United States of America\", \"United States\", country)\n    | STATS count=COUNT() BY country\n  \"\"\",\n  \"description\": \"Address counts by country\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_query/view/{name}`

Stores an ES|QL query that runs whenever the view is referenced.
A query that cannot be parsed is rejected. Replacing a reserved view fails.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `create_view`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-views">Define reusable queries with ES|QL views</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM addresses\n    | RENAME city.country.name AS country\n    | EVAL country = CASE(country == \"United States of America\", \"United States\", country)\n    | STATS count=COUNT() BY country\n  \"\"\",\n  \"description\": \"Address counts by country\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The view name to create or update.|
|validate|query|boolean|false|Whether to analyze the view query and return a warning when validation fails.<br><br>Validation reports an unknown index or column, including an index the caller cannot read.<br>The view is saved even when validation reports a problem.<br>Failures unrelated to the query, such as an overloaded cluster, produce no warning.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» query|body|string|true|The ES\|QL query string that defines the view. A query that cannot be parsed is rejected.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-text description of the view.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-esql-view-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get an ES|QL view

<a id="opIdesql-get-view"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query/view \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_query/view`

Returns one or more stored views. A reserved view includes `reserved` set to `true`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read_view_metadata`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-views">Define reusable queries with ES|QL views</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"views\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"country_addresses\",\n      \"query\": \"\"\"\n        FROM addresses\n        | RENAME city.country.name AS country\n        | EVAL country = CASE(country == \"United States of America\", \"United States\", country)\n        | STATS count=COUNT() BY country\n      \"\"\",\n      \"description\": \"Address counts by country\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-an-esql-view-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-an-esql-view-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|views|[[esql._types.ESQLView](#schemaesql._types.esqlview)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

Returns an object containing IDs and other information about the running ES|QL queries.

```json
      "query": "string"

    "property2": {

      "node": {},

}
```

## Run an ES|QL query

<a id="opIdesql-query"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM library,remote-*:library\n    | EVAL year = DATE_TRUNC(1 YEARS, release_date)\n    | STATS MAX(page_count) BY year\n    | SORT year\n    | LIMIT 5\n  \"\"\",\n  \"include_ccs_metadata\": true\n}"'
```

`POST /_query`

Get search results for an ES|QL (Elasticsearch query language) query.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql">More about ES|QL reference</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": \"\"\"\n    FROM library,remote-*:library\n    | EVAL year = DATE_TRUNC(1 YEARS, release_date)\n    | STATS MAX(page_count) BY year\n    | SORT year\n    | LIMIT 5\n  \"\"\",\n  \"include_ccs_metadata\": true\n}"
```

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-features">features</h1>

## Get the features

<a id="opIdfeatures-get-features"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_features \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_features`

Get a list of features that can be included in snapshots using the `feature_states` field when creating a snapshot.
You can use this API to determine which feature states to include when taking a snapshot.
By default, all feature states are included in a snapshot if that snapshot includes the global state, or none if it does not.

A feature state includes one or more system indices necessary for a given feature to function.
In order to ensure data integrity, all system indices that comprise a feature state are snapshotted and restored together.

The features listed by this API are a combination of built-in features and features defined by plugins.
In order for a feature state to be listed in this API and recognized as a valid feature state by the create snapshot API, the plugin that defines that feature must be installed on the master node.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/tools/snapshot-and-restore/create-snapshots">More about managing snapshots</a>

<h3 id="get-the-features-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"features\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"tasks\",\n      \"description\": \"Manages task results\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"kibana\",\n      \"description\": \"Manages Kibana configuration and reports\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-the-features-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-the-features-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|features|[[features._types.Feature](#schemafeatures._types.feature)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Reset the features

<a id="opIdfeatures-reset-features"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_features/_reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_features/_reset`

Clear all of the state information stored in system indices by Elasticsearch features, including the security and machine learning indices.

WARNING: Intended for development and testing use only. Do not reset features on a production cluster.

Return a cluster to the same state as a new installation by resetting the feature state for all Elasticsearch features.
This deletes all state information stored in system indices.

The response code is HTTP 200 if the state is successfully reset for all features.
It is HTTP 500 if the reset operation failed for any feature.

Note that select features might provide a way to reset particular system indices.
Using this API resets all features, both those that are built-in and implemented as plugins.

To list the features that will be affected, use the get features API.

IMPORTANT: The features installed on the node you submit this request to are the features that will be reset. Run on the master node if you have any doubts about which plugins are installed on individual nodes.

<h3 id="reset-the-features-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"features\" : [\n    {\n      \"feature_name\" : \"security\",\n      \"status\" : \"SUCCESS\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"feature_name\" : \"tasks\",\n      \"status\" : \"SUCCESS\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="reset-the-features-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-fleet">fleet</h1>

## Get global checkpoints

<a id="opIdfleet-global-checkpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_fleet/global_checkpoints \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_fleet/global_checkpoints`

Get the current global checkpoints for an index.
This API is designed for internal use by the Fleet server project.

<h3 id="get-global-checkpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias)|true|A single index or index alias that resolves to a single index.|
|wait_for_advance|query|boolean|false|A boolean value which controls whether to wait (until the timeout) for the global checkpoints<br>to advance past the provided `checkpoints`.|
|wait_for_index|query|boolean|false|A boolean value which controls whether to wait (until the timeout) for the target index to exist<br>and all primary shards be active. Can only be true when `wait_for_advance` is true.|
|checkpoints|query|[[fleet._types.Checkpoint](#schemafleet._types.checkpoint)]|false|A comma separated list of previous global checkpoints. When used in combination with `wait_for_advance`,<br>the API will only return once the global checkpoints advances past the checkpoints. Providing an empty list<br>will cause Elasticsearch to immediately return the current global checkpoints.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a global checkpoints to advance past `checkpoints`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "global_checkpoints": [
    0
  ],
  "timed_out": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-global-checkpoints-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-global-checkpoints-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|global_checkpoints|[[fleet._types.Checkpoint](#schemafleet._types.checkpoint)]|true|none|none|
|timed_out|boolean|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run multiple Fleet searches

<a id="opIdfleet-msearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_fleet/_fleet_msearch \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {
      "allow_no_indices": true,
      "expand_wildcards": {},
      "ignore_unavailable": true,
      "index": {},
      "preference": "string",
      "project_routing": {},
      "request_cache": true,
      "routing": {},
      "search_type": {},
      "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
      "allow_partial_search_results": true,
      "ignore_throttled": true
    }
  ]'
```

`GET /_fleet/_fleet_msearch`

Run several Fleet searches with a single API request.
The API follows the same structure as the multi search API.
However, similar to the Fleet search API, it supports the `wait_for_checkpoints` parameter.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "allow_no_indices": true,
    "expand_wildcards": {},
    "ignore_unavailable": true,
    "index": {},
    "preference": "string",
    "project_routing": {},
    "request_cache": true,
    "routing": {},
    "search_type": {},
    "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
    "allow_partial_search_results": true,
    "ignore_throttled": true
  }
]
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-fleet-searches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_types.ExpandWildcards](#schema_types.expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|wait_for_checkpoints|query|[[fleet._types.Checkpoint](#schemafleet._types.checkpoint)]|false|A comma separated list of checkpoints. When configured, the search API will only be executed on a shard<br>after the relevant checkpoint has become visible for search. Defaults to an empty list which will cause<br>Elasticsearch to immediately execute the search.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|If true, returns partial results if there are shard request timeouts or shard failures.<br>If false, returns an error with no partial results.<br>Defaults to the configured cluster setting `search.default_allow_partial_results`, which is true by default.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

<h3 id="run-multiple-fleet-searches-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|docs|[[_global.msearch.ResponseItem](#schema_global.msearch.responseitem)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run multiple Fleet searches

<a id="opIdfleet-msearch-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_fleet/_fleet_msearch \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {
      "allow_no_indices": true,
      "expand_wildcards": {},
      "ignore_unavailable": true,
      "index": {},
      "preference": "string",
      "project_routing": {},
      "request_cache": true,
      "routing": {},
      "search_type": {},
      "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
      "allow_partial_search_results": true,
      "ignore_throttled": true
    }
  ]'
```

`GET /{index}/_fleet/_fleet_msearch`

Run several Fleet searches with a single API request.
The API follows the same structure as the multi search API.
However, similar to the Fleet search API, it supports the `wait_for_checkpoints` parameter.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "allow_no_indices": true,
    "expand_wildcards": {},
    "ignore_unavailable": true,
    "index": {},
    "preference": "string",
    "project_routing": {},
    "request_cache": true,
    "routing": {},
    "search_type": {},
    "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
    "allow_partial_search_results": true,
    "ignore_throttled": true
  }
]
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-fleet-searches-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias)|true|A single target to search. If the target is an index alias, it must resolve to a single index.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_types.ExpandWildcards](#schema_types.expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|wait_for_checkpoints|query|[[fleet._types.Checkpoint](#schemafleet._types.checkpoint)]|false|A comma separated list of checkpoints. When configured, the search API will only be executed on a shard<br>after the relevant checkpoint has become visible for search. Defaults to an empty list which will cause<br>Elasticsearch to immediately execute the search.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|If true, returns partial results if there are shard request timeouts or shard failures.<br>If false, returns an error with no partial results.<br>Defaults to the configured cluster setting `search.default_allow_partial_results`, which is true by default.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

## Run multiple Fleet searches

<a id="opIdfleet-msearch-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_fleet/_fleet_msearch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {
      "allow_no_indices": true,
      "expand_wildcards": {},
      "ignore_unavailable": true,
      "index": {},
      "preference": "string",
      "project_routing": {},
      "request_cache": true,
      "routing": {},
      "search_type": {},
      "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
      "allow_partial_search_results": true,
      "ignore_throttled": true
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /{index}/_fleet/_fleet_msearch`

Run several Fleet searches with a single API request.
The API follows the same structure as the multi search API.
However, similar to the Fleet search API, it supports the `wait_for_checkpoints` parameter.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "allow_no_indices": true,
    "expand_wildcards": {},
    "ignore_unavailable": true,
    "index": {},
    "preference": "string",
    "project_routing": {},
    "request_cache": true,
    "routing": {},
    "search_type": {},
    "ccs_minimize_roundtrips": true,
    "allow_partial_search_results": true,
    "ignore_throttled": true
  }
]
```

<h3 id="run-multiple-fleet-searches-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias)|true|A single target to search. If the target is an index alias, it must resolve to a single index.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_types.ExpandWildcards](#schema_types.expandwildcards)|false|Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|max_concurrent_searches|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.|
|max_concurrent_shard_requests|query|number|false|Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.|
|pre_filter_shard_size|query|number|false|Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.|
|search_type|query|[_types.SearchType](#schema_types.searchtype)|false|Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.|
|wait_for_checkpoints|query|[[fleet._types.Checkpoint](#schemafleet._types.checkpoint)]|false|A comma separated list of checkpoints. When configured, the search API will only be executed on a shard<br>after the relevant checkpoint has become visible for search. Defaults to an empty list which will cause<br>Elasticsearch to immediately execute the search.|
|allow_partial_search_results|query|boolean|false|If true, returns partial results if there are shard request timeouts or shard failures.<br>If false, returns an error with no partial results.<br>Defaults to the configured cluster setting `search.default_allow_partial_results`, which is true by default.|
|body|body|[[_global.msearch.RequestItem](#schema_global.msearch.requestitem)]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_type|query_then_fetch|
|search_type|dfs_query_then_fetch|

`GET /{index}/_fleet/_fleet_search`

The purpose of the Fleet search API is to provide an API where the search will be run only
after the provided checkpoint has been processed and is visible for searches inside of Elasticsearch.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`

<h3 id="run-a-fleet-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias)|true|A single target to search. If the target is an index alias, it must resolve to a single index.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|analyzer|query|string|false|none|
|analyze_wildcard|query|boolean|false|none|
|batched_reduce_size|query|number|false|none|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|query|boolean|false|none|
|default_operator|query|[_types.query_dsl.Operator](#schema_types.query_dsl.operator)|false|none|
|df|query|string|false|none|
|docvalue_fields|query|[_types.Fields](#schema_types.fields)|false|none|
|expand_wildcards|query|[_types.ExpandWildcards](#schema_types.expandwildcards)|false|none|

`POST /{index}/_fleet/_fleet_search`

The purpose of the Fleet search API is to provide an API where the search will be run only
after the provided checkpoint has been processed and is visible for searches inside of Elasticsearch.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-graph">graph</h1>

## Explore graph analytics

<a id="opIdgraph-explore"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_graph/explore \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"match\": {\n      \"query.raw\": \"midi\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"vertices\": [\n    {\n      \"field\": \"product\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": {\n    \"vertices\": [\n      {\n        \"field\": \"query.raw\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_graph/explore`

Extract and summarize information about the documents and terms in an Elasticsearch data stream or index.
The easiest way to understand the behavior of this API is to use the Graph UI to explore connections.
An initial request to the `_explore` API contains a seed query that identifies the documents of interest and specifies the fields that define the vertices and connections you want to include in the graph.
Subsequent requests enable you to spider out from one more vertices of interest.
You can exclude vertices that have already been returned.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/visualize/graph">Learn more about graphs</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"match\": {\n      \"query.raw\": \"midi\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"vertices\": [\n    {\n      \"field\": \"product\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": {\n    \"vertices\": [\n      {\n        \"field\": \"query.raw\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"
```

## Explore graph analytics

<a id="opIdgraph-explore-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_graph/explore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"match\": {\n      \"query.raw\": \"midi\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"vertices\": [\n    {\n      \"field\": \"product\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": {\n    \"vertices\": [\n      {\n        \"field\": \"query.raw\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_graph/explore`

Extract and summarize information about the documents and terms in an Elasticsearch data stream or index.
The easiest way to understand the behavior of this API is to use the Graph UI to explore connections.
An initial request to the `_explore` API contains a seed query that identifies the documents of interest and specifies the fields that define the vertices and connections you want to include in the graph.
Subsequent requests enable you to spider out from one more vertices of interest.
You can exclude vertices that have already been returned.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/visualize/graph">Learn more about graphs</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"match\": {\n      \"query.raw\": \"midi\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"vertices\": [\n    {\n      \"field\": \"product\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": {\n    \"vertices\": [\n      {\n        \"field\": \"query.raw\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}"
```

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-healthreport">health_report</h1>

## Get the cluster health

<a id="opIdhealth-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_health_report \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_health_report`

Get a report with the health status of an Elasticsearch cluster.
The report contains a list of indicators that compose Elasticsearch functionality.

Each indicator has a health status of: green, unknown, yellow or red.
The indicator will provide an explanation and metadata describing the reason for its current health status.

The cluster’s status is controlled by the worst indicator status.

In the event that an indicator’s status is non-green, a list of impacts may be present in the indicator result which detail the functionalities that are negatively affected by the health issue.
Each impact carries with it a severity level, an area of the system that is affected, and a simple description of the impact on the system.

Some health indicators can determine the root cause of a health problem and prescribe a set of steps that can be performed in order to improve the health of the system.
The root cause and remediation steps are encapsulated in a diagnosis.
A diagnosis contains a cause detailing a root cause analysis, an action containing a brief description of the steps to take to fix the problem, the list of affected resources (if applicable), and a detailed step-by-step troubleshooting guide to fix the diagnosed problem.

NOTE: The health indicators perform root cause analysis of non-green health statuses. This can be computationally expensive when called frequently.
When setting up automated polling of the API for health status, set verbose to false to disable the more expensive analysis logic.

<h3 id="get-the-cluster-health-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Explicit operation timeout.|
|verbose|query|boolean|false|Opt-in for more information about the health of the system.|
|size|query|number|false|Limit the number of affected resources the health report API returns.|

## Get the cluster health

<a id="opIdhealth-report-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_health_report/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_health_report/{feature}`

Get a report with the health status of an Elasticsearch cluster.
The report contains a list of indicators that compose Elasticsearch functionality.

Each indicator has a health status of: green, unknown, yellow or red.
The indicator will provide an explanation and metadata describing the reason for its current health status.

The cluster’s status is controlled by the worst indicator status.

In the event that an indicator’s status is non-green, a list of impacts may be present in the indicator result which detail the functionalities that are negatively affected by the health issue.
Each impact carries with it a severity level, an area of the system that is affected, and a simple description of the impact on the system.

Some health indicators can determine the root cause of a health problem and prescribe a set of steps that can be performed in order to improve the health of the system.
The root cause and remediation steps are encapsulated in a diagnosis.
A diagnosis contains a cause detailing a root cause analysis, an action containing a brief description of the steps to take to fix the problem, the list of affected resources (if applicable), and a detailed step-by-step troubleshooting guide to fix the diagnosed problem.

NOTE: The health indicators perform root cause analysis of non-green health statuses. This can be computationally expensive when called frequently.
When setting up automated polling of the API for health status, set verbose to false to disable the more expensive analysis logic.

<h3 id="get-the-cluster-health-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|feature|path|string \| [string]|true|A feature of the cluster, as returned by the top-level health report API.|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Explicit operation timeout.|
|verbose|query|boolean|false|Opt-in for more information about the health of the system.|
|size|query|number|false|Limit the number of affected resources the health report API returns.|

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-ilm">ilm</h1>

## Get lifecycle policies

<a id="opIdilm-get-lifecycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ilm/policy/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ilm/policy/{policy}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ilm`,`read_ilm`


<h3 id="get-lifecycle-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Identifier for the policy.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"my_policy\": {\n    \"version\": 1,\n    \"modified_date\": 82392349,\n    \"policy\": {\n      \"phases\": {\n        \"warm\": {\n          \"min_age\": \"10d\",\n          \"actions\": {\n            \"forcemerge\": {\n              \"max_num_segments\": 1\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        \"delete\": {\n          \"min_age\": \"30d\",\n          \"actions\": {\n            \"delete\": {\n              \"delete_searchable_snapshot\": true\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"in_use_by\" : {\n      \"indices\" : [],\n      \"data_streams\" : [],\n      \"composable_templates\" : []\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-lifecycle-policies-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-lifecycle-policies-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|[ilm.get_lifecycle.Lifecycle](#schemailm.get_lifecycle.lifecycle)|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a lifecycle policy

<a id="opIdilm-put-lifecycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ilm/policy/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"policy\": {\n    \"_meta\": {\n      \"description\": \"used for nginx log\",\n      \"project\": {\n        \"name\": \"myProject\",\n        \"department\": \"myDepartment\"\n      }\n    },\n    \"phases\": {\n      \"warm\": {\n        \"min_age\": \"10d\",\n        \"actions\": {\n          \"forcemerge\": {\n            \"max_num_segments\": 1\n          }\n        }\n      },\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"min_age\": \"30d\",\n        \"actions\": {\n          \"delete\": {}\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ilm/policy/{policy}`

If the specified policy exists, it is replaced and the policy version is incremented.

NOTE: Only the latest version of the policy is stored, you cannot revert to previous versions.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ilm`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/lifecycle/index-lifecycle-management/index-lifecycle">About index lifecycle management</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"policy\": {\n    \"_meta\": {\n      \"description\": \"used for nginx log\",\n      \"project\": {\n        \"name\": \"myProject\",\n        \"department\": \"myDepartment\"\n      }\n    },\n    \"phases\": {\n      \"warm\": {\n        \"min_age\": \"10d\",\n        \"actions\": {\n          \"forcemerge\": {\n            \"max_num_segments\": 1\n          }\n        }\n      },\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"min_age\": \"30d\",\n        \"actions\": {\n          \"delete\": {}\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-lifecycle-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Identifier for the policy.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» policy|body|object|false|none|
|» » phases|body|object|true|none|
|» » » cold|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » actions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » » allocate|body|object|false|Phases allowed: warm, cold.|

## Explain the lifecycle state

<a id="opIdilm-explain-lifecycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_ilm/explain \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /{index}/_ilm/explain`

Get the current lifecycle status for one or more indices.
For data streams, the API retrieves the current lifecycle status for the stream's backing indices.

The response indicates when the index entered each lifecycle state, provides the definition of the running phase, and information about any failures.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `view_index_metadata`,`manage_ilm`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/explain-lifecycle">About explaining lifecycle state</a>

<h3 id="explain-the-lifecycle-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to target. Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>To target all data streams and indices, use `*` or `_all`.|
|only_errors|query|boolean|false|Filters the returned indices to only indices that are managed by ILM and are in an error state, either due to an encountering an error while executing the policy, or attempting to use a policy that does not exist.|
|only_managed|query|boolean|false|Filters the returned indices to only indices that are managed by ILM.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"indices\": {\n    \"my-index-000001\": {\n      \"index\": \"my-index-000001\",\n      \"index_creation_date_millis\": 1538475653281,\n      \"index_creation_date\": \"2018-10-15T13:45:21.981Z\",\n      \"time_since_index_creation\": \"15s\",\n      \"managed\": true,\n      \"policy\": \"my_policy\",\n      \"lifecycle_date_millis\": 1538475653281,\n      \"lifecycle_date\": \"2018-10-15T13:45:21.981Z\",\n      \"age\": \"15s\",\n      \"phase\": \"new\",\n      \"phase_time_millis\": 1538475653317,\n      \"phase_time\": \"2018-10-15T13:45:22.577Z\",\n      \"action\": \"complete\"\n      \"action_time_millis\": 1538475653317,\n      \"action_time\": \"2018-10-15T13:45:22.577Z\",\n      \"step\": \"complete\",\n      \"step_time_millis\": 1538475653317,\n      \"step_time\": \"2018-10-15T13:45:22.577Z\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```
