## Migrate to data tiers routing

<a id="opIdilm-migrate-to-data-tiers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ilm/migrate_to_data_tiers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"legacy_template_to_delete\": \"global-template\",\n  \"node_attribute\": \"custom_attribute_name\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ilm/migrate_to_data_tiers`

Switch the indices, ILM policies, and legacy, composable, and component templates from using custom node attributes and attribute-based allocation filters to using data tiers.
Optionally, delete one legacy index template.
Using node roles enables ILM to automatically move the indices between data tiers.

Migrating away from custom node attributes routing can be manually performed.
This API provides an automated way of performing three out of the four manual steps listed in the migration guide:

1. Stop setting the custom hot attribute on new indices.
1. Remove custom allocation settings from existing ILM policies.
1. Replace custom allocation settings from existing indices with the corresponding tier preference.

ILM must be stopped before performing the migration.
Use the stop ILM and get ILM status APIs to wait until the reported operation mode is `STOPPED`.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/lifecycle/index-lifecycle-management/migrate-index-allocation-filters-to-node-roles">About migrating index allocation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"legacy_template_to_delete\": \"global-template\",\n  \"node_attribute\": \"custom_attribute_name\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="migrate-to-data-tiers-routing-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dry_run|query|boolean|false|If true, simulates the migration from node attributes based allocation filters to data tiers, but does not perform the migration.<br>This provides a way to retrieve the indices and ILM policies that need to be migrated.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» legacy_template_to_delete|body|string|false|none|
|» node_attribute|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"dry_run\": false,\n  \"removed_legacy_template\":\"global-template\",\n  \"migrated_ilm_policies\":[\"policy_with_allocate_action\"],\n  \"migrated_indices\":[\"warm-index-to-migrate-000001\"],\n  \"migrated_legacy_templates\":[\"a-legacy-template\"],\n  \"migrated_composable_templates\":[\"a-composable-template\"],\n  \"migrated_component_templates\":[\"a-component-template\"]\n}"
```

<h3 id="migrate-to-data-tiers-routing-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="migrate-to-data-tiers-routing-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dry_run|boolean|true|none|none|
|removed_legacy_template|string|true|none|The name of the legacy index template that was deleted.<br>This information is missing if no legacy index templates were deleted.|
|migrated_ilm_policies|[string]|true|none|The ILM policies that were updated.|
|migrated_indices|object|true|none|The indices that were migrated to tier preference routing.|
|» *oneOf*|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|none|none|
|» *oneOf*|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|none|
|migrated_legacy_templates|[string]|true|none|The legacy index templates that were updated to not contain custom routing settings for the provided data attribute.|
|migrated_composable_templates|[string]|true|none|The composable index templates that were updated to not contain custom routing settings for the provided data attribute.|
|migrated_component_templates|[string]|true|none|The component templates that were updated to not contain custom routing settings for the provided data attribute.|

This operation does not require authentication

## Move to a lifecycle step

<a id="opIdilm-move-to-step"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ilm/move/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"current_step\": {\n    \"phase\": \"new\",\n    \"action\": \"complete\",\n    \"name\": \"complete\"\n  },\n  \"next_step\": {\n    \"phase\": \"warm\",\n    \"action\": \"forcemerge\",\n    \"name\": \"forcemerge\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ilm/move/{index}`

Manually move an index into a specific step in the lifecycle policy and run that step.

WARNING: This operation can result in the loss of data. Manually moving an index into a specific step runs that step even if it has already been performed. This is a potentially destructive action and this should be considered an expert level API.

You must specify both the current step and the step to be executed in the body of the request.
The request will fail if the current step does not match the step currently running for the index
This is to prevent the index from being moved from an unexpected step into the next step.

When specifying the target (`next_step`) to which the index will be moved, either the name or both the action and name fields are optional.
If only the phase is specified, the index will move to the first step of the first action in the target phase.
If the phase and action are specified, the index will move to the first step of the specified action in the specified phase.
Only actions specified in the ILM policy are considered valid.
An index cannot move to a step that is not part of its policy.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage_ilm`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"current_step\": {\n    \"phase\": \"new\",\n    \"action\": \"complete\",\n    \"name\": \"complete\"\n  },\n  \"next_step\": {\n    \"phase\": \"warm\",\n    \"action\": \"forcemerge\",\n    \"name\": \"forcemerge\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="move-to-a-lifecycle-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|The name of the index whose lifecycle step is to change|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» current_step|body|object|true|The step that the index is expected to be in.|
|» » action|body|string|false|The optional action to which the index will be moved.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The optional step name to which the index will be moved.|
|» » phase|body|string|true|none|
|» next_step|body|object|true|The step that you want to run.|
|» » action|body|string|false|The optional action to which the index will be moved.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The optional step name to which the index will be moved.|
|» » phase|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="move-to-a-lifecycle-step-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<a id="opIdilm-stop"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ilm/stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ilm/stop`

Halt all lifecycle management operations and stop the index lifecycle management plugin.
This is useful when you are performing maintenance on the cluster and need to prevent ILM from performing any actions on your indices.

The API returns as soon as the stop request has been acknowledged, but the plugin might continue to run until in-progress operations complete and the plugin can be safely stopped.
Use the get ILM status API to check whether ILM is running.

`PUT /_create_from/{source}/{dest}`

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Reindex legacy backing indices

<a id="opIdindices-migrate-reindex"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_migration/reindex \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"source\": {\n        \"index\": \"my-data-stream\"\n    },\n    \"mode\": \"upgrade\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_migration/reindex`

Reindex all legacy backing indices for a data stream.
This operation occurs in a persistent task.
The persistent task ID is returned immediately and the reindexing work is completed in that task.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/reindex-data-stream">About reindexing data streams</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"source\": {\n        \"index\": \"my-data-stream\"\n    },\n    \"mode\": \"upgrade\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="reindex-legacy-backing-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[indices.migrate_reindex.MigrateReindex](#schemaindices.migrate_reindex.migratereindex)|true|none|
|» mode|body|object|true|Reindex mode. Currently only 'upgrade' is supported.|
|» source|body|object|true|The source index or data stream (only data streams are currently supported).|
|» » index|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="reindex-legacy-backing-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get deprecation information

<a id="opIdmigration-deprecations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_migration/deprecations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_migration/deprecations`

Returns information about deprecated features which are in use in the cluster.
The reported features include cluster, node, and index level settings that will be removed or changed in the next major version.
You must address the reported issues before upgrading to the next major version.
However, no action is required when upgrading within the current major version.
Deprecated features remain fully supported and will continue to work in the current version, and when upgrading to a newer minor or patch release in the same major version.
Use this API to review your usage of these features and migrate away from them at your own pace, before upgrading to a new major version.

> info
> This API is designed for indirect use by the [Upgrade Assistant](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/upgrade/prepare-to-upgrade/upgrade-assistant).
> We recommend learning about deprecated features using the Upgrade Assistant rather than calling this API directly.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"cluster_settings\": [\n    {\n      \"level\": \"critical\",\n      \"message\": \"Cluster name cannot contain ':'\",\n      \"url\": \"https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.0/breaking-changes-7.0.html#_literal_literal_is_no_longer_allowed_in_cluster_name\",\n      \"details\": \"This cluster is named [mycompany:logging], which contains the illegal character ':'.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"node_settings\": [],\n  \"index_settings\": {\n    \"logs:apache\": [\n      {\n        \"level\": \"warning\",\n        \"message\": \"Index name cannot contain ':'\",\n        \"url\": \"https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.0/breaking-changes-7.0.html#_literal_literal_is_no_longer_allowed_in_index_name\",\n        \"details\": \"This index is named [logs:apache], which contains the illegal character ':'.\"\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"ml_settings\": []\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-deprecation-information-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-deprecation-information-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_settings|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|true|none|Cluster-level deprecation warnings.|
|index_settings|object|true|none|Index warnings are sectioned off per index and can be filtered using an index-pattern in the query.<br>This section includes warnings for the backing indices of data streams specified in the request path.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|false|none|none|
|data_streams|object|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|false|none|none|
|node_settings|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|true|none|Node-level deprecation warnings.<br>Since only a subset of your nodes might incorporate these settings, it is important to read the details section for more information about which nodes are affected.|
|ml_settings|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|true|none|Machine learning-related deprecation warnings.|
|templates|object|true|none|Template warnings are sectioned off per template and include deprecations for both component templates and<br>index templates.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|false|none|none|
|ilm_policies|object|true|none|ILM policy warnings are sectioned off per policy.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[[migration.deprecations.Deprecation](#schemamigration.deprecations.deprecation)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Start the feature migration

<a id="opIdmigration-post-feature-upgrade"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_migration/system_features`

Version upgrades sometimes require changes to how features store configuration information and data in system indices.
This API starts the automatic migration process.

Some functionality might be temporarily unavailable during the migration process.

TIP: The API is designed for indirect use by the Upgrade Assistant. We strongly recommend you use the Upgrade Assistant.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`
* Cluster privileges: `manage`

## Downsample an index

<a id="opIdindices-downsample"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_downsample/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"fixed_interval\": \"1d\"\n}"'
```

`POST /{index}/_downsample/{target_index}`

Downsamples a time series (TSDS) index and reduces its size by keeping the last value or by pre-aggregating metrics:

- When running in `aggregate` mode, it pre-calculates and stores statistical summaries (`min`, `max`, `sum`, `value_count` and `avg`)
for each metric field grouped by a configured time interval and their dimensions.
- When running in `last_value` mode, it keeps the last value for each metric in the configured interval and their dimensions.

For example, a TSDS index that contains metrics sampled every 10 seconds can be downsampled to an hourly index.
All documents within an hour interval are summarized and stored as a single document in the downsample index.

NOTE: Only indices in a time series data stream are supported.
Neither field nor document level security can be defined on the source index.
The source index must be read-only (`index.blocks.write: true`).

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"fixed_interval\": \"1d\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="downsample-an-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the time series index to downsample.|
|target_index|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the index to create.|
|body|body|[indices._types.DownsampleConfig](#schemaindices._types.downsampleconfig)|true|none|
|» fixed_interval|body|object|true|The interval at which to aggregate the original time series index.|
|» sampling_method|body|object|false|The sampling method used to reduce the documents; it can be either `aggregate` or `last_value`. Defaults to `aggregate`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="downsample-an-index-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /_data_stream/{name}/_mappings`

This API can be used to override mappings on specific data streams. These overrides will take precedence over what
is specified in the template that the data stream matches. The mapping change is only applied to new write indices
that are created during rollover after this API is called. No indices are changed by this API.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`

```json
"{\n   \"properties\":{\n      \"field1\":{\n         \"type\":\"ip\"\n      },\n      \"field3\":{\n         \"type\":\"text\"\n      }\n   }\n}"
```

<a id="opIdindices-put-data-stream-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_data_stream/string/_settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index.lifecycle.name\" : \"new-test-policy\",\n  \"index.number_of_shards\": 11\n}"'
```

`PUT /_data_stream/{name}/_settings`

NOTE: Available in 8.19. Not available in earlier versions.

This API can be used to override settings on specific data streams. These overrides will take precedence over what
is specified in the template that the data stream matches. To prevent your data stream from getting into an invalid state,
only certain settings are allowed. If possible, the setting change is applied to all
backing indices. Otherwise, it will be applied when the data stream is next rolled over.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index.lifecycle.name\" : \"new-test-policy\",\n  \"index.number_of_shards\": 11\n}"
```

## Convert an index alias to a data stream

<a id="opIdindices-migrate-to-data-stream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_data_stream/_migrate/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_data_stream/_migrate/{name}`

Converts an index alias to a data stream.
You must have a matching index template that is data stream enabled.
The alias must meet the following criteria:
The alias must have a write index;
All indices for the alias must have a `@timestamp` field mapping of a `date` or `date_nanos` field type;
The alias must not have any filters;
The alias must not use custom routing.
If successful, the request removes the alias and creates a data stream with the same name.
The indices for the alias become hidden backing indices for the stream.
The write index for the alias becomes the write index for the stream.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="convert-an-index-alias-to-a-data-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|Name of the index alias to convert to a data stream.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="convert-an-index-alias-to-a-data-stream-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update data streams

<a id="opIdindices-modify-data-stream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_data_stream/_modify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"actions\": [\n    {\n      \"remove_backing_index\": {\n        \"data_stream\": \"my-data-stream\",\n        \"index\": \".ds-my-data-stream-2023.07.26-000001\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"add_backing_index\": {\n        \"data_stream\": \"my-data-stream\",\n        \"index\": \".ds-my-data-stream-2023.07.26-000001-downsample\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_data_stream/_modify`

Performs one or more data stream modification actions in a single atomic operation.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"actions\": [\n    {\n      \"remove_backing_index\": {\n        \"data_stream\": \"my-data-stream\",\n        \"index\": \".ds-my-data-stream-2023.07.26-000001\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"add_backing_index\": {\n        \"data_stream\": \"my-data-stream\",\n        \"index\": \".ds-my-data-stream-2023.07.26-000001-downsample\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Promote a data stream

<a id="opIdindices-promote-data-stream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_data_stream/_promote/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_data_stream/_promote/{name}`

Promote a data stream from a replicated data stream managed by cross-cluster replication (CCR) to a regular data stream.

With CCR auto following, a data stream from a remote cluster can be replicated to the local cluster.
These data streams can't be rolled over in the local cluster.
These replicated data streams roll over only if the upstream data stream rolls over.
In the event that the remote cluster is no longer available, the data stream in the local cluster can be promoted to a regular data stream, which allows these data streams to be rolled over in the local cluster.

NOTE: When promoting a data stream, ensure the local cluster has a data stream enabled index template that matches the data stream.
If this is missing, the data stream will not be able to roll over until a matching index template is created.
This will affect the lifecycle management of the data stream and interfere with the data stream size and retention.

<h3 id="promote-a-data-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|The name of the data stream to promote|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="promote-a-data-stream-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-inference">inference</h1>

## Perform streaming chat completion inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-chat-completion-unified"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/chat_completion/string/_stream \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"model\": \"gpt-4o\",\n  \"messages\": [\n      {\n          \"role\": \"user\",\n          \"content\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n      }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_inference/chat_completion/{inference_id}/_stream`

The chat completion inference API enables real-time responses for chat completion tasks by delivering answers incrementally, reducing response times during computation.
It only works with the `chat_completion` task type.

NOTE: The `chat_completion` task type supports both streaming and non-streaming.
The Chat completion inference API and the Stream inference API differ in their response structure and capabilities.
The Chat completion inference API provides more comprehensive customization options through more fields and function calling support.
To determine whether a given inference service supports this task type, please see the page for that service.

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"model\": \"gpt-4o\",\n  \"messages\": [\n      {\n          \"role\": \"user\",\n          \"content\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n      }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-streaming-chat-completion-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The inference Id|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|[inference._types.RequestChatCompletion](#schemainference._types.requestchatcompletion)|true|none|
|» messages|body|[[inference._types.Message](#schemainference._types.message)]|true|A list of objects representing the conversation.<br>Requests should generally only add new messages from the user (role `user`).<br>The other message roles (`assistant`, `system`, or `tool`) should generally only be copied from the response to a previous completion request, such that the messages array is built up throughout a conversation.|
|» model|body|string|false|The ID of the model to use. By default, the model ID is set to the value included when creating the inference endpoint.|
|» max_completion_tokens|body|number|false|The upper bound limit for the number of tokens that can be generated for a completion request.|
|» reasoning|body|object|false|The reasoning configuration for the completion request.<br>This controls the model's reasoning process in one of two ways:<br><br>* By specifying the model’s reasoning effort level with the `effort` field.<br>* By enabling reasoning with default settings by setting `enabled` field to `true`.<br><br>It also includes optional settings to control:<br><br>* The level of detail in the summary returned in the response with the `summary` field.<br>* Whether reasoning details are included in the response at all with the `exclude` field.<br><br>Example (effort):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "effort": "high",<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Example (enabled):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "enabled": true,<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.|
|» » effort|body|object|false|The level of effort the model should put into reasoning.<br>This is a hint that guides the model in how much effort to put into reasoning,<br>with `xhigh` being the most effort and `none` being no effort.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable reasoning with default settings.<br>This is a shortcut for enabling reasoning without having to specify the other parameters.<br>If `enabled` is set to `true`, then reasoning at the `medium` effort level is enabled.<br>Ignored if `effort` is specified,<br>in which case that parameter will control the reasoning process instead.|
|» » exclude|body|boolean|false|Whether to exclude reasoning information from the response.<br>If `true`, the response will not include any reasoning details.|
|» » summary|body|object|false|The level of detail included in the reasoning summary returned in the response.<br>This is a hint on how much detail to include in the summary of the reasoning that is returned in the response,<br>with `auto` being the default level of detail, `concise` being less detail, and `detailed` being more detail.|
|» stop|body|[string]|false|A sequence of strings to control when the model should stop generating additional tokens.|
|» temperature|body|number|false|The sampling temperature to use.|
|» tool_choice|body|object|false|Controls which tool is called by the model.<br>String representation: One of `auto`, `none`, or `requrired`. `auto` allows the model to choose between calling tools and generating a message. `none` causes the model to not call any tools. `required` forces the model to call one or more tools.<br>Example (object representation):<br>```<br>{<br>  "tool_choice": {<br>      "type": "function",<br>      "function": {<br>          "name": "get_current_weather"<br>      }<br>  }<br>}<br>```|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference._types.CompletionToolChoice](#schemainference._types.completiontoolchoice)|false|Controls which tool is called by the model.|
|» tools|body|[[inference._types.CompletionTool](#schemainference._types.completiontool)]|false|A list of tools that the model can call.<br>Example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>      {<br>          "type": "function",<br>          "function": {<br>              "name": "get_price_of_item",<br>              "description": "Get the current price of an item",<br>              "parameters": {<br>                  "type": "object",<br>                  "properties": {<br>                      "item": {<br>                          "id": "12345"<br>                      },<br>                      "unit": {<br>                          "type": "currency"<br>                      }<br>                  }<br>              }<br>          }<br>      }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```|
|» top_p|body|number|false|Nucleus sampling, an alternative to sampling with temperature.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"event: message\ndata: {\"chat_completion\":{\"id\":\"chatcmpl-Ae0TWsy2VPnSfBbv5UztnSdYUMFP3\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"\",\"role\":\"assistant\"},\"index\":0}],\"model\":\"gpt-4o-2024-08-06\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\"}}\n\nevent: message\ndata: {\"chat_completion\":{\"id\":\"chatcmpl-Ae0TWsy2VPnSfBbv5UztnSdYUMFP3\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":Elastic\"},\"index\":0}],\"model\":\"gpt-4o-2024-08-06\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\"}}\n\nevent: message\ndata: {\"chat_completion\":{\"id\":\"chatcmpl-Ae0TWsy2VPnSfBbv5UztnSdYUMFP3\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\" is\"},\"index\":0}],\"model\":\"gpt-4o-2024-08-06\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\"}}\n\n(...)\n\nevent: message\ndata: {\"chat_completion\":{\"id\":\"chatcmpl-Ae0TWsy2VPnSfBbv5UztnSdYUMFP3\",\"choices\":[],\"model\":\"gpt-4o-2024-08-06\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\",\"usage\":{\"completion_tokens\":28,\"prompt_tokens\":16,\"total_tokens\":44}}} \n\nevent: message\ndata: [DONE]"
```

<h3 id="perform-streaming-chat-completion-inference-on-the-service-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.StreamResult](#schema_types.streamresult)|

## Perform completion inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-completion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"input\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_inference/completion/{inference_id}`

Get responses for completion tasks.
This API works only with the completion task type.

IMPORTANT: The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Azure, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face. For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models. However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

This API requires the `monitor_inference` cluster privilege (the built-in `inference_admin` and `inference_user` roles grant this privilege).

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"input\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-completion-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The inference Id|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» input|body|string \| [string]|true|Inference input.<br>Either a string or an array of strings.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request. These settings are specific to the <task_type> you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"completion\": [\n    {\n      \"result\": \"Elastic is a company that provides a range of software solutions for search, logging, security, and analytics. Their flagship product is Elasticsearch, an open-source, distributed search engine that allows users to search, analyze, and visualize large volumes of data in real-time. Elastic also offers products such as Kibana, a data visualization tool, and Logstash, a log management and pipeline tool, as well as various other tools and solutions for data analysis and management.\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-completion-inference-on-the-service-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.CompletionInferenceResult](#schemainference._types.completioninferenceresult)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create an inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n \"service\": \"cohere\",\n \"service_settings\": {\n   \"model_id\": \"rerank-english-v3.0\",\n   \"api_key\": \"{{COHERE_API_KEY}}\"\n }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{inference_id}`

IMPORTANT: The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Mistral, Azure OpenAI, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face.
For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models.
However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

The following integrations are available through the inference API. You can find the available task types next to the integration name:
* AI21 (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* AlibabaCloud AI Search (`completion`, `rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding`)
* Amazon Bedrock (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Amazon SageMaker (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding`)
* Anthropic (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* Azure AI Studio (`completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Azure OpenAI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Cohere (`completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* DeepSeek (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* Elasticsearch (`rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding` - this service is for built-in models and models uploaded through Eland)
* ELSER (`sparse_embedding`)
* Fireworks AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Google AI Studio (`completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Google Vertex AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Groq (`chat_completion`)
* Hugging Face (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* JinaAI (`embedding`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Llama (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Mistral (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Nvidia (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`, `rerank`)
* OpenAI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* OpenShift AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* VoyageAI (`rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Watsonx (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n \"service\": \"cohere\",\n \"service_settings\": {\n   \"model_id\": \"rerank-english-v3.0\",\n   \"api_key\": \"{{COHERE_API_KEY}}\"\n }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The inference Id|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.<br>The default depends on the task type: 120s for `completion` and `chat_completion`, and 30s for all other task types.|
|body|body|[inference._types.InferenceEndpoint](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpoint)|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `embedding`, `sparse_embedding` and `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|string|true|The service type|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings specific to the service|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings specific to the service and task type|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-inference-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfo](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfo)|

This operation does not require authentication

## Perform inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-inference"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "input_type": "string",
    "task_settings": {}
  }'
```

`POST /_inference/{inference_id}`

This API enables you to use machine learning models to perform specific tasks on data that you provide as an input.
It returns a response with the results of the tasks.
The inference endpoint you use can perform one specific task that has been defined when the endpoint was created with the create inference API.

For details about using this API with a service, such as Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, or HuggingFace, refer to the service-specific documentation.

> info
> The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Azure, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face. For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models. However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "input_type": "string",
  "task_settings": {}
}
```

<h3 id="perform-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier for the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» query|body|string|false|The query input, which is required only for the `rerank` task.<br>It is not required for other tasks.|
|» input|body|string \| [string]|true|The text on which you want to perform the inference task.<br>It can be a single string or an array.<br><br>> info<br>> Inference endpoints for the `completion` task type currently only support a single string as input.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» input_type|body|string|false|Specifies the input data type for the embedding model. The `input_type` parameter only applies to Inference Endpoints with the `embedding` or `text_embedding` task type. Possible values include:<br>* `SEARCH`<br>* `INGEST`<br>* `CLASSIFICATION`<br>* `CLUSTERING`<br>Not all services support all values. Unsupported values will trigger a validation exception.<br>Accepted values depend on the configured inference service, refer to the relevant service-specific documentation for more info.<br><br>> info<br>> The `input_type` parameter specified on the root level of the request body will take precedence over the `input_type` parameter specified in `task_settings`.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "embeddings_bytes": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "embeddings_bits": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "embeddings": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "text_embedding_bytes": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "text_embedding_bits": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "text_embedding": [
    {
      "embedding": {}
    }
  ],
  "sparse_embedding": [
    {
      "is_truncated": true,
      "embedding": {
        "property1": 0,
        "property2": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "completion": [
    {
      "result": "string"
    }
  ],
  "rerank": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "relevance_score": 0,
      "text": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceResult](#schemainference._types.inferenceresult)|

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{inference_id}`

IMPORTANT: The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Mistral, Azure OpenAI, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face.
For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models.
However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

The following integrations are available through the inference API. You can find the available task types next to the integration name:
* AI21 (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* AlibabaCloud AI Search (`completion`, `rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding`)
* Amazon Bedrock (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Amazon SageMaker (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding`)
* Anthropic (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* Azure AI Studio (`completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Azure OpenAI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Cohere (`completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* DeepSeek (`chat_completion`, `completion`)
* Elasticsearch (`rerank`, `sparse_embedding`, `text_embedding` - this service is for built-in models and models uploaded through Eland)
* ELSER (`sparse_embedding`)
* Fireworks AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Google AI Studio (`completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Google Vertex AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Groq (`chat_completion`)
* Hugging Face (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* JinaAI (`embedding`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Llama (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Mistral (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* Nvidia (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`, `rerank`)
* OpenAI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `text_embedding`)
* OpenShift AI (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* VoyageAI (`rerank`, `text_embedding`)
* Watsonx (`chat_completion`, `completion`, `rerank`, `text_embedding`)

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n \"service\": \"cohere\",\n \"service_settings\": {\n   \"model_id\": \"rerank-english-v3.0\",\n   \"api_key\": \"{{COHERE_API_KEY}}\"\n }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-inference-endpoint-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.TaskType](#schemainference._types.tasktype)|true|The task type. Refer to the integration list in the API description for the available task types.|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The inference Id|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.<br>The default depends on the task type: 120s for `completion` and `chat_completion`, and 30s for all other task types.|
|body|body|[inference._types.InferenceEndpoint](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpoint)|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `embedding`, `sparse_embedding` and `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|string|true|The service type|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings specific to the service|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings specific to the service and task type|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|embedding|
|task_type|document_extraction|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

## Perform inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-inference-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/sparse_embedding/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "string",
    "input": "string",
    "input_type": "string",
    "task_settings": {}
  }'
```

`POST /_inference/{task_type}/{inference_id}`

This API enables you to use machine learning models to perform specific tasks on data that you provide as an input.
It returns a response with the results of the tasks.
The inference endpoint you use can perform one specific task that has been defined when the endpoint was created with the create inference API.

For details about using this API with a service, such as Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, or HuggingFace, refer to the service-specific documentation.

> info
> The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Azure, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face. For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models. However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "input_type": "string",
  "task_settings": {}
}
```

<h3 id="perform-inference-on-the-service-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.TaskType](#schemainference._types.tasktype)|true|The type of inference task that the model performs.|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier for the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» query|body|string|false|The query input, which is required only for the `rerank` task.<br>It is not required for other tasks.|
|» input|body|string \| [string]|true|The text on which you want to perform the inference task.<br>It can be a single string or an array.<br><br>> info<br>> Inference endpoints for the `completion` task type currently only support a single string as input.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» input_type|body|string|false|Specifies the input data type for the embedding model. The `input_type` parameter only applies to Inference Endpoints with the `embedding` or `text_embedding` task type. Possible values include:<br>* `SEARCH`<br>* `INGEST`<br>* `CLASSIFICATION`<br>* `CLUSTERING`<br>Not all services support all values. Unsupported values will trigger a validation exception.<br>Accepted values depend on the configured inference service, refer to the relevant service-specific documentation for more info.<br><br>> info<br>> The `input_type` parameter specified on the root level of the request body will take precedence over the `input_type` parameter specified in `task_settings`.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|embedding|
|task_type|document_extraction|

## Create or update the inference region policy

<a id="opIdinference-put-region-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/_region_policy \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"region_policy\": {\n        \"allowed_regions\": [\n            { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"us-east-1\" },\n            { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"eu-west-1\" }\n        ]\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/_region_policy`

The region policy restricts inference to a set of allowed geographic areas or cloud service provider regions.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"region_policy\": {\n        \"allowed_regions\": [\n            { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"us-east-1\" },\n            { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"eu-west-1\" }\n        ]\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-the-inference-region-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the region policy is applied even if it would deny access to inference endpoints that are currently in use by ingest pipeline or indices.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» region_policy|body|object|true|The region policy configuration.|
|» » allowed_geos|body|[string]|false|The list of allowed geographic areas.<br>Mutually exclusive with `allowed_regions`.|
|» » allowed_regions|body|[[inference._types.CspRegion](#schemainference._types.cspregion)]|false|The list of allowed cloud service provider regions.<br>Mutually exclusive with `allowed_geos`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"region_policy\": {\n    \"allowed_regions\": [\n      { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"us-east-1\" },\n      { \"csp\": \"aws\", \"region\": \"eu-west-1\" }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-07-13T12:00:00.000Z\",\n  \"created_by\": \"inference_user\"\n}"
```

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"input\": [\n      {\n          \"content\": {\n              \"type\": \"image\",\n              \"format\": \"base64\",\n              \"value\": \"data:image/jpeg;base64,...\"\n          }\n      },\n      {\n          \"content\": {\n              \"type\": \"text\",\n              \"value\": \"Some text to create an embedding\"\n          }\n      }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-dense-embedding-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[inference._types.RequestEmbedding](#schemainference._types.requestembedding)|true|none|
|» input|body|object|true|Inference input.<br>Either a string, an array of strings, a `content` object, or an array of `content` objects.<br>`content` objects may contain a single item or an array of items. Models that support multiple items per `content`<br>object will return a single embedding for each `content` object, regardless of how many items it contains.<br>Support for multiple items in a single `content` object is available in Elasticsearch 9.5.0 and later.<br><br>string example:<br>```<br>"input": "Some text"<br>```<br>string array example:<br>```<br>"input": ["Some text", "Some more text"]<br>```<br>`content` object example:<br>```<br>"input": {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "base64",<br>      "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>    }<br>  }<br>```<br>`content` object array example:<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "text",<br>      "format": "text",<br>      "value": "Some text to generate an embedding"<br>    }<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "base64",<br>      "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br>`content` object using the `url` format example (available in Elasticsearch 9.6.0 and later):<br>```<br>"input": {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "url",<br>      "value": "https://example.com/image.jpg"<br>    }<br>  }<br>```<br>Multiple items in one `content` object example (available in Elasticsearch 9.5.0 and later):<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "content": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "image",<br>        "format": "base64",<br>        "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "type": "text",<br>        "value": "Some text to create an embedding"<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>]<br>```|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference._types.EmbeddingStringInput](#schemainference._types.embeddingstringinput)|false|Allows specifying text-only inputs for the `embedding` task.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference._types.EmbeddingContentInput](#schemainference._types.embeddingcontentinput)|false|Allows specifying multimodal inputs for the `embedding` task.|
|» input_type|body|string|false|The input data type for the embedding model. Possible values include:<br>* `SEARCH`<br>* `INGEST`<br>* `CLASSIFICATION`<br>* `CLUSTERING`<br><br>Not all models support all values. Unsupported values will trigger a validation exception.<br>Accepted values depend on the configured inference service, refer to the relevant service-specific documentation for more info.<br><br>> info<br>> The `input_type` parameter specified on the root level of the request body will take precedence over the `input_type` parameter specified in `task_settings`.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request. These settings are specific to the <task_type> you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

## Perform non-streaming chat completion inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-non-streaming-chat-completion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/chat_completion/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"model\": \"gpt-4o\",\n  \"messages\": [\n      {\n          \"role\": \"user\",\n          \"content\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n      }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_inference/chat_completion/{inference_id}`

The chat completion inference API enables rich responses for chat completion tasks.
It only works with the `chat_completion` task type.

NOTE: The `chat_completion` task type supports both streaming and non-streaming.
The Chat completion inference API provides more comprehensive customization options through more fields and function calling support.
To determine whether a given inference service supports this task type, please see the page for that service.

These services support non-streaming chat completion inference:
- AI21
- Azure OpenAI
- Deepseek
- Elastic
- FireworksAI
- Groq
- Huggingface
- IBMWatsonX
- Llama
- Mistral
- NVIDIA
- OpenAI
- OpenShiftAI

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"model\": \"gpt-4o\",\n  \"messages\": [\n      {\n          \"role\": \"user\",\n          \"content\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n      }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-non-streaming-chat-completion-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The inference Id|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|[inference._types.RequestChatCompletion](#schemainference._types.requestchatcompletion)|true|none|
|» messages|body|[[inference._types.Message](#schemainference._types.message)]|true|A list of objects representing the conversation.<br>Requests should generally only add new messages from the user (role `user`).<br>The other message roles (`assistant`, `system`, or `tool`) should generally only be copied from the response to a previous completion request, such that the messages array is built up throughout a conversation.|
|» model|body|string|false|The ID of the model to use. By default, the model ID is set to the value included when creating the inference endpoint.|
|» max_completion_tokens|body|number|false|The upper bound limit for the number of tokens that can be generated for a completion request.|
|» reasoning|body|object|false|The reasoning configuration for the completion request.<br>This controls the model's reasoning process in one of two ways:<br><br>* By specifying the model’s reasoning effort level with the `effort` field.<br>* By enabling reasoning with default settings by setting `enabled` field to `true`.<br><br>It also includes optional settings to control:<br><br>* The level of detail in the summary returned in the response with the `summary` field.<br>* Whether reasoning details are included in the response at all with the `exclude` field.<br><br>Example (effort):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "effort": "high",<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Example (enabled):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "enabled": true,<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.|
|» » effort|body|object|false|The level of effort the model should put into reasoning.<br>This is a hint that guides the model in how much effort to put into reasoning,<br>with `xhigh` being the most effort and `none` being no effort.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable reasoning with default settings.<br>This is a shortcut for enabling reasoning without having to specify the other parameters.<br>If `enabled` is set to `true`, then reasoning at the `medium` effort level is enabled.<br>Ignored if `effort` is specified,<br>in which case that parameter will control the reasoning process instead.|
|» » exclude|body|boolean|false|Whether to exclude reasoning information from the response.<br>If `true`, the response will not include any reasoning details.|
|» » summary|body|object|false|The level of detail included in the reasoning summary returned in the response.<br>This is a hint on how much detail to include in the summary of the reasoning that is returned in the response,<br>with `auto` being the default level of detail, `concise` being less detail, and `detailed` being more detail.|
|» stop|body|[string]|false|A sequence of strings to control when the model should stop generating additional tokens.|
|» temperature|body|number|false|The sampling temperature to use.|
|» tool_choice|body|object|false|Controls which tool is called by the model.<br>String representation: One of `auto`, `none`, or `requrired`. `auto` allows the model to choose between calling tools and generating a message. `none` causes the model to not call any tools. `required` forces the model to call one or more tools.<br>Example (object representation):<br>```<br>{<br>  "tool_choice": {<br>      "type": "function",<br>      "function": {<br>          "name": "get_current_weather"<br>      }<br>  }<br>}<br>```|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference._types.CompletionToolChoice](#schemainference._types.completiontoolchoice)|false|Controls which tool is called by the model.|
|» tools|body|[[inference._types.CompletionTool](#schemainference._types.completiontool)]|false|A list of tools that the model can call.<br>Example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>      {<br>          "type": "function",<br>          "function": {<br>              "name": "get_price_of_item",<br>              "description": "Get the current price of an item",<br>              "parameters": {<br>                  "type": "object",<br>                  "properties": {<br>                      "item": {<br>                          "id": "12345"<br>                      },<br>                      "unit": {<br>                          "type": "currency"<br>                      }<br>                  }<br>              }<br>          }<br>      }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```|
|» top_p|body|number|false|Nucleus sampling, an alternative to sampling with temperature.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"id\": \"chatcmpl-Ae0TWsy2VPnSfBbv5UztnSdYUMFP3\",\n  \"choices\": [\n    {\n      \"message\": {\n        \"content\": \"Elastic is a company that provides a range of software solutions for search, logging, security, and analytics, built around the open-source Elasticsearch engine.\",\n        \"role\": \"assistant\"\n      },\n      \"finish_reason\": \"stop\",\n      \"index\": 0\n    }\n  ],\n  \"model\": \"gpt-4o-2024-08-06\",\n  \"object\": \"chat.completion\",\n  \"usage\": {\n    \"completion_tokens\": 34,\n    \"prompt_tokens\": 14,\n    \"total_tokens\": 48,\n    \"prompt_tokens_details\": {\n      \"cached_tokens\": 0\n    },\n    \"completion_tokens_details\": {\n      \"reasoning_tokens\": 0\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-non-streaming-chat-completion-inference-on-the-service-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.ChatCompletionInferenceResult](#schemainference._types.chatcompletioninferenceresult)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a AI21 inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-ai21"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"service\": \"ai21\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"api_key\": \"ai21-api-key\",\n    \"model_id\": \"jamba-large\" \n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{ai21_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `ai21` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"service\": \"ai21\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"api_key\": \"ai21-api-key\",\n    \"model_id\": \"jamba-large\" \n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-ai21-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.Ai21TaskType](#schemainference._types.ai21tasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|ai21_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `ai21`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `ai21` service.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the AI21 models documentation for the list of supported models and versions.<br>Service has been tested and confirmed to be working for `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks with the following models:<br>* `jamba-mini`<br>* `jamba-large`|
|» » api_key|body|string|false|A valid API key for accessing AI21 API.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the AI21 API.<br>By default, the `ai21` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 200. Please refer to AI21 documentation for more details.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-ai21-inference-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfoAi21](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfoai21)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create an AlibabaCloud AI Search inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-alibabacloud"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"alibabacloud-ai-search\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"host\" : \"default-j01.platform-cn-shanghai.opensearch.aliyuncs.com\",\n        \"api_key\": \"AlibabaCloud-API-Key\",\n        \"service_id\": \"ops-qwen-turbo\",\n        \"workspace\" : \"default\"\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{alibabacloud_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `alibabacloud-ai-search` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"alibabacloud-ai-search\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"host\" : \"default-j01.platform-cn-shanghai.opensearch.aliyuncs.com\",\n        \"api_key\": \"AlibabaCloud-API-Key\",\n        \"service_id\": \"ops-qwen-turbo\",\n        \"workspace\" : \"default\"\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-alibabacloud-ai-search-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.AlibabaCloudTaskType](#schemainference._types.alibabacloudtasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|alibabacloud_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `sparse_embedding` or `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank` or `completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `alibabacloud-ai-search`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `alibabacloud-ai-search` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key for the AlibabaCloud AI Search API.|
|» » host|body|string|true|The name of the host address used for the inference task.<br>You can find the host address in the API keys section of the documentation.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from AlibabaCloud AI Search.<br>By default, the `alibabacloud-ai-search` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to `1000`.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » service_id|body|string|true|The name of the model service to use for the inference task.<br>The following service IDs are available for the `completion` task:<br><br>* `ops-qwen-turbo`<br>* `qwen-turbo`<br>* `qwen-plus`<br>* `qwen-max ÷ qwen-max-longcontext`<br><br>The following service ID is available for the `rerank` task:<br><br>* `ops-bge-reranker-larger`<br><br>The following service ID is available for the `sparse_embedding` task:<br><br>* `ops-text-sparse-embedding-001`<br><br>The following service IDs are available for the `text_embedding` task:<br><br>`ops-text-embedding-001`<br>`ops-text-embedding-zh-001`<br>`ops-text-embedding-en-001`<br>`ops-text-embedding-002`|
|» » workspace|body|string|true|The name of the workspace used for the inference task.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » input_type|body|string|false|For a `sparse_embedding` or `text_embedding` task, specify the type of input passed to the model.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `ingest` for storing document embeddings in a vector database.<br>* `search` for storing embeddings of search queries run against a vector database to find relevant documents.|
|» » return_token|body|boolean|false|For a `sparse_embedding` task, it affects whether the token name will be returned in the response.<br>It defaults to `false`, which means only the token ID will be returned in the response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|
|task_type|text_embedding|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-alibabacloud-ai-search-inference-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfoAlibabaCloudAI](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfoalibabacloudai)|

## Required authorization

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"amazonbedrock\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"access_key\": \"AWS-access-key\",\n        \"secret_key\": \"AWS-secret-key\",\n        \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n        \"provider\": \"amazontitan\",\n        \"model\": \"amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0\"\n    }\n}"
```
