|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `chat_completion` and `completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `amazonbedrock`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `amazonbedrock` service.|
|» » access_key|body|string|true|A valid AWS access key that has permissions to use Amazon Bedrock and access to models for inference requests.|
|» » model|body|string|true|The base model ID or an ARN to a custom model based on a foundational model.<br>The base model IDs can be found in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.<br>Note that the model ID must be available for the provider chosen and your IAM user must have access to the model.|
|» » provider|body|string|false|The model provider for your deployment.<br>Note that some providers may support only certain task types.<br>Supported providers include:<br><br>* `amazontitan` - available for `text_embedding` and `completion` task types<br>* `anthropic` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `ai21labs` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `cohere` - available for `chat_completion`, `completion` and `text_embedding` task types<br>* `meta` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `mistral` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types|
|» » region|body|string|true|The region that your model or ARN is deployed in.<br>The list of available regions per model can be found in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Amazon Bedrock.<br>By default, the `amazonbedrock` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 240.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » secret_key|body|string|true|A valid AWS secret key that is paired with the `access_key`.<br>For informationg about creating and managing access and secret keys, refer to the AWS documentation.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » max_new_tokens|body|number|false|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it sets the maximum number for the output tokens to be generated.|
|» » temperature|body|number|false|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it is a number between 0.0 and 1.0 that controls the apparent creativity of the results.<br>At temperature 0.0 the model is most deterministic, at temperature 1.0 most random.<br>It should not be used if `top_p` or `top_k` is specified.|
|» » top_k|body|number|false|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it limits samples to the top-K most likely words, balancing coherence and variability.<br>It is only available for anthropic, cohere, and mistral providers.<br>It is an alternative to `temperature`; it should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|
|» » top_p|body|number|false|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it is a number in the range of 0.0 to 1.0, to eliminate low-probability tokens.<br>Top-p uses nucleus sampling to select top tokens whose sum of likelihoods does not exceed a certain value, ensuring both variety and coherence.<br>It is an alternative to `temperature`; it should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|

## Create an Amazon SageMaker inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-amazonsagemaker"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/text_embedding/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"amazon_sagemaker\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"access_key\": \"AWS-access-key\",\n        \"secret_key\": \"AWS-secret-key\",\n        \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n        \"api\": \"elastic\",\n        \"endpoint_name\": \"my-endpoint\",\n        \"dimensions\": 384,\n        \"element_type\": \"float\"\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{amazonsagemaker_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `amazon_sagemaker` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"amazon_sagemaker\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"access_key\": \"AWS-access-key\",\n        \"secret_key\": \"AWS-secret-key\",\n        \"region\": \"us-east-1\",\n        \"api\": \"elastic\",\n        \"endpoint_name\": \"my-endpoint\",\n        \"dimensions\": 384,\n        \"element_type\": \"float\"\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-amazon-sagemaker-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.TaskTypeAmazonSageMaker](#schemainference._types.tasktypeamazonsagemaker)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|amazonsagemaker_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `sparse_embedding` or `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `amazon_sagemaker`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model.<br>These settings are specific to the `amazon_sagemaker` service and `service_settings.api` you specified.|
|» » access_key|body|string|true|A valid AWS access key that has permissions to use Amazon SageMaker and access to models for invoking requests.|
|» » endpoint_name|body|string|true|The name of the SageMaker endpoint.|
|» » api|body|object|true|The API format to use when calling SageMaker.<br>Elasticsearch will convert the POST _inference request to this data format when invoking the SageMaker endpoint.|
|» » region|body|string|true|The region that your endpoint or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) is deployed in.<br>The list of available regions per model can be found in the Amazon SageMaker documentation.|
|» » secret_key|body|string|true|A valid AWS secret key that is paired with the `access_key`.<br>For information about creating and managing access and secret keys, refer to the AWS documentation.|
|» » similarity|body|object|false|Required when `api` is `elastic` and task type is `text_embedding`. The similarity measure used when invoking the<br>`text_embedding` task type.|
|» » element_type|body|object|false|Required when `api` is `elastic` and task type is `text_embedding`. The data type returned by the text embedding<br>model.<br>This value is used when parsing the response back to Elasticsearch data structures.|
|» » target_model|body|string|false|The model ID when calling a multi-model endpoint.|
|» » target_container_hostname|body|string|false|The container to directly invoke when calling a multi-container endpoint.|
|» » inference_component_name|body|string|false|The inference component to directly invoke when calling a multi-component endpoint.|
|» » batch_size|body|number|false|The maximum number of inputs in each batch. This value is used by inference ingestion pipelines<br>when processing semantic values. It correlates to the number of times the SageMaker endpoint is<br>invoked (one per batch of input).|
|» » dimensions|body|number|false|The number of dimensions returned by the text embedding models. If this value is not provided, then<br>it is guessed by making invoking the endpoint for the `text_embedding` task.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type and `service_settings.api` you specified.|
|» » custom_attributes|body|string|false|The AWS custom attributes passed verbatim through to the model running in the SageMaker Endpoint.<br>Values will be returned in the `X-elastic-sagemaker-custom-attributes` header.|
|» » enable_explanations|body|string|false|The optional JMESPath expression used to override the EnableExplanations provided during endpoint creation.|
|» » inference_id|body|string|false|The capture data ID when enabled in the endpoint.|
|» » session_id|body|string|false|The stateful session identifier for a new or existing session.<br>New sessions will be returned in the `X-elastic-sagemaker-new-session-id` header.<br>Closed sessions will be returned in the `X-elastic-sagemaker-closed-session-id` header.|
|» » target_variant|body|string|false|Specifies the variant when running with multi-variant Endpoints.|

## Create an Anthropic inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-anthropic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"anthropic\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"Anthropic-Api-Key\",\n        \"model_id\": \"claude-sonnet-4-5\"\n    },\n    \"task_settings\": {\n        \"max_tokens\": 1024\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{anthropic_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `anthropic` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"anthropic\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"Anthropic-Api-Key\",\n        \"model_id\": \"claude-sonnet-4-5\"\n    },\n    \"task_settings\": {\n        \"max_tokens\": 1024\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-anthropic-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.AnthropicTaskType](#schemainference._types.anthropictasktype)|true|The task type.<br>The valid task types for the model to perform are `completion` and `chat_completion`.<br>NOTE: The `chat_completion` task type only supports streaming and only through the _stream API.|
|anthropic_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `anthropic`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `anthropic` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key for the Anthropic API.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the Anthropic documentation for the list of supported models.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Anthropic.<br>By default, the `anthropic` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 50.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » max_tokens|body|number|true|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it is the maximum number of tokens to generate before stopping.|
|» » temperature|body|number|false|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it is the amount of randomness injected into the response.<br>For more details about the supported range, refer to Anthropic documentation.|
|» » top_k|body|number|false|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it specifies to only sample from the top K options for each subsequent token.<br>It is recommended for advanced use cases only.<br>You usually only need to use `temperature`.|
|» » top_p|body|number|false|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it specifies to use Anthropic's nucleus sampling.<br>In nucleus sampling, Anthropic computes the cumulative distribution over all the options for each subsequent token in decreasing probability order and cuts it off once it reaches the specified probability.<br>You should either alter `temperature` or `top_p`, but not both.<br>It is recommended for advanced use cases only.<br>You usually only need to use `temperature`.|

|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key of your Azure AI Studio model deployment.<br>This key can be found on the overview page for your deployment in the management section of your Azure AI Studio account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|

|» » do_sample|body|number|false|For a `completion` task, instruct the inference process to perform sampling.<br>It has no effect unless `temperature` or `top_p` is specified.|

|» » temperature|body|number|false|For a `completion` task, control the apparent creativity of generated completions with a sampling temperature.<br>It must be a number in the range of 0.0 to 2.0.<br>It should not be used if `top_p` is specified.|
|» » top_p|body|number|false|For a `completion` task, make the model consider the results of the tokens with nucleus sampling probability.<br>It is an alternative value to `temperature` and must be a number in the range of 0.0 to 2.0.<br>It should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|
|» » user|body|string|false|For a `text_embedding` task, specify the user issuing the request.<br>This information can be used for abuse detection.|
|» » return_documents|body|boolean|false|For a `rerank` task, return doc text within the results.|
|» » top_n|body|number|false|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.|

## Create an Azure OpenAI inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-azureopenai"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"azureopenai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"Api-Key\",\n        \"resource_name\": \"Resource-name\",\n        \"deployment_id\": \"Deployment-id\",\n        \"api_version\": \"2024-02-01\"\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{azureopenai_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `azureopenai` service.

The list of chat completion models that you can choose from in your Azure OpenAI deployment include:

* [GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models?tabs=global-standard%2Cstandard-chat-completions#gpt-4-and-gpt-4-turbo-models)
* [GPT-3.5](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models?tabs=global-standard%2Cstandard-chat-completions#gpt-35)

The list of embeddings models that you can choose from in your deployment can be found in the [Azure models documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models?tabs=global-standard%2Cstandard-chat-completions#embeddings).

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"azureopenai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"Api-Key\",\n        \"resource_name\": \"Resource-name\",\n        \"deployment_id\": \"Deployment-id\",\n        \"api_version\": \"2024-02-01\"\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-azure-openai-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.AzureOpenAITaskType](#schemainference._types.azureopenaitasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.<br>NOTE: The `chat_completion` task type only supports streaming and only through the _stream API.|
|azureopenai_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `completion` and `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `azureopenai`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `azureopenai` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|false|A valid API key for your Azure OpenAI account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » api_version|body|string|true|The Azure API version ID to use.<br>It is recommended to use the latest supported non-preview version.|
|» » client_id|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application ID that's assigned to your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » client_secret|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application secret that you created in the Microsoft app registration portal for your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » deployment_id|body|string|true|The deployment name of your deployed models.<br>Your Azure OpenAI deployments can be found though the Azure OpenAI Studio portal that is linked to your subscription.|
|» » entra_id|body|string|false|A valid Microsoft Entra token.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Azure.<br>The `azureopenai` service sets a default number of requests allowed per minute depending on the task type.<br>For `text_embedding`, it is set to `1440`.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion`, it is set to `120`.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » resource_name|body|string|true|The name of your Azure OpenAI resource.<br>You can find this from the list of resources in the Azure Portal for your subscription.|
|» » scopes|body|[string]|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The resource identifier (application ID URI) of the resource you want, suffixed with .default<br>For example:<br>```<br>"scopes": [<br>  "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"<br>]<br>```<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » tenant_id|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The directory tenant the application plans to operate against.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » user|body|string|false|Specifies the user issuing the request.<br>This information can be used for abuse detection.|
|» » headers|body|object|false|Specifies custom HTTP header parameters.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"headers": {<br>  "Custom-Header": "Some-Value",<br>  "Another-Custom-Header": "Another-Value"<br>}<br>```|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|text_embedding|

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{cohere_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `cohere` service.

|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|

|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `cohere`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model.<br>These settings are specific to the `cohere` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key for your Cohere account.<br>You can find or create your Cohere API keys on the Cohere API key settings page.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » embedding_type|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the types of embeddings you want to get back.<br>Use `binary` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision.<br>Use `bit` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision (this is a synonym of `binary`).<br>Use `byte` for signed int8 embeddings (this is a synonym of `int8`).<br>Use `float` for the default float embeddings.<br>Use `int8` for signed int8 embeddings.|

|» » similarity|body|object|false|The similarity measure.<br>If the `embedding_type` is `float`, the default value is `dot_product`.<br>If the `embedding_type` is `int8` or `byte`, the default value is `cosine`.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|

|» » return_documents|body|boolean|false|For a `rerank` task, return doc text within the results.|
|» » top_n|body|number|false|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.<br>If this inference endpoint is used in a `text_similarity_reranker` retriever query and `top_n` is set, it must be greater than or equal to `rank_window_size` in the query.|

## Create a custom inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-custom"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/text_embedding/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"custom\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"secret_parameters\": {\n            \"api_key\": \"<api key>\"\n        },\n        \"url\": \"https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings\",\n        \"headers\": {\n            \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ${api_key}\",\n            \"Content-Type\": \"application/json;charset=utf-8\"\n        },\n        \"request\": \"{\\\"input\\\": ${input}, \\\"model\\\": \\\"text-embedding-3-small\\\"}\",\n        \"response\": {\n            \"json_parser\": {\n                \"text_embeddings\": \"$.data[*].embedding[*]\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{custom_inference_id}`

The custom service gives more control over how to interact with external inference services that aren't explicitly supported through dedicated integrations.
The custom service gives you the ability to define the headers, url, query parameters, request body, and secrets.
The custom service supports the template replacement functionality, which enables you to define a template that can be replaced with the value associated with that key.
Templates are portions of a string that start with `${` and end with `}`.
The parameters `secret_parameters` and `task_settings` are checked for keys for template replacement. Template replacement is supported in the `request`, `headers`, `url`, and `query_parameters`.
If the definition (key) is not found for a template, an error message is returned.
In case of an endpoint definition like the following:
```
PUT _inference/text_embedding/test-text-embedding
{
  "service": "custom",
  "service_settings": {
     "secret_parameters": {
          "api_key": "<some api key>"
     },
     "url": "...endpoints.huggingface.cloud/v1/embeddings",
     "headers": {
         "Authorization": "Bearer ${api_key}",
         "Content-Type": "application/json"
     },
     "request": "{\"input\": ${input}}",
     "response": {
         "json_parser": {
             "text_embeddings":"$.data[*].embedding[*]"
         }
     }
  }
}
```
To replace `${api_key}` the `secret_parameters` and `task_settings` are checked for a key named `api_key`.

> info
> Templates should not be surrounded by quotes.

Pre-defined templates:
* `${input}` refers to the array of input strings that comes from the `input` field of the subsequent inference requests.
* `${input_type}` refers to the input type translation values.
* `${query}` refers to the query field used specifically for reranking tasks.
* `${top_n}` refers to the `top_n` field available when performing rerank requests.
* `${return_documents}` refers to the `return_documents` field available when performing rerank requests.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"custom\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"secret_parameters\": {\n            \"api_key\": \"<api key>\"\n        },\n        \"url\": \"https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings\",\n        \"headers\": {\n            \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ${api_key}\",\n            \"Content-Type\": \"application/json;charset=utf-8\"\n        },\n        \"request\": \"{\\\"input\\\": ${input}, \\\"model\\\": \\\"text-embedding-3-small\\\"}\",\n        \"response\": {\n            \"json_parser\": {\n                \"text_embeddings\": \"$.data[*].embedding[*]\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.CustomTaskType](#schemainference._types.customtasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|custom_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `sparse_embedding` or `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank` or `completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|

|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `custom`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model.<br>These settings are specific to the `custom` service.|
|» » batch_size|body|number|false|Specifies the batch size used for the semantic_text field. If the field is not provided, the default is 10.<br>The batch size is the maximum number of inputs in a single request to the upstream service.<br>The chunk within the batch are controlled by the selected chunking strategy for the semantic_text field.|
|» » headers|body|object|false|Specifies the HTTP header parameters – such as `Authorization` or `Content-Type` – that are required to access the custom service.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"headers": {<br>  "Authorization": "Bearer ${api_key}",<br>  "Content-Type": "application/json;charset=utf-8"<br>}<br>```|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » input_type|body|object|false|Specifies the input type translation values that are used to replace the `${input_type}` template in the request body.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"input_type": {<br>  "translation": {<br>    "ingest": "do_ingest",<br>    "search": "do_search"<br>  },<br>  "default": "a_default"<br>},<br>```<br>If the subsequent inference requests come from a search context, the `search` key will be used and the template will be replaced with `do_search`.<br>If it comes from the ingest context `do_ingest` is used. If it's a different context that is not specified, the default value will be used. If no default is specified an empty string is used.<br>`translation` can be:<br>* `classification`<br>* `clustering`<br>* `ingest`<br>* `search`|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » query_parameters|body|[[inference._types.CustomServiceQueryParameter](#schemainference._types.customservicequeryparameter)]|false|Specifies the query parameters as a list of tuples. The arrays inside the `query_parameters` must have two items, a key and a value.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"query_parameters":[<br>  ["param_key", "some_value"],<br>  ["param_key", "another_value"],<br>  ["other_key", "other_value"]<br>]<br>```<br>If the base url is `https://www.elastic.co` it results in: `https://www.elastic.co?param_key=some_value&param_key=another_value&other_key=other_value`.|

|» » » content|body|string|true|The body structure of the request. It requires passing in the string-escaped result of the JSON format HTTP request body.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"request": "{\"input\":${input}}"<br>```<br>> info<br>> The content string needs to be a single line except when using the Kibana console.|
|» » response|body|object|true|The response configuration object.|

## Create an Elasticsearch inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-elasticsearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/rerank/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"elasticsearch\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"adaptive_allocations\": { \n        \"enabled\": true,\n        \"min_number_of_allocations\": 1,\n        \"max_number_of_allocations\": 4\n        },\n        \"num_threads\": 1,\n        \"model_id\": \".elser_model_2\" \n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{elasticsearch_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `elasticsearch` service.

> info
> Your Elasticsearch deployment contains preconfigured ELSER and E5 inference endpoints, you only need to create the enpoints using the API if you want to customize the settings.

If you use the ELSER or the E5 model through the `elasticsearch` service, the API request will automatically download and deploy the model if it isn't downloaded yet.

> info
> You might see a 502 bad gateway error in the response when using the Kibana Console. This error usually just reflects a timeout, while the model downloads in the background. You can check the download progress in the Machine Learning UI. If using the Python client, you can set the timeout parameter to a higher value.

After creating the endpoint, wait for the model deployment to complete before using it.
To verify the deployment status, use the get trained model statistics API.
Look for `"state": "fully_allocated"` in the response and ensure that the `"allocation_count"` matches the `"target_allocation_count"`.
Avoid creating multiple endpoints for the same model unless required, as each endpoint consumes significant resources.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"elasticsearch\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"adaptive_allocations\": { \n        \"enabled\": true,\n        \"min_number_of_allocations\": 1,\n        \"max_number_of_allocations\": 4\n        },\n        \"num_threads\": 1,\n        \"model_id\": \".elser_model_2\" \n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-elasticsearch-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.ElasticsearchTaskType](#schemainference._types.elasticsearchtasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|elasticsearch_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.<br>The must not match the `model_id`.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `sparse_embedding` and `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank` task type.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `elasticsearch`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `elasticsearch` service.|
|» » adaptive_allocations|body|object|false|Adaptive allocations configuration details.<br>If `enabled` is true, the number of allocations of the model is set based on the current load the process gets.<br>When the load is high, a new model allocation is automatically created, respecting the value of `max_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>When the load is low, a model allocation is automatically removed, respecting the value of `min_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>If `enabled` is true, do not set the number of allocations manually.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Turn on `adaptive_allocations`.|
|» » » max_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|The maximum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to `min_number_of_allocations`.|
|» » » min_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|The minimum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to 0.<br>If not defined, the deployment scales to 0.|
|» » deployment_id|body|string|false|The deployment identifier for a trained model deployment.<br>When `deployment_id` is used the `model_id` is optional.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>It can be the ID of a built-in model (for example, `.multilingual-e5-small` for E5) or a text embedding model that was uploaded by using the Eland client.|
|» » num_allocations|body|number|false|The total number of allocations that are assigned to the model across machine learning nodes.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the throughput.<br>If adaptive allocations are enabled, do not set this value because it's automatically set.|
|» » num_threads|body|number|true|The number of threads used by each model allocation during inference.<br>This setting generally increases the speed per inference request.<br>The inference process is a compute-bound process; `threads_per_allocations` must not exceed the number of available allocated processors per node.<br>The value must be a power of 2.<br>The maximum value is 32.|
|» » long_document_strategy|body|string|false|Available only for the `rerank` task type using the Elastic reranker model.<br>Controls the strategy used for processing long documents during inference.<br><br>Possible values:<br>- `truncate` (default): Processes only the beginning of each document.<br>- `chunk`: Splits long documents into smaller parts (chunks) before inference.<br><br>When `long_document_strategy` is set to `chunk`, Elasticsearch splits each document into smaller parts but still returns a single score per document.<br>That score reflects the highest relevance score among all chunks.|
|» » max_chunks_per_doc|body|number|false|Only for the `rerank` task type.<br>Limits the number of chunks per document that are sent for inference when chunking is enabled.<br>If not set, all chunks generated for the document are processed.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » return_documents|body|boolean|false|For a `rerank` task, return the document instead of only the index.|

|Parameter|Value|

|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|
|task_type|text_embedding|

> Example responses

## Create an ELSER inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-elser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/sparse_embedding/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"elser\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"num_allocations\": 1,\n        \"num_threads\": 1\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{elser_inference_id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `elser` service.
You can also deploy ELSER by using the Elasticsearch inference integration.

> info
> Your Elasticsearch deployment contains a preconfigured ELSER inference endpoint, you only need to create the enpoint using the API if you want to customize the settings.

The API request will automatically download and deploy the ELSER model if it isn't already downloaded.

> info
> You might see a 502 bad gateway error in the response when using the Kibana Console. This error usually just reflects a timeout, while the model downloads in the background. You can check the download progress in the Machine Learning UI. If using the Python client, you can set the timeout parameter to a higher value.

After creating the endpoint, wait for the model deployment to complete before using it.
To verify the deployment status, use the get trained model statistics API.
Look for `"state": "fully_allocated"` in the response and ensure that the `"allocation_count"` matches the `"target_allocation_count"`.
Avoid creating multiple endpoints for the same model unless required, as each endpoint consumes significant resources.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"elser\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"num_allocations\": 1,\n        \"num_threads\": 1\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-elser-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.ElserTaskType](#schemainference._types.elsertasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|elser_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Note that for ELSER endpoints, the max_chunk_size may not exceed `300`.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `elser`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `elser` service.|
|» » adaptive_allocations|body|object|false|Adaptive allocations configuration details.<br>If `enabled` is true, the number of allocations of the model is set based on the current load the process gets.<br>When the load is high, a new model allocation is automatically created, respecting the value of `max_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>When the load is low, a model allocation is automatically removed, respecting the value of `min_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>If `enabled` is true, do not set the number of allocations manually.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Turn on `adaptive_allocations`.|
|» » » max_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|The maximum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to `min_number_of_allocations`.|
|» » » min_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|The minimum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to 0.<br>If not defined, the deployment scales to 0.|
|» » num_allocations|body|number|true|The total number of allocations this model is assigned across machine learning nodes.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the throughput.<br>If adaptive allocations is enabled, do not set this value because it's automatically set.|
|» » num_threads|body|number|true|The number of threads used by each model allocation during inference.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the speed per inference request.<br>The inference process is a compute-bound process; `threads_per_allocations` must not exceed the number of available allocated processors per node.<br>The value must be a power of 2.<br>The maximum value is 32.<br><br>> info<br>> If you want to optimize your ELSER endpoint for ingest, set the number of threads to 1. If you want to optimize your ELSER endpoint for search, set the number of threads to greater than 1.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|

```

In this mode, do not set `url` or `streaming_url` and Elastic will construct the endpoint url from `location`, `model_id`, and `project_id` parameters.|
|» » url|body|string|false|The URL for non-streaming `completion` requests to a Google Model Garden provider endpoint.<br>If both `url` and `streaming_url` are provided, each is used for its respective mode.<br>If `streaming_url` is not provided, `url` is also used for streaming `completion` and `chat_completion`.<br>If `provider` is not provided or set to `google` (Google Vertex AI), do not set `url` (or `streaming_url`).<br>At least one of `url` or `streaming_url` must be provided for Google Model Garden endpoint usage.<br>Certain providers require separate URLs for streaming and non-streaming operations (e.g., Anthropic, Mistral, AI21). Others support both operation types through a single URL (e.g., Meta, Hugging Face).<br>Information on constructing the URL for various providers can be found in the Google Model Garden documentation for the model, or on the endpoint’s `Sample request` page. The request examples also illustrate the proper formatting for the `url`.|
|» » streaming_url|body|string|false|The URL for streaming `completion` and `chat_completion` requests to a Google Model Garden provider endpoint.<br>If both `streaming_url` and `url` are provided, each is used for its respective mode.<br>If `url` is not provided, `streaming_url` is also used for non-streaming `completion` requests.<br>If `provider` is not provided or set to `google` (Google Vertex AI), do not set `streaming_url` (or `url`).<br>At least one of `streaming_url` or `url` must be provided for Google Model Garden endpoint usage.<br>Certain providers require separate URLs for streaming and non-streaming operations (e.g., Anthropic, Mistral, AI21). Others support both operation types through a single URL (e.g., Meta, Hugging Face).<br>Information on constructing the URL for various providers can be found in the Google Model Garden documentation for the model, or on the endpoint’s `Sample request` page. The request examples also illustrate the proper formatting for the `streaming_url`.|
|» » location|body|string|false|The name of the location to use for the inference task for the Google Vertex AI inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI, when `provider` is omitted or `google`, `location` is optional.<br>When `location` is omitted, the request targets the Google Vertex AI global endpoint (`https://aiplatform.googleapis.com`); when it is provided, the corresponding regional endpoint (`https://<location>-aiplatform.googleapis.com`) is used.<br>The field must be omitted to select the global endpoint; an empty string is not a valid `location`.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `location` is ignored.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for the list of supported locations.|
|» » model_id|body|string|false|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI `model_id` is mandatory.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `model_id` will be used for some providers that require it, otherwise - ignored.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for the list of supported models for Google Vertex AI.|
|» » project_id|body|string|false|The name of the project to use for the Google Vertex AI inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI `project_id` is mandatory.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `project_id` is ignored.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Google Vertex AI.<br>By default, the `googlevertexai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 30.000.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » service_account_json|body|string|true|A valid service account in JSON format for the Google Vertex AI API.|
|» » dimensions|body|number|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>By default, the model's standard output dimension is used.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for more information.|
|» » max_batch_size|body|number|false|Only applicable for the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Controls the batch size of chunked inference requests sent to Google Vertex AI.<br><br>Setting this parameter lower reduces the risk of exceeding token limits but may result in more API calls. Setting it higher increases throughput but may risk hitting token limits.<br><br>To estimate a safe `max_batch_size` value, you can use it together with the `max_chunk_size` parameter using the following formula:<br>`max_batch_size ≈ max_chunk_size × 1.3 × 512 ÷ 20000`<br><br>Where:<br>- `1.3` is an approximate tokens-per-word ratio<br>- `512` is the maximum number of chunks that can be generated per document<br>- `20000` is the Google Vertex AI token limit per request<br><br>This estimate assumes the worst-case scenario with a document generating the maximum 512 chunks.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » auto_truncate|body|boolean|false|For a `text_embedding` task, truncate inputs longer than the maximum token length automatically.|
|» » top_n|body|number|false|For a `rerank` task, the number of the top N documents that should be returned.|
|» » thinking_config|body|object|false|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, allows configuration of the thinking features for the model.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for the allowable configurations for each model type.|
|» » » thinking_budget|body|number|false|Indicates the desired thinking budget in tokens.|
|» » max_tokens|body|number|false|For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, specifies the `max_tokens` value for requests sent to the Google Model Garden `anthropic` provider.<br>If `provider` is not set to `anthropic`, this field is ignored.<br>If `max_tokens` is specified - it must be a positive integer. If not specified, the default value of 1024 is used.<br>Anthropic models require `max_tokens` to be set for each request. Please refer to the Anthropic documentation for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|

  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

## Create a Groq inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-groq"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/chat_completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"service\": \"groq\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"api_key\": \"groq-api-key\",\n    \"model_id\": \"llama-3.3-70b-versatile\" \n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{groq_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `groq` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"service\": \"groq\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"api_key\": \"groq-api-key\",\n    \"model_id\": \"llama-3.3-70b-versatile\" \n  }\n}"
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `groq`.|

|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the Groq model documentation for the list of supported models and versions.<br>Service has been tested and confirmed to be working for `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks with the following models:<br>* `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`|
|» » api_key|body|string|false|A valid API key for accessing Groq API.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Groq API.<br>By default, the `groq` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 1000. Refer to Groq documentation for more details.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|

## Create a Hugging Face inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-hugging-face"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/chat_completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"hugging_face\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"hugging-face-access-token\", \n        \"url\": \"url-endpoint\" \n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{huggingface_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `hugging_face` service.
Supported tasks include: `text_embedding`, `completion`, and `chat_completion`.

To configure the endpoint, first visit the Hugging Face Inference Endpoints page and create a new endpoint.
Select a model that supports the task you intend to use.

For Elastic's `text_embedding` task:
The selected model must support the `Sentence Embeddings` task. On the new endpoint creation page, select the `Sentence Embeddings` task under the `Advanced Configuration` section.
After the endpoint has initialized, copy the generated endpoint URL.
Recommended models for `text_embedding` task:

* `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`
* `all-MiniLM-L12-v2`
* `all-mpnet-base-v2`
* `e5-base-v2`
* `e5-small-v2`
* `multilingual-e5-base`
* `multilingual-e5-small`

For Elastic's `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks:
The selected model must support the `Text Generation` task and expose OpenAI API. HuggingFace supports both serverless and dedicated endpoints for `Text Generation`. When creating dedicated endpoint select the `Text Generation` task.
After the endpoint is initialized (for dedicated) or ready (for serverless), ensure it supports the OpenAI API and includes `/v1/chat/completions` part in URL. Then, copy the full endpoint URL for use.
Recommended models for `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks:

* `Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2`
* `QwQ-32B`
* `Phi-3-mini-128k-instruct`

For Elastic's `rerank` task:
The selected model must support the `sentence-ranking` task and expose OpenAI API.
HuggingFace supports only dedicated (not serverless) endpoints for `Rerank` so far.
After the endpoint is initialized, copy the full endpoint URL for use.
Tested models for `rerank` task:

* `bge-reranker-base`
* `jina-reranker-v1-turbo-en-GGUF`

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"hugging_face\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"hugging-face-access-token\", \n        \"url\": \"url-endpoint\" \n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-hugging-face-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.HuggingFaceTaskType](#schemainference._types.huggingfacetasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|huggingface_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `hugging_face`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `hugging_face` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid access token for your HuggingFace account.<br>You can create or find your access tokens on the HuggingFace settings page.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Hugging Face.<br>By default, the `hugging_face` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 3000 for all supported tasks.<br>Hugging Face does not publish a universal rate limit — actual limits may vary.<br>It is recommended to adjust this value based on the capacity and limits of your specific deployment environment.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, the deployed model must be compatible with the Hugging Face Chat Completion interface (see the linked external documentation for details). The endpoint URL for the request must include `/v1/chat/completions`.<br>If the model supports the OpenAI Chat Completion schema, a toggle should appear in the interface. Enabling this toggle doesn't change any model behavior, it reveals the full endpoint URL needed (which should include `/v1/chat/completions`) when configuring the inference endpoint in Elasticsearch. If the model doesn't support this schema, the toggle may not be shown.|
|» » model_id|body|string|false|The name of the HuggingFace model to use for the inference task.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, this field is optional but may be required for certain models — particularly when using serverless inference endpoints.<br>For the `text_embedding` task, this field should not be included. Otherwise, the request will fail.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » return_documents|body|boolean|false|For a `rerank` task, return doc text within the results.|
|» » top_n|body|number|false|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|text_embedding|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-hugging-face-inference-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfoHuggingFace](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfohuggingface)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{jinaai_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `jinaai` service.

To review the available `rerank` models, refer to <https://jina.ai/reranker>.
To review the available `embedding` and `text_embedding` models, refer to <https://jina.ai/embeddings/>.

"{\n    \"service\": \"jinaai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"model_id\": \"jina-embeddings-v3\",\n        \"api_key\": \"JinaAi-Api-key\"\n    }\n}"

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
