|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `embedding` and text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank` task type.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `jinaai`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `jinaai` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key of your JinaAI account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from JinaAI.<br>By default, the `jinaai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 2000 for all task types.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » similarity|body|object|false|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.<br>The default values varies with the embedding type.<br>For example, a float embedding type uses a `dot_product` similarity measure by default.|
|» » dimensions|body|number|false|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>By default, the model's standard output dimension is used.<br>Refer to the Jina documentation for more information.|
|» » embedding_type|body|object|false|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the data type returned by the model.<br>Use `bit` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision.<br>Use `binary` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision (this is a synonym of `bit`).<br>Use `float` for the default float embeddings.|
|» » multimodal_model|body|boolean|false|For the `embedding` task, whether the model supports multimodal inputs. If true, requests sent to the Jina model<br>will use the multimodal request format (a list of objects). If false, requests sent to the model will use the same<br>format as the `text_embedding` task (a list of strings). Setting this to `false` allows the `embedding` task to be<br>used with models that do not support multimodal requests.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » return_documents|body|boolean|false|For a `rerank` task, return the doc text within the results.|
|» » input_type|body|object|false|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the task passed to the model.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `classification`: Use it for embeddings passed through a classifier.<br>* `clustering`: Use it for the embeddings run through a clustering algorithm.<br>* `ingest`: Use it for storing document embeddings in a vector database.<br>* `search`: Use it for storing embeddings of search queries run against a vector database to find relevant documents.|
|» » late_chunking|body|boolean|false|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, controls when text is split into chunks.<br>When set to `true`, a request from Elasticsearch contains only chunks related to a single document. Instead of batching chunks across documents, Elasticsearch sends them in separate requests. This ensures that chunk embeddings retain context from the entire document, improving semantic quality.<br><br>If a document exceeds the model's context limits, or if the document contains non-text inputs (relevant when using the multimodal `embedding` task), late chunking is automatically disabled for that document only and standard chunking is used instead.<br><br>If not specified, defaults to `false`.|
|» » top_n|body|number|false|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.<br>If this inference endpoint is used in a `text_similarity_reranker` retriever query and `top_n` is set, it must be greater than or equal to `rank_window_size` in the query.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|embedding|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|text_embedding|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n   \"inference_id\": \"jinaai-embeddings\",\n   \"task_type\": \"text_embedding\",\n   \"service\": \"jinaai\",\n   \"service_settings\": {\n       \"model_id\": \"jina-embeddings-v3\",\n       \"rate_limit\": {\n           \"requests_per_minute\": 2000\n       },\n       \"dimensions\": 1024,\n       \"embedding_type\": \"float\",\n       \"similarity\": \"dot_product\"\n   },\n   \"chunking_settings\": {\n       \"strategy\": \"sentence\",\n       \"max_chunk_size\": 250,\n       \"sentence_overlap\": 1\n   }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-jinaai-inference-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfoJinaAi](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfojinaai)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a Llama inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-llama"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/text_embedding/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"service\": \"llama\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"url\": \"http://localhost:8321/v1/inference/embeddings\",\n    \"dimensions\": 384,\n    \"model_id\": \"all-MiniLM-L6-v2\" \n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{llama_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `llama` service.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"service\": \"llama\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n    \"url\": \"http://localhost:8321/v1/inference/embeddings\",\n    \"dimensions\": 384,\n    \"model_id\": \"all-MiniLM-L6-v2\" \n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-llama-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.LlamaTaskType](#schemainference._types.llamatasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|llama_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `completion` or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `llama`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `llama` service.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL endpoint of the Llama stack endpoint.<br>URL must contain:<br>* For `text_embedding` task - `/v1/inference/embeddings`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `/v1/openai/v1/chat/completions`.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the Llama downloading models documentation for different ways of getting a list of available models and downloading them.<br>Service has been tested and confirmed to be working with the following models:<br>* For `text_embedding` task - `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `llama3.2:3b`.|
|» » max_input_tokens|body|number|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the maximum number of tokens per input before chunking occurs.|
|» » similarity|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Llama API.<br>By default, the `llama` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 3000.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfoLlama](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfollama)|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|

|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `nvidia`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `nvidia` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key for your Nvidia endpoint.<br>Can be found in `API Keys` section of Nvidia account settings.|
|» » url|body|string|false|The URL of the Nvidia model endpoint. If not provided, the default endpoint URL is used depending on the task type:<br><br>* For `text_embedding` task - `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/embeddings`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions`.<br>* For `rerank` task - `https://ai.api.nvidia.com/v1/retrieval/nvidia/reranking`.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the model's documentation for the name if needed.<br>Service has been tested and confirmed to be working with the following models:<br><br>* For `text_embedding` task - `nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-embedqa-1b-v2`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `microsoft/phi-3-mini-128k-instruct`.<br>* For `rerank` task - `nv-rerank-qa-mistral-4b:1`.<br>Service doesn't support `text_embedding` task `baai/bge-m3` and `nvidia/nvclip` models due to them not recognizing the `input_type` parameter.|
|» » max_input_tokens|body|number|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the maximum number of tokens per input. Inputs exceeding this value are truncated prior to sending to the Nvidia API.|
|» » similarity|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Nvidia API.<br>By default, the `nvidia` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 3000.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » input_type|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, type of input sent to the Nvidia endpoint.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `ingest`: Mapped to Nvidia's `passage` value in request. Used when generating embeddings during indexing.<br>* `search`: Mapped to Nvidia's `query` value in request. Used when generating embeddings during querying.<br><br>IMPORTANT: For Nvidia endpoints, if the `input_type` field is not specified, it defaults to `query`.|
|» » truncate|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the method used by the Nvidia model to handle inputs longer than the maximum token length.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `END`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the end of the input is discarded.<br>* `NONE`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, an error is returned.<br>* `START`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the start of the input is discarded.|

|task_type|completion|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|text_embedding|

## Create an OpenAI inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-openai"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/chat_completion/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"service\": \"openai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"OpenAI-API-Key\",\n        \"model_id\": \"text-embedding-3-small\",\n        \"dimensions\": 128\n    }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{openai_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `openai` service or `openai` compatible APIs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"openai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"api_key\": \"OpenAI-API-Key\",\n        \"model_id\": \"text-embedding-3-small\",\n        \"dimensions\": 128\n    }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-openai-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.OpenAITaskType](#schemainference._types.openaitasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.<br>NOTE: The `chat_completion` task type only supports streaming and only through the _stream API.|
|openai_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `completion` or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `openai`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `openai` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|false|A valid API key of your OpenAI account.<br>You can find your OpenAI API keys in your OpenAI account under the API keys section.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key` or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » client_id|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application ID that's assigned to your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » client_secret|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application secret that you created for your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key` or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » dimensions|body|number|false|For a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>It is supported only in `text-embedding-3` and later models.<br>If it is not set, the OpenAI defined default for the model is used.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the OpenAI documentation for the list of available text embedding models.|
|» » organization_id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for your organization.<br>You can find the Organization ID in your OpenAI account under *Settings > Organizations*.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from OpenAI.<br>The `openai` service sets a default number of requests allowed per minute depending on the task type.<br>For `text_embedding` and `embedding`, it is set to `3000`.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion`, it is set to `500`.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » scopes|body|[string]|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The resource identifier of the resource you want.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"scopes": [<br>  "scope1",<br>  "scope2"<br>]<br>```<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » similarity|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of `cosine`, `dot_product`, `l2_norm`. Defaults to `dot_product`.|
|» » token_url|body|string|false|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>An OAuth2 token endpoint where Elasticsearch sends a request to exchange client credentials for an access token.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|» » url|body|string|false|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.<br>It can be changed for testing purposes.<br>Default value is `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` for a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task,<br>`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` for a `completion` or `chat_completion` task.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Settings to configure the inference task.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified.|
|» » user|body|string|false|Specifies the user issuing the request.<br>This information can be used for abuse detection.|
|» » headers|body|object|false|Specifies custom HTTP header parameters.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"headers": {<br>  "Custom-Header": "Some-Value",<br>  "Another-Custom-Header": "Another-Value"<br>}<br>```|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|embedding|

```json
  },
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|

|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `openshift_ai`.|

|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key for your OpenShift AI endpoint.<br>Can be found in `Token authentication` section of model related information.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the OpenShift AI hosted model endpoint.|

|» » similarity|body|object|false|For a `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.<br>If not specified, the default dot_product value is used.|

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{voyageai_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `voyageai` service.

Avoid creating multiple endpoints for the same model unless required, as each endpoint consumes significant resources.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"service\": \"voyageai\",\n    \"service_settings\": {\n        \"model_id\": \"voyage-3-large\",\n        \"dimensions\": 512\n    }\n}"
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|

|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|

## Create a Watsonx inference endpoint

<a id="opIdinference-put-watsonx"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/text_embedding/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"service\": \"watsonxai\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n      \"api_key\": \"Watsonx-API-Key\", \n      \"url\": \"Wastonx-URL\", \n      \"model_id\": \"ibm/slate-30m-english-rtrvr\",\n      \"project_id\": \"IBM-Cloud-ID\", \n      \"api_version\": \"2024-03-14\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{watsonx_inference_id}`

Create an inference endpoint to perform an inference task with the `watsonxai` service.
You need an IBM Cloud Databases for Elasticsearch deployment to use the `watsonxai` inference service.
You can provision one through the IBM catalog, the Cloud Databases CLI plug-in, the Cloud Databases API, or Terraform.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"service\": \"watsonxai\",\n  \"service_settings\": {\n      \"api_key\": \"Watsonx-API-Key\", \n      \"url\": \"Wastonx-URL\", \n      \"model_id\": \"ibm/slate-30m-english-rtrvr\",\n      \"project_id\": \"IBM-Cloud-ID\", \n      \"api_version\": \"2024-03-14\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-watsonx-inference-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.WatsonxTaskType](#schemainference._types.watsonxtasktype)|true|The type of the inference task that the model will perform.|
|watsonx_inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion` or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|object|true|The type of service supported for the specified task type. In this case, `watsonxai`.|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings used to install the inference model. These settings are specific to the `watsonxai` service.|
|» » api_key|body|string|true|A valid API key of your Watsonx account.<br>You can find your Watsonx API keys or you can create a new one on the API keys page.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|» » api_version|body|string|true|A version parameter that takes a version date in the format of `YYYY-MM-DD`.<br>For the active version data parameters, refer to the Wastonx documentation.|
|» » model_id|body|string|true|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the IBM Embedding Models section in the Watsonx documentation for the list of available text embedding models.<br>Refer to the IBM library - Foundation models in Watsonx.ai.|
|» » project_id|body|string|true|The identifier of the IBM Cloud project to use for the inference task.|
|» » rate_limit|body|object|false|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Watsonx.<br>By default, the `watsonxai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 120.|
|» » » requests_per_minute|body|number|false|The number of requests allowed per minute.<br>By default, the number of requests allowed per minute is set by each service as follows:<br><br>* `alibabacloud-ai-search` service: `1000`<br>* `amazonbedrock` service: `240`<br>* `anthropic` service: `50`<br>* `azureaistudio` service: `240`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `1440`<br>* `azureopenai` service and task types `completion` or `chat_completion`: `120`<br>* `cohere` service: `10000`<br>* `contextualai` service: `1000`<br>* `elastic` service and task type `chat_completion`: `240`<br>* `fireworksai` service: `6000`<br>* `googleaistudio` service: `360`<br>* `googlevertexai` service: `30000`<br>* `hugging_face` service: `3000`<br>* `jinaai` service: `2000`<br>* `llama` service: `3000`<br>* `mistral` service: `240`<br>* `openai` service and task type `text_embedding`: `3000`<br>* `openai` service and task type `completion`: `500`<br>* `openshift_ai` service: `3000`<br>* `voyageai` service: `2000`<br>* `watsonxai` service: `120`|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the inference endpoint that you created on Watsonx.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|completion|

## Perform reranking inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-rerank"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/rerank/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"input\": [\"luke\", \"like\", \"leia\", \"chewy\",\"r2d2\", \"star\", \"wars\"],\n  \"query\": \"star wars main character\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_inference/rerank/{inference_id}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"input\": [\"luke\", \"like\", \"leia\", \"chewy\",\"r2d2\", \"star\", \"wars\"],\n  \"query\": \"star wars main character\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-reranking-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier for the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» query|body|object|true|Query input.<br>The query can be specified as a single string, or as an object.<br>The object form additionally allows specifying non-text inputs, such as images.<br><br>> info<br>> Only the `elastic` service currently supports non-text queries for the `rerank` task. For all other services, the query must be a string.<br><br>string example:<br>```<br>"query": "some query text"<br>```<br>object example:<br>```<br>"query": {<br>  "type": "image",<br>  "format": "base64",<br>  "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>}<br>```<br>object example using the `url` format (available in Elasticsearch 9.6.0 and later):<br>```<br>"query": {<br>  "type": "image",<br>  "format": "url",<br>  "value": "https://example.com/image.jpg"<br>}<br>```|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference.rerank.RerankInputObject](#schemainference.rerank.rerankinputobject)|false|An object describing a single input for the `rerank` task, which additionally allows specifying non-text inputs, such as images.|
|» input|body|object|true|The documents to rank.<br>The input can be specified as a single string or an array of strings, or as an object or an array of objects.<br>The object form additionally allows specifying non-text inputs, such as images.<br><br>> info<br>> Only the `elastic` service currently supports non-text inputs for the `rerank` task. For all other services, the input must be a string or an array of strings.<br><br>string example:<br>```<br>"input": "some document text"<br>```<br>string array example:<br>```<br>"input": ["some document text", "some more document text"]<br>```<br>object example:<br>```<br>"input": {<br>  "type": "image",<br>  "format": "base64",<br>  "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>}<br>```<br>object array example:<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "type": "text",<br>    "format": "text",<br>    "value": "some document text"<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "type": "image",<br>    "format": "base64",<br>    "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br>object array example using the `url` format (available in Elasticsearch 9.6.0 and later):<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "type": "image",<br>    "format": "url",<br>    "value": "https://example.com/image.jpg"<br>  }<br>]<br>```|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference.rerank.RerankStringInput](#schemainference.rerank.rerankstringinput)|false|Allows specifying text-only documents to rank for the `rerank` task.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inference.rerank.RerankObjectInput](#schemainference.rerank.rerankobjectinput)|false|Allows specifying documents to rank as objects, which additionally supports non-text inputs, such as images.|
|» return_documents|body|boolean|false|Include the document text in the response.|
|» top_n|body|number|false|Limit the response to the top N documents.|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request.<br>These settings are specific to the task type you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"rerank\": [\n    {\n      \"index\": \"2\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"0.011597361\",\n      \"text\": \"leia\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"0\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"0.006338922\",\n      \"text\": \"luke\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"5\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"0.0016166499\",\n      \"text\": \"star\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"4\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"0.0011695103\",\n      \"text\": \"r2d2\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"1\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"5.614787E-4\",\n      \"text\": \"like\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"6\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"3.7850367E-4\",\n      \"text\": \"wars\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"index\": \"3\",\n      \"relevance_score\": \"1.2508839E-5\",\n      \"text\": \"chewy\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Perform streaming completion inference on the service

<a id="opIdinference-stream-completion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_inference/completion/string/_stream \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"input\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_inference/completion/{inference_id}/_stream`

Get real-time responses for completion tasks by delivering answers incrementally, reducing response times during computation.
This API works only with the completion task type.

IMPORTANT: The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Azure, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face. For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models. However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

This API requires the `monitor_inference` cluster privilege (the built-in `inference_admin` and `inference_user` roles grant this privilege). You must use a client that supports streaming.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"input\": \"What is Elastic?\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="perform-streaming-completion-inference-on-the-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier for the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The amount of time to wait for the inference request to complete.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» input|body|string \| [string]|true|The text on which you want to perform the inference task.<br>It can be a single string or an array.<br><br>NOTE: Inference endpoints for the completion task type currently only support a single string as input.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings for the individual inference request. These settings are specific to the <task_type> you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

|200|OK||[_types.StreamResult](#schema_types.streamresult)|

|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|

```bash
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n \"service_settings\": {\n   \"api_key\": \"<API_KEY>\"\n },\n\"service\": \"example-service\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_inference/{task_type}/{inference_id}/_update`

Modify `task_settings`, secrets (within `service_settings`), or `num_allocations` for an inference endpoint, depending on the specific endpoint service and `task_type`.

IMPORTANT: The inference APIs enable you to use certain services, such as built-in machine learning models (ELSER, E5), models uploaded through Eland, Cohere, OpenAI, Azure, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, Watsonx.ai, or Hugging Face.
For built-in models and models uploaded through Eland, the inference APIs offer an alternative way to use and manage trained models.
However, if you do not plan to use the inference APIs to use these models or if you want to use non-NLP models, use the machine learning trained model APIs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_inference`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n \"service_settings\": {\n   \"api_key\": \"<API_KEY>\"\n },\n\"service\": \"example-service\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-an-inference-endpoint-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_type|path|[inference._types.TaskType](#schemainference._types.tasktype)|true|The type of inference task that the model performs.|
|inference_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the inference endpoint.|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the inference endpoint to be updated.<br>The default depends on the task type: 120s for `completion` and `chat_completion`, and 30s for all other task types.|
|body|body|[inference._types.InferenceEndpoint](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpoint)|true|none|
|» chunking_settings|body|object|false|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `embedding`, `sparse_embedding` and `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|» » max_chunk_size|body|number|false|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|» » overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|» » sentence_overlap|body|number|false|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|» » separator_group|body|string|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|» » separators|body|[string]|false|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|» service|body|string|true|The service type|
|» service_settings|body|object|true|Settings specific to the service|
|» task_settings|body|object|false|Task settings specific to the service and task type|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|task_type|sparse_embedding|
|task_type|text_embedding|
|task_type|rerank|
|task_type|completion|
|task_type|chat_completion|
|task_type|embedding|
|task_type|document_extraction|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunking_settings": {
    "max_chunk_size": 250,
    "overlap": 100,
    "sentence_overlap": 1,
    "separator_group": "string",
    "separators": [
      "string"
    ],
    "strategy": "sentence"
  },
  "service": "string",
  "service_settings": {},
  "task_settings": {},
  "inference_id": "string",
  "task_type": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-inference-endpoint-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[inference._types.InferenceEndpointInfo](#schemainference._types.inferenceendpointinfo)|

## Get cluster info

<a id="opIdinfo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /`

Get basic build, version, and cluster information.
::: In Serverless, `version.number` always reports the next target Elasticsearch release version at the time of the request. Serverless does not track to a traditional release versioning model; it is continuously updated. The version number is provided to maintain compatibility with existing clients, but it is not meaningful for assessing feature availability. Clients should detect a Serverless environment by checking for `build_flavor: serverless`.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/deploy/elastic-cloud/differences-from-other-elasticsearch-offerings">Learn about Serverless differences</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"name\": \"instance-0000000000\",\n  \"cluster_name\": \"my_test_cluster\",\n  \"cluster_uuid\": \"zk-HjQtYQGyL3NFSSu7InA\",\n  \"version\": {\n    \"number\": \"9.1.0\",\n    \"build_flavor\": \"default\",\n    \"build_type\": \"docker\",\n    \"build_hash\": 0,\n    \"build_date\": \"2025-07-09T22:10:13.578Z\",\n    \"build_snapshot\": false,\n    \"lucene_version\": \"10.2.2\",\n    \"minimum_wire_compatibility_version\": \"8.19.0\",\n    \"minimum_index_compatibility_version\": \"8.0.0\"\n  },\n  \"tagline\": \"You Know, for Search\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-cluster-info-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-cluster-info-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_name|object|true|none|The responding cluster's name.|
|cluster_uuid|object|true|none|none|
|name|object|true|none|The responding node's name.|
|tagline|string|true|none|none|
|version|object|true|none|Version information for the Elasticsearch cluster. In Serverless, `version.number` always reports the next target Elasticsearch release version at the time of the request, not an actual deployed version. The version number is provided to maintain client compatibility but is not meaningful for assessing feature availability. Use `build_flavor: serverless` to detect a Serverless environment.|
|» build_date|object|true|none|The Elasticsearch Git commit's date.|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|none|
|» build_flavor|string|true|none|The build flavor. For example, `default`.|
|» build_hash|string|true|none|The Elasticsearch Git commit's SHA hash.|
|» build_snapshot|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the Elasticsearch build was a snapshot.|
|» build_type|string|true|none|The build type that corresponds to how Elasticsearch was installed.<br>For example, `docker`, `rpm`, or `tar`.|
|» lucene_version|object|true|none|The version number of Elasticsearch's underlying Lucene software.|
|» minimum_index_compatibility_version|object|true|none|The minimum index version with which the responding node can read from disk.|
|» minimum_wire_compatibility_version|object|true|none|The minimum node version with which the responding node can communicate.<br>Also the minimum version from which you can perform a rolling upgrade.|
|» number|string|true|none|The Elasticsearch version number.<br><br>::: IMPORTANT: For Serverless deployments, this static value is always `8.11.0` and is used solely for backward compatibility with legacy clients.<br> Serverless environments are versionless and automatically upgraded, so this value can be safely ignored.|

|» _meta|body|object|false|Optional metadata about the ingest pipeline. May have any contents. This map is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the ingest pipeline.|
|» on_failure|body|[[ingest._types.ProcessorContainer](#schemaingest._types.processorcontainer)]|false|Processors to run immediately after a processor failure. Each processor supports a processor-level `on_failure` value. If a processor without an `on_failure` value fails, Elasticsearch uses this pipeline-level parameter as a fallback. The processors in this parameter run sequentially in the order specified. Elasticsearch will not attempt to run the pipeline's remaining processors.|
|» processors|body|[[ingest._types.ProcessorContainer](#schemaingest._types.processorcontainer)]|false|Processors used to perform transformations on documents before indexing. Processors run sequentially in the order specified.|
|» version|body|object|false|Version number used by external systems to track ingest pipelines. This parameter is intended for external systems only. Elasticsearch does not use or validate pipeline version numbers.|
|» deprecated|body|boolean|false|Marks this ingest pipeline as deprecated.<br>When a deprecated ingest pipeline is referenced as the default or final pipeline when creating or updating a non-deprecated index template, Elasticsearch will emit a deprecation warning.|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ingest/processor/grok`

Extract structured fields out of a single text field within a document.
You must choose which field to extract matched fields from, as well as the grok pattern you expect will match.
A grok pattern is like a regular expression that supports aliased expressions that can be reused.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/enrich-processor/grok-processor">More about the Grok processor</a>

> Example responses

<a id="opIdingest-simulate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ingest/pipeline/_simulate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"pipeline\" :\n  {\n    \"description\": \"_description\",\n    \"processors\": [\n      {\n        \"set\" : {\n          \"field\" : \"field2\",\n          \"value\" : \"_value\"\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_index\": \"index\",\n      \"_id\": \"id\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_index\": \"index\",\n      \"_id\": \"id\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`GET /_ingest/pipeline/_simulate`

Run an ingest pipeline against a set of provided documents.
You can either specify an existing pipeline to use with the provided documents or supply a pipeline definition in the body of the request.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `read_pipeline`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"pipeline\" :\n  {\n    \"description\": \"_description\",\n    \"processors\": [\n      {\n        \"set\" : {\n          \"field\" : \"field2\",\n          \"value\" : \"_value\"\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_index\": \"index\",\n      \"_id\": \"id\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_index\": \"index\",\n      \"_id\": \"id\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="simulate-a-pipeline-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verbose|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes output data for each processor in the executed pipeline.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» docs|body|[[ingest._types.Document](#schemaingest._types.document)]|true|Sample documents to test in the pipeline.|
|» pipeline|body|object|false|The pipeline to test.<br>If you don't specify the `pipeline` request path parameter, this parameter is required.<br>If you specify both this and the request path parameter, the API only uses the request path parameter.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description of the ingest pipeline.|
|» » on_failure|body|[[ingest._types.ProcessorContainer](#schemaingest._types.processorcontainer)]|false|Processors to run immediately after a processor failure.|
|» » processors|body|[[ingest._types.ProcessorContainer](#schemaingest._types.processorcontainer)]|false|Processors used to perform transformations on documents before indexing.<br>Processors run sequentially in the order specified.|
|» » version|body|object|false|Version number used by external systems to track ingest pipelines.|
|» » deprecated|body|boolean|false|Marks this ingest pipeline as deprecated.<br>When a deprecated ingest pipeline is referenced as the default or final pipeline when creating or updating a non-deprecated index template, Elasticsearch will emit a deprecation warning.|
|» » _meta|body|object|false|Arbitrary metadata about the ingest pipeline. This map is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » created_date|body|object|false|Date and time when the pipeline was created. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» » created_date_millis|body|object|false|Date and time when the pipeline was created, in milliseconds since the epoch.|
|» » modified_date|body|object|false|Date and time when the pipeline was last modified. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» » modified_date_millis|body|object|false|Date and time when the pipeline was last modified, in milliseconds since the epoch.|
|» » field_access_pattern|body|object|false|Controls how processors in this pipeline should read and write data on a document's source.|

> Example responses

## Simulate data ingestion

<a id="opIdsimulate-ingest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ingest/_simulate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"123\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"456\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`GET /_ingest/_simulate`

Run ingest pipelines against a set of provided documents, optionally with substitute pipeline definitions, to simulate ingesting data into an index.

This API is meant to be used for troubleshooting or pipeline development, as it does not actually index any data into Elasticsearch.

The API runs the default and final pipeline for that index against a set of documents provided in the body of the request.
If a pipeline contains a reroute processor, it follows that reroute processor to the new index, running that index's pipelines as well the same way that a non-simulated ingest would.
No data is indexed into Elasticsearch.
Instead, the transformed document is returned, along with the list of pipelines that have been run and the name of the index where the document would have been indexed if this were not a simulation.
The transformed document is validated against the mappings that would apply to this index, and any validation error is reported in the result.

This API differs from the simulate pipeline API in that you specify a single pipeline for that API, and it runs only that one pipeline.
The simulate pipeline API is more useful for developing a single pipeline, while the simulate ingest API is more useful for troubleshooting the interaction of the various pipelines that get applied when ingesting into an index.

By default, the pipeline definitions that are currently in the system are used.
However, you can supply substitute pipeline definitions in the body of the request.
These will be used in place of the pipeline definitions that are already in the system. This can be used to replace existing pipeline definitions or to create new ones. The pipeline substitutions are used only within this request.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `index`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"123\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"456\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Simulate data ingestion

<a id="opIdsimulate-ingest-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ingest/string/_simulate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"123\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"456\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`POST /_ingest/{index}/_simulate`

Run ingest pipelines against a set of provided documents, optionally with substitute pipeline definitions, to simulate ingesting data into an index.

This API is meant to be used for troubleshooting or pipeline development, as it does not actually index any data into Elasticsearch.

The API runs the default and final pipeline for that index against a set of documents provided in the body of the request.
If a pipeline contains a reroute processor, it follows that reroute processor to the new index, running that index's pipelines as well the same way that a non-simulated ingest would.
No data is indexed into Elasticsearch.
Instead, the transformed document is returned, along with the list of pipelines that have been run and the name of the index where the document would have been indexed if this were not a simulation.
The transformed document is validated against the mappings that would apply to this index, and any validation error is reported in the result.

This API differs from the simulate pipeline API in that you specify a single pipeline for that API, and it runs only that one pipeline.
The simulate pipeline API is more useful for developing a single pipeline, while the simulate ingest API is more useful for troubleshooting the interaction of the various pipelines that get applied when ingesting into an index.

By default, the pipeline definitions that are currently in the system are used.
However, you can supply substitute pipeline definitions in the body of the request.
These will be used in place of the pipeline definitions that are already in the system. This can be used to replace existing pipeline definitions or to create new ones. The pipeline substitutions are used only within this request.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `index`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"docs\": [\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"123\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"bar\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"_id\": \"456\",\n      \"_index\": \"my-index\",\n      \"_source\": {\n        \"foo\": \"rab\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Get license information

<a id="opIdlicense-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_license \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_license`

Get information about your Elastic license including its type, its status, when it was issued, and when it expires.

>info
> If the master node is generating a new cluster state, the get license API may return a `404 Not Found` response.
> If you receive an unexpected 404 response after cluster startup, wait a short period and retry the request.

<h3 id="get-license-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accept_enterprise|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If `true`, this parameter returns enterprise for Enterprise license types. If `false`, this parameter returns platinum for both platinum and enterprise license types. This behavior is maintained for backwards compatibility.<br>This parameter is deprecated and will always be set to true in 8.x.|
|local|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to retrieve local information.<br>From 9.2 onwards the default value is `true`, which means the information is retrieved from the responding node.<br>In earlier versions the default is `false`, which means the information is retrieved from the elected master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"license\" : {\n    \"status\" : \"active\",\n    \"uid\" : \"cbff45e7-c553-41f7-ae4f-9205eabd80xx\",\n    \"type\" : \"trial\",\n    \"issue_date\" : \"2018-10-20T22:05:12.332Z\",\n    \"issue_date_in_millis\" : 1540073112332,\n    \"expiry_date\" : \"2018-11-19T22:05:12.332Z\",\n    \"expiry_date_in_millis\" : 1542665112332,\n    \"max_nodes\" : 1000,\n    \"max_resource_units\" : null,\n    \"issued_to\" : \"test\",\n    \"issuer\" : \"elasticsearch\",\n    \"start_date_in_millis\" : -1\n  }\n}"
```

## Update the license

<a id="opIdlicense-post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_license \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"licenses\": [\n    {\n      \"uid\":\"893361dc-9749-4997-93cb-802e3d7fa4xx\",\n      \"type\":\"basic\",\n      \"issue_date_in_millis\":1411948800000,\n      \"expiry_date_in_millis\":1914278399999,\n      \"max_nodes\":1,\n      \"issued_to\":\"issuedTo\",\n      \"issuer\":\"issuer\",\n      \"signature\":\"xx\"\n    }\n    ]\n}"'
```

`PUT /_license`

You can update your license at runtime without shutting down your nodes.
License updates take effect immediately.
If the license you are installing does not support all of the features that were available with your previous license, however, you are notified in the response.
You must then re-submit the API request with the acknowledge parameter set to true.

NOTE: If Elasticsearch security features are enabled and you are installing a gold or higher license, you must enable TLS on the transport networking layer before you install the license.
If the operator privileges feature is enabled, only operator users can use this API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"licenses\": [\n    {\n      \"uid\":\"893361dc-9749-4997-93cb-802e3d7fa4xx\",\n      \"type\":\"basic\",\n      \"issue_date_in_millis\":1411948800000,\n      \"expiry_date_in_millis\":1914278399999,\n      \"max_nodes\":1,\n      \"issued_to\":\"issuedTo\",\n      \"issuer\":\"issuer\",\n      \"signature\":\"xx\"\n    }\n    ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-the-license-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledge|query|boolean|false|To update a license, you must accept the acknowledge messages and set this parameter to `true`.<br>In particular, if you are upgrading or downgrading a license, you must acknowlege the feature changes.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» license|body|object|false|none|
|» » expiry_date_in_millis|body|object|true|none|
|» » issue_date_in_millis|body|object|true|none|
|» » start_date_in_millis|body|object|false|none|
|» » issued_to|body|string|true|none|
|» » issuer|body|string|true|none|
|» » max_nodes|body|number \| string \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » max_resource_units|body|number|false|none|
|» » signature|body|string|true|none|
|» » type|body|object|true|none|
|» » uid|body|string|true|none|
|» licenses|body|[[license._types.License](#schemalicense._types.license)]|false|A sequence of one or more JSON documents containing the license information.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": false,\n  \"license_status\": \"valid\",\n  \"acknowledge\": {\n    \"message\": \"\\\"\\\"\\\"This license update requires acknowledgement. To acknowledge the license, please read the following messages and update the license again, this time with the \\\"acknowledge=true\\\" parameter:\\\"\\\"\\\"\",\n    \"watcher\": [\n      \"Watcher will be disabled\"\n    ],\n    \"logstash\": [\n      \"Logstash will no longer poll for centrally-managed pipelines\"\n    ],\n    \"security\": [\n      \"The following X-Pack security functionality will be disabled ...\"\n    ]\n  }\n}"
```

`POST /_license/start_basic`

Start an indefinite basic license, which gives access to all the basic features.

NOTE: In order to start a basic license, you must not currently have a basic license.

If the basic license does not support all of the features that are available with your current license, however, you are notified in the response.
You must then re-submit the API request with the `acknowledge` parameter set to `true`.

To check the status of your basic license, use the get basic license API.

<a id="opIdlicense-post-start-trial"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_license/start_trial \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_license/start_trial`

Start a 30-day trial, which gives access to all subscription features.

NOTE: You are allowed to start a trial only if your cluster has not already activated a trial for the current major product version.
For example, if you have already activated a trial for v8.0, you cannot start a new trial until v9.0. You can, however, request an extended trial at https://www.elastic.co/trialextension.

To check the status of your trial, use the get trial status API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="start-a-trial-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledge|query|boolean|false|To start a trial, you must accept the acknowledge messages and set this parameter to `true`.|
|type|query|string|false|The type of trial license to generate|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"trial_was_started\": true,\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="start-a-trial-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="start-a-trial-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|
|error_message|string|false|none|none|
|trial_was_started|boolean|true|none|none|
|type|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>
