## Create or update a Logstash pipeline

<a id="opIdlogstash-put-pipeline"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_logstash/pipeline/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"description\": \"Sample pipeline for illustration purposes\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2021-01-02T02:50:51.250Z\",\n  \"pipeline_metadata\": {\n    \"type\": \"logstash_pipeline\",\n    \"version\": 1\n  },\n  \"username\": \"elastic\",\n  \"pipeline\": \"input {}\\\\n filter { grok {} }\\\\n output {}\",\n  \"pipeline_settings\": {\n    \"pipeline.workers\": 1,\n    \"pipeline.batch.size\": 125,\n    \"pipeline.batch.delay\": 50,\n    \"queue.type\": \"memory\",\n    \"queue.max_bytes\": \"1gb\",\n    \"queue.checkpoint.writes\": 1024\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_logstash/pipeline/{id}`

Create a pipeline that is used for Logstash Central Management.
If the specified pipeline exists, it is replaced.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_logstash_pipelines`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/logstash/logstash-centralized-pipeline-management">Centralized pipeline management</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"description\": \"Sample pipeline for illustration purposes\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2021-01-02T02:50:51.250Z\",\n  \"pipeline_metadata\": {\n    \"type\": \"logstash_pipeline\",\n    \"version\": 1\n  },\n  \"username\": \"elastic\",\n  \"pipeline\": \"input {}\\\\n filter { grok {} }\\\\n output {}\",\n  \"pipeline_settings\": {\n    \"pipeline.workers\": 1,\n    \"pipeline.batch.size\": 125,\n    \"pipeline.batch.delay\": 50,\n    \"queue.type\": \"memory\",\n    \"queue.max_bytes\": \"1gb\",\n    \"queue.checkpoint.writes\": 1024\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-logstash-pipeline-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|An identifier for the pipeline.<br>Pipeline IDs must begin with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, underscores, dashes, hyphens and numbers.|
|body|body|[logstash._types.Pipeline](#schemalogstash._types.pipeline)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|true|A description of the pipeline.<br>This description is not used by Elasticsearch or Logstash.|
|» last_modified|body|object|true|The date the pipeline was last updated.<br>It must be in the `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZZ` strict_date_time format.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» pipeline|body|string|true|The configuration for the pipeline.|
|» pipeline_metadata|body|object|true|Optional metadata about the pipeline, which can have any contents.<br>This metadata is not generated or used by Elasticsearch or Logstash.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » version|body|string|true|none|
|» pipeline_settings|body|object|true|Settings for the pipeline.<br>It supports only flat keys in dot notation.|
|» » pipeline.workers|body|number|true|The number of workers that will, in parallel, execute the filter and output stages of the pipeline.|
|» » pipeline.batch.size|body|number|true|The maximum number of events an individual worker thread will collect from inputs before attempting to execute its filters and outputs.|
|» » pipeline.batch.delay|body|number|true|When creating pipeline event batches, how long in milliseconds to wait for each event before dispatching an undersized batch to pipeline workers.|
|» » queue.type|body|string|true|The internal queuing model to use for event buffering.|
|» » queue.max_bytes|body|string|true|The total capacity of the queue (`queue.type: persisted`) in number of bytes.|
|» » queue.checkpoint.writes|body|number|true|The maximum number of written events before forcing a checkpoint when persistent queues are enabled (`queue.type: persisted`).|
|» username|body|string|true|The user who last updated the pipeline.|

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-logstash-pipeline-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Clear trained model deployment cache

<a id="opIdml-clear-trained-model-deployment-cache"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/deployment/cache/_clear \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/deployment/cache/_clear`

Cache will be cleared on all nodes where the trained model is assigned.
A trained model deployment may have an inference cache enabled.
As requests are handled by each allocated node, their responses may be cached on that individual node.
Calling this API clears the caches without restarting the deployment.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="clear-trained-model-deployment-cache-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"cleared\": true\n}"
```

|200|OK||Inline|

|cleared|boolean|true|none|none|

## Get trained model configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-trained-models"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-trained-model-configuration-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model or a model alias.<br><br>You can get information for multiple trained models in a single API<br>request by using a comma-separated list of model IDs or a wildcard<br>expression.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are no models that match.<br>- Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If true, it returns an empty array when there are no matches and the<br>subset of results when there are partial matches.|
|decompress_definition|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the included model definition should be returned as a<br>JSON map (true) or in a custom compressed format (false).|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of models.|
|include|query|[ml._types.Include](#schemaml._types.include)|false|A comma delimited string of optional fields to include in the response<br>body.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of models to obtain.|
|tags|query|string \| [string]|false|A comma delimited string of tags. A trained model can have many tags, or<br>none. When supplied, only trained models that contain all the supplied<br>tags are returned.|

|Parameter|Value|

|include|definition|

|include|definition_status|

<h3 id="get-trained-model-configuration-info-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|trained_model_configs|[[ml._types.TrainedModelConfig](#schemaml._types.trainedmodelconfig)]|true|none|An array of trained model resources, which are sorted by the model_id value in ascending order.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```bash
    "ingest": "string",
    "search": "string"
  }
```
```json
}
```

## Delete an unreferenced trained model

<a id="opIdml-delete-trained-model"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}`

The request deletes a trained inference model that is not referenced by an ingest pipeline.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-an-unreferenced-trained-model-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model.|
|force|query|boolean|false|Forcefully deletes a trained model that is referenced by ingest pipelines or has a started deployment.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-an-unreferenced-trained-model-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a trained model alias

<a id="opIdml-put-trained-model-alias"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/model_aliases/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/model_aliases/{model_alias}`

A trained model alias is a logical name used to reference a single trained
model.
You can use aliases instead of trained model identifiers to make it easier to
reference your models. For example, you can use aliases in inference
aggregations and processors.
An alias must be unique and refer to only a single trained model. However,
you can have multiple aliases for each trained model.
If you use this API to update an alias such that it references a different
trained model ID and the model uses a different type of data frame analytics,
an error occurs. For example, this situation occurs if you have a trained
model for regression analysis and a trained model for classification
analysis; you cannot reassign an alias from one type of trained model to
another.
If you use this API to update an alias and there are very few input fields in
common between the old and new trained models for the model alias, the API
returns a warning.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="create-or-update-a-trained-model-alias-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The identifier for the trained model that the alias refers to.|
|model_alias|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The alias to create or update. This value cannot end in numbers.|
|reassign|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the alias gets reassigned to the specified trained<br>model if it is already assigned to a different model. If the alias is<br>already assigned and this parameter is false, the API returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-trained-model-alias-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete a trained model alias

<a id="opIdml-delete-trained-model-alias"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/model_aliases/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/model_aliases/{model_alias}`

This API deletes an existing model alias that refers to a trained model. If
the model alias is missing or refers to a model other than the one identified
by the `model_id`, this API returns an error.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-a-trained-model-alias-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The trained model ID to which the model alias refers.|
|model_alias|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The model alias to delete.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-a-trained-model-alias-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get trained model configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-trained-models-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/trained_models`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-trained-model-configuration-info-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are no models that match.<br>- Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If true, it returns an empty array when there are no matches and the<br>subset of results when there are partial matches.|
|decompress_definition|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the included model definition should be returned as a<br>JSON map (true) or in a custom compressed format (false).|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of models.|
|include|query|[ml._types.Include](#schemaml._types.include)|false|A comma delimited string of optional fields to include in the response<br>body.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of models to obtain.|
|tags|query|string \| [string]|false|A comma delimited string of tags. A trained model can have many tags, or<br>none. When supplied, only trained models that contain all the supplied<br>tags are returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|definition|
|include|feature_importance_baseline|
|include|hyperparameters|
|include|total_feature_importance|
|include|definition_status|

## Get trained models usage info

<a id="opIdml-get-trained-models-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/_stats`

You can get usage information for multiple trained
models in a single API request by using a comma-separated list of model IDs or a wildcard expression.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-trained-models-usage-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model or a model alias. It can be a<br>comma-separated list or a wildcard expression.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are no models that match.<br>- Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>- Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If true, it returns an empty array when there are no matches and the<br>subset of results when there are partial matches.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of models.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of models to obtain.|

## Evaluate a trained model

<a id="opIdml-infer-trained-model"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/_infer \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"docs\":[{\"text\": \"The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.\"}]\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/_infer`

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"docs\":[{\"text\": \"The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.\"}]\n}"
```

<h3 id="evaluate-a-trained-model-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the amount of time to wait for inference results.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» docs|body|[object]|true|An array of objects to pass to the model for inference. The objects should contain a fields matching your<br>configured trained model input. Typically, for NLP models, the field name is `text_field`.<br>Currently, for NLP models, only a single value is allowed.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» inference_config|body|object|false|The inference configuration updates to apply on the API call|
|» » regression|body|object|false|Regression configuration for inference.|
|» » » results_field|body|object|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document.|
|» » classification|body|object|false|Classification configuration for inference.|
|» » » num_top_classes|body|number|false|Specifies the number of top class predictions to return. Defaults to 0.|
|» » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document.|
|» » » prediction_field_type|body|string|false|Specifies the type of the predicted field to write. Acceptable values are: string, number, boolean. When boolean is provided 1.0 is transformed to true and 0.0 to false.|
|» » » results_field|body|string|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » » top_classes_results_field|body|string|false|Specifies the field to which the top classes are written. Defaults to top_classes.|
|» » text_classification|body|object|false|Text classification configuration for inference.|
|» » » num_top_classes|body|number|false|Specifies the number of top class predictions to return. Defaults to 0.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|
|» » » » span|body|number|false|Span options to apply|
|» » » results_field|body|string|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » » classification_labels|body|[string]|false|Classification labels to apply other than the stored labels. Must have the same deminsions as the default configured labels|
|» » zero_shot_classification|body|object|false|Zeroshot classification configuration for inference.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|
|» » » » span|body|number|false|Span options to apply|
|» » » results_field|body|string|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » » multi_label|body|boolean|false|Update the configured multi label option. Indicates if more than one true label exists. Defaults to the configured value.|
|» » » labels|body|[string]|true|The labels to predict.|
|» » fill_mask|body|object|false|Fill mask configuration for inference.|
|» » » num_top_classes|body|number|false|Specifies the number of top class predictions to return. Defaults to 0.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|
|» » » » span|body|number|false|Span options to apply|
|» » » results_field|body|string|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » ner|body|object|false|Named entity recognition configuration for inference.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|
|» » » » span|body|number|false|Span options to apply|
|» » » results_field|body|string|false|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|» » pass_through|body|object|false|Pass through configuration for inference.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|

|» » text_embedding|body|object|false|Text embedding configuration for inference.|
|» » » tokenization|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » truncate|body|object|false|Truncate options to apply|

## Create part of a trained model definition

<a id="opIdml-put-trained-model-definition-part"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/definition/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n    \"definition\": \"...\",\n    \"total_definition_length\": 265632637,\n    \"total_parts\": 64\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/definition/{part}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n    \"definition\": \"...\",\n    \"total_definition_length\": 265632637,\n    \"total_parts\": 64\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-part-of-a-trained-model-definition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model.|
|part|path|number|true|The definition part number. When the definition is loaded for inference the definition parts are streamed in the<br>order of their part number. The first part must be `0` and the final part must be `total_parts - 1`.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» definition|body|string|true|The definition part for the model. Must be a base64 encoded string.|
|» total_definition_length|body|number|true|The total uncompressed definition length in bytes. Not base64 encoded.|
|» total_parts|body|number|true|The total number of parts that will be uploaded. Must be greater than 0.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-part-of-a-trained-model-definition-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a trained model vocabulary

<a id="opIdml-put-trained-model-vocabulary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/vocabulary \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"vocabulary\": [\n    \"[PAD]\",\n    \"[unused0]\",\n  ]\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/vocabulary`

This API is supported only for natural language processing (NLP) models.
The vocabulary is stored in the index as described in `inference_config.*.vocabulary` of the trained model definition.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"vocabulary\": [\n    \"[PAD]\",\n    \"[unused0]\",\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-trained-model-vocabulary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» vocabulary|body|[string]|true|The model vocabulary, which must not be empty.|
|» merges|body|[string]|false|The optional model merges if required by the tokenizer.|
|» scores|body|[number]|false|The optional vocabulary value scores if required by the tokenizer.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

## Start a trained model deployment

<a id="opIdml-start-trained-model-deployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/trained_models/string/deployment/_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "adaptive_allocations": {
      "enabled": true,
      "min_number_of_allocations": 0,
      "max_number_of_allocations": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /_ml/trained_models/{model_id}/deployment/_start`

It allocates the model to every machine learning node.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "adaptive_allocations": {
    "enabled": true,
    "min_number_of_allocations": 0,
    "max_number_of_allocations": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-trained-model-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the trained model. Currently, only PyTorch models are supported.|
|cache_size|query|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize)|false|The inference cache size (in memory outside the JVM heap) per node for the model.<br>The default value is the same size as the `model_size_bytes`. To disable the cache,<br>`0b` can be provided.|
|deployment_id|query|string|false|A unique identifier for the deployment of the model.|
|number_of_allocations|query|number|false|The number of model allocations on each node where the model is deployed.<br>All allocations on a node share the same copy of the model in memory but use<br>a separate set of threads to evaluate the model.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the throughput.<br>If this setting is greater than the number of hardware threads<br>it will automatically be changed to a value less than the number of hardware threads.<br>If adaptive_allocations is enabled, do not set this value, because it’s automatically set.|
|priority|query|[ml._types.TrainingPriority](#schemaml._types.trainingpriority)|false|The deployment priority|
|queue_capacity|query|number|false|Specifies the number of inference requests that are allowed in the queue. After the number of requests exceeds<br>this value, new requests are rejected with a 429 error.|
|threads_per_allocation|query|number|false|Sets the number of threads used by each model allocation during inference. This generally increases<br>the inference speed. The inference process is a compute-bound process; any number<br>greater than the number of available hardware threads on the machine does not increase the<br>inference speed. If this setting is greater than the number of hardware threads<br>it will automatically be changed to a value less than the number of hardware threads.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait for the model to deploy.|
|wait_for|query|object|false|Specifies the allocation status to wait for before returning.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» adaptive_allocations|body|object|false|Adaptive allocations configuration. When enabled, the number of allocations<br>is set based on the current load.<br>If adaptive_allocations is enabled, do not set the number of allocations manually.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|If true, adaptive_allocations is enabled|
|» » min_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|Specifies the minimum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to 0.<br>If not defined, the deployment scales to 0.|
|» » max_number_of_allocations|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of allocations to scale to.<br>If set, it must be greater than or equal to min_number_of_allocations.|

|priority|low|

## Close anomaly detection jobs

<a id="opIdml-close-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_close \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allow_no_match": true,
    "force": false,
    "timeout": "30m"
  }'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_close`

A job can be opened and closed multiple times throughout its lifecycle. A closed job cannot receive data or perform analysis operations, but you can still explore and navigate results.
When you close a job, it runs housekeeping tasks such as pruning the model history, flushing buffers, calculating final results and persisting the model snapshots. Depending upon the size of the job, it could take several minutes to close and the equivalent time to re-open. After it is closed, the job has a minimal overhead on the cluster except for maintaining its meta data. Therefore it is a best practice to close jobs that are no longer required to process data.
If you close an anomaly detection job whose datafeed is running, the request first tries to stop the datafeed. This behavior is equivalent to calling stop datafeed API with the same timeout and force parameters as the close job request.
When a datafeed that has a specified end date stops, it automatically closes its associated job.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_no_match": true,
  "force": false,
  "timeout": "30m"
}
```

<h3 id="close-anomaly-detection-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. It can be a job identifier, a group name, or a wildcard expression. You can close multiple anomaly detection jobs in a single API request by using a group name, a comma-separated list of jobs, or a wildcard expression. You can close all jobs by using `_all` or by specifying `*` as the job identifier.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request: contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match; contains the  `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches; or contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches. By default, it returns an empty jobs array when there are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial matches.<br>If `false`, the request returns a 404 status code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|force|query|boolean|false|Use to close a failed job, or to forcefully close a job which has not responded to its initial close request; the request returns without performing the associated actions such as flushing buffers and persisting the model snapshots.<br>If you want the job to be in a consistent state after the close job API returns, do not set to `true`. This parameter should be used only in situations where the job has already failed or where you are not interested in results the job might have recently produced or might produce in the future.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the time to wait until a job has closed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_no_match|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `allow_no_match` query parameter.|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Refer to the descriptiion for the `force` query parameter.|
|» timeout|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `timeout` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

```json
"{\n  \"closed\": true\n}"
```

|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of calendars to obtain. This parameter is supported only when you omit the calendar identifier.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» page|body|object|false|This object is supported only when you omit the calendar identifier.|
|» » from|body|number|false|Skips the specified number of items.|
|» » size|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of items to obtain.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "calendars": [
    {
      "calendar_id": {},
      "description": "string",
      "job_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "count": 0
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-calendar-configuration-info-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|calendars|[[ml.get_calendars.Calendar](#schemaml.get_calendars.calendar)]|true|none|none|
|count|number|true|none|none|

## Get datafeeds configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-datafeeds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}`

You can get information for multiple datafeeds in a single API request by
using a comma-separated list of datafeeds or a wildcard expression. You can
get information for all datafeeds by using `_all`, by specifying `*` as the
`<feed_id>`, or by omitting the `<feed_id>`.
This API returns a maximum of 10,000 datafeeds.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-datafeeds-configuration-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|true|Identifier for the datafeed. It can be a datafeed identifier or a<br>wildcard expression. If you do not specify one of these options, the API<br>returns information about all datafeeds.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no datafeeds that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is `true`, which returns an empty `datafeeds` array<br>when there are no matches and the subset of results when there are<br>partial matches. If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a<br>`404` status code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a datafeed

<a id="opIdml-put-datafeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"indices\": [\n    \"kibana_sample_data_logs\"\n  ],\n  \"query\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"must\": [\n        {\n          \"match_all\": {}\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"job_id\": \"test-job\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}`

Datafeeds retrieve data from Elasticsearch for analysis by an anomaly detection job.
You can associate only one datafeed with each anomaly detection job.
The datafeed contains a query that runs at a defined interval (`frequency`).
If you are concerned about delayed data, you can add a delay (`query_delay') at each interval.
By default, the datafeed uses the following query: `{"match_all": {"boost": 1}}`.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, your datafeed remembers which roles the user who created it had
at the time of creation and runs the query using those same roles. If you provide secondary authorization headers,
those credentials are used instead.
You must use Kibana, this API, or the create anomaly detection jobs API to create a datafeed. Do not add a datafeed
directly to the `.ml-config` index. Do not give users `write` privileges on the `.ml-config` index.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"indices\": [\n    \"kibana_sample_data_logs\"\n  ],\n  \"query\": {\n    \"bool\": {\n      \"must\": [\n        {\n          \"match_all\": {}\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"job_id\": \"test-job\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-datafeed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed.<br>This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores.<br>It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines<br>whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, concrete, expanded, or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» aggregations|body|object|false|If set, the datafeed performs aggregation searches.<br>Support for aggregations is limited and should be used only with low cardinality data.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.aggregations.AggregationContainer](#schema_types.aggregations.aggregationcontainer)|false|none|
|» chunking_config|body|object|false|Datafeeds might be required to search over long time periods, for several months or years.<br>This search is split into time chunks in order to ensure the load on Elasticsearch is managed.<br>Chunking configuration controls how the size of these time chunks are calculated;<br>it is an advanced configuration option.|
|» » mode|body|object|true|If the mode is `auto`, the chunk size is dynamically calculated;<br>this is the recommended value when the datafeed does not use aggregations.<br>If the mode is `manual`, chunking is applied according to the specified `time_span`;<br>use this mode when the datafeed uses aggregations. If the mode is `off`, no chunking is applied.|
|» » time_span|body|object|false|The time span that each search will be querying. This setting is applicable only when the `mode` is set to `manual`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» delayed_data_check_config|body|object|false|Specifies whether the datafeed checks for missing data and the size of the window.<br>The datafeed can optionally search over indices that have already been read in an effort to determine whether<br>any data has subsequently been added to the index. If missing data is found, it is a good indication that the<br>`query_delay` is set too low and the data is being indexed after the datafeed has passed that moment in time.<br>This check runs only on real-time datafeeds.|
|» » check_window|body|object|false|The window of time that is searched for late data. This window of time ends with the latest finalized bucket.<br>It defaults to null, which causes an appropriate `check_window` to be calculated when the real-time datafeed runs.<br>In particular, the default `check_window` span calculation is based on the maximum of `2h` or `8 * bucket_span`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Specifies whether the datafeed periodically checks for delayed data.|
|» frequency|body|object|false|The interval at which scheduled queries are made while the datafeed runs in real time.<br>The default value is either the bucket span for short bucket spans, or, for longer bucket spans, a sensible<br>fraction of the bucket span. When `frequency` is shorter than the bucket span, interim results for the last<br>(partial) bucket are written then eventually overwritten by the full bucket results. If the datafeed uses<br>aggregations, this value must be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|none|

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}`



## Required authorization

<h3 id="delete-a-datafeed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This<br>identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9),<br>hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric<br>characters.|
|force|query|boolean|false|Use to forcefully delete a started datafeed; this method is quicker than<br>stopping and deleting the datafeed.|

## Delete expired ML data

<a id="opIdml-delete-expired-data"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/_delete_expired_data/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "requests_per_second": 0,
    "timeout": "8h"
  }'
```

`DELETE /_ml/_delete_expired_data/{job_id}`

Delete all job results, model snapshots and forecast data that have exceeded
their retention days period. Machine learning state documents that are not
associated with any job are also deleted.
You can limit the request to a single or set of anomaly detection jobs by
using a job identifier, a group name, a comma-separated list of jobs, or a
wildcard expression. You can delete expired data for all anomaly detection
jobs by using `_all`, by specifying `*` as the `<job_id>`, or by omitting the
`<job_id>`.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "requests_per_second": 0,
  "timeout": "8h"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-expired-ml-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for an anomaly detection job. It can be a job identifier, a<br>group name, or a wildcard expression.|
|requests_per_second|query|number|false|The desired requests per second for the deletion processes. The default<br>behavior is no throttling.|
|timeout|query|object|false|How long can the underlying delete processes run until they are canceled.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» requests_per_second|body|number|false|The desired requests per second for the deletion processes. The default<br>behavior is no throttling.|
|» timeout|body|object|false|How long can the underlying delete processes run until they are canceled.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"deleted\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-expired-ml-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="delete-expired-ml-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a filter

<a id="opIdml-put-filter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/filters/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"description\": \"A list of safe domains\",\n  \"items\": [\"*.google.com\", \"wikipedia.org\"]\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/filters/{filter_id}`

A filter contains a list of strings. It can be used by one or more anomaly detection jobs.
Specifically, filters are referenced in the `custom_rules` property of detector configuration objects.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"description\": \"A list of safe domains\",\n  \"items\": [\"*.google.com\", \"wikipedia.org\"]\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A string that uniquely identifies a filter.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the filter.|
|» items|body|[string]|false|The items of the filter. A wildcard `*` can be used at the beginning or the end of an item.<br>Up to 10000 items are allowed in each filter.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "filter_id": {},
  "items": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-filter-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-filter-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|true|none|none|
|filter_id|object|true|none|none|
|items|[string]|true|none|none|

## Predict future behavior of a time series

<a id="opIdml-forecast"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_forecast \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"duration\": \"10d\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_forecast`

Forecasts are not supported for jobs that perform population analysis; an
error occurs if you try to create a forecast for a job that has an
`over_field_name` in its configuration. Forcasts predict future behavior
based on historical data.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"duration\": \"10d\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="predict-future-behavior-of-a-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. The job must be open when you<br>create a forecast; otherwise, an error occurs.|
|duration|query|object|false|A period of time that indicates how far into the future to forecast. For<br>example, `30d` corresponds to 30 days. The forecast starts at the last<br>record that was processed.|
|expires_in|query|object|false|The period of time that forecast results are retained. After a forecast<br>expires, the results are deleted. If set to a value of 0, the forecast is<br>never automatically deleted.|
|max_model_memory|query|string|false|The maximum memory the forecast can use. If the forecast needs to use<br>more than the provided amount, it will spool to disk. Default is 20mb,<br>maximum is 500mb and minimum is 1mb. If set to 40% or more of the job’s<br>configured memory limit, it is automatically reduced to below that<br>amount.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» duration|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `duration` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expires_in|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `expires_in` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» max_model_memory|body|string|false|Refer to the description for the `max_model_memory` query parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "forecast_id": {}
}
```

<h3 id="predict-future-behavior-of-a-time-series-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="predict-future-behavior-of-a-time-series-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|
|forecast_id|object|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete forecasts from a job

<a id="opIdml-delete-forecast"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_forecast \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_forecast`

By default, forecasts are retained for 14 days. You can specify a
different retention period with the `expires_in` parameter in the forecast
jobs API. The delete forecast API enables you to delete one or more
forecasts before they expire.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-forecasts-from-a-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|allow_no_forecasts|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether an error occurs when there are no forecasts. In<br>particular, if this parameter is set to `false` and there are no<br>forecasts associated with the job, attempts to delete all forecasts<br>return an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the period of time to wait for the completion of the delete<br>operation. When this period of time elapses, the API fails and returns an<br>error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-forecasts-from-a-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`DELETE /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_forecast/{forecast_id}`

By default, forecasts are retained for 14 days. You can specify a
different retention period with the `expires_in` parameter in the forecast
jobs API. The delete forecast API enables you to delete one or more
forecasts before they expire.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-forecasts-from-a-job-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|forecast_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A comma-separated list of forecast identifiers. If you do not specify<br>this optional parameter or if you specify `_all` or `*` the API deletes<br>all forecasts from the job.|
|allow_no_forecasts|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether an error occurs when there are no forecasts. In<br>particular, if this parameter is set to `false` and there are no<br>forecasts associated with the job, attempts to delete all forecasts<br>return an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the period of time to wait for the completion of the delete<br>operation. When this period of time elapses, the API fails and returns an<br>error.|

## Get anomaly detection jobs configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-jobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}`

You can get information for multiple anomaly detection jobs in a single API
request by using a group name, a comma-separated list of jobs, or a wildcard
expression. You can get information for all anomaly detection jobs by using
`_all`, by specifying `*` as the `<job_id>`, or by omitting the `<job_id>`.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-jobs-configuration-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. It can be a job identifier, a<br>group name, or a wildcard expression. If you do not specify one of these<br>options, the API returns information for all anomaly detection jobs.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is `true`, which returns an empty `jobs` array when<br>there are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial<br>matches. If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a `404` status<br>code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-jobs-configuration-info-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|jobs|[[ml._types.Job](#schemaml._types.job)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create an anomaly detection job

<a id="opIdml-put-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"analysis_config\": {\n    \"bucket_span\": \"15m\",\n    \"detectors\": [\n      {\n        \"detector_description\": \"Sum of bytes\",\n        \"function\": \"sum\",\n        \"field_name\": \"bytes\"\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"data_description\": {\n    \"time_field\": \"timestamp\",\n    \"time_format\": \"epoch_ms\"\n  },\n  \"analysis_limits\": {\n    \"model_memory_limit\": \"11MB\"\n  },\n  \"model_plot_config\": {\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"annotations_enabled\": true\n  },\n  \"results_index_name\": \"test-job1\",\n  \"datafeed_config\": {\n    \"indices\": [\n      \"kibana_sample_data_logs\"\n    ],\n    \"query\": {\n      \"bool\": {\n        \"must\": [\n          {\n            \"match_all\": {}\n          }\n        ]\n      }\n    },\n    \"runtime_mappings\": {\n      \"hour_of_day\": {\n        \"type\": \"long\",\n        \"script\": {\n          \"source\": \"emit(doc['\''timestamp'\''].value.getHour());\"\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"datafeed_id\": \"datafeed-test-job1\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}`

If you include a `datafeed_config`, you must have read index privileges on the source index.
If you include a `datafeed_config` but do not provide a query, the datafeed uses `{"match_all": {"boost": 1}}`.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"analysis_config\": {\n    \"bucket_span\": \"15m\",\n    \"detectors\": [\n      {\n        \"detector_description\": \"Sum of bytes\",\n        \"function\": \"sum\",\n        \"field_name\": \"bytes\"\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"data_description\": {\n    \"time_field\": \"timestamp\",\n    \"time_format\": \"epoch_ms\"\n  },\n  \"analysis_limits\": {\n    \"model_memory_limit\": \"11MB\"\n  },\n  \"model_plot_config\": {\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"annotations_enabled\": true\n  },\n  \"results_index_name\": \"test-job1\",\n  \"datafeed_config\": {\n    \"indices\": [\n      \"kibana_sample_data_logs\"\n    ],\n    \"query\": {\n      \"bool\": {\n        \"must\": [\n          {\n            \"match_all\": {}\n          }\n        ]\n      }\n    },\n    \"runtime_mappings\": {\n      \"hour_of_day\": {\n        \"type\": \"long\",\n        \"script\": {\n          \"source\": \"emit(doc['timestamp'].value.getHour());\"\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"datafeed_id\": \"datafeed-test-job1\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-anomaly-detection-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The identifier for the anomaly detection job. This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|allow_no_indices|query|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|query|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines<br>whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values.|
|ignore_throttled|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If `true`, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|ignore_unavailable|query|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_lazy_open|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether this job can open when there is insufficient machine learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node. |» » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

|» » model_memory_limit|body|object|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

|» model_plot_config|body|object|false|This advanced configuration option stores model information along with the results. It provides a more detailed view into anomaly detection. If you enable model plot it can add considerable overhead to the performance of the system; it is not feasible for jobs with many entities. Model plot provides a simplified and indicative view of the model and its bounds. It does not display complex features such as multivariate correlations or multimodal data. As such, anomalies may occasionally be reported which cannot be seen in the model plot. Model plot config can be configured when the job is created or updated later. It must be disabled if performance issues are experienced.|
|» » annotations_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, enables calculation and storage of the model change annotations for each entity that is being analyzed.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, enables calculation and storage of the model bounds for each entity that is being analyzed.|
|» » terms|body|object|false|Limits data collection to this comma separated list of partition or by field values. If terms are not specified or it is an empty string, no filtering is applied. Wildcards are not supported. Only the specified terms can be viewed when using the Single Metric Viewer.|
|» model_snapshot_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job. It specifies the maximum period of time (in days) that snapshots are retained. This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job. By default, snapshots ten days older than the newest snapshot are deleted.|
|» renormalization_window_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The period over which adjustments to the score are applied, as new data is seen. The default value is the longer of 30 days or 100 bucket spans.|
|» results_index_name|body|object|false|A text string that affects the name of the machine learning results index. By default, the job generates an index named `.ml-anomalies-shared`.|
|» results_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The period of time (in days) that results are retained. Age is calculated relative to the timestamp of the latest bucket result. If this property has a non-null value, once per day at 00:30 (server time), results that are the specified number of days older than the latest bucket result are deleted from Elasticsearch. The default value is null, which means all results are retained. Annotations generated by the system also count as results for retention purposes; they are deleted after the same number of days as results. Annotations added by users are retained forever.|

|» categorization_filters|[string]|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering, use the `categorization_analyzer` property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters. |» multivariate_by_fields|boolean|false|none|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|
|» per_partition_categorization|object|false|none|Settings related to how categorization interacts with partition fields.|

|» » stop_on_warn|boolean|false|none|This setting can be set to true only if per-partition categorization is enabled. If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn. This setting makes it viable to have a job where it is expected that categorization works well for some partitions but not others; you do not pay the cost of bad categorization forever in the partitions where it works badly.|
|» summary_count_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the data that is fed to the job is expected to be pre-summarized. NOTE: The `summary_count_field_name` property cannot be used with the `metric` function.|

|» categorization_examples_limit|number|false|none|The maximum number of examples stored per category in memory and in the results data store. If you increase this value, more examples are available, however it requires that you have more storage available. If you set this value to 0, no examples are stored. NOTE: The `categorization_examples_limit` applies only to analysis that uses categorization.|
|» model_memory_limit|object|false|none|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

## Delete an anomaly detection job

<a id="opIdml-delete-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}`

All job configuration, model state and results are deleted.
It is not currently possible to delete multiple jobs using wildcards or a
comma separated list. If you delete a job that has a datafeed, the request
first tries to delete the datafeed. This behavior is equivalent to calling
the delete datafeed API with the same timeout and force parameters as the
delete job request.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-an-anomaly-detection-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|force|query|boolean|false|Use to forcefully delete an opened job; this method is quicker than<br>closing and deleting the job.|
|delete_user_annotations|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether annotations that have been added by the<br>user should be deleted along with any auto-generated annotations when the job is<br>reset.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the request should return immediately or wait until the<br>job deletion completes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-an-anomaly-detection-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete a model snapshot

<a id="opIdml-delete-model-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots/{snapshot_id}`

You cannot delete the active model snapshot. To delete that snapshot, first
revert to a different one. To identify the active model snapshot, refer to
the `model_snapshot_id` in the results from the get jobs API.

## Required authorization

## Estimate job model memory usage

<a id="opIdml-estimate-model-memory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/_estimate_model_memory \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"analysis_config\": {\n    \"bucket_span\": \"5m\",\n    \"detectors\": [\n      {\n        \"function\": \"sum\",\n        \"field_name\": \"bytes\",\n        \"by_field_name\": \"status\",\n        \"partition_field_name\": \"app\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"influencers\": [\n      \"source_ip\",\n      \"dest_ip\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"overall_cardinality\": {\n    \"status\": 10,\n    \"app\": 50\n  },\n  \"max_bucket_cardinality\": {\n    \"source_ip\": 300,\n    \"dest_ip\": 30\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/_estimate_model_memory`

Make an estimation of the memory usage for an anomaly detection job model.
The estimate is based on analysis configuration details for the job and cardinality
estimates for the fields it references.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"analysis_config\": {\n    \"bucket_span\": \"5m\",\n    \"detectors\": [\n      {\n        \"function\": \"sum\",\n        \"field_name\": \"bytes\",\n        \"by_field_name\": \"status\",\n        \"partition_field_name\": \"app\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"influencers\": [\n      \"source_ip\",\n      \"dest_ip\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"overall_cardinality\": {\n    \"status\": 10,\n    \"app\": 50\n  },\n  \"max_bucket_cardinality\": {\n    \"source_ip\": 300,\n    \"dest_ip\": 30\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="estimate-job-model-memory-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» analysis_config|body|object|false|For a list of the properties that you can specify in the<br>`analysis_config` component of the body of this API.|
|» » bucket_span|body|object|false|The size of the interval that the analysis is aggregated into, typically between `5m` and `1h`. This value should be either a whole number of days or equate to a<br>whole number of buckets in one day. If the anomaly detection job uses a datafeed with aggregations, this value must also be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » categorization_analyzer|body|object|false|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define the analyzer that is used to interpret the categorization field. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_filters`. The categorization analyzer specifies how the `categorization_field` is interpreted by the categorization process. The `categorization_analyzer` field can be specified either as a string or as an object. If it is a string, it must refer to a built-in analyzer or one added by another plugin.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[ml._types.CategorizationAnalyzerDefinition](#schemaml._types.categorizationanalyzerdefinition)|false|none|
|» » categorization_field_name|body|object|false|If this property is specified, the values of the specified field will be categorized. The resulting categories must be used in a detector by setting `by_field_name`, `over_field_name`, or `partition_field_name` to the keyword `mlcategory`.|
|» » categorization_filters|body|[string]|false|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering, use the `categorization_analyzer` property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters. The effect is exactly the same.|
|» » detectors|body|[[ml._types.Detector](#schemaml._types.detector)]|true|Detector configuration objects specify which data fields a job analyzes. They also specify which analytical functions are used. You can specify multiple detectors for a job. If the detectors array does not contain at least one detector, no analysis can occur and an error is returned.|
|» » influencers|body|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|false|A comma separated list of influencer field names. Typically these can be the by, over, or partition fields that are used in the detector configuration. You might also want to use a field name that is not specifically named in a detector, but is available as part of the input data. When you use multiple detectors, the use of influencers is recommended as it aggregates results for each influencer entity.|
|» » latency|body|object|false|The size of the window in which to expect data that is out of time order. If you specify a non-zero value, it must be greater than or equal to one second. NOTE: Latency is applicable only when you send data by using the post data API.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » model_prune_window|body|object|false|Advanced configuration option. Affects the pruning of models that have not been updated for the given time duration. The value must be set to a multiple of the `bucket_span`. If set too low, important information may be removed from the model. For jobs created in 8.1 and later, the default value is the greater of `30d` or 20 times `bucket_span`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|
|» » per_partition_categorization|body|object|false|Settings related to how categorization interacts with partition fields.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|To enable this setting, you must also set the `partition_field_name` property to the same value in every detector that uses the keyword `mlcategory`. Otherwise, job creation fails.|
|» » » stop_on_warn|body|boolean|false|This setting can be set to true only if per-partition categorization is enabled. If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn. This setting makes it viable to have a job where it is expected that categorization works well for some partitions but not others; you do not pay the cost of bad categorization forever in the partitions where it works badly.|
|» » summary_count_field_name|body|object|false|If this property is specified, the data that is fed to the job is expected to be pre-summarized. This property value is the name of the field that contains the count of raw data points that have been summarized. The same `summary_count_field_name` applies to all detectors in the job. NOTE: The `summary_count_field_name` property cannot be used with the `metric` function.|
|» max_bucket_cardinality|body|object|false|Estimates of the highest cardinality in a single bucket that is observed<br>for influencer fields over the time period that the job analyzes data.<br>To produce a good answer, values must be provided for all influencer<br>fields. Providing values for fields that are not listed as `influencers`<br>has no effect on the estimation.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number|false|none|
|» overall_cardinality|body|object|false|Estimates of the cardinality that is observed for fields over the whole<br>time period that the job analyzes data. To produce a good answer, values<br>must be provided for fields referenced in the `by_field_name`,<br>`over_field_name` and `partition_field_name` of any detectors. Providing<br>values for other fields has no effect on the estimation. It can be<br>omitted from the request if no detectors have a `by_field_name`,<br>`over_field_name` or `partition_field_name`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number|false|none|
