## Force buffered data to be processed

<a id="opIdml-flush-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_flush \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"calc_interim\": true\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_flush`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

The flush jobs API is only applicable when sending data for analysis using
the post data API. Depending on the content of the buffer, then it might
additionally calculate new results. Both flush and close operations are
similar, however the flush is more efficient if you are expecting to send
more data for analysis. When flushing, the job remains open and is available
to continue analyzing data. A close operation additionally prunes and
persists the model state to disk and the job must be opened again before
analyzing further data.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"calc_interim\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="force-buffered-data-to-be-processed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|advance_time|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Specifies to advance to a particular time value. Results are generated<br>and the model is updated for data from the specified time interval.|
|calc_interim|query|boolean|false|If true, calculates the interim results for the most recent bucket or all<br>buckets within the latency period.|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|When used in conjunction with `calc_interim` and `start`, specifies the<br>range of buckets on which to calculate interim results.|
|skip_time|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Specifies to skip to a particular time value. Results are not generated<br>and the model is not updated for data from the specified time interval.|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|When used in conjunction with `calc_interim`, specifies the range of<br>buckets on which to calculate interim results.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» advance_time|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `advance_time` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» calc_interim|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `calc_interim` query parameter.|
|» end|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `end` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» skip_time|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `skip_time` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» start|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `start` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|

```json
  "flushed": true,
  "last_finalized_bucket_end": 0
}
```

## Get anomaly detection job results for buckets

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/results/buckets/string \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"anomaly_score\": 80,\n  \"start\": \"1454530200001\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/results/buckets/{timestamp}`

The API presents a chronological view of the records, grouped by bucket.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`

```json
"{\n  \"anomaly_score\": 80,\n  \"start\": \"1454530200001\"\n}"
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|timestamp|path|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|true|The timestamp of a single bucket result. If you do not specify this<br>parameter, the API returns information about all buckets.|
|anomaly_score|query|number|false|Returns buckets with anomaly scores greater or equal than this value.|

|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of buckets to obtain.|
|sort|query|object|false|Specifies the sort field for the requested buckets.|
|start|query|object|false|Returns buckets with timestamps after this time. `-1` means it is unset<br>and results are not limited to specific timestamps.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» anomaly_score|body|number|false|Refer to the description for the `anomaly_score` query parameter.|
|» desc|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `desc` query parameter.|
|» end|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `end` query parameter.|

|» exclude_interim|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `exclude_interim` query parameter.|
|» expand|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `expand` query parameter.|
|» page|body|object|false|none|

## Get datafeed stats

<a id="opIdml-get-datafeed-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_stats`

You can get statistics for multiple datafeeds in a single API request by
using a comma-separated list of datafeeds or a wildcard expression. You can
get statistics for all datafeeds by using `_all`, by specifying `*` as the
`<feed_id>`, or by omitting the `<feed_id>`. If the datafeed is stopped, the
only information you receive is the `datafeed_id` and the `state`.
This API returns a maximum of 10,000 datafeeds.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-datafeed-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Ids](#schema_types.ids)|true|Identifier for the datafeed. It can be a datafeed identifier or a<br>wildcard expression. If you do not specify one of these options, the API<br>returns information about all datafeeds.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no datafeeds that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is `true`, which returns an empty `datafeeds` array<br>when there are no matches and the subset of results when there are<br>partial matches. If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a<br>`404` status code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "datafeeds": [
    {
      "assignment_explanation": "string",
      "datafeed_id": {},
      "node": {
        "name": {},
        "ephemeral_id": {},
        "id": {},
        "transport_address": {},
        "attributes": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        }
      },
      "state": {},
      "timing_stats": {
        "bucket_count": 0,
        "exponential_average_search_time_per_hour_ms": {},
        "exponential_average_calculation_context": {
          "incremental_metric_value_ms": {},
          "latest_timestamp": {},
          "previous_exponential_average_ms": {}
        },
        "job_id": {},
        "search_count": 0,
        "total_search_time_ms": {},
        "average_search_time_per_bucket_ms": {}
      },
      "running_state": {
        "real_time_configured": true,
        "real_time_running": true,
        "search_interval": {
          "end": {},
          "end_ms": {},
          "start": {},
          "start_ms": {}
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-datafeed-stats-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-datafeed-stats-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|datafeeds|[[ml._types.DatafeedStats](#schemaml._types.datafeedstats)]|true|none|none|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-datafeed-stats-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|datafeeds|[[ml._types.DatafeedStats](#schemaml._types.datafeedstats)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get datafeeds configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-datafeeds-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/datafeeds`

You can get information for multiple datafeeds in a single API request by
using a comma-separated list of datafeeds or a wildcard expression. You can
get information for all datafeeds by using `_all`, by specifying `*` as the
`<feed_id>`, or by omitting the `<feed_id>`.
This API returns a maximum of 10,000 datafeeds.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-datafeeds-configuration-info-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no datafeeds that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is `true`, which returns an empty `datafeeds` array<br>when there are no matches and the subset of results when there are<br>partial matches. If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a<br>`404` status code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

## Get filters

<a id="opIdml-get-filters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/filters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/filters`

You can get a single filter or all filters.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="get-filters-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of filters.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of filters to obtain.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "filters": [
    {
      "description": "string",
      "filter_id": {},
      "items": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-filters-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-filters-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|filters|[[ml._types.Filter](#schemaml._types.filter)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Get anomaly detection job results for influencers

<a id="opIdml-get-influencers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/results/influencers \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "page": {
      "from": 0,
      "size": 10000
    }
  }'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/results/influencers`

Influencers are the entities that have contributed to, or are to blame for,
the anomalies. Influencer results are available only if an
`influencer_field_name` is specified in the job configuration.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "page": {
    "from": 0,
    "size": 10000
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-results-for-influencers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|desc|query|boolean|false|If true, the results are sorted in descending order.|
|end|query|object|false|Returns influencers with timestamps earlier than this time.<br>The default value means it is unset and results are not limited to<br>specific timestamps.|
|exclude_interim|query|boolean|false|If true, the output excludes interim results. By default, interim results<br>are included.|
|influencer_score|query|number|false|Returns influencers with anomaly scores greater than or equal to this<br>value.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of influencers.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of influencers to obtain.|
|sort|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|Specifies the sort field for the requested influencers. By default, the<br>influencers are sorted by the `influencer_score` value.|
|start|query|object|false|Returns influencers with timestamps after this time. The default value<br>means it is unset and results are not limited to specific timestamps.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» page|body|object|false|Configures pagination.<br>This parameter has the `from` and `size` properties.|
|» » from|body|number|false|Skips the specified number of items.|
|» » size|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of items to obtain.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "influencers": [
    {
      "bucket_span": {},
      "influencer_score": 0,
      "influencer_field_name": {},
      "influencer_field_value": "string",
      "initial_influencer_score": 0,
      "is_interim": true,
      "job_id": {},
      "probability": 0,
      "result_type": "string",
      "timestamp": {},
      "foo": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-results-for-influencers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-results-for-influencers-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|influencers|[[ml._types.Influencer](#schemaml._types.influencer)]|true|none|Array of influencer objects|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If `true`, the API returns an empty `jobs` array when<br>there are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial<br>matches. ## Get anomaly detection job stats

<a id="opIdml-get-job-stats-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_stats`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-stats-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. It can be a job identifier, a<br>group name, a comma-separated list of jobs, or a wildcard expression. If<br>you do not specify one of these options, the API returns information for<br>all anomaly detection jobs.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If `true`, the API returns an empty `jobs` array when<br>there are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial<br>matches. If `false`, the API returns a `404` status<br>code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|

## Get anomaly detection jobs configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-jobs-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors`

You can get information for multiple anomaly detection jobs in a single API
request by using a group name, a comma-separated list of jobs, or a wildcard
expression. You can get information for all anomaly detection jobs by using
`_all`, by specifying `*` as the `<job_id>`, or by omitting the `<job_id>`.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-jobs-configuration-info-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is `true`, which returns an empty `jobs` array when<br>there are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial<br>matches. If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a `404` status<br>code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

## Get anomaly detection job model snapshot upgrade usage info

<a id="opIdml-get-model-snapshot-upgrade-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots/string/_upgrade/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots/{snapshot_id}/_upgrade/_stats`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-anomaly-detection-job-model-snapshot-upgrade-usage-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|snapshot_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the model snapshot. You can get information for multiple<br>snapshots by using a comma-separated list or a wildcard expression. You can get all snapshots by using `_all`,<br>by specifying `*` as the snapshot ID, or by omitting the snapshot ID.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br> -  Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br> -  Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br> -  Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value is true, which returns an empty jobs array when there are no matches and the subset of results<br>when there are partial matches. If this parameter is false, the request returns a 404 status code when there are<br>no matches or only partial matches.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "model_snapshot_upgrades": [
    {
      "job_id": {},
      "snapshot_id": {},
      "state": {},
      "node": {

          "name": {},

          "external_id": "string",

            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          },
          "roles": [
            "string"
          ],

          "min_index_version": 0,
          "max_index_version": 0
        },
        "property2": {
          "name": {},
          "ephemeral_id": {},
          "transport_address": {},
          "external_id": "string",
          "attributes": {
            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          },
          "roles": [
            "string"
          ],
          "version": {},
          "min_index_version": 0,
          "max_index_version": 0
        }
      },
      "assignment_explanation": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get model snapshots info

<a id="opIdml-get-model-snapshots-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"start\": \"1575402236000\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"start\": \"1575402236000\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-model-snapshots-info-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|desc|query|boolean|false|If true, the results are sorted in descending order.|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Returns snapshots with timestamps earlier than this time.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of snapshots.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of snapshots to obtain.|
|sort|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|Specifies the sort field for the requested snapshots. By default, the<br>snapshots are sorted by their timestamp.|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Returns snapshots with timestamps after this time.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» desc|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `desc` query parameter.|
|» end|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `end` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» page|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|number|false|Skips the specified number of items.|
|» » size|body|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of items to obtain.|

## Get overall bucket results

<a id="opIdml-get-overall-buckets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/results/overall_buckets \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"overall_score\": 80,\n  \"start\": \"1403532000000\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/results/overall_buckets`

Retrievs overall bucket results that summarize the bucket results of
multiple anomaly detection jobs.

The `overall_score` is calculated by combining the scores of all the
buckets within the overall bucket span. First, the maximum
`anomaly_score` per anomaly detection job in the overall bucket is
calculated. Then the `top_n` of those scores are averaged to result in
the `overall_score`. This means that you can fine-tune the
`overall_score` so that it is more or less sensitive to the number of
jobs that detect an anomaly at the same time. For example, if you set
`top_n` to `1`, the `overall_score` is the maximum bucket score in the
overall bucket. Alternatively, if you set `top_n` to the number of jobs,
the `overall_score` is high only when all jobs detect anomalies in that
overall bucket. If you set the `bucket_span` parameter (to a value
greater than its default), the `overall_score` is the maximum
`overall_score` of the overall buckets that have a span equal to the
jobs' largest bucket span.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"overall_score\": 80,\n  \"start\": \"1403532000000\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-overall-bucket-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. It can be a job identifier, a<br>group name, a comma-separated list of jobs or groups, or a wildcard<br>expression.<br><br>You can summarize the bucket results for all anomaly detection jobs by<br>using `_all` or by specifying `*` as the `<job_id>`.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If `true`, the request returns an empty `jobs` array when there are no<br>matches and the subset of results when there are partial matches. If this<br>parameter is `false`, the request returns a `404` status code when there<br>are no matches or only partial matches.|
|bucket_span|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The span of the overall buckets. Must be greater or equal to the largest<br>bucket span of the specified anomaly detection jobs, which is the default<br>value.<br><br>By default, an overall bucket has a span equal to the largest bucket span<br>of the specified anomaly detection jobs. To override that behavior, use<br>the optional `bucket_span` parameter.|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Returns overall buckets with timestamps earlier than this time.|
|exclude_interim|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the output excludes interim results.|
|overall_score|query|number|false|Returns overall buckets with overall scores greater than or equal to this<br>value.|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Returns overall buckets with timestamps after this time.|
|top_n|query|number|false|The number of top anomaly detection job bucket scores to be used in the<br>`overall_score` calculation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_no_match|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `allow_no_match` query parameter.|
|» bucket_span|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `bucket_span` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» end|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `end` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[_types.EpochTimeUnitMillis](#schema_types.epochtimeunitmillis)|false|none|
|» exclude_interim|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `exclude_interim` query parameter.|
|» overall_score|body|number|false|Refer to the description for the `overall_score` query parameter.|

## Get anomaly records for an anomaly detection job

<a id="opIdml-get-records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/results/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"sort\": \"record_score\",\n  \"desc\": true,\n  \"start\": \"1454944100000\"\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/results/records`

Records contain the detailed analytical results. They describe the anomalous
activity that has been identified in the input data based on the detector
configuration.
There can be many anomaly records depending on the characteristics and size
of the input data. In practice, there are often too many to be able to
manually process them. The machine learning features therefore perform a
sophisticated aggregation of the anomaly records into buckets.
The number of record results depends on the number of anomalies found in each
bucket, which relates to the number of time series being modeled and the
number of detectors.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"sort\": \"record_score\",\n  \"desc\": true,\n  \"start\": \"1454944100000\"\n}"
```

|desc|query|boolean|false|If true, the results are sorted in descending order.|
|end|query|object|false|Returns records with timestamps earlier than this time. The default value<br>means results are not limited to specific timestamps.|
|exclude_interim|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the output excludes interim results.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of records.|
|record_score|query|number|false|Returns records with anomaly scores greater or equal than this value.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of records to obtain.|
|sort|query|object|false|Specifies the sort field for the requested records.|
|start|query|object|false|Returns records with timestamps after this time. The default value means<br>results are not limited to specific timestamps.|

|» exclude_interim|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `exclude_interim` query parameter.|

|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of records.|
|record_score|query|number|false|Returns records with anomaly scores greater or equal than this value.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of records to obtain.|
|sort|query|object|false|Specifies the sort field for the requested records.|
|start|query|object|false|Returns records with timestamps after this time. The default value means<br>results are not limited to specific timestamps.|

## Open anomaly detection jobs

<a id="opIdml-open-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_open \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"timeout\": \"35m\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_open`

An anomaly detection job must be opened to be ready to receive and analyze
data. It can be opened and closed multiple times throughout its lifecycle.
When you open a new job, it starts with an empty model.
When you open an existing job, the most recent model state is automatically
loaded. The job is ready to resume its analysis from where it left off, once
new data is received.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"timeout\": \"35m\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="open-anomaly-detection-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the time to wait until a job has opened.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» timeout|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `timeout` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"opened\": true,\n  \"node\": \"node-1\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="open-anomaly-detection-jobs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="open-anomaly-detection-jobs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|opened|boolean|true|none|none|
|node|object|true|none|The ID of the node that the job was started on. In serverless this will be the "serverless".<br>If the job is allowed to open lazily and has not yet been assigned to a node, this value is an empty string.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Send data to an anomaly detection job for analysis

<a id="opIdml-post-data"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_data \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {}
  ]'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_data`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

IMPORTANT: For each job, data can be accepted from only a single connection at a time.
It is not currently possible to post data to multiple jobs using wildcards or a comma-separated list.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {}
]
```

<h3 id="send-data-to-an-anomaly-detection-job-for-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job. The job must have a state of open to receive and process the data.|
|reset_end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Specifies the end of the bucket resetting range.|
|reset_start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|Specifies the start of the bucket resetting range.|
|body|body|[object]|true|none|

`GET /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_preview`

This API returns the first "page" of search results from a datafeed.
You can preview an existing datafeed or provide configuration details for a datafeed
and anomaly detection job in the API. The preview shows the structure of the data
that will be passed to the anomaly detection engine.
IMPORTANT: When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the preview uses the credentials of the user that
called the API. However, when the datafeed starts it uses the roles of the last user that created or updated the
datafeed. To get a preview that accurately reflects the behavior of the datafeed, use the appropriate credentials.
You can also use secondary authorization headers to supply the credentials.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`

|» » » categorization_filters|body|[string]|false|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering, use the `categorization_analyzer` property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters. The effect is exactly the same.|

|» » » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|To enable this setting, you must also set the `partition_field_name` property to the same value in every detector that uses the keyword `mlcategory`. Otherwise, job creation fails.|
|» » » » stop_on_warn|body|boolean|false|This setting can be set to true only if per-partition categorization is enabled. If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn. This setting makes it viable to have a job where it is expected that categorization works well for some partitions but not others; you do not pay the cost of bad categorization forever in the partitions where it works badly.|
|» » » summary_count_field_name|body|object|false|If this property is specified, the data that is fed to the job is expected to be pre-summarized. |» » » model_memory_limit|body|object|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

`POST /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_preview`

This API returns the first "page" of search results from a datafeed.
You can preview an existing datafeed or provide configuration details for a datafeed
and anomaly detection job in the API. The preview shows the structure of the data
that will be passed to the anomaly detection engine.
IMPORTANT: When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the preview uses the credentials of the user that
called the API. However, when the datafeed starts it uses the roles of the last user that created or updated the
datafeed. To get a preview that accurately reflects the behavior of the datafeed, use the appropriate credentials.
You can also use secondary authorization headers to supply the credentials.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`

<h3 id="preview-a-datafeed-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This identifier can contain lowercase<br>alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric<br>characters. NOTE: If you use this path parameter, you cannot provide datafeed or anomaly detection job<br>configuration details in the request body.|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The start time from where the datafeed preview should begin|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The end time when the datafeed preview should stop|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» datafeed_config|body|object|false|The datafeed definition to preview.|
|» » aggregations|body|object|false|If set, the datafeed performs aggregation searches. Support for aggregations is limited and should be used only with low cardinality data.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.aggregations.AggregationContainer](#schema_types.aggregations.aggregationcontainer)|false|none|
|» » chunking_config|body|object|false|Datafeeds might be required to search over long time periods, for several months or years. This search is split into time chunks in order to ensure the load on Elasticsearch is managed. Chunking configuration controls how the size of these time chunks are calculated and is an advanced configuration option.|
|» » » mode|body|object|true|If the mode is `auto`, the chunk size is dynamically calculated;<br>this is the recommended value when the datafeed does not use aggregations.<br>If the mode is `manual`, chunking is applied according to the specified `time_span`;<br>use this mode when the datafeed uses aggregations. If the mode is `off`, no chunking is applied.|
|» » » time_span|body|object|false|The time span that each search will be querying. This setting is applicable only when the `mode` is set to `manual`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» » » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn. This setting makes it viable to have a job where it is expected that categorization works well for some partitions but not others; you do not pay the cost of bad categorization forever in the partitions where it works badly.|

NOTE: The `categorization_examples_limit` applies only to analysis that uses categorization.|
|» » » model_memory_limit|body|object|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

`GET /_ml/datafeeds/_preview`

This API returns the first "page" of search results from a datafeed.
You can preview an existing datafeed or provide configuration details for a datafeed
and anomaly detection job in the API. The preview shows the structure of the data
that will be passed to the anomaly detection engine.
IMPORTANT: When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the preview uses the credentials of the user that
called the API. However, when the datafeed starts it uses the roles of the last user that created or updated the
datafeed. To get a preview that accurately reflects the behavior of the datafeed, use the appropriate credentials.
You can also use secondary authorization headers to supply the credentials.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`

<h3 id="preview-a-datafeed-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The start time from where the datafeed preview should begin|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The end time when the datafeed preview should stop|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» datafeed_config|body|object|false|The datafeed definition to preview.|
|» » aggregations|body|object|false|If set, the datafeed performs aggregation searches. Support for aggregations is limited and should be used only with low cardinality data.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.aggregations.AggregationContainer](#schema_types.aggregations.aggregationcontainer)|false|none|
|» » chunking_config|body|object|false|Datafeeds might be required to search over long time periods, for several months or years. This search is split into time chunks in order to ensure the load on Elasticsearch is managed. Chunking configuration controls how the size of these time chunks are calculated and is an advanced configuration option.|
|» » » mode|body|object|true|If the mode is `auto`, the chunk size is dynamically calculated;<br>this is the recommended value when the datafeed does not use aggregations.<br>If the mode is `manual`, chunking is applied according to the specified `time_span`;<br>use this mode when the datafeed uses aggregations. If the mode is `off`, no chunking is applied.|
|» » » time_span|body|object|false|The time span that each search will be querying. This setting is applicable only when the `mode` is set to `manual`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » datafeed_id|body|object|false|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters. The default value is the job identifier.|
|» » delayed_data_check_config|body|object|false|Specifies whether the datafeed checks for missing data and the size of the window. The datafeed can optionally search over indices that have already been read in an effort to determine whether any data has subsequently been added to the index. If missing data is found, it is a good indication that the `query_delay` option is set too low and the data is being indexed after the datafeed has passed that moment in time. This check runs only on real-time datafeeds.|
|» » » check_window|body|object|false|The window of time that is searched for late data. This window of time ends with the latest finalized bucket.<br>It defaults to null, which causes an appropriate `check_window` to be calculated when the real-time datafeed runs.<br>In particular, the default `check_window` span calculation is based on the maximum of `2h` or `8 * bucket_span`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|Specifies whether the datafeed periodically checks for delayed data.|
|» » frequency|body|object|false|The interval at which scheduled queries are made while the datafeed runs in real time. The default value is either the bucket span for short bucket spans, or, for longer bucket spans, a sensible fraction of the bucket span. For example: `150s`. When `frequency` is shorter than the bucket span, interim results for the last (partial) bucket are written then eventually overwritten by the full bucket results. If the datafeed uses aggregations, this value must be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » indices|body|object|false|An array of index names. Wildcards are supported. If any indices are in remote clusters, the machine learning nodes must have the `remote_cluster_client` role.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|
|» » indices_options|body|object|false|Specifies index expansion options that are used during search.|
|» » » allow_no_indices|body|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|» » » expand_wildcards|body|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument<br>determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values,<br>such as `open,hidden`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.ExpandWildcard](#schema_types.expandwildcard)|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.ExpandWildcard](#schema_types.expandwildcard)]|false|none|
|» » » ignore_unavailable|body|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|» » » ignore_throttled|body|boolean|false|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|» » job_id|body|object|false|none|
|» » max_empty_searches|body|number|false|If a real-time datafeed has never seen any data (including during any initial training period) then it will automatically stop itself and close its associated job after this many real-time searches that return no documents. In other words, it will stop after `frequency` times `max_empty_searches` of real-time operation. If not set then a datafeed with no end time that sees no data will remain started until it is explicitly stopped.|
|» » max_consecutive_extraction_failures|body|number|false|The maximum number of consecutive real-time data extraction failures the datafeed tolerates before it automatically stops itself, leaving the associated job open. The consecutive-failure counter resets on any cycle that extracts successfully, including empty-data cycles. If not set, the threshold defaults to roughly one day's worth of searches based on the datafeed `frequency` (floored at 1). Set to `-1` to disable auto-stop and retry indefinitely. Values of `0` or less than `-1` are rejected.|
|» » query|body|object|false|The Elasticsearch query domain-specific language (DSL). This value corresponds to the query object in an Elasticsearch search POST body. All the options that are supported by Elasticsearch can be used, as this object is passed verbatim to Elasticsearch.|
|» » » bool|body|object|false|matches documents matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|» » » boosting|body|object|false|Returns documents matching a `positive` query while reducing the relevance score of documents that also match a `negative` query.|
|» » » common|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.query_dsl.CommonTermsQuery](#schema_types.query_dsl.commontermsquery)|false|none|
|» » » combined_fields|body|object|false|The `combined_fields` query supports searching multiple text fields as if their contents had been indexed into one combined field.|
|» » » » boost|body|number|false|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|

|» » » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

|» » » model_memory_limit|body|object|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

|» » model_snapshot_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job.<br>It specifies the maximum period of time (in days) that snapshots are retained.<br>This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.<br>The default value is `10`, which means snapshots ten days older than the newest snapshot are deleted.|
|» » renormalization_window_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period over which adjustments to the score are applied, as new data is seen.<br>The default value is the longer of 30 days or 100 `bucket_spans`.|

|» » results_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period of time (in days) that results are retained.<br>Age is calculated relative to the timestamp of the latest bucket result.<br>If this property has a non-null value, once per day at 00:30 (server time), results that are the specified number of days older than the latest bucket result are deleted from Elasticsearch.<br>The default value is null, which means all results are retained.<br>Annotations generated by the system also count as results for retention purposes; they are deleted after the same number of days as results.<br>Annotations added by users are retained forever.|

`POST /_ml/datafeeds/_preview`

This API returns the first "page" of search results from a datafeed.
You can preview an existing datafeed or provide configuration details for a datafeed
and anomaly detection job in the API. The preview shows the structure of the data
that will be passed to the anomaly detection engine.
IMPORTANT: When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the preview uses the credentials of the user that
called the API. However, when the datafeed starts it uses the roles of the last user that created or updated the
datafeed. To get a preview that accurately reflects the behavior of the datafeed, use the appropriate credentials.
You can also use secondary authorization headers to supply the credentials.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`

<h3 id="preview-a-datafeed-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The start time from where the datafeed preview should begin|
|end|query|[_types.DateTime](#schema_types.datetime)|false|The end time when the datafeed preview should stop|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» datafeed_config|body|object|false|The datafeed definition to preview.|
|» » aggregations|body|object|false|If set, the datafeed performs aggregation searches. Support for aggregations is limited and should be used only with low cardinality data.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.aggregations.AggregationContainer](#schema_types.aggregations.aggregationcontainer)|false|none|
|» » chunking_config|body|object|false|Datafeeds might be required to search over long time periods, for several months or years. This search is split into time chunks in order to ensure the load on Elasticsearch is managed. Chunking configuration controls how the size of these time chunks are calculated and is an advanced configuration option.|
|» » » mode|body|object|true|If the mode is `auto`, the chunk size is dynamically calculated;<br>this is the recommended value when the datafeed does not use aggregations.<br>If the mode is `manual`, chunking is applied according to the specified `time_span`;<br>use this mode when the datafeed uses aggregations. If the mode is `off`, no chunking is applied.|
|» » » time_span|body|object|false|The time span that each search will be querying. This setting is applicable only when the `mode` is set to `manual`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » datafeed_id|body|object|false|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters. The default value is the job identifier.|
|» » delayed_data_check_config|body|object|false|Specifies whether the datafeed checks for missing data and the size of the window. The datafeed can optionally search over indices that have already been read in an effort to determine whether any data has subsequently been added to the index. If missing data is found, it is a good indication that the `query_delay` option is set too low and the data is being indexed after the datafeed has passed that moment in time. This check runs only on real-time datafeeds.|
|» » » check_window|body|object|false|The window of time that is searched for late data. This window of time ends with the latest finalized bucket.<br>It defaults to null, which causes an appropriate `check_window` to be calculated when the real-time datafeed runs.<br>In particular, the default `check_window` span calculation is based on the maximum of `2h` or `8 * bucket_span`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|Specifies whether the datafeed periodically checks for delayed data.|
|» » frequency|body|object|false|The interval at which scheduled queries are made while the datafeed runs in real time. The default value is either the bucket span for short bucket spans, or, for longer bucket spans, a sensible fraction of the bucket span. For example: `150s`. When `frequency` is shorter than the bucket span, interim results for the last (partial) bucket are written then eventually overwritten by the full bucket results. If the datafeed uses aggregations, this value must be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » indices|body|object|false|An array of index names. Wildcards are supported. If any indices are in remote clusters, the machine learning nodes must have the `remote_cluster_client` role.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|
|» » indices_options|body|object|false|Specifies index expansion options that are used during search.|
|» » » allow_no_indices|body|boolean|false|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|» » » expand_wildcards|body|object|false|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument<br>determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values,<br>such as `open,hidden`.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[_types.ExpandWildcard](#schema_types.expandwildcard)|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[[_types.ExpandWildcard](#schema_types.expandwildcard)]|false|none|
|» » » ignore_unavailable|body|boolean|false|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|» » » ignore_throttled|body|boolean|false|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|
|» » job_id|body|object|false|none|
|» » max_empty_searches|body|number|false|If a real-time datafeed has never seen any data (including during any initial training period) then it will automatically stop itself and close its associated job after this many real-time searches that return no documents. In other words, it will stop after `frequency` times `max_empty_searches` of real-time operation. If not set then a datafeed with no end time that sees no data will remain started until it is explicitly stopped.|
|» » max_consecutive_extraction_failures|body|number|false|The maximum number of consecutive real-time data extraction failures the datafeed tolerates before it automatically stops itself, leaving the associated job open. The consecutive-failure counter resets on any cycle that extracts successfully, including empty-data cycles. If not set, the threshold defaults to roughly one day's worth of searches based on the datafeed `frequency` (floored at 1). Set to `-1` to disable auto-stop and retry indefinitely. Values of `0` or less than `-1` are rejected.|

|» » » multivariate_by_fields|body|boolean|false|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

|» » » model_memory_limit|body|object|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

## Reset an anomaly detection job

<a id="opIdml-reset-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_reset`

All model state and results are deleted. The job is ready to start over as if
it had just been created.
It is not currently possible to reset multiple jobs using wildcards or a
comma separated list.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="reset-an-anomaly-detection-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the job to reset.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|Should this request wait until the operation has completed before<br>returning.|
|delete_user_annotations|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether annotations that have been added by the<br>user should be deleted along with any auto-generated annotations when the job is<br>reset.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="reset-an-anomaly-detection-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Revert to a snapshot

<a id="opIdml-revert-model-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots/string/_revert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"delete_intervening_results\": true\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots/{snapshot_id}/_revert`

The machine learning features react quickly to anomalous input, learning new
behaviors in data. Highly anomalous input increases the variance in the
models whilst the system learns whether this is a new step-change in behavior
or a one-off event. In the case where this anomalous input is known to be a
one-off, then it might be appropriate to reset the model state to a time
before this event. For example, you might consider reverting to a saved
snapshot after Black Friday or a critical system failure.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"delete_intervening_results\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="revert-to-a-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|snapshot_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|You can specify `empty` as the <snapshot_id>. Reverting to the empty<br>snapshot means the anomaly detection job starts learning a new model from<br>scratch when it is started.|
|delete_intervening_results|query|boolean|false|If true, deletes the results in the time period between the latest<br>results and the time of the reverted snapshot. It also resets the model<br>to accept records for this time period. If you choose not to delete<br>intervening results when reverting a snapshot, the job will not accept<br>input data that is older than the current time. If you want to resend<br>data, then delete the intervening results.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» delete_intervening_results|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `delete_intervening_results` query parameter.|

## Start datafeeds

<a id="opIdml-start-datafeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string/_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"start\": \"2019-04-07T18:22:16Z\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_start`

A datafeed must be started in order to retrieve data from Elasticsearch. A datafeed can be started and stopped
multiple times throughout its lifecycle.

Before you can start a datafeed, the anomaly detection job must be open. Otherwise, an error occurs.

If you restart a stopped datafeed, it continues processing input data from the next millisecond after it was stopped.
If new data was indexed for that exact millisecond between stopping and starting, it will be ignored.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, your datafeed remembers which roles the last user to create or
update it had at the time of creation or update and runs the query using those same roles. If you provided secondary
authorization headers when you created or updated the datafeed, those credentials are used instead.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"start\": \"2019-04-07T18:22:16Z\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="start-datafeeds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This identifier can contain lowercase<br>alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric<br>characters.|

## Stop datafeeds

<a id="opIdml-stop-datafeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string/_stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"timeout\": \"30s\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_stop`

A datafeed that is stopped ceases to retrieve data from Elasticsearch. A datafeed can be started and stopped
multiple times throughout its lifecycle.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"timeout\": \"30s\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="stop-datafeeds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datafeed_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the datafeed. You can stop multiple datafeeds in a single API request by using a comma-separated<br>list of datafeeds or a wildcard expression. You can close all datafeeds by using `_all` or by specifying `*` as<br>the identifier.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>* Contains wildcard expressions and there are no datafeeds that match.<br>* Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>* Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If `true`, the API returns an empty datafeeds array when there are no matches and the subset of results when<br>there are partial matches. If `false`, the API returns a 404 status code when there are no matches or only<br>partial matches.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the datafeed is stopped forcefully.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Specifies the amount of time to wait until a datafeed stops.|
|close_job|query|boolean|false|If `true` the job associated with the datafeed is closed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_no_match|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `allow_no_match` query parameter.|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `force` query parameter.|
|» timeout|body|object|false|Refer to the description for the `timeout` query parameter.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» close_job|body|boolean|false|Refer to the description for the `close_job` query parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "stopped": true
}
```

<h3 id="stop-datafeeds-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stopped|boolean|true|none|none|

## Update a datafeed

<a id="opIdml-update-datafeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/datafeeds/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"term\": {\n      \"geo.src\": \"US\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/datafeeds/{datafeed_id}/_update`

You must stop and start the datafeed for the changes to be applied.
When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, your datafeed remembers which roles the user who updated it had at
the time of the update and runs the query using those same roles. If you provide secondary authorization headers,
those credentials are used instead.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"query\": {\n    \"term\": {\n      \"geo.src\": \"US\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```
