## Update a filter

<a id="opIdml-update-filter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/filters/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"description\": \"Updated list of domains\",\n  \"add_items\": [\"*.myorg.com\"],\n  \"remove_items\": [\"wikipedia.org\"]\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/filters/{filter_id}/_update`

Updates the description of a filter, adds items, or removes items from the list.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"description\": \"Updated list of domains\",\n  \"add_items\": [\"*.myorg.com\"],\n  \"remove_items\": [\"wikipedia.org\"]\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-a-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A string that uniquely identifies a filter.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» add_items|body|[string]|false|The items to add to the filter.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the filter.|
|» remove_items|body|[string]|false|The items to remove from the filter.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "filter_id": {},
  "items": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-filter-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="update-a-filter-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|true|none|none|
|filter_id|object|true|none|none|
|items|[string]|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update an anomaly detection job

<a id="opIdml-update-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"description\":\"An updated job\",\n  \"detectors\": {\n    \"detector_index\": 0,\n    \"description\": \"An updated detector description\"\n  },\n  \"groups\": [\"kibana_sample_data\",\"kibana_sample_web_logs\"],\n  \"model_plot_config\": {\n    \"enabled\": true\n  },\n  \"renormalization_window_days\": 30,\n  \"background_persist_interval\": \"2h\",\n  \"model_snapshot_retention_days\": 7,\n  \"results_retention_days\": 60\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/_update`

Updates certain properties of an anomaly detection job.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"description\":\"An updated job\",\n  \"detectors\": {\n    \"detector_index\": 0,\n    \"description\": \"An updated detector description\"\n  },\n  \"groups\": [\"kibana_sample_data\",\"kibana_sample_web_logs\"],\n  \"model_plot_config\": {\n    \"enabled\": true\n  },\n  \"renormalization_window_days\": 30,\n  \"background_persist_interval\": \"2h\",\n  \"model_snapshot_retention_days\": 7,\n  \"results_retention_days\": 60\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-an-anomaly-detection-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the job.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_lazy_open|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether this job can open when<br>there is insufficient machine learning node capacity for it to be<br>immediately assigned to a node. If `false` and a machine learning node<br>with capacity to run the job cannot immediately be found, the open<br>anomaly detection jobs API returns an error. However, this is also<br>subject to the cluster-wide `xpack.ml.max_lazy_ml_nodes` setting. If this<br>option is set to `true`, the open anomaly detection jobs API does not<br>return an error and the job waits in the opening state until sufficient<br>machine learning node capacity is available.|
|» analysis_limits|body|object|false|none|
|» » model_memory_limit|body|string|true|Limits can be applied for the resources required to hold the mathematical models in memory. These limits are approximate and can be set per job. They do not control the memory used by other processes, for example the Elasticsearch Java processes.|
|» background_persist_interval|body|object|false|Advanced configuration option. The time between each periodic persistence<br>of the model.<br>The default value is a randomized value between 3 to 4 hours, which<br>avoids all jobs persisting at exactly the same time. The smallest allowed<br>value is 1 hour.<br>For very large models (several GB), persistence could take 10-20 minutes,<br>so do not set the value too low.<br>If the job is open when you make the update, you must stop the datafeed,<br>close the job, then reopen the job and restart the datafeed for the<br>changes to take effect.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» custom_settings|body|object|false|Advanced configuration option. Contains custom meta data about the job.<br>For example, it can contain custom URL information as shown in Adding<br>custom URLs to machine learning results.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» categorization_filters|body|[string]|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the job.|
|» model_plot_config|body|object|false|none|
|» » annotations_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, enables calculation and storage of the model change annotations for each entity that is being analyzed.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, enables calculation and storage of the model bounds for each entity that is being analyzed.|
|» » terms|body|object|false|Limits data collection to this comma separated list of partition or by field values. If terms are not specified or it is an empty string, no filtering is applied. Wildcards are not supported. Only the specified terms can be viewed when using the Single Metric Viewer.|
|» model_prune_window|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» daily_model_snapshot_retention_after_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old<br>model snapshots for this job. It specifies a period of time (in days)<br>after which only the first snapshot per day is retained. This period is<br>relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job. Valid<br>values range from 0 to `model_snapshot_retention_days`. For jobs created<br>before version 7.8.0, the default value matches<br>`model_snapshot_retention_days`.|
|» model_snapshot_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old<br>model snapshots for this job. It specifies the maximum period of time (in<br>days) that snapshots are retained. This period is relative to the<br>timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.|
|» renormalization_window_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The period over which adjustments to the<br>score are applied, as new data is seen.|
|» results_retention_days|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The period of time (in days) that results<br>are retained. Age is calculated relative to the timestamp of the latest<br>bucket result. If this property has a non-null value, once per day at<br>00:30 (server time), results that are the specified number of days older<br>than the latest bucket result are deleted from Elasticsearch. The default<br>value is null, which means all results are retained.|
|» groups|body|[string]|false|A list of job groups. A job can belong to no groups or many.|
|» detectors|body|[ml._types.DetectorUpdate](#schemaml._types.detectorupdate) \| [[ml._types.DetectorUpdate](#schemaml._types.detectorupdate)]|false|A detector update object or an array of detector update objects.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ml._types.DetectorUpdate](#schemaml._types.detectorupdate)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[ml._types.DetectorUpdate](#schemaml._types.detectorupdate)]|false|none|
|» per_partition_categorization|body|object|false|Settings related to how categorization interacts with partition fields.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|To enable this setting, you must also set the `partition_field_name` property to the same value in every detector that uses the keyword `mlcategory`. Otherwise, job creation fails.|
|» » stop_on_warn|body|boolean|false|This setting can be set to true only if per-partition categorization is enabled. If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn. This setting makes it viable to have a job where it is expected that categorization works well for some partitions but not others; you do not pay the cost of bad categorization forever in the partitions where it works badly.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

<h3 id="update-an-anomaly-detection-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="update-an-anomaly-detection-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_lazy_open|boolean|true|none|none|
|analysis_config|object|true|none|none|
|» bucket_span|object|true|none|The size of the interval that the analysis is aggregated into, typically between `5m` and `1h`. This value should be either a whole number of days or equate to a<br>whole number of buckets in one day. If the anomaly detection job uses a datafeed with aggregations, this value must also be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» detectors|[[ml._types.DetectorRead](#schemaml._types.detectorread)]|true|none|Detector configuration objects specify which data fields a job analyzes. They also specify which analytical functions are used. You can specify multiple detectors for a job. If the detectors array does not contain at least one detector, no analysis can occur and an error is returned.|
|» influencers|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|true|none|A comma separated list of influencer field names. Typically these can be the by, over, or partition fields that are used in the detector configuration. You might also want to use a field name that is not specifically named in a detector, but is available as part of the input data. When you use multiple detectors, the use of influencers is recommended as it aggregates results for each influencer entity.|
|» categorization_analyzer|object|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define the analyzer that is used to interpret the categorization field. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_filters`. The categorization analyzer specifies how the `categorization_field` is interpreted by the categorization process. The `categorization_analyzer` field can be specified either as a string or as an object. If it is a string, it must refer to a built-in analyzer or one added by another plugin.|
|» » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *oneOf*|[ml._types.CategorizationAnalyzerDefinition](#schemaml._types.categorizationanalyzerdefinition)|false|none|none|
|» categorization_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the values of the specified field will be categorized. The resulting categories must be used in a detector by setting `by_field_name`, `over_field_name`, or `partition_field_name` to the keyword `mlcategory`.|
|» categorization_filters|[string]|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. |» multivariate_by_fields|boolean|false|none|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|

|» model_memory_limit|object|false|none|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

## Update a snapshot

<a id="opIdml-update-model-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"_ml/anomaly_detectors/it_ops_new_logs/model_snapshots/1491852978/_update\n{\n  \"description\": \"Snapshot 1\",\n  \"retain\": true\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots/{snapshot_id}/_update`

Updates certain properties of a snapshot.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"_ml/anomaly_detectors/it_ops_new_logs/model_snapshots/1491852978/_update\n{\n  \"description\": \"Snapshot 1\",\n  \"retain\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-a-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|snapshot_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the model snapshot.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the model snapshot.|
|» retain|body|boolean|false|If `true`, this snapshot will not be deleted during automatic cleanup of<br>snapshots older than `model_snapshot_retention_days`. However, this<br>snapshot will be deleted when the job is deleted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "model": {
    "description": "string",
    "job_id": {},
    "latest_record_time_stamp": 0,
    "latest_result_time_stamp": 0,
```

## Upgrade a snapshot

<a id="opIdml-upgrade-job-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/anomaly_detectors/string/model_snapshots/string/_upgrade \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{job_id}/model_snapshots/{snapshot_id}/_upgrade`

Upgrade an anomaly detection model snapshot to the latest major version.
Over time, older snapshot formats are deprecated and removed. Anomaly
detection jobs support only snapshots that are from the current or previous
major version.
This API provides a means to upgrade a snapshot to the current major version.
This aids in preparing the cluster for an upgrade to the next major version.
Only one snapshot per anomaly detection job can be upgraded at a time and the
upgraded snapshot cannot be the current snapshot of the anomaly detection
job.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="upgrade-a-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|snapshot_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the model snapshot.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|When true, the API won’t respond until the upgrade is complete.<br>Otherwise, it responds as soon as the upgrade task is assigned to a node.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the time to wait for the request to complete.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "node": {},
  "completed": true
}
```

<h3 id="upgrade-a-snapshot-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="upgrade-a-snapshot-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node|object|true|none|The ID of the node that the upgrade task was started on if it is still running. In serverless this will be the "serverless".|
|completed|boolean|true|none|When true, this means the task is complete. When false, it is still running.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-ml-data-frame">ml data frame</h1>

## Get data frame analytics job configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}`

You can get information for multiple data frame analytics jobs in a single
API request by using a comma-separated list of data frame analytics jobs or a
wildcard expression.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-data-frame-analytics-job-configuration-info-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job. If you do not specify this<br>option, the API returns information for the first hundred data frame<br>analytics jobs.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no data frame analytics<br>jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value returns an empty data_frame_analytics array when there<br>are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial matches.<br>If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a 404 status code when<br>there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of data frame analytics jobs.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of data frame analytics jobs to obtain.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

<h3 id="get-data-frame-analytics-job-configuration-info-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|none|
|data_frame_analytics|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalyticsSummary](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalyticssummary)]|true|none|An array of data frame analytics job resources, which are sorted by the id value in ascending order.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a data frame analytics job

<a id="opIdml-put-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": [\n      \"kibana_sample_data_flights\"\n    ],\n    \"query\": {\n      \"range\": {\n        \"DistanceKilometers\": {\n          \"gt\": 0\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"includes\": [],\n      \"excludes\": [\n        \"FlightDelay\",\n        \"FlightDelayType\"\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"df-flight-delays\",\n    \"results_field\": \"ml-results\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n  \"regression\": {\n    \"dependent_variable\": \"FlightDelayMin\",\n    \"training_percent\": 90\n    }\n  },\n  \"analyzed_fields\": {\n    \"includes\": [],\n    \"excludes\": [\n      \"FlightNum\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"model_memory_limit\": \"100mb\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}`

This API creates a data frame analytics job that performs an analysis on the
source indices and stores the outcome in a destination index.
By default, the query used in the source configuration is `{"match_all": {}}`.

If the destination index does not exist, it is created automatically when you start the job.

If you supply only a subset of the regression or classification parameters, hyperparameter optimization occurs. It determines a value for each of the undefined parameters.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `create_index`,`index`,`manage`,`read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": [\n      \"kibana_sample_data_flights\"\n    ],\n    \"query\": {\n      \"range\": {\n        \"DistanceKilometers\": {\n          \"gt\": 0\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"_source\": {\n      \"includes\": [],\n      \"excludes\": [\n        \"FlightDelay\",\n        \"FlightDelayType\"\n      ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"df-flight-delays\",\n    \"results_field\": \"ml-results\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n  \"regression\": {\n    \"dependent_variable\": \"FlightDelayMin\",\n    \"training_percent\": 90\n    }\n  },\n  \"analyzed_fields\": {\n    \"includes\": [],\n    \"excludes\": [\n      \"FlightNum\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"model_memory_limit\": \"100mb\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-frame-analytics-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job. This identifier can contain<br>lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and<br>underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_lazy_start|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether this job can start when there is insufficient machine<br>learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node. If<br>set to `false` and a machine learning node with capacity to run the job<br>cannot be immediately found, the API returns an error. If set to `true`,<br>the API does not return an error; the job waits in the `starting` state<br>until sufficient machine learning node capacity is available. This<br>behavior is also affected by the cluster-wide<br>`xpack.ml.max_lazy_ml_nodes` setting.|
|» analysis|body|object|true|The analysis configuration, which contains the information necessary to<br>perform one of the following types of analysis: classification, outlier<br>detection, or regression.|
|» » classification|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|

<h3 id="create-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorization|object|false|none|none|
|» api_key|object|false|none|If an API key was used for the most recent update to the job, its name and identifier are listed in the response.|
|» » id|string|true|none|The identifier for the API key.|
|» » name|string|true|none|The name of the API key.|
|» roles|[string]|false|none|If a user ID was used for the most recent update to the job, its roles at the time of the update are listed in the response.|
|» service_account|string|false|none|If a service account was used for the most recent update to the job, the account name is listed in the response.|
|allow_lazy_start|boolean|true|none|none|
|analysis|object|true|none|none|
|» classification|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » alpha|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » dependent_variable|string|true|none|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » downsample_factor|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » early_stopping_enabled|boolean|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » eta|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » feature_bag_fraction|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » feature_processors|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » gamma|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » lambda|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » max_trees|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » num_top_feature_importance_values|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » prediction_field_name|object|false|none|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » randomize_seed|number|false|none|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » soft_tree_depth_limit|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » training_percent|object|false|none|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|

## Delete a data frame analytics job

<a id="opIdml-delete-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="delete-a-data-frame-analytics-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If `true`, it deletes a job that is not stopped; this method is quicker than stopping and deleting the job.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The time to wait for the job to be deleted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Evaluate data frame analytics

<a id="opIdml-evaluate-data-frame"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/_evaluate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index\": \"animal_classification\",\n  \"evaluation\": {\n    \"classification\": {\n      \"actual_field\": \"animal_class\",\n      \"predicted_field\": \"ml.animal_class_prediction\",\n      \"metrics\": {\n        \"multiclass_confusion_matrix\": {}\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/_evaluate`

The API packages together commonly used evaluation metrics for various types
of machine learning features. This has been designed for use on indexes
created by data frame analytics. Evaluation requires both a ground truth
field and an analytics result field to be present.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index\": \"animal_classification\",\n  \"evaluation\": {\n    \"classification\": {\n      \"actual_field\": \"animal_class\",\n      \"predicted_field\": \"ml.animal_class_prediction\",\n      \"metrics\": {\n        \"multiclass_confusion_matrix\": {}\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="evaluate-data-frame-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» evaluation|body|object|true|Defines the type of evaluation you want to perform.|
|» » classification|body|object|false|Classification evaluation evaluates the results of a classification analysis which outputs a prediction that identifies to which of the classes each document belongs.|
|» » » actual_field|body|object|true|The field of the index which contains the ground truth. The data type of this field can be boolean or integer. If the data type is integer, the value has to be either 0 (false) or 1 (true).|
|» » » predicted_field|body|object|false|The field in the index which contains the predicted value, in other words the results of the classification analysis.|
|» » » top_classes_field|body|object|false|The field of the index which is an array of documents of the form { "class_name": XXX, "class_probability": YYY }. This field must be defined as nested in the mappings.|
|» » » metrics|body|object|false|Specifies the metrics that are used for the evaluation.|

## Explain data frame analytics config

<a id="opIdml-explain-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/_explain \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics/_explain`

This API provides explanations for a data frame analytics config that either
exists already or one that has not been created yet. The following
explanations are provided:
* which fields are included or not in the analysis and why,
* how much memory is estimated to be required. The estimate can be used when deciding the appropriate value for model_memory_limit setting later on.
If you have object fields or fields that are excluded via source filtering, they are not included in the explanation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » class_assignment_objective|body|string|false|none|
|» » » num_top_classes|body|number|false|Defines the number of categories for which the predicted probabilities are reported. It must be non-negative or -1. If it is -1 or greater than the total number of categories, probabilities are reported for all categories; if you have a large number of categories, there could be a significant effect on the size of your destination index. NOTE: To use the AUC ROC evaluation method, `num_top_classes` must be set to -1 or a value greater than or equal to the total number of categories.|
|» » outlier_detection|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform outlier detection. NOTE: Advanced parameters are for fine-tuning classification analysis. They are set automatically by hyperparameter optimization to give the minimum validation error. It is highly recommended to use the default values unless you fully understand the function of these parameters.|
|» » » compute_feature_influence|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether the feature influence calculation is enabled.|
|» » » feature_influence_threshold|body|number|false|The minimum outlier score that a document needs to have in order to calculate its feature influence score. Value range: 0-1.|
|» » » method|body|string|false|The method that outlier detection uses. Available methods are `lof`, `ldof`, `distance_kth_nn`, `distance_knn`, and `ensemble`. The default value is ensemble, which means that outlier detection uses an ensemble of different methods and normalises and combines their individual outlier scores to obtain the overall outlier score.|
|» » » n_neighbors|body|number|false|Defines the value for how many nearest neighbors each method of outlier detection uses to calculate its outlier score. When the value is not set, different values are used for different ensemble members. This default behavior helps improve the diversity in the ensemble; only override it if you are confident that the value you choose is appropriate for the data set.|
|» » » outlier_fraction|body|number|false|The proportion of the data set that is assumed to be outlying prior to outlier detection. For example, 0.05 means it is assumed that 5% of values are real outliers and 95% are inliers.|
|» » » standardization_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the following operation is performed on the columns before computing outlier scores: `(x_i - mean(x_i)) / sd(x_i)`.|
|» » regression|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform regression. NOTE: Advanced parameters are for fine-tuning regression analysis. They are set automatically by hyperparameter optimization to give the minimum validation error. It is highly recommended to use the default values unless you fully understand the function of these parameters.|
|» » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|

This operation does not require authentication

## Explain data frame analytics config

<a id="opIdml-explain-data-frame-analytics-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/_explain \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/_explain`

This API provides explanations for a data frame analytics config that either
exists already or one that has not been created yet. The following
explanations are provided:
* which fields are included or not in the analysis and why,
* how much memory is estimated to be required. The estimate can be used when deciding the appropriate value for model_memory_limit setting later on.
If you have object fields or fields that are excluded via source filtering, they are not included in the explanation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|

|» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|

|» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. <aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Explain data frame analytics config

<a id="opIdml-explain-data-frame-analytics-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_explain \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_explain`

This API provides explanations for a data frame analytics config that either
exists already or one that has not been created yet. The following
explanations are provided:
* which fields are included or not in the analysis and why,
* how much memory is estimated to be required. The estimate can be used when deciding the appropriate value for model_memory_limit setting later on.
If you have object fields or fields that are excluded via source filtering, they are not included in the explanation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. |» » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. |» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|

Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. |» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|

<h3 id="explain-data-frame-analytics-config-2-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field_selection|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalyticsFieldSelection](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalyticsfieldselection)]|true|none|An array of objects that explain selection for each field, sorted by the field names.|
|memory_estimation|object|true|none|An array of objects that explain selection for each field, sorted by the field names.|
|» expected_memory_with_disk|string|true|none|Estimated memory usage under the assumption that overflowing to disk is allowed during data frame analytics. expected_memory_with_disk is usually smaller than expected_memory_without_disk as using disk allows to limit the main memory needed to perform data frame analytics.|
|» expected_memory_without_disk|string|true|none|Estimated memory usage under the assumption that the whole data frame analytics should happen in memory (i.e. without overflowing to disk).|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Explain data frame analytics config

<a id="opIdml-explain-data-frame-analytics-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_explain \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_explain`

This API provides explanations for a data frame analytics config that either
exists already or one that has not been created yet. The following
explanations are provided:
* which fields are included or not in the analysis and why,
* how much memory is estimated to be required. The estimate can be used when deciding the appropriate value for model_memory_limit setting later on.
If you have object fields or fields that are excluded via source filtering, they are not included in the explanation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n  },\n  \"analysis\": {\n    \"regression\": {\n      \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. |» » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. |» » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. If your `elasticsearch.yml` file contains an<br>`xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to<br>create data frame analytics jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values<br>greater than that setting.|
|» max_num_threads|body|number|false|The maximum number of threads to be used by the analysis. Using more<br>threads may decrease the time necessary to complete the analysis at the<br>cost of using more CPU. Note that the process may use additional threads<br>for operational functionality other than the analysis itself.|
|» analyzed_fields|body|object|false|Specify includes and/or excludes patterns to select which fields will be<br>included in the analysis. The patterns specified in excludes are applied<br>last, therefore excludes takes precedence. In other words, if the same<br>field is specified in both includes and excludes, then the field will not<br>be included in the analysis.|
|» » includes|body|[string]|false|An array of strings that defines the fields that will be excluded from the analysis. You do not need to add fields with unsupported data types to excludes, these fields are excluded from the analysis automatically.|
|» » excludes|body|[string]|false|An array of strings that defines the fields that will be included in the analysis.|
|» allow_lazy_start|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether this job can start when there is insufficient machine<br>learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node.|

<h3 id="explain-data-frame-analytics-config-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="explain-data-frame-analytics-config-3-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field_selection|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalyticsFieldSelection](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalyticsfieldselection)]|true|none|An array of objects that explain selection for each field, sorted by the field names.|
|memory_estimation|object|true|none|An array of objects that explain selection for each field, sorted by the field names.|
|» expected_memory_with_disk|string|true|none|Estimated memory usage under the assumption that overflowing to disk is allowed during data frame analytics. expected_memory_with_disk is usually smaller than expected_memory_without_disk as using disk allows to limit the main memory needed to perform data frame analytics.|
|» expected_memory_without_disk|string|true|none|Estimated memory usage under the assumption that the whole data frame analytics should happen in memory (i.e. without overflowing to disk).|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get data frame analytics job configuration info

<a id="opIdml-get-data-frame-analytics-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics`

You can get information for multiple data frame analytics jobs in a single
API request by using a comma-separated list of data frame analytics jobs or a
wildcard expression.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


<h3 id="get-data-frame-analytics-job-configuration-info-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no data frame analytics<br>jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value returns an empty data_frame_analytics array when there<br>are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial matches.<br>If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a 404 status code when<br>there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of data frame analytics jobs.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of data frame analytics jobs to obtain.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Indicates if certain fields should be removed from the configuration on<br>retrieval. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`
