|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no data frame analytics<br>jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>The default value returns an empty data_frame_analytics array when there<br>are no matches and the subset of results when there are partial matches.<br>If this parameter is `false`, the request returns a 404 status code when<br>there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of data frame analytics jobs.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of data frame analytics jobs to obtain.|
|verbose|query|boolean|false|Defines whether the stats response should be verbose.|

## Preview features used by data frame analytics

<a id="opIdml-preview-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/_preview \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics/_preview`

|» » » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. |» » » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. ## Preview features used by data frame analytics

<a id="opIdml-preview-data-frame-analytics-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/_preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/_preview`

Preview the extracted features used by a data frame analytics config.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » classification|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. |» » » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Preview features used by data frame analytics

<a id="opIdml-preview-data-frame-analytics-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_preview \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_preview`

Preview the extracted features used by a data frame analytics config.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="preview-features-used-by-data-frame-analytics-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» config|body|object|false|A data frame analytics config as described in create data frame analytics<br>jobs. Note that `id` and `dest` don’t need to be provided in the context of<br>this API.|
|» » source|body|object|true|none|
|» » » index|body|object|true|Index or indices on which to perform the analysis. It can be a single index or index pattern as well as an array of indices or patterns. |» » » classification|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|

If it is -1 or greater than the total number of categories, probabilities are reported for all categories; if you have a large number of categories, there could be a significant effect on the size of your destination index. NOTE: To use the AUC ROC evaluation method, `num_top_classes` must be set to -1 or a value greater than or equal to the total number of categories.|

## Preview features used by data frame analytics

<a id="opIdml-preview-data-frame-analytics-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_preview`

Preview the extracted features used by a data frame analytics config.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"config\": {\n    \"source\": {\n      \"index\": \"houses_sold_last_10_yrs\"\n    },\n    \"analysis\": {\n      \"regression\": {\n        \"dependent_variable\": \"price\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » classification|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » » » alpha|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » » » dependent_variable|body|string|true|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » » » downsample_factor|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » » » early_stopping_enabled|body|boolean|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » » » eta|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » » class_assignment_objective|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » num_top_classes|body|number|false|Defines the number of categories for which the predicted probabilities are reported. It must be non-negative or -1. If it is -1 or greater than the total number of categories, probabilities are reported for all categories; if you have a large number of categories, there could be a significant effect on the size of your destination index. NOTE: To use the AUC ROC evaluation method, `num_top_classes` must be set to -1 or a value greater than or equal to the total number of categories.|
|» » » outlier_detection|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform outlier detection. NOTE: Advanced parameters are for fine-tuning classification analysis. They are set automatically by hyperparameter optimization to give the minimum validation error. It is highly recommended to use the default values unless you fully understand the function of these parameters.|

|» » » » feature_influence_threshold|body|number|false|The minimum outlier score that a document needs to have in order to calculate its feature influence score. Value range: 0-1.|
|» » » » method|body|string|false|The method that outlier detection uses. Available methods are `lof`, `ldof`, `distance_kth_nn`, `distance_knn`, and `ensemble`. The default value is ensemble, which means that outlier detection uses an ensemble of different methods and normalises and combines their individual outlier scores to obtain the overall outlier score.|
|» » » » n_neighbors|body|number|false|Defines the value for how many nearest neighbors each method of outlier detection uses to calculate its outlier score. When the value is not set, different values are used for different ensemble members. This default behavior helps improve the diversity in the ensemble; only override it if you are confident that the value you choose is appropriate for the data set.|
|» » » » outlier_fraction|body|number|false|The proportion of the data set that is assumed to be outlying prior to outlier detection. For example, 0.05 means it is assumed that 5% of values are real outliers and 95% are inliers.|
|» » » » standardization_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the following operation is performed on the columns before computing outlier scores: `(x_i - mean(x_i)) / sd(x_i)`.|
|» » » regression|body|object|false|The configuration information necessary to perform regression. NOTE: Advanced parameters are for fine-tuning regression analysis. |» » » » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. |» » » » feature_bag_fraction|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » feature_processors|body|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » » » gamma|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » lambda|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » » » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » max_trees|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » » » num_top_feature_importance_values|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » » » prediction_field_name|body|object|false|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » » » randomize_seed|body|number|false|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_limit|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » » » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|body|number|false|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » » » training_percent|body|object|false|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » » loss_function|body|string|false|The loss function used during regression. Available options are `mse` (mean squared error), `msle` (mean squared logarithmic error), `huber` (Pseudo-Huber loss).|
|» » » » loss_function_parameter|body|number|false|A positive number that is used as a parameter to the `loss_function`.|
|» » model_memory_limit|body|string|false|none|
|» » max_num_threads|body|number|false|none|

## Start a data frame analytics job

<a id="opIdml-start-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "id": {},
    "timeout": "20s"
  }'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_start`

A data frame analytics job can be started and stopped multiple times
throughout its lifecycle.
If the destination index does not exist, it is created automatically the
first time you start the data frame analytics job. The
`index.number_of_shards` and `index.number_of_replicas` settings for the
destination index are copied from the source index. If there are multiple
source indices, the destination index copies the highest setting values. The
mappings for the destination index are also copied from the source indices.
If there are any mapping conflicts, the job fails to start.
If the destination index exists, it is used as is. You can therefore set up
the destination index in advance with custom settings and mappings.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `create_index`,`index`,`manage`,`read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": {},
  "timeout": "20s"
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-data-frame-analytics-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job. This identifier can contain<br>lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and<br>underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the amount of time to wait until the data frame analytics job<br>starts.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|object|false|If provided, must be the same identifier as in the path.|
|» timeout|body|object|false|Controls the amount of time to wait until the data frame analytics job<br>starts.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|-1|
|» » *oneOf*|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "node": {}
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="start-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|
|node|object|true|none|The ID of the node that the job was started on. If the job is allowed to open lazily and has not yet been assigned to a node, this value is an empty string.<br>The node ID of the node the job has been assigned to, or<br>an empty string if it hasn't been assigned to a node. In<br>serverless if the job has been assigned to run then the<br>node ID will be "serverless".|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Stop data frame analytics jobs

<a id="opIdml-stop-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "id": {},
    "allow_no_match": true,
    "force": false,
    "timeout": "20s"
  }'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_stop`

A data frame analytics job can be started and stopped multiple times
throughout its lifecycle.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": {},
  "allow_no_match": true,
  "force": false,
  "timeout": "20s"
}
```

|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no data frame analytics<br>jobs that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. ## Update a data frame analytics job

<a id="opIdml-update-data-frame-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/data_frame/analytics/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"model_memory_limit\": \"200mb\"\n}"'
```

`POST /_ml/data_frame/analytics/{id}/_update`



## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`create_index`,`manage`,`index`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"model_memory_limit\": \"200mb\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-a-data-frame-analytics-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the data frame analytics job. This identifier can contain<br>lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and<br>underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the job.|
|» model_memory_limit|body|string|false|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are permitted for<br>analytical processing. If your `elasticsearch.yml` file contains an<br>`xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try<br>to create data frame analytics jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values<br>greater than that setting.|
|» max_num_threads|body|number|false|The maximum number of threads to be used by the analysis. Using more<br>threads may decrease the time necessary to complete the analysis at the<br>cost of using more CPU. Note that the process may use additional threads<br>for operational functionality other than the analysis itself.|
|» allow_lazy_start|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether this job can start when there is insufficient machine<br>learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node.|

<h3 id="update-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="update-a-data-frame-analytics-job-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorization|object|false|none|none|
|» api_key|object|false|none|If an API key was used for the most recent update to the job, its name and identifier are listed in the response.|
|» » id|string|true|none|The identifier for the API key.|
|» » name|string|true|none|The name of the API key.|
|» roles|[string]|false|none|If a user ID was used for the most recent update to the job, its roles at the time of the update are listed in the response.|
|» service_account|string|false|none|If a service account was used for the most recent update to the job, the account name is listed in the response.|
|allow_lazy_start|boolean|true|none|none|
|analysis|object|true|none|none|
|» classification|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform classification.|
|» » alpha|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|» » dependent_variable|string|true|none|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|» » downsample_factor|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|» » early_stopping_enabled|boolean|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|» » eta|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|» » eta_growth_rate_per_tree|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|» » feature_bag_fraction|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » feature_processors|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|» » gamma|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » lambda|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|» » max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » max_trees|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|» » num_top_feature_importance_values|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|» » prediction_field_name|object|false|none|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|» » randomize_seed|number|false|none|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|» » soft_tree_depth_limit|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|» » soft_tree_depth_tolerance|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|» » training_percent|object|false|none|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|» » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|number|false|none|none|
|» » class_assignment_objective|string|false|none|none|
|» » num_top_classes|number|false|none|Defines the number of categories for which the predicted probabilities are reported. It must be non-negative or -1. If it is -1 or greater than the total number of categories, probabilities are reported for all categories; if you have a large number of categories, there could be a significant effect on the size of your destination index. NOTE: To use the AUC ROC evaluation method, `num_top_classes` must be set to -1 or a value greater than or equal to the total number of categories.|
|» outlier_detection|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform outlier detection. NOTE: Advanced parameters are for fine-tuning classification analysis. They are set automatically by hyperparameter optimization to give the minimum validation error. It is highly recommended to use the default values unless you fully understand the function of these parameters.|
|» » compute_feature_influence|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the feature influence calculation is enabled.|
|» » feature_influence_threshold|number|false|none|The minimum outlier score that a document needs to have in order to calculate its feature influence score. Value range: 0-1.|
|» » method|string|false|none|The method that outlier detection uses. Available methods are `lof`, `ldof`, `distance_kth_nn`, `distance_knn`, and `ensemble`. The default value is ensemble, which means that outlier detection uses an ensemble of different methods and normalises and combines their individual outlier scores to obtain the overall outlier score.|
|» » n_neighbors|number|false|none|Defines the value for how many nearest neighbors each method of outlier detection uses to calculate its outlier score. When the value is not set, different values are used for different ensemble members. This default behavior helps improve the diversity in the ensemble; only override it if you are confident that the value you choose is appropriate for the data set.|
|» » outlier_fraction|number|false|none|The proportion of the data set that is assumed to be outlying prior to outlier detection. For example, 0.05 means it is assumed that 5% of values are real outliers and 95% are inliers.|
|» » standardization_enabled|boolean|false|none|If true, the following operation is performed on the columns before computing outlier scores: `(x_i - mean(x_i)) / sd(x_i)`.|

## Get machine learning memory usage info

<a id="opIdml-get-memory-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/memory/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/memory/_stats`

Get information about how machine learning jobs and trained models are using memory,
on each node, both within the JVM heap, and natively, outside of the JVM.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`

|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node. If no response is received before the timeout<br>expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request<br>fails and returns an error.|

## Get machine learning information

<a id="opIdml-info"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/info \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_ml/info`

Get defaults and limits used by machine learning.
This endpoint is designed to be used by a user interface that needs to fully
understand machine learning configurations where some options are not
specified, meaning that the defaults should be used. This endpoint may be
used to find out what those defaults are. It also provides information about
the maximum size of machine learning jobs that could run in the current
cluster configuration.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_ml`


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "defaults": {
    "anomaly_detectors": {
      "categorization_analyzer": {},
      "categorization_examples_limit": 0,
      "model_memory_limit": "string",
      "model_snapshot_retention_days": 0,
      "daily_model_snapshot_retention_after_days": 0
    },
    "datafeeds": {
      "scroll_size": 0
    },
    "model_platform_variant": {}
  },
  "limits": {
    "max_single_ml_node_processors": 0,
    "total_ml_processors": 0,
    "max_model_memory_limit": {},
    "effective_max_model_memory_limit": {},
    "total_ml_memory": {}
  },
  "upgrade_mode": true,
  "native_code": {
    "build_hash": "string",
    "version": {}
  }
}
```

|200|OK||Inline|

## Set upgrade_mode for ML indices

<a id="opIdml-set-upgrade-mode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_ml/set_upgrade_mode \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_ml/set_upgrade_mode`

Sets a cluster wide upgrade_mode setting that prepares machine learning
indices for an upgrade.
When upgrading your cluster, in some circumstances you must restart your
nodes and reindex your machine learning indices. In those circumstances,
there must be no machine learning jobs running. You can close the machine
learning jobs, do the upgrade, then open all the jobs again. Alternatively,
you can use this API to temporarily halt tasks associated with the jobs and
datafeeds and prevent new jobs from opening. You can also use this API
during upgrades that do not require you to reindex your machine learning
indices, though stopping jobs is not a requirement in that case.
You can see the current value for the upgrade_mode setting by using the get
machine learning info API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_ml`


<h3 id="set-upgrademode-for-ml-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|When `true`, it enables `upgrade_mode` which temporarily halts all job<br>and datafeed tasks and prohibits new job and datafeed tasks from<br>starting.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The time to wait for the request to be completed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-upgrademode-for-ml-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a query rule

<a id="opIdquery-rules-put-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_query_rules/string/_rule/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"match_criteria\": {\n    \"query_string\": \"puggles\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_query_rules/{ruleset_id}/_rule/{rule_id}`

Create or update a query rule within a query ruleset.

IMPORTANT: Due to limitations within pinned queries, you can only pin documents using ids or docs, but cannot use both in single rule.
It is advised to use one or the other in query rulesets, to avoid errors.
Additionally, pinned queries have a maximum limit of 100 pinned hits.
If multiple matching rules pin more than 100 documents, only the first 100 documents are pinned in the order they are specified in the ruleset.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_search_query_rules`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/query-rules-ui#edit-a-rule">About editing rules and rulesets</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"match_criteria\": {\n    \"query_string\": \"puggles\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-query-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ruleset_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the query ruleset containing the rule to be created or updated.|
|rule_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The unique identifier of the query rule within the specified ruleset to be created or updated.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|object|true|The type of rule.|
|» criteria|body|[query_rules._types.QueryRuleCriteria](#schemaquery_rules._types.queryrulecriteria) \| [[query_rules._types.QueryRuleCriteria](#schemaquery_rules._types.queryrulecriteria)]|true|The criteria that must be met for the rule to be applied.<br>If multiple criteria are specified for a rule, all criteria must be met for the rule to be applied.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[query_rules._types.QueryRuleCriteria](#schemaquery_rules._types.queryrulecriteria)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[query_rules._types.QueryRuleCriteria](#schemaquery_rules._types.queryrulecriteria)]|false|none|
|» actions|body|object|true|The actions to take when the rule is matched.<br>The format of this action depends on the rule type.|
|» » ids|body|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|The unique document IDs of the documents to apply the rule to.<br>Only one of `ids` or `docs` may be specified and at least one must be specified.|
|» » docs|body|[[_types.query_dsl.PinnedDoc](#schema_types.query_dsl.pinneddoc)]|false|The documents to apply the rule to.<br>Only one of `ids` or `docs` may be specified and at least one must be specified.<br>There is a maximum value of 100 documents in a rule.<br>You can specify the following attributes for each document:<br><br>* `_index`: The index of the document to pin.<br>* `_id`: The unique document ID.|
|» priority|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {}
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-query-rule-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|object|true|none|none|

`PUT /_query_rules/{ruleset_id}`

There is a limit of 100 rules per ruleset.
This limit can be increased by using the `xpack.applications.rules.max_rules_per_ruleset` cluster setting.

IMPORTANT: Due to limitations within pinned queries, you can only select documents using `ids` or `docs`, but cannot use both in single rule.

Additionally, pinned queries have a maximum limit of 100 pinned hits.
If multiple matching rules pin more than 100 documents, only the first 100 documents are pinned in the order they are specified in the ruleset.


`GET /_rollup/job/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get the configuration, stats, and status of rollup jobs.

NOTE: This API returns only active (both `STARTED` and `STOPPED`) jobs.
If a job was created, ran for a while, then was deleted, the API does not return any details about it.
For details about a historical rollup job, the rollup capabilities API may be more useful.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_rollup`

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"jobs\": [\n    {\n      \"config\": {\n        \"id\": \"sensor\",\n        \"index_pattern\": \"sensor-*\",\n        \"rollup_index\": \"sensor_rollup\",\n        \"cron\": \"*/30 * * * * ?\",\n        \"groups\": {\n          \"date_histogram\": {\n            \"fixed_interval\": \"1h\",\n            \"delay\": \"7d\",\n            \"field\": \"timestamp\",\n            \"time_zone\": \"UTC\"\n          },\n          \"terms\": {\n            \"fields\": [\n              \"node\"\n            ]\n          }\n        },\n        \"metrics\": [\n          {\n            \"field\": \"temperature\",\n            \"metrics\": [\n              \"min\",\n              \"max\",\n              \"sum\"\n            ]\n          },\n          {\n            \"field\": \"voltage\",\n            \"metrics\": [\n              \"avg\"\n            ]\n          }\n        ],\n        \"timeout\": \"20s\",\n        \"page_size\": 1000\n      },\n      \"status\": {\n        \"job_state\": \"stopped\"\n      },\n      \"stats\": {\n        \"pages_processed\": 0,\n        \"documents_processed\": 0,\n        \"rollups_indexed\": 0,\n        \"trigger_count\": 0,\n        \"index_failures\": 0,\n        \"index_time_in_ms\": 0,\n        \"index_total\": 0,\n        \"search_failures\": 0,\n        \"search_time_in_ms\": 0,\n        \"search_total\": 0,\n        \"processing_time_in_ms\": 0,\n        \"processing_total\": 0\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Create a rollup job

<a id="opIdrollup-put-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_rollup/job/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index_pattern\": \"sensor-*\",\n  \"rollup_index\": \"sensor_rollup\",\n  \"cron\": \"*/30 * * * * ?\",\n  \"page_size\": 1000,\n  \"groups\": {\n    \"date_histogram\": {\n      \"field\": \"timestamp\",\n      \"fixed_interval\": \"1h\",\n      \"delay\": \"7d\"\n    },\n    \"terms\": {\n      \"fields\": [ \"node\" ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metrics\": [\n      {\n      \"field\": \"temperature\",\n      \"metrics\": [ \"min\", \"max\", \"sum\" ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"field\": \"voltage\",\n      \"metrics\": [ \"avg\" ]\n    }\n  ]\n}"'
```

`PUT /_rollup/job/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

WARNING: From 8.15.0, calling this API in a cluster with no rollup usage will fail with a message about the deprecation and planned removal of rollup features. A cluster needs to contain either a rollup job or a rollup index in order for this API to be allowed to run.

The rollup job configuration contains all the details about how the job should run, when it indexes documents, and what future queries will be able to run against the rollup index.

There are three main sections to the job configuration: the logistical details about the job (for example, the cron schedule), the fields that are used for grouping, and what metrics to collect for each group.

Jobs are created in a `STOPPED` state. You can start them with the start rollup jobs API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`,`manage_rollup`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index_pattern\": \"sensor-*\",\n  \"rollup_index\": \"sensor_rollup\",\n  \"cron\": \"*/30 * * * * ?\",\n  \"page_size\": 1000,\n  \"groups\": {\n    \"date_histogram\": {\n      \"field\": \"timestamp\",\n      \"fixed_interval\": \"1h\",\n      \"delay\": \"7d\"\n    },\n    \"terms\": {\n      \"fields\": [ \"node\" ]\n    }\n  },\n  \"metrics\": [\n      {\n      \"field\": \"temperature\",\n      \"metrics\": [ \"min\", \"max\", \"sum\" ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"field\": \"voltage\",\n      \"metrics\": [ \"avg\" ]\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-a-rollup-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the rollup job. This can be any alphanumeric string and uniquely identifies the<br>data that is associated with the rollup job. The ID is persistent; it is stored with the rolled<br>up data. If you create a job, let it run for a while, then delete the job, the data that the job<br>rolled up is still be associated with this job ID. You cannot create a new job with the same ID<br>since that could lead to problems with mismatched job configurations.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» cron|body|string|true|A cron string which defines the intervals when the rollup job should be executed. When the interval<br>triggers, the indexer attempts to rollup the data in the index pattern. The cron pattern is unrelated<br>to the time interval of the data being rolled up. For example, you may wish to create hourly rollups<br>of your document but to only run the indexer on a daily basis at midnight, as defined by the cron. The<br>cron pattern is defined just like a Watcher cron schedule.|
|» groups|body|object|true|Defines the grouping fields and aggregations that are defined for this rollup job. These fields will then be<br>available later for aggregating into buckets. These aggs and fields can be used in any combination. Think of<br>the groups configuration as defining a set of tools that can later be used in aggregations to partition the<br>data. Unlike raw data, we have to think ahead to which fields and aggregations might be used. Rollups provide<br>enough flexibility that you simply need to determine which fields are needed, not in what order they are needed.|
|» » date_histogram|body|object|false|A date histogram group aggregates a date field into time-based buckets.<br>This group is mandatory; you currently cannot roll up documents without a timestamp and a `date_histogram` group.|

## Delete a rollup job

<a id="opIdrollup-delete-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_rollup/job/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_rollup/job/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

A job must be stopped before it can be deleted.
If you attempt to delete a started job, an error occurs.
Similarly, if you attempt to delete a nonexistent job, an exception occurs.

IMPORTANT: When you delete a job, you remove only the process that is actively monitoring and rolling up data.
The API does not delete any previously rolled up data.
This is by design; a user may wish to roll up a static data set.
Because the data set is static, after it has been fully rolled up there is no need to keep the indexing rollup job around (as there will be no new data).
Thus the job can be deleted, leaving behind the rolled up data for analysis.
If you wish to also remove the rollup data and the rollup index contains the data for only a single job, you can delete the whole rollup index.
If the rollup index stores data from several jobs, you must issue a delete-by-query that targets the rollup job's identifier in the rollup index. For example:

```
POST my_rollup_index/_delete_by_query
{
  "query": {
    "term": {
      "_rollup.id": "the_rollup_job_id"
    }
  }
}
```

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_rollup`


<h3 id="delete-a-rollup-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the job.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

|200|OK||Inline|

## Get the rollup job capabilities

<a id="opIdrollup-get-rollup-caps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_rollup/data/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_rollup/data/{id}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get the capabilities of any rollup jobs that have been configured for a specific index or index pattern.

This API is useful because a rollup job is often configured to rollup only a subset of fields from the source index.
Furthermore, only certain aggregations can be configured for various fields, leading to a limited subset of functionality depending on that configuration.
This API enables you to inspect an index and determine:

1. Does this index have associated rollup data somewhere in the cluster?
2. If yes to the first question, what fields were rolled up, what aggregations can be performed, and where does the data live?

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_rollup`

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Index, indices or index-pattern to return rollup capabilities for.<br>`_all` may be used to fetch rollup capabilities from all jobs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Search rolled-up data

<a id="opIdrollup-rollup-search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/string/_rollup_search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"size\": 0,\n  \"aggregations\": {\n    \"max_temperature\": {\n      \"max\": {\n        \"field\": \"temperature\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /{index}/_rollup_search`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

The rollup search endpoint is needed because, internally, rolled-up documents utilize a different document structure than the original data.
It rewrites standard Query DSL into a format that matches the rollup documents then takes the response and rewrites it back to what a client would expect given the original query.

The request body supports a subset of features from the regular search API.
The following functionality is not available:

`size`: Because rollups work on pre-aggregated data, no search hits can be returned and so size must be set to zero or omitted entirely.
`highlighter`, `suggestors`, `post_filter`, `profile`, `explain`: These are similarly disallowed.

For more detailed examples of using the rollup search API, including querying rolled-up data only or combining rolled-up and live data, refer to the External documentation.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/manage-data/lifecycle/rollup/getting-started-api#historical-only-search-example">Getting started with rollups</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"size\": 0,\n  \"aggregations\": {\n    \"max_temperature\": {\n      \"max\": {\n        \"field\": \"temperature\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="search-rolled-up-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|[_types.Indices](#schema_types.indices)|true|A comma-separated list of data streams and indices used to limit the request.<br>This parameter has the following rules:<br><br>* At least one data stream, index, or wildcard expression must be specified. This target can include a rollup or non-rollup index. For data streams, the stream's backing indices can only serve as non-rollup indices. Omitting the parameter or using `_all` are not permitted.<br>* Multiple non-rollup indices may be specified.<br>* Only one rollup index may be specified. If more than one are supplied, an exception occurs.<br>* Wildcard expressions (`*`) may be used. If they match more than one rollup index, an exception occurs. However, you can use an expression to match multiple non-rollup indices or data streams.|
|rest_total_hits_as_int|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether hits.total should be rendered as an integer or an object in the rest search response|
|typed_keys|query|boolean|false|Specify whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» aggregations|body|object|false|Specifies aggregations.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.aggregations.AggregationContainer](#schema_types.aggregations.aggregationcontainer)|false|none|
|» query|body|object|false|Specifies a DSL query that is subject to some limitations.|
|» » bool|body|object|false|matches documents matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|» » boosting|body|object|false|Returns documents matching a `positive` query while reducing the relevance score of documents that also match a `negative` query.|
|» » common|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[_types.query_dsl.CommonTermsQuery](#schema_types.query_dsl.commontermsquery)|false|none|
|» » combined_fields|body|object|false|The `combined_fields` query supports searching multiple text fields as if their contents had been indexed into one combined field.|
|» » » boost|body|number|false|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
