<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-streams">streams</h1>

## Disable a named stream

<a id="opIdstreams-logs-disable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_streams/logs/_disable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_streams/{name}/_disable`

Turn off the named stream feature for this cluster.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="disable-a-named-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[streams._types.StreamType](#schemastreams._types.streamtype)|true|The stream type to disable.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|name|logs|
|name|logs.otel|
|name|logs.ecs|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="disable-a-named-stream-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Enable a named stream

<a id="opIdstreams-logs-enable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_streams/logs/_enable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_streams/{name}/_enable`

Turn on the named stream feature for this cluster.

NOTE: To protect existing data, this feature can be turned on only if the cluster does not have
existing indices or data streams that match the pattern `<name>|<name>.*` for the enabled stream
type name. If those indices or data streams exist, a `409 - Conflict` response and error is
returned.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`


<h3 id="enable-a-named-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[streams._types.StreamType](#schemastreams._types.streamtype)|true|The stream type to enable.|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|name|logs|
|name|logs.otel|
|name|logs.ecs|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

> 409 Response

```json
"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"root_cause\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"status_exception\",\n        \"reason\": \"Cannot enable logs.otel streams: indices named 'logs.otel' or starting with 'logs.otel.' already exist.\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"type\": \"status_exception\",\n    \"reason\": \"Cannot enable logs streams: indices named 'logs.otel' or starting with 'logs.otel.' already exist.\"\n  },\n  \"status\": 409\n}"
```

<h3 id="enable-a-named-stream-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|
|409|Conflict|<br>An index named `logs.otel`, or starting with `logs.otel.`, already exists.|[_types.ErrorResponseBase](#schema_types.errorresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get the status of streams

<a id="opIdstreams-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_streams/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_streams/status`

Get the current status for all types of streams.

## Required authorization

```json
"{\n  \"logs\": {\n    \"enabled\": false\n  }\n  \"logs.ecs\": {\n    \"enabled\": true\n  }\n  \"logs.otel\": {\n    \"enabled\": true\n  }\n}"
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|logs|object|true|none|none|

|logs.otel|object|true|none|none|
|» enabled|boolean|true|none|If true, the stream feature is enabled.|
|logs.ecs|object|true|none|none|

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-synonyms">synonyms</h1>

## Get a synonym set

<a id="opIdsynonyms-get-synonym"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_synonyms/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_synonyms/{id}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_search_synonyms`


<h3 id="get-a-synonym-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The synonyms set identifier to retrieve.|
|from|query|number|false|The starting offset for synonym rules to retrieve.|
|size|query|number|false|The max number of synonym rules to retrieve.|
|search_after|query|string|false|The synonym rule ID to use as a cursor for pagination.<br>The next page of results will start after this rule ID.<br>This parameter cannot be used with `from`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"count\": 3,\n  \"synonyms_set\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"test-1\",\n      \"synonyms\": \"hello, hi\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"test-2\",\n      \"synonyms\": \"bye, goodbye\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"test-3\",\n      \"synonyms\": \"test => check\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-a-synonym-set-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|The total number of synonyms rules that the synonyms set contains.|
|synonyms_set|[[synonyms._types.SynonymRuleRead](#schemasynonyms._types.synonymruleread)]|true|none|Synonym rule details.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a synonym set

<a id="opIdsynonyms-put-synonym"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_synonyms/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"\n{\n  \"synonyms_set\": {\n  \"synonyms\" : \"hello, hi, howdy\"\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_synonyms/{id}`

Synonym sets are limited to a maximum of 100,000 synonym rules per set by default.
This limit is configurable using the `synonyms.max_synonym_rules` cluster setting.

When an existing synonyms set is updated, the search analyzers that use the synonyms set are reloaded automatically for all indices.
This is equivalent to invoking the reload search analyzers API for all indices that use the synonyms set.

For practical examples of how to create or update a synonyms set, refer to the External documentation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_search_synonyms`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/full-text/create-update-synonyms-api-example">About synonym API examples</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"\n{\n  \"synonyms_set\": {\n  \"synonyms\" : \"hello, hi, howdy\"\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-synonym-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the synonyms set to be created or updated.|
|refresh|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request will refresh the analyzers with the new synonyms set and wait for the new synonyms to be available before returning.<br>If `false`, analyzers will not be reloaded with the new synonym set|
|append|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the provided synonym rules are appended to the existing set, with matching IDs overwriting existing rules.<br>If `false`, the entire synonyms set is replaced with the new synonym rules definitions.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Delete a synonym set

<a id="opIdsynonyms-delete-synonym"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_synonyms/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_synonyms/{id}`

You can only delete a synonyms set that is not in use by any index analyzer.

Synonyms sets can be used in synonym graph token filters and synonym token filters.
These synonym filters can be used as part of search analyzers.

Analyzers need to be loaded when an index is restored (such as when a node starts, or the index becomes open).
Even if the analyzer is not used on any field mapping, it still needs to be loaded on the index recovery phase.

If any analyzers cannot be loaded, the index becomes unavailable and the cluster status becomes red or yellow as index shards are not available.
To prevent that, synonyms sets that are used in analyzers can't be deleted.
A delete request in this case will return a 400 response code.

To remove a synonyms set, you must first remove all indices that contain analyzers using it.
You can migrate an index by creating a new index that does not contain the token filter with the synonyms set, and use the reindex API in order to copy over the index data.
Once finished, you can delete the index.
When the synonyms set is not used in analyzers, you will be able to delete it.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_search_synonyms`


<h3 id="delete-a-synonym-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The synonyms set identifier to delete.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-synonym-set-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a synonym rule

<a id="opIdsynonyms-put-synonym-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_synonyms/string/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"synonyms\": \"hello, hi, howdy\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_synonyms/{set_id}/{rule_id}`

Create or update a synonym rule in a synonym set.

If any of the synonym rules included is invalid, the API returns an error.

When you update a synonym rule, all analyzers using the synonyms set will be reloaded automatically to reflect the new rule.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_search_synonyms`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"synonyms\": \"hello, hi, howdy\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-synonym-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|set_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the synonym set.|
|rule_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|The ID of the synonym rule to be updated or created.|
|refresh|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request will refresh the analyzers with the new synonym rule and wait for the new synonyms to be available before returning.<br>If `false`, analyzers will not be reloaded with the new synonym rule|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» synonyms|body|object|true|The synonym rule information definition, which must be in Solr format.|

## Cancel a task

<a id="opIdtasks-cancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_tasks/_cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_tasks/_cancel`

WARNING: The task management API is new and should still be considered a beta feature.
The API may change in ways that are not backwards compatible.

A task may continue to run for some time after it has been cancelled because it may not be able to safely stop its current activity straight away.
It is also possible that Elasticsearch must complete its work on other tasks before it can process the cancellation.
The get task information API will continue to list these cancelled tasks until they complete.
The cancelled flag in the response indicates that the cancellation command has been processed and the task will stop as soon as possible.

To troubleshoot why a cancelled task does not complete promptly, use the get task information API with the `?detailed` parameter to identify the other tasks the system is running.
You can also use the node hot threads API to obtain detailed information about the work the system is doing instead of completing the cancelled task.

For relocatable tasks, this API transparently follows the task across graceful shutdown relocations,
so callers can keep using the original task ID. The returned task reports its `original_task_id` and `original_start_time_in_millis`
if it is continuing work from an earlier task.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage`

|parent_task_id|query|string|false|A parent task ID that is used to limit the tasks.|

## Get all tasks

<a id="opIdtasks-list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_tasks`

Get information about the tasks currently running on one or more nodes in the cluster.

WARNING: The task management API is new and should still be considered a beta feature.
The API may change in ways that are not backwards compatible.

For relocatable tasks, this API transparently follows the task across graceful shutdown relocations,
so callers can keep using the original task ID. The returned task reports its `original_task_id` and `original_start_time_in_millis`
if it is continuing work from an earlier task.

**Identifying running tasks**

The `X-Opaque-Id header`, when provided on the HTTP request header, is going to be returned as a header in the response as well as in the headers field for in the task information.
This enables you to track certain calls or associate certain tasks with the client that started them.
For example:

```
curl -i -H "X-Opaque-Id: 123456" "http://localhost:9200/_tasks?group_by=parents"
```

The API returns the following result:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Opaque-Id: 123456
content-type: application/json; charset=UTF-8
content-length: 831

{
  "tasks" : {
    "u5lcZHqcQhu-rUoFaqDphA:45" : {
      "node" : "u5lcZHqcQhu-rUoFaqDphA",
      "id" : 45,
      "type" : "transport",
      "action" : "cluster:monitor/tasks/lists",
      "start_time_in_millis" : 1513823752749,
      "running_time_in_nanos" : 293139,
      "cancellable" : false,
      "headers" : {
        "X-Opaque-Id" : "123456"
      },
      "children" : [
        {
          "node" : "u5lcZHqcQhu-rUoFaqDphA",
          "id" : 46,
          "type" : "direct",
          "action" : "cluster:monitor/tasks/lists[n]",
          "start_time_in_millis" : 1513823752750,
          "running_time_in_nanos" : 92133,
          "cancellable" : false,
          "parent_task_id" : "u5lcZHqcQhu-rUoFaqDphA:45",
          "headers" : {
            "X-Opaque-Id" : "123456"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
 }
```
In this example, `X-Opaque-Id: 123456` is the ID as a part of the response header.
The `X-Opaque-Id` in the task `headers` is the ID for the task that was initiated by the REST request.
The `X-Opaque-Id` in the children `headers` is the child task of the task that was initiated by the REST request.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-all-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actions|query|string \| [string]|false|A comma-separated list or wildcard expression of actions used to limit the request.<br>For example, you can use `cluser:*` to retrieve all cluster-related tasks.|
|detailed|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes detailed information about the running tasks.<br>This information is useful to distinguish tasks from each other but is more costly to run.|
|group_by|query|object|false|A key that is used to group tasks in the response.<br>The task lists can be grouped either by nodes or by parent tasks.|
|nodes|query|[_types.NodeIds](#schema_types.nodeids)|false|A comma-separated list of node IDs or names that is used to limit the returned information.|
|parent_task_id|query|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|false|A parent task identifier that is used to limit returned information.<br>To return all tasks, omit this parameter or use a value of `-1`.<br>If the parent task is not found, the API does not return a 404 response code.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for each node to respond.<br>If a node does not respond before its timeout expires, the response does not include its information.<br>However, timed out nodes are included in the `node_failures` property.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the request blocks until the operation is complete.|

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-textstructure">text_structure</h1>

## Find the structure of a text field

<a id="opIdtext-structure-find-field-structure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:9200/_text_structure/find_field_structure?field=string&index=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_text_structure/find_field_structure`

Find the structure of a text field in an Elasticsearch index.

This API provides a starting point for extracting further information from log messages already ingested into Elasticsearch.
For example, if you have ingested data into a very simple index that has just `@timestamp` and message fields, you can use this API to see what common structure exists in the message field.

The response from the API contains:

* Sample messages.
* Statistics that reveal the most common values for all fields detected within the text and basic numeric statistics for numeric fields.
* Information about the structure of the text, which is useful when you write ingest configurations to index it or similarly formatted text.
* Appropriate mappings for an Elasticsearch index, which you could use to ingest the text.

All this information can be calculated by the structure finder with no guidance.
However, you can optionally override some of the decisions about the text structure by specifying one or more query parameters.

If the structure finder produces unexpected results, specify the `explain` query parameter and an explanation will appear in the response.
It helps determine why the returned structure was chosen.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_text_structure`


<h3 id="find-the-structure-of-a-text-field-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|column_names|query|string \| [string]|false|If `format` is set to `delimited`, you can specify the column names in a comma-separated list.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder uses the column names from the header row of the text.<br>If the text does not have a header row, columns are named "column1", "column2", "column3", for example.|
|delimiter|query|string|false|If you have set `format` to `delimited`, you can specify the character used to delimit the values in each row.<br>Only a single character is supported; the delimiter cannot have multiple characters.<br>By default, the API considers the following possibilities: comma, tab, semi-colon, and pipe (`\|`).<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for the delimited format to be detected.<br>If you specify a delimiter, up to 10% of the rows can have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|documents_to_sample|query|object|false|The number of documents to include in the structural analysis.<br>The minimum value is 2.|
|ecs_compatibility|query|object|false|The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.<br>Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.<br>This setting primarily has an impact when a whole message Grok pattern such as `%{CATALINALOG}` matches the input.<br>If the structure finder identifies a common structure but has no idea of the meaning then generic field names such as `path`, `ipaddress`, `field1`, and `field2` are used in the `grok_pattern` output.<br>The intention in that situation is that a user who knows the meanings will rename the fields before using them.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If `true`, the response includes a field named `explanation`, which is an array of strings that indicate how the structure finder produced its result.|
|field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|true|The field that should be analyzed.|
|format|query|[text_structure._types.FormatType](#schematext_structure._types.formattype)|false|The high level structure of the text.<br>By default, the API chooses the format.<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for a delimited format to be detected.<br>If the format is set to delimited and the delimiter is not set, however, the API tolerates up to 5% of rows that have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|grok_pattern|query|[_types.GrokPattern](#schema_types.grokpattern)|false|If the format is `semi_structured_text`, you can specify a Grok pattern that is used to extract fields from every message in the text.<br>The name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match what is specified in the `timestamp_field` parameter.<br>If that parameter is not specified, the name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match "timestamp".<br>If `grok_pattern` is not specified, the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.|
|index|query|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)|true|The name of the index that contains the analyzed field.|
|quote|query|string|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to quote the values in each row if they contain newlines or the delimiter character.<br>Only a single character is supported.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the default value is a double quote (`"`).<br>If your delimited text format does not use quoting, a workaround is to set this argument to a character that does not appear anywhere in the sample.|
|should_trim_fields|query|boolean|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify whether values between delimiters should have whitespace trimmed from them.<br>If this parameter is not specified and the delimiter is pipe (`\|`), the default value is true.<br>Otherwise, the default value is `false`.|
|should_parse_recursively|query|boolean|false|If the format is `ndjson`, you can specify whether to parse nested JSON objects recursively.<br>The nested objects are parsed to a maximum depth equal to the default value of the `index.mapping.depth.limit` setting.<br>Anything beyond that depth is parsed as an `object` type field.<br>For formats other than `ndjson`, this parameter is ignored.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The maximum amount of time that the structure analysis can take.<br>If the analysis is still running when the timeout expires, it will be stopped.|
|timestamp_field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|The name of the field that contains the primary timestamp of each record in the text.<br>In particular, if the text was ingested into an index, this is the field that would be used to populate the `@timestamp` field.<br><br>If the format is `semi_structured_text`, this field must match the name of the appropriate extraction in the `grok_pattern`.<br>Therefore, for semi-structured text, it is best not to specify this parameter unless `grok_pattern` is also specified.<br><br>For structured text, if you specify this parameter, the field must exist within the text.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder makes a decision about which field (if any) is the primary timestamp field.<br>For structured text, it is not compulsory to have a timestamp in the text.|
|timestamp_format|query|string|false|The Java time format of the timestamp field in the text.<br>Only a subset of Java time format letter groups are supported:<br><br>* `a`<br>* `d`<br>* `dd`<br>* `EEE`<br>* `EEEE`<br>* `H`<br>* `HH`<br>* `h`<br>* `M`<br>* `MM`<br>* `MMM`<br>* `MMMM`<br>* `mm`<br>* `ss`<br>* `XX`<br>* `XXX`<br>* `yy`<br>* `yyyy`<br>* `zzz`<br><br>Additionally `S` letter groups (fractional seconds) of length one to nine are supported providing they occur after `ss` and are separated from the `ss` by a period (`.`), comma (`,`), or colon (`:`).<br>Spacing and punctuation is also permitted with the exception a question mark (`?`), newline, and carriage return, together with literal text enclosed in single quotes.<br>For example, `MM/dd HH.mm.ss,SSSSSS 'in' yyyy` is a valid override format.<br><br>One valuable use case for this parameter is when the format is semi-structured text, there are multiple timestamp formats in the text, and you know which format corresponds to the primary timestamp, but you do not want to specify the full `grok_pattern`.<br>Another is when the timestamp format is one that the structure finder does not consider by default.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses the best format from a built-in set.<br><br>If the special value `null` is specified, the structure finder will not look for a primary timestamp in the text.<br>When the format is semi-structured text, this will result in the structure finder treating the text as single-line messages.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|delimited|
|format|ndjson|
|format|semi_structured_text|
|format|xml|

`GET /_text_structure/find_message_structure`

Find the structure of a list of text messages.
The messages must contain data that is suitable to be ingested into Elasticsearch.

This API provides a starting point for ingesting data into Elasticsearch in a format that is suitable for subsequent use with other Elastic Stack functionality.
Use this API rather than the find text structure API if your input text has already been split up into separate messages by some other process.

The response from the API contains:

* Sample messages.
* Statistics that reveal the most common values for all fields detected within the text and basic numeric statistics for numeric fields.
* Information about the structure of the text, which is useful when you write ingest configurations to index it or similarly formatted text.
Appropriate mappings for an Elasticsearch index, which you could use to ingest the text.

All this information can be calculated by the structure finder with no guidance.
However, you can optionally override some of the decisions about the text structure by specifying one or more query parameters.

If the structure finder produces unexpected results, specify the `explain` query parameter and an explanation will appear in the response.
It helps determine why the returned structure was chosen.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_text_structure`

<h3 id="find-the-structure-of-text-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|column_names|query|string \| [string]|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the column names in a comma-separated list.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder uses the column names from the header row of the text.<br>If the text does not have a header role, columns are named "column1", "column2", "column3", for example.|
|delimiter|query|string|false|If you the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to delimit the values in each row.<br>Only a single character is supported; the delimiter cannot have multiple characters.<br>By default, the API considers the following possibilities: comma, tab, semi-colon, and pipe (`\|`).<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for the delimited format to be detected.<br>If you specify a delimiter, up to 10% of the rows can have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|ecs_compatibility|query|object|false|The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.<br>Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.<br>This setting primarily has an impact when a whole message Grok pattern such as `%{CATALINALOG}` matches the input.<br>If the structure finder identifies a common structure but has no idea of meaning then generic field names such as `path`, `ipaddress`, `field1`, and `field2` are used in the `grok_pattern` output, with the intention that a user who knows the meanings rename these fields before using it.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If this parameter is set to true, the response includes a field named `explanation`, which is an array of strings that indicate how the structure finder produced its result.|
|format|query|[text_structure._types.FormatType](#schematext_structure._types.formattype)|false|The high level structure of the text.<br>By default, the API chooses the format.<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for a delimited format to be detected.<br>If the format is `delimited` and the delimiter is not set, however, the API tolerates up to 5% of rows that have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|grok_pattern|query|[_types.GrokPattern](#schema_types.grokpattern)|false|If the format is `semi_structured_text`, you can specify a Grok pattern that is used to extract fields from every message in the text.<br>The name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match what is specified in the `timestamp_field` parameter.<br>If that parameter is not specified, the name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match "timestamp".<br>If `grok_pattern` is not specified, the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.|
|quote|query|string|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to quote the values in each row if they contain newlines or the delimiter character.<br>Only a single character is supported.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the default value is a double quote (`"`).<br>If your delimited text format does not use quoting, a workaround is to set this argument to a character that does not appear anywhere in the sample.|
|should_trim_fields|query|boolean|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify whether values between delimiters should have whitespace trimmed from them.<br>If this parameter is not specified and the delimiter is pipe (`\|`), the default value is true.<br>Otherwise, the default value is `false`.|
|should_parse_recursively|query|boolean|false|If the format is `ndjson`, you can specify whether to parse nested JSON objects recursively.<br>The nested objects are parsed to a maximum depth equal to the default value of the `index.mapping.depth.limit` setting.<br>Anything beyond that depth is parsed as an `object` type field.<br>For formats other than `ndjson`, this parameter is ignored.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The maximum amount of time that the structure analysis can take.<br>If the analysis is still running when the timeout expires, it will be stopped.|
|timestamp_field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|The name of the field that contains the primary timestamp of each record in the text.<br>In particular, if the text was ingested into an index, this is the field that would be used to populate the `@timestamp` field.<br><br>If the format is `semi_structured_text`, this field must match the name of the appropriate extraction in the `grok_pattern`.<br>Therefore, for semi-structured text, it is best not to specify this parameter unless `grok_pattern` is also specified.<br><br>For structured text, if you specify this parameter, the field must exist within the text.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder makes a decision about which field (if any) is the primary timestamp field.<br>For structured text, it is not compulsory to have a timestamp in the text.|
|timestamp_format|query|string|false|The Java time format of the timestamp field in the text.<br>Only a subset of Java time format letter groups are supported:<br><br>* `a`<br>* `d`<br>* `dd`<br>* `EEE`<br>* `EEEE`<br>* `H`<br>* `HH`<br>* `h`<br>* `M`<br>* `MM`<br>* `MMM`<br>* `MMMM`<br>* `mm`<br>* `ss`<br>* `XX`<br>* `XXX`<br>* `yy`<br>* `yyyy`<br>* `zzz`<br><br>Additionally `S` letter groups (fractional seconds) of length one to nine are supported providing they occur after `ss` and are separated from the `ss` by a period (`.`), comma (`,`), or colon (`:`).<br>Spacing and punctuation is also permitted with the exception a question mark (`?`), newline, and carriage return, together with literal text enclosed in single quotes.<br>For example, `MM/dd HH.mm.ss,SSSSSS 'in' yyyy` is a valid override format.<br><br>One valuable use case for this parameter is when the format is semi-structured text, there are multiple timestamp formats in the text, and you know which format corresponds to the primary timestamp, but you do not want to specify the full `grok_pattern`.<br>Another is when the timestamp format is one that the structure finder does not consider by default.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses the best format from a built-in set.<br><br>If the special value `null` is specified, the structure finder will not look for a primary timestamp in the text.<br>When the format is semi-structured text, this will result in the structure finder treating the text as single-line messages.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» messages|body|[string]|true|The list of messages you want to analyze.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|delimited|
|format|ndjson|
|format|semi_structured_text|
|format|xml|

`POST /_text_structure/find_message_structure`

Find the structure of a list of text messages.
The messages must contain data that is suitable to be ingested into Elasticsearch.

This API provides a starting point for ingesting data into Elasticsearch in a format that is suitable for subsequent use with other Elastic Stack functionality.
Use this API rather than the find text structure API if your input text has already been split up into separate messages by some other process.

The response from the API contains:

* Sample messages.
* Statistics that reveal the most common values for all fields detected within the text and basic numeric statistics for numeric fields.
* Information about the structure of the text, which is useful when you write ingest configurations to index it or similarly formatted text.
Appropriate mappings for an Elasticsearch index, which you could use to ingest the text.

All this information can be calculated by the structure finder with no guidance.
However, you can optionally override some of the decisions about the text structure by specifying one or more query parameters.

If the structure finder produces unexpected results, specify the `explain` query parameter and an explanation will appear in the response.
It helps determine why the returned structure was chosen.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_text_structure`

<h3 id="find-the-structure-of-text-messages-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|column_names|query|string \| [string]|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the column names in a comma-separated list.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder uses the column names from the header row of the text.<br>If the text does not have a header role, columns are named "column1", "column2", "column3", for example.|
|delimiter|query|string|false|If you the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to delimit the values in each row.<br>Only a single character is supported; the delimiter cannot have multiple characters.<br>By default, the API considers the following possibilities: comma, tab, semi-colon, and pipe (`\|`).<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for the delimited format to be detected.<br>If you specify a delimiter, up to 10% of the rows can have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|ecs_compatibility|query|object|false|The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.<br>Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.<br>This setting primarily has an impact when a whole message Grok pattern such as `%{CATALINALOG}` matches the input.<br>If the structure finder identifies a common structure but has no idea of meaning then generic field names such as `path`, `ipaddress`, `field1`, and `field2` are used in the `grok_pattern` output, with the intention that a user who knows the meanings rename these fields before using it.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If this parameter is set to true, the response includes a field named `explanation`, which is an array of strings that indicate how the structure finder produced its result.|
|format|query|[text_structure._types.FormatType](#schematext_structure._types.formattype)|false|The high level structure of the text.<br>By default, the API chooses the format.<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for a delimited format to be detected.<br>If the format is `delimited` and the delimiter is not set, however, the API tolerates up to 5% of rows that have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|grok_pattern|query|[_types.GrokPattern](#schema_types.grokpattern)|false|If the format is `semi_structured_text`, you can specify a Grok pattern that is used to extract fields from every message in the text.<br>The name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match what is specified in the `timestamp_field` parameter.<br>If that parameter is not specified, the name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match "timestamp".<br>If `grok_pattern` is not specified, the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.|
|quote|query|string|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to quote the values in each row if they contain newlines or the delimiter character.<br>Only a single character is supported.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the default value is a double quote (`"`).<br>If your delimited text format does not use quoting, a workaround is to set this argument to a character that does not appear anywhere in the sample.|
|should_trim_fields|query|boolean|false|If the format is `delimited`, you can specify whether values between delimiters should have whitespace trimmed from them.<br>If this parameter is not specified and the delimiter is pipe (`\|`), the default value is true.<br>Otherwise, the default value is `false`.|
|should_parse_recursively|query|boolean|false|If the format is `ndjson`, you can specify whether to parse nested JSON objects recursively.<br>The nested objects are parsed to a maximum depth equal to the default value of the `index.mapping.depth.limit` setting.<br>Anything beyond that depth is parsed as an `object` type field.<br>For formats other than `ndjson`, this parameter is ignored.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The maximum amount of time that the structure analysis can take.<br>If the analysis is still running when the timeout expires, it will be stopped.|
|timestamp_field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|The name of the field that contains the primary timestamp of each record in the text.<br>In particular, if the text was ingested into an index, this is the field that would be used to populate the `@timestamp` field.<br><br>If the format is `semi_structured_text`, this field must match the name of the appropriate extraction in the `grok_pattern`.<br>Therefore, for semi-structured text, it is best not to specify this parameter unless `grok_pattern` is also specified.<br><br>For structured text, if you specify this parameter, the field must exist within the text.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder makes a decision about which field (if any) is the primary timestamp field.<br>For structured text, it is not compulsory to have a timestamp in the text.|
|timestamp_format|query|string|false|The Java time format of the timestamp field in the text.<br>Only a subset of Java time format letter groups are supported:<br><br>* `a`<br>* `d`<br>* `dd`<br>* `EEE`<br>* `EEEE`<br>* `H`<br>* `HH`<br>* `h`<br>* `M`<br>* `MM`<br>* `MMM`<br>* `MMMM`<br>* `mm`<br>* `ss`<br>* `XX`<br>* `XXX`<br>* `yy`<br>* `yyyy`<br>* `zzz`<br><br>Additionally `S` letter groups (fractional seconds) of length one to nine are supported providing they occur after `ss` and are separated from the `ss` by a period (`.`), comma (`,`), or colon (`:`).<br>Spacing and punctuation is also permitted with the exception a question mark (`?`), newline, and carriage return, together with literal text enclosed in single quotes.<br>For example, `MM/dd HH.mm.ss,SSSSSS 'in' yyyy` is a valid override format.<br><br>One valuable use case for this parameter is when the format is semi-structured text, there are multiple timestamp formats in the text, and you know which format corresponds to the primary timestamp, but you do not want to specify the full `grok_pattern`.<br>Another is when the timestamp format is one that the structure finder does not consider by default.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses the best format from a built-in set.<br><br>If the special value `null` is specified, the structure finder will not look for a primary timestamp in the text.<br>When the format is semi-structured text, this will result in the structure finder treating the text as single-line messages.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» messages|body|[string]|true|The list of messages you want to analyze.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|delimited|
|format|ndjson|
|format|semi_structured_text|
|format|xml|

`POST /_text_structure/find_structure`

The text file must contain data that is suitable to be ingested into Elasticsearch.

This API provides a starting point for ingesting data into Elasticsearch in a format that is suitable for subsequent use with other Elastic Stack functionality.
Unlike other Elasticsearch endpoints, the data that is posted to this endpoint does not need to be UTF-8 encoded and in JSON format.
It must, however, be text; binary text formats are not currently supported.
The size is limited to the Elasticsearch HTTP receive buffer size, which defaults to 100 Mb.

The response from the API contains:

* A couple of messages from the beginning of the text.
* Statistics that reveal the most common values for all fields detected within the text and basic numeric statistics for numeric fields.
* Information about the structure of the text, which is useful when you write ingest configurations to index it or similarly formatted text.
* Appropriate mappings for an Elasticsearch index, which you could use to ingest the text.

All this information can be calculated by the structure finder with no guidance.
However, you can optionally override some of the decisions about the text structure by specifying one or more query parameters.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_text_structure`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/find-text-structure-examples">About finding text structure API</a>

<h3 id="find-the-structure-of-a-text-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charset|query|string|false|The text's character set.<br>It must be a character set that is supported by the JVM that Elasticsearch uses.<br>For example, `UTF-8`, `UTF-16LE`, `windows-1252`, or `EUC-JP`.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses an appropriate character set.|
|column_names|query|string \| [string]|false|If you have set format to `delimited`, you can specify the column names in a comma-separated list.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder uses the column names from the header row of the text.<br>If the text does not have a header role, columns are named "column1", "column2", "column3", for example.|
|delimiter|query|string|false|If you have set `format` to `delimited`, you can specify the character used to delimit the values in each row.<br>Only a single character is supported; the delimiter cannot have multiple characters.<br>By default, the API considers the following possibilities: comma, tab, semi-colon, and pipe (`\|`).<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for the delimited format to be detected.<br>If you specify a delimiter, up to 10% of the rows can have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|ecs_compatibility|query|string|false|The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.<br>Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.<br>Valid values are `disabled` and `v1`.<br>This setting primarily has an impact when a whole message Grok pattern such as `%{CATALINALOG}` matches the input.<br>If the structure finder identifies a common structure but has no idea of meaning then generic field names such as `path`, `ipaddress`, `field1`, and `field2` are used in the `grok_pattern` output, with the intention that a user who knows the meanings rename these fields before using it.|
|explain|query|boolean|false|If this parameter is set to `true`, the response includes a field named explanation, which is an array of strings that indicate how the structure finder produced its result.<br>If the structure finder produces unexpected results for some text, use this query parameter to help you determine why the returned structure was chosen.|
|format|query|[text_structure.find_structure.FindStructureFormat](#schematext_structure.find_structure.findstructureformat)|false|The high level structure of the text.<br>Valid values are `ndjson`, `xml`, `delimited`, and `semi_structured_text`.<br>By default, the API chooses the format.<br>In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for a delimited format to be detected.<br>If the format is set to `delimited` and the delimiter is not set, however, the API tolerates up to 5% of rows that have a different number of columns than the first row.|
|grok_pattern|query|[_types.GrokPattern](#schema_types.grokpattern)|false|If you have set `format` to `semi_structured_text`, you can specify a Grok pattern that is used to extract fields from every message in the text.<br>The name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match what is specified in the `timestamp_field` parameter.<br>If that parameter is not specified, the name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match "timestamp".<br>If `grok_pattern` is not specified, the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.|
|has_header_row|query|boolean|false|If you have set `format` to `delimited`, you can use this parameter to indicate whether the column names are in the first row of the text.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder guesses based on the similarity of the first row of the text to other rows.|
|line_merge_size_limit|query|object|false|The maximum number of characters in a message when lines are merged to form messages while analyzing semi-structured text.<br>If you have extremely long messages you may need to increase this, but be aware that this may lead to very long processing times if the way to group lines into messages is misdetected.|
|lines_to_sample|query|object|false|The number of lines to include in the structural analysis, starting from the beginning of the text.<br>The minimum is 2.<br>If the value of this parameter is greater than the number of lines in the text, the analysis proceeds (as long as there are at least two lines in the text) for all of the lines.<br><br>NOTE: The number of lines and the variation of the lines affects the speed of the analysis.<br>For example, if you upload text where the first 1000 lines are all variations on the same message, the analysis will find more commonality than would be seen with a bigger sample.<br>If possible, however, it is more efficient to upload sample text with more variety in the first 1000 lines than to request analysis of 100000 lines to achieve some variety.|
|quote|query|string|false|If you have set `format` to `delimited`, you can specify the character used to quote the values in each row if they contain newlines or the delimiter character.<br>Only a single character is supported.<br>If this parameter is not specified, the default value is a double quote (`"`).<br>If your delimited text format does not use quoting, a workaround is to set this argument to a character that does not appear anywhere in the sample.|
|should_trim_fields|query|boolean|false|If you have set `format` to `delimited`, you can specify whether values between delimiters should have whitespace trimmed from them.<br>If this parameter is not specified and the delimiter is pipe (`\|`), the default value is `true`.<br>Otherwise, the default value is `false`.|
|should_parse_recursively|query|boolean|false|If the format is `ndjson`, you can specify whether to parse nested JSON objects recursively.<br>The nested objects are parsed to a maximum depth equal to the default value of the `index.mapping.depth.limit` setting.<br>Anything beyond that depth is parsed as an `object` type field.<br>For formats other than `ndjson`, this parameter is ignored.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The maximum amount of time that the structure analysis can take.<br>If the analysis is still running when the timeout expires then it will be stopped.|
|timestamp_field|query|[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)|false|The name of the field that contains the primary timestamp of each record in the text.<br>In particular, if the text were ingested into an index, this is the field that would be used to populate the `@timestamp` field.<br><br>If the `format` is `semi_structured_text`, this field must match the name of the appropriate extraction in the `grok_pattern`.<br>Therefore, for semi-structured text, it is best not to specify this parameter unless `grok_pattern` is also specified.<br><br>For structured text, if you specify this parameter, the field must exist within the text.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder makes a decision about which field (if any) is the primary timestamp field.<br>For structured text, it is not compulsory to have a timestamp in the text.|
|timestamp_format|query|string|false|The Java time format of the timestamp field in the text.<br><br>Only a subset of Java time format letter groups are supported:<br><br>* `a`<br>* `d`<br>* `dd`<br>* `EEE`<br>* `EEEE`<br>* `H`<br>* `HH`<br>* `h`<br>* `M`<br>* `MM`<br>* `MMM`<br>* `MMMM`<br>* `mm`<br>* `ss`<br>* `XX`<br>* `XXX`<br>* `yy`<br>* `yyyy`<br>* `zzz`<br><br>Additionally `S` letter groups (fractional seconds) of length one to nine are supported providing they occur after `ss` and separated from the `ss` by a `.`, `,` or `:`.<br>Spacing and punctuation is also permitted with the exception of `?`, newline and carriage return, together with literal text enclosed in single quotes.<br>For example, `MM/dd HH.mm.ss,SSSSSS 'in' yyyy` is a valid override format.<br><br>One valuable use case for this parameter is when the format is semi-structured text, there are multiple timestamp formats in the text, and you know which format corresponds to the primary timestamp, but you do not want to specify the full `grok_pattern`.<br>Another is when the timestamp format is one that the structure finder does not consider by default.<br><br>If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses the best format from a built-in set.<br><br>If the special value `null` is specified the structure finder will not look for a primary timestamp in the text.<br>When the format is semi-structured text this will result in the structure finder treating the text as single-line messages.|
|body|body|[object]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|ndjson|
|format|xml|
|format|delimited|
|format|semi_structured_text|

## Test a Grok pattern

<a id="opIdtext-structure-test-grok-pattern"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_text_structure/test_grok_pattern \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"grok_pattern\": \"Hello %{WORD:first_name} %{WORD:last_name}\",\n  \"text\": [\n    \"Hello John Doe\",\n    \"this does not match\"\n  ]\n}"'
```

`GET /_text_structure/test_grok_pattern`

Test a Grok pattern on one or more lines of text.
The API indicates whether the lines match the pattern together with the offsets and lengths of the matched substrings.

<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/scripting/grok">Learn more about Grok patterns</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"grok_pattern\": \"Hello %{WORD:first_name} %{WORD:last_name}\",\n  \"text\": [\n    \"Hello John Doe\",\n    \"this does not match\"\n  ]\n}"
```

## Create a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-put-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\",\n    \"query\": {\n      \"term\": {\n        \"geoip.continent_name\": {\n          \"value\": \"Asia\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"description\": \"Maximum priced ecommerce data by customer_id in Asia\",\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce_transform1\",\n    \"pipeline\": \"add_timestamp_pipeline\"\n  },\n  \"frequency\": \"5m\",\n  \"sync\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"delay\": \"60s\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"retention_policy\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"max_age\": \"30d\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_transform/{transform_id}`

Creates a transform.

A transform copies data from source indices, transforms it, and persists it into an entity-centric destination index. You can also think of the destination index as a two-dimensional tabular data structure (known as
a data frame). The ID for each document in the data frame is generated from a hash of the entity, so there is a
unique row per entity.

You must choose either the latest or pivot method for your transform; you cannot use both in a single transform. If
you choose to use the pivot method for your transform, the entities are defined by the set of `group_by` fields in
the pivot object. If you choose to use the latest method, the entities are defined by the `unique_key` field values
in the latest object.

You must have `create_index`, `index`, and `read` privileges on the destination index and `read` and
`view_index_metadata` privileges on the source indices. When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the
transform remembers which roles the user that created it had at the time of creation and uses those same roles. If
those roles do not have the required privileges on the source and destination indices, the transform fails when it
attempts unauthorized operations.

NOTE: You must use Kibana or this API to create a transform. Do not add a transform directly into any
`.transform-internal*` indices using the Elasticsearch index API. If Elasticsearch security features are enabled, do
not give users any privileges on `.transform-internal*` indices. If you used transforms prior to 7.5, also do not
give users any privileges on `.data-frame-internal*` indices.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `create_index`,`read`,`index`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\",\n    \"query\": {\n      \"term\": {\n        \"geoip.continent_name\": {\n          \"value\": \"Asia\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"description\": \"Maximum priced ecommerce data by customer_id in Asia\",\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce_transform1\",\n    \"pipeline\": \"add_timestamp_pipeline\"\n  },\n  \"frequency\": \"5m\",\n  \"sync\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"delay\": \"60s\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"retention_policy\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"max_age\": \"30d\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Delete a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-delete-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_transform/{transform_id}`



## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="delete-a-transform-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the transform.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If this value is false, the transform must be stopped before it can be deleted. If true, the transform is<br>deleted regardless of its current state.|
|delete_dest_index|query|boolean|false|If this value is true, the destination index is deleted together with the transform. If false, the destination<br>index will not be deleted|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-a-transform-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get transforms

<a id="opIdtransform-get-transform-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_transform`

Get configuration information for transforms.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_transform`


<h3 id="get-transforms-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no transforms that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If this parameter is false, the request returns a 404 status code when<br>there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of transforms.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of transforms to obtain.|
|exclude_generated|query|boolean|false|Excludes fields that were automatically added when creating the<br>transform. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to<br>be retrieved and then added to another cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"count\": 1,\n  \"transforms\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"ecommerce_transform1\",\n      \"authorization\": {\n        \"roles\": [\n          \"superuser\"\n        ]\n      },\n      \"version\": \"8.4.0\",\n      \"create_time\": 1656023416565,\n      \"source\": {\n        \"index\": [\n          \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n        ],\n        \"query\": {\n          \"term\": {\n            \"geoip.continent_name\": {\n              \"value\": \"Asia\"\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      },\n      \"dest\": {\n        \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce_transform1\",\n        \"pipeline\": \"add_timestamp_pipeline\"\n      },\n      \"frequency\": \"5m\",\n      \"sync\": {\n        \"time\": {\n          \"field\": \"order_date\",\n          \"delay\": \"60s\"\n        }\n      },\n      \"pivot\": {\n        \"group_by\": {\n          \"customer_id\": {\n            \"terms\": {\n              \"field\": \"customer_id\"\n            }\n          }\n        },\n        \"aggregations\": {\n          \"max_price\": {\n            \"max\": {\n              \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      },\n      \"description\": \"Maximum priced ecommerce data by customer_id in Asia\",\n      \"settings\": {},\n      \"retention_policy\": {\n        \"time\": {\n          \"field\": \"order_date\",\n          \"max_age\": \"30d\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}"
```

## Get transform stats

<a id="opIdtransform-get-transform-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_transform/{transform_id}/_stats`

Get usage information for transforms.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `monitor_transform`


<h3 id="get-transform-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|Identifier for the transform. It can be a transform identifier or a<br>wildcard expression. You can get information for all transforms by using<br>`_all`, by specifying `*` as the `<transform_id>`, or by omitting the<br>`<transform_id>`.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request:<br><br>1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no transforms that match.<br>2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.<br>3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.<br><br>If this parameter is false, the request returns a 404 status code when<br>there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|basic|query|boolean|false|If true, the response includes `id`, `state`, `node`, `stats`, `health`,<br>and basic `checkpointing` information (the last and next checkpoint<br>numbers, and the next checkpoint's `position` and `progress`). Skips<br>statistics that require heavy computations to calculate:<br>`operations_behind`, `changes_last_detected_at`, `last_search_time`, and<br>the checkpoint timestamps.|
|from|query|number|false|Skips the specified number of transforms.|
|size|query|number|false|Specifies the maximum number of transforms to obtain.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the time to wait for the stats|

## Preview a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-preview-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_preview \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_transform/{transform_id}/_preview`

Generates a preview of the results that you will get when you create a transform with the same configuration.

It returns a maximum of 100 results. The calculations are based on all the current data in the source index. It also
generates a list of mappings and settings for the destination index. These values are determined based on the field
types of the source index and the transform aggregations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="preview-a-transform-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the transform to preview. If you specify this path parameter, you cannot provide transform<br>configuration details in the request body.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the<br>timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» dest|body|object|false|The destination for the transform.|
|» » index|body|object|false|The destination index for the transform. The mappings of the destination index are deduced based on the source<br>fields when possible. If alternate mappings are required, use the create index API prior to starting the<br>transform.|
|» » aliases|body|[[transform._types.DestinationAlias](#schematransform._types.destinationalias)]|false|The aliases that the destination index for the transform should have.<br>Aliases are manipulated using the stored credentials of the transform, which means the secondary credentials<br>supplied at creation time (if both primary and secondary credentials are specified).<br><br>The destination index is added to the aliases regardless of whether the destination index was created by the<br>transform or pre-created by the user.|
|» » pipeline|body|string|false|The unique identifier for an ingest pipeline.|
|» description|body|string|false|Free text description of the transform.|
|» frequency|body|object|false|The interval between checks for changes in the source indices when the<br>transform is running continuously. Also determines the retry interval in<br>the event of transient failures while the transform is searching or<br>indexing. The minimum value is 1s and the maximum is 1h.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

The following aggregations are currently supported: average, bucket<br>script, bucket selector, cardinality, filter, geo bounds, geo centroid, geo line, max, median absolute deviation,<br>min, missing, percentiles, rare terms, scripted metric, stats, sum, terms, top metrics, value count, weighted<br>average.|

|» » » flush_threshold_size|object|false|none|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). ## Preview a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-preview-transform-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_preview`

Generates a preview of the results that you will get when you create a transform with the same configuration.

It returns a maximum of 100 results. The calculations are based on all the current data in the source index. It also
generates a list of mappings and settings for the destination index. These values are determined based on the field
types of the source index and the transform aggregations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » flush_threshold_size|object|false|none|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|

## Preview a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-preview-transform-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/_preview \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`GET /_transform/_preview`

Generates a preview of the results that you will get when you create a transform with the same configuration.

It returns a maximum of 100 results. The calculations are based on all the current data in the source index. It also
generates a list of mappings and settings for the destination index. These values are determined based on the field
types of the source index and the transform aggregations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Preview a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-preview-transform-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/_preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_transform/_preview`

Generates a preview of the results that you will get when you create a transform with the same configuration.

It returns a maximum of 100 results. The calculations are based on all the current data in the source index. It also
generates a list of mappings and settings for the destination index. These values are determined based on the field
types of the source index and the transform aggregations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\"\n  },\n  \"pivot\": {\n    \"group_by\": {\n      \"customer_id\": {\n        \"terms\": {\n          \"field\": \"customer_id\",\n          \"missing_bucket\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"aggregations\": {\n      \"max_price\": {\n        \"max\": {\n          \"field\": \"taxful_total_price\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

|» » » flush_threshold_size|object|false|none|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|
