## Reset a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-reset-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_reset`

Before you can reset it, you must stop it; alternatively, use the `force` query parameter.
If the destination index was created by the transform, it is deleted.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="reset-a-transform-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the transform. This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9),<br>hyphens, and underscores. It has a 64 character limit and must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If this value is `true`, the transform is reset regardless of its current state. If it's `false`, the transform<br>must be stopped before it can be reset.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="reset-a-transform-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Schedule a transform to start now

<a id="opIdtransform-schedule-now-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_schedule_now \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_schedule_now`

Instantly run a transform to process data.
If you run this API, the transform will process the new data instantly,
without waiting for the configured frequency interval. After the API is called,
the transform will be processed again at `now + frequency` unless the API
is called again in the meantime.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="schedule-a-transform-to-start-now-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the transform.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Controls the time to wait for the scheduling to take place|
|defer|query|boolean|false|When true, defers the scheduling by the transform's configured sync delay<br>instead of triggering immediately. The transform will process new data after<br>the delay elapses rather than right away.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="schedule-a-transform-to-start-now-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set upgrade_mode for transform indices

<a id="opIdtransform-set-upgrade-mode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/set_upgrade_mode \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/set_upgrade_mode`

Sets a cluster wide upgrade_mode setting that prepares transform
indices for an upgrade.
When upgrading your cluster, in some circumstances you must restart your
nodes and reindex your transform indices. In those circumstances,
there must be no transforms running. You can close the transforms,
do the upgrade, then open all the transforms again. Alternatively,
you can use this API to temporarily halt tasks associated with the transforms
and prevent new transforms from opening. You can also use this API
during upgrades that do not require you to reindex your transform
indices, though stopping transforms is not a requirement in that case.
You can see the current value for the upgrade_mode setting by using the get
transform info API.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="set-upgrademode-for-transform-indices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|When `true`, it enables `upgrade_mode` which temporarily halts all<br>transform tasks and prohibits new transform tasks from<br>starting.|
|timeout|query|object|false|The time to wait for the request to be completed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-upgrademode-for-transform-indices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Start a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-start-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_start`

When you start a transform, it creates the destination index if it does not already exist. The `number_of_shards` is
set to `1` and the `auto_expand_replicas` is set to `0-1`. If it is a pivot transform, it deduces the mapping
definitions for the destination index from the source indices and the transform aggregations. If fields in the
destination index are derived from scripts (as in the case of `scripted_metric` or `bucket_script` aggregations),
the transform uses dynamic mappings unless an index template exists. If it is a latest transform, it does not deduce
mapping definitions; it uses dynamic mappings. To use explicit mappings, create the destination index before you
start the transform. Alternatively, you can create an index template, though it does not affect the deduced mappings
in a pivot transform.

When the transform starts, a series of validations occur to ensure its success. If you deferred validation when you
created the transform, they occur when you start the transform—​with the exception of privilege checks. When
Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the transform remembers which roles the user that created it had at the
time of creation and uses those same roles. If those roles do not have the required privileges on the source and
destination indices, the transform fails when it attempts unauthorized operations.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="start-a-transform-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)|true|Identifier for the transform.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|from|query|string|false|Restricts the set of transformed entities to those changed after this time. Relative times like now-30d are supported. Only applicable for continuous transforms.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="start-a-transform-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Stop transforms

<a id="opIdtransform-stop-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_stop`

Stops one or more transforms.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="stop-transforms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transform_id|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|Identifier for the transform. To stop multiple transforms, use a comma-separated list or a wildcard expression.<br>To stop all transforms, use `_all` or `*` as the identifier.|
|allow_no_match|query|boolean|false|Specifies what to do when the request: contains wildcard expressions and there are no transforms that match;<br>contains the `_all` string or no identifiers and there are no matches; contains wildcard expressions and there<br>are only partial matches.<br><br>If it is true, the API returns a successful acknowledgement message when there are no matches. When there are<br>only partial matches, the API stops the appropriate transforms.<br><br>If it is false, the request returns a 404 status code when there are no matches or only partial matches.|
|force|query|boolean|false|If it is true, the API forcefully stops the transforms.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response when `wait_for_completion` is `true`. If no response is received before the<br>timeout expires, the request returns a timeout exception. However, the request continues processing and<br>eventually moves the transform to a STOPPED state.|
|wait_for_checkpoint|query|boolean|false|If it is true, the transform does not completely stop until the current checkpoint is completed. If it is false,<br>the transform stops as soon as possible.|
|wait_for_completion|query|boolean|false|If it is true, the API blocks until the indexer state completely stops. If it is false, the API returns<br>immediately and the indexer is stopped asynchronously in the background.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="stop-transforms-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update a transform

<a id="opIdtransform-update-transform"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/string/_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\",\n    \"query\": {\n      \"term\": {\n        \"geoip.continent_name\": {\n          \"value\": \"Asia\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"description\": \"Maximum priced ecommerce data by customer_id in Asia\",\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce_transform_v2\",\n    \"pipeline\": \"add_timestamp_pipeline\"\n  },\n  \"frequency\": \"15m\",\n  \"sync\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"delay\": \"120s\"\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_transform/{transform_id}/_update`

Updates certain properties of a transform.

All updated properties except `description` do not take effect until after the transform starts the next checkpoint,
thus there is data consistency in each checkpoint. To use this API, you must have `read` and `view_index_metadata`
privileges for the source indices. You must also have `index` and `read` privileges for the destination index. When
Elasticsearch security features are enabled, the transform remembers which roles the user who updated it had at the
time of update and runs with those privileges.

## Required authorization

* Index privileges: `read`,`index`,`view_index_metadata`
* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"source\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce\",\n    \"query\": {\n      \"term\": {\n        \"geoip.continent_name\": {\n          \"value\": \"Asia\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"description\": \"Maximum priced ecommerce data by customer_id in Asia\",\n  \"dest\": {\n    \"index\": \"kibana_sample_data_ecommerce_transform_v2\",\n    \"pipeline\": \"add_timestamp_pipeline\"\n  },\n  \"frequency\": \"15m\",\n  \"sync\": {\n    \"time\": {\n      \"field\": \"order_date\",\n      \"delay\": \"120s\"\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Upgrade all transforms

<a id="opIdtransform-upgrade-transforms"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_transform/_upgrade \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_transform/_upgrade`

Transforms are compatible across minor versions and between supported major versions.
However, over time, the format of transform configuration information may change.
This API identifies transforms that have a legacy configuration format and upgrades them to the latest version.
It also cleans up the internal data structures that store the transform state and checkpoints.
The upgrade does not affect the source and destination indices.
The upgrade also does not affect the roles that transforms use when Elasticsearch security features are enabled; the role used to read source data and write to the destination index remains unchanged.

If a transform upgrade step fails, the upgrade stops and an error is returned about the underlying issue.
Resolve the issue then re-run the process again.
A summary is returned when the upgrade is finished.

To ensure continuous transforms remain running during a major version upgrade of the cluster – for example, from 7.16 to 8.0 – it is recommended to upgrade transforms before upgrading the cluster.
You may want to perform a recent cluster backup prior to the upgrade.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_transform`


<h3 id="upgrade-all-transforms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dry_run|query|boolean|false|When true, the request checks for updates but does not run them.|
|timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and<br>returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"needs_update\": 0,\n  \"updated\": 2,\n  \"no_action\": 1\n}"
```

<h3 id="upgrade-all-transforms-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="upgrade-all-transforms-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|needs_update|number|true|none|The number of transforms that need to be upgraded.|
|no_action|number|true|none|The number of transforms that don’t require upgrading.|
|updated|number|true|none|The number of transforms that have been upgraded.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-watcher">watcher</h1>

## Acknowledge a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-ack-watch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string/_ack \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /_watcher/watch/{watch_id}/_ack`

Acknowledging a watch enables you to manually throttle the execution of the watch's actions.

The acknowledgement state of an action is stored in the `status.actions.<id>.ack.state` structure.

IMPORTANT: If the specified watch is currently being executed, this API will return an error
The reason for this behavior is to prevent overwriting the watch status from a watch execution.

Acknowledging an action throttles further executions of that action until its `ack.state` is reset to `awaits_successful_execution`.
This happens when the condition of the watch is not met (the condition evaluates to false).
To demonstrate how throttling works in practice and how it can be configured for individual actions within a watch, refer to External documentation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/actions#example">Learn more about actions</a>

<h3 id="acknowledge-a-watch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|watch_id|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The watch identifier.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"status\": {\n    \"state\": {\n      \"active\": true,\n      \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.723Z\"\n    },\n    \"last_checked\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.753Z\",\n    \"last_met_condition\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.763Z\",\n    \"actions\": {\n      \"test_index\": {\n        \"ack\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.713Z\",\n          \"state\": \"acked\"\n        },\n        \"last_execution\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-25T18:04:27.733Z\",\n          \"successful\": true\n        },\n        \"last_successful_execution\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-25T18:04:27.773Z\",\n          \"successful\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"execution_state\": \"executed\",\n    \"version\": 2\n  }\n}"
```

|200|OK||Inline|

Acknowledging a watch enables you to manually throttle the execution of the watch's actions.

The acknowledgement state of an action is stored in the `status.actions.<id>.ack.state` structure.

IMPORTANT: If the specified watch is currently being executed, this API will return an error
The reason for this behavior is to prevent overwriting the watch status from a watch execution.

Acknowledging an action throttles further executions of that action until its `ack.state` is reset to `awaits_successful_execution`.
This happens when the condition of the watch is not met (the condition evaluates to false).
To demonstrate how throttling works in practice and how it can be configured for individual actions within a watch, refer to External documentation.

## Acknowledge a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-ack-watch-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string/_ack/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /_watcher/watch/{watch_id}/_ack/{action_id}`

Acknowledging a watch enables you to manually throttle the execution of the watch's actions.

The acknowledgement state of an action is stored in the `status.actions.<id>.ack.state` structure.

IMPORTANT: If the specified watch is currently being executed, this API will return an error
The reason for this behavior is to prevent overwriting the watch status from a watch execution.

Acknowledging an action throttles further executions of that action until its `ack.state` is reset to `awaits_successful_execution`.
This happens when the condition of the watch is not met (the condition evaluates to false).
To demonstrate how throttling works in practice and how it can be configured for individual actions within a watch, refer to External documentation.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/actions#example">Learn more about actions</a>

<h3 id="acknowledge-a-watch-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|watch_id|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The watch identifier.|
|action_id|path|[_types.Names](#schema_types.names)|true|A comma-separated list of the action identifiers to acknowledge.<br>If you omit this parameter, all of the actions of the watch are acknowledged.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"status\": {\n    \"state\": {\n      \"active\": true,\n      \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.723Z\"\n    },\n    \"last_checked\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.753Z\",\n    \"last_met_condition\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.763Z\",\n    \"actions\": {\n      \"test_index\": {\n        \"ack\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-26T18:04:27.713Z\",\n          \"state\": \"acked\"\n        },\n        \"last_execution\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-25T18:04:27.733Z\",\n          \"successful\": true\n        },\n        \"last_successful_execution\" : {\n          \"timestamp\": \"2015-05-25T18:04:27.773Z\",\n          \"successful\": true\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    \"execution_state\": \"executed\",\n    \"version\": 2\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-put-watch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger\" : {\n    \"schedule\" : { \"cron\" : \"0 0/1 * * * ?\" }\n  },\n  \"input\" : {\n    \"search\" : {\n      \"request\" : {\n        \"indices\" : [\n          \"logstash*\"\n        ],\n        \"body\" : {\n          \"query\" : {\n            \"bool\" : {\n              \"must\" : {\n                \"match\": {\n                  \"response\": 404\n                }\n              },\n              \"filter\" : {\n                \"range\": {\n                  \"@timestamp\": {\n                    \"from\": \"{{ctx.trigger.scheduled_time}}||-5m\",\n                    \"to\": \"{{ctx.trigger.triggered_time}}\"\n                  }\n                }\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"condition\" : {\n    \"compare\" : { \"ctx.payload.hits.total\" : { \"gt\" : 0 }}\n  },\n  \"actions\" : {\n    \"email_admin\" : {\n      \"email\" : {\n        \"to\" : \"admin@domain.host.com\",\n        \"subject\" : \"404 recently encountered\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`PUT /_watcher/watch/{id}`

When a watch is registered, a new document that represents the watch is added to the `.watches` index and its trigger is immediately registered with the relevant trigger engine.
Typically for the `schedule` trigger, the scheduler is the trigger engine.

IMPORTANT: You must use Kibana or this API to create a watch.
Do not add a watch directly to the `.watches` index by using the Elasticsearch index API.
If Elasticsearch security features are enabled, do not give users write privileges on the `.watches` index.

When you add a watch you can also define its initial active state by setting the *active* parameter.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, your watch can index or search only on indices for which the user that stored the watch has privileges.
If the user is able to read index `a`, but not index `b`, the same will apply when the watch runs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger\" : {\n    \"schedule\" : { \"cron\" : \"0 0/1 * * * ?\" }\n  },\n  \"input\" : {\n    \"search\" : {\n      \"request\" : {\n        \"indices\" : [\n          \"logstash*\"\n        ],\n        \"body\" : {\n          \"query\" : {\n            \"bool\" : {\n              \"must\" : {\n                \"match\": {\n                  \"response\": 404\n                }\n              },\n              \"filter\" : {\n                \"range\": {\n                  \"@timestamp\": {\n                    \"from\": \"{{ctx.trigger.scheduled_time}}||-5m\",\n                    \"to\": \"{{ctx.trigger.triggered_time}}\"\n                  }\n                }\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"condition\" : {\n    \"compare\" : { \"ctx.payload.hits.total\" : { \"gt\" : 0 }}\n  },\n  \"actions\" : {\n    \"email_admin\" : {\n      \"email\" : {\n        \"to\" : \"admin@domain.host.com\",\n        \"subject\" : \"404 recently encountered\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Create or update a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-put-watch-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger\" : {\n    \"schedule\" : { \"cron\" : \"0 0/1 * * * ?\" }\n  },\n  \"input\" : {\n    \"search\" : {\n      \"request\" : {\n        \"indices\" : [\n          \"logstash*\"\n        ],\n        \"body\" : {\n          \"query\" : {\n            \"bool\" : {\n              \"must\" : {\n                \"match\": {\n                  \"response\": 404\n                }\n              },\n              \"filter\" : {\n                \"range\": {\n                  \"@timestamp\": {\n                    \"from\": \"{{ctx.trigger.scheduled_time}}||-5m\",\n                    \"to\": \"{{ctx.trigger.triggered_time}}\"\n                  }\n                }\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"condition\" : {\n    \"compare\" : { \"ctx.payload.hits.total\" : { \"gt\" : 0 }}\n  },\n  \"actions\" : {\n    \"email_admin\" : {\n      \"email\" : {\n        \"to\" : \"admin@domain.host.com\",\n        \"subject\" : \"404 recently encountered\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"'
```

`POST /_watcher/watch/{id}`

When a watch is registered, a new document that represents the watch is added to the `.watches` index and its trigger is immediately registered with the relevant trigger engine.
Typically for the `schedule` trigger, the scheduler is the trigger engine.

IMPORTANT: You must use Kibana or this API to create a watch.
Do not add a watch directly to the `.watches` index by using the Elasticsearch index API.
If Elasticsearch security features are enabled, do not give users write privileges on the `.watches` index.

When you add a watch you can also define its initial active state by setting the *active* parameter.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, your watch can index or search only on indices for which the user that stored the watch has privileges.
If the user is able to read index `a`, but not index `b`, the same will apply when the watch runs.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger\" : {\n    \"schedule\" : { \"cron\" : \"0 0/1 * * * ?\" }\n  },\n  \"input\" : {\n    \"search\" : {\n      \"request\" : {\n        \"indices\" : [\n          \"logstash*\"\n        ],\n        \"body\" : {\n          \"query\" : {\n            \"bool\" : {\n              \"must\" : {\n                \"match\": {\n                  \"response\": 404\n                }\n              },\n              \"filter\" : {\n                \"range\": {\n                  \"@timestamp\": {\n                    \"from\": \"{{ctx.trigger.scheduled_time}}||-5m\",\n                    \"to\": \"{{ctx.trigger.triggered_time}}\"\n                  }\n                }\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  },\n  \"condition\" : {\n    \"compare\" : { \"ctx.payload.hits.total\" : { \"gt\" : 0 }}\n  },\n  \"actions\" : {\n    \"email_admin\" : {\n      \"email\" : {\n        \"to\" : \"admin@domain.host.com\",\n        \"subject\" : \"404 recently encountered\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}"
```

## Delete a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-delete-watch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /_watcher/watch/{id}`

When the watch is removed, the document representing the watch in the `.watches` index is gone and it will never be run again.

Deleting a watch does not delete any watch execution records related to this watch from the watch history.

IMPORTANT: Deleting a watch must be done by using only this API.
Do not delete the watch directly from the `.watches` index using the Elasticsearch delete document API
When Elasticsearch security features are enabled, make sure no write privileges are granted to anyone for the `.watches` index.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<h3 id="delete-a-watch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)|true|The watch identifier.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"found\": true,\n  \"_id\": \"my_watch\",\n  \"_version\": 2\n}"
```

<h3 id="delete-a-watch-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="delete-a-watch-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|found|boolean|true|none|none|
|_id|object|true|none|none|
|_version|object|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Run a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-execute-watch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string/_execute \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"'
```

`PUT /_watcher/watch/{id}/_execute`

This API can be used to force execution of the watch outside of its triggering logic or to simulate the watch execution for debugging purposes.

For testing and debugging purposes, you also have fine-grained control on how the watch runs.
You can run the watch without running all of its actions or alternatively by simulating them.
You can also force execution by ignoring the watch condition and control whether a watch record would be written to the watch history after it runs.

You can use the run watch API to run watches that are not yet registered by specifying the watch definition inline.
This serves as great tool for testing and debugging your watches prior to adding them to Watcher.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled on your cluster, watches are run with the privileges of the user that stored the watches.
If your user is allowed to read index `a`, but not index `b`, then the exact same set of rules will apply during execution of a watch.

When using the run watch API, the authorization data of the user that called the API will be used as a base, instead of the information who stored the watch.
Refer to the external documentation for examples of watch execution requests, including existing, customized, and inline watches.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/execute-watch">More about executing a watch</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"
```

## Run a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-execute-watch-1"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/string/_execute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"'
```

`POST /_watcher/watch/{id}/_execute`

This API can be used to force execution of the watch outside of its triggering logic or to simulate the watch execution for debugging purposes.

For testing and debugging purposes, you also have fine-grained control on how the watch runs.
You can run the watch without running all of its actions or alternatively by simulating them.
You can also force execution by ignoring the watch condition and control whether a watch record would be written to the watch history after it runs.

You can use the run watch API to run watches that are not yet registered by specifying the watch definition inline.
This serves as great tool for testing and debugging your watches prior to adding them to Watcher.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled on your cluster, watches are run with the privileges of the user that stored the watches.
If your user is allowed to read index `a`, but not index `b`, then the exact same set of rules will apply during execution of a watch.

When using the run watch API, the authorization data of the user that called the API will be used as a base, instead of the information who stored the watch.
Refer to the external documentation for examples of watch execution requests, including existing, customized, and inline watches.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/execute-watch">More about executing a watch</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"
```

## Run a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-execute-watch-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/_execute \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"'
```

`PUT /_watcher/watch/_execute`

This API can be used to force execution of the watch outside of its triggering logic or to simulate the watch execution for debugging purposes.

For testing and debugging purposes, you also have fine-grained control on how the watch runs.
You can run the watch without running all of its actions or alternatively by simulating them.
You can also force execution by ignoring the watch condition and control whether a watch record would be written to the watch history after it runs.

You can use the run watch API to run watches that are not yet registered by specifying the watch definition inline.
This serves as great tool for testing and debugging your watches prior to adding them to Watcher.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled on your cluster, watches are run with the privileges of the user that stored the watches.
If your user is allowed to read index `a`, but not index `b`, then the exact same set of rules will apply during execution of a watch.

When using the run watch API, the authorization data of the user that called the API will be used as a base, instead of the information who stored the watch.
Refer to the external documentation for examples of watch execution requests, including existing, customized, and inline watches.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/execute-watch">More about executing a watch</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"
```

## Run a watch

<a id="opIdwatcher-execute-watch-3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/watch/_execute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"'
```

`POST /_watcher/watch/_execute`

This API can be used to force execution of the watch outside of its triggering logic or to simulate the watch execution for debugging purposes.

For testing and debugging purposes, you also have fine-grained control on how the watch runs.
You can run the watch without running all of its actions or alternatively by simulating them.
You can also force execution by ignoring the watch condition and control whether a watch record would be written to the watch history after it runs.

You can use the run watch API to run watches that are not yet registered by specifying the watch definition inline.
This serves as great tool for testing and debugging your watches prior to adding them to Watcher.

When Elasticsearch security features are enabled on your cluster, watches are run with the privileges of the user that stored the watches.
If your user is allowed to read index `a`, but not index `b`, then the exact same set of rules will apply during execution of a watch.

When using the run watch API, the authorization data of the user that called the API will be used as a base, instead of the information who stored the watch.
Refer to the external documentation for examples of watch execution requests, including existing, customized, and inline watches.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<a href="https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/watcher/execute-watch">More about executing a watch</a>

> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"trigger_data\" : { \n    \"triggered_time\" : \"now\",\n    \"scheduled_time\" : \"now\"\n  },\n  \"alternative_input\" : { \n    \"foo\" : \"bar\"\n  },\n  \"ignore_condition\" : true, \n  \"action_modes\" : {\n    \"my-action\" : \"force_simulate\" \n  },\n  \"record_execution\" : true \n}"
```

## Get Watcher index settings

<a id="opIdwatcher-get-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_watcher/settings`

Get settings for the Watcher internal index (`.watches`).
Only a subset of settings are shown, for example `index.auto_expand_replicas` and `index.number_of_replicas`.

<h3 id="get-watcher-index-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"index\": {\n    \"auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-4\",\n    \"number_of_replicas\": 0\n  }\n}"
```

<h3 id="get-watcher-index-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

## Update Watcher index settings

<a id="opIdwatcher-update-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"{\n  \"index.auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-4\"\n}"'
```

`PUT /_watcher/settings`

Update settings for the Watcher internal index (`.watches`).
Only a subset of settings can be modified.
This includes `index.auto_expand_replicas`, `index.number_of_replicas`, `index.routing.allocation.exclude.*`,
`index.routing.allocation.include.*` and `index.routing.allocation.require.*`.
Modification of `index.routing.allocation.include._tier_preference` is an exception and is not allowed as the
Watcher shards must always be in the `data_content` tier.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


> Body parameter

```json
"{\n  \"index.auto_expand_replicas\": \"0-4\"\n}"
```

<h3 id="update-watcher-index-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|timeout|query|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration)|false|The period to wait for a response.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» index.auto_expand_replicas|body|string|false|none|
|» index.number_of_replicas|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acknowledged": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-watcher-index-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="update-watcher-index-settings-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledged|boolean|true|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`GET /_watcher/_query/watches`

Get all registered watches in a paginated manner and optionally filter watches by a query.

Note that only the `_id` and `metadata.*` fields are queryable or sortable.

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_watcher`

<h3 id="query-watches-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|The total number of watches found.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /_watcher/_query/watches`

Get all registered watches in a paginated manner and optionally filter watches by a query.

Note that only the `_id` and `metadata.*` fields are queryable or sortable.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_watcher`

## Start the watch service

<a id="opIdwatcher-start"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /_watcher/_start`

Start the Watcher service if it is not already running.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `manage_watcher`


<h3 id="start-the-watch-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|Period to wait for a connection to the master node.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\n  \"acknowledged\": true\n}"
```

<h3 id="start-the-watch-service-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[_types.AcknowledgedResponseBase](#schema_types.acknowledgedresponsebase)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get Watcher statistics

<a id="opIdwatcher-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_watcher/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_watcher/stats`

This API always returns basic metrics.
You retrieve more metrics by using the metric parameter.

* Cluster privileges: `monitor_watcher`

|metric|query|[watcher.stats.WatcherMetric](#schemawatcher.stats.watchermetric) \| [[watcher.stats.WatcherMetric](#schemawatcher.stats.watchermetric)]|false|Defines which additional metrics are included in the response.|

```json
"{\n  \"watcher_state\": \"started\",  \n  \"watch_count\": 1, \n  \"execution_thread_pool\": {\n    \"size\": 1000, \n    \"max_size\": 1 \n  }\n}"
```

<h1 id="elasticsearch-request-response-specification-xpack">xpack</h1>

## Get information

<a id="opIdxpack-info"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_xpack \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_xpack`

The information provided by the API includes:

* Build information including the build number and timestamp.
* License information about the currently installed license.
* Feature information for the features that are currently enabled and available under the current license.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|categories|query|[[xpack.info.XPackCategory](#schemaxpack.info.xpackcategory)]|false|A comma-separated list of the information categories to include in the response.<br>For example, `build,license,features`.|
|accept_enterprise|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If used, this otherwise ignored parameter must be set to true|
|human|query|boolean|false|Defines whether additional human-readable information is included in the response.<br>In particular, it adds descriptions and a tag line.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|categories|build|
|categories|features|
|categories|license|

## Get usage information

<a id="opIdxpack-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9200/_xpack/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /_xpack/usage`

Get information about the features that are currently enabled and available under the current license.
The API also provides some usage statistics.

## Required authorization

* Cluster privileges: `monitor`


<h3 id="get-usage-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|master_timeout|query|object|false|The period to wait for a connection to the master node.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.Duration">_types.Duration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.duration"></a>
<a id="schema__types.Duration"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.duration"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.duration"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A duration. Units can be `nanos`, `micros`, `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours) and
`d` (days). Also accepts "0" without a unit and "-1" to indicate an unspecified value.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|-1|
|*oneOf*|0|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|false|none|none|
|is_partial|boolean|true|none|When the query is no longer running, this property indicates whether the search failed or was successfully completed on all shards.<br>While the query is running, `is_partial` is always set to `true`.|
|is_running|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the search is still running or has completed.<br><br>> info<br>> If the search failed after some shards returned their results or the node that is coordinating the async search dies, results may be partial even though `is_running` is `false`.|
|expiration_time|object|false|none|Indicates when the async search will expire.|
|expiration_time_in_millis|object|true|none|none|
|start_time|object|false|none|none|
|start_time_in_millis|object|true|none|none|
|completion_time|object|false|none|Indicates when the async search completed.<br>It is present only when the search has completed.|
|completion_time_in_millis|object|false|none|none|
|error|object|false|none|none|
|response|object|true|none|none|

The absence of any type. This is commonly used in APIs that don't return a body.

Although "void" is generally used for the unit type that has only one value, this is to be interpreted as
the bottom type that has no value at all. Most languages have a unit type, but few have a bottom type.

See https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_type and https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottom_type

Cause and details about a request failure. This class defines the properties common to all error types.
Additional details are also provided, that depend on the error type.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of error|
|reason|string \| string \| null|false|none|A human-readable explanation of the error, in English.|
|stack_trace|string|false|none|The server stack trace. Present only if the `error_trace=true` parameter was sent with the request.|
|caused_by|object|false|none|none|
|root_cause|[[_types.ErrorCause](#schema_types.errorcause)]|false|none|none|
|suppressed|[[_types.ErrorCause](#schema_types.errorcause)]|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Defines the aggregations that are run as part of the search request.|
|collapse|object|false|none|Collapses search results the values of the specified field.|
|explain|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the request returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.|
|ext|object|false|none|Configuration of search extensions defined by Elasticsearch plugins.|
|from|number|false|none|The starting document offset, which must be non-negative.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.|
|highlight|object|false|none|Specifies the highlighter to use for retrieving highlighted snippets from one or more fields in your search results.|
|track_total_hits|object|false|none|Number of hits matching the query to count accurately.<br>If `true`, the exact number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance.<br>If `false`, the  response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.|
|indices_boost|[object]|false|none|Boost the `_score` of documents from specified indices.<br>The boost value is the factor by which scores are multiplied.<br>A boost value greater than `1.0` increases the score.<br>A boost value between `0` and `1.0` decreases the score.|
|docvalue_fields|[[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|none|An array of wildcard (`*`) field patterns.<br>The request returns doc values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|knn|[_types.KnnSearch](#schema_types.knnsearch) \| [[_types.KnnSearch](#schema_types.knnsearch)]|false|none|The approximate kNN search to run.|
|rank|object|false|none|The Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to use.|
|min_score|number|false|none|The minimum `_score` for matching documents.<br>Documents with a lower `_score` are not included in search results or results collected by aggregations.|
|post_filter|object|false|none|Use the `post_filter` parameter to filter search results.<br>The search hits are filtered after the aggregations are calculated.<br>A post filter has no impact on the aggregation results.|
|profile|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to return detailed timing information about the execution of individual components in a search request.<br>NOTE: This is a debugging tool and adds significant overhead to search execution.|
|query|object|false|none|The search definition using the Query DSL.|
|rescore|[_global.search._types.Rescore](#schema_global.search._types.rescore) \| [[_global.search._types.Rescore](#schema_global.search._types.rescore)]|false|none|Can be used to improve precision by reordering just the top (for example 100 - 500) documents returned by the `query` and `post_filter` phases.|
|retriever|object|false|none|A retriever is a specification to describe top documents returned from a search.<br>A retriever replaces other elements of the search API that also return top documents such as `query` and `knn`.|
|script_fields|object|false|none|Retrieve a script evaluation (based on different fields) for each hit.|
|search_after|object|false|none|Used to retrieve the next page of hits using a set of sort values from the previous page.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of hits to return, which must not be negative.<br>By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.<br>To page through more hits, use the `search_after` property.|
|slice|object|false|none|Split a scrolled search into multiple slices that can be consumed independently.|
|sort|object|false|none|A comma-separated list of <field>:<direction> pairs.|
|_source|object|false|none|The source fields that are returned for matching documents.<br>These fields are returned in the `hits._source` property of the search response.<br>If the `stored_fields` property is specified, the `_source` property defaults to `false`.<br>Otherwise, it defaults to `true`.|
|fields|[[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|none|An array of wildcard (`*`) field patterns.<br>The request returns values for field names matching these patterns in the `hits.fields` property of the response.|
|suggest|object|false|none|Defines a suggester that provides similar looking terms based on a provided text.|
|terminate_after|number|false|none|The maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.<br>If a query reaches this limit, Elasticsearch terminates the query early.<br>Elasticsearch collects documents before sorting.<br><br>IMPORTANT: Use with caution.<br>Elasticsearch applies this property to each shard handling the request.<br>When possible, let Elasticsearch perform early termination automatically.<br>Avoid specifying this property for requests that target data streams with backing indices across multiple data tiers.<br><br>If set to `0` (default), the query does not terminate early.|
|timeout|string|false|none|The period of time to wait for a response from each shard.<br>If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.<br>Defaults to no timeout.|
|track_scores|boolean|false|none|If `true`, calculate and return document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.|
|version|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the request returns the document version as part of a hit.|
|seq_no_primary_term|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the request returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.|
|stored_fields|object|false|none|A comma-separated list of stored fields to return as part of a hit.<br>If no fields are specified, no stored fields are included in the response.<br>If this field is specified, the `_source` property defaults to `false`.<br>You can pass `_source: true` to return both source fields and stored fields in the search response.|
|pit|object|false|none|Limit the search to a point in time (PIT).<br>If you provide a PIT, you cannot specify an `<index>` in the request path.|
|runtime_mappings|object|false|none|One or more runtime fields in the search request.<br>These fields take precedence over mapped fields with the same name.|
|stats|[string]|false|none|The stats groups to associate with the search.<br>Each group maintains a statistics aggregation for its associated searches.<br>You can retrieve these stats using the indices stats API.|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Sub-aggregations for this aggregation.<br>Only applies to bucket aggregations.|
|meta|object|false|none|none|
|adjacency_matrix|object|false|none|A bucket aggregation returning a form of adjacency matrix.<br>The request provides a collection of named filter expressions, similar to the `filters` aggregation.<br>Each bucket in the response represents a non-empty cell in the matrix of intersecting filters.|
|auto_date_histogram|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation similar to the date histogram, except instead of providing an interval to use as the width of each bucket, a target number of buckets is provided.|
|avg|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that computes the average of numeric values that are extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|avg_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which calculates the mean value of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation.<br>The specified metric must be numeric and the sibling aggregation must be a multi-bucket aggregation.|
|boxplot|object|false|none|A metrics aggregation that computes a box plot of numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|bucket_script|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which runs a script which can perform per bucket computations on metrics in the parent multi-bucket aggregation.|
|bucket_selector|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which runs a script to determine whether the current bucket will be retained in the parent multi-bucket aggregation.|
|bucket_sort|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which sorts the buckets of its parent multi-bucket aggregation.|
|bucket_count_ks_test|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which runs a two sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test ("K-S test") against a provided distribution and the distribution implied by the documents counts in the configured sibling aggregation.|
|bucket_correlation|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which runs a correlation function on the configured sibling multi-bucket aggregation.|
|cardinality|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that calculates an approximate count of distinct values.|
|cartesian_bounds|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that computes the spatial bounding box containing all values for a Point or Shape field.|
|cartesian_centroid|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that computes the weighted centroid from all coordinate values for point and shape fields.|
|categorize_text|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that groups semi-structured text into buckets.|
|change_point|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline that detects, spikes, dips, and change points in a metric.<br>Given a distribution of values provided by the sibling multi-bucket aggregation,<br>this aggregation indicates the bucket of any spike or dip and/or the bucket at which<br>the largest change in the distribution of values, if they are statistically significant.<br>There must be at least 22 bucketed values. Fewer than 1,000 is preferred.|
|children|object|false|none|A single bucket aggregation that selects child documents that have the specified type, as defined in a `join` field.|
|composite|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that creates composite buckets from different sources.<br>Unlike the other multi-bucket aggregations, you can use the `composite` aggregation to paginate *all* buckets from a multi-level aggregation efficiently.|
|cumulative_cardinality|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which calculates the cumulative cardinality in a parent `histogram` or `date_histogram` aggregation.|
|cumulative_sum|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which calculates the cumulative sum of a specified metric in a parent `histogram` or `date_histogram` aggregation.|
|date_histogram|object|false|none|A multi-bucket values source based aggregation that can be applied on date values or date range values extracted from the documents.<br>It dynamically builds fixed size (interval) buckets over the values.|
|date_range|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation that enables the user to define a set of date ranges - each representing a bucket.|
|derivative|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which calculates the derivative of a specified metric in a parent `histogram` or `date_histogram` aggregation.|
|diversified_sampler|object|false|none|A filtering aggregation used to limit any sub aggregations' processing to a sample of the top-scoring documents.<br>Similar to the `sampler` aggregation, but adds the ability to limit the number of matches that share a common value.|
|extended_stats|object|false|none|A multi-value metrics aggregation that computes stats over numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|extended_stats_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which calculates a variety of stats across all bucket of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation.|
|frequent_item_sets|object|false|none|A bucket aggregation which finds frequent item sets, a form of association rules mining that identifies items that often occur together.|
|filter|object|false|none|A single bucket aggregation that narrows the set of documents to those that match a query.|
|filters|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation where each bucket contains the documents that match a query.|
|geo_bounds|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that computes the geographic bounding box containing all values for a Geopoint or Geoshape field.|
|geo_centroid|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that computes the weighted centroid from all coordinate values for geo fields.|
|geo_distance|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that works on `geo_point` fields.<br>Evaluates the distance of each document value from an origin point and determines the buckets it belongs to, based on ranges defined in the request.|
|geohash_grid|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that groups `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values into buckets that represent a grid.<br>Each cell is labeled using a geohash which is of user-definable precision.|
|geo_line|object|false|none|Aggregates all `geo_point` values within a bucket into a `LineString` ordered by the chosen sort field.|
|geotile_grid|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that groups `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values into buckets that represent a grid.<br>Each cell corresponds to a map tile as used by many online map sites.|
|geohex_grid|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that groups `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values into buckets that represent a grid.<br>Each cell corresponds to a H3 cell index and is labeled using the H3Index representation.|
|global|object|false|none|Defines a single bucket of all the documents within the search execution context.<br>This context is defined by the indices and the document types you’re searching on, but is not influenced by the search query itself.|
|histogram|object|false|none|A multi-bucket values source based aggregation that can be applied on numeric values or numeric range values extracted from the documents.<br>It dynamically builds fixed size (interval) buckets over the values.|
|ip_range|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation that enables the user to define a set of IP ranges - each representing a bucket.|
|ip_prefix|object|false|none|A bucket aggregation that groups documents based on the network or sub-network of an IP address.|
|inference|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which loads a pre-trained model and performs inference on the collated result fields from the parent bucket aggregation.|
|line|object|false|none|none|
|matrix_stats|object|false|none|A numeric aggregation that computes the following statistics over a set of document fields: `count`, `mean`, `variance`, `skewness`, `kurtosis`, `covariance`, and `covariance`.|
|max|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that returns the maximum value among the numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|max_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which identifies the bucket(s) with the maximum value of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation and outputs both the value and the key(s) of the bucket(s).|
|median_absolute_deviation|object|false|none|A single-value aggregation that approximates the median absolute deviation of its search results.|
|min|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that returns the minimum value among numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|min_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which identifies the bucket(s) with the minimum value of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation and outputs both the value and the key(s) of the bucket(s).|
|missing|object|false|none|A field data based single bucket aggregation, that creates a bucket of all documents in the current document set context that are missing a field value (effectively, missing a field or having the configured NULL value set).|
|moving_avg|object|false|none|none|
|moving_percentiles|object|false|none|Given an ordered series of percentiles, "slides" a window across those percentiles and computes cumulative percentiles.|
|moving_fn|object|false|none|Given an ordered series of data, "slides" a window across the data and runs a custom script on each window of data.<br>For convenience, a number of common functions are predefined such as `min`, `max`, and moving averages.|
|multi_terms|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation where buckets are dynamically built - one per unique set of values.|
|nested|object|false|none|A special single bucket aggregation that enables aggregating nested documents.|
|normalize|object|false|none|A parent pipeline aggregation which calculates the specific normalized/rescaled value for a specific bucket value.|
|parent|object|false|none|A special single bucket aggregation that selects parent documents that have the specified type, as defined in a `join` field.|
|percentile_ranks|object|false|none|A multi-value metrics aggregation that calculates one or more percentile ranks over numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|percentiles|object|false|none|A multi-value metrics aggregation that calculates one or more percentiles over numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|percentiles_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which calculates percentiles across all bucket of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation.|
|range|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation that enables the user to define a set of ranges - each representing a bucket.|
|rare_terms|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation which finds "rare" terms — terms that are at the long-tail of the distribution and are not frequent.|
|rate|object|false|none|Calculates a rate of documents or a field in each bucket.<br>Can only be used inside a `date_histogram` or `composite` aggregation.|
|reverse_nested|object|false|none|A special single bucket aggregation that enables aggregating on parent documents from nested documents.<br>Should only be defined inside a `nested` aggregation.|
|random_sampler|object|false|none|A single bucket aggregation that randomly includes documents in the aggregated results.<br>Sampling provides significant speed improvement at the cost of accuracy.|
|sampler|object|false|none|A filtering aggregation used to limit any sub aggregations' processing to a sample of the top-scoring documents.|
|scripted_metric|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that uses scripts to provide a metric output.|
|serial_diff|object|false|none|An aggregation that subtracts values in a time series from themselves at different time lags or periods.|
|significant_terms|object|false|none|Returns interesting or unusual occurrences of terms in a set.|
|significant_text|object|false|none|Returns interesting or unusual occurrences of free-text terms in a set.|
|stats|object|false|none|A multi-value metrics aggregation that computes stats over numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|stats_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which calculates a variety of stats across all bucket of a specified metric in a sibling aggregation.|
|string_stats|object|false|none|A multi-value metrics aggregation that computes statistics over string values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|sum|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that sums numeric values that are extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|sum_bucket|object|false|none|A sibling pipeline aggregation which calculates the sum of a specified metric across all buckets in a sibling aggregation.|
|terms|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation where buckets are dynamically built - one per unique value.|
|time_series|object|false|none|The time series aggregation queries data created using a time series index.<br>This is typically data such as metrics or other data streams with a time component, and requires creating an index using the time series mode.|
|top_hits|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that returns the top matching documents per bucket.|
|t_test|object|false|none|A metrics aggregation that performs a statistical hypothesis test in which the test statistic follows a Student’s t-distribution under the null hypothesis on numeric values extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|top_metrics|object|false|none|A metric aggregation that selects metrics from the document with the largest or smallest sort value.|
|value_count|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that counts the number of values that are extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|weighted_avg|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that computes the weighted average of numeric values that are extracted from the aggregated documents.|
|variable_width_histogram|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation similar to the histogram, except instead of providing an interval to use as the width of each bucket, a target number of buckets is provided.|

An Elasticsearch Query DSL (Domain Specific Language) object that defines a query.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bool|object|false|none|matches documents matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|boosting|object|false|none|Returns documents matching a `positive` query while reducing the relevance score of documents that also match a `negative` query.|
|common|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|combined_fields|object|false|none|The `combined_fields` query supports searching multiple text fields as if their contents had been indexed into one combined field.|
|constant_score|object|false|none|Wraps a filter query and returns every matching document with a relevance score equal to the `boost` parameter value.|
|dis_max|object|false|none|Returns documents matching one or more wrapped queries, called query clauses or clauses.<br>If a returned document matches multiple query clauses, the `dis_max` query assigns the document the highest relevance score from any matching clause, plus a tie breaking increment for any additional matching subqueries.|
|distance_feature|object|false|none|Boosts the relevance score of documents closer to a provided origin date or point.<br>For example, you can use this query to give more weight to documents closer to a certain date or location.|
|exists|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain an indexed value for a field.|
|function_score|object|false|none|The `function_score` enables you to modify the score of documents that are retrieved by a query.|
|fuzzy|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms similar to the search term, as measured by a Levenshtein edit distance.|
|geo_bounding_box|object|false|none|Matches geo_point and geo_shape values that intersect a bounding box.|
|geo_distance|object|false|none|Matches `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values within a given distance of a geopoint.|
|geo_grid|object|false|none|Matches `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values that intersect a grid cell from a GeoGrid aggregation.|
|geo_polygon|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|geo_shape|object|false|none|Filter documents indexed using either the `geo_shape` or the `geo_point` type.|
|has_child|object|false|none|Returns parent documents whose joined child documents match a provided query.|
|has_parent|object|false|none|Returns child documents whose joined parent document matches a provided query.|
|ids|object|false|none|Returns documents based on their IDs.<br>This query uses document IDs stored in the `_id` field.|
|intervals|object|false|none|Returns documents based on the order and proximity of matching terms.|
|knn|object|false|none|Finds the k nearest vectors to a query vector, as measured by a similarity<br>metric. knn query finds nearest vectors through approximate search on indexed<br>dense_vectors.|
|kql|object|false|none|Returns documents matching a provided Kibana Query Language (KQL) expression.<br>The expression is parsed and rewritten into standard Query DSL.|
|match|object|false|none|Returns documents that match a provided text, number, date or boolean value.<br>The provided text is analyzed before matching.|
|match_all|object|false|none|Matches all documents, giving them all a `_score` of 1.0.|
|match_bool_prefix|object|false|none|Analyzes its input and constructs a `bool` query from the terms.<br>Each term except the last is used in a `term` query.<br>The last term is used in a prefix query.|
|match_none|object|false|none|Matches no documents.|
|match_phrase|object|false|none|Analyzes the text and creates a phrase query out of the analyzed text.|
|match_phrase_prefix|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain the words of a provided text, in the same order as provided.<br>The last term of the provided text is treated as a prefix, matching any words that begin with that term.|
|more_like_this|object|false|none|Returns documents that are "like" a given set of documents.|
|multi_match|object|false|none|Enables you to search for a provided text, number, date or boolean value across multiple fields.<br>The provided text is analyzed before matching.|
|nested|object|false|none|Wraps another query to search nested fields.<br>If an object matches the search, the nested query returns the root parent document.|
|parent_id|object|false|none|Returns child documents joined to a specific parent document.|
|percolate|object|false|none|Matches queries stored in an index.|
|pinned|object|false|none|Promotes selected documents to rank higher than those matching a given query.|
|prefix|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain a specific prefix in a provided field.|
|query_string|object|false|none|Returns documents based on a provided query string, using a parser with a strict syntax.|
|range|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms within a provided range.|
|rank_feature|object|false|none|Boosts the relevance score of documents based on the numeric value of a `rank_feature` or `rank_features` field.|
|regexp|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms matching a regular expression.|
|rule|object|false|none|none|
|script|object|false|none|Filters documents based on a provided script.<br>The script query is typically used in a filter context.|
|script_score|object|false|none|Uses a script to provide a custom score for returned documents.|
|semantic|object|false|none|A semantic query to semantic_text field types|
|shape|object|false|none|Queries documents that contain fields indexed using the `shape` type.|
|simple_query_string|object|false|none|Returns documents based on a provided query string, using a parser with a limited but fault-tolerant syntax.|
|span_containing|object|false|none|Returns matches which enclose another span query.|
|span_field_masking|object|false|none|Wrapper to allow span queries to participate in composite single-field span queries by _lying_ about their search field.|
|span_first|object|false|none|Matches spans near the beginning of a field.|
|span_multi|object|false|none|Allows you to wrap a multi term query (one of `wildcard`, `fuzzy`, `prefix`, `range`, or `regexp` query) as a `span` query, so it can be nested.|
|span_near|object|false|none|Matches spans which are near one another.<br>You can specify `slop`, the maximum number of intervening unmatched positions, as well as whether matches are required to be in-order.|
|span_not|object|false|none|Removes matches which overlap with another span query or which are within x tokens before (controlled by the parameter `pre`) or y tokens after (controlled by the parameter `post`) another span query.|
|span_or|object|false|none|Matches the union of its span clauses.|
|span_term|object|false|none|Matches spans containing a term.|
|span_within|object|false|none|Returns matches which are enclosed inside another span query.|
|sparse_vector|object|false|none|Using input query vectors or a natural language processing model to convert a query into a list of token-weight pairs, queries against a sparse vector field.|
|term|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain an exact term in a provided field.<br>To return a document, the query term must exactly match the queried field's value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|terms|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain one or more exact terms in a provided field.<br>To return a document, one or more terms must exactly match a field value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|terms_set|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain a minimum number of exact terms in a provided field.<br>To return a document, a required number of terms must exactly match the field values, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|text_expansion|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** Uses a natural language processing model to convert the query text into a list of token-weight pairs which are then used in a query against a sparse vector or rank features field.|
|weighted_tokens|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** Supports returning text_expansion query results by sending in precomputed tokens with the query.|
|wildcard|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms matching a wildcard pattern.|
|wrapper|object|false|none|A query that accepts any other query as base64 encoded string.|
|type|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|filter|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must appear in matching documents.<br>However, unlike `must`, the score of the query will be ignored.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Specifies the number or percentage of `should` clauses returned documents must match.|
|must|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must appear in matching documents and will contribute to the score.|
|must_not|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) must not appear in the matching documents.<br>Because scoring is ignored, a score of `0` is returned for all documents.|
|should|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|The clause (query) should appear in the matching document.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|negative_boost|number|true|none|Floating point number between 0 and 1.0 used to decrease the relevance scores of documents matching the `negative` query.|
|negative|object|true|none|Query used to decrease the relevance score of matching documents.|
|positive|object|true|none|Any returned documents must match this query.|
