### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|fields|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|true|none|List of fields to search. Field wildcard patterns are allowed. Only `text` fields are supported, and they must all have the same search `analyzer`.|
|query|string|true|none|Text to search for in the provided `fields`.<br>The `combined_fields` query analyzes the provided text before performing a search.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If true, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|operator|object|false|none|Boolean logic used to interpret text in the query value.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.|
|zero_terms_query|object|false|none|Indicates whether no documents are returned if the analyzer removes all tokens, such as when using a `stop` filter.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|filter|object|true|none|Filter query you wish to run. Any returned documents must match this query.<br>Filter queries do not calculate relevance scores.<br>To speed up performance, Elasticsearch automatically caches frequently used filter queries.|

|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|

|field|object|true|none|Name of the field used to calculate distances. ### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|boost_mode|object|false|none|Defines how he newly computed score is combined with the score of the query|
|functions|[[_types.query_dsl.FunctionScoreContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.functionscorecontainer)]|false|none|One or more functions that compute a new score for each document returned by the query.|
|max_boost|number|false|none|Restricts the new score to not exceed the provided limit.|
|min_score|number|false|none|Excludes documents that do not meet the provided score threshold.|
|query|object|false|none|A query that determines the documents for which a new score is computed.|
|score_mode|object|false|none|Specifies how the computed scores are combined|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|object|false|none|none|
|weight|number|false|none|none|
|_name|string|false|none|A name to identify which function matched and influenced the score.|
|exp|object|false|none|Function that scores a document with a exponential decay, depending on the distance of a numeric field value of the document from an origin.|
|gauss|object|false|none|Function that scores a document with a normal decay, depending on the distance of a numeric field value of the document from an origin.|
|linear|object|false|none|Function that scores a document with a linear decay, depending on the distance of a numeric field value of the document from an origin.|
|field_value_factor|object|false|none|Function allows you to use a field from a document to influence the score.<br>It’s similar to using the script_score function, however, it avoids the overhead of scripting.|
|random_score|object|false|none|Generates scores that are uniformly distributed from 0 up to but not including 1.<br>In case you want scores to be reproducible, it is possible to provide a `seed` and `field`.|
|script_score|object|false|none|Enables you to wrap another query and customize the scoring of it optionally with a computation derived from other numeric field values in the doc using a script expression.|

|prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged when creating expansions.|
|rewrite|object|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged when creating expansions.|
|transpositions|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether edits include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example `ab` to `ba`).|
|fuzziness|object|false|none|Maximum edit distance allowed for matching.|
|value|string \| number \| boolean|true|none|Term you wish to find in the provided field.|

<a id="tocs_types.query_dsl.geodistancequery"></a>

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "distance": {},
  "distance_type": "'arc'",
  "validation_method": "'strict'",
  "ignore_unmapped": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|distance|object|true|none|The radius of the circle centred on the specified location.<br>Points which fall into this circle are considered to be matches.|
|distance_type|object|false|none|How to compute the distance.<br>Set to `plane` for a faster calculation that's inaccurate on long distances and close to the poles.|
|validation_method|object|false|none|Set to `IGNORE_MALFORMED` to accept geo points with invalid latitude or longitude.<br>Set to `COERCE` to also try to infer correct latitude or longitude.|
|ignore_unmapped|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to ignore an unmapped field and not match any documents for this query.<br>Set to `false` to throw an exception if the field is not mapped.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|ignore_unmapped|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to ignore an unmapped `type` and not return any documents instead of an error.|
|inner_hits|object|false|none|If defined, each search hit will contain inner hits.|
|max_children|number|false|none|Maximum number of child documents that match the query allowed for a returned parent document.<br>If the parent document exceeds this limit, it is excluded from the search results.|
|min_children|number|false|none|Minimum number of child documents that match the query required to match the query for a returned parent document.<br>If the parent document does not meet this limit, it is excluded from the search results.|
|query|object|true|none|Query you wish to run on child documents of the `type` field.<br>If a child document matches the search, the query returns the parent document.|
|score_mode|object|false|none|Indicates how scores for matching child documents affect the root parent document’s relevance score.|
|type|object|true|none|Name of the child relationship mapped for the `join` field.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|false|none|none|
|boundary_chars|string|false|none|A string that contains each boundary character.|
|boundary_max_scan|number|false|none|How far to scan for boundary characters.|
|boundary_scanner|object|false|none|Specifies how to break the highlighted fragments: chars, sentence, or word.<br>Only valid for the unified and fvh highlighters.<br>Defaults to `sentence` for the `unified` highlighter. Defaults to `chars` for the `fvh` highlighter.|
|boundary_scanner_locale|string|false|none|Controls which locale is used to search for sentence and word boundaries.<br>This parameter takes a form of a language tag, for example: `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"`, `"ja-JP"`.|
|force_source|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|fragmenter|object|false|none|Specifies how text should be broken up in highlight snippets: `simple` or `span`.<br>Only valid for the `plain` highlighter.|
|fragment_size|number|false|none|The size of the highlighted fragment in characters.|
|highlight_filter|boolean|false|none|none|
|highlight_query|object|false|none|Highlight matches for a query other than the search query.<br>This is especially useful if you use a rescore query because those are not taken into account by highlighting by default.|
|max_fragment_length|number|false|none|none|
|max_analyzed_offset|number|false|none|If set to a non-negative value, highlighting stops at this defined maximum limit.<br>The rest of the text is not processed, thus not highlighted and no error is returned<br>The `max_analyzed_offset` query setting does not override the `index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset` setting, which prevails when it’s set to lower value than the query setting.|
|no_match_size|number|false|none|The amount of text you want to return from the beginning of the field if there are no matching fragments to highlight.|
|number_of_fragments|number|false|none|The maximum number of fragments to return.<br>If the number of fragments is set to `0`, no fragments are returned.<br>Instead, the entire field contents are highlighted and returned.<br>This can be handy when you need to highlight short texts such as a title or address, but fragmentation is not required.<br>If `number_of_fragments` is `0`, `fragment_size` is ignored.|
|options|object|false|none|none|
|order|object|false|none|Sorts highlighted fragments by score when set to `score`.<br>By default, fragments will be output in the order they appear in the field (order: `none`).<br>Setting this option to `score` will output the most relevant fragments first.<br>Each highlighter applies its own logic to compute relevancy scores.|
|phrase_limit|number|false|none|Controls the number of matching phrases in a document that are considered.<br>Prevents the `fvh` highlighter from analyzing too many phrases and consuming too much memory.<br>When using `matched_fields`, `phrase_limit` phrases per matched field are considered. Raising the limit increases query time and consumes more memory.<br>Only supported by the `fvh` highlighter.|
|post_tags|[string]|false|none|Use in conjunction with `pre_tags` to define the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|pre_tags|[string]|false|none|Use in conjunction with `post_tags` to define the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|require_field_match|boolean|false|none|By default, only fields that contains a query match are highlighted.<br>Set to `false` to highlight all fields.|
|tags_schema|object|false|none|Set to `styled` to use the built-in tag schema.|
|encoder|object|false|none|none|
|fields|object \| [object]|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|false|none|none|
|boundary_chars|string|false|none|A string that contains each boundary character.|
|boundary_max_scan|number|false|none|How far to scan for boundary characters.|
|boundary_scanner|object|false|none|Specifies how to break the highlighted fragments: chars, sentence, or word.<br>Only valid for the unified and fvh highlighters.<br>Defaults to `sentence` for the `unified` highlighter. Defaults to `chars` for the `fvh` highlighter.|
|boundary_scanner_locale|string|false|none|Controls which locale is used to search for sentence and word boundaries.<br>This parameter takes a form of a language tag, for example: `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"`, `"ja-JP"`.|
|force_source|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|fragmenter|object|false|none|Specifies how text should be broken up in highlight snippets: `simple` or `span`.<br>Only valid for the `plain` highlighter.|
|fragment_size|number|false|none|The size of the highlighted fragment in characters.|
|highlight_filter|boolean|false|none|none|
|highlight_query|object|false|none|Highlight matches for a query other than the search query.<br>This is especially useful if you use a rescore query because those are not taken into account by highlighting by default.|
|max_fragment_length|number|false|none|none|
|max_analyzed_offset|number|false|none|If set to a non-negative value, highlighting stops at this defined maximum limit.<br>The rest of the text is not processed, thus not highlighted and no error is returned<br>The `max_analyzed_offset` query setting does not override the `index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset` setting, which prevails when it’s set to lower value than the query setting.|
|no_match_size|number|false|none|The amount of text you want to return from the beginning of the field if there are no matching fragments to highlight.|
|number_of_fragments|number|false|none|The maximum number of fragments to return.<br>If the number of fragments is set to `0`, no fragments are returned.<br>Instead, the entire field contents are highlighted and returned.<br>This can be handy when you need to highlight short texts such as a title or address, but fragmentation is not required.<br>If `number_of_fragments` is `0`, `fragment_size` is ignored.|
|options|object|false|none|none|
|order|object|false|none|Sorts highlighted fragments by score when set to `score`.<br>By default, fragments will be output in the order they appear in the field (order: `none`).<br>Setting this option to `score` will output the most relevant fragments first.<br>Each highlighter applies its own logic to compute relevancy scores.|
|phrase_limit|number|false|none|Controls the number of matching phrases in a document that are considered.<br>Prevents the `fvh` highlighter from analyzing too many phrases and consuming too much memory.<br>When using `matched_fields`, `phrase_limit` phrases per matched field are considered. Raising the limit increases query time and consumes more memory.<br>Only supported by the `fvh` highlighter.|
|post_tags|[string]|false|none|Use in conjunction with `pre_tags` to define the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|pre_tags|[string]|false|none|Use in conjunction with `post_tags` to define the HTML tags to use for the highlighted text.<br>By default, highlighted text is wrapped in `<em>` and `</em>` tags.|
|require_field_match|boolean|false|none|By default, only fields that contains a query match are highlighted.<br>Set to `false` to highlight all fields.|
|tags_schema|object|false|none|Set to `styled` to use the built-in tag schema.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exclude_vectors|boolean|false|none|If `true`, vector fields are excluded from the returned source.<br><br>This option takes precedence over `includes`: any vector field will<br>remain excluded even if it matches an `includes` rule.|
|excludes|object|false|none|A list of fields to exclude from the returned source.|
|includes|object|false|none|A list of fields to include in the returned source.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|ignore_unmapped|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to ignore an unmapped `parent_type` and not return any documents instead of an error.<br>You can use this parameter to query multiple indices that may not contain the `parent_type`.|
|inner_hits|object|false|none|If defined, each search hit will contain inner hits.|
|parent_type|object|true|none|Name of the parent relationship mapped for the `join` field.|
|query|object|true|none|Query you wish to run on parent documents of the `parent_type` field.<br>If a parent document matches the search, the query returns its child documents.|
|score|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the relevance score of a matching parent document is aggregated into its child documents.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that follow an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|before|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that occur before an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|contained_by|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals contained by an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|containing|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that contain an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|not_contained_by|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that are **not** contained by an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|not_containing|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that do **not** contain an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|not_overlapping|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that do **not** overlap with an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|overlapping|object|false|none|Query used to return intervals that overlap with an interval from the `filter` rule.|
|script|object|false|none|Script used to return matching documents.<br>This script must return a boolean value: `true` or `false`.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|field|object|true|none|The name of the vector field to search against|
|query_vector|object|false|none|The query vector|
|query_vector_builder|object|false|none|The query vector builder. You must provide a query_vector_builder or query_vector, but not both.|
|num_candidates|number|false|none|The number of nearest neighbor candidates to consider per shard|
|visit_percentage|number|false|none|The percentage of vectors to explore per shard while doing knn search with bbq_disk|
|k|number|false|none|The final number of nearest neighbors to return as top hits|
|filter|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|Filters for the kNN search query|
|similarity|number|false|none|The minimum similarity for a vector to be considered a match|
|rescore_vector|object|false|none|Apply oversampling and rescoring to quantized vectors|

<h2 id="tocS__types.query_dsl.KqlQuery">_types.query_dsl.KqlQuery</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.query_dsl.kqlquery"></a>
<a id="schema__types.query_dsl.KqlQuery"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.query_dsl.kqlquery"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.query_dsl.kqlquery"></a>

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "case_insensitive": false,
  "default_field": {},
  "query": "string",
  "time_zone": {}
}
```

Returns documents matching a provided Kibana Query Language (KQL) expression.
The expression is parsed and rewritten into standard Query DSL.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|case_insensitive|boolean|false|none|If `true`, performs case-insensitive matching for field names and keyword or text terms.|
|default_field|object|false|none|Default field, or field pattern with wildcards, to target when a bare term does not specify a field.<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field` index setting, which has a default value of `*`.|
|query|string|true|none|The KQL expression to parse.|
|time_zone|object|false|none|Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) offset or IANA time zone used to interpret date literals in the expression.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.query_dsl.MatchQuery">_types.query_dsl.MatchQuery</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.query_dsl.matchquery"></a>
<a id="schema__types.query_dsl.MatchQuery"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.query_dsl.matchquery"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.query_dsl.matchquery"></a>

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "analyzer": "string",
  "auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query": true,
  "cutoff_frequency": 0,
  "fuzziness": {},
  "fuzzy_rewrite": {},
  "fuzzy_transpositions": true,
  "lenient": false,
  "max_expansions": 50,
  "minimum_should_match": {},
  "operator": "'or'",
  "prefix_length": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "zero_terms_query": "'none'"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert the text in the query value into tokens.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|cutoff_frequency|number|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|fuzziness|object|false|none|Maximum edit distance allowed for matching.|
|fuzzy_rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text query value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|max_expansions|number|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query will expand.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.|
|operator|object|false|none|Boolean logic used to interpret text in the query value.|
|prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|query|string \| number \| boolean|true|none|Text, number, boolean value or date you wish to find in the provided field.|
|zero_terms_query|object|false|none|Indicates whether no documents are returned if the `analyzer` removes all tokens, such as when using a `stop` filter.|

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "analyzer": "string",
  "fuzziness": {},
  "fuzzy_rewrite": {},
  "fuzzy_transpositions": true,
  "max_expansions": 50,
  "minimum_should_match": {},
  "operator": "'or'",
  "prefix_length": 0,
  "query": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert the text in the query value into tokens.|
|fuzziness|object|false|none|Maximum edit distance allowed for matching.<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|fuzzy_rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|max_expansions|number|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query will expand.<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.<br>Applied to the constructed bool query.|
|operator|object|false|none|Boolean logic used to interpret text in the query value.<br>Applied to the constructed bool query.|
|prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|query|string|true|none|Terms you wish to find in the provided field.<br>The last term is used in a prefix query.|

```json
  ],

  "like": "string",

  "max_word_length": 0,
  "min_doc_freq": 5,
  "minimum_should_match": {},
  "min_term_freq": 2,
  "min_word_length": 0,
  "routing": "string",
  "stop_words": {},
  "unlike": "string",
  "version": {},
  "version_type": "'internal'"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|The analyzer that is used to analyze the free form text.<br>Defaults to the analyzer associated with the first field in fields.|
|boost_terms|number|false|none|Each term in the formed query could be further boosted by their tf-idf score.<br>This sets the boost factor to use when using this feature.<br>Defaults to deactivated (0).|
|fail_on_unsupported_field|boolean|false|none|Controls whether the query should fail (throw an exception) if any of the specified fields are not of the supported types (`text` or `keyword`).|
|fields|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|false|none|A list of fields to fetch and analyze the text from.<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field` index setting, which has a default value of `*`.|
|include|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the input documents should also be included in the search results returned.|
|like|[_types.query_dsl.Like](#schema_types.query_dsl.like) \| [[_types.query_dsl.Like](#schema_types.query_dsl.like)]|true|none|Specifies free form text and/or a single or multiple documents for which you want to find similar documents.|
|max_doc_freq|number|false|none|The maximum document frequency above which the terms are ignored from the input document.|
|max_query_terms|number|false|none|The maximum number of query terms that can be selected.|
|max_word_length|number|false|none|The maximum word length above which the terms are ignored.<br>Defaults to unbounded (`0`).|
|min_doc_freq|number|false|none|The minimum document frequency below which the terms are ignored from the input document.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|After the disjunctive query has been formed, this parameter controls the number of terms that must match.|
|min_term_freq|number|false|none|The minimum term frequency below which the terms are ignored from the input document.|
|min_word_length|number|false|none|The minimum word length below which the terms are ignored.|
|routing|string|false|none|none|
|stop_words|object|false|none|An array of stop words.<br>Any word in this set is ignored.|
|unlike|[_types.query_dsl.Like](#schema_types.query_dsl.like) \| [[_types.query_dsl.Like](#schema_types.query_dsl.like)]|false|none|Used in combination with `like` to exclude documents that match a set of terms.|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|version_type|object|false|none|none|

Each language value corresponds to a predefined list of stop words in Lucene. See Stop words by language for supported language values and their stop words.
Also accepts an array of stop words.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert the text in the query value into tokens.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|cutoff_frequency|number|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|fields|object|false|none|The fields to be queried.<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field` index settings, which in turn defaults to `*`.|
|fuzziness|object|false|none|Maximum edit distance allowed for matching.|
|fuzzy_rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).<br>Can be applied to the term subqueries constructed for all terms but the final term.|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text query value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|max_expansions|number|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query will expand.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.|
|operator|object|false|none|Boolean logic used to interpret text in the query value.|
|prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|query|string|true|none|Text, number, boolean value or date you wish to find in the provided field.|
|slop|number|false|none|Maximum number of positions allowed between matching tokens.|
|tie_breaker|number|false|none|Determines how scores for each per-term blended query and scores across groups are combined.|
|type|object|false|none|How `the` multi_match query is executed internally.|
|zero_terms_query|object|false|none|Indicates whether no documents are returned if the `analyzer` removes all tokens, such as when using a `stop` filter.|

<a id="tocS_types.query_dsl.percolatequery"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.query_dsl.percolatequery"></a>

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "document": {},
  "documents": [
    {}
  ],
  "field": {},
  "id": {},
  "index": {},
  "name": "string",
  "preference": "string",
  "routing": "string",
  "version": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|document|object|false|none|The source of the document being percolated.|
|documents|[object]|false|none|An array of sources of the documents being percolated.|
|field|object|true|none|Field that holds the indexed queries. The field must use the `percolator` mapping type.|
|id|object|false|none|The ID of a stored document to percolate.|
|index|object|false|none|The index of a stored document to percolate.|
|name|string|false|none|The suffix used for the `_percolator_document_slot` field when multiple `percolate` queries are specified.|
|preference|string|false|none|Preference used to fetch document to percolate.|
|routing|string|false|none|Routing used to fetch document to percolate.|
|version|object|false|none|The expected version of a stored document to percolate.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|organic|object|true|none|Any choice of query used to rank documents which will be ranked below the "pinned" documents.|
|ids|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|none|Document IDs listed in the order they are to appear in results.<br>Required if `docs` is not specified.|
|docs|[[_types.query_dsl.PinnedDoc](#schema_types.query_dsl.pinneddoc)]|false|none|Documents listed in the order they are to appear in results.<br>Required if `ids` is not specified.|

```json
{
  "boost": 1,
  "_name": "string",
  "rewrite": {},
  "value": "string",
  "case_insensitive": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.|
|value|string|true|none|Beginning characters of terms you wish to find in the provided field.|
|case_insensitive|boolean|false|none|Allows case insensitive matching of the value with the indexed field values when set to `true`.<br>Default is `false` which means the case sensitivity of matching depends on the underlying field’s mapping.|

```json
{

    "string"
  ],
  "fuzziness": {},

  "fuzzy_prefix_length": 0,
  "fuzzy_rewrite": {},
  "fuzzy_transpositions": true,
  "lenient": false,
  "max_determinized_states": 10000,
  "minimum_should_match": {},
  "phrase_slop": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "quote_analyzer": "string",
  "quote_field_suffix": "string",
  "rewrite": {},
  "tie_breaker": 0,
  "time_zone": {},
  "type": "'best_fields'"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|allow_leading_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the wildcard characters `*` and `?` are allowed as the first character of the query string.|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert text in the query string into tokens.|
|analyze_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.|
|default_field|object|false|none|Default field to search if no field is provided in the query string.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field` index setting, which has a default value of `*`.|
|default_operator|object|false|none|Default boolean logic used to interpret text in the query string if no operators are specified.|
|enable_position_increments|boolean|false|none|If `true`, enable position increments in queries constructed from a `query_string` search.|
|escape|boolean|false|none|none|
|fields|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|false|none|Array of fields to search. Supports wildcards (`*`).|
|fuzziness|object|false|none|Maximum edit distance allowed for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_max_expansions|number|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query expands for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|max_determinized_states|number|false|none|Maximum number of automaton states required for the query.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.|
|phrase_slop|number|false|none|Maximum number of positions allowed between matching tokens for phrases.|
|query|string|true|none|Query string you wish to parse and use for search.|
|quote_analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert quoted text in the query string into tokens.<br>For quoted text, this parameter overrides the analyzer specified in the `analyzer` parameter.|
|quote_field_suffix|string|false|none|Suffix appended to quoted text in the query string.<br>You can use this suffix to use a different analysis method for exact matches.|
|rewrite|object|false|none|Method used to rewrite the query.|
|tie_breaker|number|false|none|How to combine the queries generated from the individual search terms in the resulting `dis_max` query.|
|time_zone|object|false|none|Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) offset or IANA time zone used to convert date values in the query string to UTC.|
|type|object|false|none|Determines how the query matches and scores documents.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|organic|object|true|none|none|
|ruleset_ids|[_types.Id](#schema_types.id) \| [[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|none|none|
|ruleset_id|string|false|none|none|
|match_criteria|object|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Analyzer used to convert text in the query string into tokens.|
|analyze_wildcard|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string.|
|auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the parser creates a match_phrase query for each multi-position token.|
|default_operator|object|false|none|Default boolean logic used to interpret text in the query string if no operators are specified.|
|fields|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|false|none|Array of fields you wish to search.<br>Accepts wildcard expressions.<br>You also can boost relevance scores for matches to particular fields using a caret (`^`) notation.<br>Defaults to the `index.query.default_field index` setting, which has a default value of `*`.|
|flags|object|false|none|List of enabled operators for the simple query string syntax.|
|fuzzy_max_expansions|number|false|none|Maximum number of terms to which the query expands for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_prefix_length|number|false|none|Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.|
|fuzzy_transpositions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text value for a numeric field, are ignored.|
|minimum_should_match|object|false|none|Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.|
|query|string|true|none|Query string in the simple query string syntax you wish to parse and use for search.|
|quote_field_suffix|string|false|none|Suffix appended to quoted text in the query string.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|span_containing|object|false|none|Accepts a list of span queries, but only returns those spans which also match a second span query.|
|span_field_masking|object|false|none|Allows queries like `span_near` or `span_or` across different fields.|
|span_first|object|false|none|Accepts another span query whose matches must appear within the first N positions of the field.|
|span_gap|object|false|none|none|
|span_multi|object|false|none|Wraps a `term`, `range`, `prefix`, `wildcard`, `regexp`, or `fuzzy` query.|
|span_near|object|false|none|Accepts multiple span queries whose matches must be within the specified distance of each other, and possibly in the same order.|
|span_not|object|false|none|Wraps another span query, and excludes any documents which match that query.|
|span_or|object|false|none|Combines multiple span queries and returns documents which match any of the specified queries.|
|span_term|object|false|none|The equivalent of the `term` query but for use with other span queries.|
|span_within|object|false|none|The result from a single span query is returned as long is its span falls within the spans returned by a list of other span queries.|

```json
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "inference_id": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boost|number|false|none|Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.<br>Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.<br>A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.<br>A value greater than 1.0 increases the relevance score.|
|_name|string|false|none|none|
|field|object|true|none|The name of the field that contains the token-weight pairs to be searched against.<br>This field must be a mapped sparse_vector field.|
|query|string|false|none|The query text you want to use for search.<br>If inference_id is specified, query must also be specified.|
|prune|boolean|false|none|Whether to perform pruning, omitting the non-significant tokens from the query to improve query performance.<br>If prune is true but the pruning_config is not specified, pruning will occur but default values will be used.<br>Default: false|
|pruning_config|object|false|none|Optional pruning configuration.<br>If enabled, this will omit non-significant tokens from the query in order to improve query performance.<br>This is only used if prune is set to true.<br>If prune is set to true but pruning_config is not specified, default values will be used.|
|query_vector|object|false|none|Dictionary of precomputed sparse vectors and their associated weights.<br>Only one of inference_id or query_vector may be supplied in a request.|
|inference_id|object|false|none|The inference ID to use to convert the query text into token-weight pairs.<br>It must be the same inference ID that was used to create the tokens from the input text.<br>Only one of inference_id and query_vector is allowed.<br>If inference_id is specified, query must also be specified.<br>Only one of inference_id or query_vector may be supplied in a request.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.BucketKsAggregation">_types.aggregations.BucketKsAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.bucketksaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.BucketKsAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.bucketksaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.bucketksaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "buckets_path": {},
  "alternative": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fractions": [
    0
  ],
  "sampling_method": "string"
}
```

A sibling pipeline aggregation which executes a two sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test (referred
to as a "K-S test" from now on) against a provided distribution, and the distribution implied
by the documents counts in the configured sibling aggregation. Specifically, for some metric,
assuming that the percentile intervals of the metric are known beforehand or have been computed
by an aggregation, then one would use range aggregation for the sibling to compute the p-value
of the distribution difference between the metric and the restriction of that metric to a subset
of the documents. A natural use case is if the sibling aggregation range aggregation nested in a
terms aggregation, in which case one compares the overall distribution of metric to its restriction
to each term.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buckets_path|object|false|none|Path to the buckets that contain one set of values to correlate.|
|alternative|[string]|false|none|A list of string values indicating which K-S test alternative to calculate. The valid values<br>are: "greater", "less", "two_sided". This parameter is key for determining the K-S statistic used<br>when calculating the K-S test. Default value is all possible alternative hypotheses.|
|fractions|[number]|false|none|A list of doubles indicating the distribution of the samples with which to compare to the `buckets_path` results.<br>In typical usage this is the overall proportion of documents in each bucket, which is compared with the actual<br>document proportions in each bucket from the sibling aggregation counts. The default is to assume that overall<br>documents are uniformly distributed on these buckets, which they would be if one used equal percentiles of a<br>metric to define the bucket end points.|
|sampling_method|string|false|none|Indicates the sampling methodology when calculating the K-S test. Note, this is sampling of the returned values.<br>This determines the cumulative distribution function (CDF) points used comparing the two samples. Default is<br>`upper_tail`, which emphasizes the upper end of the CDF points. Valid options are: `upper_tail`, `uniform`,<br>and `lower_tail`.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.CategorizeTextAggregation">_types.aggregations.CategorizeTextAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.categorizetextaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.CategorizeTextAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.categorizetextaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.categorizetextaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "field": {},
  "max_unique_tokens": 50,
  "max_matched_tokens": 5,
  "similarity_threshold": 50,
  "categorization_filters": [
    "string"
  ],
  "categorization_analyzer": {},
  "shard_size": 0,
  "size": 10,
  "min_doc_count": 0,
  "shard_min_doc_count": 0
}
```

A multi-bucket aggregation that groups semi-structured text into buckets. Each text
field is re-analyzed using a custom analyzer. The resulting tokens are then categorized
creating buckets of similarly formatted text values. This aggregation works best with machine
generated text like system logs. Only the first 100 analyzed tokens are used to categorize the text.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|object|true|none|The semi-structured text field to categorize.|
|max_unique_tokens|number|false|none|The maximum number of unique tokens at any position up to max_matched_tokens. Must be larger than 1.<br>Smaller values use less memory and create fewer categories. Larger values will use more memory and<br>create narrower categories. Max allowed value is 100.|
|max_matched_tokens|number|false|none|The maximum number of token positions to match on before attempting to merge categories. Larger<br>values will use more memory and create narrower categories. Max allowed value is 100.|
|similarity_threshold|number|false|none|The minimum percentage of tokens that must match for text to be added to the category bucket. Must<br>be between 1 and 100. The larger the value the narrower the categories. Larger values will increase memory<br>usage and create narrower categories.|
|categorization_filters|[string]|false|none|This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching<br>sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization<br>by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL<br>statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as categorization_analyzer.<br>If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting<br>this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering,<br>use the categorization_analyzer property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters.|
|categorization_analyzer|object|false|none|The categorization analyzer specifies how the text is analyzed and tokenized before being categorized.<br>The syntax is very similar to that used to define the analyzer in the analyze API. This property<br>cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_filters`.|
|shard_size|number|false|none|The number of categorization buckets to return from each shard before merging all the results.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of buckets to return.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|The minimum number of documents in a bucket to be returned to the results.|
|shard_min_doc_count|number|false|none|The minimum number of documents in a bucket to be returned from the shard before merging.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|calendar_interval|object|false|none|Calendar-aware interval.<br>Can be specified using the unit name, such as `month`, or as a single unit quantity, such as `1M`.|
|extended_bounds|object|false|none|Enables extending the bounds of the histogram beyond the data itself.|
|hard_bounds|object|false|none|Limits the histogram to specified bounds.|
|field|object|false|none|The date field whose values are use to build a histogram.|
|fixed_interval|object|false|none|Fixed intervals: a fixed number of SI units and never deviate, regardless of where they fall on the calendar.|
|format|string|false|none|The date format used to format `key_as_string` in the response.<br>If no `format` is specified, the first date format specified in the field mapping is used.|
|interval|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Only returns buckets that have `min_doc_count` number of documents.<br>By default, all buckets between the first bucket that matches documents and the last one are returned.|
|missing|object|false|none|The value to apply to documents that do not have a value.<br>By default, documents without a value are ignored.|
|offset|object|false|none|Changes the start value of each bucket by the specified positive (`+`) or negative offset (`-`) duration.|
|order|object|false|none|The sort order of the returned buckets.|
|params|object|false|none|none|
|script|object|false|none|none|
|time_zone|object|false|none|Time zone used for bucketing and rounding.<br>Defaults to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|keyed|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to associate a unique string key with each bucket and return the ranges as a hash rather than an array.|

Aggregation buckets. By default they are returned as an array, but if the aggregation has keys configured for
the different buckets, the result is a dictionary.

|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|**additionalProperties**|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)|false|none|An Elasticsearch Query DSL (Domain Specific Language) object that defines a query.|
|*oneOf*|[[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.GeoHashGridAggregation">_types.aggregations.GeoHashGridAggregation</h2>

<a id="schema__types.aggregations.GeoHashGridAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.geohashgridaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.geohashgridaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "bounds": {
    "top": 0,
    "bottom": 0,
    "left": 0,
    "right": 0
  },
  "field": {},
  "precision": "5",
  "shard_size": 0,
  "size": 10000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bounds|object|false|none|The bounding box to filter the points in each bucket.|
|field|object|false|none|Field containing indexed `geo_point` or `geo_shape` values.<br>If the field contains an array, `geohash_grid` aggregates all array values.|
|precision|object|false|none|The string length of the geohashes used to define cells/buckets in the results.|
|shard_size|number|false|none|Allows for more accurate counting of the top cells returned in the final result the aggregation.<br>Defaults to returning `max(10,(size x number-of-shards))` buckets from each shard.|
|size|number|false|none|The maximum number of geohash buckets to return.|

```json
  "extended_bounds": {

  },

  },

  "interval": 0,

  "missing": 0,
  "offset": 0,

    "property1": "asc",
    "property2": "asc"
  },

    "source": {},

      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },

    }

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|extended_bounds|object|false|none|Enables extending the bounds of the histogram beyond the data itself.|
|hard_bounds|object|false|none|Limits the range of buckets in the histogram.<br>It is particularly useful in the case of open data ranges that can result in a very large number of buckets.|
|field|object|false|none|The name of the field to aggregate on.|
|interval|number|false|none|The interval for the buckets.<br>Must be a positive decimal.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Only returns buckets that have `min_doc_count` number of documents.<br>By default, the response will fill gaps in the histogram with empty buckets.|
|missing|number|false|none|The value to apply to documents that do not have a value.<br>By default, documents without a value are ignored.|
|offset|number|false|none|By default, the bucket keys start with 0 and then continue in even spaced steps of `interval`.<br>The bucket boundaries can be shifted by using the `offset` option.|
|order|object|false|none|The sort order of the returned buckets.<br>By default, the returned buckets are sorted by their key ascending.|
|script|object|false|none|none|
|format|string|false|none|none|
|keyed|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns buckets as a hash instead of an array, keyed by the bucket keys.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collect_mode|object|false|none|Specifies the strategy for data collection.|

|show_term_doc_count_error|boolean|false|none|Calculates the doc count error on per term basis.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of term buckets should be returned out of the overall terms list.|
|terms|[[_types.aggregations.MultiTermLookup](#schema_types.aggregations.multitermlookup)]|true|none|The field from which to generate sets of terms.|

<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.rateaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "format": "string",
  "unit": {},
  "mode": "sum"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|string|false|none|none|
|unit|object|false|none|The interval used to calculate the rate.<br>By default, the interval of the `date_histogram` is used.|
|mode|object|false|none|How the rate is calculated.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.RandomSamplerAggregation">_types.aggregations.RandomSamplerAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.randomsampleraggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.RandomSamplerAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.randomsampleraggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.randomsampleraggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "probability": 0,
  "seed": 0,
  "shard_seed": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|probability|number|true|none|The probability that a document will be included in the aggregated data.<br>Must be greater than 0, less than 0.5, or exactly 1.<br>The lower the probability, the fewer documents are matched.|
|seed|number|false|none|The seed to generate the random sampling of documents.<br>When a seed is provided, the random subset of documents is the same between calls.|
|shard_seed|number|false|none|When combined with seed, setting shard_seed ensures 100% consistent sampling over shards where data is exactly the same.|

```json
{

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|shard_size|number|false|none|Limits how many top-scoring documents are collected in the sample processed on each shard.|

<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.scriptedmetricaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "field": {},
  "missing": {},
  "script": {},
  "combine_script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "init_script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "map_script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "params": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "reduce_script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|object|false|none|The field on which to run the aggregation.|
|missing|object|false|none|The value to apply to documents that do not have a value.<br>By default, documents without a value are ignored.|
|script|object|false|none|none|
|combine_script|object|false|none|Runs once on each shard after document collection is complete.<br>Allows the aggregation to consolidate the state returned from each shard.|
|init_script|object|false|none|Runs prior to any collection of documents.<br>Allows the aggregation to set up any initial state.|
|map_script|object|false|none|Run once per document collected.<br>If no `combine_script` is specified, the resulting state needs to be stored in the `state` object.|
|params|object|false|none|A global object with script parameters for `init`, `map` and `combine` scripts.<br>It is shared between the scripts.|
|reduce_script|object|false|none|Runs once on the coordinating node after all shards have returned their results.<br>The script is provided with access to a variable `states`, which is an array of the result of the `combine_script` on each shard.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.SerialDifferencingAggregation">_types.aggregations.SerialDifferencingAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.serialdifferencingaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.SerialDifferencingAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.serialdifferencingaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.serialdifferencingaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "buckets_path": {},
  "format": "string",
  "gap_policy": "skip",
  "lag": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buckets_path|object|false|none|Path to the buckets that contain one set of values to correlate.|
|format|string|false|none|`DecimalFormat` pattern for the output value.<br>If specified, the formatted value is returned in the aggregation’s `value_as_string` property.|
|gap_policy|object|false|none|Policy to apply when gaps are found in the data.|
|lag|number|false|none|The historical bucket to subtract from the current value.<br>Must be a positive, non-zero integer.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|background_filter|object|false|none|A background filter that can be used to focus in on significant terms within a narrower context, instead of the entire index.|
|chi_square|object|false|none|Use Chi square, as described in "Information Retrieval", Manning et al., Chapter 13.5.2, as the significance score.|
|exclude|object|false|none|Terms to exclude.|
|execution_hint|object|false|none|Mechanism by which the aggregation should be executed: using field values directly or using global ordinals.|
|field|object|false|none|The field from which to return significant terms.|
|gnd|object|false|none|Use Google normalized distance as described in "The Google Similarity Distance", Cilibrasi and Vitanyi, 2007, as the significance score.|
|include|object|false|none|Terms to include.|
|jlh|object|false|none|Use JLH score as the significance score.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Only return terms that are found in more than `min_doc_count` hits.|
|mutual_information|object|false|none|Use mutual information as described in "Information Retrieval", Manning et al., Chapter 13.5.1, as the significance score.|
|percentage|object|false|none|A simple calculation of the number of documents in the foreground sample with a term divided by the number of documents in the background with the term.|
|script_heuristic|object|false|none|Customized score, implemented via a script.|
|p_value|object|false|none|Significant terms heuristic that calculates the p-value between the term existing in foreground and background sets.<br><br>The p-value is the probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as<br>the results actually observed, under the assumption that the null hypothesis is<br>correct. The p-value is calculated assuming that the foreground set and the<br>background set are independent https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernoulli_trial, with the null<br>hypothesis that the probabilities are the same.|
|shard_min_doc_count|number|false|none|Regulates the certainty a shard has if the term should actually be added to the candidate list or not with respect to the `min_doc_count`.<br>Terms will only be considered if their local shard frequency within the set is higher than the `shard_min_doc_count`.|
|shard_size|number|false|none|Can be used to control the volumes of candidate terms produced by each shard.<br>By default, `shard_size` will be automatically estimated based on the number of shards and the `size` parameter.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of buckets returned out of the overall terms list.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|background_filter|object|false|none|A background filter that can be used to focus in on significant terms within a narrower context, instead of the entire index.|
|chi_square|object|false|none|Use Chi square, as described in "Information Retrieval", Manning et al., Chapter 13.5.2, as the significance score.|
|exclude|object|false|none|Values to exclude.|
|execution_hint|object|false|none|Determines whether the aggregation will use field values directly or global ordinals.|
|field|object|false|none|The field from which to return significant text.|
|filter_duplicate_text|boolean|false|none|Whether to out duplicate text to deal with noisy data.|
|gnd|object|false|none|Use Google normalized distance as described in "The Google Similarity Distance", Cilibrasi and Vitanyi, 2007, as the significance score.|
|include|object|false|none|Values to include.|
|jlh|object|false|none|Use JLH score as the significance score.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Only return values that are found in more than `min_doc_count` hits.|
|mutual_information|object|false|none|Use mutual information as described in "Information Retrieval", Manning et al., Chapter 13.5.1, as the significance score.|
|percentage|object|false|none|A simple calculation of the number of documents in the foreground sample with a term divided by the number of documents in the background with the term.|
|script_heuristic|object|false|none|Customized score, implemented via a script.|
|shard_min_doc_count|number|false|none|Regulates the certainty a shard has if the values should actually be added to the candidate list or not with respect to the min_doc_count.<br>Values will only be considered if their local shard frequency within the set is higher than the `shard_min_doc_count`.|
|shard_size|number|false|none|The number of candidate terms produced by each shard.<br>By default, `shard_size` will be automatically estimated based on the number of shards and the `size` parameter.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of buckets returned out of the overall terms list.|
|source_fields|object|false|none|Overrides the JSON `_source` fields from which text will be analyzed.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.TermsAggregation">_types.aggregations.TermsAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.termsaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.TermsAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.termsaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.termsaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "collect_mode": {},
  "exclude": {},
  "execution_hint": {},
  "field": {},
  "include": {},
  "min_doc_count": 1,
  "missing": {},
  "missing_order": {},
  "missing_bucket": true,
  "value_type": "string",
  "order": {
    "property1": "asc",
    "property2": "asc"
  },
  "script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "shard_min_doc_count": 0,
  "shard_size": 0,
  "show_term_doc_count_error": true,
  "size": 10,
  "format": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collect_mode|object|false|none|Determines how child aggregations should be calculated: breadth-first or depth-first.|
|exclude|object|false|none|Values to exclude.<br>Accepts regular expressions and partitions.|
|execution_hint|object|false|none|Determines whether the aggregation will use field values directly or global ordinals.|
|field|object|false|none|The field from which to return terms.|
|include|object|false|none|Values to include.<br>Accepts regular expressions and partitions.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Only return values that are found in more than `min_doc_count` hits.|
|missing|object|false|none|The value to apply to documents that do not have a value.<br>By default, documents without a value are ignored.|
|missing_order|object|false|none|none|
|missing_bucket|boolean|false|none|none|
|value_type|string|false|none|Coerced unmapped fields into the specified type.|
|order|object|false|none|Specifies the sort order of the buckets.<br>Defaults to sorting by descending document count.|
|script|object|false|none|none|
|shard_min_doc_count|number|false|none|Regulates the certainty a shard has if the term should actually be added to the candidate list or not with respect to the `min_doc_count`.<br>Terms will only be considered if their local shard frequency within the set is higher than the `shard_min_doc_count`.|
|shard_size|number|false|none|The number of candidate terms produced by each shard.<br>By default, `shard_size` will be automatically estimated based on the number of shards and the `size` parameter.|
|show_term_doc_count_error|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to return the `doc_count_error_upper_bound`, which is an upper bound to the error on the `doc_count` returned by each shard.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of buckets returned out of the overall terms list.|
|format|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS__types.aggregations.TopHitsAggregation">_types.aggregations.TopHitsAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.aggregations.tophitsaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema__types.aggregations.TopHitsAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.aggregations.tophitsaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.aggregations.tophitsaggregation"></a>

```json
{
  "field": {},
  "missing": {},
  "script": {},
  "docvalue_fields": [
    {
      "field": {},
      "format": "string",
      "include_unmapped": true
    }
  ],
  "explain": false,
  "fields": [
    {
      "field": {},
      "format": "string",
      "include_unmapped": true
    }
  ],
  "from": 0,
  "highlight": {
    "encoder": {},
    "fields": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    }
  },
  "script_fields": {
    "property1": {
      "script": {},
      "ignore_failure": true
    },
    "property2": {
      "script": {},
      "ignore_failure": true
    }
  },
  "size": 3,
  "sort": {},
  "_source": {},
  "stored_fields": {},
  "track_scores": false,
  "version": false,
  "seq_no_primary_term": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|object|false|none|The field on which to run the aggregation.|
|missing|object|false|none|The value to apply to documents that do not have a value.<br>By default, documents without a value are ignored.|
|script|object|false|none|none|
|docvalue_fields|[[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|none|Fields for which to return doc values.|
|explain|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.|
|fields|[[_types.query_dsl.FieldAndFormat](#schema_types.query_dsl.fieldandformat)]|false|none|Array of wildcard (*) patterns. The request returns values for field names<br>matching these patterns in the hits.fields property of the response.|
|from|number|false|none|Starting document offset.|
|highlight|object|false|none|Specifies the highlighter to use for retrieving highlighted snippets from one or more fields in the search results.|
|script_fields|object|false|none|Returns the result of one or more script evaluations for each hit.|
|size|number|false|none|The maximum number of top matching hits to return per bucket.|
|sort|object|false|none|Sort order of the top matching hits.<br>By default, the hits are sorted by the score of the main query.|
|_source|object|false|none|Selects the fields of the source that are returned.|
|stored_fields|object|false|none|Returns values for the specified stored fields (fields that use the `store` mapping option).|
|track_scores|boolean|false|none|If `true`, calculates and returns document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.|
|version|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns document version as part of a hit.|
|seq_no_primary_term|boolean|false|none|If `true`, returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.|

Number of hits matching the query to count accurately. If true, the exact
number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. If false, the
response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.
Defaults to 10,000 hits.

|boost|number|false|none|Boost value to apply to kNN scores|
|filter|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|Filters for the kNN search query|
|similarity|number|false|none|The minimum similarity for a vector to be considered a match|
|inner_hits|object|false|none|If defined, each search hit will contain inner hits.|
|rescore_vector|object|false|none|Apply oversampling and rescoring to quantized vectors|
|_name|string|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|standard|object|false|none|A retriever that replaces the functionality of a traditional query.|
|knn|object|false|none|A retriever that replaces the functionality  of a knn search.|
|rrf|object|false|none|A retriever that produces top documents from reciprocal rank fusion (RRF).|
|text_similarity_reranker|object|false|none|A retriever that reranks the top documents based on a reranking model using the InferenceAPI|
|rule|object|false|none|A retriever that replaces the functionality of a rule query.|
|rescorer|object|false|none|A retriever that re-scores only the results produced by its child retriever.|
|linear|object|false|none|A retriever that supports the combination of different retrievers through a weighted linear combination.|
|pinned|object|false|none|A pinned retriever applies pinned documents to the underlying retriever.<br>This retriever will rewrite to a PinnedQueryBuilder.|
|diversify|object|false|none|A retriever that diversifies the results from its child retriever.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer) \| [[_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer](#schema_types.query_dsl.querycontainer)]|false|none|Query to filter the documents that can match.|
|min_score|number|false|none|Minimum _score for matching documents. Documents with a lower _score are not included in the top documents.|
|_name|string|false|none|Retriever name.|
|query|object|false|none|Defines a query to retrieve a set of top documents.|
|search_after|object|false|none|Defines a search after object parameter used for pagination.|
|terminate_after|number|false|none|Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.|
|sort|object|false|none|A sort object that that specifies the order of matching documents.|
|collapse|object|false|none|Collapses the top documents by a specified key into a single top document per key.|

|query_vector_builder|object|false|none|Defines a model to build a query vector.|
|k|number|true|none|Number of nearest neighbors to return as top hits.|
|num_candidates|number|false|none|Number of nearest neighbor candidates to consider per shard.|
|visit_percentage|number|false|none|The percentage of vectors to explore per shard while doing knn search with bbq_disk|
|similarity|number|false|none|The minimum similarity required for a document to be considered a match.|
|rescore_vector|object|false|none|Apply oversampling and rescoring to quantized vectors|

<h2 id="tocS__types.mapping.ChunkRescorerChunkingSettings">_types.mapping.ChunkRescorerChunkingSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.mapping.chunkrescorerchunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="schema__types.mapping.ChunkRescorerChunkingSettings"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.mapping.chunkrescorerchunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.mapping.chunkrescorerchunkingsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "max_chunk_size": 250,
  "overlap": 100,
  "sentence_overlap": 1,
  "separator_group": "string",
  "separators": [
    "string"
  ],
  "strategy": "sentence"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_chunk_size|number|true|none|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|sentence_overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|separator_group|string|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|separators|[string]|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|strategy|string|false|none|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|false|none|none|
|is_partial|boolean|true|none|When the query is no longer running, this property indicates whether the search failed or was successfully completed on all shards.<br>While the query is running, `is_partial` is always set to `true`.|

|start_time|object|false|none|none|
|start_time_in_millis|object|true|none|none|
|completion_time|object|false|none|Indicates when the async search completed.<br>It is present only when the search has completed.|
|completion_time_in_millis|object|false|none|none|
|error|object|false|none|none|
|_shards|object|true|none|The number of shards that have run the query so far.|
|_clusters|object|false|none|Metadata about clusters involved in the cross-cluster search.<br>It is not shown for local-only searches.|

```json
{
  "index": {
    "_id": {},
    "_index": {},
    "routing": "string",
    "if_primary_term": 0,
    "if_seq_no": {},
    "version": {},
    "version_type": {},
    "dynamic_templates": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },

    "require_alias": false
  },
  "create": {

    "routing": "string",
    "if_primary_term": 0,
    "if_seq_no": {},
    "version": {},
    "version_type": {},
    "dynamic_templates": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "pipeline": "string",
    "require_alias": false
  },
```
