```json
    "_id": {},
    "_index": {},
    "routing": "string",
    "if_primary_term": 0,
    "if_seq_no": {},
    "version": {},
    "version_type": {},
    "require_alias": false,
    "retry_on_conflict": 0
  },
  "delete": {
    "_id": {},
    "_index": {},
    "routing": "string",
    "if_primary_term": 0,
    "if_seq_no": {},
    "version": {},
    "version_type": {}
  }
}
```

An action line, which is the first line of each operation in a bulk request.
It specifies the action to perform (`index`, `create`, `update`, or `delete`) and its metadata, such as the target index and document ID.
All actions except `delete` expect a source line to follow.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|object|false|none|Index the specified document.<br>If the document exists, it replaces the document and increments the version.<br>The following line must contain the source data to be indexed.|
|create|object|false|none|Index the specified document if it does not already exist.<br>The following line must contain the source data to be indexed.|
|update|object|false|none|Perform a partial document update.<br>The following line must contain the partial document and update options.|
|delete|object|false|none|Remove the specified document from the index.|

```json
{
  "detect_noop": true,
  "doc": {},
  "doc_as_upsert": false,
  "script": {
    "source": {},
    "id": {},
    "params": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "lang": "painless",
    "options": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "scripted_upsert": false,
  "_source": "true",
  "upsert": {}
}
```

The source line that must follow an `update` action line.
It specifies the partial document, script, or upsert options to apply, plus optional update settings.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|detect_noop|boolean|false|none|If true, the `result` in the response is set to 'noop' when no changes to the document occur.|
|doc|object|false|none|A partial update to an existing document.|
|doc_as_upsert|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to use the contents of `doc` as the value of `upsert`.|
|script|object|false|none|The script to run to update the document.|
|scripted_upsert|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to run the script whether or not the document exists.|
|_source|object|false|none|If `false`, source retrieval is turned off.<br>You can also specify a comma-separated list of the fields you want to retrieve.|
|upsert|object|false|none|If the document does not already exist, the contents of `upsert` are inserted as a new document.<br>If the document exists, the `script` is run.|

|updated|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully updated, for example, a document with same ID already existed prior to reindex updating it.|

```json
  "failures": [

        ]

      "status": 0
    }
  ],
  "noops": 0,

  "retries": {
    "bulk": 0,
    "search": 0
  },
  "throttled_millis": {},
  "throttled_until_millis": {},

  "updated": 0,
  "version_conflicts": 0
```

The final result of a completed reindex operation, as stored in the task result.
This is the serialized form of `BulkByScrollResponse`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batches|number|false|none|The number of scroll responses pulled back by the reindex.|
|created|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully created.|
|deleted|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully deleted.|
|failures|[[_types.BulkIndexByScrollFailure](#schema_types.bulkindexbyscrollfailure)]|false|none|Any failures encountered during the reindex. If non-empty, the reindex ended because of these failures.|
|noops|number|false|none|The number of documents that were ignored because the script returned a `noop` value for `ctx.op`.|
|requests_per_second|number|false|none|The number of requests per second effectively executed during the reindex.|
|retries|object|false|none|The number of retries attempted by reindex.|
|throttled_millis|object|false|none|Number of milliseconds the request slept to conform to `requests_per_second`.|
|throttled_until_millis|object|false|none|This field should always be equal to zero in a completed reindex result.|
|timed_out|boolean|false|none|Whether any of the requests executed during the reindex timed out.|
|took|object|false|none|The total milliseconds the entire operation took.|
|total|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully processed.|
|updated|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully updated.|
|version_conflicts|number|false|none|The number of version conflicts that occurred.|

|disk.indices.forecast|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize) \| string \| null|false|none|Sum of shard size forecasts|
|disk.indices|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize) \| string \| null|false|none|Disk space used by the node’s shards. Does not include disk space for the translog or unassigned shards.<br>IMPORTANT: This metric double-counts disk space for hard-linked files, such as those created when shrinking, splitting, or cloning an index.|
|disk.used|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize) \| string \| null|false|none|Total disk space in use.<br>Elasticsearch retrieves this metric from the node’s operating system (OS).<br>The metric includes disk space for: Elasticsearch, including the translog and unassigned shards; the node’s operating system; any other applications or files on the node.<br>Unlike `disk.indices`, this metric does not double-count disk space for hard-linked files.|
|disk.avail|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize) \| string \| null|false|none|Free disk space available to Elasticsearch.<br>Elasticsearch retrieves this metric from the node’s operating system.<br>Disk-based shard allocation uses this metric to assign shards to nodes based on available disk space.|
|disk.total|[_types.ByteSize](#schema_types.bytesize) \| string \| null|false|none|Total disk space for the node, including in-use and available space.|
|disk.percent|[_types.Percentage](#schema_types.percentage) \| string \| null|false|none|Total percentage of disk space in use. Calculated as `disk.used / disk.total`.|
|host|[_types.Host](#schema_types.host) \| string \| null|false|none|Network host for the node. Set using the `network.host` setting.|
|ip|[_types.Ip](#schema_types.ip) \| string \| null|false|none|IP address and port for the node.|
|node|string|false|none|Name for the node. Set using the `node.name` setting.|
|node.role|string \| string \| null|false|none|Node roles|

Depending on the target language, code generators can keep the union or remove it and leniently parse
strings to the target type.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[_types.EpochTimeUnitSeconds](#schema_types.epochtimeunitseconds)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The datafeed identifier.|
|state|object|false|none|The status of the datafeed.|
|assignment_explanation|string|false|none|For started datafeeds only, contains messages relating to the selection of a node.|
|buckets.count|string|false|none|The number of buckets processed.|
|search.count|string|false|none|The number of searches run by the datafeed.|
|search.time|string|false|none|The total time the datafeed spent searching, in milliseconds.|
|search.bucket_avg|string|false|none|The average search time per bucket, in milliseconds.|
|search.exp_avg_hour|string|false|none|The exponential average search time per hour, in milliseconds.|
|node.id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the assigned node.<br>For started datafeeds only, this information pertains to the node upon which the datafeed is started.|
|node.name|string|false|none|The name of the assigned node.<br>For started datafeeds only, this information pertains to the node upon which the datafeed is started.|
|node.ephemeral_id|string|false|none|The ephemeral identifier of the assigned node.<br>For started datafeeds only, this information pertains to the node upon which the datafeed is started.|
|node.address|string|false|none|The network address of the assigned node.<br>For started datafeeds only, this information pertains to the node upon which the datafeed is started.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|false|none|The anomaly detection job identifier.|
|state|object|false|none|The status of the anomaly detection job.|
|opened_time|string|false|none|For open jobs only, the amount of time the job has been opened.|
|assignment_explanation|string|false|none|For open anomaly detection jobs only, contains messages relating to the selection of a node to run the job.|
|data.processed_records|string|false|none|The number of input documents that have been processed by the anomaly detection job.<br>This value includes documents with missing fields, since they are nonetheless analyzed.<br>If you use datafeeds and have aggregations in your search query, the `processed_record_count` is the number of aggregation results processed, not the number of Elasticsearch documents.|
|data.processed_fields|string|false|none|The total number of fields in all the documents that have been processed by the anomaly detection job.<br>Only fields that are specified in the detector configuration object contribute to this count.<br>The timestamp is not included in this count.|
|data.input_bytes|object|false|none|The number of bytes of input data posted to the anomaly detection job.|
|data.input_records|string|false|none|The number of input documents posted to the anomaly detection job.|
|data.input_fields|string|false|none|The total number of fields in input documents posted to the anomaly detection job.<br>This count includes fields that are not used in the analysis.<br>However, be aware that if you are using a datafeed, it extracts only the required fields from the documents it retrieves before posting them to the job.|
|data.invalid_dates|string|false|none|The number of input documents with either a missing date field or a date that could not be parsed.|
|data.missing_fields|string|false|none|The number of input documents that are missing a field that the anomaly detection job is configured to analyze.<br>Input documents with missing fields are still processed because it is possible that not all fields are missing.<br>If you are using datafeeds or posting data to the job in JSON format, a high `missing_field_count` is often not an indication of data issues.<br>It is not necessarily a cause for concern.|
|data.out_of_order_timestamps|string|false|none|The number of input documents that have a timestamp chronologically preceding the start of the current anomaly detection bucket offset by the latency window.<br>This information is applicable only when you provide data to the anomaly detection job by using the post data API.<br>These out of order documents are discarded, since jobs require time series data to be in ascending chronological order.|
|data.empty_buckets|string|false|none|The number of buckets which did not contain any data.<br>If your data contains many empty buckets, consider increasing your `bucket_span` or using functions that are tolerant to gaps in data such as mean, `non_null_sum` or `non_zero_count`.|
|data.sparse_buckets|string|false|none|The number of buckets that contained few data points compared to the expected number of data points.<br>If your data contains many sparse buckets, consider using a longer `bucket_span`.|
|data.buckets|string|false|none|The total number of buckets processed.|
|data.earliest_record|string|false|none|The timestamp of the earliest chronologically input document.|
|data.latest_record|string|false|none|The timestamp of the latest chronologically input document.|
|data.last|string|false|none|The timestamp at which data was last analyzed, according to server time.|
|data.last_empty_bucket|string|false|none|The timestamp of the last bucket that did not contain any data.|
|data.last_sparse_bucket|string|false|none|The timestamp of the last bucket that was considered sparse.|
|model.bytes|object|false|none|The number of bytes of memory used by the models.<br>This is the maximum value since the last time the model was persisted.<br>If the job is closed, this value indicates the latest size.|
|model.memory_status|object|false|none|The status of the mathematical models.|
|model.bytes_exceeded|object|false|none|The number of bytes over the high limit for memory usage at the last allocation failure.|
|model.memory_limit|string|false|none|The upper limit for model memory usage, checked on increasing values.|
|model.by_fields|string|false|none|The number of `by` field values that were analyzed by the models.<br>This value is cumulative for all detectors in the job.|
|model.over_fields|string|false|none|The number of `over` field values that were analyzed by the models.<br>This value is cumulative for all detectors in the job.|
|model.partition_fields|string|false|none|The number of `partition` field values that were analyzed by the models.<br>This value is cumulative for all detectors in the job.|
|model.bucket_allocation_failures|string|false|none|The number of buckets for which new entities in incoming data were not processed due to insufficient model memory.<br>This situation is also signified by a `hard_limit: memory_status` property value.|
|model.categorization_status|object|false|none|The status of categorization for the job.|
|model.categorized_doc_count|string|false|none|The number of documents that have had a field categorized.|
|model.total_category_count|string|false|none|The number of categories created by categorization.|
|model.frequent_category_count|string|false|none|The number of categories that match more than 1% of categorized documents.|
|model.rare_category_count|string|false|none|The number of categories that match just one categorized document.|
|model.dead_category_count|string|false|none|The number of categories created by categorization that will never be assigned again because another category’s definition makes it a superset of the dead category.<br>Dead categories are a side effect of the way categorization has no prior training.|
|model.failed_category_count|string|false|none|The number of times that categorization wanted to create a new category but couldn’t because the job had hit its `model_memory_limit`.<br>This count does not track which specific categories failed to be created.<br>Therefore you cannot use this value to determine the number of unique categories that were missed.|
|model.log_time|string|false|none|The timestamp when the model stats were gathered, according to server time.|
|model.timestamp|string|false|none|The timestamp of the last record when the model stats were gathered.|
|forecasts.total|string|false|none|The number of individual forecasts currently available for the job.<br>A value of one or more indicates that forecasts exist.|
|forecasts.memory.min|string|false|none|The minimum memory usage in bytes for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.memory.max|string|false|none|The maximum memory usage in bytes for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.memory.avg|string|false|none|The average memory usage in bytes for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.memory.total|string|false|none|The total memory usage in bytes for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.records.min|string|false|none|The minimum number of `model_forecast` documents written for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.records.max|string|false|none|The maximum number of `model_forecast` documents written for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.records.avg|string|false|none|The average number of `model_forecast` documents written for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.records.total|string|false|none|The total number of `model_forecast` documents written for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.time.min|string|false|none|The minimum runtime in milliseconds for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.time.max|string|false|none|The maximum runtime in milliseconds for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.time.avg|string|false|none|The average runtime in milliseconds for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|forecasts.time.total|string|false|none|The total runtime in milliseconds for forecasts related to the anomaly detection job.|
|node.id|object|false|none|The uniqe identifier of the assigned node.|
|node.name|string|false|none|The name of the assigned node.|
|node.ephemeral_id|object|false|none|The ephemeral identifier of the assigned node.|
|node.address|string|false|none|The network address of the assigned node.|

|index|object|false|none|The index name.|
|shard|string|false|none|The shard name.|
|start_time|object|false|none|The recovery start time.<br>For recoveries in the `created` stage (not yet started), this value is the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z).|
|start_time_millis|object|false|none|The recovery start time in epoch milliseconds.<br>For recoveries in the `created` stage (not yet started), this value is 0.|
|stop_time|object|false|none|The recovery stop time.<br>For recoveries that have not yet completed, this value is the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z).|
|stop_time_millis|object|false|none|The recovery stop time in epoch milliseconds.<br>For recoveries that have not yet completed, this value is 0.|
|time|object|false|none|The recovery time.<br>For recoveries in the `created` stage (not yet started), this value is 0.|
|type|string|false|none|The recovery type.|
|stage|string|false|none|The recovery stage.|
|local_retries|string|false|none|The number of times this recovery has failed in a way which is retried locally (i.e. on the data node).|
|priority|string|false|none|The recovery priority.|
|gate|string|false|none|The name of the recovery gate that blocked recovery on the target node.<br><br>The value is `n/a` unless the recovery is queued in the `created` stage and blocked by a recovery gate.|
|blocked_for_millis|string|false|none|The elapsed time in milliseconds recovery is blocked for.<br><br>The value is `n/a` when the recovery is not blocked by a recovery gate.|
|source_host|string|false|none|The source host.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|object|false|none|The index name.|
|shard|string|false|none|The shard name.|
|prirep|string|false|none|The shard type: `primary` or `replica`.|
|ip|string|false|none|The IP address of the node where it lives.|
|id|object|false|none|The unique identifier of the node where it lives.|
|segment|string|false|none|The segment name, which is derived from the segment generation and used internally to create file names in the directory of the shard.|
|generation|string|false|none|The segment generation number.<br>Elasticsearch increments this generation number for each segment written then uses this number to derive the segment name.|
|docs.count|string|false|none|The number of documents in the segment.<br>This excludes deleted documents and counts any nested documents separately from their parents.<br>It also excludes documents which were indexed recently and do not yet belong to a segment.|
|docs.deleted|string|false|none|The number of deleted documents in the segment, which might be higher or lower than the number of delete operations you have performed.<br>This number excludes deletes that were performed recently and do not yet belong to a segment.<br>Deleted documents are cleaned up by the automatic merge process if it makes sense to do so.<br>Also, Elasticsearch creates extra deleted documents to internally track the recent history of operations on a shard.|
|size|object|false|none|The segment size in bytes.|
|size.memory|object|false|none|The segment memory in bytes.<br>A value of `-1` indicates Elasticsearch was unable to compute this number.|
|committed|string|false|none|If `true`, the segment is synced to disk.<br>Segments that are synced can survive a hard reboot.<br>If `false`, the data from uncommitted segments is also stored in the transaction log so that Elasticsearch is able to replay changes on the next start.|
|searchable|string|false|none|If `true`, the segment is searchable.<br>If `false`, the segment has most likely been written to disk but needs a refresh to be searchable.|
|version|object|false|none|The version of Lucene used to write the segment.|
|compound|string|false|none|If `true`, the segment is stored in a compound file.<br>This means Lucene merged all files from the segment in a single file to save file descriptors.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|string|false|none|The index name.|
|shard|string|false|none|The shard name.|
|prirep|string|false|none|The shard type: `primary` or `replica`.|
|state|string|false|none|The shard state.<br>Returned values include:<br>`INITIALIZING`: The shard is recovering from a peer shard or gateway.<br>`RELOCATING`: The shard is relocating.<br>`STARTED`: The shard has started.<br>`UNASSIGNED`: The shard is not assigned to any node.|
|docs|string \| string \| null|false|none|The number of documents in the shard.|
|store|string \| string \| null|false|none|The disk space used by the shard.|
|dataset|string \| string \| null|false|none|total size of dataset (including the cache for partially mounted indices)|
|ip|string \| string \| null|false|none|The IP address of the node.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the node.|
|node|string \| string \| null|false|none|The name of node.|
|sync_id|string|false|none|The sync identifier.|
|unassigned.reason|string|false|none|The reason for the last change to the state of an unassigned shard.<br>It does not explain why the shard is currently unassigned; use the cluster allocation explain API for that information.<br>Returned values include:<br>`ALLOCATION_FAILED`: Unassigned as a result of a failed allocation of the shard.<br>`CLUSTER_RECOVERED`: Unassigned as a result of a full cluster recovery.<br>`DANGLING_INDEX_IMPORTED`: Unassigned as a result of importing a dangling index.<br>`EXISTING_INDEX_RESTORED`: Unassigned as a result of restoring into a closed index.<br>`FORCED_EMPTY_PRIMARY`: The shard’s allocation was last modified by forcing an empty primary using the cluster reroute API.<br>`INDEX_CLOSED`: Unassigned because the index was closed.<br>`INDEX_CREATED`: Unassigned as a result of an API creation of an index.<br>`INDEX_REOPENED`: Unassigned as a result of opening a closed index.<br>`MANUAL_ALLOCATION`: The shard’s allocation was last modified by the cluster reroute API.<br>`NEW_INDEX_RESTORED`: Unassigned as a result of restoring into a new index.<br>`NODE_LEFT`: Unassigned as a result of the node hosting it leaving the cluster.<br>`NODE_RESTARTING`: Similar to `NODE_LEFT`, except that the node was registered as restarting using the node shutdown API.<br>`PRIMARY_FAILED`: The shard was initializing as a replica, but the primary shard failed before the initialization completed.<br>`REALLOCATED_REPLICA`: A better replica location is identified and causes the existing replica allocation to be cancelled.<br>`REINITIALIZED`: When a shard moves from started back to initializing.<br>`REPLICA_ADDED`: Unassigned as a result of explicit addition of a replica.<br>`REROUTE_CANCELLED`: Unassigned as a result of explicit cancel reroute command.|
|unassigned.at|string|false|none|The time at which the shard became unassigned in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|unassigned.for|string|false|none|The time at which the shard was requested to be unassigned in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|unassigned.details|string|false|none|Additional details as to why the shard became unassigned.<br>It does not explain why the shard is not assigned; use the cluster allocation explain API for that information.|
|recoverysource.type|string|false|none|The type of recovery source.|
|completion.size|string|false|none|The size of completion.|
|fielddata.memory_size|string|false|none|The used fielddata cache memory.|
|fielddata.evictions|string|false|none|The fielddata cache evictions.|
|query_cache.memory_size|string|false|none|The used query cache memory.|
|query_cache.evictions|string|false|none|The query cache evictions.|
|flush.total|string|false|none|The number of flushes.|
|flush.total_time|string|false|none|The time spent in flush.|
|get.current|string|false|none|The number of current get operations.|
|get.time|string|false|none|The time spent in get operations.|
|get.total|string|false|none|The number of get operations.|
|get.exists_time|string|false|none|The time spent in successful get operations.|
|get.exists_total|string|false|none|The number of successful get operations.|
|get.missing_time|string|false|none|The time spent in failed get operations.|
|get.missing_total|string|false|none|The number of failed get operations.|
|indexing.delete_current|string|false|none|The number of current deletion operations.|
|indexing.delete_time|string|false|none|The time spent in deletion operations.|
|indexing.delete_total|string|false|none|The number of delete operations.|
|indexing.index_current|string|false|none|The number of current indexing operations.|
|indexing.index_time|string|false|none|The time spent in indexing operations.|
|indexing.index_total|string|false|none|The number of indexing operations.|
|indexing.index_failed|string|false|none|The number of failed indexing operations.|
|merges.current|string|false|none|The number of current merge operations.|
|merges.current_docs|string|false|none|The number of current merging documents.|
|merges.current_size|string|false|none|The size of current merge operations.|
|merges.total|string|false|none|The number of completed merge operations.|
|merges.total_docs|string|false|none|The nuber of merged documents.|
|merges.total_size|string|false|none|The size of current merges.|
|merges.total_time|string|false|none|The time spent merging documents.|
|refresh.total|string|false|none|The total number of refreshes.|
|refresh.time|string|false|none|The time spent in refreshes.|
|refresh.external_total|string|false|none|The total nunber of external refreshes.|
|refresh.external_time|string|false|none|The time spent in external refreshes.|
|refresh.listeners|string|false|none|The number of pending refresh listeners.|
|search.fetch_current|string|false|none|The current fetch phase operations.|
|search.fetch_time|string|false|none|The time spent in fetch phase.|
|search.fetch_total|string|false|none|The total number of fetch operations.|
|search.open_contexts|string|false|none|The number of open search contexts.|
|search.query_current|string|false|none|The current query phase operations.|
|search.query_time|string|false|none|The time spent in query phase.|
|search.query_total|string|false|none|The total number of query phase operations.|
|search.scroll_current|string|false|none|The open scroll contexts.|
|search.scroll_time|string|false|none|The time scroll contexts were held open.|
|search.scroll_total|string|false|none|The number of completed scroll contexts.|
|segments.count|string|false|none|The number of segments.|
|segments.memory|string|false|none|The memory used by segments.|
|segments.index_writer_memory|string|false|none|The memory used by the index writer.|
|segments.version_map_memory|string|false|none|The memory used by the version map.|
|segments.fixed_bitset_memory|string|false|none|The memory used by fixed bit sets for nested object field types and export type filters for types referred in `_parent` fields.|
|seq_no.max|string|false|none|The maximum sequence number.|
|seq_no.local_checkpoint|string|false|none|The local checkpoint.|
|seq_no.global_checkpoint|string|false|none|The global checkpoint.|
|warmer.current|string|false|none|The number of current warmer operations.|
|warmer.total|string|false|none|The total number of warmer operations.|
|warmer.total_time|string|false|none|The time spent in warmer operations.|
|path.data|string|false|none|The shard data path.|
|path.state|string|false|none|The shard state path.|
|bulk.total_operations|string|false|none|The number of bulk shard operations.|
|bulk.total_time|string|false|none|The time spent in shard bulk operations.|
|bulk.total_size_in_bytes|string|false|none|The total size in bytes of shard bulk operations.|
|bulk.avg_time|string|false|none|The average time spent in shard bulk operations.|
|bulk.avg_size_in_bytes|string|false|none|The average size in bytes of shard bulk operations.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|false|none|The transform identifier.|
|state|string|false|none|The status of the transform.<br>Returned values include:<br>`aborting`: The transform is aborting.<br>`failed: The transform failed. For more information about the failure, check the `reason` field.<br>`indexing`: The transform is actively processing data and creating new documents.<br>`started`: The transform is running but not actively indexing data.<br>`stopped`: The transform is stopped.<br>`stopping`: The transform is stopping.|
|checkpoint|string|false|none|The sequence number for the checkpoint.|
|documents_processed|string|false|none|The number of documents that have been processed from the source index of the transform.|
|checkpoint_progress|string \| string \| null|false|none|The progress of the next checkpoint that is currently in progress.|
|last_search_time|string \| string \| null|false|none|The timestamp of the last search in the source indices.<br>This field is shown only if the transform is running.|
|changes_last_detection_time|string \| string \| null|false|none|The timestamp when changes were last detected in the source indices.|
|create_time|string|false|none|The time the transform was created.|
|version|object|false|none|The version of Elasticsearch that existed on the node when the transform was created.|
|source_index|string|false|none|The source indices for the transform.|
|dest_index|string|false|none|The destination index for the transform.|
|pipeline|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the ingest pipeline.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the transform.|
|transform_type|string|false|none|The type of transform: `batch` or `continuous`.|
|frequency|string|false|none|The interval between checks for changes in the source indices when the transform is running continuously.|
|max_page_search_size|string|false|none|The initial page size that is used for the composite aggregation for each checkpoint.|
|docs_per_second|string|false|none|The number of input documents per second.|
|reason|string|false|none|If a transform has a `failed` state, these details describe the reason for failure.|
|search_total|string|false|none|The total number of search operations on the source index for the transform.|
|search_failure|string|false|none|The total number of search failures.|
|search_time|string|false|none|The total amount of search time, in milliseconds.|
|index_total|string|false|none|The total number of index operations done by the transform.|
|index_failure|string|false|none|The total number of indexing failures.|
|index_time|string|false|none|The total time spent indexing documents, in milliseconds.|
|documents_indexed|string|false|none|The number of documents that have been indexed into the destination index for the transform.|
|delete_time|string|false|none|The total time spent deleting documents, in milliseconds.|
|documents_deleted|string|false|none|The number of documents deleted from the destination index due to the retention policy for the transform.|
|trigger_count|string|false|none|The number of times the transform has been triggered by the scheduler.<br>For example, the scheduler triggers the transform indexer to check for updates or ingest new data at an interval specified in the `frequency` property.|
|pages_processed|string|false|none|The number of search or bulk index operations processed.<br>Documents are processed in batches instead of individually.|
|processing_time|string|false|none|The total time spent processing results, in milliseconds.|
|checkpoint_duration_time_exp_avg|string|false|none|The exponential moving average of the duration of the checkpoint, in milliseconds.|
|indexed_documents_exp_avg|string|false|none|The exponential moving average of the number of new documents that have been indexed.|
|processed_documents_exp_avg|string|false|none|The exponential moving average of the number of documents that have been processed.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether soft deletes are enabled on the index.|
|retention_lease|object|false|none|The maximum period to retain a shard history retention lease before it is considered expired.<br>Shard history retention leases ensure that soft deletes are retained during merges on the Lucene<br>index. If a soft delete is merged away before it can be replicated to a follower the following<br>process will fail due to incomplete history on the leader.|

Some APIs will return values such as numbers also as a string (notably epoch timestamps). This behavior

strings to the target type.

<a id="schema__spec_utils.NullValue"></a>
<a id="tocS_spec_utils.nullvalue"></a>
<a id="tocs_spec_utils.nullvalue"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A `null` value that is to be interpreted as an actual value, unless other uses of `null` that are equivalent
to a missing value. It is used for exemple in settings, where using the `NullValue` for a setting will reset
it to its default value.

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.IndexSettingsLifecycle">indices._types.IndexSettingsLifecycle</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.indexsettingslifecycle"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.IndexSettingsLifecycle"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.indexsettingslifecycle"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.indexsettingslifecycle"></a>

```json
{
  "name": {},
  "indexing_complete": "false",
  "origination_date": 0,
  "parse_origination_date": true,
  "step": {
    "wait_time_threshold": {}
  },
  "rollover_alias": "",
  "prefer_ilm": "true"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|object|false|none|The name of the policy to use to manage the index. For information about how Elasticsearch applies policy changes, see Policy updates.|
|indexing_complete|object|false|none|Indicates whether or not the index has been rolled over. Automatically set to true when ILM completes the rollover action.<br>You can explicitly set it to skip rollover.|
|origination_date|number|false|none|If specified, this is the timestamp used to calculate the index age for its phase transitions. Use this setting<br>if you create a new index that contains old data and want to use the original creation date to calculate the index<br>age. Specified as a Unix epoch value in milliseconds.|
|parse_origination_date|boolean|false|none|Set to true to parse the origination date from the index name. This origination date is used to calculate the index age<br>for its phase transitions. The index name must match the pattern ^.*-{date_format}-\\d+, where the date_format is<br>yyyy.MM.dd and the trailing digits are optional. An index that was rolled over would normally match the full format,<br>for example logs-2016.10.31-000002). If the index name doesn’t match the pattern, index creation fails.|
|step|object|false|none|none|
|rollover_alias|string|false|none|The index alias to update when the index rolls over. Specify when using a policy that contains a rollover action.<br>When the index rolls over, the alias is updated to reflect that the index is no longer the write index. For more<br>information about rolling indices, see Rollover.|
|prefer_ilm|boolean \| string|false|none|Preference for the system that manages a data stream backing index (preferring ILM when both ILM and DLM are<br>applicable for an index).|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.Translog">indices._types.Translog</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.translog"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.Translog"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.translog"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.translog"></a>

```json
{
  "sync_interval": "5s",
  "durability": "string",
  "flush_threshold_size": "512mb",
  "retention": {
    "size": "512mb",
    "age": "12h"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sync_interval|object|false|none|How often the translog is fsynced to disk and committed, regardless of write operations.<br>Values less than 100ms are not allowed.|
|durability|object|false|none|Whether or not to `fsync` and commit the translog after every index, delete, update, or bulk request.|
|flush_threshold_size|object|false|none|The translog stores all operations that are not yet safely persisted in Lucene (i.e., are not<br>part of a Lucene commit point). Although these operations are available for reads, they will need<br>to be replayed if the shard was stopped and had to be recovered. This setting controls the<br>maximum total size of these operations, to prevent recoveries from taking too long. Once the<br>maximum size has been reached a flush will happen, generating a new Lucene commit point.|
|retention|object|false|none|none|

<a id="tocSindices._types.translogretention"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.translogretention"></a>

```json
{
  "size": "512mb",
  "age": "12h"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|size|object|false|none|This controls the total size of translog files to keep for each shard. Keeping more translog files increases<br>the chance of performing an operation based sync when recovering a replica. If the translog files are not<br>sufficient, replica recovery will fall back to a file based sync. This setting is ignored, and should not be<br>set, if soft deletes are enabled. Soft deletes are enabled by default in indices created in Elasticsearch<br>versions 7.0.0 and later.|
|age|object|false|none|This controls the maximum duration for which translog files are kept by each shard. Keeping more<br>translog files increases the chance of performing an operation based sync when recovering replicas. If<br>the translog files are not sufficient, replica recovery will fall back to a file based sync. This setting<br>is ignored, and should not be set, if soft deletes are enabled. Soft deletes are enabled by default in<br>indices created in Elasticsearch versions 7.0.0 and later.|

```json
{
  "version": {},
  "max_subword_size": 0,
  "min_subword_size": 0,
  "min_word_size": 0,
  "only_longest_match": true,
  "word_list": [
    "string"
  ],
  "word_list_path": "string",
  "type": "hyphenation_decompounder",
  "hyphenation_patterns_path": "string",
  "no_sub_matches": true,
  "no_overlapping_matches": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|max_subword_size|number|false|none|Maximum subword character length. Longer subword tokens are excluded from the output. Defaults to `15`.|

|min_word_size|number|false|none|Minimum word character length. Shorter word tokens are excluded from the output. Defaults to `5`.|
|only_longest_match|boolean|false|none|If `true`, only include the longest matching subword. Defaults to `false`.|
|word_list|[string]|false|none|A list of subwords to look for in the token stream. If found, the subword is included in the token output.<br>Either this parameter or `word_list_path` must be specified.|
|word_list_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains a list of subwords to find in the token stream. If found, the subword is included in the token output.<br>This path must be absolute or relative to the config location, and the file must be UTF-8 encoded. Each token in the file must be separated by a line break.<br>Either this parameter or `word_list` must be specified.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|hyphenation_patterns_path|string|true|none|Path to an Apache FOP (Formatting Objects Processor) XML hyphenation pattern file.<br>This path must be absolute or relative to the `config` location. Only FOP v1.2 compatible files are supported.|
|no_sub_matches|boolean|false|none|If `true`, do not match sub tokens in tokens that are in the word list. Defaults to `false`.|
|no_overlapping_matches|boolean|false|none|If `true`, do not allow overlapping tokens. Defaults to `false`.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

<a id="tocS_types.analysis.shingletokenfilter"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.analysis.shingletokenfilter"></a>

```json
{
  "version": {},
  "type": "shingle",
  "filler_token": "string",
  "max_shingle_size": {},
  "min_shingle_size": {},
  "output_unigrams": true,
  "output_unigrams_if_no_shingles": true,
  "token_separator": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|filler_token|string|false|none|String used in shingles as a replacement for empty positions that do not contain a token. This filler token is only used in shingles, not original unigrams. Defaults to an underscore (`_`).|
|max_shingle_size|object|false|none|Maximum number of tokens to concatenate when creating shingles. Defaults to `2`.|
|min_shingle_size|object|false|none|Minimum number of tokens to concatenate when creating shingles. Defaults to `2`.|
|output_unigrams|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the output includes the original input tokens. If `false`, the output only includes shingles; the original input tokens are removed. Defaults to `true`.|
|output_unigrams_if_no_shingles|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the output includes the original input tokens only if no shingles are produced; if shingles are produced, the output only includes shingles. Defaults to `false`.|
|token_separator|string|false|none|Separator used to concatenate adjacent tokens to form a shingle. Defaults to a space (`" "`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|shingle|

```json
{
  "version": {},
  "type": "stop",
  "ignore_case": true,
  "remove_trailing": true,
  "stopwords": {},
  "stopwords_path": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|ignore_case|boolean|false|none|If `true`, stop word matching is case insensitive. For example, if `true`, a stop word of the matches and removes `The`, `THE`, or `the`. Defaults to `false`.|
|remove_trailing|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the last token of a stream is removed if it’s a stop word. Defaults to `true`.|
|stopwords|object|false|none|Language value, such as `_arabic_` or `_thai_`. Defaults to `_english_`.|
|stopwords_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains a list of stop words to remove.<br>This path must be absolute or relative to the `config` location, and the file must be UTF-8 encoded. Each stop word in the file must be separated by a line break.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|stop|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|expand|boolean|false|none|Expands definitions for equivalent synonym rules. Defaults to `true`.|
|format|object|false|none|Sets the synonym rules format.|
|lenient|boolean|false|none|If `true` ignores errors while parsing the synonym rules. It is important to note that only those synonym rules which cannot get parsed are ignored. Defaults to the value of the `updateable` setting.|
|synonyms|[string]|false|none|Used to define inline synonyms.|
|synonyms_path|string|false|none|Used to provide a synonym file. This path must be absolute or relative to the `config` location.|
|synonyms_set|string \| [string]|false|none|Provide one or more synonym sets created through the Synonyms Management APIs. Maximum 100 sets per filter.|
|tokenizer|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Controls the tokenizers that will be used to tokenize the synonym, this parameter is for backwards compatibility for indices that created before 6.0.|
|updateable|boolean|false|none|If `true` allows reloading search analyzers to pick up changes to synonym files. Only to be used for search analyzers. Defaults to `false`.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|synonym_graph|

<h2 id="tocS__types.analysis.WordDelimiterGraphTokenFilter">_types.analysis.WordDelimiterGraphTokenFilter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.analysis.worddelimitergraphtokenfilter"></a>
<a id="schema__types.analysis.WordDelimiterGraphTokenFilter"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.analysis.worddelimitergraphtokenfilter"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.analysis.worddelimitergraphtokenfilter"></a>

```json
{
  "version": {},
  "catenate_all": true,
  "catenate_numbers": true,
  "catenate_words": true,
  "generate_number_parts": true,
  "generate_word_parts": true,
  "preserve_original": {},
  "protected_words": [
    "string"
  ],
  "protected_words_path": "string",
  "split_on_case_change": true,
  "split_on_numerics": true,
  "stem_english_possessive": true,
  "type_table": [
    "string"
  ],
  "type_table_path": "string",
  "type": "word_delimiter_graph",
  "adjust_offsets": true,
  "ignore_keywords": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|catenate_all|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter produces catenated tokens for chains of alphanumeric characters separated by non-alphabetic delimiters. Defaults to `false`.|
|catenate_numbers|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter produces catenated tokens for chains of numeric characters separated by non-alphabetic delimiters. Defaults to `false`.|
|catenate_words|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter produces catenated tokens for chains of alphabetical characters separated by non-alphabetic delimiters. Defaults to `false`.|
|generate_number_parts|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter includes tokens consisting of only numeric characters in the output. If `false`, the filter excludes these tokens from the output. Defaults to `true`.|
|generate_word_parts|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter includes tokens consisting of only alphabetical characters in the output. If `false`, the filter excludes these tokens from the output. Defaults to `true`.|
|preserve_original|object|false|none|If `true`, the filter includes the original version of any split tokens in the output. This original version includes non-alphanumeric delimiters. Defaults to `false`.|
|protected_words|[string]|false|none|Array of tokens the filter won’t split.|
|protected_words_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains a list of tokens the filter won’t split.<br>This path must be absolute or relative to the `config` location, and the file must be UTF-8 encoded. Each token in the file must be separated by a line break.|
|split_on_case_change|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter splits tokens at letter case transitions. For example: camelCase -> [ camel, Case ]. Defaults to `true`.|
|split_on_numerics|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter splits tokens at letter-number transitions. For example: j2se -> [ j, 2, se ]. Defaults to `true`.|
|stem_english_possessive|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter removes the English possessive (`'s`) from the end of each token. For example: O'Neil's -> [ O, Neil ]. Defaults to `true`.|
|type_table|[string]|false|none|Array of custom type mappings for characters. This allows you to map non-alphanumeric characters as numeric or alphanumeric to avoid splitting on those characters.|
|type_table_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains custom type mappings for characters. This allows you to map non-alphanumeric characters as numeric or alphanumeric to avoid splitting on those characters.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|adjust_offsets|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter adjusts the offsets of split or catenated tokens to better reflect their actual position in the token stream. Defaults to `true`.|
|ignore_keywords|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter skips tokens with a keyword attribute of true. Defaults to `false`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|word_delimiter_graph|

|stem_english_possessive|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the filter removes the English possessive (`'s`) from the end of each token. For example: O'Neil's -> [ O, Neil ]. Defaults to `true`.|
|type_table|[string]|false|none|Array of custom type mappings for characters. This allows you to map non-alphanumeric characters as numeric or alphanumeric to avoid splitting on those characters.|
|type_table_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains custom type mappings for characters. This allows you to map non-alphanumeric characters as numeric or alphanumeric to avoid splitting on those characters.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|word_delimiter|

```json
{
  "version": {},
  "max_subword_size": 0,
  "min_subword_size": 0,
  "min_word_size": 0,
  "only_longest_match": true,
  "word_list": [
    "string"
  ],
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|max_subword_size|number|false|none|Maximum subword character length. Longer subword tokens are excluded from the output. Defaults to `15`.|
|min_subword_size|number|false|none|Minimum subword character length. Shorter subword tokens are excluded from the output. Defaults to `2`.|
|min_word_size|number|false|none|Minimum word character length. Shorter word tokens are excluded from the output. Defaults to `5`.|
|only_longest_match|boolean|false|none|If `true`, only include the longest matching subword. Defaults to `false`.|
|word_list|[string]|false|none|A list of subwords to look for in the token stream. If found, the subword is included in the token output.<br>Either this parameter or `word_list_path` must be specified.|
|word_list_path|string|false|none|Path to a file that contains a list of subwords to find in the token stream. If found, the subword is included in the token output.<br>This path must be absolute or relative to the config location, and the file must be UTF-8 encoded. Each token in the file must be separated by a line break.<br>Either this parameter or `word_list` must be specified.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|dictionary_decompounder|

```json
  "ignore_dynamic_beyond_limit": "false"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|number \| string|false|none|The maximum number of fields in an index. Field and object mappings, as well as field aliases count towards this limit.<br>The limit is in place to prevent mappings and searches from becoming too large. Higher values can lead to performance<br>degradations and memory issues, especially in clusters with a high load or few resources.|
|ignore_dynamic_beyond_limit|boolean \| string|false|none|This setting determines what happens when a dynamically mapped field would exceed the total fields limit. When set<br>to false (the default), the index request of the document that tries to add a dynamic field to the mapping will fail<br>with the message Limit of total fields [X] has been exceeded. When set to true, the index request will not fail.<br>Instead, fields that would exceed the limit are not added to the mapping, similar to dynamic: false.<br>The fields that were not added to the mapping will be added to the _ignored field.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "max_outstanding_write_requests": 0,

  "max_read_request_size": {},
  "max_retry_delay": {},
  "max_write_buffer_count": 0,
  "max_write_buffer_size": {},
  "max_write_request_operation_count": 0,
  "max_write_request_size": {},
```

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_outstanding_read_requests|number|false|none|The maximum number of outstanding reads requests from the remote cluster.|
|max_outstanding_write_requests|number|false|none|The maximum number of outstanding write requests on the follower.|
|max_read_request_operation_count|number|false|none|The maximum number of operations to pull per read from the remote cluster.|
|max_read_request_size|object|false|none|The maximum size in bytes of per read of a batch of operations pulled from the remote cluster.|
|max_retry_delay|object|false|none|The maximum time to wait before retrying an operation that failed exceptionally. An exponential backoff strategy is employed when<br>retrying.|
|max_write_buffer_count|number|false|none|The maximum number of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will be<br>deferred until the number of queued operations goes below the limit.|
|max_write_buffer_size|object|false|none|The maximum total bytes of operations that can be queued for writing. When this limit is reached, reads from the remote cluster will<br>be deferred until the total bytes of queued operations goes below the limit.|
|max_write_request_operation_count|number|false|none|The maximum number of operations per bulk write request executed on the follower.|
|max_write_request_size|object|false|none|The maximum total bytes of operations per bulk write request executed on the follower.|
|read_poll_timeout|object|false|none|The maximum time to wait for new operations on the remote cluster when the follower index is synchronized with the leader index.<br>When the timeout has elapsed, the poll for operations will return to the follower so that it can update some statistics.<br>Then the follower will immediately attempt to read from the leader again.|

```json
  "downsampling": [

    }
  ],
```


Data stream lifecycle with rollover can be used to display the configuration including the default rollover conditions,
if asked.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_retention|object|false|none|If defined, every document added to this data stream will be stored at least for this time frame.<br>Any time after this duration the document could be deleted.<br>When empty, every document in this data stream will be stored indefinitely.|
|effective_retention|object|false|none|The least amount of time data should be kept by elasticsearch.|
|retention_determined_by|object|false|none|Configuration source that can influence the retention of a data stream.|
|downsampling|[[indices._types.DownsamplingRound](#schemaindices._types.downsamplinground)]|false|none|The list of downsampling rounds to execute as part of this downsampling configuration|
|downsampling_method|object|false|none|The method used to downsample the data. There are two options `aggregate` and `last_value`. It requires<br>`downsampling` to be defined. Defaults to `aggregate`.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|If defined, it turns data stream lifecycle on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream lifecycle<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will have no effect on the data stream.|
|frozen_after|object|false|none|The period after which data stream backing indices are automatically converted to partially mounted searchable snapshots.<br>This field is valid only on main data stream lifecycles and cannot be set on failure-store lifecycles.|
|rollover|object|false|none|The conditions which will trigger the rollover of a backing index as configured by the cluster setting `cluster.lifecycle.default.rollover`.<br>This property is an implementation detail and it will only be retrieved when the query param `include_defaults` is set to true.<br>The contents of this field are subject to change.|

|enabled|boolean|false|none|If defined, it turns data stream lifecycle on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream lifecycle<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will have no effect on the data stream.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|multi_value|boolean|false|none|If `false`, the field is treated as single-valued, enabling optimized storage.<br>Only has an effect when columnar index mode is active.|
|nullability|boolean|false|none|If `false`, every document must provide a non-null value for the field: a document that<br>omits the field, sets it to `null`, or supplies only null values (an empty array or an<br>all-null array) is rejected at index time.<br>A field that defines `null_value` is always exempt, since the configured default removes<br>the absence of a value.<br>Only has an effect when columnar index mode is active.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.mapping.MatchOnlyTextProperty">_types.mapping.MatchOnlyTextProperty</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.mapping.matchonlytextproperty"></a>
<a id="schema__types.mapping.MatchOnlyTextProperty"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.mapping.matchonlytextproperty"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.mapping.matchonlytextproperty"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "match_only_text",
  "fields": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "meta": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "copy_to": {}
}
```

A variant of text that trades scoring and efficiency of positional queries for space efficiency. This field
effectively stores data the same way as a text field that only indexes documents (index_options: docs) and
disables norms (norms: false). Term queries perform as fast if not faster as on text fields, however queries
that need positions such as the match_phrase query perform slower as they need to look at the _source document
to verify whether a phrase matches. All queries return constant scores that are equal to 1.0.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|fields|object|false|none|Multi-fields allow the same string value to be indexed in multiple ways for different purposes, such as one<br>field for search and a multi-field for sorting and aggregations, or the same string value analyzed by different analyzers.|
|meta|object|false|none|Metadata about the field.|
|copy_to|object|false|none|Allows you to copy the values of multiple fields into a group<br>field, which can then be queried as a single field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|match_only_text|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|confidence_interval|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** The confidence interval to use when quantizing the vectors. Can be any value between and including `0.90` and<br>`1.0` or exactly `0`. When the value is `0`, this indicates that dynamic quantiles should be calculated for<br>optimized quantization. When between `0.90` and `1.0`, this value restricts the values used when calculating<br>the quantization thresholds.<br><br>For example, a value of `0.95` will only use the middle `95%` of the values when calculating the quantization<br>thresholds (e.g. the highest and lowest `2.5%` of values will be ignored).<br><br>Defaults to `1/(dims + 1)` for `int8` quantized vectors and `0` for `int4` for dynamic quantile calculation.<br><br>Only applicable to `int8_hnsw`, `int4_hnsw`, `int8_flat`, and `int4_flat` index types.|
|ef_construction|number|false|none|The number of candidates to track while assembling the list of nearest neighbors for each new node.<br><br>Only applicable to `hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`, `bbq_hnsw`, and `int4_hnsw` index types.|
|m|number|false|none|The number of neighbors each node will be connected to in the HNSW graph.<br><br>Only applicable to `hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`, `bbq_hnsw`, and `int4_hnsw` index types.|
|type|object|true|none|The type of kNN algorithm to use.|
|rescore_vector|object|false|none|The rescore vector options. This is only applicable to `bbq_disk`, `bbq_hnsw`, `int4_hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`, `bbq_flat`, `int4_flat`, and `int8_flat` index types.|
|on_disk_rescore|boolean|false|none|`true` if vector rescoring should be done on-disk<br><br>Only applicable to `bbq_disk`, `bbq_hnsw`, `int4_hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`|
|flat_index_threshold|number|false|none|The segment document count threshold below which HNSW graph construction is skipped in favor of brute-force flat<br>search. `-1` (default) defers to format defaults: `300` for `bbq_hnsw`, `150` for `hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`, and<br>`int4_hnsw`. `0` always builds the graph. A positive value overrides the format default.<br><br>Only applicable to `hnsw`, `int8_hnsw`, `int4_hnsw`, `bbq_hnsw`, and `bbq_disk` index types.|
|cluster_size|number|false|none|Only applicable to `bbq_disk`. The number of vectors per cluster. Must be between 64 and 65536.|
|default_visit_percentage|number|false|none|Only applicable to `bbq_disk`. The percentage of clusters to visit during search. Must be between 0 and 100.<br>A value of 0 defaults to using `num_candidates` for calculating the visit percentage.|
|bits|number|false|none|Only applicable to `bbq_disk`. The number of bits per dimension for quantization encoding.<br>Valid values are `1`, `2`, `4`, or `7`. When no `rescore_vector` is explicitly set,<br>the default oversampling is automatically adjusted based on the bits value.<br>This setting can be changed without reindexing.|
|precondition|boolean|false|none|Only applicable to `bbq_disk`. When `true`, transforms indexed vectors using a random orthogonal<br>projection before quantization, which can improve accuracy when vector components are not normally<br>distributed. Cannot be changed after the field is created.|
|auto_calibrate|boolean|false|none|Only applicable to `bbq_disk`. When `true`, Elasticsearch automatically selects the optimal<br>quantization encoding, oversampling factor, and preconditioning for each merged segment based<br>on estimated recall characteristics. Cannot be changed after the field is created.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prune|boolean|false|none|Whether to perform pruning, omitting the non-significant tokens from the query to improve query performance.<br>If prune is true but the pruning_config is not specified, pruning will occur but default values will be used.<br>Default: false|
|pruning_config|object|false|none|Optional pruning configuration.<br>If enabled, this will omit non-significant tokens from the query in order to improve query performance.<br>This is only used if prune is set to true.<br>If prune is set to true but pruning_config is not specified, default values will be used.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.mapping.ChunkingSettings">_types.mapping.ChunkingSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.mapping.chunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="schema__types.mapping.ChunkingSettings"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.mapping.chunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.mapping.chunkingsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "strategy": "sentence",
  "max_chunk_size": 250,
  "overlap": 100,
  "sentence_overlap": 1,
  "separator_group": "string",
  "separators": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|strategy|string|true|none|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|
|max_chunk_size|number|true|none|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|sentence_overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|separator_group|string|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|separators|[string]|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|object|false|none|Query used to limit documents the alias can access.|
|index_routing|string|false|none|Value used to route indexing operations to a specific shard.<br>If specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for indexing operations.|
|is_write_index|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the index is the write index for the alias.|
|routing|string|false|none|Value used to route indexing and search operations to a specific shard.|
|search_routing|string|false|none|Value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>If specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for search operations.|
|is_hidden|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the alias is hidden.<br>All indices for the alias must have the same `is_hidden` value.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.DataStreamOptions">indices._types.DataStreamOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.datastreamoptions"></a>

<a id="tocsindices._types.datastreamoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "failure_store": {
    "enabled": true,
    "lifecycle": {
      "data_retention": {},
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Data stream options contain the configuration of data stream level features for a given data stream, for example,
the failure store configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|failure_store|object|false|none|If defined, it specifies configuration for the failure store of this data stream.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.DataStreamFailureStore">indices._types.DataStreamFailureStore</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.datastreamfailurestore"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.DataStreamFailureStore"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.datastreamfailurestore"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.datastreamfailurestore"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "lifecycle": {
    "data_retention": {},
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

Data stream failure store contains the configuration of the failure store for a given data stream.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|If defined, it turns the failure store on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream failure store<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will redirect no new failed indices to the failure store; however, it will<br>not remove any existing data from the failure store.|
|lifecycle|object|false|none|If defined, it specifies the lifecycle configuration for the failure store of this data stream.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycle">indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycle</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.failurestorelifecycle"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycle"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.failurestorelifecycle"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.failurestorelifecycle"></a>

```json
{
  "data_retention": {},
  "enabled": true
}
```

The failure store lifecycle configures the data stream lifecycle configuration for failure indices.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_retention|object|false|none|If defined, every document added to this data stream will be stored at least for this time frame.<br>Any time after this duration the document could be deleted.<br>When empty, every document in this data stream will be stored indefinitely.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|If defined, it turns data stream lifecycle on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream lifecycle<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will have no effect on the data stream.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|count|number|true|none|Total number of documents ingested during the lifetime of this node.|
|current|number|true|none|Total number of documents currently being ingested.|
|failed|number|true|none|Total number of failed ingest operations during the lifetime of this node.|
|processors|[object]|true|none|Total number of ingest processors.|
|time|object|false|none|Total time spent preprocessing ingest documents during the lifetime of this node.|
|time_in_millis|object|true|none|Total time, in milliseconds, spent preprocessing ingest documents during the lifetime of this node.|
|ingested_as_first_pipeline|object|false|none|Total size of all documents ingested by the pipeline.<br>The value counts documents for which this pipeline was the first to process them; for pipelines that are not the first to process a document (for example, a final pipeline after a default pipeline, a pipeline run after a reroute processor, or a pipeline invoked by a pipeline processor), the value is `0`.|
|ingested_as_first_pipeline_in_bytes|number|true|none|Total number of bytes of all documents ingested by the pipeline.<br>The value counts documents for which this pipeline was the first to process them; for pipelines that are not the first to process a document, the value is `0`.|
|produced_as_first_pipeline|object|false|none|Total size of all documents produced by the pipeline.<br>The value counts documents for which this pipeline was the first to process them; for pipelines that are not the first to process a document, the value is `0`.<br>In situations where there are subsequent pipelines, the value represents the size of the document after all pipelines have run.|
|produced_as_first_pipeline_in_bytes|number|true|none|Total number of bytes of all documents produced by the pipeline.<br>The value counts documents for which this pipeline was the first to process them; for pipelines that are not the first to process a document, the value is `0`.<br>In situations where there are subsequent pipelines, the value represents the size of the document after all pipelines have run.|

<a id="tocSnodes._types.threadcount"></a>
<a id="tocsnodes._types.threadcount"></a>

```json
{
  "active": 0,
  "completed": 0,
  "largest": 0,
  "queue": 0,
  "rejected": 0,
  "threads": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|number|false|none|Number of active threads in the thread pool.|
|completed|number|false|none|Number of tasks completed by the thread pool executor.|
|largest|number|false|none|Highest number of active threads in the thread pool.|
|queue|number|false|none|Number of tasks in queue for the thread pool.|
|rejected|number|false|none|Number of tasks rejected by the thread pool executor.|
|threads|number|false|none|Number of threads in the thread pool.|

<h2 id="tocS_nodes._types.Scripting">nodes._types.Scripting</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanodes._types.scripting"></a>
<a id="schema_nodes._types.Scripting"></a>
<a id="tocSnodes._types.scripting"></a>
<a id="tocsnodes._types.scripting"></a>

```json
{
  "cache_evictions": 0,
  "compilations": 0,
  "compilations_history": {
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "compilation_limit_triggered": 0,
  "contexts": [
    {
      "context": "string",
      "compilations": 0,
      "cache_evictions": 0,
      "compilation_limit_triggered": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cache_evictions|number|false|none|Total number of times the script cache has evicted old data.|
|compilations|number|false|none|Total number of inline script compilations performed by the node.|
|compilations_history|object|false|none|Contains this recent history of script compilations.|
|compilation_limit_triggered|number|false|none|Total number of times the script compilation circuit breaker has limited inline script compilations.|
|contexts|[[nodes._types.Context](#schemanodes._types.context)]|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_cluster.pending_tasks.PendingTask">cluster.pending_tasks.PendingTask</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacluster.pending_tasks.pendingtask"></a>
<a id="schema_cluster.pending_tasks.PendingTask"></a>
<a id="tocScluster.pending_tasks.pendingtask"></a>
<a id="tocscluster.pending_tasks.pendingtask"></a>

```json
{
  "executing": true,
  "insert_order": 0,
  "priority": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "time_in_queue": {},
  "time_in_queue_millis": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|executing|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the pending tasks are currently executing or not.|
|insert_order|number|true|none|The number that represents when the task has been inserted into the task queue.|
|priority|string|true|none|The priority of the pending task.<br>The valid priorities in descending priority order are: `IMMEDIATE` > `URGENT` > `HIGH` > `NORMAL` > `LOW` > `LANGUID`.|
|source|string|true|none|A general description of the cluster task that may include a reason and origin.|
|time_in_queue|object|false|none|The time since the task is waiting for being performed.|
|time_in_queue_millis|object|true|none|The time expressed in milliseconds since the task is waiting for being performed.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aliases|object|false|none|Aliases to add.<br>If the index template includes a `data_stream` object, these are data stream aliases.<br>Otherwise, these are index aliases.<br>Data stream aliases ignore the `index_routing`, `routing`, and `search_routing` options.|
|mappings|object|false|none|Mapping for fields in the index.<br>If specified, this mapping can include field names, field data types, and mapping parameters.|
|settings|object|false|none|Configuration options for the index.|
|lifecycle|object|false|none|none|
|data_stream_options|[indices._types.DataStreamOptionsTemplate](#schemaindices._types.datastreamoptionstemplate) \| string \| null|false|none|none|

|is_hidden|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the alias is hidden.<br>All indices for the alias must have the same `is_hidden` value.|
|is_write_index|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the index is the write index for the alias.|
|routing|string|false|none|Value used to route indexing and search operations to a specific shard.|
|search_routing|string|false|none|Value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>If specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for search operations.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.DataStreamOptionsTemplate">indices._types.DataStreamOptionsTemplate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.datastreamoptionstemplate"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.DataStreamOptionsTemplate"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.datastreamoptionstemplate"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.datastreamoptionstemplate"></a>

```json
{
  "failure_store": {
    "enabled": "true",
    "lifecycle": {
      "data_retention": "string",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Data stream options template contains the same information as DataStreamOptions but allows them to be set explicitly to null.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|failure_store|[indices._types.DataStreamFailureStoreTemplate](#schemaindices._types.datastreamfailurestoretemplate) \| string \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.DataStreamFailureStoreTemplate">indices._types.DataStreamFailureStoreTemplate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.datastreamfailurestoretemplate"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.DataStreamFailureStoreTemplate"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.datastreamfailurestoretemplate"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.datastreamfailurestoretemplate"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": "true",
  "lifecycle": {
    "data_retention": "string",
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

Template equivalent of DataStreamFailureStore that allows nullable values.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean \| string \| null|false|none|If defined, it turns the failure store on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream failure store<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will redirect no new failed indices to the failure store; however, it will<br>not remove any existing data from the failure store.|
|lifecycle|[indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycleTemplate](#schemaindices._types.failurestorelifecycletemplate) \| string \| null|false|none|If defined, it specifies the lifecycle configuration for the failure store of this data stream.|

<h2 id="tocS_indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycleTemplate">indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycleTemplate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices._types.failurestorelifecycletemplate"></a>
<a id="schema_indices._types.FailureStoreLifecycleTemplate"></a>
<a id="tocSindices._types.failurestorelifecycletemplate"></a>
<a id="tocsindices._types.failurestorelifecycletemplate"></a>

```json
{
  "data_retention": "string",
  "enabled": true
}
```

Template equivalent of FailureStoreLifecycle that allows nullable values.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_retention|[_types.Duration](#schema_types.duration) \| string \| null|false|none|If defined, every document added to this data stream will be stored at least for this time frame.<br>Any time after this duration the document could be deleted.<br>When empty, every document in this data stream will be stored indefinitely.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|If defined, it turns data stream lifecycle on/off (`true`/`false`) for this data stream. A data stream lifecycle<br>that's disabled (enabled: `false`) will have no effect on the data stream.|
