<h2 id="tocS_cluster.remote_info.ClusterRemoteSniffInfo">cluster.remote_info.ClusterRemoteSniffInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacluster.remote_info.clusterremotesniffinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_cluster.remote_info.ClusterRemoteSniffInfo"></a>
<a id="tocScluster.remote_info.clusterremotesniffinfo"></a>
<a id="tocscluster.remote_info.clusterremotesniffinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "sniff",
  "connected": true,
  "max_connections_per_cluster": 0,
  "num_nodes_connected": 0,
  "initial_connect_timeout": {},
  "skip_unavailable": true,
  "seeds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|The connection mode for the remote cluster.|
|connected|boolean|true|none|If it is `true`, there is at least one open connection to the remote cluster.<br>If it is `false`, it means that the cluster no longer has an open connection to the remote cluster.<br>It does not necessarily mean that the remote cluster is down or unavailable, just that at some point a connection was lost.|
|max_connections_per_cluster|number|true|none|The maximum number of connections maintained for the remote cluster when sniff mode is configured.|
|num_nodes_connected|number|true|none|The number of connected nodes in the remote cluster when sniff mode is configured.|
|initial_connect_timeout|object|true|none|The initial connect timeout for remote cluster connections.|
|skip_unavailable|boolean|true|none|If `true`, cross-cluster search skips the remote cluster when its nodes are unavailable during the search and ignores errors returned by the remote cluster.|
|seeds|[string]|true|none|The initial seed transport addresses of the remote cluster when sniff mode is configured.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|sniff|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|The connection mode for the remote cluster.|
|connected|boolean|true|none|If it is `true`, there is at least one open connection to the remote cluster.<br>If it is `false`, it means that the cluster no longer has an open connection to the remote cluster.<br>It does not necessarily mean that the remote cluster is down or unavailable, just that at some point a connection was lost.|
|initial_connect_timeout|object|true|none|The initial connect timeout for remote cluster connections.|
|skip_unavailable|boolean|true|none|If `true`, cross-cluster search skips the remote cluster when its nodes are unavailable during the search and ignores errors returned by the remote cluster.|
|proxy_address|string|true|none|The address for remote connections when proxy mode is configured.|
|server_name|string|true|none|none|
|num_proxy_sockets_connected|number|true|none|The number of open socket connections to the remote cluster when proxy mode is configured.|
|max_proxy_socket_connections|number|true|none|The maximum number of socket connections to the remote cluster when proxy mode is configured.|
|cluster_credentials|string|false|none|This field is present and has a value of `::es_redacted::` only when the remote cluster is configured with the API key based model. Otherwise, the field is not present.|

|---|---|

<h2 id="tocS_cluster.reroute.Command">cluster.reroute.Command</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacluster.reroute.command"></a>
<a id="schema_cluster.reroute.Command"></a>
<a id="tocScluster.reroute.command"></a>
<a id="tocscluster.reroute.command"></a>

```json
{
  "cancel": {
    "index": {},
    "shard": 0,
    "node": "string",
    "allow_primary": true
  },
  "move": {
    "index": {},
    "shard": 0,
    "from_node": "string",
    "to_node": "string"
  },
  "allocate_replica": {
    "index": {},
    "shard": 0,
    "node": "string"
  },
  "allocate_stale_primary": {
    "index": {},
    "shard": 0,
    "node": "string",
    "accept_data_loss": true
  },
  "allocate_empty_primary": {
    "index": {},
    "shard": 0,
    "node": "string",
    "accept_data_loss": true
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cancel|object|false|none|Cancel allocation of a shard (or recovery). Accepts index and shard for index name and shard number, and node for the node to cancel the shard allocation on. This can be used to force resynchronization of existing replicas from the primary shard by cancelling them and allowing them to be reinitialized through the standard recovery process. By default only replica shard allocations can be cancelled. If it is necessary to cancel the allocation of a primary shard then the allow_primary flag must also be included in the request.|
|move|object|false|none|Move a started shard from one node to another node. Accepts index and shard for index name and shard number, from_node for the node to move the shard from, and to_node for the node to move the shard to.|
|allocate_replica|object|false|none|Allocate an unassigned replica shard to a node. Accepts index and shard for index name and shard number, and node to allocate the shard to. Takes allocation deciders into account.|
|allocate_stale_primary|object|false|none|Allocate a primary shard to a node that holds a stale copy. Accepts the index and shard for index name and shard number, and node to allocate the shard to. Using this command may lead to data loss for the provided shard id. If a node which has the good copy of the data rejoins the cluster later on, that data will be deleted or overwritten with the data of the stale copy that was forcefully allocated with this command. To ensure that these implications are well-understood, this command requires the flag accept_data_loss to be explicitly set to true.|
|allocate_empty_primary|object|false|none|Allocate an empty primary shard to a node. Accepts the index and shard for index name and shard number, and node to allocate the shard to. Using this command leads to a complete loss of all data that was indexed into this shard, if it was previously started. If a node which has a copy of the data rejoins the cluster later on, that data will be deleted. To ensure that these implications are well-understood, this command requires the flag accept_data_loss to be explicitly set to true.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_nodes|object|false|none|Contains statistics about the number of nodes selected by the request’s node filters.|
|cluster_name|object|true|none|Name of the cluster, based on the cluster name setting.|
|cluster_uuid|object|true|none|Unique identifier for the cluster.|
|indices|object|true|none|Contains statistics about indices with shards assigned to selected nodes.|
|nodes|object|true|none|Contains statistics about nodes selected by the request’s node filters.|
|repositories|object|true|none|Contains stats on repository feature usage exposed in cluster stats for telemetry.|
|snapshots|object|true|none|Contains stats cluster snapshots.|
|status|object|false|none|Health status of the cluster, based on the state of its primary and replica shards.|
|timestamp|number|true|none|Unix timestamp, in milliseconds, for the last time the cluster statistics were refreshed.|
|ccs|object|true|none|Cross-cluster stats|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|analysis|object|false|none|Contains statistics about analyzers and analyzer components used in selected nodes.|
|completion|object|true|none|Contains statistics about memory used for completion in selected nodes.|
|count|number|true|none|Total number of indices with shards assigned to selected nodes.|
|docs|object|true|none|Contains counts for documents in selected nodes.|
|fielddata|object|true|none|Contains statistics about the field data cache of selected nodes.|
|query_cache|object|true|none|Contains statistics about the query cache of selected nodes.|
|search|object|true|none|Holds a snapshot of the search usage statistics.<br>Used to hold the stats for a single node that's part of a ClusterStatsNodeResponse, as well as to<br>accumulate stats for the entire cluster and return them as part of the ClusterStatsResponse.|
|segments|object|true|none|Contains statistics about segments in selected nodes.|
|shards|object|true|none|Contains statistics about indices with shards assigned to selected nodes.|
|store|object|true|none|Contains statistics about the size of shards assigned to selected nodes.|
|mappings|object|false|none|Contains statistics about field mappings in selected nodes.|
|versions|[[cluster.stats.IndicesVersions](#schemacluster.stats.indicesversions)]|false|none|Contains statistics about analyzers and analyzer components used in selected nodes.|
|dense_vector|object|true|none|Contains statistics about indexed dense vector|
|sparse_vector|object|true|none|Contains statistics about indexed sparse vector|

```json
{
```
```json
  "cluster_uuid": "string",
  "mode": "string",
  "skip_unavailable": true,
  "transport.compress": "string",
  "status": {},
  "version": [
    "string"
  ],
  "nodes_count": 0,
  "shards_count": 0,
  "indices_count": 0,
  "indices_total_size_in_bytes": 0,
  "indices_total_size": "string",

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_uuid|string|true|none|The UUID of the remote cluster.|
|mode|string|true|none|The connection mode used to communicate with the remote cluster.|
|skip_unavailable|boolean|true|none|The `skip_unavailable` setting used for this remote cluster.|
|transport.compress|string|true|none|Transport compression setting used for this remote cluster.|
|status|object|true|none|Health status of the cluster, based on the state of its primary and replica shards.|
|version|[[_types.VersionString](#schema_types.versionstring)]|true|none|The list of Elasticsearch versions used by the nodes on the remote cluster.|
|nodes_count|number|true|none|The total count of nodes in the remote cluster.|
|shards_count|number|true|none|The total number of shards in the remote cluster.|
|indices_count|number|true|none|The total number of indices in the remote cluster.|
|indices_total_size_in_bytes|number|true|none|Total data set size, in bytes, of all shards assigned to selected nodes.|
|indices_total_size|string|false|none|Total data set size of all shards assigned to selected nodes, as a human-readable string.|
|max_heap_in_bytes|number|true|none|Maximum amount of memory, in bytes, available for use by the heap across the nodes of the remote cluster.|
|max_heap|string|false|none|Maximum amount of memory available for use by the heap across the nodes of the remote cluster, as a human-readable string.|
|mem_total_in_bytes|number|true|none|Total amount, in bytes, of physical memory across the nodes of the remote cluster.|
|mem_total|string|false|none|Total amount of physical memory across the nodes of the remote cluster, as a human-readable string.|

```json
        "avg": {},
        "p90": {}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total|number|true|none|The total number of cross-cluster search requests that have been executed by the cluster.|
|success|number|true|none|The total number of cross-cluster search requests that have been successfully executed by the cluster.|
|skipped|number|true|none|The total number of cross-cluster search requests (successful or failed) that had at least one remote cluster skipped.|
|took|object|true|none|Statistics about the time taken to execute cross-cluster search requests.|
|took_mrt_true|object|false|none|Statistics about the time taken to execute cross-cluster search requests for which the `ccs_minimize_roundtrips` setting was set to `true`.|
|took_mrt_false|object|false|none|Statistics about the time taken to execute cross-cluster search requests for which the `ccs_minimize_roundtrips` setting was set to `false`.|
|remotes_per_search_max|number|true|none|The maximum number of remote clusters that were queried in a single cross-cluster search request.|
|remotes_per_search_avg|number|true|none|The average number of remote clusters that were queried in a single cross-cluster search request.|
|failure_reasons|object|true|none|Statistics about the reasons for cross-cluster search request failures. The keys are the failure reason names and the values are the number of requests that failed for that reason.|
|features|object|true|none|The keys are the names of the search feature, and the values are the number of requests that used that feature. Single request can use more than one feature (e.g. both `async` and `wildcard`).|
|clients|object|true|none|Statistics about the clients that executed cross-cluster search requests. The keys are the names of the clients, and the values are the number of requests that were executed by that client. Only known clients (such as `kibana` or `elasticsearch`) are counted.|
|clusters|object|true|none|Statistics about the clusters that were queried in cross-cluster search requests. The keys are cluster names, and the values are per-cluster telemetry data. This also includes the local cluster itself, which uses the name `(local)`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|cancelled|boolean|false|none|none|
|cancellable|boolean|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|Human readable text that identifies the particular request that the task is performing.<br>For example, it might identify the search request being performed by a search task.<br>Other kinds of tasks have different descriptions, like `_reindex` which has the source and the destination, or `_bulk` which just has the number of requests and the destination indices.<br>Many requests will have only an empty description because more detailed information about the request is not easily available or particularly helpful in identifying the request.|
|headers|object|true|none|none|
|id|number|true|none|none|
|node|object|true|none|none|
|running_time|object|false|none|none|
|running_time_in_nanos|object|true|none|none|
|start_time_in_millis|object|true|none|none|
|status|object|false|none|The internal status of the task, which varies from task to task.<br>The format also varies.<br>While the goal is to keep the status for a particular task consistent from version to version, this is not always possible because sometimes the implementation changes.<br>Fields might be removed from the status for a particular request so any parsing you do of the status might break in minor releases.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|parent_task_id|object|false|none|none|
|original_task_id|object|false|none|The task ID of the original task. Only present when the task is continuing the work of an earlier task that was running on a node which has since shut down (i.e. a relocatable task).<br>For tasks that have not been relocated this is always equal to the task's own ID and is omitted from the response.|
|original_start_time_in_millis|object|false|none|The time at which the original task started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Only present together with `original_task_id`.|
|original_start_time|string|false|none|The time at which the original task started, as an ISO 8601 formatted string. Only present together with `original_task_id` and when the request includes the `?human=true` query parameter.|

Per-query settings supplied through the request body.
This is the request-body equivalent of the in-query `SET` command.
Only settings that are exposed as request-body parameters can be set here; other `SET`-only
settings (such as `unmapped_fields`) must be supplied in the query itself.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|time_zone|string|false|none|The default timezone to be used in the query.<br>It defaults to UTC and overrides the `time_zone` request parameter.|
|approximation|object|false|none|Enables query approximation if possible for the query.<br>`false` (the default) disables query approximation and `true` enables it with default settings.<br>A map value enables query approximation with custom settings.|
|column_metadata|object|false|none|When enabled, column metadata is added to the query response as additional `_meta` properties.<br>Currently, only `_meta.bucket` is added for columns corresponding to the `BUCKET` function, containing the bucket interval and unit for queries where it can be determined.|

```json
        "format": "string"
      },

      }
    },

      "path": "string"

  }
```

Represents a dataset definition stored in cluster state. A dataset is a named reference
to external data that participates in the index namespace alongside indices, aliases, and views.
Datasets inherit credentials from their referenced data source at query time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|object|true|none|The dataset name.|
|data_source|object|true|none|The name of the referenced data source.|
|resource|string|true|none|The URI that identifies the data to read, resolved against the referenced data source.<br>It can include glob patterns, for example a recursive pattern that matches<br>Parquet files under `s3://logs-bucket/access`.|
|description|string|false|none|A free-text description.|
|settings|object|false|none|Format- and parsing-specific settings that configure how the resource is read.<br>Common keys include `format` and `partition_detection`. Additional keys depend on the format reader;<br>compression can be inferred from the resource URI.|
|mappings|object|false|none|The user-declared mapping on the dataset definition.|

```json
      "type": "string",
```

A user-declared mapping (the `mappings` block) attached to a dataset.
It is entirely optional: a dataset with no declared mapping relies on inference.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dynamic|object|false|none|The policy for columns that are not declared in `properties`.<br>`true` (the default) infers undeclared columns and overlays the declarations; `false` makes the declaration the entire schema, so undeclared columns are not queryable.|
|properties|object|false|none|The per-column declarations, keyed by logical column name.|
|_id|object|false|none|The `_id` meta-field configuration, sourcing the document identity from a column.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregatable|boolean|true|none|Whether this field can be aggregated on all indices.|
|indices|object|false|none|The list of indices where this field has the same type family, or null if all indices have the same type family for the field.|
|meta|object|false|none|Merged metadata across all indices as a map of string keys to arrays of values. A value length of 1 indicates that all indices had the same value for this key, while a length of 2 or more indicates that not all indices had the same value for this key.|
|non_aggregatable_indices|object|false|none|The list of indices where this field is not aggregatable, or null if all indices have the same definition for the field.|
|non_searchable_indices|object|false|none|The list of indices where this field is not searchable, or null if all indices have the same definition for the field.|
|searchable|boolean|true|none|Whether this field is indexed for search on all indices.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|inference|boolean|false|none|Whether this field is an inference field, meaning a field that automatically performs inference (for example, `semantic_text` fields), on all indices.|
|non_inference_indices|object|false|none|The list of indices where this field is not an inference field, or null if all indices have the same definition for the field.|
|passthrough|boolean|false|none|Whether this field is a passthrough source on all indices.<br>This property is present only for field types that support passthrough.|
|non_passthrough_indices|object|false|none|The list of indices where this field is not a passthrough source, or null if all indices have the same definition for the field.|
|metadata_field|boolean|false|none|Whether this field is registered as a metadata field.|
|time_series_dimension|boolean|false|none|Whether this field is used as a time series dimension.|
|time_series_metric|object|false|none|Contains metric type if this fields is used as a time series<br>metrics, absent if the field is not used as metric.|
|non_dimension_indices|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|If this list is present in response then some indices have the<br>field marked as a dimension and other indices, the ones in this list, do not.|
|metric_conflicts_indices|[[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|false|none|The list of indices where this field is present if these indices<br>don’t have the same `time_series_metric` value for this field.|

Contains parameters used to limit or change the subsequent search body request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|boolean|false|none|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|object|false|none|none|
|ignore_unavailable|boolean|false|none|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|index|object|false|none|none|
|preference|string|false|none|none|
|project_routing|object|false|none|none|
|request_cache|boolean|false|none|none|
|routing|object|false|none|A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the target index; use `_slice` instead.|
|search_type|object|false|none|none|
|ccs_minimize_roundtrips|boolean|false|none|none|
|allow_partial_search_results|boolean|false|none|none|
|ignore_throttled|boolean|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_index|object|true|none|The name of the index the document belongs to.|

|_ignored|[string]|false|none|none|
|found|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the document exists.|
|_id|object|true|none|The unique identifier for the document.|
|_primary_term|number|false|none|The primary term assigned to the document for the indexing operation.|
|_routing|string|false|none|The explicit routing, if set.|
|_seq_no|object|false|none|The sequence number assigned to the document for the indexing operation.<br>Sequence numbers are used to ensure an older version of a document doesn't overwrite a newer version.|
|_source|object|false|none|If `found` is `true`, it contains the document data formatted in JSON.<br>If the `_source` parameter is set to `false` or the `stored_fields` parameter is set to `true`, it is excluded.|
|_version|object|false|none|The document version, which is ncremented each time the document is updated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exclude|[string]|false|none|Prevents the specified terms from being included in the results.|
|field|object|true|none|Identifies a field in the documents of interest.|
|include|[[graph._types.VertexInclude](#schemagraph._types.vertexinclude)]|false|none|Identifies the terms of interest that form the starting points from which you want to spider out.|
|min_doc_count|number|false|none|Specifies how many documents must contain a pair of terms before it is considered to be a useful connection.<br>This setting acts as a certainty threshold.|
|shard_min_doc_count|number|false|none|Controls how many documents on a particular shard have to contain a pair of terms before the connection is returned for global consideration.|
|size|number|false|none|Specifies the maximum number of vertex terms returned for each field.|

```json
{
  "sample_diversity": {
    "field": {},
    "max_docs_per_value": 0
  },
  "sample_size": 100,
  "timeout": {},
  "use_significance": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sample_diversity|object|false|none|To avoid the top-matching documents sample being dominated by a single source of results, it is sometimes necessary to request diversity in the sample.<br>You can do this by selecting a single-value field and setting a maximum number of documents per value for that field.|
|sample_size|number|false|none|Each hop considers a sample of the best-matching documents on each shard.<br>Using samples improves the speed of execution and keeps exploration focused on meaningfully-connected terms.<br>Very small values (less than 50) might not provide sufficient weight-of-evidence to identify significant connections between terms.<br>Very large sample sizes can dilute the quality of the results and increase execution times.|
|timeout|object|false|none|The length of time in milliseconds after which exploration will be halted and the results gathered so far are returned.<br>This timeout is honored on a best-effort basis.<br>Execution might overrun this timeout if, for example, a long pause is encountered while FieldData is loaded for a field.|
|use_significance|boolean|true|none|Filters associated terms so only those that are significantly associated with your query are included.|

<h2 id="tocS__global.health_report.DlmFrozenTransitionsIndicatorDetails">_global.health_report.DlmFrozenTransitionsIndicatorDetails</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_global.health_report.dlmfrozentransitionsindicatordetails"></a>
<a id="schema__global.health_report.DlmFrozenTransitionsIndicatorDetails"></a>
<a id="tocS_global.health_report.dlmfrozentransitionsindicatordetails"></a>
<a id="tocs_global.health_report.dlmfrozentransitionsindicatordetails"></a>

```json
{
  "transitions_enabled": true,
  "service_running": true,
  "default_repository_configured": true,
  "overdue_indices_count": 0,
  "overdue_indices_count_by_state": {
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "overdue_indices_sample": [
    {
      "index_name": {},
      "transition_state": {}
    }
  ],
  "generated_at_millis": 0
}
```

An index is overdue when it has passed its `frozen_after` age by more than the configured threshold and has not yet completed its transition to the frozen tier.
Indices with a running transition are making progress and are not counted as overdue.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transitions_enabled|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether frozen-tier transitions are enabled by the `dlm.frozen_transitions.enabled` cluster setting.|
|service_running|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the frozen transition service is running on the current master node.|
|default_repository_configured|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether a default snapshot repository is configured with the `repositories.default_repository` cluster setting.|
|overdue_indices_count|number|false|none|The total number of overdue indices in the cluster.|
|overdue_indices_count_by_state|object|false|none|The number of overdue indices in the cluster for each transition state.<br>Only present when there are overdue indices.|
|overdue_indices_sample|[[_global.health_report.DlmFrozenTransitionOverdueIndex](#schema_global.health_report.dlmfrozentransitionoverdueindex)]|false|none|A sample of the overdue indices and their transition states, sorted by index name.<br>The sample is limited to 100 indices for each transition state, so it can contain fewer indices than `overdue_indices_count`.<br>Only present when there are overdue indices.|
|generated_at_millis|number|false|none|The time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, when the master node generated the health snapshot.<br>Only present when the indicator status is `unknown`, meaning the health snapshot is stale.|

|store_size|object|false|none|Total size of all shards for the data stream’s backing indices.<br>This parameter is only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|store_size_bytes|number|true|none|Total size, in bytes, of all shards for the data stream’s backing indices.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_meta|object|false|none|Custom metadata for the stream, copied from the `_meta` object of the stream’s matching index template.<br>If empty, the response omits this property.|
|allow_custom_routing|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the data stream allows custom routing on write request.|
|failure_store|object|false|none|Information about failure store backing indices|
|generation|number|true|none|Current generation for the data stream. This number acts as a cumulative count of the stream’s rollovers, starting at 1.|
|hidden|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the data stream is hidden.|
|ilm_policy|object|false|none|Name of the current ILM lifecycle policy in the stream’s matching index template.<br>This lifecycle policy is set in the `index.lifecycle.name` setting.<br>If the template does not include a lifecycle policy, this property is not included in the response.<br>NOTE: A data stream’s backing indices may be assigned different lifecycle policies. To retrieve the lifecycle policy for individual backing indices, use the get index settings API.|
|next_generation_managed_by|object|true|none|Name of the lifecycle system that'll manage the next generation of the data stream.|
|prefer_ilm|boolean|true|none|Indicates if ILM should take precedence over DSL in case both are configured to managed this data stream.|
|indices|[[indices._types.DataStreamIndex](#schemaindices._types.datastreamindex)]|true|none|Array of objects containing information about the data stream’s backing indices.<br>The last item in this array contains information about the stream’s current write index.|
|lifecycle|object|false|none|Contains the configuration for the data stream lifecycle of this data stream.|
|name|object|true|none|Name of the data stream.|
|replicated|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the data stream is created and managed by cross-cluster replication and the local cluster can not write into this data stream or change its mappings.|
|rollover_on_write|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the next write to this data stream will trigger a rollover first and the document will be indexed in the new backing index. If the rollover fails the indexing request will fail too.|
|settings|object|true|none|The settings specific to this data stream that will take precedence over the settings in the matching index<br>template.|
|mappings|object|false|none|The mappings specific to this data stream that will take precedence over the mappings in the matching index<br>template.|
|status|object|true|none|Health status of the data stream.<br>This health status is based on the state of the primary and replica shards of the stream’s backing indices.|
|system|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the data stream is created and managed by an Elastic stack component and cannot be modified through normal user interaction.|
|template|object|true|none|Name of the index template used to create the data stream’s backing indices.<br>The template’s index pattern must match the name of this data stream.|
|timestamp_field|object|true|none|Information about the `@timestamp` field in the data stream.|
|index_mode|object|false|none|The index mode for the data stream that will be used for newly created backing indices.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|template|object|false|none|Template to be applied.<br>It may optionally include an `aliases`, `mappings`, or `settings` configuration.|
|index_patterns|object|true|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) expressions used to match the names of data streams and indices during creation.|
|composed_of|[[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)]|true|none|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|version|object|false|none|Version number used to manage index templates externally.<br>This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|priority|number|false|none|Priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|_meta|object|false|none|Optional user metadata about the index template. May have any contents.<br>This map is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|allow_auto_create|boolean|false|none|none|
|data_stream|object|false|none|If this object is included, the template is used to create data streams and their backing indices.<br>Supports an empty object.<br>Data streams require a matching index template with a `data_stream` object.|
|deprecated|boolean|false|none|Marks this index template as deprecated.<br>When creating or updating a non-deprecated index template that uses deprecated components,<br>Elasticsearch will emit a deprecation warning.|
|ignore_missing_component_templates|object|false|none|A list of component template names that are allowed to be absent.|
|created_date|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was created. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|created_date_millis|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was created, in milliseconds since the epoch.|
|modified_date|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was last modified. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|modified_date_millis|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was last modified, in milliseconds since the epoch.|

|mappings|object|false|none|Mapping for fields in the index.<br>If specified, this mapping can include field names, field data types, and mapping parameters.|
|settings|object|false|none|Configuration options for the index.|
|data_stream_options|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_indices.modify_data_stream.Action">indices.modify_data_stream.Action</h2>

<a id="tocSindices.modify_data_stream.action"></a>
<a id="tocsindices.modify_data_stream.action"></a>

```json
{
  "add_backing_index": {
    "data_stream": {},
    "index": {}
  },
  "remove_backing_index": {
    "data_stream": {},
    "index": {}
  },
  "delete_backing_index": {
    "data_stream": {},
    "index": {}
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_backing_index|object|false|none|Adds an existing index as a backing index for a data stream.<br>The index is hidden as part of this operation.<br>WARNING: Adding indices with the `add_backing_index` action can potentially result in improper data stream behavior.<br>This should be considered an expert level API.|
|remove_backing_index|object|false|none|Removes a backing index from a data stream.<br>The index is unhidden as part of this operation.<br>A data stream’s write index cannot be removed.|
|delete_backing_index|object|false|none|Deletes a backing index from a data stream.<br>A data stream’s write index cannot be deleted because it is the write index.|

|mappings|object|false|none|The mappings that are specfic to this data stream that will override any mappings from the matching index template.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|object|true|none|The data stream name.|
|applied_to_data_stream|boolean|true|none|If the settings were successfully applied to the data stream (or would have been, if running in `dry_run`<br>mode), it is `true`. If an error occurred, it is `false`.|
|error|string|false|none|A message explaining why the settings could not be applied to the data stream.|
|settings|object|true|none|The settings that are specfic to this data stream that will override any settings from the matching index template.|
|effective_settings|object|true|none|The settings that are effective on this data stream, taking into account the settings from the matching index<br>template and the settings specific to this data stream.|
|index_settings_results|object|true|none|Information about whether and where each setting was applied.|

|applied_to_data_stream_and_backing_indices|[string]|true|none|The list of settings that were applied to the data stream and to all of its backing indices. These settings will<br>also be applied to the write index the next time the data stream is rolled over.|

|priority|object|false|none|The recovery priority.|
|gate|string|false|none|The name of the recovery gate that blocked recovery on the target node.<br><br>Only present for queued recoveries in the `CREATED` stage that are blocked by a recovery gate.|
|blocked_for_millis|object|false|none|The elapsed time in milliseconds recovery is blocked for.<br><br>Only present with `gate`.|
|start|object|false|none|none|
|start_time|object|false|none|The time the recovery started.<br>For recoveries in the `CREATED` stage (not yet started), this value is the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z).|
|start_time_in_millis|object|true|none|The time the recovery started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.<br>For recoveries in the `CREATED` stage (not yet started), this value is 0.|
|stop_time|object|false|none|The time the recovery completed. Only present for completed recoveries (`DONE` stage).|
|stop_time_in_millis|object|false|none|The time the recovery completed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.<br>Only present for completed recoveries (`DONE` stage).|
|target|object|true|none|none|
|total_time|object|false|none|none|
|total_time_in_millis|object|true|none|The total elapsed recovery time in milliseconds.<br>For recoveries in the `CREATED` stage (not yet started), this value is 0.|
|translog|object|true|none|none|
|type|object|true|none|The recovery source type.|
|verify_index|object|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_indices.resolve_cluster.ResolveClusterInfo">indices.resolve_cluster.ResolveClusterInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindices.resolve_cluster.resolveclusterinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_indices.resolve_cluster.ResolveClusterInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSindices.resolve_cluster.resolveclusterinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsindices.resolve_cluster.resolveclusterinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "connected": true,
  "skip_unavailable": true,
  "matching_indices": true,
  "error": "string",
  "version": {
    "build_flavor": "string",
    "minimum_index_compatibility_version": {},
    "minimum_wire_compatibility_version": {},
    "number": "string"
  }
}
```

Provides information about each cluster request relevant to doing a cross-cluster search.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connected|boolean|true|none|Whether the remote cluster is connected to the local (querying) cluster.|
|skip_unavailable|boolean|true|none|The `skip_unavailable` setting for a remote cluster.|
|matching_indices|boolean|false|none|Whether the index expression provided in the request matches any indices, aliases or data streams<br>on the cluster.|
|error|string|false|none|Provides error messages that are likely to occur if you do a search with this index expression<br>on the specified cluster (for example, lack of security privileges to query an index).|
|version|object|false|none|Provides version information about the cluster.|

<a id="schemaindices.segments.segment"></a>
<a id="schema_indices.segments.Segment"></a>
<a id="tocSindices.segments.segment"></a>
<a id="tocsindices.segments.segment"></a>

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "committed": true,
  "compound": true,
  "deleted_docs": 0,
  "generation": 0,
  "search": true,
  "size_in_bytes": 0,
  "num_docs": 0,
  "version": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attributes|object|true|none|Contains information about whether high compression was enabled and per-field vector formats.|
|committed|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the segment is synced to disk. Segments that are synced can survive a hard reboot.<br>If `false`, the data from uncommitted segments is also stored in the transaction log so that Elasticsearch is able to replay changes on the next start.|
|compound|boolean|true|none|If `true`, Lucene merged all files from the segment into a single file to save file descriptors.|
|deleted_docs|number|true|none|The number of deleted documents as reported by Lucene, which may be higher or lower than the number of delete operations you have performed.<br>This number excludes deletes that were performed recently and do not yet belong to a segment.<br>Deleted documents are cleaned up by the automatic merge process if it makes sense to do so.<br>Also, Elasticsearch creates extra deleted documents to internally track the recent history of operations on a shard.|
|generation|number|true|none|Generation number, such as `0`. Elasticsearch increments this generation number for each segment written then uses this number to derive the segment name.|
|search|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the segment is searchable.<br>If `false`, the segment has most likely been written to disk but needs a refresh to be searchable.|
|size_in_bytes|number|true|none|Disk space used by the segment, in bytes.|
|num_docs|number|true|none|The number of documents as reported by Lucene.<br>This excludes deleted documents and counts any nested documents separately from their parents.<br>It also excludes documents which were indexed recently and do not yet belong to a segment.|
|version|object|true|none|Version of Lucene used to write the segment.|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index_patterns|object|true|none|Array of wildcard (`*`) expressions used to match the names of data streams and indices during creation.|
|composed_of|[[_types.Name](#schema_types.name)]|true|none|An ordered list of component template names.<br>Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.|
|template|object|false|none|Template to be applied.<br>It may optionally include an `aliases`, `mappings`, or `settings` configuration.|
|version|object|false|none|Version number used to manage index templates externally.<br>This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|priority|number|false|none|Priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.<br>The index template with the highest priority is chosen.<br>If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).<br>This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|_meta|object|false|none|Optional user metadata about the index template. May have any contents.<br>This map is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.|
|allow_auto_create|boolean|false|none|none|
|data_stream|object|false|none|If this object is included, the template is used to create data streams and their backing indices.<br>Supports an empty object.<br>Data streams require a matching index template with a `data_stream` object.|
|deprecated|boolean|false|none|Marks this index template as deprecated.<br>When creating or updating a non-deprecated index template that uses deprecated components,<br>Elasticsearch will emit a deprecation warning.|
|ignore_missing_component_templates|object|false|none|A list of component template names that are allowed to be absent.|
|created_date|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was created. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|created_date_millis|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was created, in milliseconds since the epoch.|
|modified_date|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was last modified. Only returned if the `human` query parameter is `true`.|
|modified_date_millis|object|false|none|Date and time when the index template was last modified, in milliseconds since the epoch.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aliases|object|false|none|Aliases to add.<br>If the index template includes a `data_stream` object, these are data stream aliases.<br>Otherwise, these are index aliases.<br>Data stream aliases ignore the `index_routing`, `routing`, and `search_routing` options.|
|mappings|object|false|none|Mapping for fields in the index.<br>If specified, this mapping can include field names, field data types, and mapping parameters.|
|settings|object|false|none|Configuration options for the index.|
|lifecycle|object|false|none|none|
|data_stream_options|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alias|object|false|none|Alias for the action.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|aliases|[_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias) \| [[_types.IndexAlias](#schema_types.indexalias)]|false|none|Aliases for the action.<br>Index alias names support date math.|
|filter|object|false|none|Query used to limit documents the alias can access.|
|index|object|false|none|Data stream or index for the action.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>Wildcard patterns that match both data streams and indices return an error.|
|indices|object|false|none|Data streams or indices for the action.<br>Supports wildcards (`*`).<br>Wildcard patterns that match both data streams and indices return an error.|
|index_routing|string|false|none|Value used to route indexing operations to a specific shard.<br>If specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for indexing operations.<br>Data stream aliases don’t support this parameter.|
|is_hidden|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the alias is hidden.|
|is_write_index|boolean|false|none|If `true`, sets the write index or data stream for the alias.|
|routing|string|false|none|Value used to route indexing and search operations to a specific shard.<br>Data stream aliases don’t support this parameter.|
|search_routing|string|false|none|Value used to route search operations to a specific shard.<br>If specified, this overwrites the `routing` value for search operations.<br>Data stream aliases don’t support this parameter.|
|must_exist|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the alias must exist to perform the action.|

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "content": {},
      "role": "string",
      "tool_call_id": {},
      "tool_calls": [
        {
          "id": {},
          "function": {
            "arguments": "string",
            "name": "string"
          },
          "type": "string"
        }
      ],
      "reasoning": "string",

        {
          "format": "string",
          "id": "string",
          "index": 0,
          "type": "reasoning.encrypted",
          "data": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "model": "string",
  "max_completion_tokens": 0,
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": {},
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude": true,
    "summary": {}
  },
  "stop": [
    "string"
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "tool_choice": {},
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "function": {
        "description": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "parameters": {},
        "strict": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "top_p": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[inference._types.Message](#schemainference._types.message)]|true|none|A list of objects representing the conversation.<br>Requests should generally only add new messages from the user (role `user`).<br>The other message roles (`assistant`, `system`, or `tool`) should generally only be copied from the response to a previous completion request, such that the messages array is built up throughout a conversation.|
|model|string|false|none|The ID of the model to use. By default, the model ID is set to the value included when creating the inference endpoint.|
|max_completion_tokens|number|false|none|The upper bound limit for the number of tokens that can be generated for a completion request.|
|reasoning|object|false|none|The reasoning configuration for the completion request.<br>This controls the model's reasoning process in one of two ways:<br><br>* By specifying the model’s reasoning effort level with the `effort` field.<br>* By enabling reasoning with default settings by setting `enabled` field to `true`.<br><br>It also includes optional settings to control:<br><br>* The level of detail in the summary returned in the response with the `summary` field.<br>* Whether reasoning details are included in the response at all with the `exclude` field.<br><br>Example (effort):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "effort": "high",<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Example (enabled):<br>```<br>{<br>   "reasoning": {<br>       "enabled": true,<br>       "summary": "concise",<br>       "exclude": false<br>   }<br>}<br>```<br>Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.|
|stop|[string]|false|none|A sequence of strings to control when the model should stop generating additional tokens.|
|temperature|number|false|none|The sampling temperature to use.|
|tool_choice|object|false|none|Controls which tool is called by the model.<br>String representation: One of `auto`, `none`, or `requrired`. `auto` allows the model to choose between calling tools and generating a message. `none` causes the model to not call any tools. `required` forces the model to call one or more tools.<br>Example (object representation):<br>```<br>{<br>  "tool_choice": {<br>      "type": "function",<br>      "function": {<br>          "name": "get_current_weather"<br>      }<br>  }<br>}<br>```|
|tools|[[inference._types.CompletionTool](#schemainference._types.completiontool)]|false|none|A list of tools that the model can call.<br>Example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>      {<br>          "type": "function",<br>          "function": {<br>              "name": "get_price_of_item",<br>              "description": "Get the current price of an item",<br>              "parameters": {<br>                  "type": "object",<br>                  "properties": {<br>                      "item": {<br>                          "id": "12345"<br>                      },<br>                      "unit": {<br>                          "type": "currency"<br>                      }<br>                  }<br>              }<br>          }<br>      }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```|
|top_p|number|false|none|Nucleus sampling, an alternative to sampling with temperature.|

```json
  ]
```

An object representing part of the conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content|object|false|none|The content of the message.<br><br>String example:<br>```<br>{<br>   "content": "Some string"<br>}<br>```<br><br>Text example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "content": [<br>      {<br>       "text": "Some text",<br>       "type": "text"<br>      }<br>   ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>Image example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "content": [<br>      {<br>       "image_url": {<br>         "url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>       },<br>       "type": "image_url"<br>      }<br>   ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>File example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "content": [<br>      {<br>       "file": {<br>         "file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,...",<br>         "filename": "somePDF"<br>       },<br>       "type": "file"<br>      }<br>   ]<br>}<br>```|
|role|string|true|none|The role of the message author. Valid values are `user`, `assistant`, `system`, and `tool`.|
|tool_call_id|object|false|none|Only for `tool` role messages. The tool call that this message is responding to.|
|tool_calls|[[inference._types.ToolCall](#schemainference._types.toolcall)]|false|none|Only for `assistant` role messages. The tool calls generated by the model. If it's specified, the `content` field is optional.<br>Example:<br>```<br>{<br>  "tool_calls": [<br>      {<br>          "id": "call_KcAjWtAww20AihPHphUh46Gd",<br>          "type": "function",<br>          "function": {<br>              "name": "get_current_weather",<br>              "arguments": "{\"location\":\"Boston, MA\"}"<br>          }<br>      }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```|
|reasoning|string|false|none|Only for `assistant` role messages. The reasoning details generated by the model as plaintext.<br>Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.|
|reasoning_details|[[inference._types.ReasoningDetail](#schemainference._types.reasoningdetail)]|false|none|Only for `assistant` role messages. The reasoning details generated by the model as structured data.<br>Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.|

The reasoning configuration to use for the completion request.
Currently supported only for `elastic` provider.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|effort|object|false|none|The level of effort the model should put into reasoning.<br>This is a hint that guides the model in how much effort to put into reasoning,<br>with `xhigh` being the most effort and `none` being no effort.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable reasoning with default settings.<br>This is a shortcut for enabling reasoning without having to specify the other parameters.<br>If `enabled` is set to `true`, then reasoning at the `medium` effort level is enabled.<br>Ignored if `effort` is specified,<br>in which case that parameter will control the reasoning process instead.|
|exclude|boolean|false|none|Whether to exclude reasoning information from the response.<br>If `true`, the response will not include any reasoning details.|
|summary|object|false|none|The level of detail included in the reasoning summary returned in the response.<br>This is a hint on how much detail to include in the summary of the reasoning that is returned in the response,<br>with `auto` being the default level of detail, `concise` being less detail, and `detailed` being more detail.|

<h2 id="tocS_inference._types.RequestEmbedding">inference._types.RequestEmbedding</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference._types.requestembedding"></a>
<a id="schema_inference._types.RequestEmbedding"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.requestembedding"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.requestembedding"></a>

```json
{
  "input": {},
  "input_type": "string",
  "task_settings": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input|object|true|none|Inference input.<br>Either a string, an array of strings, a `content` object, or an array of `content` objects.<br>`content` objects may contain a single item or an array of items. Models that support multiple items per `content`<br>object will return a single embedding for each `content` object, regardless of how many items it contains.<br>Support for multiple items in a single `content` object is available in Elasticsearch 9.5.0 and later.<br><br>string example:<br>```<br>"input": "Some text"<br>```<br>string array example:<br>```<br>"input": ["Some text", "Some more text"]<br>```<br>`content` object example:<br>```<br>"input": {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "base64",<br>      "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>    }<br>  }<br>```<br>`content` object array example:<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "text",<br>      "format": "text",<br>      "value": "Some text to generate an embedding"<br>    }<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "base64",<br>      "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>    }<br>  }<br>]<br>```<br>`content` object using the `url` format example (available in Elasticsearch 9.6.0 and later):<br>```<br>"input": {<br>    "content": {<br>      "type": "image",<br>      "format": "url",<br>      "value": "https://example.com/image.jpg"<br>    }<br>  }<br>```<br>Multiple items in one `content` object example (available in Elasticsearch 9.5.0 and later):<br>```<br>"input": [<br>  {<br>    "content": [<br>      {<br>        "type": "image",<br>        "format": "base64",<br>        "value": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."<br>      },<br>      {<br>        "type": "text",<br>        "value": "Some text to create an embedding"<br>      }<br>    ]<br>  }<br>]<br>```|
|input_type|string|false|none|The input data type for the embedding model. Possible values include:<br>* `SEARCH`<br>* `INGEST`<br>* `CLASSIFICATION`<br>* `CLUSTERING`<br><br>Not all models support all values. Unsupported values will trigger a validation exception.<br>Accepted values depend on the configured inference service, refer to the relevant service-specific documentation for more info.<br><br>> info<br>> The `input_type` parameter specified on the root level of the request body will take precedence over the `input_type` parameter specified in `task_settings`.|
|task_settings|object|false|none|Task settings for the individual inference request. These settings are specific to the <task_type> you specified and override the task settings specified when initializing the service.|

Configuration options when storing the inference endpoint

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|chunking_settings|object|false|none|The chunking configuration object.<br>Applies only to the `embedding`, `sparse_embedding` and `text_embedding` task types.<br>Not applicable to the `rerank`, `completion`, or `chat_completion` task types.|
|service|string|true|none|The service type|
|service_settings|object|true|none|Settings specific to the service|

<h2 id="tocS_inference._types.InferenceChunkingSettings">inference._types.InferenceChunkingSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference._types.inferencechunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_inference._types.InferenceChunkingSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.inferencechunkingsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.inferencechunkingsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "max_chunk_size": 250,
  "overlap": 100,
  "sentence_overlap": 1,
  "separator_group": "string",
  "separators": [
    "string"
  ],
  "strategy": "sentence"
}
```

Chunking configuration object

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_chunk_size|number|false|none|The maximum size of a chunk in words.<br>This value cannot be lower than `20` (for `sentence` strategy) or `10` (for `word` strategy).<br>This value should not exceed the window size for the associated model.|
|overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping words for chunks.<br>It is applicable only to a `word` chunking strategy.<br>This value cannot be higher than half the `max_chunk_size` value.|
|sentence_overlap|number|false|none|The number of overlapping sentences for chunks.<br>It is applicable only for a `sentence` chunking strategy.<br>It can be either `1` or `0`.|
|separator_group|string|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>Sets a predefined list of separators in the saved chunking settings based on the selected text type.<br>Values can be `markdown` or `plaintext`.<br><br>Using this parameter is an alternative to manually specifying a custom `separators` list.|
|separators|[string]|false|none|Only applicable to the `recursive` strategy and required when using it.<br><br>A list of strings used as possible split points when chunking text.<br><br>Each string can be a plain string or a regular expression (regex) pattern.<br>The system tries each separator in order to split the text, starting from the first item in the list.<br><br>After splitting, it attempts to recombine smaller pieces into larger chunks that stay within<br>the `max_chunk_size` limit, to reduce the total number of chunks generated.|
|strategy|string|false|none|The chunking strategy: `sentence`, `word`, `none` or `recursive`.<br><br> * If `strategy` is set to `recursive`, you must also specify:<br><br>- `max_chunk_size`<br>- either `separators` or`separator_group`<br><br>Learn more about different chunking strategies in the linked documentation.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_key|string|true|none|A valid AWS access key that has permissions to use Amazon Bedrock and access to models for inference requests.|
|model|string|true|none|The base model ID or an ARN to a custom model based on a foundational model.<br>The base model IDs can be found in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.<br>Note that the model ID must be available for the provider chosen and your IAM user must have access to the model.|
|provider|string|false|none|The model provider for your deployment.<br>Note that some providers may support only certain task types.<br>Supported providers include:<br><br>* `amazontitan` - available for `text_embedding` and `completion` task types<br>* `anthropic` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `ai21labs` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `cohere` - available for `chat_completion`, `completion` and `text_embedding` task types<br>* `meta` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types<br>* `mistral` - available for `chat_completion` and `completion` task types|
|region|string|true|none|The region that your model or ARN is deployed in.<br>The list of available regions per model can be found in the Amazon Bedrock documentation.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Amazon Bedrock.<br>By default, the `amazonbedrock` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 240.|
|secret_key|string|true|none|A valid AWS secret key that is paired with the `access_key`.<br>For informationg about creating and managing access and secret keys, refer to the AWS documentation.|

<h2 id="tocS_inference._types.AmazonBedrockTaskSettings">inference._types.AmazonBedrockTaskSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference._types.amazonbedrocktasksettings"></a>
<a id="schema_inference._types.AmazonBedrockTaskSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.amazonbedrocktasksettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.amazonbedrocktasksettings"></a>

```json
{
  "max_new_tokens": 64,
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_k": 0,
  "top_p": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_new_tokens|number|false|none|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it sets the maximum number for the output tokens to be generated.|
|temperature|number|false|none|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it is a number between 0.0 and 1.0 that controls the apparent creativity of the results.<br>At temperature 0.0 the model is most deterministic, at temperature 1.0 most random.<br>It should not be used if `top_p` or `top_k` is specified.|
|top_k|number|false|none|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it limits samples to the top-K most likely words, balancing coherence and variability.<br>It is only available for anthropic, cohere, and mistral providers.<br>It is an alternative to `temperature`; it should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|
|top_p|number|false|none|For `chat_completion` and `completion` tasks, it is a number in the range of 0.0 to 1.0, to eliminate low-probability tokens.<br>Top-p uses nucleus sampling to select top tokens whose sum of likelihoods does not exceed a certain value, ensuring both variety and coherence.<br>It is an alternative to `temperature`; it should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_key|string|true|none|A valid AWS access key that has permissions to use Amazon SageMaker and access to models for invoking requests.|

|element_type|object|false|none|Required when `api` is `elastic` and task type is `text_embedding`. The data type returned by the text embedding<br>model.<br>This value is used when parsing the response back to Elasticsearch data structures.|
|target_model|string|false|none|The model ID when calling a multi-model endpoint.|
|target_container_hostname|string|false|none|The container to directly invoke when calling a multi-container endpoint.|
|inference_component_name|string|false|none|The inference component to directly invoke when calling a multi-component endpoint.|
|batch_size|number|false|none|The maximum number of inputs in each batch. This value is used by inference ingestion pipelines<br>when processing semantic values. It correlates to the number of times the SageMaker endpoint is<br>invoked (one per batch of input).|

<h2 id="tocS_inference._types.AnthropicTaskSettings">inference._types.AnthropicTaskSettings</h2>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_tokens|number|true|none|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it is the maximum number of tokens to generate before stopping.|
|temperature|number|false|none|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it is the amount of randomness injected into the response.<br>For more details about the supported range, refer to Anthropic documentation.|
|top_k|number|false|none|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it specifies to only sample from the top K options for each subsequent token.<br>It is recommended for advanced use cases only.<br>You usually only need to use `temperature`.|
|top_p|number|false|none|For a `completion` or `chat_completion` task, it specifies to use Anthropic's nucleus sampling.<br>In nucleus sampling, Anthropic computes the cumulative distribution over all the options for each subsequent token in decreasing probability order and cuts it off once it reaches the specified probability.<br>You should either alter `temperature` or `top_p`, but not both.<br>It is recommended for advanced use cases only.<br>You usually only need to use `temperature`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid API key of your Azure AI Studio model deployment.<br>This key can be found on the overview page for your deployment in the management section of your Azure AI Studio account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|endpoint_type|string|true|none|The type of endpoint that is available for deployment through Azure AI Studio: `token` or `realtime`.<br>The `token` endpoint type is for "pay as you go" endpoints that are billed per token.<br>The `realtime` endpoint type is for "real-time" endpoints that are billed per hour of usage.|
|target|string|true|none|The target URL of your Azure AI Studio model deployment.<br>This can be found on the overview page for your deployment in the management section of your Azure AI Studio account.|
|provider|string|true|none|The model provider for your deployment.<br>Note that some providers may support only certain task types.<br>Supported providers include:<br><br>* `cohere` - available for `text_embedding`, `rerank` and `completion` task types<br>* `databricks` - available for `completion` task type only<br>* `meta` - available for `completion` task type only<br>* `microsoft_phi` - available for `completion` task type only<br>* `mistral` - available for `completion` task type only<br>* `openai` - available for `text_embedding` and `completion` task types|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Azure AI Studio.<br>By default, the `azureaistudio` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 240.|

<h2 id="tocS_inference._types.AzureAiStudioTaskSettings">inference._types.AzureAiStudioTaskSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference._types.azureaistudiotasksettings"></a>
<a id="schema_inference._types.AzureAiStudioTaskSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.azureaistudiotasksettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.azureaistudiotasksettings"></a>

```json
{
  "do_sample": 0,
  "max_new_tokens": 0,
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_p": 0,
  "user": "string",
  "return_documents": true,
  "top_n": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|do_sample|number|false|none|For a `completion` task, instruct the inference process to perform sampling.<br>It has no effect unless `temperature` or `top_p` is specified.|
|max_new_tokens|number|false|none|For a `completion` task, provide a hint for the maximum number of output tokens to be generated.|
|temperature|number|false|none|For a `completion` task, control the apparent creativity of generated completions with a sampling temperature.<br>It must be a number in the range of 0.0 to 2.0.<br>It should not be used if `top_p` is specified.|
|top_p|number|false|none|For a `completion` task, make the model consider the results of the tokens with nucleus sampling probability.<br>It is an alternative value to `temperature` and must be a number in the range of 0.0 to 2.0.<br>It should not be used if `temperature` is specified.|
|user|string|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, specify the user issuing the request.<br>This information can be used for abuse detection.|
|return_documents|boolean|false|none|For a `rerank` task, return doc text within the results.|
|top_n|number|false|none|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|false|none|A valid API key for your Azure OpenAI account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|api_version|string|true|none|The Azure API version ID to use.<br>It is recommended to use the latest supported non-preview version.|
|client_id|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application ID that's assigned to your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|client_secret|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application secret that you created in the Microsoft app registration portal for your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|deployment_id|string|true|none|The deployment name of your deployed models.<br>Your Azure OpenAI deployments can be found though the Azure OpenAI Studio portal that is linked to your subscription.|
|entra_id|string|false|none|A valid Microsoft Entra token.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key`, `entra_id`, or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Azure.<br>The `azureopenai` service sets a default number of requests allowed per minute depending on the task type.<br>For `text_embedding`, it is set to `1440`.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion`, it is set to `120`.|
|resource_name|string|true|none|The name of your Azure OpenAI resource.<br>You can find this from the list of resources in the Azure Portal for your subscription.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The resource identifier (application ID URI) of the resource you want, suffixed with .default<br>For example:<br>```<br>"scopes": [<br>  "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"<br>]<br>```<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|tenant_id|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The directory tenant the application plans to operate against.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `tenant_id`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid API key for your Cohere account.<br>You can find or create your Cohere API keys on the Cohere API key settings page.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|embedding_type|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the types of embeddings you want to get back.<br>Use `binary` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision.<br>Use `bit` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision (this is a synonym of `binary`).<br>Use `byte` for signed int8 embeddings (this is a synonym of `int8`).<br>Use `float` for the default float embeddings.<br>Use `int8` for signed int8 embeddings.|
|model_id|string|true|none|For a `completion`, `rerank`, or `text_embedding` task, the name of the model to use for the inference task.<br><br>* For the available `completion` models, refer to the [Cohere command docs](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/models#command).<br>* For the available `rerank` models, refer to the [Cohere rerank docs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/rerank-1).<br>* For the available `text_embedding` models, refer to [Cohere embed docs](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/embed).|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Cohere.<br>By default, the `cohere` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 10000.|
|similarity|object|false|none|The similarity measure.<br>If the `embedding_type` is `float`, the default value is `dot_product`.<br>If the `embedding_type` is `int8` or `byte`, the default value is `cosine`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input_type|object|true|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the type of input passed to the model.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `classification`: Use it for embeddings passed through a text classifier.<br>* `clustering`: Use it for the embeddings run through a clustering algorithm.<br>* `ingest`: Use it for storing document embeddings in a vector database.<br>* `search`: Use it for storing embeddings of search queries run against a vector database to find relevant documents.<br><br>IMPORTANT: The `input_type` field is required when using embedding models `v3` and higher.|
|return_documents|boolean|false|none|For a `rerank` task, return doc text within the results.|
|top_n|number|false|none|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.<br>If this inference endpoint is used in a `text_similarity_reranker` retriever query and `top_n` is set, it must be greater than or equal to `rank_window_size` in the query.|
|truncate|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the method to handle inputs longer than the maximum token length.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `END`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the end of the input is discarded.<br>* `NONE`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, an error is returned.<br>* `START`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the start of the input is discarded.|

```json
    "property1": "string",

  },
  "input_type": {

  },
  "query_parameters": [
    [
      "string"
    ]
  ],
  "request": {
    "content": "string"
  },
  "response": {
    "json_parser": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "secret_parameters": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_size|number|false|none|Specifies the batch size used for the semantic_text field. If the field is not provided, the default is 10.<br>The batch size is the maximum number of inputs in a single request to the upstream service.<br>The chunk within the batch are controlled by the selected chunking strategy for the semantic_text field.|
|headers|object|false|none|Specifies the HTTP header parameters – such as `Authorization` or `Content-Type` – that are required to access the custom service.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"headers": {<br>  "Authorization": "Bearer ${api_key}",<br>  "Content-Type": "application/json;charset=utf-8"<br>}<br>```|
|input_type|object|false|none|Specifies the input type translation values that are used to replace the `${input_type}` template in the request body.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"input_type": {<br>  "translation": {<br>    "ingest": "do_ingest",<br>    "search": "do_search"<br>  },<br>  "default": "a_default"<br>},<br>```<br>If the subsequent inference requests come from a search context, the `search` key will be used and the template will be replaced with `do_search`.<br>If it comes from the ingest context `do_ingest` is used. If it's a different context that is not specified, the default value will be used. If no default is specified an empty string is used.<br>`translation` can be:<br>* `classification`<br>* `clustering`<br>* `ingest`<br>* `search`|
|query_parameters|[[inference._types.CustomServiceQueryParameter](#schemainference._types.customservicequeryparameter)]|false|none|Specifies the query parameters as a list of tuples. The arrays inside the `query_parameters` must have two items, a key and a value.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"query_parameters":[<br>  ["param_key", "some_value"],<br>  ["param_key", "another_value"],<br>  ["other_key", "other_value"]<br>]<br>```<br>If the base url is `https://www.elastic.co` it results in: `https://www.elastic.co?param_key=some_value&param_key=another_value&other_key=other_value`.|
|request|object|true|none|The request configuration object.|
|response|object|true|none|The response configuration object.|
|secret_parameters|object|true|none|Specifies secret parameters, like `api_key` or `api_token`, that are required to access the custom service.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"secret_parameters":{<br>  "api_key":"<api_key>"<br>}<br>```|
|url|string|false|none|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.|
