
### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|json_parser|object|true|none|Specifies the JSON parser that is used to parse the response from the custom service.<br>Different task types require different json_parser parameters.<br>For example:<br>```<br># text_embedding<br># For a response like this:<br><br>{<br> "object": "list",<br> "data": [<br>     {<br>       "object": "embedding",<br>       "index": 0,<br>       "embedding": [<br>           0.014539449,<br>           -0.015288644<br>       ]<br>     }<br> ],<br> "model": "text-embedding-ada-002-v2",<br> "usage": {<br>     "prompt_tokens": 8,<br>     "total_tokens": 8<br> }<br>}<br><br># the json_parser definition should look like this:<br><br>"response":{<br>  "json_parser":{<br>    "text_embeddings":"$.data[*].embedding[*]"<br>  }<br>}<br><br># Elasticsearch supports the following embedding types:<br>* float<br>* byte<br>* bit (or binary)<br><br>To specify the embedding type for the response, the `embedding_type`<br>field should be added in the `json_parser` object. Here's an example:<br>"response":{<br>  "json_parser":{<br>    "text_embeddings":"$.data[*].embedding[*]",<br>    "embedding_type":"bit"<br>  }<br>}<br><br>If `embedding_type` is not specified, it defaults to `float`.<br><br># sparse_embedding<br># For a response like this:<br><br>{<br>  "request_id": "75C50B5B-E79E-4930-****-F48DBB392231",<br>  "latency": 22,<br>  "usage": {<br>     "token_count": 11<br>  },<br>  "result": {<br>     "sparse_embeddings": [<br>        {<br>          "index": 0,<br>          "embedding": [<br>            {<br>              "token_id": 6,<br>              "weight": 0.101<br>            },<br>            {<br>              "token_id": 163040,<br>              "weight": 0.28417<br>            }<br>          ]<br>        }<br>     ]<br>  }<br>}<br><br># the json_parser definition should look like this:<br><br>"response":{<br>  "json_parser":{<br>    "token_path":"$.result.sparse_embeddings[*].embedding[*].token_id",<br>    "weight_path":"$.result.sparse_embeddings[*].embedding[*].weight"<br>  }<br>}<br><br># rerank<br># For a response like this:<br><br>{<br>  "results": [<br>    {<br>      "index": 3,<br>      "relevance_score": 0.999071,<br>      "document": "abc"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "index": 4,<br>      "relevance_score": 0.7867867,<br>      "document": "123"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "index": 0,<br>      "relevance_score": 0.32713068,<br>      "document": "super"<br>    }<br>  ],<br>}<br><br># the json_parser definition should look like this:<br><br>"response":{<br>  "json_parser":{<br>    "reranked_index":"$.result.scores[*].index",    // optional<br>    "relevance_score":"$.result.scores[*].score",<br>    "document_text":"xxx"    // optional<br>  }<br>}<br><br># completion<br># For a response like this:<br><br>{<br> "id": "chatcmpl-B9MBs8CjcvOU2jLn4n570S5qMJKcT",<br> "object": "chat.completion",<br> "created": 1741569952,<br> "model": "gpt-4.1-2025-04-14",<br> "choices": [<br>   {<br>    "index": 0,<br>    "message": {<br>      "role": "assistant",<br>      "content": "Hello! How can I assist you today?",<br>      "refusal": null,<br>      "annotations": []<br>    },<br>    "logprobs": null,<br>    "finish_reason": "stop"<br>  }<br> ]<br>}<br><br># the json_parser definition should look like this:<br><br>"response":{<br>  "json_parser":{<br>    "completion_result":"$.choices[*].message.content"<br>  }<br>}|

<a id="schema_inference._types.ElasticsearchServiceSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.elasticsearchservicesettings"></a>

```json
{
  "adaptive_allocations": {
    "enabled": false,
    "max_number_of_allocations": 0,
    "min_number_of_allocations": 0
  },
  "deployment_id": "string",
  "model_id": "string",
  "num_allocations": 0,
  "num_threads": 0,
  "long_document_strategy": "string",
  "max_chunks_per_doc": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adaptive_allocations|object|false|none|Adaptive allocations configuration details.<br>If `enabled` is true, the number of allocations of the model is set based on the current load the process gets.<br>When the load is high, a new model allocation is automatically created, respecting the value of `max_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>When the load is low, a model allocation is automatically removed, respecting the value of `min_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>If `enabled` is true, do not set the number of allocations manually.|
|deployment_id|string|false|none|The deployment identifier for a trained model deployment.<br>When `deployment_id` is used the `model_id` is optional.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>It can be the ID of a built-in model (for example, `.multilingual-e5-small` for E5) or a text embedding model that was uploaded by using the Eland client.|
|num_allocations|number|false|none|The total number of allocations that are assigned to the model across machine learning nodes.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the throughput.<br>If adaptive allocations are enabled, do not set this value because it's automatically set.|
|num_threads|number|true|none|The number of threads used by each model allocation during inference.<br>This setting generally increases the speed per inference request.<br>The inference process is a compute-bound process; `threads_per_allocations` must not exceed the number of available allocated processors per node.<br>The value must be a power of 2.<br>The maximum value is 32.|
|long_document_strategy|string|false|none|Available only for the `rerank` task type using the Elastic reranker model.<br>Controls the strategy used for processing long documents during inference.<br><br>Possible values:<br>- `truncate` (default): Processes only the beginning of each document.<br>- `chunk`: Splits long documents into smaller parts (chunks) before inference.<br><br>When `long_document_strategy` is set to `chunk`, Elasticsearch splits each document into smaller parts but still returns a single score per document.<br>That score reflects the highest relevance score among all chunks.|
|max_chunks_per_doc|number|false|none|Only for the `rerank` task type.<br>Limits the number of chunks per document that are sent for inference when chunking is enabled.<br>If not set, all chunks generated for the document are processed.|

```json
{
  "adaptive_allocations": {
    "enabled": false,
    "max_number_of_allocations": 0,
    "min_number_of_allocations": 0
  },
  "num_allocations": 0,
  "num_threads": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adaptive_allocations|object|false|none|Adaptive allocations configuration details.<br>If `enabled` is true, the number of allocations of the model is set based on the current load the process gets.<br>When the load is high, a new model allocation is automatically created, respecting the value of `max_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>When the load is low, a model allocation is automatically removed, respecting the value of `min_number_of_allocations` if it's set.<br>If `enabled` is true, do not set the number of allocations manually.|
|num_allocations|number|true|none|The total number of allocations this model is assigned across machine learning nodes.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the throughput.<br>If adaptive allocations is enabled, do not set this value because it's automatically set.|
|num_threads|number|true|none|The number of threads used by each model allocation during inference.<br>Increasing this value generally increases the speed per inference request.<br>The inference process is a compute-bound process; `threads_per_allocations` must not exceed the number of available allocated processors per node.<br>The value must be a power of 2.<br>The maximum value is 32.<br><br>> info<br>> If you want to optimize your ELSER endpoint for ingest, set the number of threads to 1. If you want to optimize your ELSER endpoint for search, set the number of threads to greater than 1.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid API key for your Fireworks AI account.<br>You can find or create your API keys in the Fireworks AI dashboard.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the Fireworks AI documentation for the list of available models for chat completion, completion, and text embedding.<br>For text embedding, supported models include the Qwen3 embedding family (e.g. `fireworks/qwen3-embedding-8b`) and other models in the Fireworks model library.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.<br>If not provided, the default Fireworks AI API endpoint is used.|
|dimensions|number|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>Variable-length embeddings are supported via this parameter.|
|similarity|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Fireworks AI API.<br>Rate limit grouping is per API key only.<br>By default, the `fireworksai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 6000.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference._types.googlevertexaiservicesettings"></a>
<a id="schema_inference._types.GoogleVertexAIServiceSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.googlevertexaiservicesettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.googlevertexaiservicesettings"></a>

```json
{
  "provider": {},
  "url": "string",
  "streaming_url": "string",
  "location": "string",
  "model_id": "string",
  "project_id": "string",
  "rate_limit": {
    "requests_per_minute": 0
  },
  "service_account_json": "string",
  "dimensions": 0,
  "max_batch_size": 250
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|object|false|none|The name of the Google Model Garden Provider for `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks.<br>In order for a Google Model Garden endpoint to be used `provider` must be defined and be other than `google`.<br>Modes:<br>- Google Model Garden (third-party models): set `provider` to a supported non-`google` value and provide `url` and/or `streaming_url`.<br>- Google Vertex AI: omit `provider` or set it to `google`. In this mode, do not set `url` or `streaming_url` and Elastic will construct the endpoint url from `location`, `model_id`, and `project_id` parameters.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL for non-streaming `completion` requests to a Google Model Garden provider endpoint.<br>If both `url` and `streaming_url` are provided, each is used for its respective mode.<br>If `streaming_url` is not provided, `url` is also used for streaming `completion` and `chat_completion`.<br>If `provider` is not provided or set to `google` (Google Vertex AI), do not set `url` (or `streaming_url`).<br>At least one of `url` or `streaming_url` must be provided for Google Model Garden endpoint usage.<br>Certain providers require separate URLs for streaming and non-streaming operations (e.g., Anthropic, Mistral, AI21). Others support both operation types through a single URL (e.g., Meta, Hugging Face).<br>Information on constructing the URL for various providers can be found in the Google Model Garden documentation for the model, or on the endpoint’s `Sample request` page. The request examples also illustrate the proper formatting for the `url`.|
|streaming_url|string|false|none|The URL for streaming `completion` and `chat_completion` requests to a Google Model Garden provider endpoint.<br>If both `streaming_url` and `url` are provided, each is used for its respective mode.<br>If `url` is not provided, `streaming_url` is also used for non-streaming `completion` requests.<br>If `provider` is not provided or set to `google` (Google Vertex AI), do not set `streaming_url` (or `url`).<br>At least one of `streaming_url` or `url` must be provided for Google Model Garden endpoint usage.<br>Certain providers require separate URLs for streaming and non-streaming operations (e.g., Anthropic, Mistral, AI21). Others support both operation types through a single URL (e.g., Meta, Hugging Face).<br>Information on constructing the URL for various providers can be found in the Google Model Garden documentation for the model, or on the endpoint’s `Sample request` page. The request examples also illustrate the proper formatting for the `streaming_url`.|
|location|string|false|none|The name of the location to use for the inference task for the Google Vertex AI inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI, when `provider` is omitted or `google`, `location` is optional.<br>When `location` is omitted, the request targets the Google Vertex AI global endpoint (`https://aiplatform.googleapis.com`); when it is provided, the corresponding regional endpoint (`https://<location>-aiplatform.googleapis.com`) is used.<br>The field must be omitted to select the global endpoint; an empty string is not a valid `location`.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `location` is ignored.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for the list of supported locations.|
|model_id|string|false|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI `model_id` is mandatory.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `model_id` will be used for some providers that require it, otherwise - ignored.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for the list of supported models for Google Vertex AI.|
|project_id|string|false|none|The name of the project to use for the Google Vertex AI inference task.<br>For Google Vertex AI `project_id` is mandatory.<br>For Google Model Garden's `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, when `provider` is a supported non-`google` value - `project_id` is ignored.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Google Vertex AI.<br>By default, the `googlevertexai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 30.000.|
|service_account_json|string|true|none|A valid service account in JSON format for the Google Vertex AI API.|
|dimensions|number|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>By default, the model's standard output dimension is used.<br>Refer to the Google documentation for more information.|
|max_batch_size|number|false|none|Only applicable for the `text_embedding` task type.<br>Controls the batch size of chunked inference requests sent to Google Vertex AI.<br><br>Setting this parameter lower reduces the risk of exceeding token limits but may result in more API calls. Setting it higher increases throughput but may risk hitting token limits.<br><br>To estimate a safe `max_batch_size` value, you can use it together with the `max_chunk_size` parameter using the following formula:<br>`max_batch_size ≈ max_chunk_size × 1.3 × 512 ÷ 20000`<br><br>Where:<br>- `1.3` is an approximate tokens-per-word ratio<br>- `512` is the maximum number of chunks that can be generated per document<br>- `20000` is the Google Vertex AI token limit per request<br><br>This estimate assumes the worst-case scenario with a document generating the maximum 512 chunks.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_truncate|boolean|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, truncate inputs longer than the maximum token length automatically.|
|top_n|number|false|none|For a `rerank` task, the number of the top N documents that should be returned.|

|max_tokens|number|false|none|For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, specifies the `max_tokens` value for requests sent to the Google Model Garden `anthropic` provider.<br>If `provider` is not set to `anthropic`, this field is ignored.<br>If `max_tokens` is specified - it must be a positive integer. If not specified, the default value of 1024 is used.<br>Anthropic models require `max_tokens` to be set for each request. Please refer to the Anthropic documentation for more information.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid access token for your HuggingFace account.<br>You can create or find your access tokens on the HuggingFace settings page.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from Hugging Face.<br>By default, the `hugging_face` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 3000 for all supported tasks.<br>Hugging Face does not publish a universal rate limit — actual limits may vary.<br>It is recommended to adjust this value based on the capacity and limits of your specific deployment environment.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, the deployed model must be compatible with the Hugging Face Chat Completion interface (see the linked external documentation for details). The endpoint URL for the request must include `/v1/chat/completions`.<br>If the model supports the OpenAI Chat Completion schema, a toggle should appear in the interface. Enabling this toggle doesn't change any model behavior, it reveals the full endpoint URL needed (which should include `/v1/chat/completions`) when configuring the inference endpoint in Elasticsearch. If the model doesn't support this schema, the toggle may not be shown.|
|model_id|string|false|none|The name of the HuggingFace model to use for the inference task.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks, this field is optional but may be required for certain models — particularly when using serverless inference endpoints.<br>For the `text_embedding` task, this field should not be included. Otherwise, the request will fail.|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid API key of your JinaAI account.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You need to provide the API key only once, during the inference model creation.<br>The get inference endpoint API does not retrieve your API key.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from JinaAI.<br>By default, the `jinaai` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 2000 for all task types.|
|similarity|object|false|none|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.<br>The default values varies with the embedding type.<br>For example, a float embedding type uses a `dot_product` similarity measure by default.|
|dimensions|number|false|none|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>By default, the model's standard output dimension is used.<br>Refer to the Jina documentation for more information.|
|embedding_type|object|false|none|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the data type returned by the model.<br>Use `bit` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision.<br>Use `binary` for binary embeddings, which are encoded as bytes with signed int8 precision (this is a synonym of `bit`).<br>Use `float` for the default float embeddings.|
|multimodal_model|boolean|false|none|For the `embedding` task, whether the model supports multimodal inputs. If true, requests sent to the Jina model<br>will use the multimodal request format (a list of objects). If false, requests sent to the model will use the same<br>format as the `text_embedding` task (a list of strings). Setting this to `false` allows the `embedding` task to be<br>used with models that do not support multimodal requests.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_inference._types.JinaAITaskSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference._types.jinaaitasksettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference._types.jinaaitasksettings"></a>

```json
{
  "return_documents": true,
  "input_type": {},
  "late_chunking": true,
  "top_n": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|return_documents|boolean|false|none|For a `rerank` task, return the doc text within the results.|
|input_type|object|false|none|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, the task passed to the model.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `classification`: Use it for embeddings passed through a classifier.<br>* `clustering`: Use it for the embeddings run through a clustering algorithm.<br>* `ingest`: Use it for storing document embeddings in a vector database.<br>* `search`: Use it for storing embeddings of search queries run against a vector database to find relevant documents.|
|late_chunking|boolean|false|none|For an `embedding` or `text_embedding` task, controls when text is split into chunks.<br>When set to `true`, a request from Elasticsearch contains only chunks related to a single document. Instead of batching chunks across documents, Elasticsearch sends them in separate requests. This ensures that chunk embeddings retain context from the entire document, improving semantic quality.<br><br>If a document exceeds the model's context limits, or if the document contains non-text inputs (relevant when using the multimodal `embedding` task), late chunking is automatically disabled for that document only and standard chunking is used instead.<br><br>If not specified, defaults to `false`.|
|top_n|number|false|none|For a `rerank` task, the number of most relevant documents to return.<br>It defaults to the number of the documents.<br>If this inference endpoint is used in a `text_similarity_reranker` retriever query and `top_n` is set, it must be greater than or equal to `rank_window_size` in the query.|

|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Mistral API.<br>By default, the `mistral` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 240.|

```json
  }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|true|none|A valid API key for your Nvidia endpoint.<br>Can be found in `API Keys` section of Nvidia account settings.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of the Nvidia model endpoint. If not provided, the default endpoint URL is used depending on the task type:<br><br>* For `text_embedding` task - `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/embeddings`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions`.<br>* For `rerank` task - `https://ai.api.nvidia.com/v1/retrieval/nvidia/reranking`.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the model's documentation for the name if needed.<br>Service has been tested and confirmed to be working with the following models:<br><br>* For `text_embedding` task - `nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-embedqa-1b-v2`.<br>* For `completion` and `chat_completion` tasks - `microsoft/phi-3-mini-128k-instruct`.<br>* For `rerank` task - `nv-rerank-qa-mistral-4b:1`.<br>Service doesn't support `text_embedding` task `baai/bge-m3` and `nvidia/nvclip` models due to them not recognizing the `input_type` parameter.|
|max_input_tokens|number|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the maximum number of tokens per input. Inputs exceeding this value are truncated prior to sending to the Nvidia API.|
|similarity|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of cosine, dot_product, l2_norm.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from the Nvidia API.<br>By default, the `nvidia` service sets the number of requests allowed per minute to 3000.|

```json
  "input_type": {},
  "truncate": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|input_type|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, type of input sent to the Nvidia endpoint.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `ingest`: Mapped to Nvidia's `passage` value in request. Used when generating embeddings during indexing.<br>* `search`: Mapped to Nvidia's `query` value in request. Used when generating embeddings during querying.<br><br>IMPORTANT: For Nvidia endpoints, if the `input_type` field is not specified, it defaults to `query`.|
|truncate|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` task, the method used by the Nvidia model to handle inputs longer than the maximum token length.<br>Valid values are:<br><br>* `END`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the end of the input is discarded.<br>* `NONE`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, an error is returned.<br>* `START`: When the input exceeds the maximum input token length, the start of the input is discarded.|

```json
  "dimensions": 0,
  "model_id": "string",
  "organization_id": "string",
  "rate_limit": {
    "requests_per_minute": 0
  },
  "scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "similarity": {},
  "token_url": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|string|false|none|A valid API key of your OpenAI account.<br>You can find your OpenAI API keys in your OpenAI account under the API keys section.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key` or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|client_id|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application ID that's assigned to your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|client_secret|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The application secret that you created for your app.<br><br>IMPORTANT: You must specify either `api_key` or `client_secret`.<br>If you do not provide one or you provide more than one of them, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|dimensions|number|false|none|For a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task, the number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.<br>It is supported only in `text-embedding-3` and later models.<br>If it is not set, the OpenAI defined default for the model is used.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the OpenAI documentation for the list of available text embedding models.|
|organization_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for your organization.<br>You can find the Organization ID in your OpenAI account under *Settings > Organizations*.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from OpenAI.<br>The `openai` service sets a default number of requests allowed per minute depending on the task type.<br>For `text_embedding` and `embedding`, it is set to `3000`.<br>For `completion` and `chat_completion`, it is set to `500`.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>The resource identifier of the resource you want.<br>For example:<br>```<br>"scopes": [<br>  "scope1",<br>  "scope2"<br>]<br>```<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|similarity|object|false|none|For a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task, the similarity measure. One of `cosine`, `dot_product`, `l2_norm`. Defaults to `dot_product`.|
|token_url|string|false|none|For OAuth 2.0 authorization using the client credentials grant flow.<br>An OAuth2 token endpoint where Elasticsearch sends a request to exchange client credentials for an access token.<br><br>IMPORTANT: To configure OAuth 2.0, you must specify `client_id`, `scopes`, `token_url`, and `client_secret` together.<br>If one of the fields is missing, you will receive an error when you try to create your endpoint.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL endpoint to use for the requests.<br>It can be changed for testing purposes.<br>Default value is `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` for a `text_embedding` or `embedding` task,<br>`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` for a `completion` or `chat_completion` task.|

```json
{
  "dimensions": 0,
  "model_id": "string",
  "rate_limit": {
    "requests_per_minute": 0
  },
  "embedding_type": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimensions|number|false|none|The number of dimensions for resulting output embeddings.<br>This setting maps to `output_dimension` in the VoyageAI documentation.<br>Only for the `text_embedding` task type.|
|model_id|string|true|none|The name of the model to use for the inference task.<br>Refer to the VoyageAI documentation for the list of available text embedding and rerank models.|
|rate_limit|object|false|none|This setting helps to minimize the number of rate limit errors returned from VoyageAI.<br>The `voyageai` service sets a default number of requests allowed per minute depending on the task type.<br>For both `text_embedding` and `rerank`, it is set to `2000`.|
|embedding_type|number|false|none|The data type for the embeddings to be returned.<br>This setting maps to `output_dtype` in the VoyageAI documentation.<br>Permitted values: float, int8, bit.<br>`int8` is a synonym of `byte` in the VoyageAI documentation.<br>`bit` is a synonym of `binary` in the VoyageAI documentation.<br>Only for the `text_embedding` task type.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|object|true|none|The type of input. Not all services and models support all input types.|
|format|object|false|none|The format of the input. For the `text` type this must be `text`. For the `image` type this must be `base64` or `url`.<br>If not specified, this defaults to `text` for the `text` type and `base64` for the `image` type.<br>The `url` format is available in Elasticsearch 9.6.0 and later.<br>Not all services and models support all formats.|
|value|string|true|none|The value of the input. For the `base64` format, this must be a base64-encoded data URI, that is, "data:content/type;base64,...".<br>For the `url` format, this must be a URL that points to the content, that is, "https://example.com/image.jpg".|

The configuration necessary to identify which IP geolocation provider to use to download a database, as well as any provider-specific configuration necessary for such downloading.
At present, the only supported providers are `maxmind` and `ipinfo`, and the `maxmind` provider requires that an `account_id` (string) is configured.
A provider (either `maxmind` or `ipinfo`) must be specified. The web and local providers can be returned as read only configurations.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|object|true|none|The provider-assigned name of the IP geolocation database to download.|
|maxmind|object|false|none|none|
|ipinfo|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|append|object|false|none|Appends one or more values to an existing array if the field already exists and it is an array.<br>Converts a scalar to an array and appends one or more values to it if the field exists and it is a scalar.<br>Creates an array containing the provided values if the field doesn’t exist.<br>Accepts a single value or an array of values.|
|attachment|object|false|none|The attachment processor lets Elasticsearch extract file attachments in common formats (such as PPT, XLS, and PDF) by using the Apache text extraction library Tika.|
|bytes|object|false|none|Converts a human readable byte value (for example `1kb`) to its value in bytes (for example `1024`).<br>If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.<br>Supported human readable units are "b", "kb", "mb", "gb", "tb", "pb" case insensitive.<br>An error will occur if the field is not a supported format or resultant value exceeds 2^63.|
|cef|object|false|none|Converts a CEF message into a structured format.|
|circle|object|false|none|Converts circle definitions of shapes to regular polygons which approximate them.|
|community_id|object|false|none|Computes the Community ID for network flow data as defined in the<br>Community ID Specification. You can use a community ID to correlate network<br>events related to a single flow.|
|convert|object|false|none|Converts a field in the currently ingested document to a different type, such as converting a string to an integer.<br>If the field value is an array, all members will be converted.|
|csv|object|false|none|Extracts fields from CSV line out of a single text field within a document.<br>Any empty field in CSV will be skipped.|
|date|object|false|none|Parses dates from fields, and then uses the date or timestamp as the timestamp for the document.|
|date_index_name|object|false|none|The purpose of this processor is to point documents to the right time based index based on a date or timestamp field in a document by using the date math index name support.|
|dissect|object|false|none|Extracts structured fields out of a single text field by matching the text field against a delimiter-based pattern.|
|dot_expander|object|false|none|Expands a field with dots into an object field.<br>This processor allows fields with dots in the name to be accessible by other processors in the pipeline.<br>Otherwise these fields can’t be accessed by any processor.|
|drop|object|false|none|Drops the document without raising any errors.<br>This is useful to prevent the document from getting indexed based on some condition.|
|enrich|object|false|none|The `enrich` processor can enrich documents with data from another index.|
|fail|object|false|none|Raises an exception.<br>This is useful for when you expect a pipeline to fail and want to relay a specific message to the requester.|
|fingerprint|object|false|none|Computes a hash of the document’s content. You can use this hash for<br>content fingerprinting.|
|foreach|object|false|none|Runs an ingest processor on each element of an array or object.|
|ip_location|object|false|none|Currently an undocumented alias for GeoIP Processor.|
|geo_grid|object|false|none|Converts geo-grid definitions of grid tiles or cells to regular bounding boxes or polygons which describe their shape.<br>This is useful if there is a need to interact with the tile shapes as spatially indexable fields.|
|geoip|object|false|none|The `geoip` processor adds information about the geographical location of an IPv4 or IPv6 address.|
|grok|object|false|none|Extracts structured fields out of a single text field within a document.<br>You choose which field to extract matched fields from, as well as the grok pattern you expect will match.<br>A grok pattern is like a regular expression that supports aliased expressions that can be reused.|
|gsub|object|false|none|Converts a string field by applying a regular expression and a replacement.<br>If the field is an array of string, all members of the array will be converted.<br>If any non-string values are encountered, the processor will throw an exception.|
|html_strip|object|false|none|Removes HTML tags from the field.<br>If the field is an array of strings, HTML tags will be removed from all members of the array.|
|inference|object|false|none|Uses a pre-trained data frame analytics model or a model deployed for natural language processing tasks to infer against the data that is being ingested in the pipeline.|
|join|object|false|none|Joins each element of an array into a single string using a separator character between each element.<br>Throws an error when the field is not an array.|
|json|object|false|none|Parses a string containing JSON data into a structured object, string, or other value.|
|kv|object|false|none|This processor helps automatically parse messages (or specific event fields) which are of the `foo=bar` variety.|
|lowercase|object|false|none|Converts a string to its lowercase equivalent.<br>If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.|
|network_direction|object|false|none|Calculates the network direction given a source IP address, destination IP<br>address, and a list of internal networks.|
|pipeline|object|false|none|Executes another pipeline.|
|redact|object|false|none|The Redact processor uses the Grok rules engine to obscure text in the input document matching the given Grok patterns.<br>The processor can be used to obscure Personal Identifying Information (PII) by configuring it to detect known patterns such as email or IP addresses.<br>Text that matches a Grok pattern is replaced with a configurable string such as `<EMAIL>` where an email address is matched or simply replace all matches with the text `<REDACTED>` if preferred.|
|registered_domain|object|false|none|Extracts the registered domain (also known as the effective top-level<br>domain or eTLD), sub-domain, and top-level domain from a fully qualified<br>domain name (FQDN). Uses the registered domains defined in the Mozilla<br>Public Suffix List.|
|remove|object|false|none|Removes existing fields.<br>If one field doesn’t exist, an exception will be thrown.|
|rename|object|false|none|Renames an existing field.<br>If the field doesn’t exist or the new name is already used, an exception will be thrown.|
|reroute|object|false|none|Routes a document to another target index or data stream.<br>When setting the `destination` option, the target is explicitly specified and the dataset and namespace options can’t be set.<br>When the `destination` option is not set, this processor is in a data stream mode. Note that in this mode, the reroute processor can only be used on data streams that follow the data stream naming scheme.|
|script|object|false|none|Runs an inline or stored script on incoming documents.<br>The script runs in the `ingest` context.|
|set|object|false|none|Adds a field with the specified value.<br>If the field already exists, its value will be replaced with the provided one.|
|set_security_user|object|false|none|Sets user-related details (such as `username`, `roles`, `email`, `full_name`, `metadata`, `api_key`, `realm` and `authentication_type`) from the current authenticated user to the current document by pre-processing the ingest.|
|sort|object|false|none|Sorts the elements of an array ascending or descending.<br>Homogeneous arrays of numbers will be sorted numerically, while arrays of strings or heterogeneous arrays of strings + numbers will be sorted lexicographically.<br>Throws an error when the field is not an array.|
|split|object|false|none|Splits a field into an array using a separator character.<br>Only works on string fields.|
|terminate|object|false|none|Terminates the current ingest pipeline, causing no further processors to be run.<br>This will normally be executed conditionally, using the `if` option.|
|trim|object|false|none|Trims whitespace from a field.<br>If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be trimmed.<br>This only works on leading and trailing whitespace.|
|uppercase|object|false|none|Converts a string to its uppercase equivalent.<br>If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.|
|urldecode|object|false|none|URL-decodes a string.<br>If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be decoded.|
|uri_parts|object|false|none|Parses a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) string and extracts its components as an object.<br>This URI object includes properties for the URI’s domain, path, fragment, port, query, scheme, user info, username, and password.|
|user_agent|object|false|none|The `user_agent` processor extracts details from the user agent string a browser sends with its web requests.<br>This processor adds this information by default under the `user_agent` field.|

Some APIs will return values such as numbers also as a string (notably epoch timestamps). This behavior
is used to capture this behavior while keeping the semantics of the field type.

Depending on the target language, code generators can keep the union or remove it and leniently parse
strings to the target type.

<h2 id="tocS__types.ReindexTaskInfo">_types.ReindexTaskInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.reindextaskinfo"></a>
<a id="schema__types.ReindexTaskInfo"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.reindextaskinfo"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.reindextaskinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "id": {},
  "description": "string",
  "start_time_in_millis": {},
  "start_time": "string",
  "running_time": {},
  "running_time_in_nanos": {},
  "cancelled": true,
  "status": {
    "slice_id": 0,
    "batches": 0,
    "created": 0,
    "deleted": 0,
    "noops": 0,
    "requests_per_second": 0,
    "retries": {
      "bulk": 0,
      "search": 0
    },
    "throttled": {},
    "throttled_millis": {},
    "throttled_until": {},
    "throttled_until_millis": {},
    "total": 0,
    "updated": 0,
    "version_conflicts": 0,
    "cancelled": "string"
  }
}
```

Information about a single parent reindex task, as returned by the reindex management APIs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|true|none|The ID of the reindex task. The ID is assigned when the task was first created and remains the same across graceful shutdown relocations.|
|description|string|false|none|A sanitized description of the reindex operation (source and destination indices, and optionally remote host info).|
|start_time_in_millis|object|true|none|The time at which the reindex task started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Remains the same across graceful shutdown relocations.|
|start_time|string|false|none|The time at which the reindex task started, as an ISO-8601 formatted string. Remains the same across graceful shutdown relocations.<br>Only present when the request includes the `?human=true` query parameter.|
|running_time|object|false|none|The elapsed running time of the reindex task, including relocations, in a human-readable format.<br>Only present when the request includes the `?human=true` query parameter.|
|running_time_in_nanos|object|true|none|The elapsed running time of the reindex task, including relocations, in nanoseconds.|
|cancelled|boolean|true|none|Whether the reindex task has been cancelled.|
|status|object|false|none|The current progress of the reindex operation.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.AnalysisConfig">ml._types.AnalysisConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.analysisconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.AnalysisConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.analysisconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.analysisconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "bucket_span": "5m",
  "categorization_analyzer": {},
  "categorization_field_name": {},
  "categorization_filters": [
    "string"
  ],
  "detectors": [
    {
      "by_field_name": {},
      "custom_rules": [
        {
          "actions": [
            "skip_result"
          ],
          "conditions": [
            {
              "applies_to": {},
              "operator": {},
              "value": 0
            }
          ],
          "scope": {
            "property1": {
              "filter_id": {},
              "filter_type": "include"
            },
            "property2": {
              "filter_id": {},
              "filter_type": "include"
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      "detector_description": "string",
      "detector_index": 0,
      "exclude_frequent": {},
      "field_name": {},
      "function": "string",
      "over_field_name": {},
      "partition_field_name": {},
      "use_null": false
    }
  ],
  "influencers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "latency": "0",
  "model_prune_window": {},
  "multivariate_by_fields": true,
  "per_partition_categorization": {
    "enabled": true,
    "stop_on_warn": true
  },
  "summary_count_field_name": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucket_span|object|false|none|The size of the interval that the analysis is aggregated into, typically between `5m` and `1h`. This value should be either a whole number of days or equate to a<br>whole number of buckets in one day. If the anomaly detection job uses a datafeed with aggregations, this value must also be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|categorization_analyzer|object|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define the analyzer that is used to interpret the categorization field. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_filters`. The categorization analyzer specifies how the `categorization_field` is interpreted by the categorization process. The `categorization_analyzer` field can be specified either as a string or as an object. If it is a string, it must refer to a built-in analyzer or one added by another plugin.|
|categorization_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the values of the specified field will be categorized. The resulting categories must be used in a detector by setting `by_field_name`, `over_field_name`, or `partition_field_name` to the keyword `mlcategory`.|
|categorization_filters|[string]|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering, use the `categorization_analyzer` property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters. The effect is exactly the same.|
|detectors|[[ml._types.Detector](#schemaml._types.detector)]|true|none|Detector configuration objects specify which data fields a job analyzes. They also specify which analytical functions are used. You can specify multiple detectors for a job. If the detectors array does not contain at least one detector, no analysis can occur and an error is returned.|
|influencers|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|false|none|A comma separated list of influencer field names. Typically these can be the by, over, or partition fields that are used in the detector configuration. You might also want to use a field name that is not specifically named in a detector, but is available as part of the input data. When you use multiple detectors, the use of influencers is recommended as it aggregates results for each influencer entity.|
|latency|object|false|none|The size of the window in which to expect data that is out of time order. If you specify a non-zero value, it must be greater than or equal to one second. NOTE: Latency is applicable only when you send data by using the post data API.|
|model_prune_window|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Affects the pruning of models that have not been updated for the given time duration. The value must be set to a multiple of the `bucket_span`. If set too low, important information may be removed from the model. For jobs created in 8.1 and later, the default value is the greater of `30d` or 20 times `bucket_span`.|
|multivariate_by_fields|boolean|false|none|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|
|per_partition_categorization|object|false|none|Settings related to how categorization interacts with partition fields.|
|summary_count_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the data that is fed to the job is expected to be pre-summarized. This property value is the name of the field that contains the count of raw data points that have been summarized. The same `summary_count_field_name` applies to all detectors in the job. NOTE: The `summary_count_field_name` property cannot be used with the `metric` function.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.CategorizationAnalyzerDefinition">ml._types.CategorizationAnalyzerDefinition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.categorizationanalyzerdefinition"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.CategorizationAnalyzerDefinition"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.categorizationanalyzerdefinition"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.categorizationanalyzerdefinition"></a>

```json
{
  "char_filter": [
    "string"
  ],
  "filter": [
    "string"
  ],
  "tokenizer": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|char_filter|[[_types.analysis.CharFilter](#schema_types.analysis.charfilter)]|false|none|One or more character filters. In addition to the built-in character filters, other plugins can provide more character filters. If this property is not specified, no character filters are applied prior to categorization. If you are customizing some other aspect of the analyzer and you need to achieve the equivalent of `categorization_filters` (which are not permitted when some other aspect of the analyzer is customized), add them here as pattern replace character filters.|
|filter|[[_types.analysis.TokenFilter](#schema_types.analysis.tokenfilter)]|false|none|One or more token filters. In addition to the built-in token filters, other plugins can provide more token filters. If this property is not specified, no token filters are applied prior to categorization.|
|tokenizer|object|false|none|The name or definition of the tokenizer to use after character filters are applied. This property is compulsory if `categorization_analyzer` is specified as an object. Machine learning provides a tokenizer called `ml_standard` that tokenizes in a way that has been determined to produce good categorization results on a variety of log file formats for logs in English. If you want to use that tokenizer but change the character or token filters, specify "tokenizer": "ml_standard" in your `categorization_analyzer`. Additionally, the `ml_classic` tokenizer is available, which tokenizes in the same way as the non-customizable tokenizer in old versions of the product (before 6.2). `ml_classic` was the default categorization tokenizer in versions 6.2 to 7.13, so if you need categorization identical to the default for jobs created in these versions, specify "tokenizer": "ml_classic" in your `categorization_analyzer`.|

```json
        "property1": {
          "filter_id": {},
          "filter_type": "include"
        },
        "property2": {
          "filter_id": {},
          "filter_type": "include"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "detector_description": "string",
  "detector_index": 0,
  "exclude_frequent": {},
  "field_name": {},
  "function": "string",
  "over_field_name": {},
  "partition_field_name": {},
  "use_null": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|by_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to their own history. It is used for finding unusual values in the context of the split.|
|custom_rules|[[ml._types.DetectionRule](#schemaml._types.detectionrule)]|false|none|Custom rules enable you to customize the way detectors operate. For example, a rule may dictate conditions under which results should be skipped. Kibana refers to custom rules as job rules.|
|detector_description|string|false|none|A description of the detector.|
|detector_index|number|false|none|A unique identifier for the detector. This identifier is based on the order of the detectors in the `analysis_config`, starting at zero. If you specify a value for this property, it is ignored.|
|exclude_frequent|object|false|none|If set, frequent entities are excluded from influencing the anomaly results. Entities can be considered frequent over time or frequent in a population. If you are working with both over and by fields, you can set `exclude_frequent` to `all` for both fields, or to `by` or `over` for those specific fields.|
|field_name|object|false|none|The field that the detector uses in the function. If you use an event rate function such as count or rare, do not specify this field. The `field_name` cannot contain double quotes or backslashes.|
|function|string|false|none|The analysis function that is used. For example, `count`, `rare`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, or `sum`.|
|over_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to the history of all splits. It is used for finding unusual values in the population of all splits.|
|partition_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to segment the analysis. When you use this property, you have completely independent baselines for each value of this field.|
|use_null|boolean|false|none|Defines whether a new series is used as the null series when there is no value for the by or partition fields.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|actions|[[ml._types.RuleAction](#schemaml._types.ruleaction)]|false|none|The set of actions to be triggered when the rule applies. If more than one action is specified the effects of all actions are combined.|
|conditions|[[ml._types.RuleCondition](#schemaml._types.rulecondition)]|false|none|An array of numeric conditions when the rule applies. A rule must either have a non-empty scope or at least one condition. Multiple conditions are combined together with a logical AND.|
|scope|object|false|none|A scope of series where the rule applies. A rule must either have a non-empty scope or at least one condition. By default, the scope includes all series. Scoping is allowed for any of the fields that are also specified in `by_field_name`, `over_field_name`, or `partition_field_name`.|

If true, both categorization and subsequent anomaly detection stops for partitions where the categorization status changes to warn.       "tp": 0,

```json
      "tn": 0,
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auc_roc|object|false|none|The AUC ROC (area under the curve of the receiver operating characteristic) score and optionally the curve.|
|precision|object|false|none|Set the different thresholds of the outlier score at where the metric is calculated.|
|recall|object|false|none|Set the different thresholds of the outlier score at where the metric is calculated.|
|confusion_matrix|object|false|none|Set the different thresholds of the outlier score at where the metrics (`tp` - true positive, `fp` - false positive, `tn` - true negative, `fn` - false negative) are calculated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alpha|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|dependent_variable|string|true|none|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|downsample_factor|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|early_stopping_enabled|boolean|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|eta|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|eta_growth_rate_per_tree|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|feature_bag_fraction|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|feature_processors|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|gamma|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|lambda|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|max_trees|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|num_top_feature_importance_values|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|prediction_field_name|object|false|none|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|randomize_seed|number|false|none|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|soft_tree_depth_limit|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|soft_tree_depth_tolerance|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|training_percent|object|false|none|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|class_assignment_objective|string|false|none|none|
|num_top_classes|number|false|none|Defines the number of categories for which the predicted probabilities are reported. It must be non-negative or -1. If it is -1 or greater than the total number of categories, probabilities are reported for all categories; if you have a large number of categories, there could be a significant effect on the size of your destination index. NOTE: To use the AUC ROC evaluation method, `num_top_classes` must be set to -1 or a value greater than or equal to the total number of categories.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|frequency_encoding|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform frequency encoding.|
|multi_encoding|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform multi encoding. It allows multiple processors to be changed together. This way the output of a processor can then be passed to another as an input.|
|n_gram_encoding|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform n-gram encoding. Features created by this encoder have the following name format: <feature_prefix>.<ngram><string position>. For example, if the feature_prefix is f, the feature name for the second unigram in a string is f.11.|
|one_hot_encoding|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform one hot encoding.|
|target_mean_encoding|object|false|none|The configuration information necessary to perform target mean encoding.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.DataframeAnalysisOutlierDetection">ml._types.DataframeAnalysisOutlierDetection</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisoutlierdetection"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.DataframeAnalysisOutlierDetection"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.dataframeanalysisoutlierdetection"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.dataframeanalysisoutlierdetection"></a>

```json
{
  "compute_feature_influence": true,
  "feature_influence_threshold": 0.1,
  "method": "ensemble",
  "n_neighbors": 0,
  "outlier_fraction": 0,
  "standardization_enabled": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|compute_feature_influence|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the feature influence calculation is enabled.|
|feature_influence_threshold|number|false|none|The minimum outlier score that a document needs to have in order to calculate its feature influence score. Value range: 0-1.|
|method|string|false|none|The method that outlier detection uses. Available methods are `lof`, `ldof`, `distance_kth_nn`, `distance_knn`, and `ensemble`. The default value is ensemble, which means that outlier detection uses an ensemble of different methods and normalises and combines their individual outlier scores to obtain the overall outlier score.|
|n_neighbors|number|false|none|Defines the value for how many nearest neighbors each method of outlier detection uses to calculate its outlier score. When the value is not set, different values are used for different ensemble members. This default behavior helps improve the diversity in the ensemble; only override it if you are confident that the value you choose is appropriate for the data set.|
|outlier_fraction|number|false|none|The proportion of the data set that is assumed to be outlying prior to outlier detection. For example, 0.05 means it is assumed that 5% of values are real outliers and 95% are inliers.|
|standardization_enabled|boolean|false|none|If true, the following operation is performed on the columns before computing outlier scores: `(x_i - mean(x_i)) / sd(x_i)`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.DataframeAnalysisRegression">ml._types.DataframeAnalysisRegression</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisregression"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.DataframeAnalysisRegression"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.dataframeanalysisregression"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.dataframeanalysisregression"></a>

```json
{
  "alpha": 0,
  "dependent_variable": "string",
  "downsample_factor": 0,
  "early_stopping_enabled": true,
  "eta": 0,
  "eta_growth_rate_per_tree": 0,
  "feature_bag_fraction": 0,
  "feature_processors": [
    {
      "frequency_encoding": {
        "feature_name": {},
        "field": {},
        "frequency_map": {
          "property1": 0,
          "property2": 0
        }
      },
      "multi_encoding": {
        "processors": [
          0
        ]
      },
      "n_gram_encoding": {
        "feature_prefix": "string",
        "field": {},
        "length": 0,
        "n_grams": [
          0
        ],
        "start": 0,
        "custom": true
      },
      "one_hot_encoding": {
        "field": {},
        "hot_map": "string"
      },
      "target_mean_encoding": {
        "default_value": 0,
        "feature_name": {},
        "field": {},
        "target_map": {
          "property1": {},
          "property2": {}
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "gamma": 0,
  "lambda": 0,
  "max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter": 0,
  "max_trees": 0,
  "num_top_feature_importance_values": 0,
  "prediction_field_name": {},
  "randomize_seed": 0,
  "soft_tree_depth_limit": 0,
  "soft_tree_depth_tolerance": 0,
  "training_percent": 100,
  "loss_function": "mse",
  "loss_function_parameter": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alpha|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth. Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|dependent_variable|string|true|none|Defines which field of the document is to be predicted. It must match one of the fields in the index being used to train. If this field is missing from a document, then that document will not be used for training, but a prediction with the trained model will be generated for it. It is also known as continuous target variable.<br>For classification analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric (`integer`, `short`, `long`, `byte`), categorical (`ip` or `keyword`), or `boolean`. There must be no more than 30 different values in this field.<br>For regression analysis, the data type of the field must be numeric.|
|downsample_factor|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training. A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data. If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves. However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|early_stopping_enabled|boolean|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether the training process should finish if it is not finding any better performing models. If disabled, the training process can take significantly longer and the chance of finding a better performing model is unremarkable.|
|eta|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. The shrinkage applied to the weights. Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error. However, larger forests cause slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a value between 0.001 and 1.|
|eta_growth_rate_per_tree|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest. For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be between 0.5 and 2.|
|feature_bag_fraction|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|feature_processors|[[ml._types.DataframeAnalysisFeatureProcessor](#schemaml._types.dataframeanalysisfeatureprocessor)]|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A collection of feature preprocessors that modify one or more included fields. The analysis uses the resulting one or more features instead of the original document field. However, these features are ephemeral; they are not stored in the destination index. Multiple `feature_processors` entries can refer to the same document fields. Automatic categorical feature encoding still occurs for the fields that are unprocessed by a custom processor or that have categorical values. Use this property only if you want to override the automatic feature encoding of the specified fields.|
|gamma|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest. A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees. A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|lambda|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set. Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest. A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights. This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable. A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be a nonnegative value.|
|max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure. The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|max_trees|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest. The maximum value is 2000. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|num_top_feature_importance_values|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies the maximum number of feature importance values per document to return. By default, no feature importance calculation occurs.|
|prediction_field_name|object|false|none|Defines the name of the prediction field in the results. Defaults to `<dependent_variable>_prediction`.|
|randomize_seed|number|false|none|Defines the seed for the random generator that is used to pick training data. By default, it is randomly generated. Set it to a specific value to use the same training data each time you start a job (assuming other related parameters such as `source` and `analyzed_fields` are the same).|
|soft_tree_depth_limit|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly. This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|soft_tree_depth_tolerance|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option. This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`. By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization. It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|
|training_percent|object|false|none|Defines what percentage of the eligible documents that will be used for training. Documents that are ignored by the analysis (for example those that contain arrays with more than one value) won’t be included in the calculation for used percentage.|
|loss_function|string|false|none|The loss function used during regression. Available options are `mse` (mean squared error), `msle` (mean squared logarithmic error), `huber` (Pseudo-Huber loss).|
|loss_function_parameter|number|false|none|A positive number that is used as a parameter to the `loss_function`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anomaly_score|number|true|none|The maximum anomaly score, between 0-100, for any of the bucket influencers. This is an overall, rate-limited<br>score for the job. All the anomaly records in the bucket contribute to this score. This value might be updated as<br>new data is analyzed.|
|bucket_influencers|[[ml._types.BucketInfluencer](#schemaml._types.bucketinfluencer)]|true|none|none|
|bucket_span|object|true|none|The length of the bucket in seconds. This value matches the bucket span that is specified in the job.|
|event_count|number|true|none|The number of input data records processed in this bucket.|
|initial_anomaly_score|number|true|none|The maximum anomaly score for any of the bucket influencers. This is the initial value that was calculated at the<br>time the bucket was processed.|
|is_interim|boolean|true|none|If true, this is an interim result. In other words, the results are calculated based on partial input data.|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|processing_time_ms|object|true|none|The amount of time, in milliseconds, that it took to analyze the bucket contents and calculate results.|
|result_type|string|true|none|Internal. This value is always set to bucket.|
|timestamp|object|true|none|The start time of the bucket. This timestamp uniquely identifies the bucket. Events that occur exactly at the<br>timestamp of the bucket are included in the results for the bucket.|
|timestamp_string|object|false|none|The start time of the bucket. This timestamp uniquely identifies the bucket. Events that occur exactly at the<br>timestamp of the bucket are included in the results for the bucket.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.BucketInfluencer">ml._types.BucketInfluencer</h2>
