### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anomaly_score|number|true|none|A normalized score between 0-100, which is calculated for each bucket influencer. This score might be updated as<br>newer data is analyzed.|
|bucket_span|object|true|none|The length of the bucket in seconds. This value matches the bucket span that is specified in the job.|
|influencer_field_name|object|true|none|The field name of the influencer.|
|initial_anomaly_score|number|true|none|The score between 0-100 for each bucket influencer. This score is the initial value that was calculated at the<br>time the bucket was processed.|
|is_interim|boolean|true|none|If true, this is an interim result. In other words, the results are calculated based on partial input data.|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|probability|number|true|none|The probability that the bucket has this behavior, in the range 0 to 1. This value can be held to a high precision<br>of over 300 decimal places, so the `anomaly_score` is provided as a human-readable and friendly interpretation of<br>this.|
|raw_anomaly_score|number|true|none|Internal.|
|result_type|string|true|none|Internal. This value is always set to `bucket_influencer`.|
|timestamp|object|true|none|The start time of the bucket for which these results were calculated.|
|timestamp_string|object|false|none|The start time of the bucket for which these results were calculated.|

|category_id|object|true|none|A unique identifier for the category. category_id is unique at the job level, even when per-partition categorization is enabled.|
|examples|[string]|true|none|A list of examples of actual values that matched the category.|
|grok_pattern|object|false|none|[experimental] A Grok pattern that could be used in Logstash or an ingest pipeline to extract fields from messages that match the category. This field is experimental and may be changed or removed in a future release. The Grok patterns that are found are not optimal, but are often a good starting point for manual tweaking.|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|max_matching_length|object|true|none|The maximum length of the fields that matched the category. The value is increased by 10% to enable matching for similar fields that have not been analyzed.|
|partition_field_name|string|false|none|If per-partition categorization is enabled, this property identifies the field used to segment the categorization. It is not present when per-partition categorization is disabled.|
|partition_field_value|string|false|none|If per-partition categorization is enabled, this property identifies the value of the partition_field_name for the category. It is not present when per-partition categorization is disabled.|
|regex|string|true|none|A regular expression that is used to search for values that match the category.|
|terms|string|true|none|A space separated list of the common tokens that are matched in values of the category.|
|num_matches|number|false|none|The number of messages that have been matched by this category. This is only guaranteed to have the latest accurate count after a job _flush or _close|
|preferred_to_categories|[[_types.Id](#schema_types.id)]|false|none|A list of category_id entries that this current category encompasses. Any new message that is processed by the categorizer will match against this category and not any of the categories in this list. This is only guaranteed to have the latest accurate list of categories after a job _flush or _close|
|p|string|false|none|none|
|result_type|string|true|none|none|
|mlcategory|string|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.Hyperparameters">ml._types.Hyperparameters</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.hyperparameters"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.Hyperparameters"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.hyperparameters"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.hyperparameters"></a>

```json
{
  "alpha": 0,
  "lambda": 0,
  "gamma": 0,
  "eta": 0,
  "eta_growth_rate_per_tree": 0,
  "feature_bag_fraction": 0,
  "downsample_factor": 0,
  "max_attempts_to_add_tree": 0,
  "max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter": 0,
  "max_trees": 0,
  "num_folds": 0,
  "num_splits_per_feature": 0,
  "soft_tree_depth_limit": 0,
  "soft_tree_depth_tolerance": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alpha|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly.<br>This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier of the tree depth.<br>Higher alpha values result in shallower trees and faster training times.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be greater than or equal to zero.|
|lambda|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set.<br>Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest.<br>A high lambda value causes training to favor small leaf weights.<br>This behavior makes the prediction function smoother at the expense of potentially not being able to capture relevant relationships between the features and the dependent variable.<br>A small lambda value results in large individual trees and slower training.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be a nonnegative value.|
|gamma|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set.<br>Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest.<br>A high gamma value causes training to prefer small trees.<br>A small gamma value results in larger individual trees and slower training.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be a nonnegative value.|
|eta|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The shrinkage applied to the weights.<br>Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error.<br>However, larger forests cause slower training.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be a value between `0.001` and `1`.|
|eta_growth_rate_per_tree|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest.<br>For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be between `0.5` and `2`.|
|feature_bag_fraction|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|downsample_factor|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training.<br>A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data.<br>If this value is set to be less than 1, accuracy typically improves.<br>However, too small a value may result in poor convergence for the ensemble and so require more trees.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be greater than zero and less than or equal to 1.|
|max_attempts_to_add_tree|number|false|none|If the algorithm fails to determine a non-trivial tree (more than a single leaf), this parameter determines how many of such consecutive failures are tolerated.<br>Once the number of attempts exceeds the threshold, the forest training stops.|
|max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure.<br>The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of undefined hyperparameters times the maximum optimization rounds per hyperparameter.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|max_trees|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest.<br>The maximum value is 2000.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.|
|num_folds|number|false|none|The maximum number of folds for the cross-validation procedure.|
|num_splits_per_feature|number|false|none|Determines the maximum number of splits for every feature that can occur in a decision tree when the tree is trained.|
|soft_tree_depth_limit|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly.<br>This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to penalize trees that exceed the specified depth; the regularized loss increases quickly beyond this depth.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be greater than or equal to 0.|
|soft_tree_depth_tolerance|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>This option controls how quickly the regularized loss increases when the tree depth exceeds `soft_tree_depth_limit`.<br>By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.<br>It must be greater than or equal to 0.01.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.OutlierDetectionParameters">ml._types.OutlierDetectionParameters</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.outlierdetectionparameters"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.OutlierDetectionParameters"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.outlierdetectionparameters"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.outlierdetectionparameters"></a>

```json
{
  "compute_feature_influence": true,
  "feature_influence_threshold": 0.1,
  "method": "string",
  "n_neighbors": 0,
  "outlier_fraction": 0,
  "standardization_enabled": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|compute_feature_influence|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the feature influence calculation is enabled.|
|feature_influence_threshold|number|false|none|The minimum outlier score that a document needs to have in order to calculate its feature influence score.<br>Value range: 0-1|
|method|string|false|none|The method that outlier detection uses.<br>Available methods are `lof`, `ldof`, `distance_kth_nn`, `distance_knn`, and `ensemble`.<br>The default value is ensemble, which means that outlier detection uses an ensemble of different methods and normalises and combines their individual outlier scores to obtain the overall outlier score.|
|n_neighbors|number|false|none|Defines the value for how many nearest neighbors each method of outlier detection uses to calculate its outlier score.<br>When the value is not set, different values are used for different ensemble members.<br>This default behavior helps improve the diversity in the ensemble; only override it if you are confident that the value you choose is appropriate for the data set.|
|outlier_fraction|number|false|none|The proportion of the data set that is assumed to be outlying prior to outlier detection.<br>For example, 0.05 means it is assumed that 5% of values are real outliers and 95% are inliers.|
|standardization_enabled|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the following operation is performed on the columns before computing outlier scores: (x_i - mean(x_i)) / sd(x_i).|

Likewise, all types of analysis skip documents that contain arrays with more than one element.|

<a id="tocSml._types.datafeedtimingstats"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.datafeedtimingstats"></a>

```json
{
  "bucket_count": 0,
  "exponential_average_search_time_per_hour_ms": {},
  "exponential_average_calculation_context": {
    "incremental_metric_value_ms": {},
    "latest_timestamp": {},
    "previous_exponential_average_ms": {}
  },
  "job_id": {},
  "search_count": 0,
  "total_search_time_ms": {},
  "average_search_time_per_bucket_ms": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucket_count|number|true|none|The number of buckets processed.|
|exponential_average_search_time_per_hour_ms|object|true|none|The exponential average search time per hour, in milliseconds.|
|exponential_average_calculation_context|object|false|none|none|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|search_count|number|true|none|The number of searches run by the datafeed.|
|total_search_time_ms|object|true|none|The total time the datafeed spent searching, in milliseconds.|
|average_search_time_per_bucket_ms|object|false|none|The average search time per bucket, in milliseconds.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.DatafeedRunningState">ml._types.DatafeedRunningState</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.datafeedrunningstate"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.DatafeedRunningState"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.datafeedrunningstate"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.datafeedrunningstate"></a>

```json
{
  "real_time_configured": true,
  "real_time_running": true,
  "search_interval": {
    "end": {},
    "end_ms": {},
    "start": {},
    "start_ms": {}
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|real_time_configured|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the datafeed is "real-time"; meaning that the datafeed has no configured `end` time.|
|real_time_running|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the datafeed has finished running on the available past data.<br>For datafeeds without a configured `end` time, this means that the datafeed is now running on "real-time" data.|
|search_interval|object|false|none|Provides the latest time interval the datafeed has searched.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|none|
|authorization|object|false|none|The security privileges that the datafeed uses to run its queries. If Elastic Stack security features were disabled at the time of the most recent update to the datafeed, this property is omitted.|
|chunking_config|object|false|none|none|
|datafeed_id|object|true|none|none|
|frequency|object|false|none|The interval at which scheduled queries are made while the datafeed runs in real time. The default value is either the bucket span for short bucket spans, or, for longer bucket spans, a sensible fraction of the bucket span. For example: `150s`. When `frequency` is shorter than the bucket span, interim results for the last (partial) bucket are written then eventually overwritten by the full bucket results. If the datafeed uses aggregations, this value must be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|indices|[string]|true|none|none|
|indexes|[string]|false|none|none|
|job_id|object|true|none|none|
|max_empty_searches|number|false|none|none|
|query|object|true|none|none|
|query_delay|object|false|none|none|
|script_fields|object|false|none|none|
|scroll_size|number|false|none|none|
|delayed_data_check_config|object|true|none|none|
|runtime_mappings|object|false|none|none|
|indices_options|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.ChunkingConfig">ml._types.ChunkingConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.chunkingconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": {},
  "time_span": "3h"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|object|true|none|If the mode is `auto`, the chunk size is dynamically calculated;<br>this is the recommended value when the datafeed does not use aggregations.<br>If the mode is `manual`, chunking is applied according to the specified `time_span`;<br>use this mode when the datafeed uses aggregations. If the mode is `off`, no chunking is applied.|
|time_span|object|false|none|The time span that each search will be querying. This setting is applicable only when the `mode` is set to `manual`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.DelayedDataCheckConfig">ml._types.DelayedDataCheckConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.delayeddatacheckconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.DelayedDataCheckConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.delayeddatacheckconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.delayeddatacheckconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "check_window": {},
  "enabled": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|check_window|object|false|none|The window of time that is searched for late data. This window of time ends with the latest finalized bucket.<br>It defaults to null, which causes an appropriate `check_window` to be calculated when the real-time datafeed runs.<br>In particular, the default `check_window` span calculation is based on the maximum of `2h` or `8 * bucket_span`.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Specifies whether the datafeed periodically checks for delayed data.|

<h2 id="tocS__types.IndicesOptions">_types.IndicesOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schema_types.indicesoptions"></a>
<a id="schema__types.IndicesOptions"></a>
<a id="tocS_types.indicesoptions"></a>
<a id="tocs_types.indicesoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "allow_no_indices": true,
  "expand_wildcards": {},
  "ignore_unavailable": false,
  "ignore_throttled": true
}
```

Controls how to deal with unavailable concrete indices (closed or missing), how wildcard expressions are expanded
to actual indices (all, closed or open indices) and how to deal with wildcard expressions that resolve to no indices.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_no_indices|boolean|false|none|A setting that does two separate checks on the index expression.<br>If `false`, the request returns an error (1) if any wildcard expression<br>(including `_all` and `*`) resolves to zero matching indices or (2) if the<br>complete set of resolved indices, aliases or data streams is empty after all<br>expressions are evaluated. If `true`, index expressions that resolve to no<br>indices are allowed and the request returns an empty result.|
|expand_wildcards|object|false|none|Type of index that wildcard patterns can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument<br>determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams. Supports comma-separated values,<br>such as `open,hidden`.|
|ignore_unavailable|boolean|false|none|If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a concrete (non-wildcarded)<br>index, alias, or data stream that is missing, closed, or otherwise unavailable.<br>If `true`, unavailable concrete targets are silently ignored.|
|ignore_throttled|boolean|false|none|If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.Influencer">ml._types.Influencer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.influencer"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.Influencer"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.influencer"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.influencer"></a>

```json
{
  "bucket_span": {},
  "influencer_score": 0,
  "influencer_field_name": {},
  "influencer_field_value": "string",
  "initial_influencer_score": 0,
  "is_interim": true,
  "job_id": {},
  "probability": 0,
  "result_type": "string",
  "timestamp": {},
  "foo": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucket_span|object|true|none|The length of the bucket in seconds. This value matches the bucket span that is specified in the job.|
|influencer_score|number|true|none|A normalized score between 0-100, which is based on the probability of the influencer in this bucket aggregated<br>across detectors. Unlike `initial_influencer_score`, this value is updated by a re-normalization process as new<br>data is analyzed.|
|influencer_field_name|object|true|none|The field name of the influencer.|
|influencer_field_value|string|true|none|The entity that influenced, contributed to, or was to blame for the anomaly.|
|initial_influencer_score|number|true|none|A normalized score between 0-100, which is based on the probability of the influencer aggregated across detectors.<br>This is the initial value that was calculated at the time the bucket was processed.|
|is_interim|boolean|true|none|If true, this is an interim result. In other words, the results are calculated based on partial input data.|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|probability|number|true|none|The probability that the influencer has this behavior, in the range 0 to 1. This value can be held to a high<br>precision of over 300 decimal places, so the `influencer_score` is provided as a human-readable and friendly<br>interpretation of this value.|
|result_type|string|true|none|Internal. This value is always set to `influencer`.|
|timestamp|object|true|none|The start time of the bucket for which these results were calculated.|
|foo|string|false|none|Additional influencer properties are added, depending on the fields being analyzed. For example, if it’s<br>analyzing `user_name` as an influencer, a field `user_name` is added to the result document. This<br>information enables you to filter the anomaly results more easily.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assignment_explanation|string|false|none|For open anomaly detection jobs only, contains messages relating to the selection of a node to run the job.|
|data_counts|object|true|none|An object that describes the quantity of input to the job and any related error counts.<br>The `data_count` values are cumulative for the lifetime of a job.<br>If a model snapshot is reverted or old results are deleted, the job counts are not reset.|
|forecasts_stats|object|true|none|An object that provides statistical information about forecasts belonging to this job.<br>Some statistics are omitted if no forecasts have been made.|
|job_id|string|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|model_size_stats|object|true|none|An object that provides information about the size and contents of the model.|
|node|object|false|none|Contains properties for the node that runs the job.<br>This information is available only for open jobs.|
|open_time|object|false|none|For open jobs only, the elapsed time for which the job has been open.|
|state|object|true|none|The status of the anomaly detection job, which can be one of the following values: `closed`, `closing`, `failed`, `opened`, `opening`.|
|timing_stats|object|true|none|An object that provides statistical information about timing aspect of this job.|
|deleting|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the process of deleting the job is in progress but not yet completed. It is only reported when `true`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_lazy_open|boolean|true|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Specifies whether this job can open when there is insufficient machine learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node.|
|analysis_config|object|true|none|The analysis configuration, which specifies how to analyze the data.<br>After you create a job, you cannot change the analysis configuration; all the properties are informational.|
|analysis_limits|object|false|none|Limits can be applied for the resources required to hold the mathematical models in memory.<br>These limits are approximate and can be set per job.<br>They do not control the memory used by other processes, for example the Elasticsearch Java processes.|
|background_persist_interval|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The time between each periodic persistence of the model.<br>The default value is a randomized value between 3 to 4 hours, which avoids all jobs persisting at exactly the same time.<br>The smallest allowed value is 1 hour.|
|blocked|object|false|none|none|
|create_time|object|false|none|none|
|custom_settings|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Contains custom metadata about the job.|
|daily_model_snapshot_retention_after_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job.<br>It specifies a period of time (in days) after which only the first snapshot per day is retained.<br>This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.<br>Valid values range from 0 to `model_snapshot_retention_days`.|
|data_description|object|true|none|The data description defines the format of the input data when you send data to the job by using the post data API.<br>Note that when configuring a datafeed, these properties are automatically set.<br>When data is received via the post data API, it is not stored in Elasticsearch.<br>Only the results for anomaly detection are retained.|
|datafeed_config|object|false|none|The datafeed, which retrieves data from Elasticsearch for analysis by the job.<br>You can associate only one datafeed with each anomaly detection job.|
|deleting|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the process of deleting the job is in progress but not yet completed.<br>It is only reported when `true`.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the job.|
|finished_time|object|false|none|If the job closed or failed, this is the time the job finished, otherwise it is `null`.<br>This property is informational; you cannot change its value.|
|groups|[string]|false|none|A list of job groups.<br>A job can belong to no groups or many.|
|job_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.<br>This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores.<br>It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|job_type|string|false|none|Reserved for future use, currently set to `anomaly_detector`.|
|job_version|object|false|none|The machine learning configuration version number at which the the job was created.|
|model_plot_config|object|false|none|This advanced configuration option stores model information along with the results.<br>It provides a more detailed view into anomaly detection.<br>Model plot provides a simplified and indicative view of the model and its bounds.|
|model_snapshot_id|object|false|none|none|
|model_snapshot_retention_days|number|true|none|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job.<br>It specifies the maximum period of time (in days) that snapshots are retained.<br>This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.<br>By default, snapshots ten days older than the newest snapshot are deleted.|
|renormalization_window_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period over which adjustments to the score are applied, as new data is seen.<br>The default value is the longer of 30 days or 100 `bucket_spans`.|
|results_index_name|object|true|none|A text string that affects the name of the machine learning results index.<br>The default value is `shared`, which generates an index named `.ml-anomalies-shared`.|
|results_retention_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period of time (in days) that results are retained.<br>Age is calculated relative to the timestamp of the latest bucket result.<br>If this property has a non-null value, once per day at 00:30 (server time), results that are the specified number of days older than the latest bucket result are deleted from Elasticsearch.<br>The default value is null, which means all results are retained.<br>Annotations generated by the system also count as results for retention purposes; they are deleted after the same number of days as results.<br>Annotations added by users are retained forever.|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.AnalysisLimits">ml._types.AnalysisLimits</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.analysislimits"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.AnalysisLimits"></a>
<a id="tocSml._types.analysislimits"></a>
<a id="tocsml._types.analysislimits"></a>

```json
{
  "categorization_examples_limit": 4,
  "model_memory_limit": "1024mb"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|categorization_examples_limit|number|false|none|The maximum number of examples stored per category in memory and in the results data store. If you increase this value, more examples are available, however it requires that you have more storage available. If you set this value to 0, no examples are stored. NOTE: The `categorization_examples_limit` applies only to analysis that uses categorization.|
|model_memory_limit|object|false|none|The approximate maximum amount of memory resources that are required for analytical processing. Once this limit is approached, data pruning becomes more aggressive. Upon exceeding this limit, new entities are not modeled. If the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting has a value greater than 0 and less than 1024mb, that value is used instead of the default. The default value is relatively small to ensure that high resource usage is a conscious decision. If you have jobs that are expected to analyze high cardinality fields, you will likely need to use a higher value. If you specify a number instead of a string, the units are assumed to be MiB. Specifying a string is recommended for clarity. If you specify a byte size unit of `b` or `kb` and the number does not equate to a discrete number of megabytes, it is rounded down to the closest MiB. The minimum valid value is 1 MiB. If you specify a value less than 1 MiB, an error occurs. If you specify a value for the `xpack.ml.max_model_memory_limit` setting, an error occurs when you try to create jobs that have `model_memory_limit` values greater than that setting value.|

|---|---|---|---|---|

|time_field|object|false|none|The name of the field that contains the timestamp.|
|time_format|string|false|none|The time format, which can be `epoch`, `epoch_ms`, or a custom pattern. The value `epoch` refers to UNIX or Epoch time (the number of seconds since 1 Jan 1970). The value `epoch_ms` indicates that time is measured in milliseconds since the epoch. The `epoch` and `epoch_ms` time formats accept either integer or real values. Custom patterns must conform to the Java DateTimeFormatter class. When you use date-time formatting patterns, it is recommended that you provide the full date, time and time zone. For example: `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssX`. If the pattern that you specify is not sufficient to produce a complete timestamp, job creation fails.|
|field_delimiter|string|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actual|[number]|false|none|The actual value for the bucket.|
|anomaly_score_explanation|object|false|none|Information about the factors impacting the initial anomaly score.|
|bucket_span|object|true|none|The length of the bucket in seconds. This value matches the `bucket_span` that is specified in the job.|
|by_field_name|string|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to their own history. It is used for finding unusual values in the context of the split.|
|by_field_value|string|false|none|The value of `by_field_name`.|
|causes|[[ml._types.AnomalyCause](#schemaml._types.anomalycause)]|false|none|For population analysis, an over field must be specified in the detector. This property contains an array of anomaly records that are the causes for the anomaly that has been identified for the over field. This sub-resource contains the most anomalous records for the `over_field_name`. For scalability reasons, a maximum of the 10 most significant causes of the anomaly are returned. As part of the core analytical modeling, these low-level anomaly records are aggregated for their parent over field record. The `causes` resource contains similar elements to the record resource, namely `actual`, `typical`, `geo_results.actual_point`, `geo_results.typical_point`, `*_field_name` and `*_field_value`. Probability and scores are not applicable to causes.|
|detector_index|number|true|none|A unique identifier for the detector.|
|field_name|string|false|none|Certain functions require a field to operate on, for example, `sum()`. For those functions, this value is the name of the field to be analyzed.|
|function|string|false|none|The function in which the anomaly occurs, as specified in the detector configuration. For example, `max`.|
|function_description|string|false|none|The description of the function in which the anomaly occurs, as specified in the detector configuration.|
|geo_results|object|false|none|If the detector function is `lat_long`, this object contains comma delimited strings for the latitude and longitude of the actual and typical values.|
|influencers|[[ml._types.Influence](#schemaml._types.influence)]|false|none|If influencers were specified in the detector configuration, this array contains influencers that contributed to or were to blame for an anomaly.|
|initial_record_score|number|true|none|A normalized score between 0-100, which is based on the probability of the anomalousness of this record. This is the initial value that was calculated at the time the bucket was processed.|
|is_interim|boolean|true|none|If true, this is an interim result. In other words, the results are calculated based on partial input data.|
|job_id|string|true|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.|
|over_field_name|string|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to the history of all splits. It is used for finding unusual values in the population of all splits.|
|over_field_value|string|false|none|The value of `over_field_name`.|
|partition_field_name|string|false|none|The field used to segment the analysis. When you use this property, you have completely independent baselines for each value of this field.|
|partition_field_value|string|false|none|The value of `partition_field_name`.|
|probability|number|true|none|The probability of the individual anomaly occurring, in the range 0 to 1. For example, `0.0000772031`. This value can be held to a high precision of over 300 decimal places, so the `record_score` is provided as a human-readable and friendly interpretation of this.|
|record_score|number|true|none|A normalized score between 0-100, which is based on the probability of the anomalousness of this record. Unlike `initial_record_score`, this value will be updated by a re-normalization process as new data is analyzed.|
|result_type|string|true|none|Internal. This is always set to `record`.|
|timestamp|object|true|none|The start time of the bucket for which these results were calculated.|
|typical|[number]|false|none|The typical value for the bucket, according to analytical modeling.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anomaly_characteristics_impact|number|false|none|Impact from the duration and magnitude of the detected anomaly relative to the historical average.|
|anomaly_length|number|false|none|Length of the detected anomaly in the number of buckets.|
|anomaly_type|string|false|none|Type of the detected anomaly: `spike` or `dip`.|
|high_variance_penalty|boolean|false|none|Indicates reduction of anomaly score for the bucket with large confidence intervals. If a bucket has large confidence intervals, the score is reduced.|
|incomplete_bucket_penalty|boolean|false|none|If the bucket contains fewer samples than expected, the score is reduced.|
|lower_confidence_bound|number|false|none|Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval.|
|multi_bucket_impact|number|false|none|Impact of the deviation between actual and typical values in the past 12 buckets.|
|single_bucket_impact|number|false|none|Impact of the deviation between actual and typical values in the current bucket.|
|typical_value|number|false|none|Typical (expected) value for this bucket.|
|upper_confidence_bound|number|false|none|Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the trained model.|
|model_type|object|false|none|The model type|
|tags|[string]|true|none|A comma delimited string of tags. A trained model can have many tags, or none.|
|version|object|false|none|The Elasticsearch version number in which the trained model was created.|
|compressed_definition|string|false|none|none|
|created_by|string|false|none|Information on the creator of the trained model.|
|create_time|object|false|none|The time when the trained model was created.|
|default_field_map|object|false|none|Any field map described in the inference configuration takes precedence.|
|description|string|false|none|The free-text description of the trained model.|
|estimated_heap_memory_usage_bytes|number|false|none|The estimated heap usage in bytes to keep the trained model in memory.|
|estimated_operations|number|false|none|The estimated number of operations to use the trained model.|
|fully_defined|boolean|false|none|True if the full model definition is present.|
|inference_config|object|false|none|The default configuration for inference. This can be either a regression, classification, or one of the many NLP focused configurations. It must match the underlying definition.trained_model's target_type. For pre-packaged models such as ELSER the config is not required.|
|input|object|true|none|The input field names for the model definition.|
|license_level|string|false|none|The license level of the trained model.|
|metadata|object|false|none|An object containing metadata about the trained model. For example, models created by data frame analytics contain analysis_config and input objects.|
|model_size_bytes|object|false|none|none|
|model_package|object|false|none|none|
|location|object|false|none|none|
|platform_architecture|string|false|none|none|
|prefix_strings|object|false|none|none|

Fill mask inference options

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mask_token|string|false|none|The string/token which will be removed from incoming documents and replaced with the inference prediction(s).<br>In a response, this field contains the mask token for the specified model/tokenizer. Each model and tokenizer<br>has a predefined mask token which cannot be changed. Thus, it is recommended not to set this value in requests.<br>However, if this field is present in a request, its value must match the predefined value for that model/tokenizer,<br>otherwise the request will fail.|
|num_top_classes|number|false|none|Specifies the number of top class predictions to return. Defaults to 0.|
|tokenization|object|false|none|The tokenization options to update when inferring|
|results_field|string|false|none|The field that is added to incoming documents to contain the inference prediction. Defaults to predicted_value.|
|vocabulary|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ml._types.Hyperparameter">ml._types.Hyperparameter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaml._types.hyperparameter"></a>
<a id="schema_ml._types.Hyperparameter"></a>

{
  "absolute_importance": 0,
  "name": {},
  "relative_importance": 0,
  "supplied": true,
  "value": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|absolute_importance|number|false|none|A positive number showing how much the parameter influences the variation of the loss function. For hyperparameters with values that are not specified by the user but tuned during hyperparameter optimization.|
|name|object|true|none|Name of the hyperparameter.|
|relative_importance|number|false|none|A number between 0 and 1 showing the proportion of influence on the variation of the loss function among all tuned hyperparameters. For hyperparameters with values that are not specified by the user but tuned during hyperparameter optimization.|
|supplied|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the hyperparameter is specified by the user (true) or optimized (false).|
|value|number|true|none|The value of the hyperparameter, either optimized or specified by the user.|

|failure_count|number|true|none|The number of failures when using the model for inference.|
|inference_count|number|true|none|The total number of times the model has been called for inference.<br>This is across all inference contexts, including all pipelines.|
|missing_all_fields_count|number|true|none|The number of inference calls where all the training features for the model were missing.|
|timestamp|object|true|none|The time when the statistics were last updated.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|entities|[[ml._types.TrainedModelEntities](#schemaml._types.trainedmodelentities)]|false|none|If the model is trained for named entity recognition (NER) tasks, the response contains the recognized entities.|
|is_truncated|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the input text was truncated to meet the model's maximum sequence length limit. This property<br>is present only when it is true.|
|predicted_value|[ml._types.PredictedValue](#schemaml._types.predictedvalue) \| [[ml._types.PredictedValue](#schemaml._types.predictedvalue)]|false|none|If the model is trained for a text classification or zero shot classification task, the response is the<br>predicted class.<br>For named entity recognition (NER) tasks, it contains the annotated text output.<br>For fill mask tasks, it contains the top prediction for replacing the mask token.<br>For text embedding tasks, it contains the raw numerical text embedding values.<br>For regression models, its a numerical value<br>For classification models, it may be an integer, double, boolean or string depending on prediction type|
|predicted_value_sequence|string|false|none|For fill mask tasks, the response contains the input text sequence with the mask token replaced by the predicted<br>value.<br>Additionally|
|prediction_probability|number|false|none|Specifies a probability for the predicted value.|
|prediction_score|number|false|none|Specifies a confidence score for the predicted value.|
|top_classes|[[ml._types.TopClassEntry](#schemaml._types.topclassentry)]|false|none|For fill mask, text classification, and zero shot classification tasks, the response contains a list of top<br>class entries.|
|warning|string|false|none|If the request failed, the response contains the reason for the failure.|
|feature_importance|[[ml._types.TrainedModelInferenceFeatureImportance](#schemaml._types.trainedmodelinferencefeatureimportance)]|false|none|The feature importance for the inference results. Relevant only for classification or regression models|

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|If set, the datafeed performs aggregation searches. Support for aggregations is limited and should be used only with low cardinality data.|
|chunking_config|object|false|none|Datafeeds might be required to search over long time periods, for several months or years. This search is split into time chunks in order to ensure the load on Elasticsearch is managed. Chunking configuration controls how the size of these time chunks are calculated and is an advanced configuration option.|
|datafeed_id|object|false|none|A numerical character string that uniquely identifies the datafeed. This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores. It must start and end with alphanumeric characters. The default value is the job identifier.|
|delayed_data_check_config|object|false|none|Specifies whether the datafeed checks for missing data and the size of the window. The datafeed can optionally search over indices that have already been read in an effort to determine whether any data has subsequently been added to the index. If missing data is found, it is a good indication that the `query_delay` option is set too low and the data is being indexed after the datafeed has passed that moment in time. This check runs only on real-time datafeeds.|
|frequency|object|false|none|The interval at which scheduled queries are made while the datafeed runs in real time. The default value is either the bucket span for short bucket spans, or, for longer bucket spans, a sensible fraction of the bucket span. For example: `150s`. When `frequency` is shorter than the bucket span, interim results for the last (partial) bucket are written then eventually overwritten by the full bucket results. If the datafeed uses aggregations, this value must be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|indices|object|false|none|An array of index names. Wildcards are supported. If any indices are in remote clusters, the machine learning nodes must have the `remote_cluster_client` role.|
|indices_options|object|false|none|Specifies index expansion options that are used during search.|
|job_id|object|false|none|none|
|max_empty_searches|number|false|none|If a real-time datafeed has never seen any data (including during any initial training period) then it will automatically stop itself and close its associated job after this many real-time searches that return no documents. In other words, it will stop after `frequency` times `max_empty_searches` of real-time operation. If not set then a datafeed with no end time that sees no data will remain started until it is explicitly stopped.|
|max_consecutive_extraction_failures|number|false|none|The maximum number of consecutive real-time data extraction failures the datafeed tolerates before it automatically stops itself, leaving the associated job open. The consecutive-failure counter resets on any cycle that extracts successfully, including empty-data cycles. If not set, the threshold defaults to roughly one day's worth of searches based on the datafeed `frequency` (floored at 1). Set to `-1` to disable auto-stop and retry indefinitely. Values of `0` or less than `-1` are rejected.|
|query|object|false|none|The Elasticsearch query domain-specific language (DSL). This value corresponds to the query object in an Elasticsearch search POST body. All the options that are supported by Elasticsearch can be used, as this object is passed verbatim to Elasticsearch.|
|query_delay|object|false|none|The number of seconds behind real time that data is queried. For example, if data from 10:04 a.m. might not be searchable in Elasticsearch until 10:06 a.m., set this property to 120 seconds. The default value is randomly selected between `60s` and `120s`. This randomness improves the query performance when there are multiple jobs running on the same node.|
|runtime_mappings|object|false|none|Specifies runtime fields for the datafeed search.|
|script_fields|object|false|none|Specifies scripts that evaluate custom expressions and returns script fields to the datafeed. The detector configuration objects in a job can contain functions that use these script fields.|
|scroll_size|number|false|none|The size parameter that is used in Elasticsearch searches when the datafeed does not use aggregations. The maximum value is the value of `index.max_result_window`, which is 10,000 by default.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_lazy_open|boolean|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Specifies whether this job can open when there is insufficient machine learning node capacity for it to be immediately assigned to a node.|
|analysis_config|object|true|none|The analysis configuration, which specifies how to analyze the data.<br>After you create a job, you cannot change the analysis configuration; all the properties are informational.|
|analysis_limits|object|false|none|Limits can be applied for the resources required to hold the mathematical models in memory.<br>These limits are approximate and can be set per job.<br>They do not control the memory used by other processes, for example the Elasticsearch Java processes.|
|background_persist_interval|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The time between each periodic persistence of the model.<br>The default value is a randomized value between 3 to 4 hours, which avoids all jobs persisting at exactly the same time.<br>The smallest allowed value is 1 hour.|
|custom_settings|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>Contains custom metadata about the job.|
|daily_model_snapshot_retention_after_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job.<br>It specifies a period of time (in days) after which only the first snapshot per day is retained.<br>This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.|
|data_description|object|true|none|The data description defines the format of the input data when you send data to the job by using the post data API.<br>Note that when configure a datafeed, these properties are automatically set.|
|datafeed_config|object|false|none|The datafeed, which retrieves data from Elasticsearch for analysis by the job.<br>You can associate only one datafeed with each anomaly detection job.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the job.|
|groups|[string]|false|none|A list of job groups. A job can belong to no groups or many.|
|job_id|object|false|none|Identifier for the anomaly detection job.<br>This identifier can contain lowercase alphanumeric characters (a-z and 0-9), hyphens, and underscores.<br>It must start and end with alphanumeric characters.|
|model_plot_config|object|false|none|This advanced configuration option stores model information along with the results.<br>It provides a more detailed view into anomaly detection.<br>Model plot provides a simplified and indicative view of the model and its bounds.|
|model_snapshot_retention_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option, which affects the automatic removal of old model snapshots for this job.<br>It specifies the maximum period of time (in days) that snapshots are retained.<br>This period is relative to the timestamp of the most recent snapshot for this job.<br>The default value is `10`, which means snapshots ten days older than the newest snapshot are deleted.|
|renormalization_window_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period over which adjustments to the score are applied, as new data is seen.<br>The default value is the longer of 30 days or 100 `bucket_spans`.|
|results_index_name|object|false|none|A text string that affects the name of the machine learning results index.<br>The default value is `shared`, which generates an index named `.ml-anomalies-shared`.|
|results_retention_days|number|false|none|Advanced configuration option.<br>The period of time (in days) that results are retained.<br>Age is calculated relative to the timestamp of the latest bucket result.<br>If this property has a non-null value, once per day at 00:30 (server time), results that are the specified number of days older than the latest bucket result are deleted from Elasticsearch.<br>The default value is null, which means all results are retained.<br>Annotations generated by the system also count as results for retention purposes; they are deleted after the same number of days as results.<br>Annotations added by users are retained forever.|

  "per_partition_categorization": {
    "enabled": true,
    "stop_on_warn": true
  },
  "summary_count_field_name": {}

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucket_span|object|true|none|The size of the interval that the analysis is aggregated into, typically between `5m` and `1h`. This value should be either a whole number of days or equate to a<br>whole number of buckets in one day. If the anomaly detection job uses a datafeed with aggregations, this value must also be divisible by the interval of the date histogram aggregation.|
|detectors|[[ml._types.DetectorRead](#schemaml._types.detectorread)]|true|none|Detector configuration objects specify which data fields a job analyzes. They also specify which analytical functions are used. You can specify multiple detectors for a job. If the detectors array does not contain at least one detector, no analysis can occur and an error is returned.|
|influencers|[[_types.Field](#schema_types.field)]|true|none|A comma separated list of influencer field names. Typically these can be the by, over, or partition fields that are used in the detector configuration. You might also want to use a field name that is not specifically named in a detector, but is available as part of the input data. When you use multiple detectors, the use of influencers is recommended as it aggregates results for each influencer entity.|
|categorization_analyzer|object|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define the analyzer that is used to interpret the categorization field. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_filters`. The categorization analyzer specifies how the `categorization_field` is interpreted by the categorization process. The `categorization_analyzer` field can be specified either as a string or as an object. If it is a string, it must refer to a built-in analyzer or one added by another plugin.|
|categorization_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the values of the specified field will be categorized. The resulting categories must be used in a detector by setting `by_field_name`, `over_field_name`, or `partition_field_name` to the keyword `mlcategory`.|
|categorization_filters|[string]|false|none|If `categorization_field_name` is specified, you can also define optional filters. This property expects an array of regular expressions. The expressions are used to filter out matching sequences from the categorization field values. You can use this functionality to fine tune the categorization by excluding sequences from consideration when categories are defined. For example, you can exclude SQL statements that appear in your log files. This property cannot be used at the same time as `categorization_analyzer`. If you only want to define simple regular expression filters that are applied prior to tokenization, setting this property is the easiest method. If you also want to customize the tokenizer or post-tokenization filtering, use the `categorization_analyzer` property instead and include the filters as pattern_replace character filters. The effect is exactly the same.|
|latency|object|false|none|The size of the window in which to expect data that is out of time order. If you specify a non-zero value, it must be greater than or equal to one second. NOTE: Latency is applicable only when you send data by using the post data API.|
|model_prune_window|object|false|none|Advanced configuration option. Affects the pruning of models that have not been updated for the given time duration. The value must be set to a multiple of the `bucket_span`. If set too low, important information may be removed from the model. For jobs created in 8.1 and later, the default value is the greater of `30d` or 20 times `bucket_span`.|
|multivariate_by_fields|boolean|false|none|This functionality is reserved for internal use. It is not supported for use in customer environments and is not subject to the support SLA of official GA features. If set to `true`, the analysis will automatically find correlations between metrics for a given by field value and report anomalies when those correlations cease to hold. For example, suppose CPU and memory usage on host A is usually highly correlated with the same metrics on host B. Perhaps this correlation occurs because they are running a load-balanced application. If you enable this property, anomalies will be reported when, for example, CPU usage on host A is high and the value of CPU usage on host B is low. That is to say, you’ll see an anomaly when the CPU of host A is unusual given the CPU of host B. To use the `multivariate_by_fields` property, you must also specify `by_field_name` in your detector.|
|per_partition_categorization|object|false|none|Settings related to how categorization interacts with partition fields.|
|summary_count_field_name|object|false|none|If this property is specified, the data that is fed to the job is expected to be pre-summarized. This property value is the name of the field that contains the count of raw data points that have been summarized. The same `summary_count_field_name` applies to all detectors in the job. NOTE: The `summary_count_field_name` property cannot be used with the `metric` function.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|function|string|true|none|The analysis function that is used. For example, `count`, `rare`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, or `sum`.|
|by_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to their own history. It is used for finding unusual values in the context of the split.|
|custom_rules|[[ml._types.DetectionRule](#schemaml._types.detectionrule)]|false|none|Custom rules enable you to customize the way detectors operate. For example, a rule may dictate conditions under which results should be skipped. Kibana refers to custom rules as job rules.|
|detector_description|string|false|none|A description of the detector.|
|detector_index|number|false|none|A unique identifier for the detector. This identifier is based on the order of the detectors in the `analysis_config`, starting at zero. If you specify a value for this property, it is ignored.|
|exclude_frequent|object|false|none|If set, frequent entities are excluded from influencing the anomaly results. Entities can be considered frequent over time or frequent in a population. If you are working with both over and by fields, you can set `exclude_frequent` to `all` for both fields, or to `by` or `over` for those specific fields.|
|field_name|object|false|none|The field that the detector uses in the function. If you use an event rate function such as count or rare, do not specify this field. The `field_name` cannot contain double quotes or backslashes.|
|over_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to the history of all splits. It is used for finding unusual values in the population of all splits.|
|partition_field_name|object|false|none|The field used to segment the analysis. When you use this property, you have completely independent baselines for each value of this field.|
|use_null|boolean|false|none|Defines whether a new series is used as the null series when there is no value for the by or partition fields.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|object|false|none|The ID of the document.|
|_index|object|false|none|The index of the document.|
|doc|object|false|none|An artificial document (a document not present in the index) for which you want to retrieve term vectors.|
|fields|object|false|none|Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.<br>Used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.|
|field_statistics|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the response includes the document count, sum of document frequencies, and sum of total term frequencies.|
|filter|object|false|none|Filter terms based on their tf-idf scores.|
|offsets|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the response includes term offsets.|
|payloads|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the response includes term payloads.|
|positions|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the response includes term positions.|
|routing|object|false|none|Custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.|
|term_statistics|boolean|false|none|If true, the response includes term frequency and document frequency.|
|version|object|false|none|If `true`, returns the document version as part of a hit.|
|version_type|object|false|none|Specific version type.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_doc_freq|number|false|none|Ignore words which occur in more than this many docs.<br>Defaults to unbounded.|
|max_num_terms|number|false|none|The maximum number of terms that must be returned per field.|
|max_term_freq|number|false|none|Ignore words with more than this frequency in the source doc.<br>It defaults to unbounded.|
|max_word_length|number|false|none|The maximum word length above which words will be ignored.<br>Defaults to unbounded.|
|min_doc_freq|number|false|none|Ignore terms which do not occur in at least this many docs.|
|min_term_freq|number|false|none|Ignore words with less than this frequency in the source doc.|
|min_word_length|number|false|none|The minimum word length below which words will be ignored.|

|repository_ephemeral_id|object|true|none|An identifier that changes every time the repository is updated.|
|repository_started_at|object|true|none|Time the repository was created or updated. Recorded in milliseconds since the Unix Epoch.|
|repository_stopped_at|object|false|none|Time the repository was deleted or updated. Recorded in milliseconds since the Unix Epoch.|
|archived|boolean|true|none|A flag that tells whether or not this object has been archived. When a repository is closed or updated the<br>repository metering information is archived and kept for a certain period of time. This allows retrieving the<br>repository metering information of previous repository instantiations.|
|cluster_version|object|false|none|The cluster state version when this object was archived, this field can be used as a logical timestamp to delete<br>all the archived metrics up to an observed version. This field is only present for archived repository metering<br>information objects. The main purpose of this field is to avoid possible race conditions during repository metering<br>information deletions, i.e. deleting archived repositories metering information that we haven’t observed yet.|
|request_counts|object|true|none|An object with the number of request performed against the repository grouped by request type.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|arch|string|true|none|Name of the JVM architecture (ex: amd64, x86)|
|available_processors|number|true|none|Number of processors available to the Java virtual machine|
|allocated_processors|number|false|none|The number of processors actually used to calculate thread pool size. This number can be set with the node.processors setting of a node and defaults to the number of processors reported by the OS.|
|name|object|true|none|Name of the operating system (ex: Linux, Windows, Mac OS X)|
|pretty_name|object|true|none|none|
|refresh_interval_in_millis|object|true|none|Refresh interval for the OS statistics|
|version|object|true|none|Version of the operating system|
|cpu|object|false|none|none|
|mem|object|false|none|none|
|swap|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adaptive_selection|object|false|none|Statistics about adaptive replica selection.|
|allocations|object|false|none|Statistics about shard allocations on the node.|
|breakers|object|false|none|Statistics about the field data circuit breaker.|
|fs|object|false|none|File system information, data path, free disk space, read/write stats.|
|host|object|false|none|Network host for the node, based on the network host setting.|
|http|object|false|none|HTTP connection information.|
|ingest|object|false|none|Statistics about ingest preprocessing.|
|ip|[_types.Ip](#schema_types.ip) \| [[_types.Ip](#schema_types.ip)]|false|none|IP address and port for the node.|
|jvm|object|false|none|JVM stats, memory pool information, garbage collection, buffer pools, number of loaded/unloaded classes.|
|name|object|false|none|Human-readable identifier for the node.<br>Based on the node name setting.|
|os|object|false|none|Operating system stats, load average, mem, swap.|
|process|object|false|none|Process statistics, memory consumption, cpu usage, open file descriptors.|
|roles|object|false|none|Roles assigned to the node.|
|script|object|false|none|Contains script statistics for the node.|
|script_cache|object|false|none|none|
|thread_pool|object|false|none|Statistics about each thread pool, including current size, queue and rejected tasks.|
|timestamp|number|false|none|none|
|transport|object|false|none|Transport statistics about sent and received bytes in cluster communication.|
|transport_address|object|false|none|Host and port for the transport layer, used for internal communication between nodes in a cluster.|
|attributes|object|false|none|Contains a list of attributes for the node.|
|discovery|object|false|none|Contains node discovery statistics for the node.|
|indexing_pressure|object|false|none|Contains indexing pressure statistics for the node.|
|indices|object|false|none|Indices stats about size, document count, indexing and deletion times, search times, field cache size, merges and flushes.|
|repositories|object|false|none|Statistics about snapshot activity for the node's registered repositories, keyed by repository name.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|avg_queue_size|number|false|none|The exponentially weighted moving average queue size of search requests on the keyed node.|
|avg_response_time|object|false|none|The exponentially weighted moving average response time of search requests on the keyed node.|
|avg_response_time_ns|number|false|none|The exponentially weighted moving average response time, in nanoseconds, of search requests on the keyed node.|
|avg_service_time|object|false|none|The exponentially weighted moving average service time of search requests on the keyed node.|
|avg_service_time_ns|number|false|none|The exponentially weighted moving average service time, in nanoseconds, of search requests on the keyed node.|
|outgoing_searches|number|false|none|The number of outstanding search requests to the keyed node from the node these stats are for.|
|rank|string|false|none|The rank of this node; used for shard selection when routing search requests.|

### Properties

|forecasted_ingest_load|number|false|none|Forecasted ingest load for the node.|
|forecasted_disk_usage|string|false|none|Forecasted disk usage for the node.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|control_group|string|false|none|The `memory` control group to which the Elasticsearch process belongs.|
|limit_in_bytes|string|false|none|The maximum amount of user memory (including file cache) allowed for all tasks in the same cgroup as the Elasticsearch process.<br>This value can be too big to store in a `long`, so is returned as a string so that the value returned can exactly match what the underlying operating system interface returns.<br>Any value that is too large to parse into a `long` almost certainly means no limit has been set for the cgroup.|
|usage_in_bytes|string|false|none|The total current memory usage by processes in the cgroup, in bytes, by all tasks in the same cgroup as the Elasticsearch process.<br>This value is stored as a string for consistency with `limit_in_bytes`.|

|cluster_applier_stats|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_nodes._types.ClusterStateUpdate">nodes._types.ClusterStateUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanodes._types.clusterstateupdate"></a>
<a id="schema_nodes._types.ClusterStateUpdate"></a>

<a id="tocsnodes._types.clusterstateupdate"></a>

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "computation_time": {},
  "computation_time_millis": {},
  "publication_time": {},
  "publication_time_millis": {},
  "context_construction_time": {},
  "context_construction_time_millis": {},
  "commit_time": {},
  "commit_time_millis": {},
  "completion_time": {},
  "completion_time_millis": {},
  "master_apply_time": {},
  "master_apply_time_millis": {},
  "notification_time": {},
  "notification_time_millis": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|true|none|The number of cluster state update attempts that did not change the cluster state since the node started.|
|computation_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent computing no-op cluster state updates since the node started.|
|computation_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent computing no-op cluster state updates since the node started.|
|publication_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent publishing cluster state updates which ultimately succeeded, which includes everything from the start of the publication (just after the computation of the new cluster state) until the publication has finished and the master node is ready to start processing the next state update.<br>This includes the time measured by `context_construction_time`, `commit_time`, `completion_time` and `master_apply_time`.|
|publication_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent publishing cluster state updates which ultimately succeeded, which includes everything from the start of the publication (just after the computation of the new cluster state) until the publication has finished and the master node is ready to start processing the next state update.<br>This includes the time measured by `context_construction_time`, `commit_time`, `completion_time` and `master_apply_time`.|
|context_construction_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent constructing a publication context since the node started for publications that ultimately succeeded.<br>This statistic includes the time spent computing the difference between the current and new cluster state preparing a serialized representation of this difference.|
|context_construction_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent constructing a publication context since the node started for publications that ultimately succeeded.<br>This statistic includes the time spent computing the difference between the current and new cluster state preparing a serialized representation of this difference.|
|commit_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent waiting for a successful cluster state update to commit, which measures the time from the start of each publication until a majority of the master-eligible nodes have written the state to disk and confirmed the write to the elected master.|
|commit_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent waiting for a successful cluster state update to commit, which measures the time from the start of each publication until a majority of the master-eligible nodes have written the state to disk and confirmed the write to the elected master.|
|completion_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent waiting for a successful cluster state update to complete, which measures the time from the start of each publication until all the other nodes have notified the elected master that they have applied the cluster state.|
|completion_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds,  spent waiting for a successful cluster state update to complete, which measures the time from the start of each publication until all the other nodes have notified the elected master that they have applied the cluster state.|
|master_apply_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent successfully applying cluster state updates on the elected master since the node started.|
|master_apply_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent successfully applying cluster state updates on the elected master since the node started.|
|notification_time|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time spent notifying listeners of a no-op cluster state update since the node started.|
|notification_time_millis|object|false|none|The cumulative amount of time, in milliseconds, spent notifying listeners of a no-op cluster state update since the node started.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|true|none|The type of criteria. The following criteria types are supported:<br><br>* `always`: Matches all queries, regardless of input.<br>* `contains`: Matches that contain this value anywhere in the field meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for string values.<br>* `exact`: Only exact matches meet the criteria defined by the rule. Applicable for string or numerical values.<br>* `fuzzy`: Exact matches or matches within the allowed Levenshtein Edit Distance meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for string values.<br>* `gt`: Matches with a value greater than this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for numerical values.<br>* `gte`: Matches with a value greater than or equal to this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for numerical values.<br>* `lt`: Matches with a value less than this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for numerical values.<br>* `lte`: Matches with a value less than or equal to this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for numerical values.<br>* `prefix`: Matches that start with this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for string values.<br>* `suffix`: Matches that end with this value meet the criteria defined by the rule. Only applicable for string values.|
|metadata|string|false|none|The metadata field to match against.<br>This metadata will be used to match against `match_criteria` sent in the rule.<br>It is required for all criteria types except `always`.|
|values|[object]|false|none|The values to match against the `metadata` field.<br>Only one value must match for the criteria to be met.<br>It is required for all criteria types except `always`.|

|rule_criteria_types_counts|object|true|none|A map of criteria type (for example, `exact`) to the number of rules of that type.<br><br>NOTE: The counts in `rule_criteria_types_counts` may be larger than the value of `rule_total_count` because a rule may have multiple criteria.|
|rule_type_counts|object|true|none|A map of rule type (for example, `pinned`) to the number of rules of that type.|

Precision at K (P@k)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|k|number|false|none|Sets the maximum number of documents retrieved per query. This value will act in place of the usual size parameter in the query.|
|relevant_rating_threshold|number|false|none|Sets the rating threshold above which documents are considered to be "relevant".|
|ignore_unlabeled|boolean|false|none|Controls how unlabeled documents in the search results are counted. If set to true, unlabeled documents are ignored and neither count as relevant or irrelevant. Set to false (the default), they are treated as irrelevant.|

|index|object|true|none|The name of the data stream, index, or index alias you are copying to.|
|op_type|object|false|none|If it is `create`, the operation will only index documents that do not already exist (also known as "put if absent").<br><br>IMPORTANT: To reindex to a data stream destination, this argument must be `create`.|
|pipeline|string|false|none|The name of the pipeline to use.|
|routing|string|false|none|By default, a document's routing is preserved unless it's changed by the script.<br>If it is `keep`, the routing on the bulk request sent for each match is set to the routing on the match.<br>If it is `discard`, the routing on the bulk request sent for each match is set to `null`.<br>If it is `=value`, the routing on the bulk request sent for each match is set to all value specified after the equals sign (`=`).<br>Not allowed when `index.slice.enabled` is `true` for the destination index; use `_slice` instead.|
|version_type|object|false|none|The versioning to use for the indexing operation.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|object|true|none|The name of the data stream, index, or alias you are copying from.<br>It accepts a comma-separated list to reindex from multiple sources.|
|query|object|false|none|The documents to reindex, which is defined with Query DSL.|
|remote|object|false|none|A remote instance of Elasticsearch that you want to index from.|
|size|number|false|none|The number of documents to index per batch.<br>Use it when you are indexing from remote to ensure that the batches fit within the on-heap buffer, which defaults to a maximum size of 100 MB.|
|slice|object|false|none|Slice the reindex request manually using the provided slice ID and total number of slices.|
|sort|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** A comma-separated list of `<field>:<direction>` pairs to sort by before indexing.<br>Use it in conjunction with `max_docs` to control what documents are reindexed.<br><br>WARNING: Sort in reindex is deprecated.<br>Sorting in reindex was never guaranteed to index documents in order and prevents further development of reindex such as resilience and performance improvements.<br>If used in combination with `max_docs`, consider using a query filter instead.|
|_source|object|false|none|If `true`, reindex all source fields.<br>Set it to a list to reindex select fields.|
|runtime_mappings|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connect_timeout|object|false|none|The remote connection timeout.|
|headers|object|false|none|An object containing the headers of the request.|
|host|object|true|none|The URL for the remote instance of Elasticsearch that you want to index from.<br>This information is required when you're indexing from remote.|
|username|object|false|none|The username to use for authentication with the remote host (required when using basic auth).|
|password|object|false|none|The password to use for authentication with the remote host (required when using basic auth).|
|api_key|string|false|none|The API key to use for authentication with the remote host (as an alternative to basic auth when the remote cluster is in Elastic Cloud).<br>(It is not permitted to set this and also to set an `Authorization` header via `headers`.)|
|socket_timeout|object|false|none|The remote socket read timeout.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
