|slices|[[_types.ReindexStatus](#schema_types.reindexstatus)]|false|none|none|
|slice_id|number|false|none|The slice ID|
|batches|number|true|none|The number of scroll responses pulled back by the reindex.|
|created|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully created.|
|deleted|number|true|none|The number of documents that were successfully deleted.|
|noops|number|true|none|The number of documents that were ignored because the script used for the reindex returned a `noop` value for `ctx.op`.|
|requests_per_second|number|true|none|The number of requests per second effectively executed during the reindex.|
|retries|object|true|none|The number of retries attempted by reindex. `bulk` is the number of bulk actions retried and `search` is the number of search actions retried.|
|throttled|object|false|none|none|
|throttled_millis|object|true|none|Number of milliseconds the request slept to conform to `requests_per_second`.|
|throttled_until|object|false|none|none|
|throttled_until_millis|object|true|none|This field should always be equal to zero in a `_reindex` response.<br>It only has meaning when using the Task API, where it indicates the next time (in milliseconds since epoch) a throttled request will be executed again in order to conform to `requests_per_second`.|
|total|number|true|none|The number of documents that were successfully processed.|
|updated|number|false|none|The number of documents that were successfully updated, for example, a document with same ID already existed prior to reindex updating it.|
|version_conflicts|number|true|none|The number of version conflicts that reindex hits.|
|cancelled|string|false|none|The reason for cancellation if the slice was canceled|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date_histogram|object|false|none|A date histogram group aggregates a date field into time-based buckets.<br>This group is mandatory; you currently cannot roll up documents without a timestamp and a `date_histogram` group.|
|histogram|object|false|none|The histogram group aggregates one or more numeric fields into numeric histogram intervals.|
|terms|object|false|none|The terms group can be used on keyword or numeric fields to allow bucketing via the terms aggregation at a later point.<br>The indexer enumerates and stores all values of a field for each time-period.<br>This can be potentially costly for high-cardinality groups such as IP addresses, especially if the time-bucket is particularly sparse.|

<h2 id="tocS_rollup._types.DateHistogramGrouping">rollup._types.DateHistogramGrouping</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarollup._types.datehistogramgrouping"></a>
<a id="schema_rollup._types.DateHistogramGrouping"></a>
<a id="tocSrollup._types.datehistogramgrouping"></a>
<a id="tocsrollup._types.datehistogramgrouping"></a>

```json
{
  "delay": {},
  "field": {},
  "format": "string",
  "interval": {},
  "calendar_interval": {},
  "fixed_interval": {},
  "time_zone": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delay|object|false|none|How long to wait before rolling up new documents.<br>By default, the indexer attempts to roll up all data that is available.<br>However, it is not uncommon for data to arrive out of order.<br>The indexer is unable to deal with data that arrives after a time-span has been rolled up.<br>You need to specify a delay that matches the longest period of time you expect out-of-order data to arrive.|
|field|object|true|none|The date field that is to be rolled up.|
|format|string|false|none|none|
|interval|object|false|none|none|
|calendar_interval|object|false|none|The interval of time buckets to be generated when rolling up.|
|fixed_interval|object|false|none|The interval of time buckets to be generated when rolling up.|
|time_zone|object|false|none|Defines what `time_zone` the rollup documents are stored as.<br>Unlike raw data, which can shift timezones on the fly, rolled documents have to be stored with a specific timezone.<br>By default, rollup documents are stored in `UTC`.|

```json
  "fields": {},
  "interval": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|object|true|none|The set of fields that you wish to build histograms for.<br>All fields specified must be some kind of numeric.<br>Order does not matter.|
|interval|number|true|none|The interval of histogram buckets to be generated when rolling up.<br>For example, a value of `5` creates buckets that are five units wide (`0-5`, `5-10`, etc).<br>Note that only one interval can be specified in the histogram group, meaning that all fields being grouped via the histogram must share the same interval.|

|index|object|true|none|Index containing a mapping that's compatible with the indexed document.<br>You may specify a remote index by prefixing the index with the remote cluster alias.<br>For example, `remote1:my_index` indicates that you want to run the painless script against the "my_index" index on the "remote1" cluster.<br>This request will be forwarded to the "remote1" cluster if you have configured a connection to that remote cluster.<br><br>NOTE: Wildcards are not accepted in the index expression for this endpoint.<br>The expression `*:myindex` will return the error "No such remote cluster" and the expression `logs*` or `remote1:logs*` will return the error "index not found".|
|query|object|false|none|Use this parameter to specify a query for computing a score.|

While creating or updating a role you can provide either a JSON structure or a string to the API.
However, the response provided by Elasticsearch will only be string with a json-as-text content.

Since this is embedded in `IndicesPrivileges`, the same structure is used for clarity in both contexts.

The subset of index level privileges that can be defined for remote clusters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusters|object|true|none|A list of cluster aliases to which the permissions in this entry apply.|
|field_security|object|false|none|The document fields that the owners of the role have read access to.|
|names|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|true|none|A list of indices (or index name patterns) to which the permissions in this entry apply.|
|privileges|[[security._types.IndexPrivilege](#schemasecurity._types.indexprivilege)]|true|none|The index level privileges that owners of the role have on the specified indices.|
|query|object|false|none|A search query that defines the documents the owners of the role have access to. A document within the specified indices must match this query for it to be accessible by the owners of the role.|
|allow_restricted_indices|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` if using wildcard or regular expressions for patterns that cover restricted indices. Implicitly, restricted indices have limited privileges that can cause pattern tests to fail. If restricted indices are explicitly included in the `names` list, Elasticsearch checks privileges against these indices regardless of the value set for `allow_restricted_indices`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|true|none|Id for the API key|
|name|object|true|none|Name of the API key.|
|type|object|true|none|The type of the API key (e.g. `rest` or `cross_cluster`).|
|creation|object|true|none|Creation time for the API key in milliseconds.|
|expiration|object|false|none|Expiration time for the API key in milliseconds.|
|invalidated|boolean|true|none|Invalidation status for the API key.<br>If the key has been invalidated, it has a value of `true`. Otherwise, it is `false`.|
|invalidation|object|false|none|If the key has been invalidated, invalidation time in milliseconds.|
|username|object|true|none|Principal for which this API key was created|
|realm|string|true|none|Realm name of the principal for which this API key was created.|
|realm_type|string|false|none|Realm type of the principal for which this API key was created|
|metadata|object|true|none|Metadata of the API key|
|role_descriptors|object|false|none|The role descriptors assigned to this API key when it was created or last updated.<br>An empty role descriptor means the API key inherits the owner user’s permissions.|
|limited_by|[object]|false|none|The owner user’s permissions associated with the API key.<br>It is a point-in-time snapshot captured at creation and subsequent updates.<br>An API key’s effective permissions are an intersection of its assigned privileges and the owner user’s permissions.|
|access|object|false|none|The access granted to cross-cluster API keys.<br>The access is composed of permissions for cross cluster search and cross cluster replication.<br>At least one of them must be specified.<br>When specified, the new access assignment fully replaces the previously assigned access.|
|certificate_identity|string|false|none|The certificate identity associated with a cross-cluster API key.<br>Restricts the API key to connections authenticated by a specific TLS certificate.<br>Only applicable to cross-cluster API keys.|
|profile_uid|string|false|none|The profile uid for the API key owner principal, if requested and if it exists|
|_sort|object|false|none|Sorting values when using the `sort` parameter with the `security.query_api_keys` API.|

<h2 id="tocS_security.get_role.IndicesPrivilegesRead">security.get_role.IndicesPrivilegesRead</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasecurity.get_role.indicesprivilegesread"></a>
<a id="schema_security.get_role.IndicesPrivilegesRead"></a>
<a id="tocSsecurity.get_role.indicesprivilegesread"></a>
<a id="tocssecurity.get_role.indicesprivilegesread"></a>

```json
{
  "implicitly_granted": true,
  "field_security": {
    "except": {},
    "grant": {}
  },
  "names": "string",
  "privileges": [
    "all"
  ],
  "query": {},
  "allow_restricted_indices": false
}
```

Read-side variant of `IndicesPrivileges` returned by the get role API.
Carries the `implicitly_granted` marker that is set on entries contributed by
a registered `ImplicitPrivilegesProvider` when `include_implicit` is `true`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|implicitly_granted|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` on entries that were contributed by a registered `ImplicitPrivilegesProvider`<br>rather than explicitly stored on the role. Only present when the get role API is called with<br>`include_implicit=true`. The put role API rejects this field, so clients must not echo it back<br>on a GET-then-PUT round-trip.|
|field_security|object|false|none|The document fields that the owners of the role have read access to.|
|names|[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname) \| [[_types.IndexName](#schema_types.indexname)]|true|none|A list of indices (or index name patterns) to which the permissions in this entry apply.|
|privileges|[[security._types.IndexPrivilege](#schemasecurity._types.indexprivilege)]|true|none|The index level privileges that owners of the role have on the specified indices.|
|query|object|false|none|A search query that defines the documents the owners of the role have access to. A document within the specified indices must match this query for it to be accessible by the owners of the role.|
|allow_restricted_indices|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` if using wildcard or regular expressions for patterns that cover restricted indices. Implicitly, restricted indices have limited privileges that can cause pattern tests to fail. If restricted indices are explicitly included in the `names` list, Elasticsearch checks privileges against these indices regardless of the value set for `allow_restricted_indices`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The account was created with the put user-managed service account API.|
|roles|[string]|true|none|The names of the roles granted to the account, as sent on the last PUT of the account.<br>They are resolved when the account authenticates.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the account can authenticate.|
|description|string|false|none|A free-text description of the account, as sent on the last PUT of the account.<br>It has no meaning to Elasticsearch. Absent when the account has no description.|
|created_by|object|false|none|The user who created the account.<br>Absent for an account that was created before Elasticsearch recorded its creator.|
|created_at|object|false|none|When the account was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.<br>Absent for an account that was created before Elasticsearch recorded its creation time.|
|created_by_profile_uid|string|false|none|The profile UID of the user who created the account.<br>Returned only when `with_profile_uid` is `true` and that user has an activated user profile.|
|updated_by|object|false|none|The user who last replaced the account with the put user-managed service account API.<br>Absent until the account is first replaced.|
|updated_at|object|false|none|When the account was last replaced, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.<br>Absent until the account is first replaced.|
|updated_by_profile_uid|string|false|none|The profile UID of the user who last replaced the account.<br>Returned only when `with_profile_uid` is `true` and that user has an activated user profile.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|user_managed|

<h2 id="tocS_security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountAuthor">security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountAuthor</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccountauthor"></a>
<a id="schema_security.get_service_accounts.ServiceAccountAuthor"></a>
<a id="tocSsecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccountauthor"></a>
<a id="tocssecurity.get_service_accounts.serviceaccountauthor"></a>

```json
{
  "username": {},
  "realm": "string",
  "realm_type": "string",
  "api_key": {
    "id": {},
    "name": {}
  }
}
```

The user who wrote a user-managed service account.
If the request ran as another user, that user is recorded.
If the request was made with an API key, the owner of the key is recorded, from the owner's own realm, together with the key itself.
For an older API key that does not record its owner's realm, the realm is the API key realm, `_es_api_key`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|object|true|none|The username of the user.|
|realm|string|true|none|The name of the realm that authenticated the user.|
|realm_type|string|true|none|The type of the realm that authenticated the user.|
|api_key|object|false|none|The API key that the request was made with.<br>Absent when the request was not made with an API key, or when the API key ran as another user.|

Implicitly, restricted indices have limited privileges that can cause pattern tests to fail. ### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Sub-aggregations for this aggregation.<br>Only applies to bucket aggregations.|
|meta|object|false|none|none|
|cardinality|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that calculates an approximate count of distinct values.|
|composite|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation that creates composite buckets from different sources.<br>Unlike the other multi-bucket aggregations, you can use the `composite` aggregation to paginate *all* buckets from a multi-level aggregation efficiently.|
|date_range|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation that enables the user to define a set of date ranges - each representing a bucket.|
|filter|object|false|none|A single bucket aggregation that narrows the set of documents to those that match a query.|
|filters|object|false|none|A multi-bucket aggregation where each bucket contains the documents that match a query.|
|missing|object|false|none|none|
|range|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation that enables the user to define a set of ranges - each representing a bucket.|
|terms|object|false|none|A multi-bucket value source based aggregation where buckets are dynamically built - one per unique value.|
|value_count|object|false|none|A single-value metrics aggregation that counts the number of values that are extracted from the aggregated documents.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bool|object|false|none|Matches documents matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|exists|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain an indexed value for a field.|
|ids|object|false|none|Returns documents based on their IDs.<br>This query uses document IDs stored in the `_id` field.|
|match|object|false|none|Returns documents that match a provided text, number, date or boolean value.<br>The provided text is analyzed before matching.|
|match_all|object|false|none|Matches all documents, giving them all a `_score` of 1.0.|
|prefix|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain a specific prefix in a provided field.|
|range|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms within a provided range.|
|simple_query_string|object|false|none|Returns documents based on a provided query string, using a parser with a limited but fault-tolerant syntax.|
|term|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain an exact term in a provided field.<br>To return a document, the query term must exactly match the queried field's value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|terms|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain one or more exact terms in a provided field.<br>To return a document, one or more terms must exactly match a field value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|wildcard|object|false|none|Returns documents that contain terms matching a wildcard pattern.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bool|object|false|none|matches roles matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|exists|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain an indexed value for a field.|
|ids|object|false|none|Returns roles based on their IDs.<br>This query uses role document IDs stored in the `_id` field.|
|match|object|false|none|Returns roles that match a provided text, number, date or boolean value.<br>The provided text is analyzed before matching.|
|match_all|object|false|none|Matches all roles, giving them all a `_score` of 1.0.|
|prefix|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain a specific prefix in a provided field.|
|range|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain terms within a provided range.|
|simple_query_string|object|false|none|Returns roles based on a provided query string, using a parser with a limited but fault-tolerant syntax.|
|term|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain an exact term in a provided field.<br>To return a document, the query term must exactly match the queried field's value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|terms|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain one or more exact terms in a provided field.<br>To return a document, one or more terms must exactly match a field value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|wildcard|object|false|none|Returns roles that contain terms matching a wildcard pattern.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|object|false|none|Returns users based on their IDs.<br>This query uses the user document IDs stored in the `_id` field.|
|bool|object|false|none|matches users matching boolean combinations of other queries.|
|exists|object|false|none|Returns users that contain an indexed value for a field.|
|match|object|false|none|Returns users that match a provided text, number, date or boolean value.<br>The provided text is analyzed before matching.|
|match_all|object|false|none|Matches all users, giving them all a `_score` of 1.0.|
|prefix|object|false|none|Returns users that contain a specific prefix in a provided field.|
|range|object|false|none|Returns users that contain terms within a provided range.|
|simple_query_string|object|false|none|Returns users based on a provided query string, using a parser with a limited but fault-tolerant syntax.|
|term|object|false|none|Returns users that contain an exact term in a provided field.<br>To return a document, the query term must exactly match the queried field's value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|terms|object|false|none|Returns users that contain one or more exact terms in a provided field.<br>To return a document, one or more terms must exactly match a field value, including whitespace and capitalization.|
|wildcard|object|false|none|Returns users that contain terms matching a wildcard pattern.|

The results of ingest simulation on a single document. The _source of the document contains
the results after running all pipelines listed in executed_pipelines on the document. The
list of executed pipelines is derived from the pipelines that would be executed if this
document had been ingested into _index.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|object|true|none|Identifier for the document.|
|_index|object|true|none|Name of the index that the document would be indexed into if this were not a simulation.|
|_source|object|true|none|JSON body for the document.|
|_version|object|true|none|none|
|executed_pipelines|[string]|true|none|A list of the names of the pipelines executed on this document.|
|ignored_fields|[object]|false|none|A list of the fields that would be ignored at the indexing step. For example, a field whose<br>value is larger than the allowed limit would make it through all of the pipelines, but<br>would not be indexed into Elasticsearch.|
|error|object|false|none|Any error resulting from simulatng ingest on this doc. This can be an error generated by<br>executing a processor, or a mapping validation error when simulating indexing the resulting<br>doc.|
|effective_mapping|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ignore_unavailable|boolean|false|none|If false, the snapshot fails if any data stream or index in indices is missing or closed. If true, the snapshot ignores missing or closed data streams and indices.|
|indices|object|false|none|A comma-separated list of data streams and indices to include in the snapshot. Multi-index syntax is supported.<br>By default, a snapshot includes all data streams and indices in the cluster. If this argument is provided, the snapshot only includes the specified data streams and clusters.|
|include_global_state|boolean|false|none|If true, the current global state is included in the snapshot.|
|feature_states|[string]|false|none|A list of feature states to be included in this snapshot. A list of features available for inclusion in the snapshot and their descriptions be can be retrieved using the get features API.<br>Each feature state includes one or more system indices containing data necessary for the function of that feature. Providing an empty array will include no feature states in the snapshot, regardless of the value of include_global_state. By default, all available feature states will be included in the snapshot if include_global_state is true, or no feature states if include_global_state is false.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Attaches arbitrary metadata to the snapshot, such as a record of who took the snapshot, why it was taken, or any other useful data. Metadata must be less than 1024 bytes.|
|partial|boolean|false|none|If false, the entire snapshot will fail if one or more indices included in the snapshot do not have all primary shards available.|

<h2 id="tocS_snapshot._types.AzureRepositorySettings">snapshot._types.AzureRepositorySettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasnapshot._types.azurerepositorysettings"></a>
<a id="schema_snapshot._types.AzureRepositorySettings"></a>
<a id="tocSsnapshot._types.azurerepositorysettings"></a>
<a id="tocssnapshot._types.azurerepositorysettings"></a>

```json
{
  "chunk_size": {},
  "compress": true,
  "max_restore_bytes_per_sec": {},
  "max_snapshot_bytes_per_sec": {},
  "base_path": "string",
  "client": "default",
  "container": "elasticsearch-snapshots",
  "delete_objects_max_size": 256,
  "location_mode": "primary_only",
  "max_concurrent_batch_deletes": 10,
  "readonly": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chunk_size|object|false|none|Big files can be broken down into multiple smaller blobs in the blob store during snapshotting.<br>It is not recommended to change this value from its default unless there is an explicit reason for limiting the size of blobs in the repository.<br>Setting a value lower than the default can result in an increased number of API calls to the blob store during snapshot create and restore operations compared to using the default value and thus make both operations slower and more costly.<br>Specify the chunk size as a byte unit, for example: `10MB`, `5KB`, 500B.<br>The default varies by repository type.|
|compress|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, metadata files are stored in compressed format.<br>This setting doesn't affect index files that are already compressed by default.|
|max_restore_bytes_per_sec|object|false|none|The maximum snapshot restore rate per node.<br>It defaults to unlimited.<br>Note that restores are also throttled through recovery settings.|
|max_snapshot_bytes_per_sec|object|false|none|The maximum snapshot creation rate per node.<br>It defaults to 40mb per second.<br>Note that if the recovery settings for managed services are set, then it defaults to unlimited, and the rate is additionally throttled through recovery settings.|
|base_path|string|false|none|The path to the repository data within the container.<br>It defaults to the root directory.<br><br>NOTE: Don't set `base_path` when configuring a snapshot repository for Elastic Cloud Enterprise.<br>Elastic Cloud Enterprise automatically generates the `base_path` for each deployment so that multiple deployments can share the same bucket.|
|client|string|false|none|The name of the Azure repository client to use.|
|container|string|false|none|The Azure container.|
|delete_objects_max_size|number|false|none|The maxmimum batch size, between 1 and 256, used for `BlobBatch` requests.<br>Defaults to 256 which is the maximum number supported by the Azure blob batch API.|
|location_mode|string|false|none|Either `primary_only` or `secondary_only`.<br>Note that if you set it to `secondary_only`, it will force `readonly` to `true`.|
|max_concurrent_batch_deletes|number|false|none|The maximum number of concurrent batch delete requests that will be submitted for any individual bulk delete with `BlobBatch`.<br>Note that the effective number of concurrent deletes is further limited by the Azure client connection and event loop thread limits.<br>Defaults to 10, minimum is 1, maximum is 100.|
|readonly|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the repository is read-only.<br>The cluster can retrieve and restore snapshots from the repository but not write to the repository or create snapshots in it.<br><br>Only a cluster with write access can create snapshots in the repository.<br>All other clusters connected to the repository should have the `readonly` parameter set to `true`.<br>If `false`, the cluster can write to the repository and create snapshots in it.<br><br>IMPORTANT: If you register the same snapshot repository with multiple clusters, only one cluster should have write access to the repository.<br>Having multiple clusters write to the repository at the same time risks corrupting the contents of the repository.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chunk_size|object|false|none|Big files can be broken down into multiple smaller blobs in the blob store during snapshotting.<br>It is not recommended to change this value from its default unless there is an explicit reason for limiting the size of blobs in the repository.<br>Setting a value lower than the default can result in an increased number of API calls to the blob store during snapshot create and restore operations compared to using the default value and thus make both operations slower and more costly.<br>Specify the chunk size as a byte unit, for example: `10MB`, `5KB`, 500B.<br>The default varies by repository type.|
|compress|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, metadata files are stored in compressed format.<br>This setting doesn't affect index files that are already compressed by default.|
|max_restore_bytes_per_sec|object|false|none|The maximum snapshot restore rate per node.<br>It defaults to unlimited.<br>Note that restores are also throttled through recovery settings.|
|max_snapshot_bytes_per_sec|object|false|none|The maximum snapshot creation rate per node.<br>It defaults to 40mb per second.<br>Note that if the recovery settings for managed services are set, then it defaults to unlimited, and the rate is additionally throttled through recovery settings.|
|bucket|string|true|none|The name of the S3 bucket to use for snapshots.<br>The bucket name must adhere to Amazon's S3 bucket naming rules.|
|base_path|string|false|none|The path to the repository data within its bucket.<br>It defaults to an empty string, meaning that the repository is at the root of the bucket.<br>The value of this setting should not start or end with a forward slash (`/`).<br><br>NOTE: Don't set base_path when configuring a snapshot repository for Elastic Cloud Enterprise.<br>Elastic Cloud Enterprise automatically generates the `base_path` for each deployment so that multiple deployments may share the same bucket.|
|buffer_size|object|false|none|The minimum threshold below which the chunk is uploaded using a single request.<br>Beyond this threshold, the S3 repository will use the AWS Multipart Upload API to split the chunk into several parts, each of `buffer_size` length, and to upload each part in its own request.<br>Note that setting a buffer size lower than 5mb is not allowed since it will prevent the use of the Multipart API and may result in upload errors.<br>It is also not possible to set a buffer size greater than 5gb as it is the maximum upload size allowed by S3.<br>Defaults to `100mb` or 5% of JVM heap, whichever is smaller.|
|canned_acl|string|false|none|The S3 repository supports all S3 canned ACLs: `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `authenticated-read`, `log-delivery-write`, `bucket-owner-read`, `bucket-owner-full-control`.<br>You could specify a canned ACL using the `canned_acl` setting.<br>When the S3 repository creates buckets and objects, it adds the canned ACL into the buckets and objects.|
|client|string|false|none|The name of the S3 client to use to connect to S3.|
|delete_objects_max_size|number|false|none|The maxmimum batch size, between 1 and 1000, used for `DeleteObjects` requests.<br>Defaults to 1000 which is the maximum number supported by the  AWS DeleteObjects API.|
|get_register_retry_delay|object|false|none|The time to wait before trying again if an attempt to read a linearizable register fails.|
|max_multipart_parts|number|false|none|The maximum number of parts that Elasticsearch will write during a multipart upload of a single object.<br>Files which are larger than `buffer_size × max_multipart_parts` will be chunked into several smaller objects.<br>Elasticsearch may also split a file across multiple objects to satisfy other constraints such as the `chunk_size` limit.<br>Defaults to `10000` which is the maximum number of parts in a multipart upload in AWS S3.|
|max_multipart_upload_cleanup_size|number|false|none|The maximum number of possibly-dangling multipart uploads to clean up in each batch of snapshot deletions.<br>Defaults to 1000 which is the maximum number supported by the AWS ListMultipartUploads API.<br>If set to `0`, Elasticsearch will not attempt to clean up dangling multipart uploads.|
|readonly|boolean|false|none|If true, the repository is read-only.<br>The cluster can retrieve and restore snapshots from the repository but not write to the repository or create snapshots in it.<br><br>Only a cluster with write access can create snapshots in the repository.<br>All other clusters connected to the repository should have the `readonly` parameter set to `true`.<br><br>If `false`, the cluster can write to the repository and create snapshots in it.<br><br>IMPORTANT: If you register the same snapshot repository with multiple clusters, only one cluster should have write access to the repository.<br>Having multiple clusters write to the repository at the same time risks corrupting the contents of the repository.|
|server_side_encryption|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, files are encrypted on server side using an AES256 algorithm.|
|storage_class|string|false|none|The S3 storage class for objects written to the repository.<br>Values may be `standard`, `reduced_redundancy`, `standard_ia`, `onezone_ia`, and `intelligent_tiering`.|
|throttled_delete_retry.delay_increment|object|false|none|The delay before the first retry and the amount the delay is incremented by on each subsequent retry.<br>The default is 50ms and the minimum is 0ms.|
|throttled_delete_retry.maximum_delay|object|false|none|The upper bound on how long the delays between retries will grow to.<br>The default is 5s and the minimum is 0ms.|
|throttled_delete_retry.maximum_number_of_retries|number|false|none|The number times to retry a throttled snapshot deletion.<br>The default is 10 and the minimum value is 0 which will disable retries altogether.<br>Note that if retries are enabled in the Azure client, each of these retries comprises that many client-level retries.|

```json
  "max_multipart_upload_cleanup_size": 1000,
  "readonly": false,
  "server_side_encryption": false,
  "storage_class": "standard",
  "throttled_delete_retry.delay_increment": "50ms",
  "throttled_delete_retry.maximum_delay": "5s",
  "throttled_delete_retry.maximum_number_of_retries": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delegate_type|string|true|none|none|
|bucket|string|true|none|The name of the S3 bucket to use for snapshots.<br>The bucket name must adhere to Amazon's S3 bucket naming rules.|
|base_path|string|false|none|The path to the repository data within its bucket.<br>It defaults to an empty string, meaning that the repository is at the root of the bucket.<br>The value of this setting should not start or end with a forward slash (`/`).<br><br>NOTE: Don't set base_path when configuring a snapshot repository for Elastic Cloud Enterprise.<br>Elastic Cloud Enterprise automatically generates the `base_path` for each deployment so that multiple deployments may share the same bucket.|
|buffer_size|object|false|none|The minimum threshold below which the chunk is uploaded using a single request.<br>Beyond this threshold, the S3 repository will use the AWS Multipart Upload API to split the chunk into several parts, each of `buffer_size` length, and to upload each part in its own request.<br>Note that setting a buffer size lower than 5mb is not allowed since it will prevent the use of the Multipart API and may result in upload errors.<br>It is also not possible to set a buffer size greater than 5gb as it is the maximum upload size allowed by S3.<br>Defaults to `100mb` or 5% of JVM heap, whichever is smaller.|
|canned_acl|string|false|none|The S3 repository supports all S3 canned ACLs: `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `authenticated-read`, `log-delivery-write`, `bucket-owner-read`, `bucket-owner-full-control`.<br>You could specify a canned ACL using the `canned_acl` setting.<br>When the S3 repository creates buckets and objects, it adds the canned ACL into the buckets and objects.|
|client|string|false|none|The name of the S3 client to use to connect to S3.|
|delete_objects_max_size|number|false|none|The maxmimum batch size, between 1 and 1000, used for `DeleteObjects` requests.<br>Defaults to 1000 which is the maximum number supported by the  AWS DeleteObjects API.|
|get_register_retry_delay|object|false|none|The time to wait before trying again if an attempt to read a linearizable register fails.|
|max_multipart_parts|number|false|none|The maximum number of parts that Elasticsearch will write during a multipart upload of a single object.<br>Files which are larger than `buffer_size × max_multipart_parts` will be chunked into several smaller objects.<br>Elasticsearch may also split a file across multiple objects to satisfy other constraints such as the `chunk_size` limit.<br>Defaults to `10000` which is the maximum number of parts in a multipart upload in AWS S3.|
|max_multipart_upload_cleanup_size|number|false|none|The maximum number of possibly-dangling multipart uploads to clean up in each batch of snapshot deletions.<br>Defaults to 1000 which is the maximum number supported by the AWS ListMultipartUploads API.<br>If set to `0`, Elasticsearch will not attempt to clean up dangling multipart uploads.|
|readonly|boolean|false|none|If true, the repository is read-only.<br>The cluster can retrieve and restore snapshots from the repository but not write to the repository or create snapshots in it.<br><br>Only a cluster with write access can create snapshots in the repository.<br>All other clusters connected to the repository should have the `readonly` parameter set to `true`.<br><br>If `false`, the cluster can write to the repository and create snapshots in it.<br><br>IMPORTANT: If you register the same snapshot repository with multiple clusters, only one cluster should have write access to the repository.<br>Having multiple clusters write to the repository at the same time risks corrupting the contents of the repository.|
|server_side_encryption|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, files are encrypted on server side using an AES256 algorithm.|
|storage_class|string|false|none|The S3 storage class for objects written to the repository.<br>Values may be `standard`, `reduced_redundancy`, `standard_ia`, `onezone_ia`, and `intelligent_tiering`.|
|throttled_delete_retry.delay_increment|object|false|none|The delay before the first retry and the amount the delay is incremented by on each subsequent retry.<br>The default is 50ms and the minimum is 0ms.|
|throttled_delete_retry.maximum_delay|object|false|none|The upper bound on how long the delays between retries will grow to.<br>The default is 5s and the minimum is 0ms.|
|throttled_delete_retry.maximum_number_of_retries|number|false|none|The number times to retry a throttled snapshot deletion.<br>The default is 10 and the minimum value is 0 which will disable retries altogether.<br>Note that if retries are enabled in the Azure client, each of these retries comprises that many client-level retries.|

|Property|Value|

|first_byte_time_nanos|object|true|none|The length of time waiting for the first byte of the read operation to be received, in nanoseconds.<br>If the blob was not found, this detail is omitted.|
|found|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the blob was found by the read operation.<br>If the read was started before the write completed or the write was ended before completion, it might be false.|
|node|object|true|none|The node that performed the read operation.|
|throttled|object|false|none|The length of time spent waiting due to the `max_restore_bytes_per_sec` or `indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec` throttles during the read of the blob.<br>If the blob was not found, this detail is omitted.|
|throttled_nanos|object|false|none|The length of time spent waiting due to the `max_restore_bytes_per_sec` or `indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec` throttles during the read of the blob, in nanoseconds.<br>If the blob was not found, this detail is omitted.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorization|object|false|none|The security privileges that the transform uses to run its queries. If Elastic Stack security features were disabled at the time of the most recent update to the transform, this property is omitted.|
|create_time|object|false|none|The time the transform was created.|
|create_time_string|object|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|Free text description of the transform.|
|dest|object|true|none|The destination for the transform.|
|frequency|object|false|none|none|
|id|object|true|none|none|
|latest|object|false|none|none|
|pivot|object|false|none|The pivot method transforms the data by aggregating and grouping it.|
|retention_policy|object|false|none|none|
|settings|object|false|none|Defines optional transform settings.|
|source|object|true|none|The source of the data for the transform.|
|sync|object|false|none|Defines the properties transforms require to run continuously.|
|version|object|false|none|The version of Elasticsearch that existed on the node when the transform was created.|
|_meta|object|false|none|none|

```json
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "service_account": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|object|false|none|If an API key was used for the most recent update to the transform, its name and identifier are listed in the response.|
|roles|[string]|false|none|If a user ID was used for the most recent update to the transform, its roles at the time of the update are listed in the response.|
|service_account|string|false|none|If a service account was used for the most recent update to the transform, the account name is listed in the response.|

<h2 id="tocS_transform._types.Destination">transform._types.Destination</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocstransform._types.destination"></a>

```json
{
  "index": {},
  "aliases": [
    {
      "alias": {},
      "move_on_creation": false
    }
  ],
  "pipeline": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|object|false|none|The destination index for the transform. The mappings of the destination index are deduced based on the source<br>fields when possible. If alternate mappings are required, use the create index API prior to starting the<br>transform.|
|aliases|[[transform._types.DestinationAlias](#schematransform._types.destinationalias)]|false|none|The aliases that the destination index for the transform should have.<br>Aliases are manipulated using the stored credentials of the transform, which means the secondary credentials<br>supplied at creation time (if both primary and secondary credentials are specified).<br><br>The destination index is added to the aliases regardless of whether the destination index was created by the<br>transform or pre-created by the user.|
|pipeline|string|false|none|The unique identifier for an ingest pipeline.|

```json
  "move_on_creation": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alias|object|true|none|The name of the alias.|
|move_on_creation|boolean|false|none|Whether the destination index should be the only index in this alias.<br>If `true`, all the other indices will be removed from this alias before adding the destination index to this<br>alias. This does not delete the removed indices; it only removes them from the alias.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregations|object|false|none|Defines how to aggregate the grouped data. The following aggregations are currently supported: average, bucket<br>script, bucket selector, cardinality, filter, geo bounds, geo centroid, geo line, max, median absolute deviation,<br>min, missing, percentiles, rare terms, scripted metric, stats, sum, terms, top metrics, value count, weighted<br>average.|
|group_by|object|false|none|Defines how to group the data. More than one grouping can be defined per pivot. The following groupings are<br>currently supported: date histogram, geotile grid, histogram, terms.|

<h2 id="tocS_transform._types.Settings">transform._types.Settings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransform._types.settings"></a>
<a id="schema_transform._types.Settings"></a>
<a id="tocStransform._types.settings"></a>
<a id="tocstransform._types.settings"></a>

```json
{
  "align_checkpoints": true,
  "dates_as_epoch_millis": false,
  "deduce_mappings": true,
  "docs_per_second": 0,
  "max_page_search_size": 0,
  "use_point_in_time": true,
  "num_failure_retries": 0,
  "unattended": false,
  "indexer_request_timeout": "30s"
}
```

The source of the data for the transform.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|align_checkpoints|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the transform checkpoint ranges should be optimized for performance. Such optimization can align<br>checkpoint ranges with the date histogram interval when date histogram is specified as a group source in the<br>transform config. As a result, less document updates in the destination index will be performed thus improving<br>overall performance.|
|dates_as_epoch_millis|boolean|false|none|Defines if dates in the ouput should be written as ISO formatted string or as millis since epoch. epoch_millis was<br>the default for transforms created before version 7.11. For compatible output set this value to `true`.|
|deduce_mappings|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the transform should deduce the destination index mappings from the transform configuration.|
|docs_per_second|number|false|none|Specifies a limit on the number of input documents per second. This setting throttles the transform by adding a<br>wait time between search requests. The default value is null, which disables throttling.|
|max_page_search_size|number|false|none|Defines the initial page size to use for the composite aggregation for each checkpoint. If circuit breaker<br>exceptions occur, the page size is dynamically adjusted to a lower value. The minimum value is `10` and the<br>maximum is `65,536`. The default value is `500` for `pivot` transforms and `5000` for `latest` transforms.|
|use_point_in_time|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the transform checkpoint will use the Point In Time API while searching over the source index.<br>In general, Point In Time is an optimization that will reduce pressure on the source index by reducing the amount<br>of refreshes and merges, but it can be expensive if a large number of Point In Times are opened and closed for a<br>given index. The benefits and impact depend on the data being searched, the ingest rate into the source index, and<br>the amount of other consumers searching the same source index.|
|num_failure_retries|number|false|none|Defines the number of retries on a recoverable failure before the transform task is marked as `failed`.<br>The minimum value is `0` and the maximum is `100`, where `-1` indicates that the transform retries indefinitely.<br>If unset, the cluster-level setting `num_transform_failure_retries` is used.<br><br>This setting cannot be specified when `unattended` is `true`, because unattended transforms always retry<br>indefinitely.|
|unattended|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the transform runs in unattended mode. In unattended mode, the transform retries indefinitely in case<br>of an error which means the transform never fails. Setting the number of retries other than infinite fails in<br>validation.|
|indexer_request_timeout|object|false|none|The initial timeout for the requests the transform sends to nodes to retrieve checkpoint information.<br>Each consecutive failure doubles the timeout, up to a maximum of `12h`. The minimum value is `1ms` and the<br>maximum is `12h`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|object|true|none|The source indices for the transform. It can be a single index, an index pattern (for example, `"my-index-*""`), an<br>array of indices (for example, `["my-index-000001", "my-index-000002"]`), or an array of index patterns (for<br>example, `["my-index-*", "my-other-index-*"]`. For remote indices use the syntax `"remote_name:index_name"`. If<br>any indices are in remote clusters then the master node and at least one transform node must have the `remote_cluster_client` node role.|
|query|object|false|none|A query clause that retrieves a subset of data from the source index.|
|runtime_mappings|object|false|none|Definitions of search-time runtime fields that can be used by the transform. For search runtime fields all data<br>nodes, including remote nodes, must be 7.12 or later.|

```json
  },
```

```json
    "doc_id": {},
    "index": {},
    "refresh": {},

  }
```


The result of an index action.
It is a container that holds either the `response` of an executed index
operation, or the `request` that would have run when the action is simulated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|response|[watcher._types.IndexResultSummary](#schemawatcher._types.indexresultsummary) \| [[watcher._types.IndexResultSummary](#schemawatcher._types.indexresultsummary)]|false|none|The outcome of the index operation.<br>A single summary is returned when a single document is indexed, or an array<br>when several documents are indexed at once. When a bulk operation ends in<br>`failure` or `partial_failure`, the array includes failed items.|
|request|object|false|none|The request that would have been executed.<br>It is only present when the action is simulated.|

<h2 id="tocS_watcher._types.IndexResultSummary">watcher._types.IndexResultSummary</h2>

```json
{
  "id": {},
  "index": {},
  "created": true,
  "result": {},
  "version": {},
  "failed": true,
  "message": "string"
}
```

A single item of an index action result.
Successful items and failed items expose different fields; only `id` and `index`
are present in both. Failed items appear when a bulk index action ends in
`failure` or `partial_failure`.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|object|true|none|none|
|index|object|true|none|none|
|created|boolean|false|none|none|
|result|object|false|none|none|
|version|object|false|none|none|
|failed|boolean|false|none|Only present for failed items|
|message|string|false|none|Only present for failed items|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|current_watches|[[watcher.stats.WatchRecordStats](#schemawatcher.stats.watchrecordstats)]|false|none|The current executing watches metric gives insight into the watches that are currently being executed by Watcher.<br>Additional information is shared per watch that is currently executing.<br>This information includes the `watch_id`, the time its execution started and its current execution phase.<br>To include this metric, the `metric` option should be set to `current_watches` or `_all`.<br>In addition you can also specify the `emit_stacktraces=true` parameter, which adds stack traces for each watch that is being run.<br>These stack traces can give you more insight into an execution of a watch.|
|execution_thread_pool|object|true|none|none|
|queued_watches|[[watcher.stats.WatchRecordQueuedStats](#schemawatcher.stats.watchrecordqueuedstats)]|false|none|Watcher moderates the execution of watches such that their execution won't put too much pressure on the node and its resources.<br>If too many watches trigger concurrently and there isn't enough capacity to run them all, some of the watches are queued, waiting for the current running watches to finish.s<br>The queued watches metric gives insight on these queued watches.<br><br>To include this metric, the `metric` option should include `queued_watches` or `_all`.|
|watch_count|number|true|none|The number of watches currently registered.|
|watcher_state|object|true|none|The current state of Watcher.|
|node_id|object|true|none|none|

Usage statistics for data stream lifecycle (DLM), reported by `_xpack/usage` under `data_lifecycle`.
Besides `available` and `enabled`, all the following statistics are only present when the feature is enabled.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h2 id="tocS_xpack.usage.Logging">xpack.usage.Logging</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocSxpack.usage.logging"></a>
<a id="tocsxpack.usage.logging"></a>

```json
{
  "querylog": {
    "enabled": true,
    "user": true,
    "system": true,
    "threshold": {}
  },
  "esql": {
    "enabled": true,
    "user": true,
    "thresholds": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

Usage statistics about logging configuration reported by `_xpack/usage`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|querylog|object|true|none|Search query log configuration.|
|esql|object|true|none|ES\|QL query log configuration.|

<h2 id="tocS_xpack.usage.QueryLoggingConfig">xpack.usage.QueryLoggingConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaxpack.usage.queryloggingconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_xpack.usage.QueryLoggingConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSxpack.usage.queryloggingconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsxpack.usage.queryloggingconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "user": true,
  "system": true,
  "threshold": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether query logging is enabled.|
|user|boolean|true|none|Whether user information is included in the query log.|
|system|boolean|true|none|Whether system queries are included in the query log.|
|threshold|object|false|none|The configured logging threshold, if any.|

```json
  "thresholds": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether ES\|QL query logging is enabled.|
|user|boolean|true|none|Whether user information is included in the ES\|QL query log.|
|thresholds|object|false|none|The configured logging thresholds, keyed by threshold name, if any.|

Usage statistics for indices using the `vectordb_document` index mode.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|boolean|true|none|none|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|none|

|num_docs|number|true|none|The total number of documents held across all `vectordb_document` indices.|
